TITLE: CANEX Create-Thon 2026 ($50,000 prize pool)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 25, 2026

Applications for the CANEX Create-Thon 2026 are now open. The CANEX Create-Thon 2026, powered by Gebeya is a Pan-African creative technology competition designed to discover and showcase Africa’s next generation of innovators across Gaming, Video, and Music.

Brought to you by CANEX in partnership with Gebeya and Afreximbank Innovation Lab, participants will take part in an intensive 4 day build sprint, using DALA Studio’s AI technology to transform creative ideas into working projects. Beyond the competition, CANEX Create-thon connects creators with cutting edge AI technical tools, continental exposure and the opportunity to showcase the selected finalists at CANEX Weekend 2026 in Lagos.

Categories

Showcase your brand on one platform with industry leaders from around the world.

Gaming: Create African-inspired games, immersive experiences, gameplay innovations- leveraging AI tools for building.

Video: Develop African-inspired storytelling experiences and video production using AI-powered content or visual media elements.

Music: Build African-inspired music experiences, leveraging AI-powered sound innovation tools and components.

Benefits

Access to cash prizes: Compete for a share of the US$50,000 prize pool, awarded to the top creators in recognition of outstanding innovation, creativity, and technical excellence across the Gaming, Video, and Music categories. Additional prizes for top 20 submissions per country.

Build with AI – DALA Studios: Turn bold ideas into working prototypes during an intensive 4 day Create-thon, leveraging Gebeya’s AI-powered, DALA Studios, compute resources, and technical infrastructure provided through the programme.

Mentorship from Industry Experts: Receive hands-on guidance from Gebeya’s network of Dala Studio experts and community ambassadors who will support throughout the build sprint.

Continental Recognition, exposure to industry leaders: Showcase your project to leading voices in Africa’s creative and technology ecosystem through CANEX and Afreximbank Innovation Lab, positioning your work for greater visibility across the continent.

Eligibility

Open to African creators, innovators and builders living on the continent and in the diaspora who are passionate about using technology to shape the future of the creative economy.

Participants may apply as individuals in one of three competition categories: Gaming, Video or Music. The competition welcomes game developers, musicians and producers, filmmakers, video creators, designers, digital artists, developers, creative technologists, AI builders, startups and multidisciplinary teams.

Applicants must be 18 years or older at the time of registration. All submissions must be originally developed during the official CANEX Create-thon build sprint on DALA Studio by Gebeya.

Participants may be required to provide proof of identity, age, or ownership of their submitted project during the selection process.

Application

Participants are required to:

Register for CANEX Create-thon 2026, powered by Gebeya

Get familiar with the tools and build some test projects ahead of the Create-thon

Build sprint Opens officially:

Select one competition category: Gaming, Video or Music.

Build an original project during the official build sprint.

Submit a working project before the submission deadline, accompanied by a project brief.

Ensure all submitted work is original and complies with the competition rules.

Click here to apply

For more information, visit CANEX Creative Pitch Competition.

TITLE: Official Launch of the AAU Europe Regional Office – Nottingham University, UK

All stakeholders are invited to join us for the launch of the AAU Europe Regional Office. For virtual participation, kindly find below the streaming Link- https://tinyurl.com/AAUEROLaunch

Details

On behalf of the University of Nottingham and the Association of African Universities (AAU), we are delighted to invite you to virtually join the opening celebration of the AAU Europe Regional Office, a new division of the Association based at the campus of the University of Nottingham, United Kingdom. The Europe Regional Office’s role is to centrally coordinate AAU’s existing and emerging partnerships across Europe, facilitating cooperation between AAU member institutions across the European academic community.

This launch event is being held on Wednesday, March 6, 2024, at the University of Nottingham, UK, featuring a showcase of collaborative research and the projects of the Office, plenary discussions concerning the future development of higher education across Africa, and a formal opening ceremony.

TITLE: AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator 2026: Global Volunteer Leadership Opportunity with Full Scholarship to the 2027 Youth Assembly in Geneva

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The AFS Youth Assembly is inviting its alumni to apply to become Impact Coordinators, a significant global leadership opportunity designed for young changemakers who want to help transform ideas into measurable social impact while strengthening youth-led initiatives across different regions of the world.

Launched as part of the next phase of the AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network, the Impact Coordinator opportunity places selected alumni at the center of regional youth engagement, project development, mentorship, collaboration, and impact-building. Impact Coordinators will serve for a two-year term, working with Youth Assembly alumni in their respective regions and helping them develop ideas, identify resources, connect with relevant opportunities, and advance projects that contribute to positive social change.

A particularly attractive benefit of the opportunity is that selected Impact Coordinators will receive a full scholarship to attend the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva, Switzerland. Coordinators will also receive training support and an AFS Global Competence Certificate while developing practical leadership, communication, organizational, mentoring, networking, and project coordination skills.

About the AFS Youth Assembly

The AFS Youth Assembly is an international platform that brings together young leaders, changemakers, social entrepreneurs, activists, students, professionals, educators, and other individuals committed to building more inclusive, peaceful, sustainable, and equitable societies.

The platform focuses on helping emerging leaders connect across borders, develop global competence, acquire practical skills, build partnerships, and translate ideas into action.

The Youth Assembly was founded in 2004 by the Friendship Ambassadors Foundation and is now part of AFS Intercultural Programs. AFS is an international nonprofit organization focused on intercultural learning and the development of knowledge, skills, and understanding that can contribute to a more just and peaceful world.

The Youth Assembly is intended to be more than a stand-alone international gathering. Participants are encouraged to continue their development and community engagement after attending the Assembly through opportunities such as the Alumni Impact Network, leadership roles, mentoring, project development, collaboration, and other AFS activities.

What Is the AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network?

The AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network is a global community created to help former Youth Assembly participants continue developing their ideas and generating impact after the Assembly.

Rather than allowing the Youth Assembly experience to end when delegates return home, the network provides a structure through which alumni can remain connected, collaborate with other changemakers, obtain mentorship, access useful resources, develop their skills, pursue project support, and showcase their achievements.

The network is designed to support alumni in several important areas, including:

Developing and implementing action-oriented projects;

Receiving mentorship and connections to relevant experts;

Accessing opportunities for seed funding;

Building regional and international partnerships;

Connecting with other Youth Assembly alumni;

Showcasing successful projects and achievements internationally;

Participating in skills-development activities; and

Receiving peer-to-peer support from other young changemakers.

The Alumni Impact Network is open to people who have previously participated in a session of the Youth Assembly.

Why AFS Is Recruiting Impact Coordinators

Following the 31st AFS Youth Assembly held in Geneva in August 2026, the Alumni Impact Network is moving into another stage of its development.

AFS is coordinating alumni engagement and impact activities across six major geographic regions:

Africa

Asia and Oceania

Europe

Latin America and the Caribbean

Middle East and North Africa

North America

Impact Coordinators are intended to provide the regional leadership needed to connect alumni, encourage collaboration and help turn promising ideas into practical initiatives.

They will effectively serve as an important connection between the wider AFS Youth Assembly network and alumni working on projects and initiatives within their regions.

What Does an AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator Do?

An Impact Coordinator is expected to be more than a representative or titleholder. The position involves actively engaging with Youth Assembly alumni and helping create an environment where ideas, partnerships, resources, mentorship, and youth-led action can come together.

Coordinators will help alumni progress from having an idea to developing and implementing meaningful activities.

Their work can involve motivating alumni, connecting changemakers with one another, identifying useful resources, helping projects gain visibility and keeping AFS informed about the progress being made within their region.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to applicants who already have practical experience in youth engagement, social entrepreneurship, community projects, mentoring, sustainable development, advocacy, nonprofit activities or other forms of social impact.

Key Responsibilities of an Impact Coordinator

Selected Impact Coordinators will take on several major responsibilities during their two-year leadership term.

1. Provide Regional Leadership

Impact Coordinators will help organize and mobilize Youth Assembly alumni within the region they represent.

This requires maintaining engagement among alumni rather than simply communicating with them occasionally. Coordinators should be capable of encouraging participation, building relationships and creating a stronger regional community of changemakers.

2. Organize Alumni Engagement Activities

Coordinators are expected to bring alumni together through regular engagement.

Depending on circumstances, this may include:

Virtual meetings;

In-person gatherings;

Networking activities;

Collaborative discussions;

Project-focused sessions; and

Other opportunities that encourage alumni to work together.

The broader purpose is to create meaningful collaboration rather than allowing alumni projects to operate entirely in isolation.

3. Help Alumni Turn Ideas into Action

An important part of the position involves supporting alumni who have ideas for social-impact projects or initiatives.

Impact Coordinators should understand how ideas can be developed into practical projects and should be able to help other young changemakers move through this process.

This is one reason AFS is specifically looking for candidates who understand project ideation and who have previously started or participated in successful projects, initiatives or social ventures.

4. Provide Mentorship and Support

Impact Coordinators will have an important mentoring function.

They will help Youth Assembly alumni navigate the challenges involved in developing projects and generating social impact. Candidates with previous mentoring experience or experience working directly with young people are therefore particularly relevant to the role.

5. Connect Alumni with Resources

Successful social-impact initiatives often require more than a good idea. They may require partnerships, mentorship, technical knowledge, networks, visibility or financial resources.

Impact Coordinators are therefore expected to understand the youth and social-impact ecosystem and have knowledge of useful resources such as:

Impact hubs;

Youth networks;

Potential partners;

Mentors;

Relevant organizations;

Project-development resources; and

Other opportunities that could assist alumni.

The wider Alumni Impact Network itself is designed to connect participants with support mechanisms that include mentorship, expert connections and opportunities for seed funding.

6. Encourage Collaboration

Another major responsibility will be connecting Youth Assembly alumni with one another.

Instead of individual changemakers working separately on similar problems, the network aims to encourage cooperation, knowledge sharing and partnerships.

Strong coordinators should therefore be comfortable bringing people together, facilitating communication and encouraging collaborative action.

7. Track Projects and Progress

Impact Coordinators will also help monitor the progress of projects being implemented or supported within their regions.

They will communicate relevant updates to AFS staff, helping the organization understand how alumni projects and initiatives are progressing.

For candidates interested in international development, project management, monitoring, community engagement or nonprofit leadership, this responsibility provides particularly useful practical experience.

8. Promote Alumni Projects Globally

Successful initiatives should not remain invisible.

Impact Coordinators will help showcase the projects and achievements of Youth Assembly alumni to a wider international audience.

This can increase recognition for youth-led initiatives while allowing successful ideas, experiences and lessons to reach other members of the international AFS community.

Benefits of Becoming an AFS Impact Coordinator

Although the Impact Coordinator position is a volunteer role, it comes with substantial professional-development, leadership and networking benefits.

Full Scholarship to the 2027 Youth Assembly in Geneva

One of the most significant benefits is a full scholarship to attend the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva, Switzerland.

This gives selected coordinators the opportunity to return to the international Youth Assembly environment while continuing their leadership journey within the AFS community.

Two Years of Global Leadership Experience

Selected candidates will serve as Impact Coordinators for two years.

A two-year term provides considerably more opportunity to build meaningful relationships, support projects and demonstrate sustained leadership than a short-term volunteer assignment.

International Recognition

Impact Coordinators and the projects they facilitate may be highlighted through social networks and other AFS visibility channels.

This can help coordinators demonstrate their contributions to social impact while increasing the visibility of the initiatives they support.

Leadership and Professional Skills Development

The position provides opportunities to practice skills that can be valuable in future academic and professional settings, including:

Leadership;

Project coordination;

Mentoring;

Community building;

Stakeholder engagement;

Communication;

Networking;

Organization;

Teamwork;

Independent working;

Project monitoring; and

Social-impact development.

AFS Global Competence Certificate

Impact Coordinators will receive an AFS Global Competence Certificate, together with additional training support.

The experience can therefore provide both practical leadership exposure and structured professional development.

Access to a Global Changemaker Community

Impact Coordinators will operate within an established international community of Youth Assembly alumni and changemakers.

The Alumni Impact Network exists specifically to encourage regional and international collaboration, mentorship, project development, access to resources and opportunities for alumni to increase their impact.

Eligibility Requirements for the Impact Coordinator Opportunity

Applicants should review the requirements carefully because this opportunity is not open to the general public.

The most important eligibility requirement is previous participation in the AFS Youth Assembly.

Previous AFS Youth Assembly Participation Is Mandatory

Applicants must have previously attended the AFS Youth Assembly.

AFS explicitly states that the Impact Coordinator position is open only to Youth Assembly alumni. Therefore, someone with excellent leadership or social-impact experience who has never attended the Youth Assembly would not satisfy this fundamental requirement.

Applicants Must Live in the Region They Want to Represent

Candidates must currently live in the geographic region for which they want to serve as an Impact Coordinator.

The six regions covered by the initiative are Africa, Asia and Oceania, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, Middle East and North Africa, and North America.

Strong Interest in Social Impact and the SDGs

Applicants should demonstrate a genuine commitment to social impact and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

This is central to the wider mission of the Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network, which seeks to translate youth leadership into practical action addressing social, environmental and development challenges.

Experience Working with Young People

AFS is seeking applicants with experience working with youth.

Relevant experience could include areas such as mentoring young people or participating in the creation and implementation of action-oriented projects.

Project or Social Venture Experience

Applicants should have started or participated in a successful:

Project;

Initiative; or

Social venture.

This requirement reflects the practical nature of the coordinator role. Candidates will be helping other alumni develop their own initiatives, making previous firsthand project experience particularly valuable.

Understanding of Project Ideation

Candidates should have strong knowledge of the ideation process and understand how social projects and ventures are developed.

This can help coordinators guide alumni from identifying a problem or opportunity through to shaping and advancing a workable initiative.

Networks and Knowledge of Resources

Applicants should have useful connections or knowledge of resources relevant to social-impact work.

These may include impact hubs, organizations, youth resources, partners and other networks that could help Youth Assembly alumni move their projects forward.

Leadership and Communication Skills

AFS is looking for candidates who can demonstrate strong:

Leadership skills;

Communication skills;

Coordination skills; and

Organizational abilities.

These competencies are particularly important because coordinators will be responsible for bringing together people from different backgrounds and supporting multiple activities and initiatives.

Ability to Work Independently and Collaboratively

Candidates should be capable of managing responsibilities independently while also working effectively as part of a wider international network.

Computer and Internet Access

Applicants must have personal access to:

A computer; and

Stable internet connectivity.

This is particularly important because regional and international coordination may involve substantial online communication and virtual engagement.

Time Commitment

Applicants must be willing and able to dedicate sufficient time and effort to the role throughout the appointment.

Potential candidates should therefore consider whether they can realistically maintain an active leadership commitment alongside their academic, professional and personal responsibilities.

English Language Proficiency

Candidates must be proficient in written and spoken English.

Because the position operates within an international network, effective English communication is an important requirement.

Social Media Skills

Applicants should also be comfortable using social media and digital tools for communication and networking.

This aligns with the coordinator’s responsibility to connect alumni and help promote youth-led projects and achievements.

Connection to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals

The Impact Coordinator initiative has a strong relationship with the Sustainable Development Goals.

The AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network is built around supporting youth-led action on major global and regional challenges. The Declaration of Impact 2026, launched during the 31st AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva, establishes shared global and regional priorities and emphasizes collaboration, inclusion, education, equality, sustainability, innovation, health and well-being, and youth leadership.

Impact Coordinators can therefore play an important role in helping young changemakers translate broad sustainable-development ambitions into practical regional and community-level initiatives.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity is particularly suitable for eligible Youth Assembly alumni who see themselves as facilitators and community builders rather than individuals interested only in adding another title to their résumé.

Strong potential applicants are likely to be people who enjoy:

Helping other young leaders succeed;

Mentoring and advising peers;

Developing social-impact projects;

Building partnerships;

Organizing communities and networks;

Connecting people with resources;

Promoting youth-led initiatives;

Working toward the Sustainable Development Goals;

Communicating across cultures; and

Taking responsibility for long-term initiatives.

Applicants should also be prepared for the reality that this is an active two-year volunteer commitment rather than a passive honorary position.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is stated in the official AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator announcement.

Because the official announcement provides an application link without publishing a closing date, interested and eligible Youth Assembly alumni should check the current application status and consider submitting their application as early as possible rather than assuming that applications will remain open indefinitely.

How to Apply for the AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator Opportunity

Eligible applicants should complete the official Impact Coordinator application provided by the AFS Youth Assembly.

Before applying, candidates should ensure that they:

Have previously participated in the AFS Youth Assembly;

Currently live in the region they intend to represent;

Can demonstrate youth engagement or mentoring experience;

Have relevant experience with projects, initiatives or social ventures;

Understand social-project development and ideation;

Can demonstrate leadership, communication, coordination and organizational abilities;

Have sufficient time to commit to the two-year role;

Have reliable access to a computer and stable internet;

Are proficient in spoken and written English; and

Are comfortable using social media and online networking tools.

Official AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator Announcement and Application

Why This Opportunity Matters

The AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator opportunity provides alumni with a chance to move from participating in an international youth platform to helping shape what happens after delegates return to their communities.

The role is particularly significant because it focuses on the stage where many promising youth initiatives face their greatest challenge: converting enthusiasm and ideas into sustained action.

By connecting alumni with mentorship, resources, partnerships, collaboration and wider visibility, Impact Coordinators can help create stronger regional ecosystems for youth-led change.

For the coordinators themselves, the opportunity combines practical leadership experience, international networking, skills development, global recognition, training support and a full scholarship to attend the 2027 Youth Assembly in Geneva.

Conclusion

The AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator 2026 opportunity is an attractive international leadership opportunity for Youth Assembly alumni who have demonstrated commitment to youth empowerment, social impact and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Selected coordinators will undertake a two-year volunteer leadership role, helping organize and motivate alumni, support youth-led projects, connect changemakers with useful resources, encourage collaboration, monitor project progress and increase the global visibility of alumni initiatives.

In return, coordinators can gain significant leadership and professional-development experience, receive training support and an AFS Global Competence Certificate, strengthen their international networks, gain recognition for their contributions and receive a full scholarship to attend the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva.

However, prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the principal eligibility condition: only previous Youth Assembly participants are eligible to become Impact Coordinators.

Since no closing date is currently stated in the official announcement, eligible alumni interested in the opportunity should review the official application information and apply promptly.

TITLE: Mercor Research Fellowship 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 26, 2026

Applications are open for the Mercor Research Fellowship 2026. The Mercor Research Fellowship funds people to build the next generation of benchmarks, evaluation techniques, and economic analyses of AI. You can pitch a benchmark or eval methodology you want to build — a new domain, a harder task format, a better way to measure agentic reliability — and if selected, you get the time, compute, expert labor, and mentorship to design, implement, and release it end to end. Or, on the economics side, you can pitch a study using Mercor’s proprietary data to better understand an aspect of AI’s impact on the economy and firms.

You’ll work directly with the APEX research team, get access to real enterprise evaluation problems from Mercor’s Fortune 500 and frontier-lab partners, and see your work shape how the industry measures AI capability.

Focus Areas

Long-horizon, multi-app agentic tasks in professional services (law, finance, consulting) — extending APEX-Agents

Real-world software engineering evaluation beyond issue resolution — extending APEX-SWE

Professional accounting and finance workflows — extending APEX-Accounting

AI-for-Science evals: research-level mathematics, biology, materials science, and theoretical physics

New economic benchmarks — negotiation, management, and other capabilities that carry economic value but resist standard task formats

Novel evaluation methodology: contamination resistance, rubric design, human-vs-model grading agreement, cost-adjusted scoring

The economics of human data platforms like Mercor – pricing, matching, elasticity of supply and demand.

AI Theory of the Firm: what an AI-native firm looks like from the inside, and how work is actually organized within one, with a focus on empirical work.

Strong pitches outside this list are welcome — we fund the best ideas, not the closest fit to a template.

Benefits

3-month stipend of $40,000 or 6-month stipend of $80,000

Unlimited API credits, plus a dedicated budget for GPU compute and paid expert/human-data time

Weekly 1:1 mentorship with a member of the APEX research team, plus regular access to the broader research org

Access to Mercor’s marketplace and expert-network data for empirical work, subject to review

Access to frontier model APIs, Mercor’s internal evaluation infrastructure, and — where appropriate — real enterprise evaluation problems from Mercor’s customers

Optional desk in Mercor’s San Francisco office for fellows who want to be in person

Introductions to Mercor’s network of researchers across frontier labs and academia

Standout fellows are considered for a full-time offer on the APEX research team at the end of the fellowship

Eligibility

They seek genuine interest in evaluation as a research discipline — not just a stepping stone to a model-building role.

Background in economics, CS, ML, statistics, or an adjacent field (measurement, psychometrics, HCI, social science)

A specific, well-scoped idea for a benchmark, eval technique, or empirical study you want to build — the fellowship is built around your pitch.

Comfortable in a startup environment: fast iteration, direct access to real customer problems, less hand-holding than an academic lab.

Able to commit at least 30 hours/week for the duration of the fellowship — during a leave, over a summer, or a flexible stretch of a PhD.

Bonus: experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, or domain expertise in law, finance, medicine, or a scientific field.

Application

The application deadline is September 26, 2026 at 7:00 AM GMT+1.

Click here to apply

For more information, visit Mercor Research Fellowship.

TITLE: SEAOHUN 2026 ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship: Fully Supported Fellowship for Early- to Mid-Career Professionals in Southeast Asia

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The SEAOHUN 2026 ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship Programme offers an opportunity for early- to mid-career professionals working across human health, animal health, environmental health, climate change, and related One Health disciplines to gain practical experience with leading organizations and institutions across Southeast Asia.

Organized by the Southeast Asia One Health University Network (SEAOHUN), the fellowship is designed to strengthen the regional workforce’s capacity to understand and address climate-related health threats while promoting cross-sectoral collaboration, professional development, knowledge exchange, and evidence-based policy.

The programme is particularly relevant for professionals who want to build expertise at the intersection of One Health and climate change and gain hands-on experience through a fellowship placement with a host organization.

Opportunity category: Fellowship

Application deadline: 20 September 2026

Fellowship period: Approximately four months, from November 2026 to February 2027

Location: Southeast Asia, at the assigned host organization

What Is the SEAOHUN 2026 Fellowship Programme?

The SEAOHUN Fellowship Programme supports early- to mid-career professionals from SEAOHUN member countries by placing them with leading organizations and institutions where they can gain practical experience addressing One Health challenges.

The 2026 programme has a particular focus on climate-related health challenges through the ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship.

The fellowship recognizes that human health, animal health, environmental health, and climate change are interconnected. Climate change can affect disease transmission, ecosystems, food systems, biodiversity, water security, agriculture, and community health.

Consequently, addressing emerging health threats increasingly requires professionals from different disciplines and countries to work together.

The programme seeks to develop this capacity by connecting fellows with organizations across sectors, including:

Academic institutions

Research organizations

Government agencies

International organizations

Non-governmental organizations

Private-sector organizations

Other institutions working on One Health and climate-related issues

Through these placements, fellows can develop practical skills while working alongside national and international experts.

Main Objectives of the ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship

The fellowship is designed around several interconnected objectives.

1. Strengthen the One Health Workforce

The programme seeks to develop a stronger workforce capable of responding to complex health challenges involving humans, animals, and the environment.

2. Address Climate-Related Health Threats

Climate change is creating and intensifying a range of health challenges. The fellowship provides professionals with opportunities to develop practical knowledge and skills relevant to climate-health issues.

3. Promote Cross-Sectoral Collaboration

One Health problems cannot always be addressed by a single profession or institution. The fellowship encourages collaboration across human health, veterinary medicine, environmental science, public health, biological sciences, climate science, and related fields.

4. Strengthen Cross-Country Cooperation

The programme brings together professionals from different ASEAN countries and creates opportunities for regional knowledge exchange.

5. Generate Actionable Knowledge

Fellows are expected to contribute to knowledge and outputs that can help inform climate-health policies and practices at both national and ASEAN levels.

6. Develop Professional Networks

Working with established institutions and experts can help fellows develop professional relationships that continue beyond the fellowship period.

Who Can Apply for the SEAOHUN 2026 Fellowship?

The programme is intended for early- to mid-career professionals with experience in One Health-related disciplines.

Applicants should have an academic and/or professional background relevant to One Health and climate-related issues.

Potentially relevant fields include:

Environmental health

Biological sciences

Epidemiology

Human health

Public health

Veterinary medicine

Climate change

Environmental science

One Health

Other related disciplines

Applicants should carefully review the specific Terms of Reference for their intended fellowship placement because individual host organizations may have additional requirements.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be:

40 years old or younger at the time of the application deadline.

Therefore, candidates should make sure they meet the age requirement as of 20 September 2026.

Citizenship Requirement

The fellowship is specifically intended for citizens of SEAOHUN member countries.

Eligible countries listed by SEAOHUN are:

Cambodia

Indonesia

Lao PDR

Malaysia

Philippines

Thailand

Vietnam

Applicants from countries outside this SEAOHUN member-country list are not eligible under the stated criteria.

This means the opportunity is geographically focused on Southeast Asia and the ASEAN region, rather than being a global fellowship open to applicants from every country.

Race or Ethnicity Requirements

The information provided by SEAOHUN does not specify any race or ethnicity-based eligibility requirement.

Eligibility is instead determined primarily by factors such as:

Citizenship

Age

Professional experience

Academic or professional background

One Health-related expertise

English proficiency

Communication skills

Availability for the fellowship

Suitability for the selected placement

Therefore, there is no stated requirement that applicants belong to a particular racial or ethnic group.

Professional Backgrounds That May Be Relevant

The fellowship is particularly suited to professionals whose work connects with One Health, climate change, health systems, environmental issues, or related areas.

Relevant backgrounds may include:

Human and Public Health

Professionals working in:

Public health

Epidemiology

Human health

Disease surveillance

Health policy

Global health

Environmental health

may find the programme relevant.

Veterinary and Animal Health

Professionals working in:

Veterinary medicine

Animal health

Veterinary public health

Zoonotic diseases

Animal disease surveillance

Wildlife health

may also be strong candidates.

Environmental and Climate Sciences

Applicants with backgrounds in:

Environmental science

Climate change

Environmental health

Ecology

Biodiversity

Conservation

Biological sciences

may also be eligible where their experience aligns with the relevant fellowship placement.

The precise requirements may differ according to the host organization’s Terms of Reference.

English Language Requirement

Applicants must demonstrate professional proficiency in both oral and written English.

Strong English communication skills are required because fellows will work in professional environments and interact with national and international experts.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable with:

Professional written communication

Meetings and discussions

Presentations

Collaboration with colleagues

Reading professional and technical materials

Communicating ideas clearly in English

Communication Skills

Strong communication skills are explicitly required.

This is important because the fellowship is not simply an academic programme. Fellows will be placed within professional organizations and expected to engage with colleagues, experts, researchers, practitioners, and other stakeholders.

Applicants should therefore be able to communicate effectively in professional settings.

Full-Time and On-Site Requirement

One of the most important conditions is that selected fellows must be available to work:

Full-time and on-site with the host organization for the entire fellowship.

The fellowship is expected to last approximately four months, from November 2026 to February 2027.

This means applicants should consider their existing employment, academic commitments, personal responsibilities, and travel arrangements before applying.

The opportunity is not presented as a remote or part-time fellowship.

Fellowship Placement Locations

The fellowship placements take place with host organizations in Southeast Asia.

What Can Fellows Gain From the Programme?

The SEAOHUN Fellowship is primarily designed as a practical professional-development experience.

Fellows can gain exposure to real-world One Health challenges and work alongside experienced professionals.

Practical Experience

Exposure to Experts

Cross-Cultural Experience

Regional Networking

Cross-Disciplinary Learning

Professional Growth

Frequently Asked Questions About the SEAOHUN 2026 Fellowship

Is the SEAOHUN Fellowship open worldwide?

No. The stated eligibility criteria require applicants to be citizens of a SEAOHUN member country.

The eligible countries are Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam.

Can applicants from Africa, Europe, the Americas, or other parts of Asia apply?

Based on the stated citizenship requirement, applicants who are citizens of countries outside the seven listed SEAOHUN member countries are not eligible.

The fellowship is specifically designed for professionals from SEAOHUN member countries in Southeast Asia.

Is there a specific race or ethnic group that can apply?

No race or ethnicity requirement is stated. Eligibility is based on citizenship, professional background, age, skills, and the other programme requirements.

Can students apply?

The information provided describes the target applicants as early- to mid-career professionals with experience in One Health-related disciplines. It does not state a general student eligibility category. Prospective applicants who are currently students should therefore check the specific Terms of Reference before applying.

What is the maximum age?

Applicants must be 40 years old or younger at the application deadline.

Do applicants need One Health experience?

Yes. The eligibility criteria specify that applicants should be professionals with experience in One Health-related disciplines.

Can someone from a non-medical background apply?

Potentially, yes. The fellowship is multidisciplinary. Relevant backgrounds can include environmental science, biological sciences, climate change, veterinary medicine, epidemiology, public health, human health, and other related disciplines.

The specific requirements depend on the fellowship placement.

Does the fellowship require full-time participation?

Yes. Applicants must be available to work full-time and on-site with the host organization throughout the fellowship.

How long is the fellowship?

Approximately four months, with placements scheduled from November 2026 to February 2027.

Do applicants need English proficiency?

Yes. Applicants must demonstrate professional proficiency in both written and spoken English.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although meeting the eligibility criteria is essential, applicants should also make sure their application clearly demonstrates why they are a strong fit for the programme.

1. Clearly Connect Your Experience to One Health

Do not simply list your academic qualifications.

Explain how your professional experience relates to interconnected human, animal, environmental, or climate-health challenges.

2. Highlight Climate-Related Experience

Because the 2026 fellowship has a strong climate-health focus, applicants should emphasize relevant experience involving:

Climate change

Environmental health

Disease patterns

Ecosystem health

Biodiversity

Public health

Veterinary health

Climate-related health risks

where applicable.

3. Demonstrate Cross-Sectoral Thinking

One Health requires professionals to look beyond their individual discipline.

Applicants should demonstrate an ability or willingness to collaborate with professionals from different sectors.

4. Emphasize Practical Experience

The programme is intended to provide practical professional exposure.

Candidates should therefore clearly describe relevant projects, research, fieldwork, professional assignments, policy work, or other practical experience.

5. Demonstrate Strong Communication

Because professional communication is an explicit requirement, applicants should ensure that their application is clear, organized, and professionally written.

6. Check the Host Organization’s Requirements

The general eligibility criteria do not necessarily capture every requirement for every fellowship placement.

Applicants should read the relevant Terms of Reference carefully before selecting or applying for a placement.

Why This Fellowship Is Valuable for One Health Professionals

The challenges associated with climate change increasingly cross the boundaries between human health, animal health, environmental systems, and society.

For example, changes in ecosystems and climate can affect:

Disease transmission

Wildlife populations

Agriculture

Food security

Water systems

Human health

Animal health

Biodiversity

Public health preparedness

Professionals capable of working across these interconnected areas are therefore increasingly important.

The SEAOHUN 2026 ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship provides an opportunity for professionals in Southeast Asia to develop this kind of interdisciplinary capacity through direct exposure to established organizations and experts.

Evidence of the Fellowship’s Potential Career Impact

Previous SEAOHUN fellowship experiences demonstrate that the programme can contribute to professional development beyond the placement itself.

For example, a previous fellow, Dr. Khao Keonam, a lecturer from the National University of Laos, reported involvement in activities including:

Reviewing regulations concerning pangolin scale-related cases in Lao PDR and Thailand

Supporting legal review and a policy brief concerning zoonotic disease surveillance systems

Reviewing wildlife and One Health-related university courses in Lao PDR and Vietnam

Completing monitoring and evaluation training

Developing project-management skills to share with students

Following the fellowship, Dr. Khao was selected for the Wildlife Conservation Society’s Pandemic Prevention Leadership Initiative roster of regional leaders addressing threats to global health security and biodiversity associated with unregulated wildlife trade.

He subsequently obtained a PhD in Veterinary Medicine from Khon Kaen University in Thailand.

This example illustrates how a fellowship placement can potentially contribute to professional networks, practical expertise, leadership development, and future opportunities.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The SEAOHUN 2026 Fellowship may be particularly suitable for professionals who:

Are citizens of Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, or Vietnam

Are 40 years old or younger by the application deadline

Are early- to mid-career professionals

Can communicate professionally in English

The SEAOHUN 2026 ASEAN One Health Climate Fellowship is a regional professional-development opportunity for early- to mid-career professionals seeking practical experience in One Health and climate-related health challenges.

The programme brings together professionals from Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam and connects successful fellows with organizations working across human health, animal health, environmental health, climate change, research, policy, conservation, agriculture, and related areas.

Applicants must be 40 years old or younger, have experience in a One Health-related discipline, demonstrate strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English, and be able to work full-time and on-site for approximately four months from November 2026 to February 2027.

TITLE: Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship 2027: Full-Cost Funding for South African Women to Pursue Master’s or PhD Studies Abroad

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship 2027 is offering an exceptional opportunity for eligible South African women seeking to pursue postgraduate studies at an international university. The scholarship is designed to support high-achieving postgraduate scholars who wish to undertake a Master’s or PhD programme abroad, providing full-cost funding for successful candidates.

According to the current Rhodes University postgraduate funding notice, applications for the 2027 scholarship are open from 24 August 2026 until 24 September 2026. Applicants are required to submit their application documents as a single PDF document to the designated Rhodes University contact.

The scholarship is administered through Rhodes University, which provides information on overseas study funding and postgraduate opportunities.

About the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship

The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship is a prestigious international postgraduate scholarship associated with Rhodes University and the Patrick and Margaret Flanagan Trust. Its purpose is to enable outstanding South African women graduates to pursue advanced postgraduate qualifications at universities outside South Africa.

The scholarship has a long history of supporting South African women to undertake postgraduate studies at leading international universities. Rhodes University has described it as a prestigious international scholarship intended to enable South African women graduates to obtain postgraduate qualifications overseas.

The scholarship has supported scholars across a wide range of academic disciplines. Historical records of recipients show that beneficiaries have undertaken Master’s and doctoral-level studies at international institutions, including universities in the United Kingdom and the United States.

Importantly, the scholarship is not limited to one specific academic discipline. Historical information about the award indicates that it has supported postgraduate study across different fields of academic and professional endeavour.

What Does the 2027 Scholarship Offer?

The 2027 announcement describes the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship as providing full-cost funding for international Master’s and doctoral studies.

This makes the opportunity particularly valuable for applicants who have strong academic ambitions but may face financial barriers to pursuing postgraduate education at an overseas university.

Successful scholars can use the award to pursue full-time postgraduate studies at an international institution, subject to the terms and conditions of the scholarship.

Rather than simply providing a contribution toward tuition, the scholarship is presented as a full-cost funding opportunity. Applicants should, however, carefully review the official scholarship documentation and any award conditions before making financial or academic commitments.

Level of Study Supported

The scholarship is specifically intended for postgraduate-level study.

Eligible study levels include:

Master’s degree programmes

Doctoral or PhD programmes

Full-time postgraduate study at an international university

Applicants should therefore have a clear postgraduate academic plan and demonstrate why studying internationally is important to their academic, research, and professional development.

The scholarship’s historical record confirms that recipients have undertaken both Master’s and doctoral studies at overseas universities.

International Study Opportunity

One of the most attractive features of the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship is the opportunity to undertake postgraduate studies outside South Africa.

The scholarship allows successful applicants to identify an international university that is appropriate for their intended course of study and research.

In the application, candidates are specifically asked to explain:

Why they want to study at an international university.

What they intend to do after completing their Master’s or PhD.

Their intended research focus.

Which university they intend to attend.

Why they have selected that particular university.

This means applicants are expected to demonstrate that their proposed institution is not simply prestigious but also appropriate for their academic interests, research objectives, and long-term career plans.

Past scholarship recipients have studied at internationally recognised institutions. Rhodes University records, for example, document recipients undertaking postgraduate study at institutions including Oxford and Cambridge.

Who Can Apply for the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship?

The current opportunity is intended for South African women pursuing postgraduate study overseas.

Rhodes University’s published information about previous recipients states that the scholarship aims to enable South African women graduates to attain postgraduate qualifications overseas.

Historical Rhodes University information also describes the scholarship as having been established specifically to support South African women scholars and notes that it was intended to give them opportunities to pursue postgraduate studies at leading international universities.

Eligibility at a Glance

Potential applicants should therefore be understood as:

Women applicants

South African citizens or women of South African descent, subject to the applicable scholarship terms

Applicants seeking postgraduate Master’s or PhD study

Candidates intending to study full-time at an international university

Strong academic performers with a compelling postgraduate or research plan

Applicants capable of demonstrating how their proposed international studies will contribute to their future academic, professional, or societal contribution

The available official material does not establish a separate racial quota or racial restriction. The key eligibility distinction identified in the scholarship’s published history is its focus on South African women. Earlier Rhodes University material describes the award as benefiting South African women scholars without restriction as to creed or colour.

Applicants should nevertheless consult the latest official application documentation because eligibility conditions can be updated.

Academic Background and Excellence

The scholarship is highly competitive and is aimed at academically strong candidates.

Previous Rhodes University information has described the award as being open to high-calibre applicants, with historical recipients demonstrating strong academic records. A Rhodes University report on a previous winner, for example, described the scholarship as being open to English-speaking South African postgraduate women with a first-class academic record.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic CV clearly communicates the following:

Previous university qualifications

Academic achievements

Research experience

Relevant academic awards

Publications, where applicable

Conference participation, where applicable

Research projects

Professional or academic leadership

Relevant work experience

Any other achievements demonstrating academic excellence and potential

Required Application Documents

For the 2027 application, Rhodes University requires applicants to submit a number of important documents.

All required materials should be combined into one single PDF document before submission.

The required application package includes the following.

1. Letter of Motivation

The motivation letter is one of the most important components of the application.

According to the official Rhodes University announcement, the motivation should address four central issues:

Why do you plan to study at an international university?

Applicants should explain why studying abroad is important to their academic and professional objectives.

Rather than simply stating that an overseas university is prestigious, applicants should explain the specific academic, research, institutional, or professional advantages that international study would provide.

For example, an applicant might discuss access to the following:

Specialised research facilities

Leading scholars in a particular field

Unique archives or datasets

Advanced laboratories

Specialised academic programmes

International research networks

Research methodologies unavailable or less accessible locally

Global professional networks

Collaborative opportunities

The strongest responses will connect the international study experience directly to the applicant’s research and long-term objectives.

2. Plans After Completing the Master’s or PhD

Applicants must explain what they intend to do after completing their postgraduate studies.

This section should demonstrate that the applicant has a clear vision for how the qualification will be used.

Potential areas to discuss include:

Returning to South Africa

Academic research

University teaching

Public service

Policy development

Professional practice

Entrepreneurship

Research and innovation

Community development

Institutional leadership

Knowledge transfer

Contribution to national development

Previous scholarship recipients have emphasised their intention to return to South Africa and apply the knowledge and skills gained abroad for the benefit of their country.

3. Intended Research Focus

Applicants should clearly explain what they intend to research.

A strong research focus should demonstrate:

A clearly defined topic

A significant research problem

Academic relevance

Potential societal or professional impact

Alignment with the proposed postgraduate programme

A realistic research direction

Why the selected international institution is particularly suitable

Applicants pursuing a PhD should pay particular attention to demonstrating the originality, relevance and potential contribution of their proposed research.

4. Proposed International University

Candidates must identify the university where they wish to study and explain why they have selected it.

The explanation should go beyond university rankings.

Applicants could consider discussing:

The university’s expertise in their field

Relevant professors or research groups

Research centres

Academic resources

Laboratories or specialised facilities

Institutional partnerships

Programme structure

Research environment

Availability of supervisors

International research networks

The institution’s relevance to the applicant’s career objectives

The goal is to demonstrate that there is a strong academic match between the applicant, the proposed programme and the university.

Detailed Academic CV

Applicants must provide a detailed academic CV.

The CV must also include the email contact details of three academic referees.

Importantly, one of the three academic referees must be a Head of Department or Dean.

Applicants should therefore select referees who are sufficiently familiar with their academic performance, research potential, intellectual abilities, and postgraduate ambitions.

A strong academic CV should clearly present the following:

Educational qualifications

Academic achievements

Research experience

Employment history, where relevant

Publications

Academic presentations

Conferences

Research projects

Scholarships and awards

Leadership activities

Professional memberships

Relevant technical or research skills

Academic referees

The CV should be carefully structured and tailored to demonstrate suitability for an internationally focused postgraduate scholarship.

Full Academic Transcript

Applicants are required to provide a full academic transcript.

The transcript must be certified.

Candidates should ensure that their transcript is complete and clearly shows their academic record.

Because the scholarship is highly competitive, applicants should also ensure that their academic achievements are clearly reflected in their motivation letter and CV rather than relying solely on the transcript to communicate their academic strengths.

Certified Identification Document

Applicants must also provide a certified copy of their ID or passport.

This document forms part of the formal application package and should therefore be prepared in advance.

Applicants should ensure that the copy is clear and properly certified according to the requirements applicable to their application.

How to Submit the Application

The application process requires candidates to combine all required documentation into one single PDF document.

The documents should not be sent as multiple separate attachments if following the published instructions.

The required application materials are:

Letter of motivation

Detailed academic CV

Contact details for three academic referees

Full certified academic transcript

Certified ID or passport copy

The resulting PDF should be saved using the prescribed naming convention:

“Your Surname P&M Flanagan Scholarship Application”

The completed application should then be submitted to the designated Rhodes University contact at tasmin.jones@ru.ac.za.

Applicants should carefully check the official Rhodes University announcement and application documents before submitting their application because scholarship requirements may change.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their documents. Preparing a strong postgraduate scholarship application can take considerable time, particularly when applicants need to obtain certified academic documents and coordinate references.

Why This Scholarship Is Highly Competitive

The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship has a long-standing reputation for supporting high-achieving South African women pursuing postgraduate studies overseas.

Rhodes University has previously described the competition for the award as becoming increasingly difficult as the number and quality of applications increased.

This means that simply meeting the basic eligibility requirements may not be sufficient.

Applicants should aim to demonstrate a combination of:

Excellent academic performance

Strong intellectual potential

A clearly defined research agenda

A convincing reason for studying abroad

A carefully selected international university

Strong academic references

A realistic post-study career plan

Potential to contribute to South Africa

Evidence of leadership, initiative, or impact where applicable

How to Strengthen Your Application

1. Develop a compelling motivation

Your motivation should tell a coherent story.

Explain where you have come from academically, what you want to study, why you need to study it internationally, and what you intend to do with the knowledge afterwards.

Avoid generic statements such as “I have always wanted to study abroad.” Instead, explain precisely why the international institution and programme are important to your academic and research goals.

2. Demonstrate academic excellence

Use your CV and motivation letter to highlight your strongest academic achievements.

Where appropriate, demonstrate:

Outstanding grades

Research achievements

Academic awards

Publications

Conference presentations

Research assistantships

Academic leadership

Independent research experience

3. Explain the research problem clearly

If you are applying for Ph.D. study, your research focus should be particularly well developed.

Clearly communicate the problem you intend to investigate, why it matters, and what contribution your research could make.

4. Carefully justify your university choice

Do not select an institution simply because it is highly ranked.

Explain why the university is particularly suitable for your research.

If there is a relevant professor, research centre, laboratory, archive, programme or research group, explain how it connects to your proposed work.

5. Choose strong academic references

Your referees should be individuals who can provide meaningful evidence of your academic abilities and potential.

Because the application specifically requires three academic referees and one must be a Head of Department or Dean, candidates should contact their proposed referees well before the deadline.

6. Make your long-term contribution clear

Applicants should explain how the scholarship will contribute to their long-term career and how their postgraduate education will ultimately benefit South Africa.

A strong application should show that the candidate sees overseas study as a means of acquiring knowledge and expertise that can later be applied meaningfully.

What Makes the Scholarship Different?

The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship stands out because it combines postgraduate academic support with an opportunity to study internationally.

It is particularly relevant for talented South African women who have reached the stage of pursuing advanced academic qualifications and want to gain exposure to international research and academic environments.

The historical record of the scholarship demonstrates that its beneficiaries have gone on to study at respected international universities and pursue careers across diverse academic and professional fields.

The scholarship has also supported scholars in different disciplines rather than restricting applicants to one specific subject area. Historical Rhodes University information indicates that postgraduate study could be pursued in any field of study.

Important Note for Prospective Applicants

Applicants should distinguish between the general Rhodes University page listing overseas scholarships and the specific eligibility requirements of the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship.

The current Rhodes University page presents the scholarship under its overseas study funding opportunities and provides the 2027 application dates and required documents.

However, the scholarship’s historical and recent Rhodes University materials identify it specifically as an opportunity for South African women.

Prospective applicants should therefore verify all current eligibility conditions in the official application documentation before preparing a submission.

Official Application Information

Applicants should use the official Rhodes University postgraduate funding page for the latest information, application instructions, and supporting documents.

Rhodes University – Overseas Study Funding and Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship 2027

The official Rhodes University page is particularly important because the university warns that scholarship providers may change information about their programmes without notice and advises applicants to check current scholarship information.

Conclusion

The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship 2027 presents a significant opportunity for academically outstanding South African women seeking to pursue full-time Master’s or PhD studies at an international university.

With applications opening on 24 August 2026 and closing on 24 September 2026, prospective candidates have a limited period in which to prepare a competitive application.

The application requires more than academic qualifications. Candidates need to present a convincing case for international study, explain their intended research focus, identify an appropriate university, demonstrate their academic achievements, and provide a clear vision for what they intend to accomplish after completing their postgraduate studies.

Applicants should begin preparing early, particularly because the application requires a detailed academic CV, three academic referees, a certified academic transcript, and a certified identification document. The motivation letter should be carefully developed to demonstrate academic excellence, research potential, institutional fit, and a clear commitment to using the knowledge gained through international study.

For eligible South African women with strong academic records and ambitious postgraduate goals, the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship could provide an important pathway to advanced international education, research exposure, and professional development.

TITLE: Call for Participants- 2nd International Leadership Conference for Women in Higher Education (WoHE, 2019)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Theme: Promoting Women in Science to Address the 21st Century Challenges

March
6-8, 2019

Nairobi, Kenya

The Association of African Universities is calling for participants for its second edition of The International Leadership Conference for Women in Higher Education . This conference is one of the key platforms provided by AAU for the discussion of innovative and creative ways of empowering women, especially young women in higher education to reach their full potential and aspire to the topmost leadership positions in their chosen fields.

Download the full concept note here – http://blogmain.aau.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/Concept-Note_Womens-Conference-in-Kenya.pdf

Background
To date, women continue to have unequal opportunities as their male counterparts. African higher education, for instance, continues to see fewer women occupying leadership positions in the universities, polytechnics and research institutions among others. Indeed, very few women have risen to positions such as Vice-chancellors, Heads of Departments, Deans and Registrars across the continent. This conference seeks to provide the platform to change the narrative. The maiden edition, which was held in Accra, Ghana was highly successful and brought women across national and international boundaries together to share knowledge, ideas and strategic management skills required for success in various leadership positions.

Focus
on Women in STEM

As reflected by the theme, the focus of
the 2019 Conference is on Promoting Women in Science to Address the 21st
Century Challenges.

Africa’s progress is challenged by a myriad of
problems ranging from lack of employment for its youth, the existence of
tropical diseases, weak entrepreneurial drive and low levels of university-industry
linkages, among others. It is widely accepted, that Science and
Technology do have a key role to play in overcoming the continent’s
developmental challenges.

However, studies have revealed that though the number of women in science and engineering is growing, men continue to outnumber women, especially at the upper levels of these professions (AAUW, 2010).

Africa needs to ensure that its human
resource – both men and women, are fully engaged in the STEM fields in solving
its developmental challenges, and thus should make significant investment into
women in STEM to increase their contribution to solving the continent’s
challenges. The promotion of Women in
Science to contribute massively and equally to a developed Africa must therefore
form an integral part of various plans and strategies aimed at achieving the
African Union’s vision of ‘Africa We
Want’ by the year 2063.

AIM

The
Conference seeks to:

-Inspire
and empower the next generation of African women in STEM to actively and effectively
contribute to solving Africa’s Challenges.

–
Provide the platform for women in STEM to share their cutting-edge research as
a way of inspiring others.

–
Build the leadership capacity of women in STEM to drive change and innovation
in the STEM field.

–
Draw attention to the important role of mentorship, through the provision of
the platform for young scientists to interact with accomplished women
scientists.

-Create
the platform for various actors – educators, policy-makers and partners to
debate on pertinent issues related to the promotion of Women in STEM.

CONFERENCE THEME AND SUBTHEMES

The
Conference Theme is: Promoting Women in Science to Address the 21st Century
Challenges. Based on the Conference theme, the AAU is calling for papers under the
following subthemes:

Addressing
Africa’s Challenges: the Role of Women in Science.
Current Developments on Women in Science, Technology,
Engineering and Mathematics in Africa.
Breaking the Glass Ceiling – Policies,
Strategies and Mechanisms to support Women in STEM.
Resource Mobilization Strategies to support
STEM research.
Barriers to Female Participation in STEM
fields.

ACTIVITIES

-Presentation
of Research Papers on the Conference subthemes

–
Panel Discussions on Topical Issues

-Leadership
Training Sessions

-Networking
and Speed Mentoring Sessions

EXPECTED
PARTICIPANTS

-Accomplished
women in various leadership positions in STEM fields from all five regions of
Africa

–
STEM women academics and researchers in African HEIs.

-Women
in industry, government and partner institutions involved in promoting STEM

SPONSORSHIP

Authors
whose papers are accepted for presentation will be funded to make their
presentation at the conference.

EVENT
INFORMATION

Date: March 6-8, 2019

Venue: Nairobi, Kenya

Host:
Centre for Innovative Leadership and Governance

Registration
Link: https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/WoHE19

Abstract Submission: www.aau.org/subs/wohe19/

NB:
Though this is an all-female event, men who are willing to be involved in the
process of developing and empowering women in STEM are also encouraged to get
involved.

Participation Fee

The Conference Registration fee is $ 200 for women participants; $50 for female students; and $300 for other participants. The conference fee covers meals and conference materials.

NAll other expenses – travel, accommodation, subsistence, etc. – are to be borne by participants.

TITLE: JPMorgan Chase 2027 Global Private Bank Investment Solutions Analyst Training Program in London

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
JPMorgan Chase is inviting applications for its 2027 Global Private Bank Investment Solutions Analyst Training Program in London, United Kingdom. This full-time graduate opportunity is designed for talented and highly motivated individuals who are interested in investment management, financial markets, wealth management, client advisory, and developing customized investment solutions.

The program offers successful candidates the opportunity to join JPMorgan Chase’s Global Private Bank, receive structured training, work with experienced investment and product specialists, develop technical and professional skills, and build a long-term career in the financial services industry.

The program is particularly suited to students who are expected to graduate between August 2026 and July 2027 and who can demonstrate strong analytical, communication, organizational, interpersonal, and problem-solving abilities.

Opportunity Overview

Opportunity: Global Private Bank – Investment Solutions Analyst Training Program

Organization: JPMorgan Chase & Co.

Business Unit: Asset & Wealth Management

Job Category: Analysts

Job Type: Full-time

Location: London, United Kingdom

Office Address: 60 Victoria Embankment, London, Greater London, EC4Y 0JP

Job Identification: 210774295

Posting Date: September 1, 2026

Application Deadline: November 1, 2026, at 11:55 p.m.

Expected Graduation Period: August 2026 to July 2027

Application Method: Online application through JPMorgan Chase Careers

Applicants should note that recruitment is conducted on a rolling basis. The employer encourages interested candidates to apply as early as possible because applications may close once the available program positions are filled.

About the JPMorgan Global Private Bank Investment Solutions Program

The Global Private Bank provides wealth management services to individuals, families, entrepreneurs, and institutional clients with complex financial needs. Its services cover areas such as investment management, banking, lending, trust and estate planning, and other wealth-related solutions.

As an Investment Solutions Analyst, the successful candidate will work with specialists to research, analyze, and develop investment strategies and opportunities for clients. The role combines financial research, portfolio-related analysis, product development, market awareness, and relationship-oriented work.

Rather than being limited to classroom learning, the program is designed to expose participants to the practical operations of a global financial institution. Analysts will learn about JPMorgan Chase’s business, clients, investment products, and internal processes while developing the skills needed to contribute to a client-facing investment solutions team.

The Investment Solutions Training Program also serves as an important talent-development pipeline for JPMorgan Chase. Participants who perform well may have opportunities to progress into more advanced roles, including Associate-level positions, and build long-term careers within the firm.

Five-Week Global Training Programme

The program begins with a five-week immersive global training experience. During this period, incoming analysts from different locations will learn more about JPMorgan Chase, its businesses, and its approach to serving clients.

The training is intended to help participants:

Understand the firm’s business operations and organizational culture.

Develop technical knowledge relevant to investment solutions and wealth management.

Strengthen professional and workplace skills.

Learn from senior executives and experienced professionals.

Build relationships with colleagues from different countries and backgrounds.

Expand their professional networks across the organization.

Gain a better understanding of client needs and financial markets.

Following the initial training, analysts will continue to receive formal and informal learning opportunities throughout the program. These may include mentorship, learning sessions, networking activities, business initiatives, and professional development events.

Key Responsibilities

Successful candidates will work with investment specialists, client advisors, bankers, and other professionals to help develop solutions that respond to client needs. The main responsibilities may include the following:

1. Research Financial Markets and Investment Opportunities

Analysts will examine market activities, economic developments, investment trends, and other information relevant to client portfolios and investment strategies.

This may require following macroeconomic developments, understanding market movements, reviewing investment research, and identifying opportunities or risks that could influence financial decisions.

2. Support Investment Strategy Development

Participants will work with specialists to research and develop global investment strategies and opportunities. They may contribute to the analysis of different asset classes, investment approaches, and portfolio objectives.

The goal is to help create solutions that are aligned with clients’ financial goals, risk considerations, and long-term wealth-management needs.

3. Collaborate with Client Advisors and Specialists

Investment Solutions Analysts will collaborate with a range of professionals, including:

Client advisors

Bankers

Global investment specialists

Market strategy teams

Equity investment teams

Alternative investment teams

Estate planning experts

Lending specialists

Other wealth management professionals

This cross-functional collaboration is essential because private banking clients often require solutions that combine investments, banking, lending, tax considerations, estate planning, and other financial services.

4. Assist with Product Development

Analysts may contribute to the research, analysis, and development of investment products and solutions. This could involve reviewing market opportunities, assessing client needs, supporting product-related projects, and helping teams respond to changes in the investment environment.

5. Support Portfolio Construction and Financial Analysis

The position may involve activities connected to building investment portfolios, conducting research, analyzing financial information, and supporting the development of investment recommendations.

Candidates should therefore be comfortable working with information, interpreting data, examining financial trends, and communicating findings clearly.

6. Gain Exposure to Wealth Management

The program provides exposure to several areas of wealth management, including:

Investment management

Lending

Banking

Trust and estate planning

Portfolio construction

Financial strategy

Client relationship management

Investment research

Product and solution development

This broad exposure can help participants understand how different financial services work together to meet clients’ needs.

7. Develop Client-Facing and Relationship-Building Skills

Although the role has a strong analytical component, JPMorgan Chase is also looking for candidates who are interested in eventually working with external clients in a relationship-building and sales capacity.

Analysts will be expected to develop the ability to understand client needs, communicate financial concepts, collaborate with internal teams, and contribute to customized wealth-management solutions.

Training, Mentorship, and Career Development

One of the major advantages of the JPMorgan Chase Investment Solutions Analyst Training Program is its focus on continuous development.

Participants can expect opportunities to:

Receive structured technical and professional training.

Learn from senior executives and experienced professionals.

Participate in formal learning sessions.

Receive one-on-one mentorship.

Build relationships with colleagues across the firm.

Join professional networking and engagement activities.

Participate in program initiatives.

Explore future career opportunities within JPMorgan Chase.

The firm describes the program as a major source of homegrown talent and a development pipeline for future subject-matter experts. After completing the program, many full-time analysts may progress into Associate positions, depending on performance, business needs, and available opportunities.

While career progression is not automatically guaranteed, the program is designed to provide a strong foundation for individuals seeking long-term careers in private banking, investment solutions, wealth management, and financial services.
