Up to 30 women will be selected as 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellows, with each recipient receiving a US$12,000 fellowship to support their advanced doctoral studies.

Established in 1938 in honor of renowned aviator and Zontian Amelia Earhart, the fellowship has a long history of supporting women who are breaking barriers in aerospace-related disciplines and developing the knowledge and technologies that shape the future of aviation, space exploration and science.

The 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship application deadline is 15 November 2026.

About the Amelia Earhart Fellowship

Women have made important contributions to aerospace engineering, aviation, astronomy, space exploration and other scientific fields. However, they remain significantly underrepresented in many areas of aerospace engineering and space sciences.

The Amelia Earhart Fellowship was created to help address this imbalance by providing talented women with financial resources to continue advanced research and doctoral studies.

For almost 90 years, Zonta International has supported women who are pursuing ambitious academic and professional goals. The fellowship specifically recognizes women whose doctoral research is applied to aerospace engineering or space sciences.

The fellowship reflects Amelia Earhart’s pioneering spirit and Zonta International’s commitment to helping women gain access to the resources and opportunities necessary to become leaders and decision-makers in highly competitive fields.

For the 2027 fellowship cycle:

Up to 30 Fellows will be selected.

Each Fellow will receive US$12,000.

The fellowship can support doctoral studies at an accredited university or college offering postgraduate courses and degrees in the relevant fields.

Applicants can be studying at eligible institutions in different countries around the world.

The program is designed specifically for women pursuing doctoral-level research connected to aerospace engineering or space sciences.

What Makes the Amelia Earhart Fellowship Prestigious?

The Amelia Earhart Fellowship has an extensive history of supporting women in aerospace and space-related disciplines.

Since the program began, Zonta International has awarded:

1,824 Amelia Earhart Fellowships

More than US$12.5 million in fellowship funding

Support to 1,395 women

Recipients from 81 countries

Past Amelia Earhart Fellows have gone on to build influential careers in a wide range of fields.

Alumnae have become:

Astronauts

Aerospace engineers

Astronomers

Professors

Geologists

Entrepreneurs

Corporate leaders

Senior public officials

One former Fellow even went on to become the U.S. Secretary of the Air Force.

These achievements demonstrate the potential impact of investing in women conducting advanced research in aerospace engineering and space sciences.

2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship Funding

Each selected Fellow will receive US$12,000.

The award is intended to provide financial support for eligible doctoral studies and research in aerospace engineering and space sciences.

The fellowships are made possible through generous contributions to the Zonta Foundation for Women Amelia Earhart Fellowship Fund.

The funding can therefore provide valuable financial assistance to doctoral researchers who are already undertaking advanced academic work and need additional resources to continue developing their research.

Eligibility Requirements

The Amelia Earhart Fellowship has specific academic and enrollment requirements.

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

1. Applicants must be women

The fellowship is specifically designed to support women pursuing advanced studies and research in aerospace engineering and space sciences.

2. Applicants may be of any nationality

The fellowship is open to women of any nationality who satisfy the academic and program requirements.

This means the opportunity is not restricted to applicants from a particular country or continent.

3. Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. or doctoral degree

Applicants must be actively pursuing a Ph.D. or other doctoral degree.

The doctoral program must involve research applied to aerospace engineering or space sciences.

4. Applicants must demonstrate a superior academic record

Candidates are expected to demonstrate strong academic performance and evidence of excellence in their field.

A competitive applicant should therefore be able to demonstrate a strong academic background alongside significant potential in aerospace engineering or space sciences.

5. Applicants must be conducting aerospace- or space-science-related research

The applicant’s research must be applied to:

Aerospace engineering; or

Space sciences.

Applicants whose doctoral research falls outside these areas would not meet the central academic focus of the fellowship.

6. Applicants must be registered in a full-time doctoral program

Applicants must be registered in a full-time Ph.D. or doctoral program.

Part-time doctoral study does not satisfy this requirement.

7. Applicants must have completed at least one year of their doctoral program

At the time of submitting the application, applicants must have either:

Completed at least one year of their Ph.D./doctoral program; or

Received a master’s degree in an aerospace-applied field.

This requirement is important because the fellowship is intended for researchers who have already progressed beyond the very beginning of their advanced academic journey.

8. Applicants must not graduate before April 2028

Applicants must remain enrolled in their doctoral program long enough to meet the fellowship’s timing requirements.

Specifically, applicants must not graduate from their Ph.D. or doctoral program before April 2028.

Candidates whose doctoral studies are scheduled to end before this date are therefore not eligible for the 2027 fellowship.

Who Is Not Eligible?

Certain individuals are specifically excluded from applying.

The following people are not eligible:

Zonta club members

Individuals with direct membership with Zonta International

Employees of Zonta International

Employees of the Zonta Foundation for Women

Applicants participating in post-doctoral research programs

Previous Amelia Earhart Fellows applying to renew the fellowship for a second year

Applicants should carefully review their status before beginning the application process.

Previous Amelia Earhart Fellows

Previous recipients of the Amelia Earhart Fellowship cannot apply to renew the fellowship for a second year.

However, Zonta notes that recipients of another Zonta fellowship or award who received a complimentary one-year supporting membership from Zonta International may still be eligible to apply during that complimentary membership year, provided they are not applying for the same fellowship or scholarship they previously received from Zonta International.

The Sharon Langenbeck Amelia Earhart Fellow

A special distinction has been introduced within the Amelia Earhart Fellowship program.

In 2025, Sharon Langenbeck, Ph.D., a Past International President and a two-time Amelia Earhart Fellow from 1977 and 1978, made an extraordinary contribution to the Amelia Earhart Endowment Fund.

In recognition of her generosity and lasting contribution to the fellowship program, one of the 30 Amelia Earhart Fellows selected each year will be designated the Sharon Langenbeck Amelia Earhart Fellow.

The Fellow will be selected by the Zonta International Amelia Earhart Committee according to pre-established criteria.

Sharon Langenbeck continues to support the legacy of Amelia Earhart and the women following in her footsteps.

From 2026 to 2028, she is also serving as the Amelia Earhart Fellowship 90th Anniversary Ambassador.

This role forms part of Zonta International’s preparations to celebrate the fellowship’s 90th anniversary during the 2026–2028 Biennium.

How the Application Is Evaluated

Applications are reviewed by the Zonta International Amelia Earhart Fellowship Committee.

The committee reviews submitted applications and recommends selected recipients to the Zonta International Board.

Applicants are evaluated according to the criteria established in the fellowship requirements and application.

The evaluation process is confidential.

Zonta International states that:

Application evaluations are kept confidential.

Evaluations are not disclosed to applicants.

Applicants will be notified of their application status by the end of April.

Because the fellowship is highly competitive, prospective applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates their academic excellence, doctoral progress and relevance of their research to aerospace engineering or space sciences.

Application Deadline

The deadline for the 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship is:

15 November 2026

The complete application must be submitted by this date to be considered.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Preparing an application for a highly competitive doctoral fellowship may require sufficient time to gather academic information and prepare the required supporting materials.

Where Can Applicants Come From?

The Amelia Earhart Fellowship is open to women of any nationality.

The program’s history demonstrates its international reach, with previous Fellows coming from 81 countries.

Therefore, eligible applicants can come from different countries and continents, including applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions, provided they satisfy all of the fellowship’s academic, doctoral-program and research requirements.

For example, an eligible woman pursuing a qualifying Ph.D. in Ghana or another African country can potentially apply, provided that she meets all of the stated requirements.

Nationality alone does not determine eligibility; the applicant’s doctoral program, research area, academic record and stage of study are particularly important.

Who Should Apply?

The fellowship is particularly relevant to women who are already undertaking advanced doctoral research in areas such as:

Aerospace engineering

Space sciences

Aviation-related engineering research

Astronomical research

Space exploration technologies

Aerospace systems

Other doctoral research directly applied to aerospace engineering or space sciences

Applicants should carefully determine whether their specific research topic falls within the fellowship’s scope before submitting an application.

Why This Fellowship Matters

The Amelia Earhart Fellowship offers more than financial assistance.

For doctoral researchers, receiving a prestigious international fellowship can provide recognition of their academic achievements and research potential.

The opportunity can help women:

Receive financial support

The US$12,000 fellowship can help support advanced doctoral studies and research.

Gain international recognition

Becoming an Amelia Earhart Fellow places a researcher within a distinguished international network of women working in aerospace and space sciences.

Strengthen their academic profile

A competitive international fellowship can become a valuable addition to an academic CV and professional profile.

Join a distinguished fellowship legacy

Fellows become part of a program that has supported women for almost nine decades.

Connect with an international community

The program’s history includes Fellows from 81 countries, creating a broad international legacy.

Advance research in cutting-edge fields

Successful applicants are contributing to scientific and technological developments in aerospace engineering and space sciences.

Develop future leadership opportunities

Former Fellows have progressed into influential careers as scientists, engineers, academics, entrepreneurs, corporate leaders and public officials.

2026 Amelia Earhart Fellows

The 2026 cohort demonstrates the international nature of the fellowship.

The 2026 Amelia Earhart Fellows include women from countries and territories such as:

India

United States

Canada

Democratic Republic of Congo

Italy

Ireland

United Kingdom

South Korea

Thailand

Hong Kong and China

China

The 2026 cohort includes 30 Fellows, one of whom was designated the 2026 Sharon Langenbeck Amelia Earhart Fellow.

This international representation highlights the fellowship’s commitment to supporting talented women regardless of nationality.

Program Documents and Additional Information

Zonta International provides several documents relating to the Amelia Earhart Fellowship.

Prospective applicants can consult the available program materials for additional information, including:

2026 Amelia Earhart Fellows

2026 Amelia Earhart Fellows’ biographies

Amelia Earhart Fellowship Map

Amelia Earhart Fellowship School List

Amelia Earhart Fellowship Statistics and Program Overview

Amelia Earhart Fellowship Description

These materials can help prospective applicants understand the fellowship’s history, previous recipients, participating institutions and overall program structure.

Important Things Applicants Should Remember

Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully check that they satisfy the major requirements.

In particular, applicants should confirm that:

They are women.

They are of any nationality and meet the program requirements.

They are pursuing a Ph.D. or doctoral degree.

Their research is applied to aerospace engineering or space sciences.

They are enrolled in a full-time doctoral program.

They have completed at least one year of the doctoral program, or have a master’s degree in an aerospace-applied field.

They will not graduate from their doctoral program before April 2028.

They are not applying for a second year as a previous Amelia Earhart Fellow.

They are not excluded because of Zonta membership or employment.

They submit the complete application by the deadline.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Amelia Earhart Fellowship?

The Amelia Earhart Fellowship is an international fellowship program established by Zonta International to support women pursuing Ph.D. and doctoral research in aerospace engineering and space sciences.

How much funding does the fellowship provide?

Each selected Fellow receives US$12,000.

How many Fellows are selected?

Up to 30 Fellows are selected each year.

Is the fellowship open to international applicants?

Yes. Women of any nationality can apply if they satisfy the fellowship’s eligibility requirements.

Can a master’s student apply?

The fellowship is primarily for women pursuing a Ph.D. or doctoral degree. Applicants must either have completed at least one year of their doctoral program or have received a master’s degree in an aerospace-applied field at the time of application.

Can someone in a postdoctoral program apply?

No. Post-doctoral research programs are not eligible for the fellowship.

Can previous Amelia Earhart Fellows apply again?

Previous Amelia Earhart Fellows are not eligible to apply for a second year of the same fellowship.

When is the application deadline?

The deadline for the 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship is 15 November 2026.

When will applicants be notified?

Zonta International states that applicants will be notified of their status by the end of April.

What fields of study are eligible?

The fellowship focuses on doctoral research applied to aerospace engineering and space sciences.

Conclusion

The 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship represents a significant opportunity for women pursuing advanced doctoral research in aerospace engineering and space sciences. With up to 30 awards of US$12,000 each, the program provides meaningful financial support while connecting successful applicants to an internationally recognized legacy of women advancing aerospace, science and technology.

The fellowship is particularly attractive to women who have already progressed in their doctoral studies, demonstrate a superior academic record and are conducting research with a clear application to aerospace engineering or space sciences.

With recipients historically coming from 81 countries, the program has a strong international focus and is open to qualified women regardless of nationality.

Eligible applicants should carefully review the requirements and prepare their applications well before the deadline.

TITLE: D-Prize Global Competition 2026 for Entrepreneurs ($20K grants)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: December 6, 2026

Applications are open for the D-Prize Global Competition 2026. The D-Prize awards startup grants of up to $20,000 to entrepreneurs launching new organizations. They believe the world needs more social impact organizations, and they seed for-profit ventures, NGOs, and charities. They support organizations in any low-or-middle income country where extreme poverty still exists.

They believe social impact organizations are uniquely positioned to distribute an existing product or service known to improve lives where need still exists.

Challenges

Childhood Diarrhea Treatment: Can you get free ORS and zinc into homes before a child gets sick and prevent one of the leading killers of children under five?

DMPA-SC: Reach Underserved Populations: Can you distribute DMPA-SC to underserved population?

DMPA-SC: Improve Provider Training: Can you improve mandatory provider training for DMPA-SC?

DMPA-SC: Last Mile Inventory Management: Can you improve last mile inventory management of DMPA-SC?

DMPA-SC: Medical Waste Management: Can you increase safe disposal of DMPA-SC needles?

Reading Glasses: Can you distribute non-prescription reading/ working glasses to those in need?

Childcare: Can you help low-income families access quality childcare services?

ConnectEd Phone-based Tutoring: Can you distribute a phone-based intervention to improve learning?

Teaching at the Right Level: Can you improve foundational literacy and numeracy in resource-limited classrooms?

Road Safety: Can you reduce road deaths by replicating a proven public transport safety campaign?

Government Transparency: Can you monitor and report data to reduce corruption and improve public service?

Poverty Graduation: Can you provide coaching, capital, and social support to lift people out of ultra poverty?

Agriculture: Propose Your Own: Propose distribution of an evidence-based agriculture intervention not on the list.

Post-Harvest Support: Can you provide post-harvest loans and storage technology proven to smallholders?

Quality Inputs: Can you provide smallholders quality inputs and training to increase their harvests?

Water Filters: Can you sell ceramic water filters to people in areas without access to clean water?

Kangaroo Care: Can you provide access to Kangaroo Care (KC), a proven but underused intervention for infants born too soon or too small?

Oxygen: Can you develop a team of technicians to service and repair existing oxygen concentrators to improve access to medical oxygen?

Patient Identification: Can you develop a way to identify patients needing treatment for either obstetric fistula, cervical cancer, club foot, or cataracts, then connect them with existing treatment services in your area?

Maternal Health: Can you train birth attendants to administer misoprostol to prevent maternal deaths from postpartum hemorrhaging?

Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission: Can you counsel and motivate HIV-positive pregnant women to adhere to their ART regimen, and thus prevent mother-to-child HIV transmission?

Child Immunization: Can you direct caregivers to bring children to health facilities for routine immunizations that would otherwise not occur?

Sugar Daddy Awareness: Can you teach Sugar Daddy Awareness to 8th grade classes to reduce unwanted teen pregnancies and HIV infections?

Propose your own: Pitch distribution of an intervention backed by credible evidence and not on the list.

Eligibility

New organizations only. Most awardees are first-time entrepreneurs who have not yet launched or raised outside funding.

They especially encourage applicants from low- and middle-income countries.

Orgs with more than 18 months of full-time operations or more than $30,000 USD raised typically not supported.

Existing organizations considered only if your core focus is distributing an existing, evidence-based poverty intervention.

Application

Select an intervention and be prepared for the following deadlines:

The Global Competition launches on 14 September 2026

Early Submission Deadline: 25 October 2026 at midnight PT (Pacific Time)

Regular Submission Deadline: 15 November 2026 at midnight PT (Pacific Time)

Extension Deadline: 6 December 2026 at midnight PT (Pacific Time)

For more information, visit D-Prize Global Competition.

TITLE: Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026: Up to US$30,000 for Community-Led Climate Resilience Projects in East Africa and the South Caucasus

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
SEO Title: Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026: Up to US$30,000 for Mountain Community Climate Resilience

Meta Description: Apply for the Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026 and receive up to US$30,000 to implement community-led climate adaptation and nature-based solutions in East Africa and the South Caucasus. Deadline: 15 September 2026.

Focus Keywords: Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026, UNEP grants 2026, climate adaptation grants, mountain community grants, East Africa climate grants, South Caucasus grants, community-based organization grants, nature-based solutions funding, climate resilience funding

Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026

Community-based organizations and other eligible local organizations working with mountain communities in East Africa and the South Caucasus have an opportunity to apply for the Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Project for Mountain Community Resilience.

The initiative, implemented by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), is designed to support locally driven solutions that help mountain communities respond to the impacts of climate change while protecting ecosystems, strengthening livelihoods and improving food security. UNEP describes the project as a small-grants scheme providing funding of up to US$30,000 per project for needs-based, community-led adaptation solutions.

The programme is particularly relevant for organizations that are already working directly with mountain communities and have practical solutions that can address climate-related challenges through ecosystem-based and nature-based approaches.

For the 2026 call, solution proposals must be submitted by 15 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. East African Time/South Caucasus Time.

What Is the Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Project?

The Mountains ADAPT initiative focuses on strengthening the resilience of communities living in mountain areas that are increasingly exposed to climate change.

Mountain regions face a range of climate-related pressures, including changing rainfall patterns, rising temperatures, loss of snow and ice, water-related challenges and worsening natural hazards. These risks can be intensified by structural challenges such as remoteness, limited investment and inadequate access to resources. UNEP emphasizes that local-level adaptation action is important for implementing broader climate policies and achieving climate goals.

The Mountains ADAPT small-grants approach therefore seeks to place communities at the centre of climate adaptation.

Rather than focusing only on large-scale infrastructure or externally designed interventions, the programme supports community-led solutions that respond to locally identified climate risks and needs.

According to the application form, the initiative is intended to help organizations turn practical ideas into solutions that can preserve or restore ecosystems, strengthen livelihoods, improve food security and safeguard natural resources.

What Funding Is Available?

Successful applicants can receive up to US$30,000 per project.

The funding is intended to support the design and implementation of impactful solutions that respond to climate change impacts affecting mountain communities.

The grant can therefore provide an opportunity for eligible organizations to move beyond identifying a climate problem and actually implement a practical intervention within their communities.

The programme also goes beyond financial assistance.

Successful organizations are expected to receive:

Capacity development support

Training

Support for implementing their proposed solution

Opportunities for learning and exchange with other grantees and mountain adaptation stakeholders

Support for strengthening locally led adaptation action

UNEP states that successful applicants will receive capacity development and training support from UNEP and regional implementing partners, while cross-sectoral learning and exchange are an integral part of the project.

Who Is the Mountains ADAPT Grant Designed For?

The opportunity is intended for local organizations working with mountain communities, rather than individual applicants applying in their personal capacity.

The official application form specifically identifies eligible applicants as registered local non-profit organizations or enterprises, including civil society organizations, community-based organizations, youth organizations and women’s organizations, provided they can supply supporting documentation.

The organizations should:

Be based in an eligible country in the East African Community or South Caucasus.

Be locally registered and able to provide supporting documentation.

Work with mountain communities.

Have activities connected to climate change adaptation or related community resilience work.

Have a solution addressing a climate-related challenge.

Aim to preserve, restore or improve livelihoods, ecosystems or food security.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to community-based organizations, local NGOs, civil society organizations, youth-led organizations, women’s organizations and other locally registered organizations with an established connection to mountain communities.

Which Countries Are Eligible?

The programme covers countries in the East African Community (EAC) and the South Caucasus.

UNEP identifies the programme location as EAC partner states and South Caucasus countries.

East African Community

As of 2026, the EAC has eight Partner States:

Burundi

Democratic Republic of the Congo

Kenya

Rwanda

Somalia

South Sudan

Uganda

Tanzania

The EAC’s official website confirms these eight countries as its current Partner States.

South Caucasus

The South Caucasus region generally includes:

Armenia

Azerbaijan

Georgia

The Mountains ADAPT application form confirms that applicants must be based in a country of the East African Community or the South Caucasus.

Important: The eligibility requirement is based on the location and status of the applying organization, not on an individual’s nationality or ethnicity.

What Types of Projects Are Encouraged?

The central focus is climate adaptation and mountain community resilience, particularly projects that combine community action with ecosystem protection.

The programme encourages solutions that can address climate-related challenges while also producing benefits for people and the natural environment.

Potential areas include:

1. Nature-Based Solutions

Projects can use ecosystems and natural processes to help communities adapt to climate change.

Examples may include:

Ecosystem restoration

Restoration of degraded landscapes

Protection of natural resources

Community-based conservation

Restoration of natural water systems

UNEP specifically identifies Nature-based Solutions as a core approach for Mountains ADAPT projects.

2. Climate-Smart Agriculture

Organizations working with mountain farmers can consider approaches that make agricultural systems more resilient to changing climate conditions.

Possible areas include:

Climate-resilient agricultural practices

Sustainable farming

Climate-resilient crops

Soil conservation

Sustainable land management

Improved agricultural productivity under changing climatic conditions

3. Water Management

Water availability is an increasingly important issue for mountain communities.

Potential interventions may include:

Water harvesting

Water retention

Improved water management

Community-based water conservation

Protection of water resources

UNEP specifically lists water harvesting and retention among examples of possible adaptation solutions.

4. Food Security

Projects can focus on helping communities maintain reliable access to food despite climate-related disruptions.

This could involve approaches that strengthen:

Local food production

Climate-resilient agriculture

Sustainable natural-resource management

Food systems

Community livelihoods

The official application form explicitly highlights enhancing food security as one of the objectives of eligible solutions.

5. Livelihood Improvement

Climate change can place significant pressure on mountain livelihoods.

Projects may therefore seek to diversify or protect income sources while ensuring that natural resources are not degraded.

The programme is intended to support solutions that preserve, restore or improve livelihoods while strengthening ecosystem resilience.

What Makes a Strong Mountains ADAPT Proposal?

A strong proposal should not simply describe climate change as a general problem.

It should demonstrate a clear connection between:

Climate risk → Community need → Practical solution → Ecosystem protection → Improved resilience → Sustainable livelihoods

Applicants should be able to clearly explain:

What climate-related problem affects the target community?

Which mountain communities are affected?

What is causing or worsening the problem?

What solution is being proposed?

Why is the solution appropriate for the local context?

How will the community participate?

How will the project protect or restore ecosystems?

How will the intervention improve resilience?

How will livelihoods or food security benefit?

How will the project be implemented?

How will results be measured?

How can the solution continue beyond the grant period?

The official UNEP programme page emphasizes that projects should empower local communities, respond to identified climate risks and impacts, align with relevant policies and plans, and integrate Nature-based Solutions.

Why Community-Led Climate Adaptation Matters

Mountain communities are often directly dependent on natural resources for their livelihoods.

Agriculture, water resources, forests, livestock, biodiversity and other ecosystem services can all be affected by climate change.

When these systems become less reliable, communities can experience:

Reduced agricultural productivity

Water shortages

Soil degradation

Increased exposure to natural hazards

Loss of biodiversity

Reduced household income

Increased food insecurity

Greater pressure on natural resources

This is why locally designed adaptation measures can be particularly valuable.

Communities often possess detailed knowledge of their local ecosystems, livelihoods and environmental changes. A community-led approach can help ensure that interventions respond to actual local priorities rather than applying a one-size-fits-all solution.

UNEP describes small grants as an effective way of responding to local needs and strengthening local capacities, particularly among women, youth and other groups.

Key Benefits of the Mountains ADAPT Small Grants

The opportunity offers several potential benefits to successful organizations.

Financial support

Eligible organizations can receive up to US$30,000 to implement their proposed climate adaptation project.

Capacity development

Successful applicants will receive capacity development and training support from UNEP and regional implementing partners.

Community impact

The programme allows organizations to implement solutions directly within mountain communities and respond to locally identified climate challenges.

Environmental protection

Projects are expected to integrate ecosystem-based and nature-based approaches, linking community resilience with environmental sustainability.

Livelihood improvement

Projects can help communities protect, restore or improve livelihoods affected by climate change.

Food security

Solutions can contribute to more resilient food systems and improved food security.

Knowledge exchange

The programme provides opportunities for cross-sectoral learning and exchange among grantees and other stakeholders working on mountain adaptation.

The Importance of Women, Youth and Inclusive Community Participation

Mountains ADAPT is not only concerned with environmental outcomes.

The programme also emphasizes strengthening capacities among women, youth and other groups, while supporting inclusive approaches to climate adaptation.

For organizations preparing applications, this means it can be useful to demonstrate how the proposed project will involve different groups within the target community.

Applicants should consider questions such as:

Who participates in decision-making?

Who benefits from the intervention?

Are women meaningfully involved?

Are young people involved?

Are vulnerable or marginalized groups considered?

Does the project create opportunities for different community groups?

How will community knowledge inform the project?

A strong community-led project should demonstrate not only what will be implemented, but also who will participate and benefit.

What Kind of Organization Should Apply?

This opportunity could be particularly relevant to organizations working in areas such as:

Climate change adaptation

Environmental conservation

Community development

Sustainable agriculture

Food security

Water management

Ecosystem restoration

Natural resource management

Rural development

Livelihood development

Mountain conservation

Disaster risk reduction

Women’s empowerment

Youth development

Community resilience

However, organizations should not apply simply because they work in one of these sectors.

The proposed project needs to have a clear connection to mountain communities and climate change adaptation, and the organization must satisfy the programme’s geographical and registration requirements.

Examples of Relevant Project Concepts

Based on the programme’s stated focus, eligible organizations could potentially develop projects around concepts such as:

Climate-smart farming for mountain communities

A project could help farmers adopt agricultural practices that are better suited to changing rainfall patterns, temperature changes and other climate pressures.

Community water harvesting

An organization could develop or strengthen community-level water harvesting and retention systems to improve water availability and resilience.

Ecosystem restoration

A project could restore degraded mountain ecosystems while creating livelihood or environmental benefits for surrounding communities.

Climate-resilient livelihoods

Organizations could develop approaches that diversify household income while reducing pressure on natural resources.

Community food-security initiatives

Projects could strengthen local food production and improve resilience to climate-related disruptions.

These are examples of the types of approaches that align with the programme’s stated themes; applicants should ensure their actual proposal responds to a clearly identified local climate risk.

The deadline for the first call is:

15 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m.

The deadline is specified according to East African Time/South Caucasus Time.

Organizations should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their proposals. The application may require time to gather organizational documentation, develop the project concept and ensure that the proposed solution clearly addresses the eligibility requirements.

Where the Mountains ADAPT Programme Operates

The programme operates across the East African Community and South Caucasus.

UNEP identifies its location as EAC Partner States and South Caucasus countries.

The programme is therefore relevant to organizations working in mountain areas across these two regions rather than being a global grant open to organizations from every country.

The EAC currently consists of eight Partner States: Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Uganda and Tanzania.

UNEP’s Previous Mountains ADAPT Experience

Mountains ADAPT is not an entirely new concept.

UNEP states that the Mountains ADAPT scheme was pilot tested in EAC and South Caucasus countries in 2025.

The previous work provides examples of the types of community-level interventions that can be supported.

For example, UNEP highlights:

Georgia: Installation of hydrometeorological stations in public schools alongside climate change knowledge and disaster preparedness activities.

Kenya: Training on climate-smart agriculture and dissemination of climate-resilient crops to Indigenous communities north of Mount Kenya.

Burundi: Activities addressing soil erosion and diversification of income sources.

Azerbaijan: Revitalization of traditional culture and knowledge through a water mill and improved irrigation for public parks.

Tanzania: Strengthening village structures through bamboo seedlings and training on sustainable agricultural practices.

These examples demonstrate the broad range of approaches that can contribute to mountain resilience, from agriculture and water management to ecosystem restoration, local knowledge and community capacity building.

Final Takeaway

The Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026 opportunity provides an important funding pathway for locally registered organizations working with mountain communities in the East African Community and South Caucasus.

With funding of up to US$30,000 per project, the programme is designed to help community-based and other eligible local organizations turn climate adaptation ideas into practical interventions. The emphasis is on community-led action, ecosystem-based adaptation, nature-based solutions, resilient livelihoods, food security and environmental protection.

Organizations should focus on developing proposals that are locally relevant, clearly connected to climate risks and capable of producing tangible benefits for both communities and ecosystems.

The deadline is 15 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. East African Time/South Caucasus Time. Eligible organizations should review the requirements carefully and submit their applications through the official UNEP application platform before the deadline.

TITLE: Quantum Information Science

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
There is a worldwide research effort exploring the potentials of quantum mechanics for applications. The field began with Feynman’s proposal in 1981 at MIT Endicott House to build a computer that takes advantage of quantum mechanics and has grown enormously since Peter Shor‘s 1994 quantum factoring algorithm. The idea of utilizing quantum mechanics to process information has since grown from computation and communication to encompass diverse topics such as sensing and simulations in biology and chemistry. Leaving aside the extensive experimental efforts to build controllable large-scale quantum devices, theory research in quantum information science (QIS) investigates several themes:

Quantum algorithms and complexity. If a perfectly functioning quantum computer were built, which problems could it solve faster than conventional computers, and which problems do not admit any speedup? What is the fundamental limitation in the computational power of our universe governed by quantum mechanics?

Quantum information theory. How can we store, transfer, or manipulate quantum information in the presence of noise? How can we efficiently communicate and compute in the presence of errors? What are the basic properties of quantum entanglement and information?

Measurement and control. How can we efficiently manipulate and characterize quantum devices? Apart from computations and communications, what other applications can benefit from quantum hardwares? What are the ways to improve applications such as ultra-sensitive sensors or precise clocks?

Applications and connections. How can ideas from QIS contribute to other research areas as diverse as convex optimizations, black holes, and exotic quantum phases of matter? Is there a unified framework to efficiently describe quantum entanglement and information in complex systems?

QIS theory research at MIT spans all of these areas. The CTP faculty involved are Soonwon Choi and Aram Harrow, and the larger group at MIT includes Isaac Chuang (EECS/physics), Seth Lloyd (Mech. Eng.), Anand Natarajan (EECS) and Peter Shor (Math) and Hengyun (Harry) Zhou (EECS). Other faculty in the area include Eddie Farhi (emeritus), Jeffrey Goldstone (emeritus) and Jeff Shapiro (EECS, emeritus). Together this forms a large and vibrant group working in all areas of QIS.

Some of the notable contributions involving the CTP include the quantum adiabatic algorithm and quantum walk algorithms (Farhi, Goldstone), the first example of a problem for which quantum computers exhibit no speedup (Farhi, Goldstone), proposals for unforgeable quantum money (Farhi, Shor), a quantum algorithm for linear systems of equations (Harrow, Lloyd), efficient protocols for simulating quantum channels (Harrow, Shor), both algorithms and hardness results for testing entanglement (Harrow), proposals for quantum approximate optimization algorithms (Farhi, Goldstone), proposals and experimental observations of exotic quantum dynamics such as slow thermalization or a discrete time crystalline phase in quantum simulators (Choi), quantum sensing protocols using strongly interacting spin ensembles (Choi), and quantum convolutional neural networks (Choi). Ongoing research at MIT in QIS includes work on new quantum algorithms, efficient simulations of quantum systems, methods to characterize and control existing or near-term quantum hardwares, connections to many-body physics, applications in high-energy physics, and many other topics.

The larger QIS group at MIT shares a seminar series, a weekly group meeting, regular events for grad students.

Interdepartmental course offerings include an introductory and an advanced class in core QI/QC, as well as occasional advanced special topics classes. Quantum information has also entered the undergraduate physics curriculum with a junior lab experiment on NMR quantum computing and some lectures in the 8.04/8.05/8.06 sequence on quantum computing.

TITLE: Direct observations of strong jets transporting deep and bottom water into the Indian Ocean through the fracture zones of the Southwest Indian Ridge

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Menezes, V., Furey, H., Torres, D., Bahr, F., & Baker, L. (2026). Direct Observations of Strong Jets Transporting Deep and Bottom Water Into the Indian Ocean Through the Fracture Zones of the Southwest Indian Ridge. Journal of Geophysical Research – Oceans, 131(3), e2025JC023864.https://doi.org/10.1029/2025jc023864

Figure courtesy of Viviane de Menezes

The Deep Madagascar Basin Experiment was designed to study the pathways of the Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) into the subtropics in the Southwest Indian Ocean. Particular focus was given to the meridionally oriented, narrow fracture zones of the Southwest Indian Ridge, which separate the Crozet Basin in the Southern Ocean from the Madagascar Basin in the subtropics. These fracture zones serve as chokepoints for the abyssal overturning circulation. In this paper, we report the discovery of two strong abyssal jets transporting Antarctic Bottom Water northward and assess the strength of diapycnal turbulent mixing in the region. One jet was identified at the Novara fracture zone (46 cm/s), where turbulent mixing in the abyss is weak. The second jet was detected at the Melville fracture zone (24 cm/s), where abyssal mixing is high. These newly identified jets complement the previously known deep jet in the Atlantis II fracture zone, which was also measured during the experiment.

Research Areas

Applications are welcomed across different areas of research, but proposed projects must align with UniSQ’s flagship research areas.

Applicants should discuss the flagship area that most closely matches their proposed research with their potential supervisor before submitting their application.

This alignment is important because applicants are assessed partly on the relationship between their proposed research and UniSQ’s research priorities.

Prospective applicants can also explore UniSQ’s current research thesis topics and connect with UniSQ experts to identify appropriate research opportunities and potential supervisory arrangements.

Industry Stream

The scholarship also provides an optional Industry Stream.

The Industry Stream is designed to create stronger connections between doctoral research and industry by requiring successful participants to complete a:

60-day industry internship

Applicants interested in this stream are responsible for identifying an appropriate industry partner, either independently or with support from their prospective supervisor.

The industry partner must complete a Letter of Support as part of the application.

If the scholarship is awarded under the Industry Stream, all required contractual agreements must be completed before the student begins the programme.

Continuing Student Requirements for the Industry Stream

Continuing students applying for the Industry Stream must meet additional timing requirements.

They must be:

Within 18 months of commencing full-time study, or

Within 36 months of commencing part-time study.

Applicants are advised to consult UniSQ’s Senior Coordinator for Commercialisation and Partnerships before applying to ensure that the proposed internship meets the university’s requirements.

Dedicated Opportunities for Women in STEMM and Students With Disabilities

In addition to the Industry Stream, the scholarship offering includes dedicated scholarships for:

Women in STEMM

Students with disabilities

This provides additional opportunities for applicants from groups specifically supported through UniSQ’s research scholarship offerings.

Applicants should review the relevant scholarship requirements when preparing their application.

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered for the UniSQ International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship, applicants must meet the university’s eligibility requirements.

Applicants must:

Hold the Required Academic Qualification

Applicants must have completed a Bachelor Degree with First Class Honours, or an equivalent qualification.

Applicants should provide evidence of their academic qualifications and transcripts as part of the application.

Be Eligible for Full-Time PhD Study

Applicants must be eligible to enrol full-time and on-campus in the Doctor of Philosophy programme at UniSQ.

The scholarship is therefore intended for students who satisfy the university’s requirements for admission to its PhD programme.

Be an International Student

Applicants must be international students.

They must not be:

Australian citizens

New Zealand citizens

Australian permanent residents

Commence or Continue Study in 2027

Applicants must either:

Commence their PhD studies in 2027, or

Continue their existing PhD studies in 2027.

Academic and Research Selection Criteria

Eligibility does not automatically guarantee a scholarship.

Applications are assessed using several selection criteria designed to identify applicants with strong academic and research potential.

Academic Achievement

The university considers applicants’ academic records, including:

Honours classification or equivalent

Performance in postgraduate study

Academic prizes

Academic awards

Overall academic achievement

Applicants with a strong academic history are therefore likely to be more competitive.

Research Capability

Applicants are also assessed on evidence of their ability to conduct high-quality research.

Relevant evidence may include:

Research publications in high-quality journals

Conference presentations

Research internship experience

Creative works, where applicable

Other evidence demonstrating research capability

Applicants should clearly demonstrate their previous research experience and achievements.

Research Project and Environment

The proposed PhD project is another important part of the assessment.

The university may consider:

Alignment with UniSQ research priorities

Relevance to the Australian research context

External support for the proposed research

Potential impact of the research

Resources required to successfully complete the research

Applicants should therefore ensure that their research proposal is clear, realistic, relevant, and well aligned with UniSQ’s research strengths.

Supervisory Team

The proposed supervisory team is also considered.

Applicants are encouraged to work closely with prospective supervisors and demonstrate:

The supervisors’ publication records

Complementary research expertise

Supervisor capacity

Available resources to support the proposed research

Finding an appropriate supervisor before applying can therefore be an important part of preparing a competitive application.

PhD Admission Is a Separate Process

An important requirement is that applying for the scholarship and applying for admission to the PhD programme are separate processes.

Applicants must begin the application process for admission into the Doctor of Philosophy programme in order to be eligible for the scholarship.

Prospective students should therefore allow sufficient time to complete both processes.

Required Application Documents

Applicants should prepare digital copies of the required supporting documents before beginning the scholarship application.

These include:

Statement of Claim completed by the student and supervisor

Curriculum vitae, including research publications and/or presentations

Preliminary Research Thesis Topic Proposal

Documentation confirming citizenship

Testamurs and academic transcripts for all undergraduate and postgraduate qualifications

Applicants applying through the Industry Stream must also provide:

Letter of Support completed by the industry partner

All documents should be prepared carefully and submitted according to UniSQ’s application requirements.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should follow the university’s application process.

Step 1: Identify Your Research Area

Review UniSQ’s flagship research areas and identify the area that most closely aligns with your proposed PhD research.

Step 2: Find a Potential Supervisor

Applicants should connect with a potential supervisor whose research expertise matches their proposed project.

Discussing the proposed research with the supervisor can help applicants refine their research direction and identify the appropriate UniSQ flagship area.

Step 3: Begin the PhD Admission Process

Applicants must start the separate application process for admission to the Doctor of Philosophy programme.

Step 4: Prepare the Scholarship Documents

Prepare the required academic records, CV, research proposal, Statement of Claim, citizenship documentation, and other supporting materials.

Step 5: Submit the Scholarship Application

The scholarship application must be submitted through the UniSQ Scholarship Application Management System before the closing date.

Application Portal: https://scholarships-apply.usq.edu.au/

Applicants who need assistance can consult the university’s Scholarship Online Application Manual.

Application Deadline

The closing date for the scholarship is:

27 September 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and allow enough time to obtain supporting documents and complete the separate PhD admission process.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly suitable for international students who:

Have completed a Bachelor’s degree with First Class Honours or equivalent

Have strong academic achievements

Have research experience or demonstrated research capability

Have a clear and original PhD research idea

Want to pursue doctoral research in Australia

Can align their proposed research with a UniSQ flagship area

Are able to enrol full-time and on-campus

Plan to commence or continue their PhD studies in 2027

Researchers with publications, conference presentations, research internships, or other evidence of research capability may be particularly competitive.

Why Consider the UniSQ Scholarship?

Pursuing a PhD internationally can involve significant tuition and living costs. This scholarship can substantially reduce the financial burden by combining an annual stipend with tuition-fee support.

The AUD $39,000 annual stipend provides financial assistance throughout the supported scholarship period, while UniSQ covers tuition fees for up to three years of full-time equivalent study.

The opportunity also provides access to a research environment where doctoral candidates can work with experienced supervisors and engage with research projects aligned with UniSQ’s flagship areas.

The optional Industry Stream adds another dimension by providing an opportunity for eligible scholarship recipients to undertake a 60-day industry internship.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Applicants should not wait until the final days before the deadline to begin their applications.

Finding a suitable supervisor, developing a research proposal, obtaining academic documents, and completing the separate PhD admission process can require considerable preparation.

Applicants should also ensure that their proposed research is genuinely aligned with UniSQ’s research priorities and that they can clearly explain the expected contribution and impact of their project.

For the Industry Stream, applicants should begin discussions with a potential industry partner early enough to obtain the required Letter of Support and complete any necessary agreements.

Conclusion

The UniSQ International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship 2027 is a significant opportunity for high-achieving international students seeking to undertake PhD research in Australia.

Successful applicants can receive AUD $39,000 per year and tuition-fee coverage for up to three years of full-time equivalent study. The scholarship welcomes research proposals across multiple areas, provided they align with UniSQ’s flagship research priorities.

In addition to the standard scholarship, applicants can explore the optional Industry Stream, which includes a mandatory 60-day industry internship, as well as dedicated opportunities for women in STEMM and students with disabilities.

With a deadline of 27 September 2026, prospective applicants should begin preparing their research proposal, identifying a potential supervisor, gathering supporting documents, and starting the separate PhD admission process well in advance.

TITLE: WWF Amano Fellows Program 2027 for Zimbabweans

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 16, 2026

Are you a young Zimbabwean leader aged 21–30 with a proven track record of creating positive change in your community and a strong commitment to inclusive conservation and sustainable development? WWF Zimbabwe, in partnership with Amano, invites young leaders from Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities to apply for the Amano Fellows Program.

The Amano Fellows Program is a 9-month mentorship initiative designed to support and nurture the next generation of conservation leaders. Fellows will participate in expert-led workshops, peer-to-peer learning and mentorship sessions focused on leadership, conservation and sustainable development.

Benefits

Selected fellows will have the opportunity to:

Develop their leadership and communication skills

Learn from experienced conservation and development practitioners

Participate in expert-led workshops and peer discussions

Receive guidance through mentorship sessions

Build networks with other young leaders working to create positive change

Strengthen their capacity to advance inclusive and community-centred conservation

Open to Zimbabwean young leaders aged 21–30 who have demonstrated leadership experience and a proven track record of making a meaningful impact in their communities or region.

Applicants should have a strong commitment to inclusive conservation and sustainable development and preferably be from or work closely with Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities.

TITLE: Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship 2027 in Sharjah: One-Year Residency for Scholars of African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the 2027 Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship in African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies, offered by The Africa Institute at Global Studies University in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.

The Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship is a full-time, one-year residential research opportunity for established scholars, independent authors and public intellectuals whose work engages seriously with African and African diaspora literature, culture and related fields. The fellowship is intended for senior researchers and thinkers with an established body of intellectual work rather than early-career researchers or doctoral students.

Based at The Africa Institute in Sharjah, UAE, the fellowship provides its holder with an opportunity to pursue a substantial research project within an institution dedicated to the study of Africa and its global diaspora across the humanities and social sciences.

The residency normally runs from September to June, making it a substantial academic commitment rather than a short visiting fellowship.

Applications for the 2027 Research Fellowships Program are currently open.

Application deadline: Wednesday, September 30, 2026.

Prospective applicants can submit a new application through the Global Studies University application portal.

For application questions or technical assistance, applicants may contact:

applications@theafricainstitute.org

About the Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship

The Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship is one of several research fellowships hosted by The Africa Institute, Global Studies University.

The fellowship is named in honor of Toni Morrison, whose literary, intellectual and critical contributions transformed understandings of African American experience, race, culture, memory, history and identity.

Morrison was one of the most influential writers and intellectuals of the modern era. Her major recognitions included the:

National Book Critics Circle Award in 1977

Pulitzer Prize in 1988

Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993

The Africa Institute describes Morrison’s significance as extending well beyond fiction. Her work also made major contributions to cultural criticism, critical theory and intellectual debates surrounding Black experience and identity.

The fellowship builds upon this legacy by supporting senior researchers and writers whose work contributes to the understanding of African and African diaspora literature and culture.

About The Africa Institute

The Africa Institute is part of Global Studies University in Sharjah.

It describes itself as a globally oriented centre for:

Research

Documentation

Study

Teaching

focused on Africa and its diaspora, particularly within the humanities and social sciences.

The Institute has been developed as both a:

Research-based think tank

Postgraduate education institution

Its academic mission includes training new generations of scholars and critical thinkers while developing new approaches to research, teaching and documentation concerning Africa and African diaspora studies.

The institution offers graduate education at the:

Master’s level

PhD level

while also hosting senior and postdoctoral researchers through its Research Fellowships Program.

This wider institutional environment means the Toni Morrison Senior Fellow becomes part of a scholarly community specifically structured around research into Africa and its global diasporas.

A Fellowship for Established Scholars and Public Intellectuals

The Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship is specifically a senior-level opportunity.

Eligible applicants include individuals who are:

Associate Professors

Full Professors

Scholars holding equivalent senior positions inside or outside academia

Independent authors

Public intellectuals

Independent scholars do not necessarily need to hold a conventional university professorship.

However, independent authors and public intellectuals should have achieved critical recognition for their writing and intellectual contributions in fields connected with Africa, African diaspora studies and culture.

This makes the fellowship potentially relevant to accomplished intellectuals whose careers developed outside conventional academic structures.

Who Is Not the Primary Target?

Because this is a Senior Fellowship, it should not be confused with a postdoctoral programme.

The supplied eligibility conditions distinguish senior fellowships from The Africa Institute’s postdoctoral opportunities.

Applicants who have recently completed a PhD would generally be better aligned with one of the Institute’s separately advertised postdoctoral fellowships unless they already satisfy the senior-level or equivalent criteria.

The Toni Morrison Fellowship is therefore primarily aimed at people with an established research, publishing or intellectual profile.

Academic and Research Focus

The fellowship focuses on:

African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies.

This provides a broad intellectual framework within which applicants may develop research concerned with literature, culture and the wider African diaspora.

Potentially relevant fields may include areas such as:

African diaspora literature

African American literature

Black literary studies

Cultural studies

Literary criticism

Postcolonial literature

Diaspora studies

African literature

Comparative literature

Cultural theory

Black studies

Memory and literature

Race and representation

Migration and cultural production

Identity and belonging

Global Black intellectual traditions

These examples illustrate the breadth of the fellowship’s stated area rather than constituting an official closed list of eligible disciplines.

Applicants should ensure that their proposed work clearly fits the fellowship’s central emphasis on African and African diaspora literature and culture.

Why Toni Morrison’s Legacy Matters to the Fellowship

The fellowship’s intellectual orientation reflects Toni Morrison’s importance not only as a novelist but also as a thinker whose work addressed major questions about:

History

Memory

Race

Language

Community

Violence

Identity

Culture

Belonging

African American experience

Morrison’s writing created powerful ways of understanding Black experience while also contributing to broader questions in world literature and the humanities.

The Africa Institute therefore uses the fellowship to encourage scholarship capable of placing African diaspora cultural and literary production within wider intellectual and global contexts.

A Global African Diaspora Perspective

One particularly important dimension of the fellowship is its location within an institution explicitly concerned with both Africa and its diaspora.

This opens space for research that crosses conventional geographic boundaries.

For example, research may explore relationships between:

Africa and African America

Africa and the Caribbean

Africa and Europe

Africa and the Middle East

Literature and migration

Postcolonial Africa and diaspora cultures

Black cultural production across different regions

The fellowship can therefore support scholarship that approaches African diaspora studies comparatively, transnationally or historically.

The Fellowship Is Residential

The Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship is a:

Full-time, one-year residency in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.

The residency typically runs:

September to June.

Applicants should take this condition seriously.

This is not advertised as:

A remote fellowship

A part-time appointment

A short research visit

A fellowship that can ordinarily be completed while maintaining full-time residence elsewhere

Successful Fellows should therefore be prepared to base themselves in Sharjah for the fellowship period in accordance with the programme’s requirements.

Why Sharjah?

Sharjah provides a distinctive geographic setting for scholarship connecting Africa, the Middle East and the wider world.

The location of The Africa Institute in the UAE enables scholars to work from an intellectual environment that is not centred exclusively in North American or European institutions.

For scholars examining transnational literary and cultural relationships, this institutional position can provide a valuable setting for thinking about:

Africa’s relationships with other regions

Diaspora movements

Intellectual exchange

Postcolonial cultural formations

Global African studies

Applicants should nevertheless frame their research according to the fellowship’s stated scholarly priorities rather than assuming that every project concerning the Middle East is automatically eligible.

Current Toni Morrison Senior Fellow

For the 2026–2027 academic year, Carolyn Denard, founder and board chair of the Toni Morrison Society, continues as the Toni Morrison Senior Fellow.

Her fellowship illustrates the kind of substantial scholarly work that the programme can support.

During her fellowship, Denard is working on:

Bearing Witness: Culture and Meaning in Toni Morrison’s Fiction

Her reflections on the fellowship emphasize how the residency expanded her understanding of Morrison as a writer situated within the broader African diaspora and opened new connections between Morrison’s work and postcolonial Africa.

This provides useful context for prospective applicants: the fellowship is not narrowly restricted to textual analysis of Morrison’s novels.

Rather, it provides space for broader intellectual work connecting African diaspora literature and culture to questions concerning Africa and its global relationships.

Does Your Research Have to Be About Toni Morrison?

The fellowship is named in honor of Toni Morrison, but the description does not state that every proposed project must focus exclusively on Morrison herself.

Instead, eligibility is framed more broadly around:

African and African diaspora literature and culture.

Therefore, prospective applicants should focus primarily on whether their work meaningfully contributes to the fellowship’s stated field.

Researchers working specifically on Toni Morrison may naturally be strongly aligned, but the fellowship’s intellectual scope extends beyond a single author.

The Wider Senior and Postdoctoral Fellowships Program

The Toni Morrison Fellowship forms part of a wider collection of named research fellowships at The Africa Institute.

The 2027 programme includes both senior and postdoctoral opportunities.

Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship

Focus:

African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies

Target applicants:

Associate Professors

Full Professors

Equivalent senior scholars

Critically recognized independent authors and public intellectuals

Duration:

One year

Location:

Sharjah, UAE

Ali A. Mazrui Senior Fellowship in Global African Studies

The Ali A. Mazrui Senior Fellowship is named after the influential African studies scholar Ali A. Mazrui.

It is intended for established scholars whose work emphasizes:

African studies

African diaspora studies

Humanities

Social sciences

Intersections between these areas

Eligible applicants similarly include recognized Associate or Full Professors as well as established independent authors and public intellectuals.

It is also normally a full-time, one-year residency in Sharjah.

Okwui Enwezor Postdoctoral Fellowship

This fellowship is named in honor of scholar, curator and art critic Okwui Enwezor.

Its focus includes:

Visual culture

Performance studies

Art history

Art criticism

Critical humanities

Applicants must have earned their PhD within the five years before assuming the fellowship.

Unlike the senior fellowships, the Okwui Enwezor Fellowship is a:

Full-time, two-year residency in Sharjah.

Fatema Mernissi Postdoctoral Fellowship

Named after Moroccan scholar Fatema Mernissi, this fellowship supports emerging scholars whose work addresses areas including:

Gender

Feminism

Social sciences

Cultural studies

Visual cultures

The work should intersect with:

African and African diaspora studies.

Applicants must also have earned their PhD within the previous five years before taking up the fellowship.

This is likewise a:

Full-time, two-year residency in Sharjah.

Senior Fellowship Versus Postdoctoral Fellowship

Prospective applicants should choose carefully between the two fellowship levels.

Senior Fellowship applicants

Should generally be:

Associate Professors

Full Professors

Equivalent established researchers

Distinguished independent authors

Recognized public intellectuals

Postdoctoral Fellowship applicants

Must have:

A PhD

Awarded within the previous five years before assuming the fellowship

The Toni Morrison opportunity belongs firmly to the Senior Fellowship category.

What Kind of Applicant Would Be Particularly Well Aligned?

Based on the published description, strong applicants may include established scholars working in:

Literature

African diaspora studies

Cultural studies

African studies

Black studies

Comparative literature

Postcolonial studies

Critical theory

Humanities

An independent writer or public intellectual could also be competitive if they have achieved substantial recognition for work connected to these areas.

What Does “Critical Recognition” Mean for Independent Applicants?

The Institute does not provide a numeric or standardized definition in the supplied information.

However, the wording suggests that independent authors and public intellectuals should have an established record of serious intellectual or literary work.

This could potentially be evidenced through things such as:

Books

Major publications

Critical essays

Recognized scholarship

Significant cultural commentary

Public intellectual contributions

Professional recognition

Applicants should consult the complete application guidance for any specific documentation required to demonstrate this status.

Is a PhD Required?

For Associate and Full Professors, a doctoral-level academic profile would normally be expected within conventional academic career structures.

However, the fellowship’s eligibility statement specifically includes:

Independent authors and public intellectuals who have earned critical recognition for their writings.

The supplied information therefore does not state that every applicant must hold a PhD.

This distinction is important.

Independent writers and recognized intellectuals should not automatically exclude themselves solely because their career path differs from the traditional professoriate, provided they otherwise meet the programme’s senior-level requirements.

Is There an Age Limit?

No age restriction is stated in the information provided.

Eligibility is based on:

Career level

Intellectual standing

Research field

Relevance to African and African diaspora studies

rather than a published age threshold.

Fellowship Funding and Financial Support

The information supplied for the 2027 open call does not specify the financial package attached to the Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship.

In particular, it does not state in the material provided whether the fellowship includes:

A fixed salary

Monthly stipend

Housing allowance

Accommodation

Relocation funding

Airfare

Health insurance

Research allowance

Applicants should therefore not assume any specific financial benefits based on the information currently provided.

Prospective applicants should consult the full application guidance or contact The Africa Institute directly for the current 2027 financial and logistical terms.

For questions:

applications@theafricainstitute.org

Application Requirements

The public information supplied confirms the eligibility framework and application portal but does not reproduce the complete list of materials required for the 2027 Toni Morrison Fellowship.

Applicants should therefore review the official application system carefully.

Depending on the complete call instructions, applicants may be asked for materials related to their:

Academic or professional record

Research project

Publications

Intellectual contributions

Career experience

However, applicants should follow the official portal rather than relying on assumptions about required documents.

How to Apply

The application is completed through the Global Studies University application system.

Step 1: Review the Fellowship

Applicants should first make sure that their profile matches the Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship, particularly its:

Senior-level eligibility

African diaspora focus

Full-time residential requirement

Step 2: Prepare Your Research Project

Applicants should develop a project that clearly fits the fellowship’s emphasis on:

African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies.

A strong proposal should make the intellectual contribution of the work clear and show why The Africa Institute provides an appropriate environment for completing it.

Step 3: Start a New Application

New applicants should use the official registration portal:

https://register.gsu.ac.ae/psc/reg/EMPLOYEE/SA/c/X_ADMISSION.X_AD_REGISTRATION.GBL?&languageCD=ENG

Step 4: Returning Applicants

Applicants who have already started an application can return through the existing application system:

https://admission.gsu.ac.ae/psp/ps/EMPLOYEE/SA/?cmd=logout

Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline

The final application deadline is:

Wednesday, September 30, 2026.

Applicants should submit well before the closing date in case additional materials or technical corrections are needed.

Application Support

For questions or technical assistance, applicants can contact:

applications@theafricainstitute.org

This is particularly useful if an applicant is uncertain about:

Eligibility

Application documentation

Application portal problems

Senior-equivalent status

Fellowship residency requirements

How to Prepare a Strong Application

1. Show Clear Relevance to African Diaspora Studies

Do not assume that any literature or cultural studies project will automatically fit.

Explain explicitly how the work contributes to understanding:

Africa

African diasporas

Black cultural production

Related literary or cultural questions

2. Demonstrate Senior-Level Intellectual Achievement

The programme is seeking established scholars and intellectuals.

Your application should therefore communicate:

Your scholarly contribution

Major publications

Intellectual trajectory

Recognition in the field

Previous research achievements

For independent writers and public intellectuals, demonstrating critical recognition is especially important.

3. Explain the Original Contribution

A strong senior fellowship proposal should go beyond stating a topic.

Explain:

What question you are addressing

What is missing from existing scholarship

How your work changes or expands current understanding

Why the project matters now

4. Explain Why The Africa Institute Matters

The fellowship is not merely free time to write.

Applicants should consider why an institution devoted to African and African diaspora studies is particularly relevant to the proposed research.

A convincing application may demonstrate potential engagement with:

The Institute’s scholarly community

African studies debates

Diaspora scholarship

Interdisciplinary research

5. Be Prepared for a Full-Time Residency

Applicants should ensure that they can genuinely spend the required fellowship period in Sharjah.

The programme normally runs from September to June and is explicitly residential.

Applicants with substantial teaching, administrative or professional responsibilities at their home institution should make appropriate arrangements if selected.

Key Details at a Glance

Opportunity: Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship in African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies

Host: The Africa Institute, Global Studies University

Location: Sharjah, United Arab Emirates

Format: Full-time residential fellowship

Duration: One year

Typical residency period: September–June

Academic focus: African diaspora literature and cultural studies

Eligible academic level: Associate Professor, Full Professor or equivalent

Also eligible: Critically recognized independent authors and public intellectuals

Applications: Open

Deadline: Wednesday, September 30, 2026

Application year: 2027 Research Fellowships Program

Financial package: Not specified in the supplied 2027 open-call information

Application support: applications@theafricainstitute.org

Conclusion

The 2027 Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship in African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies at The Africa Institute offers established scholars, authors and public intellectuals the opportunity to spend a full academic year pursuing substantial research within a globally oriented institution devoted to the study of Africa and its diasporas.

The fellowship is particularly relevant to scholars whose work crosses the boundaries of literature, African diaspora studies, cultural studies, Black studies, comparative literature, postcolonial studies and related humanities fields.

Unlike a postdoctoral fellowship aimed at researchers immediately after the PhD, this programme is specifically designed for senior scholars at Associate Professor or Full Professor level or equivalent, while also creating a route for independent authors and public intellectuals whose writing has achieved significant critical recognition.

Successful applicants will undertake a full-time, one-year residency in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, normally from September through June.

The opportunity’s association with Toni Morrison also creates an important intellectual framework: one in which African diaspora literature is understood not simply through one national tradition, but in relation to the wider histories, cultures and intellectual connections linking Africa and its diasporas.

The 2027 application deadline is:

Wednesday, September 30, 2026.

Applicants should carefully review the official application system and contact The Africa Institute directly if clarification is needed concerning documents, financial support or residency arrangements.
