TITLE: Titech MEXT Scholarship 2027 in Japan | Fully Funded | Japanese Government Scholarship

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are open for the MEXT Scholarship 2027 at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (Titech). International students from all over the world are eligible for the Titech MEXT Scholarship 2027 in Japan. The Titech MEXT Scholarship is a fully funded international scholarship in Japan. The fully funded Titech MEXT Scholarships are offered to international students pursuing master’s and doctorate degrees in Japan. If you are a graduate and looking for a fully funded scholarship in Japan, then you should apply for a master’s scholarship in Japan.

Titech Institute is a National Research university located in the Greater Tokyo Area, Japan. The International Graduate Program by Tokyo Institute of Technology (Titech) offers five different English-language-based programs related to 14 different departments and helps students obtain a master’s or doctoral degree.

There are two types of programs under the International Graduate Program: one is the Integrated Doctoral Education Program, and the second is the Master’s Program. Furthermore, some programs are set up as an Integrated Doctoral Education Program, and these programs aim to combine Master’s and Doctoral programs so that a graduate student can obtain both degrees (Master’s and Doctoral) within three to five years.

The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology offers a MEXT scholarship at Science Tokyo to international students who wish to study at Japanese universities for free under the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship Program. In addition, the Japanese language is optional for this Titech MEXT Scholarship for international students, as all the lectures and seminars will held in English. However, international students will have an opportunity to attend Japanese language classes in order to learn, and this will help them in their daily lives. The Titech MEXT Scholarship in Japan duration for the master’s program is two years, and an extension for a doctoral degree is offered.

Science Tokyo recommends the eligible applicants for Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship among the applicants for the International Graduate Program (A) to MEXT. Applicants who want to get the MEXT scholarship must apply for it with the International Graduate Program (A) application. TITLE: Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program 2027: $70,000 Fellowship for Interdisciplinary Researchers in Computation

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Neukom Institute at Dartmouth College has announced the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Competition 2027, an exceptional opportunity for recent PhD graduates and emerging scholars whose research crosses traditional academic boundaries and incorporates computation as a significant intellectual, methodological, or practical component.

The prestigious fellowship is designed for highly motivated interdisciplinary researchers who are interested in exploring complex questions that cannot easily be confined to a single academic discipline. Successful candidates will receive the opportunity to conduct independent research at Dartmouth College while working across departments, collaborating with faculty mentors, teaching seminars, and becoming part of a vibrant intellectual community focused on computational thinking and interdisciplinary scholarship.

The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship positions are scheduled to begin on September 1, 2027. Selected Fellows will receive appointments lasting two years, with the possibility of requesting a third year. For the 2027–2028 academic year, Neukom Fellows will receive a stipend of $70,000, alongside additional financial support for equipment, travel, and research materials.

The competition provides an important platform for scholars whose work sits at the intersection of disciplines and computation. Whether computation serves as a methodological tool, a conceptual framework, or an explicit component of a research project, the fellowship encourages innovative approaches that challenge conventional academic boundaries.

About the Dartmouth Neukom Institute Postdoctoral Fellows Program

The Neukom Institute at Dartmouth College supports research and intellectual exploration at the intersection of computation and multiple academic disciplines. Its Postdoctoral Fellows Program brings together scholars whose work demonstrates the potential to bridge fields, develop new approaches to research, and expand how computational ideas can contribute to the understanding of complex problems.

The fellowship is particularly suited to researchers who do not fit neatly into traditional academic categories. Applicants may come from disciplines across the sciences, humanities, social sciences, arts, engineering, and other fields, provided they can demonstrate a meaningful connection between their research interests and the broader theme of computation.

A central feature of the Neukom Fellowship is its interdisciplinary structure. Fellows are expected to engage with faculty members and academic departments across Dartmouth College rather than working exclusively within a single disciplinary environment.

The program seeks individuals who can demonstrate both:

A history of successful collaboration across disciplinary boundaries; and

Strong evidence of independence, initiative, and the ability to develop original research ideas.

This balance between collaboration and independent scholarship makes the fellowship particularly attractive to researchers seeking to establish themselves as leaders in emerging interdisciplinary fields.

Why the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship Is Unique

Many postdoctoral opportunities are structured around a specific department, laboratory, or narrowly defined research area. The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship takes a broader approach by encouraging scholars to connect different academic perspectives through computational research and thinking.

Successful Fellows will have the opportunity to:

Conduct independent interdisciplinary research.

Work with faculty members from two Dartmouth College departments.

Develop relationships across multiple academic disciplines.

Explore innovative research questions.

Engage with computational concepts and methodologies.

Teach one seminar course each year.

Access financial support for research activities.

Participate in Dartmouth’s academic and intellectual community.

Build professional networks with scholars across different disciplines.

Develop new approaches that move beyond conventional academic paradigms.

The program recognizes that some of the most important contemporary research challenges require perspectives from multiple disciplines. By supporting scholars who can work across these boundaries, the Neukom Institute aims to encourage new forms of intellectual collaboration and discovery.

Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship Funding and Financial Benefits

One of the major advantages of the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship is the financial support provided to selected candidates.

For the 2027–2028 academic year, Neukom Fellows will receive a stipend of:

$70,000

In addition to the annual stipend, Fellows can access additional funding for important research-related needs.

Additional support may be available for:

Research equipment.

Academic travel.

Conference participation.

Research materials.

Other resources necessary to support the Fellow’s scholarly work.

This financial structure allows Fellows to focus significantly on their research and professional development while receiving institutional support for activities that contribute to their academic projects.

The fellowship appointment is initially structured as a two-year position, providing researchers with substantial time to develop and advance an interdisciplinary research agenda. Fellows may also have the option to request a third year, depending on program arrangements and individual circumstances.

Fellowship Structure and Academic Experience

The Neukom Fellows Program provides more than financial support. It offers a comprehensive academic environment designed to help emerging scholars expand their research networks and intellectual perspectives.

1. Two-Year Fellowship Appointment

Selected candidates will receive appointments lasting two years. This extended period gives Fellows the opportunity to undertake substantial research projects rather than focusing only on short-term academic activities.

The possibility of requesting a third year may provide additional flexibility for scholars whose research requires further development.

2. Mentorship Across Two Departments

One of the defining features of the program is interdisciplinary mentorship.

Neukom Fellows will be mentored by faculty members representing two different departments at Dartmouth College. This structure encourages Fellows to actively engage with different intellectual traditions and methodologies.

Working across departments can help researchers:

Develop broader perspectives.

Establish collaborations outside their original discipline.

Access different methodological approaches.

Test research ideas with diverse academic audiences.

Build interdisciplinary professional networks.

Develop innovative approaches to complex research questions.

3. Departmental Residence

While Fellows will work across two academic departments, they will take up residence in one department at Dartmouth College.

This arrangement provides Fellows with an academic home while simultaneously allowing them to maintain meaningful engagement with another disciplinary environment.

4. Teaching Opportunity

Neukom Fellows will teach one seminar course each year on a subject related to their interests and expertise.

This teaching component provides an opportunity for Fellows to:

Develop university-level teaching experience.

Design an original seminar.

Share their research interests with students.

Explore interdisciplinary topics in a classroom setting.

Strengthen their academic portfolio.

Gain valuable experience for future faculty and research positions.

5. Focus on Research

Apart from the teaching seminar, Fellows do not have additional duties specified by the program.

This allows successful candidates to devote substantial attention to their research projects, collaborations, and scholarly development.

Research Focus: Computation and Interdisciplinary Scholarship

A central requirement of the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship is a meaningful connection between an applicant’s research and the theme of computation.

Importantly, computation does not necessarily have to be interpreted narrowly.

According to the program description, computation may serve as:

A framing concept for intellectual exploration.

An explicit methodological component of research.

A tool for investigating complex questions.

A foundation for interdisciplinary collaboration.

A means of connecting different academic fields.

This broad approach makes the fellowship relevant to researchers working in a wide range of disciplines.

For example, applicants may explore intersections between computation and areas such as:

Computer science.

Artificial intelligence.

Data science.

Digital humanities.

Computational social science.

Mathematics.

Engineering.

Biology.

Environmental studies.

Economics.

Philosophy.

Linguistics.

Media studies.

Creative arts.

Public policy.

History.

Literature.

Psychology.

Physics.

Education.

Communication studies.

Cultural studies.

The specific research area does not need to belong exclusively to a computational discipline. However, applicants must clearly demonstrate how computation meaningfully intersects with their proposed work.

Eligibility Requirements for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027

The Neukom Institute welcomes applications from scholars across different academic backgrounds.

To be eligible for the fellowship, applicants should meet the following requirements.

Academic Qualification

Applicants must hold or expect to receive one of the following qualifications by September 2027:

PhD in any discipline.

Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA).

Master of Fine Arts (MFA), where applicable to the fellowship requirements.

The program specifically indicates that candidates may be expected to complete their doctoral qualification by September 2027.

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant for:

Recent PhD graduates.

Final-stage doctoral candidates.

Emerging scholars preparing to transition into postdoctoral research.

Researchers seeking an interdisciplinary academic environment after completing their doctoral studies.

Research Connection to Computation

Applicants must demonstrate research interests that strongly intersect with the broader theme of computation.

Candidates should clearly explain:

How computation relates to their research.

How computational ideas, methods, or frameworks contribute to their work.

Why interdisciplinary collaboration is important for their proposed research.

How the fellowship environment would strengthen their intellectual development.

Interest in Multidisciplinary Research

The Neukom Institute is specifically looking for scholars who are interested in working beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate:

Experience collaborating across disciplines.

Interest in multidisciplinary research.

Openness to different academic perspectives.

Ability to communicate with researchers from different fields.

Willingness to explore new methodologies and intellectual frameworks.

Independent Thinking and Initiative

Although collaboration is important, successful applicants must also demonstrate independence.

The program seeks candidates with evidence of:

Original thinking.

Research initiative.

Intellectual independence.

Leadership potential.

The ability to develop and pursue innovative research questions.

Ability to Think Beyond Traditional Paradigms

The fellowship strongly emphasizes innovative and unconventional thinking.

Applicants should demonstrate the capacity to:

Challenge traditional academic boundaries.

Connect ideas from different disciplines.

Develop creative research methodologies.

Explore emerging questions.

Think critically about established assumptions.

Build new intellectual frameworks.

Required Application Materials

Applicants for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program must prepare several important documents.

Candidates are encouraged to begin preparing their applications early, particularly because identifying and contacting potential Dartmouth faculty mentors may require significant research and communication.

The required application materials include the following.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a comprehensive academic curriculum vitae.

The CV should clearly highlight relevant experience, including:

Academic qualifications.

Research experience.

Publications.

Academic appointments.

Teaching experience.

Research collaborations.

Conferences and presentations.

Awards and honors.

Technical or methodological skills.

Interdisciplinary projects.

Candidates should ensure that their CV clearly demonstrates their academic development and capacity to contribute to an interdisciplinary research environment.

2. Publications List

Applicants are required to provide a list of publications.

This may include:

Journal articles.

Book chapters.

Books.

Conference papers.

Working papers.

Research reports.

Other relevant scholarly publications.

Where appropriate, candidates should clearly identify publications that demonstrate interdisciplinary or computational aspects of their work.

3. Statement of Research Interests

Applicants must submit a statement of research interests with a maximum length of two pages.

The statement should include a short description of the research the applicant would like to pursue as a Neukom Fellow.

A strong research statement should clearly address:

The central research question.

The importance of the proposed research.

The relationship between the project and computation.

The interdisciplinary nature of the work.

The proposed methodology.

Expected research outcomes.

Potential academic or societal contributions.

Why Dartmouth College provides an appropriate environment for the research.

Because the fellowship is highly interdisciplinary, applicants should ensure that their research statement is understandable to readers from multiple academic backgrounds.

4. Proposed Departments and Faculty Mentors

Applicants must describe:

Which Dartmouth College departments they are interested in working with.

Which Dartmouth faculty members they would like to collaborate with.

Why these academic connections are relevant to their proposed research.

How working across multiple departments would enhance their scholarship.

The Neukom Institute strongly encourages applicants to research Dartmouth’s departments and faculty listings when preparing this section.

Candidates are also strongly encouraged to identify potential faculty mentors and contact them while developing their applications.

This is an important part of the application strategy because demonstrating a clear understanding of Dartmouth’s academic environment can strengthen the connection between the applicant’s proposed research and the fellowship.

Applicants should therefore consider:

Identifying departments relevant to their research.

Reviewing faculty profiles.

Reading about faculty research interests.

Identifying potential interdisciplinary connections.

Contacting prospective mentors where appropriate.

Explaining clearly how those academic relationships could support the proposed research.

5. Three Referees and Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must provide details for three referees.

The letters of recommendation should speak directly to the aims and objectives of the fellowship.

Applicants will provide the referees’ email addresses through the application system. Referees will then receive an email with access to upload their letters directly.

Applicants will not have access to the submitted recommendation letters.

Candidates should carefully select referees who can discuss areas such as:

Research ability.

Academic independence.

Interdisciplinary experience.

Collaborative skills.

Intellectual creativity.

Leadership potential.

Ability to develop innovative research.

Suitability for a postdoctoral academic environment.

Although applicants are encouraged to have their applications completed by the main deadline, referees have an additional period to submit their letters.

6. Optional Writing Sample or Creative Work

Applicants may optionally submit one paper written in English.

The work may be:

Published; or

Unpublished.

Applicants whose work involves creative practice may submit comparable creative work instead.

A strong optional submission could provide additional evidence of:

Research quality.

Writing ability.

Originality.

Methodological expertise.

Interdisciplinary thinking.

7. Optional Teaching Statement

Applicants may also submit a teaching statement.

This can be particularly useful for candidates who want to demonstrate their readiness to teach the required annual seminar.

A teaching statement may discuss:

Teaching philosophy.

Previous teaching experience.

Approaches to interdisciplinary education.

Student engagement strategies.

Proposed seminar ideas.

8. Optional Cover Letter

Candidates may submit an optional cover letter.

A well-written cover letter could briefly summarize:

Academic background.

Research interests.

Interdisciplinary experience.

Connection to computation.

Motivation for applying.

Why the Neukom Fellowship is an appropriate next step.

Importance of Contacting Potential Dartmouth Mentors

One of the strongest recommendations provided by the program is that applicants should actively identify and contact prospective mentors at Dartmouth College.

Candidates are encouraged to begin making these academic connections while drafting their applications.

This approach can be valuable because it allows applicants to:

Better understand Dartmouth’s research environment.

Identify faculty whose expertise aligns with their work.

Develop stronger interdisciplinary research proposals.

Explain why specific departments are relevant.

Demonstrate genuine interest in collaboration.

Clarify how their proposed research could fit within Dartmouth’s academic community.

Applicants should approach potential mentors professionally and thoughtfully.

Before contacting a faculty member, candidates should:

Carefully review the faculty member’s research profile.

Understand their major research interests.

Identify a genuine connection with their own work.

Prepare a concise introduction.

Briefly explain the proposed research idea.

Explain why the faculty member’s expertise is relevant.

Avoid sending generic messages to multiple academics.

Early preparation is particularly important because identifying appropriate mentors and developing meaningful academic connections may take time.

Residence Requirement

Neukom Fellows are generally expected to be in residence at Dartmouth College.

The primary exception relates to travel associated with:

Research activities.

Academic conferences.

Other approved scholarly engagements.

Candidates should therefore be prepared to participate actively in Dartmouth’s academic community during the fellowship period.

Being in residence provides Fellows with opportunities to:

Meet regularly with faculty mentors.

Participate in academic discussions.

Collaborate with researchers.

Engage with students.

Attend seminars and events.

Build interdisciplinary networks.

Important Dates and Application Timeline

Applicants should pay close attention to the official competition schedule.

Application Site Opens

August 1, 2026

The online application system becomes available through Interfolio.

Application Deadline

December 1, 2026

Applicants should submit their complete applications by this date.

The program indicates that application review will begin on December 1, 2026.

Letters of Recommendation Deadline

December 8, 2026

Letters of recommendation must be submitted no later than this date.

Applicants should contact their referees well in advance to ensure they have sufficient time to prepare strong recommendation letters.

Fellowship Start Date

September 1, 2027

Successful Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows are expected to begin their appointments.

How to Apply for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027

The application process is completed online through the Interfolio application platform.

Interested candidates should follow these general steps.

Step 1: Review the Fellowship Requirements

Carefully read all eligibility criteria and application requirements before beginning the application.

Ensure that your academic qualifications and research interests align with the program.

Step 2: Develop Your Research Proposal

Prepare a strong research statement explaining:

Your proposed research.

Its interdisciplinary nature.

Its connection to computation.

Why the research is important.

How Dartmouth College would support the project.

Step 3: Identify Relevant Dartmouth Departments

Explore Dartmouth College’s academic departments and identify those connected to your research interests.

Consider how different departments could contribute complementary perspectives to your project.

Step 4: Identify Potential Faculty Mentors

Review Dartmouth faculty profiles and identify scholars whose research aligns with your proposed work.

The program strongly encourages applicants to explore potential academic connections while preparing their applications.

Step 5: Contact Potential Mentors

Where appropriate, reach out professionally to prospective mentors.

Explain your research interests and your interest in the interdisciplinary environment provided by the Neukom Fellowship.

Step 6: Prepare Your Supporting Documents

Compile the required materials, including:

Curriculum vitae.

Publications list.

Two-page research statement.

Description of relevant departments and faculty mentors.

Referee information.

Consider including optional materials where they strengthen your application.

Step 7: Notify Your Referees Early

Contact your three referees well before the deadline.

Provide them with:

Information about the fellowship.

Your research proposal.

Your CV.

Relevant application deadlines.

This will help them prepare letters that are specifically tailored to the aims of the Neukom Fellowship.

Step 8: Submit Your Application Online

Applications can be submitted through Interfolio once the application system opens.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day, as early submission provides time to address any technical issues.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship is designed for ambitious scholars working at the intersection of disciplines. Applicants should therefore ensure that their applications clearly communicate both academic depth and interdisciplinary vision.

Clearly Explain the Computational Connection

Do not assume that reviewers will automatically understand how your research relates to computation.

Clearly explain whether computation functions as:

A research methodology.

A theoretical framework.

A conceptual lens.

A practical tool.

A core component of your proposed project.

Demonstrate Genuine Interdisciplinarity

Simply mentioning multiple disciplines may not be sufficient.

Applicants should demonstrate how different fields will actively contribute to the proposed research.

Explain:

What each discipline contributes.

Why one discipline alone is insufficient.

How interdisciplinary collaboration will create new insights.

Balance Collaboration and Independence

The fellowship seeks candidates who can collaborate effectively while also pursuing independent scholarship.

Use examples from your academic experience to demonstrate both qualities.

Research Dartmouth Thoroughly

A strong application should demonstrate why Dartmouth College is particularly suitable for the proposed project.

Avoid generic statements.

Instead, identify:

Relevant departments.

Potential faculty collaborators.

Academic resources.

Interdisciplinary opportunities.

Select Referees Strategically

Choose referees who understand your research trajectory and can provide detailed examples of your abilities.

Ideally, recommendation letters should reinforce the themes emphasized throughout the application.

Begin Preparation Early

Because the application involves:

Developing a research proposal.

Identifying multiple departments.

Researching Dartmouth faculty.

Contacting potential mentors.

Coordinating recommendation letters.

Applicants should begin preparing well before the December deadline.

Diversity and Equal Opportunity

Dartmouth College states that it is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer with a strong commitment to diversity.

The institution encourages applications from a broad spectrum of individuals, including:

Women.

Persons of color.

Persons with disabilities.

Veterans.

Other legally protected groups.

This commitment reflects the Neukom Institute’s interest in building a diverse intellectual community that brings together different perspectives, experiences, academic backgrounds, and approaches to research.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship may be particularly suitable for scholars who answer yes to several of the following questions:

Are you completing a PhD or recently completed doctoral research?

Does your work intersect meaningfully with computation?

Does your research cross traditional academic boundaries?

Are you interested in working with scholars from multiple disciplines?

Do you have an innovative research idea that requires diverse academic perspectives?

Are you comfortable developing independent research projects?

Do you want postdoctoral teaching experience?

Are you interested in becoming part of an interdisciplinary academic community?

Can you identify Dartmouth faculty members whose expertise could strengthen your research?

If these characteristics align with your academic goals, the Neukom Fellowship could provide an important opportunity to develop an innovative research agenda.

Key Benefits of the Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship

Successful Fellows can benefit from a combination of financial support, research opportunities, mentorship, teaching experience, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Key benefits include:

A $70,000 stipend for 2027–2028.

A two-year fellowship appointment.

The possibility of requesting a third year.

Additional support for equipment.

Funding support for research travel.

Support for research materials.

Mentorship from faculty in two Dartmouth departments.

An opportunity to conduct interdisciplinary research.

Residence within Dartmouth College’s academic community.

The opportunity to teach one seminar course per year.

No additional duties beyond the specified fellowship responsibilities.

Opportunities to collaborate across traditional academic boundaries.

Access to an intellectually diverse research environment.

Professional development through research and teaching.

Opportunities to expand academic networks.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Competition 2027 is: December 1, 2026

Applicants should note that letters of recommendation are due no later than: December 8, 2026

The application portal opens on August 1, 2026, and selected Fellows are expected to begin their appointments on September 1, 2027.

APPLY HERE

How to Access the Official Application

Interested applicants should submit their applications online through the Interfolio application platform after the application portal opens.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program 2027.

Conclusion

The Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program 2027 represents an outstanding opportunity for emerging scholars whose work challenges traditional disciplinary boundaries and engages meaningfully with the broad field of computation. With a $70,000 stipend, additional research support, mentorship across two academic departments, teaching opportunities, and a two-year appointment with the potential for extension, the fellowship provides an exceptional environment for developing ambitious interdisciplinary research.

Candidates who can demonstrate a strong connection between their research and computation, an interest in multidisciplinary collaboration, and the ability to think independently and creatively are encouraged to consider applying.

Given the fellowship’s emphasis on innovative scholarship and interdisciplinary collaboration, a carefully developed application that clearly communicates both intellectual originality and the value of cross-disciplinary research could significantly strengthen a candidate’s prospects.

TITLE: DAAD University Summer Courses Scholarship 2027: Funded 4-Week German Language Programme With Accommodation, €475 Allowance and Travel Support

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are open for the DAAD University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates, an international scholarship programme that enables eligible university students to spend four intensive weeks studying German language and regional studies at participating higher education institutions in Germany.

The programme is administered by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) and funded by Germany’s Federal Foreign Office. Its central objective is to help international students deepen their knowledge of German as a general and technical language while expanding their understanding of German society, culture and regional studies.

For the upcoming cycle, applications are accepted from:

1 September 2026

until:

30 October 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time

The funded courses themselves take place between June and September 2027. Courses last four weeks, normally operate no more than five days per week and provide at least 25 teaching hours per week. They are taught entirely in German and must be attended physically in Germany; remote participation is not permitted.

The scholarship package includes:

Full coverage of the selected language course costs

Accommodation arranged by the course provider for the duration of the course

A one-time allowance of €475

A country-specific travel allowance for applicants from selected countries

Health insurance

Accident insurance

Personal liability insurance

The accommodation is normally provided in a single room, which may be located in a student residence, shared apartment or private household.

The programme is open across academic disciplines. Students do not need to be studying German, linguistics or another humanities subject. Eligible applicants may come from fields ranging from engineering and medicine to social sciences, law, arts, natural sciences and economics.

However, several important eligibility conditions apply. Applicants must be enrolled at an eligible university outside Germany, must remain enrolled throughout the scholarship period, must have sufficient German-language knowledge, and undergraduate students must have completed at least two years of university study by the beginning of the funded course.

Below is a detailed guide to the DAAD University Summer Courses Scholarship 2027, including funding, eligibility, German-language requirements, application documents, selection criteria, course choice and the application process.

About the DAAD University Summer Courses Programme

The programme is officially known as:

University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates

and is commonly associated with the German abbreviation HSK, referring to university summer language courses.

Unlike a full Bachelor’s, Master’s or doctoral scholarship, this programme funds a short, intensive study period in Germany.

Its purpose is specifically to help participants improve:

General German

Technical or subject-specific German

Knowledge of German society

Understanding of German culture

Knowledge of regional studies

Ability to communicate in academic and professional environments

The programme therefore combines language development with direct exposure to Germany.

Participants do not simply complete an online German course from their home countries. They travel to Germany and study in person at a participating course provider.

What Can Be Studied?

Funding is available for participation in:

German language courses

Cultural and regional studies courses

Technical and specialized language courses

The precise courses available vary according to the participating German universities and course providers.

DAAD publishes a dedicated course list containing information such as:

Host institution

Course dates

Required language level

Course focus

Subject specialization

Location

Applicants should review the course list before completing their scholarship application.

The scholarship application requires candidates to indicate three preferred courses, although these preferences do not guarantee placement in one of the three choices.

Courses Are Conducted Entirely in German

One of the most important conditions is that:

Courses are taught exclusively in German.

This is not a beginner programme designed for candidates with no knowledge of German.

Applicants need sufficient German-language ability to:

Follow lessons

Understand instructors

Participate in discussions

Complete group work

Engage meaningfully with course activities

Proof of German proficiency must therefore be submitted with the application.

In-Person Participation Is Mandatory

The programme takes place:

Exclusively in person in Germany.

DAAD explicitly states that:

Remote participation is not possible.

Applicants should therefore be ready to travel to Germany and remain there for the full duration of their assigned course.

This physical immersion is an important part of the programme because students develop their German not only through classroom study but also through everyday interaction and cultural exposure.

Duration of the DAAD Summer Course Scholarship

Each funded course lasts:

Four weeks

The programme normally involves:

Maximum five teaching days per week

At least 25 teaching hours per week

This means participants may complete at least approximately:

100 teaching hours

during the four-week period.

The scholarship cannot be extended beyond the approved course period.

When Do the Courses Take Place?

University Summer Courses funded under the programme take place between:

June and September

For applicants submitting during the September–October 2026 application window, the relevant courses are therefore expected to take place during summer 2027.

Exact dates depend on the course selected and the host institution.

Applicants should consult the DAAD course list because different universities may run their programmes at different times within this summer period.

Scholarship Benefits

The DAAD package contains several significant forms of financial and practical support.

1. Language Course Fees

DAAD covers the:

Cost of the funded language course.

This means scholarship recipients do not need to pay the normal tuition or participation fee for their assigned course.

2. Accommodation Is Provided

The course provider arranges accommodation for the scholarship holder during the programme.

Accommodation is provided in a:

Single room

and may be located in settings such as:

Student dormitory

Shared apartment

Private household

This is a particularly useful component of the scholarship because students do not need to independently find short-term accommodation in Germany for the four-week programme.

3. €475 One-Time Allowance

Scholarship recipients receive a:

One-time allowance of €475.

This allowance can help with personal costs associated with participation.

It is important to understand how it is paid.

DAAD does not transfer the €475 allowance abroad before the programme begins.

Instead, DAAD transfers the relevant funds to the course provider, which distributes the allowance to scholarship recipients in Germany.

4. Country-Specific Travel Allowance

Applicants from selected countries may also receive a:

Country-specific travel allowance.

The exact value is determined according to the applicant’s eligible country and DAAD’s applicable travel allowance schedule.

Applicants should not assume that every participant receives the same amount.

It is also important not to describe the programme as providing universal full airfare reimbursement. DAAD describes this component as a country-specific allowance for selected countries, rather than guaranteeing reimbursement of every travel expense.

As with the €475 allowance, applicable travel support is distributed through the course provider on site rather than transferred abroad before the scholarship begins.

5. Health Insurance

The scholarship includes:

Health insurance benefits

during the funded period.

This provides important protection for international students temporarily studying in Germany.

6. Accident Insurance

The scholarship also includes:

Accident insurance

for scholarship holders during the programme period.

7. Personal Liability Insurance

Participants additionally receive:

Personal liability insurance benefits.

Taken together, these insurance components provide a broader support package than a simple course-fee waiver.

Is This a Fully Funded Scholarship?

The programme provides substantial funding, but it is best described as a:

Funded short-term scholarship

rather than automatically calling it completely cost-free.

DAAD covers:

Course fees

Accommodation

€475 allowance

Insurance

Travel support for selected countries

However, applicants should still budget carefully for personal expenses that may exceed the provided allowance.

The programme description does not state that every possible expense—such as all meals, all local transport, visa expenses or every euro of international airfare—is universally reimbursed.

Who Can Apply?

The current DAAD call states that applications are open to:

Undergraduate students

Master’s students

from:

All academic disciplines.

Despite the programme title referring to “Foreign Students and Graduates,” the current live eligibility conditions require applicants to be enrolled at a university at the time of application and throughout the scholarship period.

Applicants should therefore follow the current country-specific DAAD scholarship database requirements rather than assuming that anyone who has already graduated and is no longer enrolled automatically qualifies.

Undergraduate Eligibility

Bachelor’s or equivalent undergraduate students can apply.

However, they must have completed at least:

Two academic years of university study

by the time the funded course begins.

For example, a student who applies in October 2026 may qualify if they will have completed two full academic years by summer 2027.

Master’s Students

Students enrolled in Master’s programmes may also apply.

The programme is not restricted to particular Master’s disciplines.

Candidates may come from subjects including:

International relations

Engineering

Computer science

Economics

Law

Medicine

Languages

Sociology

Political science

Natural sciences

Arts

Business

Agriculture

Environmental sciences

Other recognised fields

The central requirement is not the applicant’s major but their overall eligibility and motivation for improving their German.

Applicants Must Be Enrolled Outside Germany

Applicants must be enrolled at a university in one of DAAD’s eligible programme countries:

Outside Germany

both:

At the time of application

During the entire scholarship period

This programme is therefore not designed to fund students who are already studying at a German university as their normal degree institution.

Minimum Age

Scholarship holders must be:

At least 18 years old

when the language course begins.

The published call does not state a general maximum age limit.

Scholarship Can Only Be Used Once

DAAD states that funding under this programme can be claimed:

Only once.

Previous recipients of the same University Summer Courses scholarship should therefore check their eligibility carefully before attempting another application.

German-Language Requirement

Applicants must demonstrate that they can:

Follow lectures in German

Participate in German-language group work

German knowledge must be documented at the time of application.

The precise minimum level may depend on the country-specific version of the scholarship call. DAAD’s current country-specific database results show different thresholds in some cases, so applicants should select their own country in the scholarship database and follow the requirement displayed for them rather than relying on a universal minimum level.

Accepted German-Language Certificates

DAAD lists accepted certificates including:

onSET-Deutsch

TestDaF

Goethe-Institut Zertifikat

DSD

DSH

telc Deutsch

ÖSD-Zertifikat

Baccalaureate certificate for specialized language courses where applicable

Some country-specific calls may also accept the DAAD Language Certificate German under specified conditions.

How Recent Must the Language Certificate Be?

Generally, the German certificate must not be older than:

One year

at the time of application.

This rule also applies to DSH.

However, certificates demonstrating at least:

B2, or

TDN4 in all TestDaF components

may be up to:

Two years old.

Applicants should therefore check the date of their language test well before beginning the application.

Academic Discipline Requirements

One major advantage of the programme is that it is not restricted to German Studies students.

The DAAD scholarship database lists eligible academic fields across the full disciplinary spectrum, including:

Languages and Cultural Studies

Law

Economics

Social Sciences

Mathematics

Natural Sciences

Human Medicine

Veterinary Medicine

Agriculture

Forestry

Nutrition

Ecology

Engineering

Art

Music

Sport

This makes the scholarship potentially valuable to students who need German for:

Future postgraduate study

Research

Professional careers

International cooperation

Academic exchange

Technical work

Selection Process

Applications are reviewed by a:

Selection committee

rather than being awarded automatically to all eligible candidates.

Two principal selection considerations are highlighted by DAAD:

Previous academic achievements

A convincing motivation letter explaining the chosen programme and future academic plans

Meeting the minimum eligibility conditions therefore does not guarantee selection.

Academic Achievement

Applicants should demonstrate solid performance in their university studies.

DAAD requests academic records covering recent university examinations.

The selection committee can use these records to assess:

Academic consistency

Performance

Study progress

Preparation for the scholarship

Applicants should provide complete records rather than selecting only their strongest grades.

Motivation Letter

A convincing:

Letter of motivation

is one of the central selection criteria.

The motivation letter should explain why the applicant wants to improve their German and how the summer course relates to their:

Academic degree

Future postgraduate plans

Research interests

Professional plans

Engagement with Germany

Academic development

A generic statement such as “I like German culture and want to improve my language skills” is unlikely to communicate the same level of purpose as a detailed explanation connecting German proficiency with future academic objectives.

Application Documents

A complete application requires several documents.

1. Online Application Form

Applicants must complete the official:

DAAD online application form.

The application is submitted through the DAAD portal.

2. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants need a:

Complete CV in tabular form.

The general DAAD call requests the CV in German.

Some country-specific rules may provide limited language exceptions, so applicants should follow the instructions displayed for their own country.

3. Motivation Letter

Applicants must provide a:

Letter of motivation

normally in German.

The letter should present a clear connection among:

Current studies

German-language development

Course choice

Future academic plans

4. University Transcripts

Applicants need transcripts covering:

University examinations taken during the previous two years

including individual grades.

If the documents are not already in German or English, a:

German translation, or

English translation

must be included.

If a student has been enrolled for less than two years and therefore cannot provide two full years of records, they should provide evidence of academic achievements from their current period of study.

5. School-Leaving Certificate for Undergraduate Applicants

Bachelor’s-level applicants must also submit their:

School-leaving certificate with grades.

A German or English translation should be included where necessary.

6. Previous Degree for Postgraduate Students

Applicants already studying at postgraduate level should provide their:

Most recent university degree certificate

including final grades.

7. German-Language Certificate

Applicants must upload proof of their German-language proficiency.

If necessary, the certificate should be accompanied by a:

German translation, or

English translation

as appropriate.

8. Additional Supporting Documents

Candidates may also upload other documents they consider relevant.

Examples provided by DAAD include:

Internship certificates

Employment certificates

Applicants should use this option strategically.

Additional material should strengthen the case for the scholarship rather than overwhelm the application with unrelated documents.

Do Documents Need to Be Certified?

At the initial application stage, DAAD states that:

Certificates

Transcripts

Attestations

Translations

may be submitted in:

Uncertified form.

However, DAAD reserves the right to request certified copies later.

Applicants should therefore retain access to official originals.

Incomplete Applications Are Not Considered

DAAD makes clear that all required documents must be uploaded by the deadline.

Incomplete applications:

Cannot be considered in the further selection process.

Candidates should therefore avoid submitting at the last moment.

Choosing Three Preferred Courses

The application asks candidates to identify:

Three course preferences.

DAAD attempts to take these choices into consideration when placing scholarship holders.

However, capacity is limited.

DAAD reserves the right to place a successful scholarship recipient in:

A different course

if the preferred courses are full or placement requirements make another course more appropriate.

Course Preferences Cannot Be Changed Later

Once the application has been received:

Course preferences cannot be changed.

Applicants also cannot simply switch to another course after receiving their placement.

Candidates should therefore research their three selections carefully before submitting.

Consider:

Course level

Academic relevance

Step-by-Step Application Process

Go to the DAAD scholarship database and select:

Your country

Your student status

Step 9: Submit Before October 30

How to Write a Strong Motivation Letter

4. Demonstrate Existing Commitment to German

TITLE: 2027 Switzer Fellowship in the USA | $18,000 Award for Environmental Leaders

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications for the 2027 Switzer Fellowship will open in September 2026, offering graduate students in the United States and U.S. territories an opportunity to receive an $18,000 unrestricted cash award, leadership training, career support, and access to a professional network of more than 800 environmental leaders.

The fellowship is designed for graduate students whose academic and career goals focus on environmental improvement and who demonstrate leadership, applied problem-solving, interdisciplinary collaboration, and a commitment to advancing social equity through environmental work.

About the Switzer Fellowship

The Switzer Fellowship is a one-year graduate fellowship supporting emerging and established environmental leaders across a broad range of disciplines.

Switzer Fellows work in areas including:

Environmental science

Public policy

Environmental justice

Public health

Economics

Advocacy

Planning

Business

Law

Research and academia

The fellowship welcomes applicants from diverse academic, professional, social and economic backgrounds, particularly those who are committed to interdisciplinary approaches, practical environmental solutions, collaborative leadership and social equity.

For the 2027 fellowship cycle, the programme has expanded nationwide and is no longer restricted to applicants studying in New England or California.

What Does the Switzer Fellowship Provide?

Selected fellows receive an $18,000 unrestricted cash award, paid in two installments in June and January.

The fellowship also provides opportunities for:

1. Leadership Development

Fellows participate in two multi-day retreats focused on cohort building, networking, equity-centered leadership and professional skills development.

2. Career Coaching

Switzer Fellows have access to career coaching and leadership guidance during their fellowship year and beyond. The Foundation helps fellows identify leadership opportunities and establish connections throughout the Switzer Network.

3. Switzer Network Membership

One of the major advantages of the fellowship is lifelong access to the Switzer Network, a community of more than 800 fellows selected since 1986.

Network activities include:

Professional networking events

Job and information sharing

Webinars and training

Social gatherings

Professional development opportunities

Additional grant opportunities

4. Future Grant Opportunities

After completing the fellowship year, fellows can access additional grant programmes designed to strengthen leadership and professional development, including leadership and professional development grants.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must meet the Switzer Fellowship’s eligibility requirements.

To qualify, applicants must:

Be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, DACA recipient, refugee or asylee according to the specified U.S. Department of Homeland Security definition.

Be enrolled in an accredited graduate institution in the United States or U.S. territories.

Not be enrolled in an online programme.

Plan to remain enrolled throughout the entire 2027–2028 academic year.

Have strong academic qualifications and academic and career goals focused on environmental improvement.

Requirements for Master’s Students

Master’s degree candidates, including J.D. students, must have completed at least one semester or quarter of coursework when applying and must be pursuing the Master’s degree as their terminal degree.

Students planning to continue into a Ph.D. are advised to wait and apply once they are enrolled in their doctoral programme. Students entering a one-year Master’s programme may apply before enrollment, but they must have been formally accepted before they can be interviewed.

Requirements for Ph.D. Students

Ph.D. candidates must have completed their qualifying examinations by the time of application.

Mid-Career Applicants

Mid-career students are encouraged to apply. They must demonstrate how their academic programme will strengthen their effectiveness as environmental leaders.

Who Is Especially Encouraged to Apply?

The Switzer Foundation particularly encourages applications from:

Black students

Indigenous students

Students of color

First-generation college students

Individuals from groups traditionally underrepresented in environmental graduate programmes

Students from a wide range of universities, including state universities

How Are Fellows Selected?

The Foundation selects approximately 20 fellows each year from hundreds of applicants.

Applications are assessed according to several criteria, including:

Environmental commitment

Applied focus

Innovative problem-solving

Leadership potential

Collaboration and engagement

Social equity awareness and experience

Communication skills

Successful candidates should therefore demonstrate more than strong academic performance. Their applications should clearly show how their environmental work addresses practical problems and affects human communities.

Ph.D. applicants are expected to have a clearly defined research focus and explain how their academic goals can contribute to positive change in applied environmental problems.

Application Review Process

After an initial eligibility review, applications go through three rounds of review by Switzer Fellowship alumni.

The alumni reviewers are selected to provide broad representation across areas such as:

Race

Gender

Educational background

Degree programme

Professional sector

Fellowship cohort

Geography

Selected applicants participate in a virtual panel interview in May with Switzer Foundation fellows and representatives. Award decisions are communicated in writing within two weeks following the interviews.

2027 Application Timeline

The application timeline provided by the Switzer Foundation is:

Applications open: September 2026

Interviews: Early May

Award notifications: June

Application deadline: The source currently states that applications will begin being accepted in September 2026 but does not provide a specific closing date. Applicants should therefore check the official application page once the 2027 application cycle opens.

Fellowship Responsibilities

Being selected as a Switzer Fellow comes with participation requirements.

Attend Two Retreats

All fellows must attend two multi-day, in-person retreats held in September and April during the fellowship year.

The retreats focus on:

Cohort building

Networking

Equity-centered leadership

Skills development

Participate in the Switzer Network

Fellows are expected to remain active members of the Switzer Network during and after their fellowship year.

Participation can include:

Attending or hosting networking events

Participating in network discussions

Coaching earlier-career fellows

Serving on the Fellows Advisory Committee

Participating in the selection of future fellows

Submit a Fellowship Report

Fellows must submit a brief written report at the conclusion of their fellowship year. An optional interim report may also be requested in January.

How Can the $18,000 Award Be Used?

The unrestricted fellowship award may be used for one or more of the following:

Tuition

Matriculation and university fees

Living expenses

Education-related expenses

Research-related expenses

If the fellowship funds are not used for these purposes, they may be considered taxable income and the fellow may be responsible for applicable income tax.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Switzer Fellowship could be particularly relevant for graduate students who are developing solutions to environmental challenges and want to connect their work to broader social outcomes.

Potential applicants may include students working on environmental problems related to:

Climate and environmental change

Environmental justice

Public health

Environmental policy

Sustainable development

Natural resources

Community resilience

Environmental planning

Environmental science and research

However, the fellowship is not restricted to a single academic discipline. The Foundation’s existing fellows work across science, policy, health, economics, advocacy, planning, business, law and other fields.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

If you intend to apply when applications open in September 2026, consider preparing early.

1. Clearly Explain Your Environmental Focus

Your application should make it easy for reviewers to understand the environmental problem you are addressing and why it matters.

2. Demonstrate Practical Impact

The Foundation places emphasis on applied environmental problem-solving. Explain how your research, studies or professional work can contribute to real-world solutions.

3. Highlight Leadership

Provide concrete examples showing how you have taken initiative, influenced others, collaborated with stakeholders or contributed to environmental change.

4. Connect Environment and Social Equity

Social equity is an important part of the Switzer Fellowship’s selection criteria. Applicants should clearly demonstrate how their environmental work affects people and communities.

5. Show Collaboration

The selection criteria include collaboration and engagement, so demonstrate your ability to work across disciplines, communities or professional sectors.

Important Exclusions

Employees and trustees of the Robert and Patricia Switzer Foundation, as well as their family members, are not eligible to apply.

The Foundation states that it does not discriminate in selection on the basis of race, color, gender, gender expression, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, or national or ethnic origin.

How to Apply

Applications for the 2027 Switzer Fellowship are scheduled to open in September 2026.

Applicants should use the official How to Apply information provided by the Switzer Network when the application window opens.

Applicants can also explore the Switzer Network and learn more about previous fellows to understand the range of environmental and social-impact work represented within the fellowship community.

Conclusion

The 2027 Switzer Fellowship provides an opportunity for graduate students in the United States and U.S. territories to develop as environmental leaders while receiving an $18,000 award, leadership development, career coaching, professional networking and access to a long-term community of environmental change-makers.

With only about 20 fellows selected each year, applicants should prepare carefully and demonstrate a clear connection between their academic or professional work, practical environmental problem-solving, leadership and social equity.

Applications are expected to open in September 2026, making this an opportunity prospective applicants should begin preparing for now.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

TITLE: Research

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Physics Department strives to be at the forefront of many areas where new physics can be found. Consequently, we work on problems where extreme conditions may reveal new behavior. We study the largest things in the universe: clusters of galaxies or even the entire universe itself. We study the smallest things in the universe: elementary particles or even the strings that may be the substructure of these particles. We study the hottest things in the universe: collisions of nuclei at relativistic velocities that make droplets of matter hotter than anything since the Big Bang. We study the coldest things in the universe: laser-cooled atoms so cold that their wave functions overlap resulting in a macroscopic collective state–the Bose-Einstein condensate. While we often study the simplest things, such as individual atoms, we study the most complicated things too: unusual materials like high temperature superconductors and those that are important in biology. By pushing the limits, we have the chance to observe new general principles and to test theories of the structure and behavior of matter and energy.
The links at the left will lead you to overviews of the research done in the Physics Department, organized in four broad areas, as well as to the web pages of the faculty working in each area.
