TITLE: Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027: Fully Funded Master’s Fellowship in China for International Students

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for outstanding students from China and around the world to pursue an interdisciplinary graduate education focused on China at Peking University in Beijing, China.

Through the Yenching Academy, approximately 120 new students are enrolled annually, bringing together students from the Chinese Mainland and international students to study, live and learn in a highly diverse academic environment. International students make up approximately 75% of the student body, creating an environment in which scholars from different countries and academic backgrounds can engage with one another and develop a deeper understanding of China.

The programme is designed for academically outstanding students who have a strong interest in the interdisciplinary study of China and who can demonstrate extracurricular achievements, community engagement, social responsibility and leadership potential.

One of the most attractive aspects of the Yenching Academy opportunity is its generous fellowship package. Selected Yenching Scholars receive support covering tuition fees, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip travel fare and field study costs.

For the 2027 cohort, applications from international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions open on September 1, 2026, with the application deadline set for November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

About the Yenching Academy of Peking University

The Yenching Academy is a graduate-level academic programme at Peking University, one of China’s leading universities.

The Academy brings together students from China and other parts of the world with the aim of encouraging interdisciplinary learning and deeper engagement with China.

Rather than restricting students to a single narrow academic discipline, the programme emphasizes an interdisciplinary approach to the study of China. This allows scholars with different academic backgrounds and interests to explore China from multiple perspectives.

The Academy’s international composition is also an important part of the programme. Approximately 120 new students are admitted each year, with international students accounting for roughly 75 percent of the student body.

This creates opportunities for students to develop international networks while studying alongside peers from different countries, academic disciplines and cultural backgrounds.

What Is the Yenching Academy Scholarship?

The Yenching Academy provides a generous fellowship to all scholars admitted to the programme.

The fellowship is intended to provide comprehensive financial support for selected students during their studies.

The fellowship includes:

Tuition fees

Accommodation

Monthly stipend

One round-trip travel fare

Field study costs

This combination of financial benefits makes the Yenching Academy particularly attractive to students seeking an internationally oriented graduate education in China with substantial financial support.

Yenching Academy 2027 Application Timeline

Applications for the 2027 cohort from international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions open on:

September 1, 2026

The application deadline is:

November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time

Applicants should pay close attention to the time zone because the deadline is specified according to Beijing time, rather than the applicant’s local time.

Students should also begin preparing their application materials well before the deadline because the application requires several documents, including academic records, recommendation letters, a personal statement, a research-interest statement and proof of English proficiency where applicable.

Who Can Apply for the Yenching Academy?

The Yenching Academy welcomes applications from both Chinese Mainland candidates and students from abroad, although the application procedures differ depending on the applicant’s location and status.

The Academy generally expects applicants to demonstrate strong academic performance, intellectual curiosity, interest in China and evidence of leadership and community engagement.

Applicants should meet the following core qualifications.

1. Bachelor’s Degree or Current Bachelor’s Student

Applicants must either:

Hold a minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in any field; or

Be currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s programme and expect to receive their diploma by August of the intended enrollment year.

This means that students who have not yet completed their undergraduate education may still be eligible if they are expected to graduate by the specified date.

The Academy does not restrict the Bachelor’s degree to a particular discipline. Applicants from different academic backgrounds can therefore be considered as long as they satisfy the other requirements.

2. Outstanding Academic Record

Applicants are expected to have an outstanding academic record.

Academic excellence is an important part of the Yenching Academy selection process because the programme is designed for high-achieving students capable of engaging with rigorous graduate-level interdisciplinary study.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their transcripts accurately demonstrate their academic strengths.

3. Strong Interest in the Interdisciplinary Study of China

A key requirement is a strong interest in interdisciplinary study of China.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate why they want to study China and how their academic, professional, research or personal interests connect with the interdisciplinary focus of the Academy.

A generic interest in studying abroad may not adequately demonstrate this requirement. Applicants should instead develop a clear explanation of the questions, issues or areas concerning China that they want to explore.

4. Extracurricular Achievement and Community Engagement

The Academy also looks for applicants with a record of:

Extracurricular achievement

Community engagement

Social responsibility

Leadership potential

This means that academic performance is not the only consideration.

Applicants should demonstrate how they have contributed beyond the classroom, whether through community initiatives, student organizations, volunteering, professional activities, social-impact projects, leadership roles or other meaningful engagements.

The strongest applications should show evidence of initiative and a willingness to contribute to communities beyond one’s immediate academic environment.

5. English Proficiency

Applicants must demonstrate sufficient English proficiency unless they fall within an exemption category specified by the Academy.

The required minimum scores include:

IELTS Academic: Overall 7.0

TOEFL iBT: Overall 100

Cambridge English Scale (Advanced): Overall 185

CET 6: Overall 600

TEM 4: Pass level of “良好” or above

Applicants should carefully determine which English-language qualification applies to them and ensure that their test results meet the minimum requirement.

English Language Test Exemptions

Not every applicant is required to submit an English proficiency test report.

International applicants whose native language is English do not need to provide an English proficiency test report.

Applicants who have graduated from an English-taught degree programme at undergraduate level or above are also exempt from providing an English proficiency test report.

However, there is an important exception for applicants from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions.

Applicants from these regions must provide an English proficiency test report even if they have attended or graduated from an English-taught degree programme.

Without an English proficiency test report, such candidates will need to take English as a Second Language after enrolling at Peking University.

For applicants from the Chinese Mainland, an English proficiency test report is a compulsory application material.

Validity Period for English Tests

The Yenching Academy specifies that English proficiency tests must have been taken after September 1, 2025.

Applicants should therefore check the date of their examination before submitting their application.

The Academy also specifies that certain alternative or modified test formats are not accepted.

The following are not accepted:

TOEFL MyBest Scores

TOEFL iBT Home Edition

IELTS Indicator

IELTS Online

IELTS One Skill Retake

Applicants should make sure that their English test meets the Academy’s accepted format and validity requirements.

How English Test Scores Must Be Submitted

For IELTS, TOEFL and Cambridge English tests, applicants cannot simply rely on uploading a copy of their score report where the Academy requires scores to be sent directly.

The Academy states that these scores must be sent directly by the relevant testing organizations.

When registering for the examination, applicants should select Yenching Academy of Peking University as the designated recipient of their scores.

For TOEFL applicants, the institution code is:

C488

Applicants should arrange this early enough to ensure that their scores reach the Academy before the application deadline.

Application Materials

Applicants are required to submit several materials through the Yenching Academy’s online application portal.

The application must be completed in English.

Required materials include:

Completed online application form

Personal statement of no more than 750 words

Statement of Research Interest of no more than 1,500 words, excluding citations

Curriculum Vitae

Official transcript or transcripts

Diploma or Certificate of Enrollment

Two academic letters of recommendation

Required English proficiency evidence, where applicable

Each component serves a different purpose in demonstrating the applicant’s academic preparation, research interests, leadership potential and suitability for the programme.

Personal Statement

The personal statement must be 750 words or less.

This is an opportunity for applicants to present their background and explain why they are suitable candidates for the Yenching Academy.

Rather than simply repeating information already available in the CV, applicants should use the statement to provide context around their academic journey, interests, achievements and motivation.

A strong personal statement should help admissions reviewers understand the applicant as a person and explain why the Yenching Academy is an appropriate next step.

Statement of Research Interest

Applicants must also submit a Statement of Research Interest of no more than 1,500 words, excluding citations.

This is particularly important because the Yenching Academy emphasizes interdisciplinary study of China.

Applicants should use the statement to explain the research questions or areas they are interested in exploring and demonstrate their intellectual engagement with issues concerning China.

The statement should be focused, coherent and academically grounded.

Applicants should avoid treating the statement as a generic essay about why they want to study in China. Instead, they should clearly communicate their research interests and explain the issues they would like to investigate.

Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a Curriculum Vitae.

The CV should provide a clear overview of the applicant’s:

Academic background

Research experience

Professional experience, where applicable

Leadership activities

Extracurricular achievements

Community engagement

Relevant projects

Awards and accomplishments

Because the Academy specifically values extracurricular achievement, social responsibility and leadership potential, applicants should ensure that their CV captures relevant activities beyond academic qualifications.

Academic Transcripts

Applicants must provide official transcript(s).

The transcripts allow the Academy to assess the applicant’s academic record and verify educational performance.

Applicants should ensure that their academic documents are official and complete and that any required translation or certification requirements are satisfied where applicable.

Diploma or Certificate of Enrollment

Applicants must also submit the appropriate educational-status documentation.

This may be:

A diploma demonstrating completion of a Bachelor’s degree; or

A Certificate of Enrollment for applicants who are still completing their Bachelor’s programme.

Students who are currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s programme must expect to receive their diploma by August of the intended enrollment year.

Academic Recommendation Letters

Applicants must provide two academic letters of recommendation.

The recommendation letters may be written in:

Chinese; or

English.

However, the Academy imposes specific requirements concerning who may write these letters.

Peking University will only accept recommendation letters written by:

Full professors; or

Associate professors; or

Individuals holding equivalent academic titles.

In addition, the recommendation letters must be submitted by professors in the applicant’s intended field of study.

Applicants should therefore select their referees carefully.

A recommendation from an individual who does not meet the specified academic rank or who is not connected to the applicant’s intended field may not satisfy the Academy’s requirements.

International Student Eligibility

For the 2027 cohort, international applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport.

This is an important nationality requirement for candidates applying through the international admissions route.

Former citizens of the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan who have emigrated to another country and are applying to Peking University as international students have additional documentation requirements.

They must provide:

Valid passport or citizenship documents dating from before April 30, 2021; and

Proof of cancellation of Chinese nationality.

Applicants with complicated nationality or citizenship histories should carefully consult Peking University’s international student admissions information before submitting an application.

Applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan

Candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions have a separate application process.

Applications for the 2027 Yenching Scholars cohort open on:

September 1, 2026

The deadline is:

November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time

Candidates from these regions must apply through the Yenching Academy application portal and also complete a supplementary application through the Peking University Graduate Admissions website.

Additional information is provided through Peking University’s admissions resources.

Applicants from the Chinese Mainland

The application process for candidates from the Chinese Mainland is handled through the relevant Peking University graduate admissions system.

The Academy directs Mainland Chinese candidates to the Graduate School of Peking University for additional information about the application process.

Applicants from the Chinese Mainland should therefore carefully follow the specific admissions instructions applicable to their applicant category rather than assuming that the international application procedure applies to them.

Learn More HERE

Partner University Applicants

Students and alumni of Yenching Academy’s Partner Universities must complete their home university’s internal pre-selection process before submitting an application to the Yenching Academy.

This is a particularly important requirement for candidates associated with partner institutions.

Applicants should therefore determine whether their university is included among the Academy’s partner universities and, if it is, find out whether their university has an internal nomination or pre-selection process.

Waiting until the Yenching Academy application deadline may be too late if the applicant’s university has an earlier internal deadline.

Application Portal

Candidates can submit their applications through the Yenching Academy’s online application portal.

Applicants are required to create an account before accessing additional application information and submitting their materials.

The application portal is also where applicants can find further instructions concerning the admissions process.

Applicants should make sure that all information entered into the portal is accurate and consistent with the supporting documents they submit.

APPLY HERE

Important Rule Regarding Other Degree Programmes

Peking University does not allow students to be enrolled in another degree programme while studying at the university.

Applicants who are currently enrolled in another degree programme should therefore consider this rule when planning their studies.

They should review their existing academic commitments and ensure that they understand Peking University’s requirements before accepting an offer.

Fellowship Benefits

The Yenching Academy provides a comprehensive fellowship package to all scholars.

The fellowship includes five major forms of support.

Tuition Fees

Selected scholars receive coverage of tuition fees.

This removes one of the major financial costs associated with pursuing graduate education.

Accommodation

The fellowship also provides accommodation.

This is particularly valuable for international students relocating to Beijing because housing can represent a significant component of the overall cost of studying abroad.

Monthly Stipend

Scholars receive a monthly stipend.

The supplied programme information does not specify the exact amount of the monthly stipend, so applicants should consult the admissions portal or official programme information for the current figure.

One Round-Trip Travel Fare

The fellowship includes one round-trip travel fare.

This provides travel support for the scholar and can help reduce the cost associated with travelling to and from Beijing.

Field Study Costs

The fellowship also covers field study costs.

This component is particularly relevant to the Academy’s interdisciplinary approach, as field-based academic experiences can provide scholars with opportunities to deepen their understanding of China beyond classroom-based study.

Why Study at Yenching Academy?

The Yenching Academy offers more than financial support.

Its structure is particularly suited to students who want to develop a deeper understanding of China through interdisciplinary academic inquiry.

Several characteristics make the programme distinctive.

Interdisciplinary Academic Environment

Students can explore China through different academic perspectives rather than being limited to a single disciplinary framework.

This can be particularly beneficial for students interested in complex issues that cross traditional academic boundaries.

International Community

With international students making up approximately 75 percent of the student body, the Academy provides a highly international learning environment.

Students can interact with peers from different countries and backgrounds while developing a deeper understanding of China.

Leadership Development

The Academy looks for applicants with leadership potential, community engagement and social responsibility.

This creates an environment where academic development can be combined with broader leadership and social-impact interests.

Research Opportunities

The requirement for a Statement of Research Interest highlights the programme’s emphasis on intellectual inquiry.

Students with clearly developed research interests can use the programme to investigate questions relating to China from an interdisciplinary perspective.

Field Study

The fellowship’s inclusion of field study costs provides scholars with financial support for field-based academic activities.

Such experiences can complement classroom learning and help scholars connect academic concepts with real-world contexts.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Because the Yenching Academy attracts high-achieving candidates, applicants should begin preparing well before the deadline.

Start With Eligibility

First, confirm that you meet the fundamental requirements.

Check:

Your Bachelor’s degree status

Your expected graduation date if you are still an undergraduate

Your academic record

Your interest in interdisciplinary study of China

Your extracurricular and leadership experience

Your English proficiency

Your nationality and applicant category

Develop a Clear Research Interest

The Statement of Research Interest is one of the most important components of the application.

Applicants should spend sufficient time identifying a focused area of inquiry.

Rather than selecting an extremely broad topic, consider a specific question or problem related to China that can be examined through an interdisciplinary perspective.

Choose Recommendation Writers Early

Because recommendation letters must come from full professors, associate professors or equivalent academic titles and should be from professors in the intended field of study, applicants should approach potential referees early.

This is especially important because academic referees may have multiple commitments and may require considerable time to prepare a thoughtful recommendation.

Prepare English Test Scores Early

Applicants who require an English proficiency test should avoid waiting until immediately before the deadline.

The Academy requires eligible English tests to have been taken after September 1, 2025 and does not accept several alternative test formats.

Applicants should also allow sufficient time for scores to be sent directly from the testing organization to Yenching Academy.

Review Every Document

Before submitting the application, applicants should ensure that:

Names are consistent across documents.

Academic dates are accurate.

Transcripts are official.

Recommendation letters meet the academic-rank requirements.

The personal statement does not exceed 750 words.

The Statement of Research Interest does not exceed 1,500 words excluding citations.

The CV is complete and professionally presented.

English test scores meet the required minimum where applicable.

Required documents have been submitted in the correct format.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027 Yenching Scholars cohort for international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions is:

November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

Applications open on September 1, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their applications because the process involves multiple supporting documents and, for some candidates, university-level pre-selection procedures.

Important Application Considerations

Applicants should keep several requirements in mind when preparing their applications.

First, students and alumni of Partner Universities must complete their university’s internal pre-selection process before submitting their Yenching Academy application.

Second, applicants who need English proficiency tests must ensure that their test was taken after September 1, 2025 and that the examination format is accepted.

Third, international candidates must satisfy the nationality requirements for international admission.

Finally, applicants should carefully follow any additional instructions displayed in the admissions portal after creating an account.

What is the English requirement?

Accepted minimum scores include IELTS Academic 7.0, TOEFL iBT 100, Cambridge English Scale 185, CET 6 600 or TEM 4 at the required “良好” or above level.

Are English tests required for everyone?

No. International applicants whose native language is English or who have graduated from an English-taught degree programme at undergraduate level or above do not need to provide an English proficiency test report. However, applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan must provide one even if their degree was taught in English.

How many recommendation letters are required?

Two academic recommendation letters are required.

Who can write the recommendation letters?

Letters must be written by full professors, associate professors or individuals with equivalent academic titles, and they must come from professors in the applicant’s intended field of study.

How much is the monthly stipend?

The supplied programme information confirms that a monthly stipend is provided but does not specify the amount. Applicants should check the admissions portal for the current stipend amount.

Does the fellowship cover tuition?

Yes. Tuition fees are included in the fellowship.

Does the fellowship cover accommodation?

Yes. Accommodation is included.

Does the fellowship include travel support?

Yes. The fellowship includes one round-trip travel fare.

Does it cover field study?

Yes. Field study costs are included in the fellowship.

When does the 2027 application open?

Applications for international candidates and candidates from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan open on September 1, 2026.

When is the application deadline?

The deadline is November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

Can students from Partner Universities apply directly?

Students and alumni of Partner Universities must first complete their home university’s internal pre-selection process before submitting the Yenching Academy application.

Can international students who were previously Chinese citizens apply?

Potentially, but additional documentation requirements apply. Former citizens of the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan who have emigrated to other countries must provide qualifying passport or citizenship documents dating from before April 30, 2021, together with proof of cancellation of Chinese nationality.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027.

Conclusion

The Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027 is a highly attractive opportunity for academically outstanding students who want to pursue an interdisciplinary graduate education focused on China in an international academic environment.

The programme combines rigorous academic study with an internationally diverse student community and places considerable emphasis on intellectual curiosity, leadership potential, community engagement and social responsibility.

For successful scholars, the financial package is particularly significant. The Yenching Academy provides tuition fees, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip travel fare and field study costs, allowing selected students to undertake their studies with substantial financial support.

Applicants should nevertheless recognize that this is a competitive programme. A strong application should go beyond meeting the minimum eligibility requirements. Candidates should present an outstanding academic record, demonstrate meaningful extracurricular and community engagement, articulate a convincing interest in the interdisciplinary study of China and submit carefully prepared application materials.

For international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions, applications for the 2027 cohort open on September 1, 2026, and the application deadline is November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

Prospective applicants should begin preparing their transcripts, CV, personal statement, research-interest statement, recommendation letters and English-language documentation well in advance. Candidates from Partner Universities should also investigate their institution’s internal pre-selection deadline because this process must be completed before submitting the Yenching Academy application.

Overall, the Yenching Academy provides an opportunity for talented students from diverse academic and geographic backgrounds to study at Peking University, deepen their understanding of China and develop an international network while receiving substantial fellowship support.

TITLE: NASA Open Science Training: Free Open Science Essentials and Open Science 101 Courses

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
NASA is offering free Open Science training courses designed to help researchers, students, managers, and members of the public develop practical knowledge of open science principles and practices.

The training includes Open Science Essentials, a concise introductory course that takes approximately 2 hours, and Open Science 101, a comprehensive five-module course that takes approximately 12 hours to complete.

Both courses are available to the public through NASA’s digital learning platform. Learners can complete the courses at their own pace, and those who successfully complete the training are eligible to receive a digital badge and certificate.

About NASA Open Science Training

Open science is a collaborative approach to research that promotes the sharing of scientific data, information, tools, knowledge, and results to make research more transparent, accessible, reproducible, and collaborative.

NASA describes open science as a culture enabled by technology that supports the sharing of data, information, and knowledge within the scientific community and with the wider public.

The NASA Open Science training programme provides learners with practical knowledge they can use to understand and apply open science practices in research.

Open Science Essentials

Open Science Essentials is designed as a high-level introduction to the principles, practices, and tools associated with open science.

The course takes approximately 2 hours to complete and is intended for learners looking for a concise overview of open science concepts. Researchers, managers, and students outside NASA can create an account and register for the course online. The training can be completed at the learner’s own pace, with progress saved between sessions.

What You Will Learn

The Open Science Essentials course covers topics including:

The meaning and principles of open science

Common challenges and barriers to adopting open science

Open data and data ethics

Open peer review

Collaborative research practices

FAIR principles

Open Science and Data Management Plans

Open-source software

Open research results

Persistent identifiers

Open licensing

Repositories and version control

Pre-registration

The role of artificial intelligence in open science

The course is structured into five lessons covering the fundamentals and practical tools needed to begin applying open science approaches.

How to Register for Open Science Essentials

Researchers, managers, and students outside NASA can register through NASA’s online learning platform.

Course: Open Science Essentials

Duration: Approximately 2 hours

Format: Online and self-paced

Eligibility: Open to the public

Register: NASA Open Science Essentials

Open Science 101

Open Science 101 is a more comprehensive training programme for learners who want to develop a deeper understanding of open science and how it can be incorporated into research projects.

The course consists of five modules, with the complete training taking approximately 12 hours. Each module takes around 2.5 hours to complete. Like Open Science Essentials, the course is free and self-paced for public learners.

What You Will Learn

The five modules cover:

Module 1: Open Science Fundamentals

Explore what open science is, current practices, benefits, and challenges.

Module 2: Open Science Tools and Practices

Learn about open science fundamentals, including the Use, Make, Share framework, FAIR principles, and essential tools.

Module 3: Open Data

Learn practical approaches for finding, assessing, creating, and sharing open data.

Module 4: Open Code

Discover how to apply open-code practices throughout the development lifecycle using the Use, Make, Share framework.

Module 5: Open Results and Collaboration

Learn how to establish scientific collaborations, develop ethical contributor guidelines, discover and assess open results, and publish and properly credit research outputs.

How to Register for Open Science 101

Researchers and students outside NASA can create an account and register for the course through NASA’s online learning platform.

Course: Open Science 101

Duration: Approximately 12 hours

Modules: 5

Format: Online and self-paced

Eligibility: Open to the public

Register: NASA Open Science 101

Who Can Take the Training?

The NASA Open Science courses are available to the general public, including:

Researchers

Students

Scientists

Research managers

University professionals

Early-career researchers

Members of the public interested in open science

NASA also provides access to the training for its internal workforce through SATERN, the agency’s learning management system.

Course Certificates and Digital Badges

Learners who successfully complete the NASA Open Science training can receive a digital badge and certificate, allowing them to demonstrate their completion of the training and showcase their achievement.

Why Open Science Matters

Open science promotes greater transparency and collaboration in research. NASA’s approach emphasizes making scientific processes and results as open as possible while improving accessibility, reproducibility, and participation.

NASA identifies several key principles of open science, including open and transparent research, accessible scientific data and tools, reproducible research, and collaboration among researchers and organizations.

The training therefore provides learners with an opportunity to understand how modern research can be conducted and shared more openly.

How to Apply for the NASA Open Science Training

There is no competitive application process described for the public courses. Interested learners can register directly through NASA’s online learning platform.

Step 1: Choose a Course

Select Open Science Essentials if you want a short introduction to the fundamentals of open science.

Choose Open Science 101 if you want a more comprehensive five-module learning experience.

Step 2: Create an Account

Follow the registration instructions on the relevant NASA course page.

Step 3: Complete the Training

Both public courses are self-paced, allowing learners to progress through the material according to their own schedule.

Step 4: Receive Your Certificate and Digital Badge

After successfully completing the course requirements, eligible learners can receive a digital badge and certificate.

Conclusion

The NASA Open Science Training programme provides free online learning opportunities for researchers, students, managers, and members of the public who want to understand and apply open science practices.

With Open Science Essentials providing a two-hour introduction and Open Science 101 offering a deeper five-module learning experience, learners can choose the course that best matches their needs.

Those interested in open data, open research, scientific collaboration, research transparency, reproducibility, open-source software, and modern research practices can register through NASA’s official training platform.

TITLE: Indigenous Women’s Program Fellowship 2027 – Cohort V

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 24, 2026

Applications are invited for the Indigenous Women’s Program Fellowship 2027 – Cohort V. Beginning in 2023, under the Indigenous Women’s Program, the year-long fellowship nurtures the next generation of Indigenous women leaders by supporting those who are taking innovative steps that contribute to gender equality, the well-being of their communities, and the recognition of their land and resource rights. Through the Fellowship Program, over 15 women have successfully implemented their projects in their communities.

Land is Life launched the Indigenous Women’s Program in 2022. Designed and led by Indigenous women, the program supports Indigenous women and their organisations in Africa, Asia, and throughout the Americas in effectively asserting their individual and collective rights to access, use, and control land and natural resources; to improve their livelihoods; and to promote and protect their peoples’ entitlements. The Program has provided Indigenous women leaders with funding, direct support (including stipends), as well as mentorship and training opportunities. This support has led to many women’s participation in international spaces.

Themes

Climate change and environmental justice: adaptation/mitigation, biodiversity protection, false solutions critique

Land rights and territorial defense: securing territories against extractives, evictions, illegal logging/mining; FPIC protocols

Food sovereignty and livelihoods: agroecology, seed sovereignty, economic alternatives to industrial agribusiness

Health and well-being: access to traditional medicine, mental health support post-disaster, maternal/child health, violence prevention

Economic empowerment and livelihoods strengthening: community enterprises, market access, sustainable income generation, women’s economic leadership

Governance: supporting organization’s internal structures, autonomy models rooted in traditional governance systems

Benefits

Personalized mentoring from Indigenous women leaders with proven experience advancing Indigenous Peoples’ rights.

Funding and technical support (up to $3,000 USD) to design and implement a community-level project.

A stipend of $3,600 USD to support your participation throughout the program.

Knowledge sharing through bimonthly trainings on key topics related to Indigenous Peoples’ rights.

Leadership development to strengthen Indigenous women’s voices and decision-making power.

Networking opportunities to build or strengthen alliances with local, regional, and global partners and allies.

Advocacy support to participate in national and international decision-making spaces.

Eligibility

Open to Indigenous women who are between 18 and 35 years old.

To expand access to advanced learning opportunities, priority will be given to Indigenous women who do not hold a master’s or doctoral degree.

Applicants must be able to speak fluently in English, French, or Spanish.

The applicant should not have been a former Land is Life fellow.

Priority will be given to applicants from countries that have not been previously selected to participate in The Indigenous Women’s Fellowship Program.

Countries previously represented: Indonesia, Tanzania, Panama, Ecuador, Peru, Colombia, Kenya, Mali, Philippines, Democratic Republic of Congo, Nepal, Mexico, Bolivia.

Application

Fill out the application form

Develop a community project that promotes the rights of Indigenous Peoples, with particular attention to the rights of Indigenous women and girls. The applicant’s community project proposal should align with the aforementioned central themes of the Program.

Provide a letter of recommendation from an Indigenous Peoples organization, representative/leader from applicant’s territory, or equivalent official source.

For applicants with little to no internet access:

Begin by sending an email to info@landislife.org. Include that you are experiencing difficulties filling out the form and request to receive the application questions via email. Once questions are received, prepare responses and send a follow-up email to info@landislife.org. Applications must be submitted before the application deadline. Late or incomplete applications will not be considered.

For more information, visit Indigenous Women’s Program Fellowship.

TITLE: Kleinhans Fellowship for Community Forestry Research 2027 (up to $20,000)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: February 28, 2027

Applications are open for the Kleinhans Fellowship for Community Forestry Research 2027. Recognizing that sound scientific inquiry can help to guide technical assistance for local development, the Kleinhans Fellowship supports research that seeks solutions to the challenges faced by the community forestry model.

The fellowship provides funds for research that is oriented toward solving real-world problems as defined by community forest enterprises (CFEs). Moreover, the planning, implementation and dissemination of research results will be carried out in participatory manner to ensure that it has practical value for communities and helps to inform their action plans.

Research Topics

The Kleinhans Fellowship provides a two-year stipend of US$20,000 per year to support research that addresses one of the following topics:

Markets for lesser-known species and non-timber forest products (NTFPs). Most community forestry products are unlikely to reach international markets, but domestic markets in many tropical forest countries are being flooded with illegal wood products, making it hard for legitimate operations—especially CFEs—to compete. The absence of markets for lesser-known species and NTFPs further impedes optimal forest management and is a critical hurdle that must be overcome if CFEs are to become economically viable. The fellowship supports research that systematically documents and analyzes the creation and maintenance of domestic markets for diversified forest products, helps determine what drives success and recommends future actions.

Biodiversity management practices. Sustainable forest management requires practices that conserve biodiversity, such as the protection of High Conservation Value Forests and the creation of riparian buffers. The Kleinhans Fellowship supports research that explores the feasibility of implementing such practices at the community level and their effects on the economic viability of CFEs.

Social organization and governance. Technical assistance programs are often limited in their ability to invest in organizational capacity building. The fellowship supports research that investigates modes of social organization and highlights both problems and innovative, replicable solutions for CFE governance. Topics of interest include equitable participation and transparency in decision-making and benefit-sharing; human resource management and business training; and governance aspects such as CFE bylaws, compliance and legal status.

Multi-community enterprises. Without access to financing, CFEs often get mired in debt, are beholden to high-risk, high-cost lenders and cannot invest in developing their businesses. CFEs are often encouraged to work together to aggregate supply, invest collectively and access financing, but it can be difficult to put these strategies into practice. The fellowship supports research that examines multi-community enterprises, documents and analyzes their successes and failures, and makes recommendations for future investment in the development of such ventures.

Award

The fellowship provides a grant of $20,000 per year for two years. Note that the fellowship will not subsidize academic tuition or fees, nor will it cover the cost of purchasing transport vehicles or equipment that is unnecessary or unreasonable.

Eligibility

Applicants must have a master’s degree in forestry, ecology, botany, environmental science or an appropriate related field.

Doctoral candidates or post-doctoral researchers are preferred, although applicants may substitute relevant experience for higher-level degrees.

Application

Applications will be accepted starting six months before the deadline, on February 28, 2027:

A proposal that does not exceed seven typed pages in length. The proposal should include an abstract, a review of the relevant literature, detailed methodology and a discussion of the project’s practical applications

A budget

A copy of the candidate’s curriculum vitae or resume

Two letters of recommendation

A list of past, current and potential funding sources for both the applicant and the project

Applications can be submitted in English, Spanish or Portuguese.

Applicants are required to submit their completed application by email to Elena Degli Innocenti at kleinhans@ra.org or by regular mail to:

Rainforest Alliance
Kleinhans Fellowship
298 Fifth Avenue
7th Floor
New York, NY 10001
United States

For more information, visit Kleinhans Fellowship for Community Forestry Research.

TITLE: Tara’s Circle 2026 Global Open Call Offers €100,000 to Women-Led Impact Projects

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are open for Tara’s Circle 2026, an international initiative supporting women-led projects that generate measurable social, environmental or economic impact.

Organised by Tara for Women, the 2026 programme will distribute up to €100,000 among 15 winning projects across five thematic areas. Within each area, three projects will receive cash support of €10,000, €6,000 or €4,000.

In addition to the financial support, all 15 winners will enter a six-month development programme offering strategic mentoring, specialised training, international visibility, networking opportunities and potential connections with investors.

The call is open to women aged 18 and above from any country. Applicants must be founders or co-founders of their projects and play an active leadership role. Eligible projects should be at the seed, defined minimum viable product or functional minimum viable product stage and demonstrate the potential to become sustainable and scalable.

Applications must be submitted by September 17, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central European Summer Time. This is a midday deadline rather than an end-of-day deadline, so applicants should carefully convert it to their local time.

All information is based on the official Tara’s Circle 2026 Open Call Guidelines.

About Tara for Women

Tara for Women is a Spanish nonprofit foundation with a global mission to advance women’s talent and help women and girls develop projects capable of creating sustainable impact.

The foundation supports women through:

Project financing

Individual and strategic mentorship

Professional training

International visibility

Access to networks

Entrepreneurship support

Partnerships and collaboration opportunities

Connections with members of the investment ecosystem

Its work is organised around education and entrepreneurship, with an emphasis on sustainability, inclusion, empowerment, transparency and measurable social impact.

The foundation seeks to address the barriers that prevent women from turning ideas into sustainable projects. Its initiatives are designed to provide women with the financing, confidence, knowledge and professional relationships required to grow their projects and contribute to positive change.

More information about the foundation’s mission and values is available on the official Tara for Women website.

Purpose of Tara’s Circle 2026

Tara’s Circle 2026 supports women-led projects that combine innovation with a clear social, environmental or economic purpose.

The programme is not limited to one industry or type of business. Applicants may propose commercial ventures, social enterprises, technology projects, cultural initiatives, educational models, healthcare solutions, sustainability projects or other ventures that fit within the five thematic areas.

The programme seeks projects that demonstrate:

A clearly identified problem

A relevant and innovative solution

Meaningful social, environmental or economic impact

A capable and committed team

Potential to become financially sustainable

Capacity to scale or expand

A defined or operating minimum viable product

A coherent business or operating model

Measurable outcomes

Alignment with one or more programme themes

The emphasis is on women-led initiatives that can move beyond a general idea and demonstrate how their proposed solution could be implemented, sustained and expanded.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must satisfy the following main conditions:

Be a woman aged 18 or older when the application is submitted.

Be the founder or co-founder of the project.

Play an active role in leading the project.

Submit a project with national or international scope.

Have a project at an eligible development stage.

Demonstrate a commitment to creating social, environmental or economic impact.

Show potential for scalability and long-term sustainability.

Submit all required documents through the official platform before the deadline.

Projects may be based in any country. No geographic or nationality restriction is stated.

The application may be submitted by a woman working with a wider team, provided she is a founder or co-founder and remains actively involved in project leadership.

Women-Led Project Requirement

A project is considered women-led when a woman:

Founded or co-founded the initiative

Participates actively in strategic decision-making

Exercises a genuine leadership role

Is substantially involved in developing and implementing the project

Is not included merely as a nominal or symbolic founder

Applicants should explain their position, responsibilities and decision-making role clearly in the application and pitch deck.

Projects that include men or other team members are not automatically excluded. The essential condition is that an eligible woman founder or co-founder actively leads the initiative.

International Eligibility

Tara’s Circle 2026 is open to applicants worldwide.

Projects may operate:

Within one country

Across multiple countries

Regionally

Internationally

Through physical operations

Through digital or hybrid models

No citizenship, nationality, racial or continental restriction is published.

However, international eligibility does not guarantee that the foundation can transfer cash to every country. Financial disbursement remains subject to applicable laws, banking mechanisms, international regulations and sanctions.

Cash Awards and Funding Structure

Each of the five thematic areas receives a total cash allocation of €20,000.

The amount is distributed among three winning projects in each thematic area:

Across all five thematic areas, the programme plans to provide:

Five first-place awards worth €10,000 each

Five second-place awards worth €6,000 each

Five third-place awards worth €4,000 each

Fifteen awards in total

Up to €100,000 in total financial support

The funding is non-repayable, subject to the applicable terms, agreements, tax rules and transfer restrictions.

International Funding Restrictions

Although applications are accepted internationally, the transfer of funding is subject to legal and operational conditions.

Tara for Women states that it may postpone, restrict or cancel a financial transfer if payment is prevented by:

Applicable laws or regulations

International sanctions

Banking restrictions

Lack of a safe or lawful payment mechanism

Force majeure

Other conditions outside the foundation’s control

If financial support cannot be transferred, Tara for Women may consider providing an alternative form of non-financial assistance where appropriate.

International applicants should therefore understand that being selected does not override banking laws, sanctions or other transfer restrictions.

The Five Thematic Areas

Applicants may submit their project under one or more thematic areas, provided that the selection is consistent with the project’s activities, impact model and objectives.

The categories are indicative rather than exhaustive. Cross-cutting and hybrid projects may still qualify.

1. Sustainability, Environment and Mobility

This area seeks projects contributing to a more sustainable, resilient and environmentally responsible future.

Relevant projects may address:

Circular economy models

Waste reduction and waste valorisation

Recycling and material recovery

Clean and renewable energy

Energy efficiency

Decarbonisation

Sustainable transport

Low-emission mobility

Climate adaptation

Community climate resilience

Carbon capture

Carbon reduction and compensation

Biodiversity conservation

Ecosystem protection and restoration

Efficient resource management

Environmental technology

Sustainable urban systems

Projects should explain the environmental problem being addressed, the measurable benefit of the solution and how the model can be sustained or expanded.

2. Health and Well-Being

This area supports projects that improve physical, mental or social well-being while expanding fair and inclusive access to healthcare.

Special consideration is given to women’s health and caregiving.

Relevant initiatives may include:

Preventive healthcare

Community-based health services

Mental health support

Emotional well-being

Women’s health across different stages of life

Maternal or reproductive health

Caregiving products and services

New models of care delivery

Healthcare-access solutions

Technology supporting health services

Projects reducing inequalities in access to care

Community health education

Affordable health-related products

Applicants should demonstrate how their project responds to a real health need and why their approach can improve access, quality, equity or outcomes.

3. Social Innovation, Education and Community Development

This thematic area supports projects that strengthen communities through education, inclusion, entrepreneurship and new economic opportunities.

Relevant initiatives may address:

Community-led innovation

Support for underserved communities

Solutions for vulnerable populations

Inclusive and accessible education

Quality education

Workforce development

Employment creation

Projects generating measurable community impact

Applicants should explain how the proposed model will create meaningful, lasting benefits rather than temporary or unmeasurable activities.

4. Technology and Science

This area supports projects with a substantial technological or scientific foundation.

Eligible initiatives may involve:

Scalable technology with measurable social or environmental value

Projects should demonstrate that technology is a meaningful part of the solution rather than an unnecessary feature added only to appear innovative.

Applicants should explain:

What makes it different

5. Design, Culture and Impact-Driven Fashion

This area focuses on creativity as a means of generating positive social, environmental or economic change.

Relevant projects may include:

Sustainable fashion

Circular fashion

Responsible production

Ethical supply chains

Design responding to social challenges

Design addressing environmental problems

Cultural projects with measurable community value

Creative industries

Projects preserving cultural heritage

Initiatives protecting traditional knowledge

Innovative cultural-production models

New approaches to cultural consumption

Inclusive design

Responsible material use

Creative merit alone is not enough. Projects should demonstrate how their design, cultural or fashion model produces measurable impact and can remain economically or operationally sustainable.

Applying Under More Than One Area

Projects may be submitted under one or more thematic areas.

A project combining health and technology, for example, may have a legitimate connection to both categories. Similarly, a circular-fashion initiative may fit under sustainability and impact-driven fashion.

Applicants should select multiple categories only where there is a clear and defensible connection. The application should remain coherent and should not be stretched artificially to fit every available theme.

The declared thematic area is one part of the evaluation but does not independently determine whether a project will be selected.

Eligible Project Stages

The call supports projects that have progressed beyond a vague or completely untested concept.

Three development stages are described.

Seed-Stage Projects

These are early-stage initiatives with significant growth potential.

They may have the following characteristics:

The product or service is still under development.

The underlying business idea has already been validated.

The project is seeking initial external funding.

Potential funding sources may include angel investors, incubators or seed funds.

The founding team is being formed or strengthened.

The project has begun defining how its solution will work.

A seed-stage applicant should still provide evidence that the problem and proposed solution have been investigated and validated.

Defined MVP Stage

A minimum viable product, or MVP, is the simplest workable version of a product or service that can be tested with users.

At the defined MVP stage:

The project has moved beyond the general idea phase.

The value proposition is clear.

A functional MVP design exists.

Essential features have been identified.

The team is actively developing the MVP.

The product is not yet fully operational.

Applicants should show that they understand what must be built, who will use it and what must be tested.

Functional MVP Stage

At this stage:

An operational and demonstrable MVP already exists.

The product or service has been tested with real users.

The project has received initial market or user feedback.

The team is ready to improve or scale the model.

The founders are prepared to receive mentoring and financial support.

The project can demonstrate early evidence of relevance or demand.

Projects that are only abstract ideas without validation, a defined solution or meaningful development work are unlikely to meet the published stage requirements.

Six-Month Support Programme for Winners

The 15 winning projects will receive access to a comprehensive six-month development programme.

The support is intended to strengthen the founders’ capabilities, improve project visibility and accelerate sustainable growth.

The programme will also help participants communicate their value propositions more clearly to investors and other members of the entrepreneurship ecosystem.

Applicants should use only one official form and ensure that every required field and attachment is complete.

TITLE: Young Leaders Programme 2026 in Vietnam: Fully Funded Opportunity for Young Researchers to Attend the South China Sea International Conference

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Young Leaders Programme 2026 is inviting emerging researchers and young professionals with an interest in maritime security, international relations, political science, international law and related social sciences to apply for an opportunity to participate in the 18th South China Sea International Conference, taking place in Hanoi, Vietnam, from 6 to 8 October 2026.

The programme is designed to give the next generation of regional and global leaders an opportunity to engage directly with leading scholars, policymakers, practitioners and experts working on some of the most important geopolitical and maritime issues affecting the South China Sea and the wider Indo-Pacific region.

Selected participants will have the opportunity to attend the conference, participate in discussions and side events, develop professional networks, and present their own policy ideas during a dedicated Young Leaders Special Session. The organisers will provide substantial financial support covering round-trip economy airfare, accommodation, local transportation and meals.

For young researchers seeking international exposure, policy experience and connections with established experts in maritime affairs and regional cooperation, this programme offers a valuable platform to learn, contribute and build relationships with peers from around the world.

About the Young Leaders Programme 2026

The Young Leaders Programme is an initiative organised as part of the South China Sea International Conference, a major regional forum focused on maritime security, geopolitics and issues affecting the South China Sea and the broader Indo-Pacific.

The annual conference brings together prominent scholars, practitioners and policymakers to examine developments in regional and international affairs. Participants have the opportunity to hear from leading experts, exchange perspectives and discuss complex challenges relating to maritime security, regional cooperation and sustainable development.

The Young Leaders Programme extends this platform to the next generation of researchers and emerging leaders.

Rather than simply attending the conference as observers, selected Young Leaders are encouraged to actively contribute their perspectives. The programme is intended to help participants strengthen their knowledge, develop practical policy-thinking skills and engage constructively with experts and fellow young researchers.

The 2026 programme is particularly focused on regional cooperation and next-generation solutions, encouraging young participants to consider innovative approaches to achieving a peaceful, stable and prosperous South China Sea.

When and Where Will the Programme Take Place?

The Young Leaders Programme 2026 will take place in:

Location: Hanoi, Vietnam

Dates: 6–8 October 2026

Event: 18th South China Sea International Conference

Programme focus: Regional cooperation and next-generation solutions

Participants will be able to follow presentations and discussions throughout the conference while also taking part in activities specifically designed for Young Leaders.

What Is the South China Sea International Conference?

The South China Sea International Conference, organised by the Diplomatic Academy of Viet Nam, is an established regional forum dealing with maritime security and geopolitical issues.

The conference attracts participation from scholars, practitioners, policymakers and other experts from Vietnam and abroad. Its discussions address matters that are important not only to countries directly connected to the South China Sea but also to the wider Indo-Pacific region.

The conference provides a setting where participants can examine complex issues from different perspectives and engage with people working in academia, government, think tanks and other policy communities.

For young researchers, participation therefore offers more than an academic conference experience. It can provide exposure to current debates, policy discussions and professional networks connected to maritime affairs and international relations.

What Will Young Leaders Do at the Conference?

One of the most important aspects of the programme is that selected Young Leaders are expected to actively engage with the conference rather than simply attend sessions.

Participants will have the opportunity to:

1. Attend the South China Sea International Conference

Young Leaders will receive full participation in the 18th South China Sea International Conference.

This means they can follow presentations, listen to expert discussions and gain firsthand exposure to debates surrounding the South China Sea and broader regional issues.

2. Engage With Leading Experts

The programme provides opportunities for young researchers to interact with prominent scholars, practitioners and policymakers.

Participants may use these interactions to ask questions, exchange ideas and gain perspectives from individuals with substantial experience in international affairs, maritime security and regional cooperation.

3. Present a Policy Pitch

A particularly valuable component of the programme is the dedicated Young Leaders Special Session.

During this session, selected Young Leaders will have an opportunity to present their policy pitches in front of peers and the wider conference audience.

This gives participants a platform to transform their research, observations or ideas into practical policy proposals and communicate them to an audience interested in regional affairs.

4. Participate in Side Events

Young Leaders will also participate in side events connected to the conference.

These activities provide opportunities for deeper exchanges with speakers and experts about topics discussed during the main conference.

Such interactions can help participants explore issues beyond formal presentations and develop a better understanding of different viewpoints.

5. Contribute Ideas for the Future of the Region

The programme encourages Young Leaders to think creatively about how to promote a peaceful, stable and prosperous South China Sea.

Participants are therefore expected to bring their own perspectives and ideas to discussions about regional cooperation, maritime security and development.

Key Benefits of the Young Leaders Programme 2026

The programme offers both financial and professional benefits to successful applicants.

Fully Sponsored Travel and Participation

One of the most significant benefits is the financial support provided by the organisers.

The sponsorship covers:

Round-trip economy-class airfare

Three-night accommodation

Local transportation

Meals during the programme

This substantially reduces the financial barriers associated with travelling to Vietnam for an international conference.

Full Participation in the Conference

Selected Young Leaders will receive full participation in the 18th South China Sea International Conference.

This gives them access to conference presentations and discussions involving experts working on important geopolitical and maritime issues.

International Professional Networking

Participants will become part of a network involving scholars and professionals from around the world.

The programme specifically highlights connections with individuals from prestigious think tanks and universities.

For early-career researchers, such networks can be valuable for discovering future research collaborations, academic opportunities, professional relationships and broader international engagements.

Opportunity to Present a Policy Pitch

The Young Leaders Special Session gives participants an opportunity to publicly present their ideas.

This can help participants gain experience in:

Policy communication

Public speaking

Presenting research

Defending ideas

Engaging with expert audiences

Translating research into policy recommendations

Certificate of Attendance

Participants will receive Certificates of Attendance at the Conference.

This can serve as formal documentation of participation in an international conference and may be useful when documenting professional, academic or research experience.

Access to the Alumni Network

Successful participants will become part of the South China Sea Conference Young Leaders Programme Alumni Network.

This creates the possibility of maintaining connections with other Young Leaders after the conference and continuing to engage with a broader community of researchers and emerging professionals interested in regional affairs.

Who Can Apply for the Young Leaders Programme 2026?

The programme is intended for young researchers and emerging leaders between the ages of 20 and 35 who have relevant academic or professional interests.

Applicants must meet several eligibility requirements.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be between 20 and 35 years old at the start of the programme.

Because the programme takes place in October 2026, applicants should ensure that they meet the specified age requirement when the programme begins.

English Language Requirement

Candidates must be able to use English fluently.

This requirement is important because the programme involves participation in international discussions, interaction with experts and presentation of ideas.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating, listening, reading and participating in discussions in English.

Academic or Professional Background

Candidates should have background knowledge in relevant disciplines, including:

Political science

International relations

International law

Other social sciences

Applicants whose academic or professional work intersects with these fields may find the programme particularly relevant.

Interest in Maritime Security

Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to maritime security and related issues.

This means applicants should be able to demonstrate genuine interest or experience related to maritime affairs, geopolitical developments, international cooperation or other relevant areas.

Simply meeting the age requirement is therefore not enough. Applicants should clearly communicate their interest and engagement with the subject matter.

How Many Young Leaders Will Be Selected?

The programme will select eight Young Leaders from the applicant pool.

Because the number of available places is limited, applicants should make their applications as strong and relevant as possible.

A competitive application should clearly demonstrate the candidate’s academic or professional background, interest in maritime security and ability to contribute meaningful perspectives to discussions surrounding the South China Sea and the Indo-Pacific.

Countries and Regions Eligible to Apply

The programme description states that it seeks to bring together young potential leaders from across the region while also positioning the initiative within the broader Indo-Pacific context.

The information provided does not specify an exhaustive list of eligible countries or a particular race or ethnicity requirement.

Therefore, applicants should carefully review the official application form and any accompanying instructions to determine whether there are additional geographic eligibility conditions that may apply.

The programme is designed around regional and international engagement, and its stated objective is to connect young researchers interested in the South China Sea with experts and peers from across the region and globally.

What Kind of Applicant Is the Programme Looking For?

Beyond the formal eligibility requirements, the programme is particularly relevant to individuals who can demonstrate a strong intellectual or professional interest in regional and international affairs.

A strong candidate may have:

An academic background in political science, international relations, international law or another social science discipline.

Research interests connected to the South China Sea, maritime security or regional cooperation.

Knowledge of geopolitical or maritime issues affecting the Indo-Pacific.

Experience conducting research or writing about relevant policy issues.

A demonstrated interest in peace, stability and regional development.

Strong English communication skills.

An ability to engage constructively with people holding different perspectives.

Ideas that could contribute to discussions about practical solutions to regional challenges.

Applicants should focus on showing why their experience and perspective would add value to the Young Leaders Programme.

Why This Opportunity Matters for Young Researchers

International conferences can be difficult for early-career researchers to access because of travel costs, registration fees and limited opportunities to interact with senior experts.

The Young Leaders Programme addresses some of these barriers by providing financial support while creating a dedicated platform for emerging researchers.

The opportunity is particularly significant because participants are not merely being invited to listen to experts. They are being encouraged to contribute their own ideas through the Young Leaders Special Session and other programme activities.

For researchers interested in international relations, diplomacy, maritime affairs and regional security, this can provide practical experience in communicating research beyond traditional academic settings.

It also gives participants an opportunity to understand how academic research, policy discussions and international diplomacy intersect.

Sponsorship and Financial Support

The organisers will sponsor the participation of selected Young Leaders.

The sponsorship includes:

Round-trip economy-class airfare

Three-night accommodation

Local transportation

Meals

The sponsored accommodation is specified as covering the period associated with the programme from 6 to 8 October 2026.

Applicants should carefully review the invitation and detailed guidelines if selected, as those documents will provide the specific arrangements and instructions for participation.

Application Process

Interested candidates are required to complete the official application form.

Applicants should provide accurate and complete information and ensure that the email address entered in the application is correct.

The organisers state that selected candidates will receive an invitation containing detailed guidelines for the conference through the email address provided in the application.

23:59 on 13 September 2026 (GMT+7).

Applications submitted after the stated deadline will not be accepted.

Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their forms. Completing the application early provides time to review responses, check supporting information and resolve any technical issues before the deadline.

After applications close, the application review board will assess the submissions.

According to the programme information, the review process may take approximately two weeks or longer.

Applicants are therefore advised to be patient while the review is conducted.

If selected, successful candidates will receive an invitation through the email address supplied in their application. The invitation will contain detailed guidelines and information concerning participation in the conference.

Applicants should therefore regularly check the email account they provide in the application.

How to Make Your Application Stronger

Although the final selection is determined by the programme’s review board, applicants can take practical steps to present a compelling application.

Demonstrate a Clear Interest in Maritime Security

Do not simply state that you are interested in maritime security. Explain what specifically interests you and why the subject matters to your academic, professional or research goals.

Connect Your Background to the Programme

Show how your studies, research, professional experience or other relevant activities relate to the programme’s themes.

Show What You Can Contribute

The programme is designed around active participation.

Applicants should therefore consider what perspectives, research findings or policy ideas they could bring to discussions about the South China Sea and regional cooperation.

Be Specific

Strong applications generally benefit from specific examples rather than broad statements.

Instead of simply describing yourself as passionate about international affairs, explain the particular issues you have researched, projects you have undertaken or questions you are currently exploring.

Check Your English

Because fluency in English is an eligibility requirement, applicants should make sure their written responses are clear, professional and easy to understand.
