3. $12,000 for Travel and Professional Development

Fellows receive $12,000 per year for travel and professional development.

This can support activities that help fellows expand their technical and professional networks and continue developing their leadership and entrepreneurial capabilities.

4. Health Insurance Stipend

The fellowship provides a health insurance stipend, adding another form of financial support for fellows as they dedicate themselves to their projects.

5. Relocation Allowance

A relocation allowance is also included among the fellowship benefits.

This can help fellows manage relocation-related expenses associated with participating in the program.

Community and Collaboration

The Activate Fellowship is not only a financial support program. Community participation is an important part of the fellowship experience.

Fellows participate in community-based programming every two weeks, including:

Workshops

Fellow talks

Networking opportunities

Collaborative activities

Professional development opportunities

The program also facilitates what Activate describes as “Collisions”, which are opportunities for fellows to connect with inspiring people, expand their networks, and develop unexpected professional relationships.

Activate emphasizes a community culture that prioritizes people and authentic relationships.

The organization highlights principles such as putting people before the company and being genuine even when difficult situations arise.

This community environment is intended to give fellows access to peers and experienced individuals who can provide perspectives, connections, and support throughout their entrepreneurial journey.

Entrepreneurship Education and Support

Scientists and engineers may have extensive technical expertise but limited experience with entrepreneurship, commercialization, company building, or business leadership.

The Activate Fellowship provides education specifically designed to help address this transition.

Elements of Entrepreneurship

Fellows receive education tailored to the needs of the scientist-turned-founder.

During the first quarter, fellows participate in a weekly Elements of Entrepreneurship course designed to help them develop the business and leadership knowledge needed to commercialize their technology.

One-on-One Mentorship

Fellows receive regular one-on-one mentorship with their community’s Managing Director.

These sessions can be used to work through challenges, evaluate strategies, and refine the direction of the company or proposed project.

Quarterly Advisory Meetings

The fellowship also provides quarterly advisory meetings that function similarly to board meetings.

These meetings are intended to help fellows focus on the most important issues facing their companies and projects.

Personal Development

Activate also places emphasis on the individual fellow rather than focusing exclusively on the company.

Annual retreats and reunions are designed to support fellows’ personal development and provide opportunities for continued connection within the Activate community.

Who Is Eligible for the Activate Fellowship?

Applicants must satisfy specific requirements relating to their education, technical experience, entrepreneurial stage, work authorization, and commitment to their proposed project.

Bachelor’s Degree Requirement

Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree.

Scientific, Engineering, or Technology Experience

Applicants must have at least four years of post-baccalaureate experience in:

Scientific research

Engineering

Technology development

This means the fellowship is intended for individuals who have already developed substantial technical experience beyond their undergraduate education.

First-Time Hard-Tech Founder

Applicants must be leading the commercial development of a hardware-based technology innovation for the first time if awarded the fellowship.

In other words, the program is not designed for repeat hard-tech founders.

The applicant should be moving toward commercializing a hard-tech innovation and taking on a leadership role in the proposed company or project.

Full-Time Commitment

Selected fellows must be prepared to commit full-time to their proposed project or company.

Activate notes that applicants do not necessarily have to have already left their current job or incorporated their company when applying.

The fellowship is designed in part to help enable that transition.

U.S. Work Authorization

Applicants must be legally able to work in the United States for the duration of the fellowship.

This is an important requirement for applicants who are currently outside the United States or who do not currently have U.S. work authorization.

English Communication

Applicants must be able to communicate proficiently in English.

This is important because fellows participate in entrepreneurship education, mentorship, community programming, networking, and other activities that require effective communication.

Project Eligibility

In addition to meeting the individual fellow requirements, the proposed technology must meet Activate’s project eligibility requirements.

Technology Must Be Based in Relevant Scientific or Engineering Fields

The proposed project must be based in:

Physical sciences

Biological sciences

Related engineering disciplines

The program therefore focuses on technology that has a substantial scientific or engineering foundation.

Technology Must Still Be in Development

The project must still be in development at the application deadline.

It must not yet be ready for full-scale product sales.

This requirement reflects the fellowship’s focus on helping technical innovations move through development and toward commercialization.

Funding Limit

At the time of the application deadline, the proposed project must not have raised more than $2 million in debt or equity funding from non-governmental sources.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider the amount and type of funding their project has already received when determining eligibility.

What Activate Looks For in Fellows

Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not automatically mean that an applicant will be selected.

Activate describes several characteristics it looks for when evaluating potential fellows.

1. Hard-Tech Leadership

Activate wants applicants who can demonstrate leadership in developing transformative technologies.

The ideal applicant should have a strong understanding of the technology they are proposing and be capable of independently leading the technical work involved.

2. Technical Expertise

Applicants should have substantial technical knowledge in the field of their proposed project.

They should be able to:

Understand the technical challenges facing their technology

Lead technical development

Conduct or oversee research and development

Reduce technical risks

Explain complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences

Activate notes that many successful applicants have completed PhDs or postdoctoral training.

However, a PhD or postdoctoral background is not presented as an absolute requirement. Activate also welcomes people with technical or R&D experience in industry or equivalent backgrounds.

3. Proof of Concept or Prototype

Activate indicates that many successful applicants have already established an early proof of concept or prototype supported by experimental data demonstrating that their innovation works.

This suggests that applicants should be able to provide evidence supporting the technical feasibility of their proposed innovation.

The technology does not need to be ready for full-scale sales, but applicants should be able to demonstrate meaningful progress in development.

4. Transformative Potential

Activate is interested in technologies that could make a significant difference in the world.

The program looks beyond incremental improvements and asks applicants to consider the potential long-term impact of their technology.

Applicants should be able to explain what the world could look like if their technology were successfully developed and implemented at scale.

5. Leadership Readiness

Activate also looks for applicants who are ready to develop beyond their technical expertise and grow as business leaders.

Applicants should demonstrate the ability or potential to:

Lead a company

Manage conflict

Operate in uncertain situations

Act with integrity

Mobilize resources

Make important decisions

Work toward commercialization

The applicant should have a leadership role in the proposed company or project.

6. High Potential Impact of the Fellowship

Activate emphasizes additionality in its selection process.

This means the organization wants to understand whether receiving the fellowship would meaningfully accelerate the applicant’s professional development and the progress of their proposed project.

Applicants should therefore be able to explain why the Activate Fellowship is important at this particular stage of their journey.

A strong application should make clear how the fellowship’s financial support, mentorship, education, community, and resources could change the trajectory of the technology and the applicant’s development as a leader.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Activate Fellowship may be relevant for technical professionals who are moving from research or engineering into commercialization.

Potential applicants may include:

Scientists developing a new technology

Engineers working on hardware-based innovations

Researchers transitioning toward entrepreneurship

Technology developers with substantial R&D experience

Industry professionals developing a transformative technology

Technical experts preparing to commercialize a prototype

Scientists or engineers preparing to become first-time hard-tech founders

Applicants should have a strong technical foundation and a project that fits Activate’s hard-tech focus.

APPLY HERE

Application Process

Applicants should follow the application instructions provided by Activate.

The application page states that applicants should first click the “Apply for US Cohort 2027” button and complete the application interest form to receive the link to begin the application.

Applicants should ensure that their proposed project clearly demonstrates:

The scientific or engineering basis of the technology.

The problem the technology is intended to address.

The current development stage.

Evidence that the technology works, where applicable.

The potential impact of the technology.

Their technical expertise and experience.

Their leadership role in the project.

Their plans for commercial development.

Why the Activate Fellowship would significantly accelerate the project.

Their ability to commit to the fellowship full-time if selected.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Activate Fellowship 2027

Application Deadline

Applications for the Activate U.S. Fellowship Cohort 2027 will close on:

October 30 at 12:00 p.m. Pacific Time.

Applicants should submit their application before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Before starting an application, prospective applicants should carefully assess both their own eligibility and the eligibility of their proposed technology.

In particular, applicants should confirm that they:

Have a bachelor’s degree.

Have at least four years of post-baccalaureate scientific research, engineering, or technology development experience.

Are developing a hardware-based technology.

Are commercializing the technology for the first time.

Can commit full-time to the proposed project if selected.

Are legally able to work in the United States for the duration of the fellowship.

Can communicate proficiently in English.

Have a project based in the physical sciences, biological sciences, or related engineering disciplines.

Have not reached full-scale product sales.

Have not raised more than $2 million in non-governmental debt or equity funding.

Applicants should also consider whether they can clearly demonstrate the technical expertise, leadership potential, transformative impact, and development progress that Activate looks for in its fellows.

Conclusion

The Activate Fellowship 2027 is designed to help experienced scientists, engineers, and technology developers transition from technical innovation into hard-tech entrepreneurship and commercialization.

Selected fellows receive significant financial support, including a $100,000 annual living stipend, $100,000 in R&D support, $12,000 in annual travel and professional development funds, a health insurance stipend, and a relocation allowance. Beyond financial assistance, the program provides entrepreneurship education, mentorship, advisory support, community programming, networking, and personal development opportunities.

The fellowship is particularly focused on first-time hard-tech founders who have substantial scientific, engineering, or technology development experience and are working on technologies that are still in development.

For applicants who meet the eligibility requirements and are developing a potentially transformative technology, the program provides a structured environment for developing both the technology and the leadership skills needed to take it toward commercialization.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.

TITLE: Connecting European Science: ESF Joins Horizon Europe Initiatives to Streamline Research Infrastructure Access

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
News | Project News

Photo credits: Eric Berghen

ESF is pleased to announce it is taking active role in a new coordinated effort funded under the Horizon Europe INFRADEV-05 framework. Launched jointly in Brussels on 3 June 2026, three interconnected initiatives (Access2Access, FUND-RI, and COORDINA-INNOV) aim to optimize how we fund, access and innovate through Europe’s world-class research infrastructures.

Exploring stakeholder needs and expectations

As part of the 20-month Access2Access consortium, which brings together 17 leading European research organisations, ESF is leading the task of mapping stakeholder requirements so that the new scheme is grounded on the actual needs of its users. The focus will be on surveying the divergent expectations among national funders, facility managers, academic scientists, and industrial users, among others, regarding the newly proposed platform.
The ultimate goal of the project is to provide the structural foundation for an intelligent, AI-supported “one-stop shop” discovery tool that allows researchers to seamlessly identify and access optimal facilities across Europe.
A triad for systemic reform

The Brussels kick-off meeting underscored that structural coherence requires addressing the infrastructure lifecycle from multiple angles. The three sister projects will operate concurrently to deliver a unified blueprint for future EU research policy:

Access2Access: Dedicated to creating an integrated, user-centred framework for facility access and digital service discovery.

FUND-RI: Focused on developing sustainable, coherent financial and long-term investment strategies for European infrastructures.

COORDINA-INNOV: Aimed at enhancing co-innovation and strategic collaboration between research infrastructures and industry.

Through its contribution to the Access2Access consortium, ESF looks forward to collaborating with partners across Europe to build a simpler, fairer, and more resilient ecosystem for European Research Infrastructures.

TITLE: Workshop on Strategic Foresight and Strategic Intelligence for Leaders, Managers, Academics and Administrators in Higher Education Institutions in Africa

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Association of African Universities (AAU), a Pan-African Higher Education organization, invites stakeholders to participate in an upcoming training program being organized on Strategic Foresight and Strategic Intelligence in Africa with the following details:

Workshop Title: Strategic Foresight and Strategic Intelligence for Leaders, Managers, Academics and Administrators in Higher Education Institutions in Africa

Date: 8th -11th October 2024

Venue: Association of African Universities Secretariat, Accra, Ghana

Target Participants: The workshop is recommended for Academics, Leaders, Librarians, Registrars, Administrators, University Management, Heads of Resource Mobilization & Partnership Development in institutions, Executive Directors, Directors, Program Coordinators, Staff of International Relations Offices, Finance and Budgeting Managers, Project Managers and Officers, Staff Responsible for Resource Development, Partnership & Policy Managers, and Planning Officers.

Registration Fee: The registration fees for the 4-day event are as follows:

AAU Member Institutions – $700

Non – AAU Member Institutions – $800

This will cover workshop attendance fees, snacks and lunches, training materials, certificates, and other logistics.

Overall Objective of the Workshop

This workshop aims to create future-ready and alert African higher education institutions that can adapt as the future evolves (anticipation, awareness, agility, and capability). This four-day practical capacity-building workshop focuses on foresight for strategic decision-making in higher education institutional contexts and helps participants understand and deal with the complexity underlying the operations of universities and research institutions. Participants will gain hands-on experience in applying strategic foresight tools (e.g., STEEP driver mapping, futures wheel, visioning, backcasting, wind tunneling, three horizons, archetypes, and roadmap) and working in groups. Participants will apply theoretical perspectives from cognitive and social psychology, decision theory, economics, organizational behavior, political science, or other behavioral science disciplines.

Specific Objectives

The training workshop is intended to help participants:

Expand their thinking beyond the present and/or near-term future.

Consider the long-term implications of current assumptions, decisions, and courses of action.

Think backward in time to better anticipate how the situation may evolve in the future.

Think holistically about multiple factors and their interactions to anticipate potential second-and third-order effects.

Develop a system thinking mindset and the skills and tools to apply that mindset to complex challenges and management problems for decision-makers in higher education institutions in Africa.

Critically evaluate the complexity of grand challenges in higher education and systematically address them.

Use strategic foresight for effective strategic planning in the context of the SDGs –building vision, resilience, and capability.

Delivery Mode

The workshop will be face-to-face, hands-on, and interactive through a combination of lecture, discussion, and group work. The workshop will give participants a structured approach to developing and implementing strategic foresight. The approach is proven and incorporates tools and techniques to aid analysis, the creation of options, and the evaluation of alternatives. Participants will learn to use one of the most compelling strategic foresight methodologies in use today, The Actionable Futures Toolkit and the Horizons Strategic Foresight Approach.

Expected Outcomes

On completing the workshop, participants will be able to:

Characterise grand challenges in higher education in Africa and delineate the potential of strategic foresight in addressing them.

Apply strategic foresight to institutional challenges and societal problems to identify leverage points for transformative change.

Critically reflect upon the strengths and limitations of strategic foresight to solve complex problems in higher education, and society, at large.

About our facilitators

Our facilitators are distinguished experts in the field of strategic foresight and strategic intelligence, with many years of experience in higher education. They have dedicated their careers to advancing strategic thinking and intelligence among leaders and managers in academia. These are:

Professor Tobias De Coning, Dean and Chair, Department of Innovation, and Entrepreneurship, ISM, Paris

Professor Frederick Ato Armah, Director of Research and Programmes (DRAP), Association of African Universities

Participants are encouraged to confirm their participation early enough to ensure they have enough time to process their visas. It is suggested that participants arrive on Monday, as the training starts on Tuesday morning.

The Association of African Universities (AAU) is an international non-governmental organization set up by the universities in Africa to promote cooperation among and between them and the international academic community. With over 440 members across the African continent and beyond, AAU is the largest and most comprehensive organization representing Universities and Higher Education bodies in Africa. It is also the apex organization and forum for consultation, exchange of information, and cooperation among institutions of higher education in Africa, and represents the voice of higher education in Africa on regional and international bodies and supports networking by institutions of higher education in teaching, research, information exchange, and dissemination. Applications are open for the Berenson Fellowship 2027-2028. This Fellowship, made possible by The Lila Wallace – Reader’s Digest Fund, is designed for scholars who explore “Italy in the World.” Projects should address the transnational dialogues between Italy and other cultures (e.g. Latin American, Mediterranean, African, Asian etc.) during the Renaissance, broadly understood historically to include the period from the 14th to the 17th century.

It is named after Bernard Berenson, who in his 1956 statement ‘On the Future of I Tatti’ expressed the hope that not only would scholars come from many countries, but that they would also travel in “what was the ancient Oecumene, not going farther East than the Euphrates and not farther South than Egypt and the great desert of North Africa” and be intimately acquainted with the Mediterranean countries and their “Hinterland.” Taking a broad geographic view of the Renaissance more than half a century ago, Berenson was a pioneer of the geographically expansive approach to the early modern world that this Fellowship wishes to encourage. Scholars working in all the fields supported by I Tatti—architecture and the arts, history, philosophy, literature, music and history of science—are encouraged to apply.

I Tatti offers Fellows the precious time they need to pursue their studies with a minimum of obligations and interruptions together with a maximum of scholarly resources—a combination that distinguishes the Harvard Center from similar institutions. Each year, a limited number of activities organized at I Tatti are reserved for the Fellows, and they are expected to join the wider community at conferences, lectures, and concerts. This is a residential fellowship of 4 or 6 months in length. Up to four fellowships will be awarded every year.

Benefits

The grant is USD $5,200 per month, plus a one-time supplement (maximum USD $1,800) towards relocation expenses.

If an apartment is not available, a housing subsidy will be offered to help offset rental costs.

Eligibility

At the time of application, scholars must have a PhD in hand and will be asked to upload a scan of the certificate.

They may not be working on a second PhD at the time of application.

They should work solely on the project with which they applied and are not permitted to work simultaneously on editing other book or article projects. The proposed research project may represent a segment of a larger project.

Priority will be given to early and mid-career scholars.

I Tatti welcomes applications from scholars from all nations and gives special consideration to candidates without regular access to research materials and facilities in Italy.

Application

TITLE: TTS Nigeria Programme 2026–2027: Applications Open for Free Technology and Workforce Development Programme for Young Nigerian Women

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Technology Talent Services (TTS) Nigeria Programme is a free technology skills and workforce development initiative designed to equip young Nigerian women with practical, career-focused skills and strengthen their pathways into employment within Nigeria’s growing technology and Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) sector. Implemented by the Technology for Social Change and Development Initiative (Tech4Dev) with funding support from the Mastercard Foundation, the programme provides free application, training, and tech-enabled job placement opportunities for eligible women aged 18 to 35.

Running from February 2026 to July 2027, the 18-month initiative aims to help participants develop in-demand skills, improve their workforce readiness, and access career pathways across areas including software engineering, cybersecurity, Data and AI, full-stack development, virtual assistance, executive administrative support, and other technology-enabled roles.

About the Technology Talent Services (TTS) Nigeria Programme

The Technology Talent Services (TTS) Nigeria Programme is a workforce development initiative led by Tech4Dev and funded by the Mastercard Foundation.

The programme has been established within a broader effort to improve workforce participation, employment pathways, economic inclusion, and the development of Nigeria’s technology-enabled BPO sector.

TTS Nigeria will run for 18 months, beginning in February 2026 and concluding in July 2027.

Key programme information includes:

Programme Name: Technology Talent Services (TTS) Nigeria

Lead Implementing Organization: Technology for Social Change and Development Initiative (Tech4Dev)

Funding Partner: Mastercard Foundation

Programme Duration: February 2026 to July 2027

Duration: 18 months

Programme Location: 12 states in Nigeria

Programme Cost: Free

Target Applicants: Female Nigerian citizens aged 18–35

The programme’s approach goes beyond participation in training. Information collected throughout the initiative will help organizers monitor skills development, workforce readiness, employment outcomes, programme effectiveness, and opportunities to improve future workforce-development initiatives.

What Is the TTS Nigeria Programme Designed to Achieve?

TTS Nigeria is focused on helping create stronger workforce and employment pathways, particularly for young women.

The programme will collect and evaluate information relating to participation, skill development, workforce readiness, employment outcomes, and participant experiences. These insights will be used to improve programme delivery and understand how workforce-development interventions can contribute to greater economic participation.

The initiative is also connected to efforts to support the growth of Nigeria’s technology BPO sector.

Among the areas the programme intends to monitor and strengthen are:

Programme participation and completion.

Participants’ development of relevant skills.

Workforce readiness.

Employment and placement outcomes.

Employer alignment.

Economic inclusion.

Employment pathways for young Nigerians.

Opportunities for women and underserved groups.

The development of Nigeria’s technology BPO workforce.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to young Nigerian women interested in improving their skills and positioning themselves for future workforce opportunities.

Who Can Apply for the TTS Nigeria Programme?

The initial eligibility requirements are clearly defined.

To proceed with an application, an individual must be:

Female

Between 18 and 35 years old

A Nigerian citizen

Applicants are required to complete an initial eligibility screening before they are asked to provide additional personal and contact information.

If an applicant’s answers do not meet any of these basic eligibility requirements, the applicant will not be able to continue to the full application.

This initial screening process is intended to avoid unnecessarily collecting additional personal information from individuals who do not qualify for the programme.

Applicants should therefore carefully confirm their eligibility before starting the application.

Why the Eligibility Check Comes Before the Full Application

TTS Nigeria has structured its application process so that applicants first answer a small number of basic eligibility questions.

These include questions relating to:

Gender

Nationality

Age

Only applicants who meet the programme’s fundamental eligibility criteria can proceed to the next stage.

According to the programme information, this process has been established to protect applicants’ data and time. More detailed information, including names and contact information, is requested only after the basic eligibility requirements have been confirmed.

Applicants must provide accurate information throughout the process. Providing false or misleading information may result in disqualification at any stage of the application or selection process.

The TTS Nigeria Programme Is Free

One of the most important details prospective applicants should know is that the TTS Nigeria Programme is free.

Eligible applicants should therefore not interpret the programme as requiring tuition or a participation fee based on the information provided in the official registration form.

Applicants should also remember that submitting an application does not automatically guarantee selection.

The registration form is described as the first step in applying to the programme. Applications and responses will be used to understand each applicant’s background, training needs, and suitability for available opportunities.

Training, Skills and Workforce Development

TTS Nigeria is structured around skills and workforce development, with programme monitoring covering areas such as specialization tracks, skill assessments, workforce readiness, employer alignment, and employment outcomes.

Participants may have information recorded relating to:

Their training cohort

Their specialization track

Attendance

Skill-assessment outcomes

Workforce-readiness indicators

Employer-alignment assessments

Employment status

Placement outcomes

This demonstrates the programme’s strong focus on the relationship between training and participants’ eventual workforce outcomes.

Rather than considering training as an isolated activity, TTS Nigeria aims to understand how participants progress through the programme and how their skills can translate into stronger employment pathways.

Employment Matching and Placement Opportunities

Another important component of the programme is its connection with BPO partner firms, employers and hiring partners.

The programme information indicates that participant data may eventually be shared with BPO partner firms for employment matching and placement purposes, subject to additional explicit consent from participants at the placement stage.

This employment-oriented component is significant because the initiative is designed not only to develop skills but also to contribute to workforce participation and employment pathways.

Participants should, however, understand that the available programme information does not guarantee that every individual who completes the programme will automatically receive employment.

Focus on Women and Inclusive Economic Opportunities

TTS Nigeria places particular emphasis on creating opportunities for young women.

The programme also recognizes the importance of improving opportunities for groups that may experience additional barriers to economic participation.

Information provided in the programme’s consent documentation specifically refers to creating more opportunities for:

Young women

Persons with disabilities

Internally displaced persons

Where applicable, participants may be asked about disability or Internally Displaced Person (IDP) status so that programme organizers can understand participant circumstances and support inclusive programme delivery.

However, the fundamental eligibility criteria remain that applicants must be female Nigerian citizens between 18 and 35 years old.

Programme Locations

TTS Nigeria is scheduled to operate across 12 states in Nigeria.

The registration information provided does not list the names of all 12 states. Applicants should therefore rely on the official TTS Nigeria application platform and programme communications for confirmation of participating states, training locations, and any location-specific requirements.

Applicants may be asked to provide their:

State of residence

Local government area of residence

Residential information

These details may help organizers understand participant distribution and manage programme delivery across the participating locations.

What Information May Applicants and Participants Be Asked to Provide?

Applicants who successfully pass the basic eligibility stage may be required to provide further personal, educational, professional, and programme-related information.

TTS Nigeria indicates that it may collect some or all of the following information:

Full name and age.

Gender.

Phone number and email address.

Residential address.

State of residence.

Local government area of residence.

Training cohort information.

Specialization track.

Attendance records.

Marital status.

Disability status, where applicable.

Internally Displaced Person status, where applicable.

Educational background.

Previous work experience.

Skill-assessment results.

Workforce-readiness indicators.

Employer-alignment assessments.

Employment status.

Placement outcomes.

Feedback and survey responses.

Photographs or video recordings from programme activities, with separate consent where required.

Applicants should carefully read the programme’s consent and privacy information before submitting personal information.

Why Does TTS Nigeria Collect Participant Information?

According to the programme, participant information is collected to help Tech4Dev and its partners understand programme participation and outcomes while improving delivery.

The information may be used for purposes including:

Tracking participation and completion rates.

Assessing participants’ skill development.

Understanding employment outcomes.

Monitoring and evaluating programme effectiveness.

Improving programme design and delivery.

Supporting participant success.

Reporting programme progress and impact to the Mastercard Foundation.

Conducting research relating to workforce participation.

Studying employment pathways.

Understanding economic inclusion.

Supporting research relating to the growth of Nigeria’s technology BPO sector.

The programme states that information identifying participants will not be shared without permission except where required by law or programme safeguarding requirements.

Data Sharing and Programme Partners

TTS Nigeria explains that participant data may be shared with relevant organizations involved in programme implementation, evaluation and employment support.

Depending on consent and the purpose involved, these may include:

Mastercard Foundation, the programme’s funding partner.

Other implementing partners involved in similar Mastercard Foundation programmes.

Third-party data processors working with the Mastercard Foundation for monitoring and evaluation.

Third-party processors legitimately engaged by Tech4Dev for programme implementation with the necessary Mastercard Foundation approval.

BPO employers and hiring partners for employment matching and placement, subject to additional explicit participant consent at the placement stage.

Applicants are encouraged to read the relevant privacy policies before deciding whether to provide consent for data sharing.

Giving Consent Is Separate From Programme Participation

An important feature of the TTS Nigeria application process is the distinction between programme participation and consent to data sharing.

According to the consent information, applicants are not obligated to provide consent to data sharing in order to participate in the programme.

The programme states that a participant’s decision regarding data sharing will not affect their eligibility to participate in the programme.

Applicants therefore have a choice regarding whether they agree to share their data with TTS Nigeria, Mastercard Foundation, and relevant third-party data processors for the purposes described in the consent documentation.

Applicants should carefully read the consent statement before selecting their preferred option.

Participants’ Data Rights

TTS Nigeria outlines several rights participants have regarding their personal information.

These include:

Right to Access

Participants can request a copy of the personal information held about them.

Right to Rectification

Participants can ask for inaccurate information to be corrected.

Right to Erasure

Participants may request deletion of their information.

Right to Restriction of Processing

Participants can request restrictions on how their information is processed.

Right to Object to Processing

Participants can object to certain processing of their information.

Right to Data Portability

Participants can request that their data be transferred to another organization where applicable.

These rights are particularly important for applicants who want greater control over how their personal information is handled throughout the programme.

Can Participants Withdraw Their Consent?

Yes.

Participants who initially consent to sharing their information can withdraw that consent later.

The programme states that withdrawing consent will not affect an individual’s ability to participate in TTS Nigeria.

Participants wishing to withdraw consent can contact the TTS Nigeria Data Protection Officer through the contact information supplied by the programme.

Email: monitoring@ttsnigeria.org

Phone: +2347068556072

Applicants should retain relevant programme documentation and consent information for their records.

Why Participant Data Matters to the Programme

TTS Nigeria explains that participant information can help the programme better understand whether its interventions are achieving their intended objectives.

Data and participant feedback can help the programme:

Demonstrate programme impact to funders and stakeholders.

Improve programme design.

Strengthen workforce-readiness support.

Improve the participant experience.

Support advocacy around youth employment.

Generate insights into Nigeria’s technology BPO sector.

Support the development of additional opportunities for young women.

Improve inclusion for persons with disabilities and internally displaced persons.

Applicants should nevertheless make their own informed decision regarding consent after reviewing the programme’s privacy information.

How to Apply for the TTS Nigeria Programme

Eligible candidates interested in participating should complete the official TTS Nigeria Programme Registration Form.

The application begins with basic programme information, consent information, and an eligibility screening.

The general process is:

Access the official TTS Nigeria registration form.

Read the programme information carefully before beginning.

Review the participant consent and data-protection information.

Indicate your decision regarding data-sharing consent.

Confirm that you understand the eligibility requirements.

Complete the initial eligibility screening.

Confirm that you are female.

Confirm that you are a Nigerian citizen.

Confirm that you fall within the required age range of 18–35.

If eligible, proceed to the full application.

Provide the requested information accurately and honestly.

Review your responses before submitting the form.

Applicants should remember that completion of the application does not guarantee admission or selection into the programme.

The application is the first stage through which TTS Nigeria can assess applicants’ backgrounds, training needs, and suitability for available opportunities.

Important Information Before Applying

Prospective applicants should keep several important points in mind.

First, the programme is free, so applicants should be cautious about any unofficial individual or platform requesting payment in exchange for programme admission.

Second, applicants must provide accurate information. False information can lead to disqualification during the application or selection process.

Third, only female Nigerian citizens aged 18–35 meet the stated basic eligibility requirements.

Fourth, completing the registration form does not guarantee selection.

Finally, applicants should carefully review all consent and privacy information before providing personal information.

Application Deadline

No specific application deadline is stated in the programme registration information provided.

Prospective applicants are therefore encouraged to complete their applications as early as possible and check the official TTS Nigeria platform for any subsequently announced deadline, cohort timelines, or application updates.

The overall programme runs from February 2026 to July 2027.

APPLY NOW

About Tech4Dev

The Technology for Social Change and Development Initiative (Tech4Dev) is the lead implementing organization for the Technology Talent Services Nigeria Programme.

Through TTS Nigeria, the organization is working with the Mastercard Foundation to support skills development, workforce participation, employment pathways, and economic inclusion, particularly for young Nigerian women.

The programme also seeks to generate insights that can strengthen workforce-development initiatives and contribute to the growth of Nigeria’s technology BPO sector.

About the Mastercard Foundation’s Role

The Mastercard Foundation is identified as the funding partner for the TTS Nigeria Programme.

Programme monitoring and evaluation information may be used to report progress and impact to the Foundation and to generate broader insights into workforce development, economic inclusion, and employment pathways.

Applicants should consult the respective privacy policies of Tech4Dev/TTS Nigeria and the Mastercard Foundation for further information about personal-data processing.

Conclusion

The TTS Nigeria Programme 2026–2027 presents an important skills and workforce-development opportunity for young Nigerian women interested in strengthening their capabilities and positioning themselves for employment opportunities within a changing technology-driven economy.

Implemented by the Technology for Social Change and Development Initiative (Tech4Dev) and funded by the Mastercard Foundation, the free 18-month programme will operate across 12 Nigerian states between February 2026 and July 2027.

With an emphasis on skills development, workforce readiness, employment pathways, economic inclusion, and Nigeria’s growing technology BPO sector, TTS Nigeria is designed to help participants move beyond training toward stronger workforce participation.

To meet the basic eligibility requirements, applicants must be female Nigerian citizens between 18 and 35 years old. Candidates who satisfy these requirements can proceed through the eligibility screening and complete the full programme application.

Because no specific application deadline is included in the registration information provided, interested and eligible candidates should apply as early as possible and continue checking official TTS Nigeria communications for application deadlines, cohort information, participating locations, and other programme updates.

Applicants should also remember that registration does not guarantee selection and that all information submitted during the application process should be complete, accurate, and truthful.

Theme : Revitalizing the 21st Century Higher Education Quality Assurance (QA) Personnel, Systems, Tools, Processes and Procedures

Access Concept Note Here – UNISA QA Workshop Concept Note

Aim of the workshop

Intensive training to equip HE QA personnel with the foundations for efficient and effective operations. Key aspects to be covered include internal and external QA: Strategies for developing, promoting and sustaining the quality culture, QA policies, manuals and management systems, research quality, curriculum design and review, teaching and learning, effective student assessment, dealing with resistance to QA, preparing for institutional and programme accreditation.

The designing and use of communication, documentation and data collection tools in QA for monitoring and evaluation of students and staff. In addition, the workshop aims to sensitize and bring awareness on what quality in HE is now all about and the current continental and regional activities related to QA and assist to develop QA knowledge and skills of Higher and Tertiary Education personnel since most of them do not have the professional qualifications.

Objectives of the workshop

Create an awareness on the Pan African Quality Assurance and Accreditation Framework (PAQAF) and the associated aspects including the Addis Convention, Agenda 2063, Continental Education Strategy for Africa (CESA), African Quality Rating Mechanism (AQRM), African Standards and Guidelines (ASG-QA), Tuning Africa, the Pan-African University and the Harmonization of African Higher Education Quality Assurance and Accreditation (HAQAA)
Share knowledge and information on the important endowments and characteristics of a robust higher education QA system.
Equip participants with the background knowledge that informs good QA practices in HE.
Share knowledge and skills of the diverse ways of assuring quality in institutions of higher learning in order to expose to participants the importance of viable QA systems.
Make known to participants the recommended new modes and models of QA for HE institutions.
Bring awareness of Quality Assurance and increase the visibility of the Quality Assurance activities in African Higher Education.
Foster cooperation with other Quality Assurance Officers of higher education within the continent.
Disseminate Quality Assurance endeavours and benchmarks in African Higher education through all the possible means of communication.
Encourage the harmonization of African Higher Education through the African Standards, Guidelines and Benchmarks as well as the African Quality Rating Mechanism (AQRM) tool for institutional evaluations for QA in HEIs.
Train and sustain a pool of QA Officers in the region for the multiplier effect of quality assurance in African Higher Education Institutions.

TITLE: Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships 2027

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: December 1, 2026

Applications are open for the Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships 2027. The Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships support visual storytellers undertaking long-term documentary photography projects that explore environmental and conservation challenges and, importantly, the people and communities working toward solutions.

The program has a dual purpose: to provide financial support and mentorship to photographers developing significant bodies of work while fostering meaningful collaboration with communities and organizations engaged in environmental and wildlife conservation. They are particularly interested in stories that move beyond documenting environmental problems to illuminate the people, communities, and initiatives working toward meaningful solutions.

Benefits

In 2027, Vital Impacts will award:

One $20,000 fellowship to an established environmental photographer;

Six $5,000 fellowships to emerging photographers from around the world; and

Ten mentorships to photographers whose work demonstrates strong potential and would benefit from additional guidance and professional support.

Eligibility

Vital Impacts is particularly interested in photographers who have a meaningful, established relationship with the people, places, and issues they are documenting. They believe the strongest environmental stories often emerge from photographers who have taken the time to listen, build trust, understand context, and return to a story over time.

They strongly encourage applications from photographers documenting environmental and conservation stories in their own communities. Local photographers bring perspectives, knowledge, access, and relationships that can offer a depth and authenticity that outsiders may not have.

At the same time, they recognize that meaningful relationships with a community or issue can take many forms. You do not have to live permanently in a place to have a genuine connection to it. They will also consider photographers who can demonstrate sustained knowledge and engagement through recurring travel, long-term collaboration, professional or academic experience, or other meaningful relationships with the community or issue they propose to document.

Applicants should clearly demonstrate why they are the right person to tell this story: what they know, whom they know, what relationships they have built, and what perspective they bring that will allow them to tell the story with depth, context, and care.

They are looking for photographers who are committed to long-term storytelling rather than short-term access—photographers willing to invest the time necessary for trust to develop, relationships to deepen, and more nuanced stories to emerge.

Application

All applicants must:

Submit up to 20 JPEG images representing one or two bodies of work or photo stories. Applicants may submit 10 images from one project and 10 from another, or, if preferred, up to 15-20 images from a single project. The selection should demonstrate the applicant’s experience and ability in documentary storytelling, rather than simply present a collection of individual photographs.

Submit a 25-word synopsis of the proposed project.

Submit a 500-word project statement that describes the project, the environmental issue it explores, and the personal connection that drives the work. The statement should articulate what the photographer hopes the project will reveal, communicate, or change—and the impact they hope it will have on audiences, communities, or conservation efforts.

Submit a biography of up to 1,500 characters.

Provide requested social media information.

Agree to abide by the Vital Impacts Code of Ethics.

Agree to and sign the Vital Impacts Environmental Fellowship or Mentorship Agreement if selected.

Click here to apply

For more information, visit Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships.

TITLE: Comic Relief Community Fund 2026/27: Grants of Up to £5,000 for Grassroots Organisations in England

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Grassroots organisations working to address pressing social challenges in their local communities can apply for funding through the Comic Relief Community Fund (England) 2026/27. Delivered by Groundwork in partnership with Comic Relief, the programme is designed to provide financial support to community-led organisations that are creating positive change and improving the lives of people in their communities.

For the 2026/27 funding round, grants of up to £5,000 will be awarded to organisations in England. The programme has a particular focus on initiatives addressing homelessness and the cost of living, early childhood development, violence against women and girls, and the safety and wellbeing of refugees, asylum seekers and people experiencing forced migration.

With a total funding allocation of just over £600,000, the programme expects to support approximately 120 organisations across England.

What Is the Comic Relief Community Fund?

The Comic Relief Community Fund is a grant programme supporting grassroots and community-led organisations that are working to make a meaningful difference in their local communities.

Groundwork has partnered with Comic Relief to deliver the programme in England since 2019. The initiative recognises that smaller, locally rooted organisations often have a strong understanding of the challenges faced by their communities because they work directly with people experiencing those challenges.

The fund therefore seeks to support organisations that draw on the lived experience of the people and communities they serve when developing and delivering their work.

For the 2026/27 programme, funding will be directed towards organisations undertaking projects that respond to some of the most significant social and economic challenges affecting communities in England.

Comic Relief Community Fund 2026/27 Key Details

Applicants should take note of the following important information:

Funding amount: Grants of up to £5,000

Total funding available: Just over £600,000

Expected number of organisations supported: Approximately 120

Location: England

Application opening date: Tuesday, 1 September 2026

Application deadline: 5pm on Wednesday, 30 September 2026

Project completion deadline: All funded projects must be delivered by 30 September 2027

Eligible costs: Funding can support project costs, core organisational costs, or a combination of both

Geographical requirement: Organisations must be located in the same region in which their funded projects will be delivered

Previous grant recipients: Organisations receiving a 2025/26 grant may apply for the new funding round provided their previous project is completed and the required end-of-grant report has been submitted by 30 September 2026

Applicants are encouraged to review the full programme criteria and application guidance before submitting an application.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Successful organisations can receive a grant of up to £5,000.

Although the individual grant size is relatively small, the funding is intended to provide flexible support to grassroots organisations that may have limited access to larger funding opportunities.

The programme has a total allocation of just over £600,000, with approximately 120 organisations expected to receive funding.

The funding can be particularly useful for community organisations seeking to:

Launch a new local project.

Expand an existing community initiative.

Respond to an emerging need within their community.

Cover eligible core organisational costs.

Strengthen the delivery of an existing programme.

Combine organisational and project-related expenditure.

Support activities designed around the needs and experiences of local beneficiaries.

What Will the Comic Relief Community Fund Support?

The 2026/27 programme has identified several priority areas. Organisations should ensure that their proposed activities clearly demonstrate how they respond to the needs addressed by the fund.

1. Tackling Homelessness

One of the major priorities of the 2026/27 programme is tackling homelessness.

Funding may therefore be relevant to grassroots organisations working with people who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, or experiencing barriers to secure and stable housing.

Community-led organisations addressing homelessness may be involved in initiatives that respond to local needs and help vulnerable people access appropriate support, improve their circumstances or strengthen their connection with community services.

2. Addressing Cost-of-Living Concerns

The fund also focuses on initiatives supporting people experiencing cost-of-living concerns.

Rising household costs can place significant pressure on individuals and families, particularly those already experiencing financial insecurity or other forms of disadvantage.

Grassroots organisations with initiatives designed to help communities cope with cost-of-living challenges may therefore find this funding opportunity relevant to their work.

Projects should demonstrate an understanding of the challenges facing the communities they serve and explain how the proposed activities can contribute to positive local change.

3. Supporting Early Childhood Development

Another priority area is early childhood development.

The programme recognises the importance of supporting children during the early stages of life and initiatives that contribute to positive childhood development may be considered within the fund’s priorities.

Community organisations working with children, families and caregivers can consider whether their existing or proposed activities align with this focus.

Projects should demonstrate a clear connection between the proposed activities and the needs of the children, families or communities they seek to support.

4. Preventing Violence Against Women and Girls

The 2026/27 fund also prioritises projects supporting the prevention of violence against women and girls.

This provides an opportunity for grassroots organisations working to improve safety, awareness, prevention, community support and related areas to seek financial assistance for eligible activities.

Organisations should clearly explain the problem they are addressing, the communities affected and how their proposed work can contribute to preventing violence or improving safety and support.

5. Supporting Refugees and Asylum Seekers

The fund includes initiatives that support the safety of refugees and asylum seekers.

Organisations working directly with refugee and asylum-seeking communities may therefore consider whether their activities meet the programme’s criteria.

This could be particularly relevant to community-led organisations with strong local relationships and an understanding of the challenges faced by refugees and asylum seekers.

6. Supporting People Experiencing Forced Migration

The programme also recognises the needs of people experiencing forced migration.

Grassroots organisations supporting people affected by displacement and forced migration can explore the programme criteria to determine whether their proposed activities qualify for funding.

A strong application should demonstrate how the organisation’s work responds to locally identified needs and how the project can create meaningful benefits for the people it supports.

What Can the Grant Funding Be Used For?

One of the important features of the Comic Relief Community Fund is the flexibility around eligible expenditure.

Funding can be used for:

Project costs

Core organisational costs

A combination of project and core organisational costs

This flexibility can be particularly valuable for grassroots organisations because smaller community organisations may require support not only for individual activities but also for the organisational capacity needed to deliver those activities effectively.

Applicants should nevertheless consult the official application guidance to understand the specific costs and activities permitted under the programme.

Who Can Apply?

The Comic Relief Community Fund is intended for grassroots, community-led organisations based in England that are working to create positive change within their local communities.

The programme places importance on organisations that understand the needs of their communities and draw on the lived experience of the people they support.

An organisation considering applying should carefully assess the full eligibility requirements contained in the official application guidance before preparing its application.

Geographic Eligibility

The 2026/27 programme is specifically for organisations in England.

An important requirement is that an organisation must be located in the same region where the funded project will be delivered.

This means organisations should pay close attention to the geographic relationship between their own location and the location of their proposed activities.

The opportunity is therefore not a general international grant programme. Organisations based outside England should not assume that they are eligible simply because their work addresses one of the programme’s priority areas.

Organisational Size and Grassroots Focus

Groundwork has worked with Comic Relief since 2019 as an intermediary funder supporting grassroots community organisations in England, particularly organisations with a turnover of under £250,000.

Applicants should check the current application guidance to confirm the precise eligibility requirements for the 2026/27 funding round rather than relying solely on previous programme information.

The grassroots focus is important because the fund is designed to reach organisations that are closely connected to the communities they serve.

Can Previous Comic Relief Community Fund Recipients Apply?

Yes, organisations that received a 2025/26 grant can apply to the new 2026/27 fund.

However, there is an important condition.

Their previous project must have been completed and the required end-of-grant report submitted by Wednesday, 30 September 2026.

Organisations that received previous funding should therefore ensure that they have completed all reporting requirements before applying for the new funding round.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although receiving a grant is not guaranteed, applicants can improve the quality of their submissions by clearly demonstrating the relevance and impact of their proposed work.

1. Clearly Identify the Community Need

Start by explaining the issue your organisation is addressing.

A strong application should make it easy for the funder to understand:

What problem exists?

Who is affected?

Where does the problem occur?

Why is the issue important?

What evidence or lived experience demonstrates the need?

Why is your organisation well positioned to respond?

2. Connect Your Project to a Priority Area

Your proposal should clearly demonstrate how it relates to one or more of the fund’s 2026/27 priorities.

These include:

Homelessness

Cost-of-living concerns

Early childhood development

Prevention of violence against women and girls

Safety of refugees and asylum seekers

Support for people experiencing forced migration

Avoid presenting a project without clearly explaining its connection to the programme’s priorities.

3. Demonstrate Community Involvement

The programme places emphasis on community-led approaches and lived experience.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate how the people they support have influenced the organisation’s understanding of the issue and, where relevant, the design and delivery of the proposed project.

4. Explain How the Money Will Be Used

Because grants are limited to a maximum of £5,000, applicants should present a realistic and clearly structured budget.

Explain how the requested funding will contribute to the proposed activities and how each major cost supports the project’s objectives.

5. Demonstrate Local Impact

Applicants should explain the expected benefits of the project for the local community.

Consider describing:

Who will benefit.

How many people may benefit.

What activities will be delivered.

What changes the project is expected to achieve.

How the organisation will know whether the project has made a difference.

6. Check the Eligibility Criteria Carefully

Before submitting an application, organisations should read the full programme criteria and application guidance.

This is especially important because the fund has specific requirements relating to organisational location, project delivery, previous grants and other eligibility considerations.

Previous Impact of the Comic Relief and Groundwork Partnership

The partnership between Groundwork and Comic Relief has been operating since 2019.

According to the programme information, the partnership has so far achieved significant reach across communities in England.

The programme reports:

£6.3 million in grant funding awarded.

1,462 grants awarded.

Approximately 156,000 beneficiaries supported.

Around 3,000 volunteering opportunities created.

These figures illustrate the scale of the partnership’s support for grassroots organisations and the communities they serve.

Important Deadline for the Comic Relief Community Fund 2026/27

The application window opens on:

Tuesday, 1 September 2026

The deadline for applications is:

5pm on Wednesday, 30 September 2026

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. Organisations should allow sufficient time to review the eligibility criteria, prepare their project information, develop a realistic budget and check the application before submission.

All successful projects must be delivered by:

30 September 2027

Organisations that received a 2025/26 grant and intend to apply for the new funding round must also ensure that their previous project has been completed and the end-of-grant report submitted by 30 September 2026.

How to Apply for the Comic Relief Community Fund

Organisations interested in applying should visit the official Groundwork Comic Relief Community Fund website and access the How to Apply section.

The application guidance provides the detailed programme criteria that applicants need to understand before submitting their proposals.

Applicants should use the official guidance as the authoritative source for determining eligibility, eligible expenditure, application requirements and other conditions.
