TITLE: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship Spring 2027: Fully Funded Three-Month Programme With $18,000–$24,000 Stipends

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy AI Policy Fellowship Spring 2027, a fully funded, three-month professional programme designed for people seeking to build practical careers in artificial intelligence policy, governance and strategy.

The fellowship offers participants the opportunity to work directly on live AI policy projects, receive individual mentorship from experienced policy specialists, strengthen their professional networks and develop the practical skills needed to address the risks and opportunities associated with increasingly powerful artificial intelligence systems.

Full-time participants will receive a stipend of US$18,000 as Fellows or US$24,000 as Senior Fellows. Participants based in Washington, D.C., or London will receive an additional US$3,000. The programme will also fund travel and accommodation for the mandatory opening residency in Washington, D.C.

The Spring 2027 programme will run from February 22 to May 14, 2027. Applications must be submitted by September 27, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time.

IAPS AI Policy Fellowship Spring 2027 at a Glance

Organising institution: Institute for AI Policy and Strategy

Programme dates: February 22–May 14, 2027

Duration: Three months

Programme locations: Washington, D.C.; London; or remote

Opening residency: February 22–March 5, 2027, in Washington, D.C.

Available tracks: Research Track and Applied Track

Regular Fellow stipend: US$18,000

Senior Fellow stipend: US$24,000

Additional location stipend: US$3,000 for Washington, D.C., or London participants

Professional development support: US$500

Travel and accommodation: Financially supported for the opening Washington, D.C., residency

Expected cohort size: Up to 45 participants

Application deadline: September 27, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time

Official reference and application information: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship

About the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy

The Institute for AI Policy and Strategy, commonly known as IAPS, is a nonpartisan think tank conducting policy research on the consequences of advanced artificial intelligence.

Its work covers the implications of today’s most advanced AI systems as well as the possibility of future artificial general intelligence and superintelligence. IAPS seeks to develop practical policy solutions that can help governments, policymakers and industry leaders protect innovation while responsibly navigating significant risks and opportunities.

The organisation’s research sits at the intersection of:

Artificial intelligence policy

National security

International security

Geopolitics

Technology governance

Advanced computing

AI verification and compliance

Cybersecurity

Institutional resilience

Frontier AI governance

IAPS operates as a United States 501(c)(3) nonprofit organisation and describes its work as nonpartisan.

Purpose of the Spring 2027 Programme

The IAPS AI Policy Fellowship is a talent-development programme intended to expand the number of capable professionals working on important AI policy challenges.

As frontier AI systems become more powerful, governments and other institutions will need people who understand not only the technology but also its political, regulatory, economic and national-security implications.

The fellowship responds to this need by allowing participants to enter the active AI policy field rather than studying it only at a theoretical level. Fellows work on practical projects connected to current policy priorities and receive guidance from established experts.

The programme aims to help participants:

Develop practical AI policy skills

Gain experience working on policy-relevant projects

Understand the implications of frontier AI

Build professional relationships across the AI governance sector

Produce work that may influence national or international policy

Translate existing professional skills into AI policy expertise

Prepare for future positions in government, industry, academia or think tanks

Programme Dates and Structure

The Spring 2027 programme will run from February 22 to May 14, 2027.

The fellowship is divided into two main stages.

Opening Residency in Washington, D.C.

The first two weeks, from February 22 to March 5, 2027, will consist of an in-person programme in Washington, D.C.

Under the standard programme arrangement, all fellows—including those who select the London or remote options—must attend this opening event.

During the residency, participants will:

Meet the IAPS team and other fellows

Connect with their assigned supervisors

Receive training on advanced AI systems

Examine current AI policy challenges

Refine and workshop their fellowship projects

Attend policy briefings and expert roundtables

Participate in networking activities

Exchange ideas with researchers and policy professionals

Become familiar with the broader AI policy ecosystem

IAPS will provide financial support for travel and accommodation connected with this two-week event.

Ten-Week Project Period

Following the Washington residency, fellows will spend approximately ten weeks working with an AI policy expert on an assigned or approved project.

Projects may address policy challenges with potential national or international significance. Examples of policy areas highlighted by IAPS include:

Semiconductor and AI chip export controls

AI verification technology

Compliance mechanisms for international AI agreements

AI-enabled cyberattacks

Integrity and security of advanced AI systems

Institutional resilience

Democratic oversight of AI

International AI governance

Risks of extreme concentration of technological power

The exact project will be determined through discussion between the fellow, IAPS and the relevant supervisor.

Research Track

The Research Track is designed for participants interested in producing a substantial piece of AI policy research.

Research Track fellows are paired with an IAPS researcher or, in some cases, an external supervisor at a partner organisation. During the first part of the programme, the fellow and supervisor define a specific research question and agree on the project’s scope.

The fellow then takes primary responsibility for:

Conducting the research

Identifying and assessing relevant evidence

Selecting appropriate research methods

Developing evidence-based conclusions

Writing for a policy audience

Responding to supervisory feedback

Revising and improving the final output

The objective is to develop the ability to take a research project from an open policy question to a rigorous and potentially publishable final product.

Former participants have published reports and other policy outputs based on work completed during the programme.

Applied Track

The Applied Track focuses on hands-on policy work rather than requiring every participant to produce one major research paper.

Projects on the Applied Track may change in response to real-world policy developments. Participants must therefore be prepared to work flexibly and respond to changing priorities.

Applied projects may involve:

Drafting policy briefings

Preparing proposals

Supporting legislative analysis

Reviewing legislative drafts

Developing technical policy guidelines

Organising high-level convenings

Planning policy workshops

Evaluating grant applications

Supporting policy communications

Collaborating on policy memoranda

Conducting research for immediate policy decisions

This track is particularly useful for professionals moving into AI policy from adjacent areas such as government, operations, programme management, public administration, event organisation, grantmaking or nonprofit leadership.

It may also suit researchers who want to transition from primarily academic work into more practical policy roles.

Applicants who are uncertain about the most suitable track may express interest in both. IAPS can then assess where the applicant’s professional background, interests and abilities are likely to fit best.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

Fellows are expected to take considerable ownership of their work.

Depending on the project and track, regular responsibilities may include:

Conducting policy research

Reviewing academic and policy literature

Preparing briefings and proposals

Producing policy memoranda

Organising ambitious convenings

Analysing proposed legislation

Contributing to technical guidelines

Engaging with experts and stakeholders

Presenting work to IAPS staff

Revising outputs following expert feedback

Managing project timelines and deliverables

Fellows will have weekly meetings with their AI policy mentor and an IAPS manager. They will also present their projects during the final week of the programme.

Mentorship, Coaching and Professional Support

Every fellow will be paired with an expert mentor from IAPS or its wider professional network.

The mentorship relationship is intended to provide practical exposure to AI policy work rather than general career advice alone.

In addition to project supervision, fellows will receive:

Weekly one-to-one coaching from an IAPS Fellowship Coordinator

Career-development guidance

Project-management support

Productivity coaching

Ongoing assistance from IAPS researchers and policy staff

Direct feedback through weekly work-in-progress sessions

Access to the IAPS professional network

Additional financial assistance for career transitions in selected cases

The weekly work-in-progress sessions provide an opportunity to discuss challenges, receive feedback and learn from the work of other fellows.

How Fellows Are Matched With Mentors and Projects

After the cohort has been selected, IAPS will collect information about each fellow’s:

Policy interests

Professional background

Existing skills

Career objectives

Preferred research or applied-policy areas

Project preferences

IAPS will use this information to identify an appropriate project and mentor. Mentors retain the final decision on whether to supervise a particular fellow.

The normal arrangement is for fellows to become embedded within an existing supervisor’s workstream. This gives participants direct experience contributing to projects with a realistic route to policy influence.

A limited number of independent projects may also be approved. Independent proposals are most likely to be considered when an applicant presents a particularly strong project idea and has the skills required to carry it forward under supervision.

Applicants may indicate their interest in pursuing an independent project in the application.

Financial Support and Benefits

The programme provides a substantial funding package to enable fellows to focus on their work.

Full-Time Stipends

Regular Fellows will receive US$18,000 for the three-month programme.

Senior Fellows will receive US$24,000 for the three-month programme.

The distinction between a Fellow and Senior Fellow will be determined by IAPS based on the candidate’s experience and suitability.

Additional Location Stipend

Participants based in Washington, D.C., or London for the full programme will receive an additional US$3,000 stipend.

Professional Development Support

Fellows will receive a US$500 professional development stipend for the duration of the programme.

Healthcare Benefits

The official programme information states that fellows will receive access to healthcare benefits during their participation.

Travel and Accommodation

IAPS will provide financial support for travel and accommodation for the two-week Washington, D.C., opening residency.

Part-Time Stipends

Part-time participation may be offered to a limited number of exceptional candidates with employment or other significant commitments. Any stipend offered under a part-time arrangement will be calculated on a proportional basis.

Career-Transition Assistance

Additional financial assistance may be available in selected cases to support a fellow’s transition into an AI policy career. This is discretionary and should not be treated as an automatic benefit for every participant.

Washington, D.C., Programme Option

Participants choosing the Washington, D.C., option will work from the IAPS office alongside the D.C. cohort.

They will receive:

Access to IAPS office space

A dedicated desk and monitor

Daily lunch at the office

An additional US$3,000 stipend

Opportunities to interact regularly with IAPS staff

Access to visiting AI policy specialists

Additional office events and policy discussions

More frequent in-person networking opportunities

Applicants selecting this option must already have the right to work in the United States from February 22 to May 14, 2027. IAPS cannot sponsor a United States work visa for the programme.

London Programme Option

IAPS also maintains a hub and office space in London.

UK-based participants may work from the London office and receive the additional US$3,000 location stipend. They will have access to an in-person professional community, although IAPS states that London will have less active programming than Washington, D.C.

IAPS does not provide United Kingdom work visas. Applicants should therefore have appropriate existing permission to work in the United Kingdom if they want to select this option.

Remote Programme Option

IAPS operates as a remote-first organisation and can support participants working from many countries.

However, the ability to engage a remote fellow depends on legal and administrative requirements in the fellow’s country. There may therefore be country-specific exceptions.

Applicants with questions about whether IAPS can legally engage them in their country should contact fellowship@iaps.ai.

Remote participants are still expected, under the standard programme structure, to attend the opening two-week event in Washington, D.C.

Visa Arrangements for the Washington Residency

IAPS can provide invitation letters to support the visa application process for remote and international fellows attending the Washington residency.

However:

IAPS cannot guarantee that a visa will be issued.

Fellows are responsible for applying for and obtaining the required visa.

IAPS does not provide additional individual visa-processing support.

IAPS cannot provide work-visa sponsorship for the full Washington or London tracks.

Applicants who may need a United States visa should consider processing times before accepting an offer.

Part-Time Participation

The default arrangement is full-time participation.

IAPS may provide part-time options to exceptional candidates who have existing employment or other major commitments. The number of part-time places is normally limited, and accepted part-time fellows receive a proportionately reduced stipend.

Applicants should not assume that a part-time request will automatically be approved.

Flexibility and Possible Extensions

IAPS may allow some flexibility in the programme dates under exceptional circumstances.

A participant may be permitted to begin a few weeks after February 22. However, a delayed start may mean missing part or all of the Washington opening programme.

The standard end date is May 14, 2027. During the programme, participants may be allowed to apply for an extension. In the previous cohort, more than half of the fellows extended their participation by approximately four to twelve weeks.

An extension is not automatic and will depend on approval during the fellowship.

Expected Cohort Size

IAPS expects to select up to 45 fellows.

The final number may be lower depending on the strength of the applications, cohort composition and availability of suitable supervisors and projects.

Career Development and Alumni Outcomes

The fellowship is intended to provide a bridge into long-term AI policy careers.

Former participants have secured positions in:

Government

Technology and other industries

Research institutions

Universities

Policy organisations

Leading think tanks

Organisations where former fellows have progressed include:

AI Futures Project

Future of Life Institute

RAND

Institute for Progress

Center for Health Security

The Future Society

Institute for AI Policy and Strategy

Former fellows have also established new projects and organisations, published policy work and received recognition as emerging AI policy researchers.

Examples highlighted by IAPS include fellows who worked on AI integrity, international AI Safety Institute networks, democratic oversight of advanced AI and verification mechanisms for international AI agreements.

Examples of Fellowship Mentors

The IAPS network includes experts working across several specialist areas.

Featured mentors include professionals with experience in:

Technology and national-security policy

United States government institutions

AI verification

International AI agreements

International governance

AI system trustworthiness

Compute policy

Hardware-enabled compliance mechanisms

Institutional resilience

Risks arising from advanced AI systems

This range of expertise enables fellows to work on projects combining technical understanding with legal, political, regulatory and national-security considerations.

Application Structure

The current GuidedTrack application is expected to take approximately 45 minutes and contains five sections.

1. About You — Approximately Five Minutes

This section collects basic information and checks programme eligibility.

2. Your Experience — Approximately Five Minutes

Applicants provide information about:

Organisations where they have worked

The length of their experience

Positions or responsibilities held

The type of work they performed

3. Your Motivation — Approximately Ten Minutes

Applicants rank the AI policy issues that most strongly motivate them and complete two written responses:

A research-interest response of up to 300 words

A career-goals response of approximately 150–200 words

4. Communicating With Stakeholders — Approximately Ten Minutes

Applicants prepare a written response to a policy conversation. The expected length is approximately 100–200 words.

This section appears designed to assess how effectively an applicant can understand a policy discussion and communicate appropriately with relevant stakeholders.

5. Timed Reasoning — Approximately Fifteen Minutes

The final section contains timed logic and reasoning questions.

Applicants can choose when to begin the timed section, but once it has started, they cannot return to revise earlier answers within that section.

Restrictions on Using AI and Outside Assistance

The application specifically states that certain sections must be completed without:

Generative AI tools

Search engines

Assistance from another person

Other external help

The form will inform applicants when a restricted section begins and will require them to agree to the relevant conditions.

Applicants should follow these rules strictly. Submitting AI-generated or externally assisted responses in a prohibited section could undermine the integrity of the application.

Saving and Revising Application Answers

Answers are saved automatically as applicants progress.

Applicants may return to earlier sections using the back arrow and revise their responses, except after beginning the timed reasoning component.

Despite the automatic-save function, the organisers recommend completing the application in one sitting to reduce the risk of technical problems.

Applicants should prepare their employment history, career information and non-restricted written material before starting.

Accommodations

Applicants who require reasonable accommodations—such as additional time for the timed reasoning section—should contact fellowship@iaps.ai before beginning the application.

Applicants should make this request early rather than waiting until the application deadline.

AI-Assisted Application Assessment and Data Processing

The application requires applicants to consent to AI-assisted processing of their application data, including written responses.

The public consent statement explains that:

IAPS is the data controller.

Spark Wave operates the assessment platform and AI-assisted scoring on behalf of IAPS.

Third-party AI providers supply the underlying AI technology.

Optional demographic responses are excluded from AI-assisted scoring.

Special-category information, such as racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs or health information, is not intended to be used in AI evaluation.

Applicants may request human review of an AI-assisted assessment.

Applicants may exercise applicable rights to access, correct or request deletion of their information.

Applicants may withdraw consent subject to the applicable process.

Application information may be retained for up to 36 months after the selection round unless the applicant separately agrees to longer retention.

Applicants should read the current transparency and privacy notices carefully before providing consent and submitting personal information.

Selection Process and Timeline

The selection process will take place in several stages.

Initial Application Review

IAPS expects to respond to initial applicants by approximately mid-October 2026.

Written Task and Pre-Recorded Interview

Candidates selected from the initial application stage will be invited to complete:

A written assessment

A short pre-recorded interview

Live Interview

Applicants who progress further will participate in a live interview during November 2026.

Final Decisions

IAPS expects to finalise the Spring 2027 cohort by early December 2026.

Applicants should monitor their email regularly during the selection period, including spam or junk folders.

Live Question-and-Answer Webinar

IAPS will hold a live application webinar on September 10, 2026, at:

7:30 AM Pacific Time

10:30 AM Eastern Time

3:30 PM British Summer Time

Prospective applicants can register through the official IAPS fellowship page.

The webinar provides an opportunity to learn more about the programme, understand the application process and raise questions directly with the organisers.

How to Apply

Applicants should follow these steps:

Visit the official IAPS AI Policy Fellowship page.

Read the programme description and frequently asked questions.

Review the Research and Applied Tracks.

Consider the most suitable location option.

Confirm availability for the Washington, D.C., opening residency.

Check work-authorisation and visa requirements.

Review the application’s AI-use restrictions.

Request accommodations before starting, if necessary.

Follow the official application link to GuidedTrack.

Complete and submit the application before the deadline.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

September 27, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time

The exact closing time is confirmed in the official IAPS LinkedIn announcement.

International applicants should convert the deadline into their local time zone and avoid waiting until the final hours to submit.

Conclusion

The IAPS AI Policy Fellowship Spring 2027 provides a substantial opportunity for professionals who want to enter or advance within the rapidly developing field of artificial intelligence policy.

With stipends of US$18,000 for Fellows and US$24,000 for Senior Fellows, additional support for Washington and London participants, funded travel and accommodation for the opening residency, expert mentorship, weekly coaching and direct exposure to real policy projects, the programme combines financial assistance with serious professional development.

Its two-track structure makes it relevant to both research-focused candidates and professionals who want to apply existing skills to practical AI governance work. The possibility of remote participation also makes the programme internationally accessible, although applicants must carefully consider country-specific hiring restrictions and the mandatory Washington residency.

Interested candidates should review all conditions through the official IAPS fellowship page and submit their applications by September 27, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time.

TITLE: Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship 2027: Up to $10,000 in Project Funding and Leadership Support for Community Health Equity Leaders

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship 2027 is now accepting applications from community leaders with ideas for projects that can advance health equity and address social determinants of health within the M Health Fairview service area. The year-long fellowship is designed to help participants strengthen their leadership, develop their project ideas, receive expert guidance, and turn community-focused ideas into practical action.

The program, offered through the M Health Fairview Center for Community Health Equity, combines leadership development, education, coaching, technical assistance, peer learning, networking, and financial support. Each selected fellow can receive up to $10,000 in project funding, in addition to a $3,000 participation stipend intended to help support costs associated with participating in the fellowship.

For the 2027 cohort, eight fellows will be selected. The fellowship will run from January through December 2027, with sessions delivered through a combination of in-person meetings across the seven-county metro area and virtual sessions.

What Is the Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship?

The Accelerator Fellowship is a 12-month leadership development program created to support community leaders who are working on innovative approaches to health equity and the social conditions that influence people’s health and wellbeing.

Rather than requiring applicants to already have a completely developed project, the fellowship provides space for participants to develop, test, refine, and implement their ideas during the fellowship year.

The program is particularly focused on helping community leaders move from an identified community challenge toward a practical project with achievable goals and measurable activities.

According to M Health Fairview, fellows receive structured support to:

Build and strengthen leadership capacity

Sharpen their vision for community change

Develop and refine a health equity project

Receive coaching and technical assistance

Learn about health equity and project implementation

Connect with other community leaders

Develop partnerships and community relationships

Put their project ideas into action

Receive financial resources to support project implementation

Each fellow will be part of a cohort of eight community leaders who learn and grow together throughout the year.

Up to $10,000 in Project Funding

One of the major components of the 2027 Accelerator Fellowship is financial support for fellows’ community projects.

Each fellow can receive up to $10,000 in project funding to help bring their health equity project to life.

Importantly, applicants do not need to have a fully developed project when they apply. The fellowship provides the full year for fellows to build, test, and refine their approaches with support from coaches, experts, and peers.

The application specifically asks applicants to explain how the project funding will support their proposed activities and requires a draft project budget outlining expected expenses of up to $10,000.

In addition to project funding, the official FAQ states that fellows receive a $3,000 stipend to support participation in the fellowship. This may help cover costs such as compensation for time, transportation, childcare, or other incidental expenses. (mhealthfairview.org)

What Does the Fellowship Provide?

The Accelerator Fellowship offers several forms of support throughout the year.

1. Health Equity Education

Fellows participate in an educational curriculum covering health equity, program development, implementation, and related areas of community work.

The curriculum is designed to give participants both conceptual knowledge and practical tools that they can apply to their projects.

2. Coaching and Technical Assistance

Participants receive coaching and technical assistance from experts working in relevant fields.

This allows fellows to receive guidance while developing their projects, addressing challenges, refining their approaches, and moving from ideas toward implementation.

3. Project Funding

Fellows receive up to $10,000 to support implementation of their health equity projects.

This funding is intended to help participants turn their ideas into practical community initiatives rather than simply developing theoretical proposals.

4. Networking and Peer Learning

The fellowship creates opportunities for participants to build relationships with other community leaders and professionals whose interests align with their work.

Because the eight fellows progress through the program together, the cohort provides an environment for shared learning, collaboration, and exchange of different perspectives.

What Types of Projects Can Applicants Propose?

The fellowship is focused on projects that address health equity or social determinants of health within the eligible service area.

A project does not necessarily need to be a traditional healthcare project.

Health equity can involve the broader conditions that influence people’s ability to live healthy lives, including issues involving housing, food, education, community connection, environment, access to resources, and other structural or social factors.

The 2026 cohort illustrates the breadth of projects that can fit within the program. Previous fellows worked on initiatives involving culturally responsive nutrition, community barbering and mentorship, rural wellness, housing stability, Indigenous food and knowledge systems, transitional housing and recovery, and grief and trauma education.

This demonstrates that applicants can approach health equity from different professional, cultural, community, and disciplinary perspectives.

What Makes a Strong Project Idea?

According to the fellowship’s published criteria, a strong project should be community-rooted, meaning that it responds to a real and identified need within a specific community and demonstrates community engagement in shaping the idea.

The project should also be equity-focused, with the goal of reducing health disparities or addressing structural barriers to equity.

Applicants should also demonstrate that their project is:

Realistic

Actionable

Appropriately scoped for the fellowship period

Supported by achievable objectives

Based on a reasonable budget

Connected to an identified community need

The program also states that it values diversity of perspective over formal titles, meaning applicants are not required to rely solely on conventional professional credentials to demonstrate their ability to contribute. (mhealthfairview.org)

Who Is the Fellowship Looking For?

The Accelerator Fellowship is designed for community leaders, and applicants can come from different professional backgrounds and career stages.

The published FAQ states that applicants from all backgrounds, professions, and career stages are welcome. The fellowship looks for individuals who have contributed to their communities professionally or personally and who demonstrate commitment to health equity. (mhealthfairview.org)

Applicants are expected to demonstrate qualities such as:

Community orientation

Commitment to health equity

Collaboration

Resourcefulness

Commitment to participating fully

Authenticity

Openness and curiosity

A solution-oriented approach

The fellowship is specifically for individual applicants rather than organizations. (mhealthfairview.org)

Eligibility Requirements for the 2027 Cohort

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

Have a project idea focused on advancing health equity in their community.

Plan to implement the project within Fairview’s service area.

Be at least 18 years old.

Not currently be employed by Fairview Health Services.

Have related experience, relationships, or community ties to the issue or topic they want to address.

Be available to attend all required fellowship sessions.

The program is therefore not simply looking for people with an interesting idea. Applicants should be able to demonstrate some meaningful relationship with the issue or community they want to serve.

Where Must the Project Be Implemented?

A particularly important eligibility requirement is geography.

The project must be implemented within the M Health Fairview service area.

Therefore, this is not an open worldwide fellowship. The proposed project must be located within the specified M Health Fairview service-area geography. (mhealthfairview.org)

Fellowship Duration and Format

The 2027 Accelerator Fellowship runs for 12 months, from January through December 2027.

Sessions will combine:

In-person sessions

Virtual sessions

Workshops

Learning activities

Leadership development

Project work

Coaching

Peer learning

Most months will include two sessions, which may consist of full-day in-person meetings or shorter virtual sessions.

The published FAQ estimates approximately 105 hours of in-class time over the fellowship, in addition to the time fellows need to spend implementing their individual projects. (mhealthfairview.org)

Areas Covered by the Fellowship Curriculum

The program’s curriculum is designed to develop both leadership and practical project-management capabilities.

Topics include:

Orientation and foundations

Funding and evaluation

Project planning

Project management

Strategic communications

Community engagement

Community mapping and collaboration

Public health, policy, environment and systems change

Leadership and partnerships

Learning and coaching

Reflection and sharing

Celebration and showcase

The curriculum can adapt to the needs of the cohort, and the organizers note that session topics may change. (mhealthfairview.org)

Application Requirements

Applicants should prepare several components before submitting the application.

The required materials include:

Basic personal information

Two letters of recommendation

Narrative responses to the application questions

Additional information about the proposed project

A draft project budget

If the proposed project is affiliated with an organization, at least one recommendation/support letter should come from that organization.

Applicants should also download and review the full application and budget template before completing the online application.

The application process involves:

Reviewing the full application form.

Reviewing and completing the draft budget template.

Completing the online application.

Uploading two recommendation/support letters.

Uploading the draft budget.

Submitting the complete application before the deadline.

Application Questions

The application asks applicants to explain both their health equity vision and their leadership journey.

Your Vision for Health Equity

Applicants are asked to explain:

What health equity challenge they want to address

Why the issue matters to their community

What has contributed to their understanding of the issue

Why they are personally positioned to address it

What transformation they hope to achieve

What impact they intend to make

What their proposed project involves

How the $10,000 project funding would support the work

Their three primary objectives for the fellowship period

The application places a 1,500-character limit on the problem, proposal, and objectives responses.

Your Leadership Journey

Applicants are also asked to discuss their leadership experience and how their background, identity, relationships, and life experiences have shaped their approach to leadership.

The application allows applicants to provide examples of formal or informal leadership and explain how their leadership journey connects to their proposed project.

This section has a 2,000-character limit or a three-minute video option, with applicants choosing one format.

Applicants are additionally asked how the fellowship could support their leadership development, what they could contribute to the cohort, why the timing is appropriate, and what skills, resources, or technical assistance would help them achieve their health equity vision.

Selection and Number of Fellows

The 2027 fellowship will select eight applicants.

The selection process is competitive. Semi-finalists are expected to be notified in late October and invited to participate in an interview in early November. The interview can be conducted virtually if needed.

Final cohort selections are expected to be announced in mid-November, with all applicants notified of final decisions by late November.

Important Application Deadline

The deadline for the Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship 2027 is:

Thursday, October 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CST.

Applicants should ensure that the complete application, required recommendation letters, and draft budget are submitted before the deadline.

Is This a Scholarship or a Grant?

The Accelerator Fellowship is structured primarily as a leadership development fellowship with project funding, rather than a traditional academic scholarship.

The program combines:

Leadership development

Health equity education

Coaching

Technical assistance

Peer networking

Project implementation support

Up to $10,000 in project funding

A $3,000 participation stipend

It is also not a degree or credit-bearing academic program. (mhealthfairview.org)

Why This Fellowship May Be Relevant to Community Leaders

The fellowship is designed around the idea that many health challenges cannot be addressed through healthcare services alone.

Community conditions, social environments, access to resources, housing, food, education, relationships, and other factors can influence health outcomes. M Health Fairview’s Center for Community Health Equity works with community partners to address these broader determinants and reduce disparities. (mhealthfairview.org)

The Accelerator Fellowship therefore provides a structured environment in which community leaders can develop projects that respond to issues they understand through direct community experience.

The combination of project funding and leadership development also allows fellows to work on both sides of the challenge: strengthening their own capacity as leaders while developing a practical response to a community health equity issue.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants should pay close attention to the relationship between their community, problem, project, leadership experience, and proposed outcomes.

A strong application should clearly explain:

1. The community problem

Identify a specific health equity challenge rather than describing a broad social issue without context.

2. Why the problem matters

Explain how the issue affects the community and why addressing it is important.

3. Your connection to the issue

The fellowship specifically asks applicants to demonstrate related experience, relationships, or community ties.

4. Your proposed solution

Explain what you want to do and how the project would address the identified problem.

5. Your objectives

Define three realistic objectives that can be pursued between January and December 2027.

6. Your use of funding

Show how the proposed $10,000 would directly support project activities.

7. Your leadership story

The application is interested not only in the project but also in the person leading it. Explain how your experiences have shaped your approach to leadership.

8. Your readiness

Because fellows are expected to participate throughout the year, applicants should demonstrate that they can commit to the program’s sessions and project implementation requirements.

Conclusion

The Center for Community Health Equity Accelerator Fellowship 2027 provides a year-long opportunity for community leaders to develop health equity projects while strengthening their leadership skills and community connections. The program combines education, coaching, technical assistance, networking, and financial support, with each fellow eligible for up to $10,000 in project funding and a $3,000 participation stipend. The fellowship is particularly focused on individuals who understand a community health equity challenge through their experience, relationships, or community ties and who have an idea they want to develop into practical action. TITLE: City of Boston Special Projects Fellow 2026–2027: Apply for a One-Year Public Service Fellowship

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The City of Boston is inviting qualified candidates to apply for the Special Projects Fellow position within the Office of Youth Engagement and Advancement (OYEA) under the Department of Human Services. This is a one-year rotating, full-time position designed for an organized and proactive professional who is interested in public service, youth development, civic engagement and community-based initiatives.

The opportunity provides successful applicants with the chance to work directly on projects designed to strengthen youth participation in decision-making and connect young people with resources and opportunities across Boston. The Fellow will collaborate with city departments, schools, community organizations and other stakeholders while supporting a variety of seasonal and rotating projects.

About the City of Boston Special Projects Fellow Position

The Special Projects Fellow will work within the Office of Youth Engagement and Advancement, an office focused on ensuring that young people have meaningful opportunities to participate in decisions and initiatives that affect their lives.

OYEA works across three interconnected areas of youth development:

Spaces and programmes for young people—supporting environments and initiatives where young people can learn, participate and develop.

Adults and professionals working with young people – strengthening the capacity of youth workers and other professionals who support Boston’s youth.

Young people themselves – creating opportunities for youth leadership, participation, civic engagement and community development.

The Fellow will therefore have an opportunity to contribute to initiatives that operate across these three areas rather than being restricted to one specific project.

The position is particularly suited to someone who enjoys coordinating projects, communicating with different stakeholders, working with communities and managing multiple responsibilities simultaneously.

What Makes This Opportunity Important?

The Special Projects Fellow will contribute to initiatives intended to empower young people to become community leaders and agents of change.

The City of Boston’s youth engagement approach recognizes that young people should not simply be recipients of services. Instead, they should have opportunities to participate in conversations, programmes and decisions that influence their communities.

As a result, the Fellow will work in an environment where activities can involve the following:

Youth engagement and outreach

Civic education

Community partnerships

Public service initiatives

Youth programmes

Focus groups and listening sessions

City-wide events

Outreach campaigns

Resource connections

Community development

Interagency collaboration

The role also requires meaningful engagement with diverse communities throughout Boston.

1. Project Management and Coordination

One of the central responsibilities will be overseeing rotating and seasonal projects within OYEA.

The Fellow will help move projects from planning through implementation and follow-up. This includes keeping track of:

Project timelines

Deliverables

Follow-up activities

Implementation requirements

Project documentation

Stakeholder responsibilities

Shared resources

This makes project management skills particularly valuable for applicants.

2. Maintaining Project Documentation

The Fellow will be expected to maintain organized project files, documentation and shared resources.

Strong organizational skills will therefore be important because the position involves managing multiple initiatives and ensuring that relevant information can be easily accessed by colleagues and partners.

3. Building Relationships With Stakeholders

The position involves active communication and relationship-building with a wide range of stakeholders.

These may include:

City agencies

Community organizations

Schools

External partners

Youth-serving organizations

Community stakeholders

The purpose of these relationships is to support youth-focused initiatives and strengthen collaboration between the City and organizations working with young people.

The Fellow will assist with meaningful youth engagement activities.

Youth engagement activities

Other operational requirements associated with OYEA projects

Responsibilities include helping to track:

Project budgets

Invoices

Procurement requirements

This work will be carried out in coordination with OYEA staff. Applicants with experience handling project budgets, invoices or administrative records may therefore have an advantage.

The position includes helping connect speakers of languages other than English with available translation and language services.

This is particularly relevant to the City’s goal of meaningful engagement with diverse communities.

Applicants who have experience working across language or cultural differences may find this aspect of the position especially relevant.

The Fellow must demonstrate professionalism, discretion and accountability when interacting with:

Young people

Community organizations

City employees

External partners

Other stakeholders

Because the role involves working with youth and public-sector partners, sound judgment and responsible handling of information are important.

Staff meetings

Professional development opportunities

TITLE: 2026-2027 Fulbright-Nehru Master’s Fellowships

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Fulbright-Nehru Master’s Fellowships are designed for highly motivated individuals who demonstrate outstanding leadership qualities, have completed the equivalent of a U.S. bachelor’s degree, have at least three years professional work experience, and are committed to return and contribute to their communities in India.

These fellowships are awarded for up to two years to pursue a master’s degree at U.S. colleges and universities.

Grant Benefits

The fellowship will provide J-1 visa support, round-trip economy class air travel from fellow’s home city to the host institution in the U.S., funding for tuition and fees, living and related costs, and accident and sickness coverage per U.S. Government guidelines.*

The Fulbright-Nehru Master’s Fellowships provide no financial support for dependents.

* USIEF funding may not cover all costs and the fellow may need to supplement grant benefits with other resources.

Eligibility Requirements

In addition to the General Prerequisites, the applicant:

Must have completed an equivalent of a U.S. bachelor’s degree from a recognized Indian university with at least 55% marks. Applicants must either possess a four-year bachelor’s degree or a completed master’s degree; or a full-time postgraduate diploma from a recognized Indian institution, if the bachelor’s degree is of less than four years’ duration;

Must have at least three years’ full-time (paid) professional work experience relevant to the proposed field of study by the application deadline;

Should demonstrate experience in leadership and community service;

Must not have another degree from a U.S. university or be enrolled in a U.S. degree program; and

If employed, should follow the instructions carefully regarding employer’s endorsement. If applicable, obtain the endorsement from the appropriate administrative authority on the FNMasters Employer’s Endorsement Form. The employer must indicate that leave will be granted for the fellowship period.

Employees of the Government of India and Indian State Governments are not eligible for any Fulbright-Nehru Fellowships. This includes civil servants in central services (such as IAS, IPS, IRS, IFS, and allied services), state government services (including state civil services), and bureaucratic staff employed in central and state ministries or departments.

Fields of Study

Each applicant must choose one field of study that matches their main area of interest. The following field descriptions are illustrative, and applicants should note that individual academic host institution programs of study may differ in course offerings, subspecialties, and academic requirements.

Applications are invited in the following fields only:

Economics

Environmental Science/Studies

Higher Education Administration

International Legal Studies

Journalism and Mass Communication

Public Health

Sustainable Development/Sustainability

Urban and Regional Planning

Application Process

Applications must be submitted online at: https://apply.iie.org/ffsp2026

Please carefully review the FNMaster’s Applicant Instructions before starting your online application

Please refer to FNMaster’s Applicant Checklist before submitting the application.

In addition, you must complete FNMaster’s Applicant Annexure and FNMaster’s Employer’s Endorsement Form (if applicable) and upload on your online application.

TITLE: Postdoctoral Fellowship at Stellenbosch University 2026: Tax-Free Stipend, Up to 3 Years, Pathogen Genomics and Climate Research

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Stellenbosch University in South Africa is inviting applications for an exciting Postdoctoral Research Fellowship focused on One Health, pathogen genomics, climate, environmental data and infectious disease modelling across Africa.

The fellowship is hosted by the Centre for Epidemic Response and Innovation (CERI) at Stellenbosch University and provides an opportunity for an experienced early-career researcher to work at the intersection of genomic epidemiology, infectious diseases, climate science, environmental modelling, data science and public health.

The successful fellow will investigate how environmental and climate-related factors influence the emergence, transmission, persistence and resurgence of cholera and other climate-sensitive infectious diseases across Africa. The project will combine pathogen genomic information with environmental, climatic, demographic and human-related data to develop models that can help improve disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness and public-health decision-making.

The fellowship offers a competitive tax-free stipend and can run for up to three years. It also provides opportunities to collaborate with major international research partners, including the University of Oxford and Cornell University.

Overview of the Stellenbosch University Postdoctoral Fellowship

This is a highly interdisciplinary research opportunity designed for researchers who want to contribute to understanding and predicting infectious disease outbreaks in Africa.

The fellowship brings together several rapidly developing areas of science, including:

Pathogen genomics

Genomic epidemiology

Phylogenetics

Phylodynamics

Phylogeography

Infectious disease epidemiology

Climate-health research

Environmental science

Disease ecology

Spatial epidemiology

Geospatial modelling

Machine learning

Bayesian statistics

Data science

One Health

Public health

Rather than examining infectious diseases through a single discipline, the project takes an integrated approach. Researchers will combine pathogen genomic information with environmental and climate data and other factors that can influence how diseases emerge and spread.

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant to researchers interested in understanding how climate change, environmental disruption and human activity can alter infectious disease risks across African populations.

About the Host Institution

The fellowship is based at the Centre for Epidemic Response and Innovation (CERI) at Stellenbosch University in South Africa.

CERI is an academic and research centre focused on strengthening Africa’s ability to identify, monitor and respond to epidemics and pandemics. The centre combines genomics, data science, epidemiology and other disciplines to address infectious disease threats.

The successful candidate will become part of the centre’s One Health Program and Data Science Unit and will participate in the CLIMADE consortium.

CLIMADE focuses on understanding diseases that are amplified or influenced by climate and environmental changes. Its research brings together pathogen genomics, epidemiology, environmental information and modelling to better understand and respond to climate-sensitive epidemics.

What Will the Postdoctoral Fellow Research?

The central research theme involves understanding the relationship between pathogens, climate, environmental conditions and human populations.

The researcher will work particularly on cholera and other infectious diseases whose emergence or transmission can be influenced by environmental and climate conditions.

The project aims to develop models that can help answer questions such as:

Where are climate-sensitive disease outbreaks most likely to occur?

How do pathogens move between different populations and geographical regions?

How do flooding, rainfall, drought and temperature influence disease transmission?

How do human movement and displacement affect the spread of pathogens?

How do environmental changes influence pathogen persistence?

How can genomic information reveal transmission pathways?

How can genomic and environmental information be combined to improve outbreak prediction?

How can scientific evidence support disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness?

The fellow will therefore work with complex datasets covering both biological and environmental information.

Integrating Pathogen Genomics With Climate and Environmental Data

One of the most important features of this fellowship is its emphasis on data integration.

Pathogen genomes can provide information about how infectious organisms evolve and spread. However, genomic information alone may not fully explain why outbreaks occur in particular locations or at particular times.

The project therefore seeks to combine genomic data with other forms of information, including:

Climate data

Rainfall

Temperature

Flooding

Drought

Environmental data

Land-use change

Urbanisation

Mining

Human mobility

Population and demographic information

Human displacement

Conflict

Healthcare access

Epidemiological information

By combining these datasets, researchers can build a more comprehensive understanding of disease dynamics across different African settings.

Focus on Cholera and Other Climate-Sensitive Diseases

Cholera is a major component of the research focus.

The disease is particularly relevant to climate and environmental research because factors such as rainfall, flooding, water availability, sanitation and environmental conditions can influence transmission patterns.

The research will not necessarily be limited to cholera. The broader focus includes other infectious diseases whose emergence, transmission or persistence can be influenced by climate and environmental conditions.

This provides an opportunity for researchers with backgrounds in infectious diseases, epidemiology, environmental health, disease ecology, genomics and quantitative modelling to contribute to a broader One Health research agenda.

Key Responsibilities of the Postdoctoral Fellow

The successful candidate is expected to undertake substantial independent research while contributing to the wider activities of the research team.

Key responsibilities include:

1. Integrating multiple datasets

The researcher will work with genomic, epidemiological, environmental, climatic, demographic and anthropogenic datasets.

This will require the ability to manage and analyse large and complex datasets and identify relationships between biological, environmental and population-level factors.

2. Applying advanced analytical methods

The fellow may use several analytical approaches, depending on their expertise and the research question.

These include:

Phylogenetic analysis

Phylodynamic modelling

Phylogeographic analysis

Geospatial analysis

Statistical modelling

Ecological modelling

Bayesian methods

Machine learning

Spatial modelling

Climate-health modelling

Applicants do not necessarily need to be experts in every method. The advertised requirements indicate expertise in at least one relevant area is important.

3. Modelling pathogen movement

An important part of the research will involve understanding how pathogens move through populations and geographical areas.

This can include investigating:

Transmission corridors

Human mobility

Population displacement

Pathogen persistence

Spillover

Disease resurgence

Cross-border transmission

4. Developing predictive frameworks

The research will contribute to spatially explicit and predictive frameworks capable of linking genomic epidemiology with climate, environmental and human-related factors.

The ultimate objective is to generate evidence that can support practical public-health activities such as surveillance, preparedness and resource allocation.

5. Publishing research

The fellow will be expected to contribute to and lead scientific publications arising from the research.

This is an important opportunity for researchers seeking to strengthen their publication record and establish themselves as independent researchers.

6. Contributing to grant development

The position may also involve contributing to research funding applications and broader grant-development activities.

7. Mentoring students

The fellow may contribute to student mentorship and research training within the programme.

8. Stakeholder engagement

The researcher will have opportunities to engage with stakeholders and research partners, helping translate scientific findings into useful evidence for public health.

9. International collaboration

The project involves African and international research partners, creating opportunities for collaboration beyond South Africa, including links with the University of Oxford and Cornell University.

Fellowship Duration

The fellowship is available for up to three years.

This relatively long duration is significant for a postdoctoral research position because it can provide sufficient time to:

Develop the research programme.

Analyse complex datasets.

Build and test models.

Produce scientific publications.

Develop international collaborations.

Contribute to grant applications.

Build an independent research profile.

The exact continuation of the fellowship will be subject to the applicable fellowship and institutional conditions.

Stipend and Financial Support

The position offers a competitive tax-free fellowship stipend.

The tax-free nature of the stipend can make the opportunity particularly attractive to researchers considering an international postdoctoral appointment.

However, applicants should carefully review the official fellowship terms and application information for the complete financial conditions before making relocation or financial decisions.

Academic Eligibility and Qualifications

The fellowship is primarily intended for researchers who have already completed doctoral-level training.

According to the current CERI announcement, applicants should normally hold a PhD or equivalent qualification obtained within the past five years. Relevant disciplines include:

Bioinformatics

Computational biology

Epidemiology

Data science

Disease ecology

Geography

Public health

Or another closely related field

This means the opportunity is particularly suitable for researchers whose doctoral research involved quantitative analysis, infectious diseases, genomics, environmental health or related areas.

Quantitative and Programming Skills

Applicants should have strong quantitative abilities.

The fellowship specifically identifies proficiency in R and/or Python as an important requirement, particularly for analysing large and complex datasets.

Experience in programming and data analysis can therefore be an important component of a competitive application.

Researchers who have worked with large genomic, epidemiological, environmental or spatial datasets may be particularly well positioned for the role.

Relevant Research Expertise

Applicants should have expertise in at least one relevant research area.

These may include:

Genomic epidemiology

Phylogenetics

Phylodynamics

Spatial modelling

Climate-health analysis

Ecological modelling

Bayesian statistics

Machine learning

The interdisciplinary nature of the project means that candidates may enter from different academic backgrounds, provided their expertise can contribute meaningfully to the research programme.

Additional Experience That Can Strengthen an Application

While some experience is described as desirable rather than essential, applicants may strengthen their profile through experience with:

BEAST or related phylodynamic tools

GIS

Remote sensing

Reproducible research workflows

Climate-sensitive diseases

Environmental surveillance

Humanitarian settings

Infectious disease research in Africa

Collaborative or multidisciplinary research

Experience in these areas can demonstrate that the applicant is prepared to work across disciplines rather than focusing exclusively on one type of dataset.

Research Independence and Publications

The fellowship is aimed at postdoctoral researchers who can demonstrate scientific independence.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate:

Independent research experience

Peer-reviewed publications

Quantitative research experience

Strong scientific writing

Ability to work collaboratively

Ability to communicate research findings effectively

A strong CV should clearly demonstrate what the applicant personally contributed to previous research projects rather than simply listing the projects they participated in.

International Collaboration and Research Exposure

Another major attraction of this fellowship is its international research environment.

The fellow will work alongside African and international partners and will have opportunities for collaboration involving institutions such as the University of Oxford and Cornell University.

This can provide valuable exposure to:

International research networks

Multidisciplinary scientific teams

Global infectious disease research

Genomic epidemiology

Climate-health research

Advanced computational methods

Collaborative publications

International scientific communication

For researchers planning an academic career, this type of international collaboration can be valuable for developing a strong research network.

Training and Mentorship

The fellowship also offers access to research training and mentorship.

According to the CERI announcement, fellows will receive hands-on exposure to infectious disease genomic epidemiology and will be mentored by researchers working at a high level of international scientific research. The programme notes researchers publishing in journals including Science, Nature, Cell and The Lancet.

This makes the opportunity particularly attractive to researchers seeking to deepen their expertise in genomic epidemiology and quantitative infectious-disease research.

Where Is the Fellowship Based?

The fellowship is based at Stellenbosch University in Stellenbosch, South Africa, through CERI.

The position may also provide opportunities for fieldwork and international collaboration.

Applicants outside South Africa should therefore consider the practical requirements associated with relocating to South Africa if selected.

Why This Fellowship Is Important for Africa

Africa continues to face substantial infectious disease challenges, while climate and environmental changes are creating additional complexities for disease prevention and control.

Understanding these challenges requires more than traditional epidemiological surveillance.

Researchers increasingly need to combine:

Genomics + Epidemiology + Climate Data + Environmental Science + Human Mobility + Data Science

This fellowship is designed around precisely that type of integrated approach.

The research could contribute to better understanding of where and when outbreaks are likely to occur, how pathogens move between populations, and which environmental or human factors may contribute to disease emergence and resurgence.

Importantly, the project seeks to translate research findings into evidence that can support surveillance, preparedness and resource allocation.

Career Benefits of the Fellowship

A successful postdoctoral fellow could gain several important professional benefits, including:

Up to three years of postdoctoral research experience.

A competitive tax-free fellowship stipend.

Experience at a major African research institution.

Exposure to pathogen genomic research.

Experience combining genomic and environmental datasets.

Training in infectious disease genomic epidemiology.

Opportunities to strengthen scientific publications.

International research collaboration.

Exposure to interdisciplinary research.

Experience in advanced quantitative modelling.

Opportunities for student mentorship.

Experience contributing to grant development.

Opportunities to build a global scientific network.

Experience addressing major public-health challenges affecting Africa.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This fellowship could be particularly suitable for researchers who have recently completed a PhD and want to build a career in areas such as:

Infectious disease research

Genomic epidemiology

Bioinformatics

Computational biology

Public health

Epidemiology

Climate and health

Disease ecology

Environmental health

Spatial epidemiology

Data science

Machine learning

Pathogen surveillance

One Health research

Researchers with interdisciplinary backgrounds may be particularly interested because the project brings biological, environmental, computational and public-health approaches together.

Application Deadline

Deadline: 25 September 2026 at 22:00 SAST.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day because they may need time to prepare a strong CV, cover letter and supporting information.

How to Apply

Interested researchers should review the official CERI announcement and application instructions carefully before submitting their application.

The application requires a cover letter explaining the applicant’s motivation, expertise and career goals.

APPLY HERE

Applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates the connection between their previous research and the proposed fellowship.

Recommended application preparation

Before applying, candidates should:

Update their academic CV.

Highlight their PhD research.

Clearly list relevant publications.

Highlight programming experience in R and/or Python.

Explain experience with genomic, epidemiological or environmental datasets.

Identify relevant modelling or statistical expertise.

Highlight interdisciplinary research experience.

Explain their interest in climate-sensitive infectious diseases.

Prepare a focused cover letter.

Demonstrate how the fellowship fits their long-term research career.

Learn more about this opportunity HERE

Application Tip

One of the strongest ways to approach this application is to connect your previous research directly to the fellowship’s research objectives.

For example, instead of simply stating that you have experience in Python, R, epidemiology or genomics, explain what you have actually used those skills to accomplish.

An effective application should make it easy for the selection team to see:

Your previous research → your technical skills → your publications → your research interests → how they fit this fellowship.

Candidates should also demonstrate that they understand the importance of integrating genomic data with environmental and climate information rather than presenting themselves as interested in only one component of the project.

Conclusion

The Stellenbosch University Postdoctoral Fellowship in One Health Genomic and Environmental Modelling of Infectious Diseases in Africa represents an important opportunity for researchers working at the intersection of infectious diseases, genomics, climate, environmental science and data analytics.

With a tax-free stipend, a duration of up to three years, international collaboration opportunities and access to CERI’s One Health and Data Science research environment, the fellowship can provide a strong platform for researchers seeking to develop an independent scientific career.

The research focus is especially relevant to Africa because it seeks to understand how pathogens interact with changing environmental and climatic conditions and how these relationships can influence outbreaks.

Researchers with a PhD in a relevant discipline, strong quantitative skills, R and/or Python experience, relevant expertise in areas such as genomic epidemiology, phylodynamics, spatial modelling, climate-health research or machine learning, and evidence of scientific independence should consider this opportunity.
