Students should carefully consider their academic background and professional interests before selecting the organization to which they will apply.

Important Rule: Apply to Only One Organization

Applicants should pay close attention to one of the most important application rules:

You can apply to only one participating organization.

Applicants should therefore not submit separate applications to several entities in an attempt to increase their chances.

The official announcement states that double applications will not be considered.

This makes it particularly important to choose an organization strategically.

Students should consider factors such as:

Their academic specialization

Research interests

Career ambitions

Professional interests

The type of international work they want to understand better

A carefully targeted application is preferable to submitting multiple applications.

Who Can Apply for the UN Shadowing Programme 2026?

The programme specifically encourages applications from students enrolled in:

Master’s programmes

PhD programmes

Students must be enrolled at universities in one of the countries identified in the official call.

Does Your Field of Study Matter?

The official announcement asks applicants to state their:

University

Field of study

Whether they are enrolled in a Master’s or PhD programme

Field of interest

However, it does not specify one mandatory academic discipline.

This means the source does not restrict applications only to students of international relations, law, political science or similar subjects.

Applicants should nevertheless select an organization whose work has a credible connection with their studies, research interests or professional goals.

Information Required in the Application

Applications must contain several specific pieces of information.

Students should provide:

Nationality

Telephone number

Email address

University

Field of study

Whether they are enrolled in a Master’s or PhD programme

Field of interest

Information on whether they have participated in the Shadowing Programme previously and, if so, in which year

A response explaining what they expect to gain from the Shadowing Programme if selected, with a maximum of 50 words.

Applicants should ensure that every requested item is included.

The official announcement explicitly states that incomplete applications will not be considered.

The 50-Word Motivation Response

One of the most important parts of the application is the question:

If selected, what would you expect to get out of the Shadowing Programme?

Applicants must answer this question in a maximum of:

50 words.

Because the response is short, applicants should use the available space carefully.

A strong response should focus on specific learning objectives rather than generic statements.

Students may wish to explain how participating would help them:

Understand the professional responsibilities of international-organization staff

Explore a specific career field

Connect academic study with professional practice

Better understand a participating organization

Inform future career decisions

Learn about international organizational environments

The official call does not provide a required template for this response, so applicants should remain concise and directly answer the question.

Previous Participants Can Apply, but New Participants Receive Priority

The application asks whether students have previously participated in the Shadowing Programme.

Previous participation does not appear to create an automatic exclusion.

However, the organizers explicitly state that:

Students who have not participated in the Shadowing Programme before will be given priority.

First-time applicants may therefore have an advantage when places are allocated.

Number of Places Is Limited

The programme has limited capacity.

The organizers warn that there is a limit to the number of applications that can be accepted and encourage interested students to submit their applications as early as possible.

Applicants should not interpret the 27 September deadline as a reason to wait until the final day.

Preparing and submitting a complete application early may reduce the risk of missing the application window.

Applicants May Be Matched With a Different Organization

Students are asked to identify the organization they would like to shadow.

However, the organizers make clear that this preference cannot always be guaranteed.

Depending on the availability of places, a selected participant may be placed with a different organization from the one originally indicated.

Applicants should therefore approach the programme with some flexibility.

The central purpose is to gain insight into international-organization careers and the professional work of staff members rather than to guarantee access to one particular entity.

How to Apply for the United Nations Shadowing Programme 2026

Applications are submitted by email directly to the participating organization the student wishes to shadow.

There is no single application email for all organizations.

Applicants should complete the following process:

Confirm that they are currently enrolled in a Master’s or PhD programme at a university in one of the eligible countries.

Review the participating organizations.

Select one organization only.

Prepare all required personal and academic information.

Write a concise response of no more than 50 words explaining what they hope to gain from participation.

Send the complete application to the email address corresponding with the chosen organization.

Submit the application no later than 27 September 2026.

Monitor the provided email account for information concerning selection.

Application Period and Deadline

The application period runs from:

14 September 2026 to 27 September 2026.

Final Application Deadline: 27 September 2026

Because places are limited, students are encouraged to apply before the final day.

How Selection Works

After the application period closes, the organizers will review the registrations received.

The selection of participants will take place after all applications have been collected.

Successful applicants will then be:

Contacted by email.

Applicants should therefore provide an accurate email address and monitor it regularly after the application deadline.

The announcement does not specify a particular date by which selection results will be released.

The Programme Is Not a Recruitment Process

Applicants should understand an important distinction.

The Shadowing Programme is not part of a United Nations recruitment process.

Participation therefore does not constitute:

Employment with the United Nations

A job offer

An internship appointment

Preferential treatment in future recruitment

Automatic eligibility for employment

Entry into a UN recruitment roster

Its purpose is educational and career-oriented.

The programme gives students an opportunity to understand more about the work of UN and international-organization professionals.

Students should therefore apply because they want to learn, explore careers and obtain professional insight rather than because they expect direct employment afterward.

What Participants Can Gain From the Programme

The official announcement identifies the central benefit as the opportunity to gain insight into the work of a UN staff member.

For postgraduate students considering careers in international organizations, this can provide valuable exposure to professional realities that may not be visible through university courses alone.

Participants can potentially use the interaction to better understand:

What professionals actually do in their roles

How academic expertise connects with international work

The skills relevant to international organizations

Career pathways within large multilateral institutions

Professional working environments

How international organizations approach their mandates

The virtual career workshop adds a broader career-development dimension to the individual shadowing encounter.

Is the Programme Paid?

The official 2026 announcement does not state that participants receive a stipend, salary, grant or financial payment.

Because the programme is virtual, the call also does not advertise travel or accommodation funding.

It should therefore not be promoted as a paid opportunity unless the organizers later publish additional information stating otherwise.

Does the Programme Require Travel to Vienna?

No physical travel requirement is stated.

The 2026 edition is explicitly described as a virtual edition.

The shadowing encounter and career workshop are therefore intended to take place virtually.

Students should not assume that selection includes a funded trip to Austria or access to the Vienna International Centre.

Relationship With United Nations Day

The programme is organized partly to mark United Nations Day on 24 October.

The 2026 programme begins on 24 October and continues until 24 November.

Its connection to United Nations Day reinforces the programme’s focus on helping students better understand the institutions, professionals and activities associated with the United Nations family in Vienna.

Sustainable Development Goal Connection

The United Nations source associates this initiative with:

Sustainable Development Goal 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

The participating organizations work across a range of specialized international mandates, while the programme itself contributes to awareness and understanding of multilateral institutions and international professional environments.

Who Coordinates the Programme?

The Shadowing Programme 2026 is:

Coordinated by the United Nations Information Service Vienna, with support from UNIC Kyiv, and organized in cooperation with the participating Vienna-based organizations.

This makes the programme a collaborative initiative involving several parts of the wider United Nations and international-organization community in Vienna.

Key Dates at a Glance

Applications Open: 14 September 2026

Application Deadline: 27 September 2026

Programme Starts: 24 October 2026

Programme Ends: 24 November 2026

Format: Virtual

Programme Language: English

Academic Level: Master’s and PhD students

Application Method: Email directly to one participating organization only.

Tips Before Submitting an Application

Students should check their applications carefully before sending them.

In particular:

Confirm that the university is located in an eligible country.

Confirm current enrolment in a Master’s or PhD programme.

Select only one participating organization.

Use the correct application email.

Include every requested piece of information.

Keep the motivation response within the 50-word limit.

Do not submit duplicate applications.

Clearly state whether you have participated previously.

Ensure that your email address and phone number are accurate.

Submit before 27 September rather than waiting until the final hours.

The explicit rules concerning incomplete and double applications make administrative accuracy especially important.

Why the UN Shadowing Programme 2026 Is Worth Considering

For many postgraduate students, careers in the United Nations and other international organizations can appear difficult to understand from the outside.

Job descriptions may explain formal responsibilities, but they do not always provide a clear picture of what professionals actually do in their day-to-day work.

The Shadowing Programme addresses this gap by allowing selected students to interact directly with an individual working inside one of several Vienna-based international organizations.

Its virtual structure also removes the need for participants to travel to Austria.

The programme may therefore be particularly valuable for students who want to make better-informed decisions about their future academic specialization, research interests or international career plans.

Conclusion

The United Nations Shadowing Programme 2026 offers eligible Master’s and PhD students a focused opportunity to gain direct insight into professional work within the United Nations and other major international organizations based in Vienna.

Running virtually from 24 October to 24 November 2026, the programme will provide selected students with a one-hour virtual encounter with a staff member as well as access to a virtual career workshop.

Participating organizations include the IAEA, CTBTO, UNODC, UNODA, UNIDO, UNIS Vienna, ICPDR and UNSCEAR.

Applications are encouraged from students enrolled in Master’s and PhD programmes at universities in Armenia, Austria, Czechia, Georgia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Türkiye and Ukraine.

Students must choose only one organization, submit all required application information by email and include a maximum 50-word explanation of what they hope to gain from the programme. Incomplete and duplicate applications will not be considered, while applicants who have never participated in the Shadowing Programme before will receive priority.

The deadline to apply is:

27 September 2026.

TITLE: AU Enterprise Africa Network (EAN) Fellowship Programme 2026/2027 [Cohort 2]

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 30, 2026

Applications are invited for the AU Enterprise Africa Network (EAN) Fellowship Programme 2026/2027 [Cohort 2]. The Enterprise Africa Network (EAN) Fellowship Programme is an AUC Startup Acceleration Initiative and the African Union’s flagship programme for the development of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

Implemented by the AU Commission’s Department of Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry and Minerals (ETTIM), the programme provides Africa’s most promising entrepreneurs with structured training, expert mentorship, intellectual property support, and direct market access opportunities across the continent and beyond.

The EAN’s inaugural cohort (2024/25) trained 56 fellows from 30 African countries and produced over USD 1 million in deals and contracts. Cohort 2 (2026/27) will expand the programme to 100 fellows drawn from all 55 AU Member States, targeting USD 2 million in new attributable revenue and 500 new jobs.

Fellowship Sectors

Cohort 2 covers seven sectors organised into two clusters aligned with the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA):

Products Cluster (goods for intra-African trade): Manufacturing, Agro-processing, Creative Industries

Services Cluster: ICT/Digital, Fintech, Health, Logistics/Transport

Benefits

All fellows receive twelve months of structured training across ten modules differentiated by sector and tier; expert mentorship through African Union Partners, access to the African Trade Observatory (ATO) and AfCFTA market intelligence tools; and participation in continental events.

Tier 1 and 2 fellows participate in virtual market-entry sessions across ten AfCFTA pilot countries; Tier 3 fellows participate in B2B matchmaking sessions.

Eligibility

Open to youth- and women-led small enterprises that are: registered and operating in an AU Member State;

Formally registered as a business entity;

Operating for at least two years; and

Employing a minimum of three full-time staff.

Applications are particularly encouraged from women-led enterprises and businesses from underrepresented AU regions and small island Member States.

Application

The application form collects business registration details, sector, years of operation, employee count, countries currently trading, revenue range, IP status, and access to formal finance, together with a written pitch of up to 800 words describing the enterprise, its main market challenge, and the applicant’s objective for the fellowship.

Shortlisted applicants will be asked to provide one supporting document verifying finance access (bank statement, mobile money statement, or equivalent). This is not required at application stage.

The Public Policy and International Affairs (PPIA) Junior Summer Institute 2027 is inviting eligible undergraduate students to apply for a fully funded summer programme designed to prepare emerging leaders for graduate study and careers in public policy, international affairs, public administration, and public service.

Overview of the PPIA Junior Summer Institute

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute, commonly known as JSI, is a rigorous summer programme for undergraduate students who are approaching the final year of their degree and are interested in pursuing graduate education and professional careers connected to public service.

The programme is intended to help students understand how public policy is developed, how governments and institutions respond to social challenges, and how research, economics, statistics, leadership, communication, and policy analysis can be used to address real-world problems.

The 2027 programme will be hosted at:

Harvard University – Harvard Kennedy School

University of Michigan – Gerald R. Ford School of Public Policy

PPIA describes the Junior Summer Institute as a fully funded summer experience that combines academic preparation, professional development, career guidance, financial support, and community-building. Career coaching and professional guidance.

Additional support that may vary by host institution.

Academic and Professional Skills Participants Can Develop

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute is intended to strengthen a broad range of skills that are relevant to graduate study and public service careers.

Policy Analysis

Economics and Statistics

Research Skills

Interpersonal skills.

Who Can Apply?

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute is designed primarily for undergraduate students who are approaching the final year of their degree and are interested in graduate study and public service careers.

TITLE: Nature Restoration Academy 2026 in Berlin: Apply for Free Marine and Freshwater Restoration Training

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the Nature Restoration Academy 2026, a free training initiative designed to develop practical skills in marine and freshwater ecosystem restoration.

Organized and hosted by the SUBMARINER Network for Blue Growth, the programme combines an online introductory session with an intensive two-day, in-person training event at the organization’s office in Berlin, Germany. Selected participants will learn through expert lectures, practical workshops, European restoration case studies, digital monitoring approaches, and a multi-stakeholder negotiation simulation.

The programme is intended to help the next generation of restoration professionals translate environmental research and scientific knowledge into practical action. It will address the recovery of rivers, lakes, wetlands, coastal ecosystems, seas, and connected aquatic environments across the land–freshwater–marine continuum.

Participation is free, but only 30 places are available. Applicants must submit their applications by September 15, 2026. Selected participants will be notified by October 1, 2026.

Full details are available in the official SUBMARINER Network announcement.

What Is the Nature Restoration Academy?

The Nature Restoration Academy is a new capacity-building initiative focused on practical methods for restoring marine and freshwater ecosystems.

The programme responds to the growing need for people who can connect environmental science, public policy, community participation, monitoring systems, and sustainable finance with real restoration projects. Its purpose is not limited to explaining restoration concepts theoretically. Instead, the Academy aims to develop practical understanding that participants can apply in their studies, employment, research, policy work, conservation programmes, or community initiatives.

The Academy covers ecosystems as an interconnected continuum. This means restoration is not treated as a series of isolated activities. Rivers, lakes, wetlands, estuaries, coasts, and marine environments are considered connected systems in which changes in one area may affect conditions elsewhere.

For example, freshwater quality can influence coastal ecosystems, while wetland degradation may affect biodiversity, water storage, flood management, nutrient flows, and surrounding communities. An integrated restoration approach therefore requires coordination across scientific disciplines, geographic boundaries, institutions, and stakeholder groups.

The programme has been designed to help participants understand these relationships and convert restoration knowledge into implementable solutions.

Who Organizes the Nature Restoration Academy?

The Academy is organized and hosted by the SUBMARINER Network for Blue Growth.

The SUBMARINER Network is a cooperation platform that connects research and educational institutions, public authorities, civil society organizations, business support institutions, and private companies working within the sustainable blue economy.

Although the network is rooted in the Baltic Sea Region, its partnerships and activities extend across Europe and beyond. Its work includes marine conservation, protected areas, sustainable aquaculture, blue biotechnology, maritime spatial planning, ecosystem restoration, policy development, innovation, and capacity-building.

The Nature Restoration Academy is funded by EIT Water and supported by the Poul Due Jensen Foundation, also known as the Grundfos Foundation.

Why Marine and Freshwater Restoration Training Matters

Aquatic ecosystems provide essential environmental, social, and economic services. Healthy rivers, lakes, wetlands, coastal areas, and seas can support biodiversity, water quality, climate resilience, sustainable livelihoods, food systems, recreation, tourism, and community well-being.

However, restoration projects are often technically and institutionally complex. Successful implementation may require cooperation among:

Scientists and researchers

Environmental authorities

Local governments

Conservation organizations

Businesses and investors

Marine and freshwater practitioners

Community groups

Citizen scientists

Energy developers

Landowners

Fisheries and aquaculture stakeholders

Civil society organizations

Funding institutions

Restoration professionals must understand ecological processes, but they may also need skills in stakeholder engagement, monitoring, project design, policy implementation, business planning, and funding.

The Nature Restoration Academy has been structured around this practical reality. Its combination of scientific content, case studies, workshops, simulations, and financing discussions is intended to help participants understand how restoration projects move from ideas and policies to implementation.

Structure of the Nature Restoration Academy

The programme consists of three connected components.

1. Online Baseline Session

Selected participants must first attend an online baseline session on October 6, 2026.

The session will provide a common foundation before the in-person event. It will draw on relevant material from the Blue Bio Techpreneurs course, Integrated Ocean Planning: Marine Protected Areas, Multi-Use and Business Pathways.

This common starting point should enable participants from different educational and professional backgrounds to take part more effectively in the advanced discussions and workshops held in Berlin.

The application form specifically asks candidates to confirm whether they can attend the October 6 online session. Selected applicants are expected to participate in both the online and in-person components.

2. Two-Day Training Event in Berlin

The main in-person programme will take place at the SUBMARINER Network’s Berlin office on October 29 and 30, 2026.

The two-day event will combine:

Lectures delivered by programme partners and invited experts

Marine and freshwater restoration case studies

Practical and interactive workshops

Discussions on nature-based restoration approaches

A multi-stakeholder negotiation simulation

Digital monitoring and citizen-science content

Sessions on project funding and business models

A dedicated discussion on gender equality within the sector

The limited cohort of 30 participants is likely to support active engagement, group work, peer learning, and direct interaction with trainers and other participants.

3. New Online Restoration Module

Sessions delivered during the Berlin event will be recorded and used to develop a new online restoration module.

The module will be added to the Blue Bio Techpreneurs course hosted on FutureLearn. This will allow the lessons, case studies, and expertise shared in Berlin to reach a much larger international audience after the in-person event.

When announcing the Academy, SUBMARINER reported that the existing course had already reached 464 learners from more than 80 countries. The linked FutureLearn course provides theoretical foundations in marine protected areas, maritime spatial planning, ocean multi-use, conservation governance, business planning, and sustainable blue-economy development.

The Nature Restoration Academy adds a more practical, in-person restoration component to this existing learning framework.

Main Training Topics

The programme will cover a broad selection of issues affecting the planning, implementation, monitoring, and financial sustainability of restoration projects.

Nature-Based Solutions

Participants will examine how nature-based solutions can be used to restore marine and freshwater ecosystems.

Nature-based solutions generally work with natural ecological processes to address environmental and social challenges. Within aquatic restoration, these approaches may involve rebuilding ecosystem functions, improving habitat quality, strengthening biodiversity, or increasing resilience to environmental pressures.

The Academy will connect these concepts with practical marine and freshwater restoration work.

European Restoration Case Studies

Real restoration case studies from Europe will be used to demonstrate how projects are designed and implemented in practice.

Case-based learning can help participants understand:

How restoration priorities are selected

Which stakeholders need to be involved

How ecological objectives are translated into activities

What implementation challenges may arise

How project results can be monitored

Which lessons can be transferred to other locations

These examples should allow participants to compare restoration strategies across different ecosystems and institutional settings.

Citizen Science

The programme will explore the role of citizen science in restoration.

Citizen science can involve members of the public in observing environmental changes, collecting ecological data, reporting species, monitoring water conditions, or supporting long-term project evaluation.

When properly designed, citizen-science programmes can expand monitoring capacity while improving public understanding and local ownership of restoration initiatives.

Digital Monitoring

Participants will also examine digital approaches to monitoring marine and freshwater restoration.

Digital monitoring can help project teams collect, organize, analyse, and communicate environmental information more effectively. Depending on the project, this may include remote sensing, digital mapping, mobile data collection, automated sensors, databases, or online reporting systems.

The Academy will consider how these tools can contribute to evidence-based restoration planning and evaluation.

Restoration in Offshore Wind Parks

One specialized topic will address restoration within offshore wind parks.

The rapid development of offshore renewable energy creates both challenges and potential opportunities for marine ecosystems. Restoration and nature-inclusive planning must therefore consider the relationship between energy infrastructure, marine habitats, biodiversity, fishing activity, protected areas, and other uses of ocean space.

This session should be particularly relevant to professionals interested in offshore renewable energy, marine spatial planning, environmental assessment, nature-inclusive design, and biodiversity protection.

Business Models for Restoration

The Academy will examine the business models that can support restoration activities over time.

A restoration project may have a strong ecological justification but still struggle if it lacks a sustainable operational and financial structure. Participants will therefore consider how restoration initiatives can connect environmental objectives with viable delivery models.

Relevant questions may include:

Who finances the initial project?

Who is responsible for long-term management?

Which organizations benefit from restoration?

Can ecosystem services be incorporated into the project model?

How can public, private, philanthropic, and community resources be combined?

How can restoration activities continue after short-term project funding ends?

Funding Mechanisms

Closely related to business-model development, the Academy will explore financing mechanisms for marine and freshwater restoration.

This component is important because restoration projects may rely on multiple funding sources. These can include public programmes, environmental funds, foundations, private investment, corporate partnerships, research funding, community finance, or blended-finance arrangements.

The training is expected to help participants understand that securing initial funding is only one part of project development. Long-term maintenance, monitoring, governance, and institutional ownership must also be considered.

MPA Game: Multi-Stakeholder Negotiation Simulation

The Berlin programme will include the MPA Game, an interactive simulation involving multi-stakeholder negotiation.

MPA refers to a Marine Protected Area. Decisions concerning these areas may involve conservation authorities, local communities, researchers, fishing interests, tourism operators, energy developers, businesses, and other stakeholders.

The simulation will allow participants to experience the challenges of balancing environmental protection with social and economic interests. It is designed to build skills in:

Stakeholder analysis

Negotiation

Conflict management

Collaborative decision-making

Policy interpretation

Communication

Compromise and consensus-building

Gender Equality in Marine and Freshwater Sectors

The programme will include a dedicated gender-equality session delivered by WIN-BIG.

This session will examine the importance of equal participation and opportunity within marine, freshwater, conservation, and blue-economy sectors. It will help participants consider how gender perspectives can be incorporated into environmental initiatives, professional development, decision-making, and sectoral leadership.

Benefits of Participating

Selected participants can expect several potential benefits from the programme:

Free participation in a specialized restoration academy

Practical training in marine and freshwater restoration

Exposure to European restoration case studies

Interaction with experts and practitioners

Participation in workshops and negotiation simulations

Knowledge of citizen-science and digital-monitoring approaches

Better understanding of restoration business models

Exposure to restoration funding mechanisms

Learning related to offshore wind and nature-inclusive development

A stronger understanding of stakeholder engagement

Opportunities to connect with other early-career professionals, students, and practitioners

Participation in discussions concerning gender equality in the sector

A possible contribution toward travel expenses for participants travelling from outside Germany

The programme announcement does not promise employment, a research grant, a stipend, or a fully funded trip. Its principal benefit is free access to the training programme and a possible contribution toward eligible travel costs.

Participation in the Nature Restoration Academy is free of charge. Selected applicants will not be required to pay a programme registration or tuition fee.

TITLE: Heidelberg University Joint Scholarship Programme 2027: Fully Supported 3-Month Research Fellowship for Young Scholars from South Asia

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Young researchers from South Asia have an opportunity to advance their academic careers, strengthen international research networks and develop collaborative research projects through the Joint Scholarship Programme of the South Asia Institute (SAI), Heidelberg University, and the Max Weber Forum for South Asian Studies Delhi (MWF Delhi).

The programme is inviting applications for a three-month research fellowship in Heidelberg, Germany, during summer 2027. The opportunity is designed for promising young scholars from selected South Asian countries who want to establish or deepen research collaboration with the South Asia Institute at Heidelberg University.

Successful fellows will spend up to three months at the South Asia Institute in Heidelberg, where they will work on a research project previously outlined in their application. An important component of the fellowship is the development of the research project into a potential third-party funding application, which could seek support for future research, academic exchanges or scientific events.

The programme therefore offers more than a short-term research stay. It provides an opportunity for early-career researchers to gain international academic exposure, build institutional connections, participate in scholarly activities and potentially develop their research into a larger externally funded project.

Heidelberg University South Asia Joint Scholarship Programme 2027

The fellowship is being offered by the South Asia Institute of Heidelberg University in cooperation with the Max Weber Forum for South Asian Studies Delhi.

The programme is particularly intended to facilitate research collaboration between young scholars from South Asia and researchers at the South Asia Institute. Applicants are expected to propose a clearly defined research project that can be further developed during their stay in Heidelberg.

The fellowship is scheduled to begin sometime between April and June 2027 and will run for approximately three months.

During the fellowship period, the successful candidate’s place of residence will be Heidelberg, Germany.

What Does the Fellowship Offer?

The Joint Scholarship Programme provides financial and academic support to selected researchers during their stay in Heidelberg.

The fellowship package includes several important forms of support:

1. Monthly Scholarship of EUR 1,200

Successful fellows will receive a monthly scholarship instalment of EUR 1,200 during the fellowship period.

This financial support is intended to assist fellows with living expenses while undertaking their research stay in Heidelberg.

2. International Travel Support of Up to EUR 1,500

The programme also provides reimbursement of international travel expenses of up to EUR 1,500.

This can help reduce the financial burden associated with travelling to and from Germany for the research fellowship.

3. Rental Cost Support

The fellowship also includes payment of rental costs, providing additional assistance with accommodation expenses during the research stay in Heidelberg.

Together, the monthly scholarship, travel reimbursement and rental-cost support make the programme a significant opportunity for researchers seeking international academic experience without having to bear the full cost of a research stay abroad.

Duration and Location of the Fellowship

The fellowship will last for three months.

The programme is expected to begin between April and June 2027, meaning successful applicants will undertake their research stay during the summer period of 2027.

The fellowship will be based at the South Asia Institute in Heidelberg, with Heidelberg serving as the fellow’s place of residence during the programme.

Researchers should therefore be prepared to spend the fellowship period in Germany and actively engage with the academic environment at the South Asia Institute.

Research Areas Covered by the Programme

The programme is particularly interested in applications connected to a broad range of disciplines relating to South Asia.

Applicants working in the following areas are specifically encouraged to apply:

Ethnology

History

Political science

Economics

Geography

Modern languages and literatures of South Asia

Cultural history of South Asia

Religious history of South Asia

Classical Indology

The multidisciplinary nature of the programme means that researchers can approach South Asian studies from different academic perspectives.

Applicants should ensure that their proposed project is academically relevant to the areas supported by the programme and that the research can benefit from collaboration with the South Asia Institute.

What Will Fellows Do During the Three-Month Research Stay?

The fellowship is structured around a research project that applicants must already define as part of their application.

During their time at the South Asia Institute, fellows will be expected to take the proposed project forward and develop it further.

A major objective is to transform the initial research project into a potential third-party funding application.

This could involve seeking future funding for:

Research projects

Academic exchange programmes

Scientific events

Collaborative research initiatives

Other relevant academic activities

This component makes the fellowship particularly valuable for researchers who want to move beyond an individual research project and develop longer-term academic collaborations and externally funded research opportunities.

Participation in Academic Events

Fellows will also be expected to actively participate in scientific events at the South Asia Institute during their stay.

This requirement provides an opportunity for researchers to interact with scholars, exchange ideas and become part of the academic environment at the institute.

Participation in scientific activities can also help fellows:

Expand their academic networks.

Exchange knowledge with researchers working in related disciplines.

Present or discuss research ideas.

Identify potential research collaborators.

Gain exposure to international academic practices.

Develop relationships that could continue after the fellowship.

Explore future opportunities for joint research and funding.

For young scholars seeking to establish an international research profile, this networking component can be an important part of the fellowship experience.

Who Can Apply for the Heidelberg University South Asia Fellowship?

The programme is specifically aimed at young researchers from South Asia.

Applicants must be from one of the five countries identified by the programme:

India

Nepal

Pakistan

Sri Lanka

Bangladesh

The programme is therefore geographically focused on South Asia rather than being open to applicants from every country worldwide.

Researchers from other countries who do not meet the programme’s geographic eligibility requirements should not assume that they qualify based on academic qualifications alone.

Academic Qualification Required

Applicants are required to provide a copy of their doctoral certificate as part of the application documents.

This means the opportunity is intended for researchers who have completed doctoral-level studies and can demonstrate this through their doctoral certificate.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they meet the programme’s academic requirements before beginning the application process.

Application Documents Required

Applicants must submit their materials through the online application system.

The application requires several documents, which should be carefully prepared before submission.

1. Online Application Form

Applicants must complete the official online application form.

The form is the primary method through which applications are submitted to the programme.

2. Short Cover Letter

Applicants must submit a short cover letter of no more than one page.

The cover letter should clearly communicate the applicant’s motivation for applying and explain why the fellowship and proposed research collaboration are relevant to their academic development.

Because the cover letter is limited to one page, applicants should focus on the most important information rather than providing a lengthy academic biography.

3. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide a curriculum vitae of no more than two pages.

The CV should include the applicant’s top ten publications.

Researchers should therefore prioritise their strongest and most relevant academic publications rather than attempting to provide an exhaustive publication history.

4. Doctoral Certificate

A copy of the applicant’s doctoral certificate must be included.

Applicants should ensure that the submitted document is clear and readable.

5. Project Description

Applicants must prepare a project description using the designated project-description template.

The template must be downloaded, completed with the required information and uploaded together with the other application documents.

The project description is particularly important because the fellowship is built around developing the proposed research project during the three-month stay.

Applicants should therefore present a clear, academically sound and achievable research proposal.

6. List of Two Referees

Applicants must provide a list of two referees who may be contacted later to provide additional information about the applicant.

Applicants should select referees who can credibly comment on their academic background, research abilities and potential.

7. Letter of Reference from an SAI Member

A letter of reference from a member of the South Asia Institute is optional.

Although it is not listed as a mandatory requirement, applicants who have an established academic connection with an SAI member may consider whether obtaining such a reference would strengthen their application.

Important Application Document Requirement

One important instruction is that the application documents must be uploaded as a single PDF.

Applicants should therefore combine the required attachments into one PDF document before submitting the application.

The application package should contain the relevant documents, including:

Cover letter

Curriculum vitae

Doctoral certificate

Project description

List of two referees

Optional SAI member reference letter

Applicants should carefully check the document requirements before submitting the application to avoid omissions.

Heidelberg University Fellowship Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET

Applicants should submit their applications before the stated deadline.

It is advisable not to wait until the final hours of the application period, particularly because applicants need to prepare several documents and combine the required attachments into a single PDF.

The selection process is expected to take place by the end of 2026.

How to Apply for the South Asia Institute Joint Scholarship Programme

Applications must be submitted online through the official application portal.

The programme explicitly states that applications sent by email will not be considered.

Applicants should therefore follow these steps:

Step 1: Review the Eligibility Requirements

Confirm that you are a young researcher from one of the eligible South Asian countries and that you meet the academic requirements.

Step 2: Develop Your Research Project

Prepare a well-defined research project that can be undertaken and further developed during the three-month stay at the South Asia Institute.

The project should have clear academic value and potential for future development into a third-party funding application.

Step 3: Prepare the Cover Letter

Write a concise cover letter of no more than one page explaining your motivation, research interests and the relevance of the fellowship to your academic development.

Step 4: Update Your CV

Prepare a maximum two-page academic CV and include your top ten publications.

Step 5: Complete the Project Description Template

Download and complete the required project-description template.

Applicants should ensure that all requested information is properly addressed.

Step 6: Identify Two Referees

Prepare a list of two referees who may be contacted to provide additional information about your academic and research background.

Step 7: Add Supporting Documents

Include a copy of your doctoral certificate and, where applicable, an optional letter of reference from an SAI member.

Step 8: Combine the Documents into One PDF

The application attachments should be uploaded as a single PDF.

Check the document carefully before submission to ensure that all required materials are included and legible.

Step 9: Submit Through the Online Portal

Complete the online application and upload the required PDF through the designated application portal.

Applications sent by email will not be considered.

APPLY HERE

Visa Assistance for Successful Applicants

The programme also provides support for applicants who may require assistance with visa-related arrangements.

The SAI Delhi office will provide assistance with visa applications if necessary.

This is an important consideration for successful applicants who need to obtain the appropriate documentation to travel to Germany for their fellowship.

Applicants should nevertheless make sure that they understand the applicable visa requirements and follow the instructions provided by the programme after selection.

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Young Researchers

The Heidelberg University and Max Weber Forum joint fellowship offers several potential benefits for researchers at the early stages of their academic careers.

International Research Experience

Spending three months at the South Asia Institute in Heidelberg gives fellows the opportunity to work within an international academic environment.

Academic Networking

Active participation in scientific events can enable fellows to connect with researchers and academics whose interests overlap with their own.

Research Collaboration

The programme specifically seeks to establish and develop research collaboration between young scholars from South Asia and the South Asia Institute.

Funding Development Skills

A particularly important feature of the fellowship is the opportunity to develop the research project into a third-party funding application.

This can help researchers gain practical experience in developing projects suitable for future external funding.

Financial Support

The programme provides a monthly scholarship of EUR 1,200, international travel reimbursement of up to EUR 1,500, and payment of rental costs.

Exposure to Heidelberg’s Academic Environment

The fellowship provides an opportunity to conduct research while being based at Heidelberg University’s South Asia Institute in Germany.

Potential Long-Term Academic Opportunities

The relationships established during the fellowship could potentially support future research partnerships, academic exchanges, events and funding applications.

Visit HERE for more information about the Heidelberg University Joint Scholarship Programme 2027.

What Makes the Programme Different?

Unlike an opportunity focused exclusively on financial assistance, this fellowship combines funding, international research experience, academic networking and project development.

The requirement to develop the proposed project into a potential third-party funding application means fellows are expected to think beyond the three-month fellowship.

The programme can therefore serve as a platform for researchers who want to develop a longer-term research agenda and build institutional relationships with scholars at the South Asia Institute.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants interested in this fellowship should pay close attention to the quality and relevance of their application.

Make the Research Project Clear

The proposed research should be clearly defined and demonstrate why the project would benefit from being developed at the South Asia Institute.

Demonstrate Academic Strength

The CV should highlight the applicant’s strongest academic achievements, research experience and top publications.

Explain the Value of Collaboration

Applicants should clearly communicate why collaboration with the South Asia Institute is important for their research and how the fellowship could strengthen their work.

Connect the Project to Future Funding

Since the programme expects the research project to be developed into a third-party funding application, applicants should consider how the proposed research could eventually evolve into a larger externally funded initiative.

Follow Every Formatting Requirement

Applicants should respect the limits of the following:

One page for the cover letter.

Two pages for the CV.

One PDF for the application attachments.

Failure to follow instructions can make an otherwise strong application unnecessarily difficult to assess.

Submit Before the Deadline

The final deadline is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET. Applicants should allow sufficient time to complete the online form and upload their documents.

Key Details at a Glance

Joint Scholarship Programme of the South Asia Institute, Heidelberg University and Max Weber Forum for South Asian Studies Delhi

Heidelberg, Germany

1 December 2026, 23:59 CET

Selection
By the end of 2026

Final Thoughts

The Joint Scholarship Programme of the South Asia Institute, Heidelberg University and the Max Weber Forum for South Asian Studies, Delhi, provides a valuable international research opportunity for young scholars from India, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

With a three-month research stay in Heidelberg, a EUR 1,200 monthly scholarship, international travel support of up to EUR 1,500, rental-cost support and opportunities to participate in academic activities, the fellowship can provide both financial assistance and meaningful professional development.

Perhaps most importantly, the programme is designed to encourage researchers to turn an initial research idea into a potentially larger project capable of attracting third-party funding. This makes it particularly relevant to doctoral-level researchers seeking to expand their academic networks, strengthen research collaborations and develop sustainable international research initiatives.

Eligible researchers who are interested in South Asian studies and related disciplines should carefully prepare their application materials and submit their applications through the official online portal before 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

TITLE: 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme in Ghana: Apply for €8,000–€10,000 Grants Supporting Persons with Disabilities

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme is now open for applications from eligible civil society organisations in Ghana seeking financial support to implement innovative, locally grounded projects that promote the meaningful participation, economic empowerment and integration of persons with disabilities.

Launched by the Embassy of France in Ghana, the 2026 programme represents the sixth edition of the Dwabo Small Grants Programme and places a particular emphasis on economic inclusion and employability of persons with disabilities.

Successful projects can receive grants ranging from €8,000 to €10,000 for implementation over a 12-month period. The programme is designed to support practical initiatives that address barriers preventing persons with disabilities from accessing education, skills development, employment, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods.

The application deadline is 23 September 2026 at 23:59. Both hard-copy and electronic submissions are required, and applicants must ensure that all required documents are submitted before the deadline.

About the 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme

The Dwabo Small Grants Programme is an initiative of the Embassy of France in Ghana intended to support projects that address important social and economic inclusion challenges.

For the 2026 edition, the programme focuses on improving the participation and economic integration of persons with disabilities. The call seeks projects that move beyond awareness alone and produce practical, measurable outcomes that can improve access to economic opportunities.

The programme is particularly interested in initiatives that:

Develop market-relevant skills for persons with disabilities.

Improve access to employment opportunities.

Support entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods.

Remove barriers to participation in the labour market.

Improve accessibility within educational and working environments.

Promote reasonable accommodation and assistive technologies.

Reduce stigma and misconceptions surrounding disability.

Strengthen disability-inclusive policies and institutional systems.

Build partnerships between disability organisations, civil society, government, employers and the private sector.

The French Embassy describes the programme as part of broader efforts to eliminate barriers to the economic empowerment of persons with disabilities and contribute to more inclusive societies. The initiative also contributes to Sustainable Development Goal priorities, particularly SDG 4 on Quality Education, SDG 8 on Decent Work and Economic Growth, and SDG 10 on Reduced Inequalities.

What the 2026 Dwabo Grant Supports

The programme is looking for innovative and locally implementable projects that can translate disability rights and inclusion principles into practical economic opportunities.

Projects may focus on one or several areas related to disability-inclusive economic participation.

1. Economic Empowerment and Employability

Projects can address barriers that prevent persons with disabilities from obtaining and retaining meaningful employment.

Potential interventions could include initiatives that improve employability, develop job-related skills, connect beneficiaries with employers or create more accessible pathways into the labour market.

The objective is to help persons with disabilities participate more meaningfully in economic activities rather than remain excluded from employment and income-generating opportunities.

2. Inclusive Education and Skills Development

The programme supports efforts to improve access to inclusive educational, vocational and other training environments, particularly from the secondary education level onwards.

Projects could therefore address gaps that prevent persons with disabilities from participating effectively in skills development programmes.

This may include improving the accessibility of training environments, strengthening inclusive teaching approaches or creating pathways between training and employment.

3. Accessibility and Reasonable Accommodation

Another priority is adapting educational and workplace environments to meet the accessibility requirements of persons with disabilities.

Projects may address:

Physical accessibility.

Reasonable accommodation.

Accessible learning environments.

Accessible workplaces.

Assistive technology.

Other practical measures that allow persons with disabilities to participate fully.

The focus is on identifying and reducing barriers that limit participation.

4. Awareness and Community Capacity

The programme also seeks to strengthen community awareness and capacity to identify and address barriers affecting the inclusion and economic participation of persons with disabilities.

Projects may therefore work with communities, employers, institutions or other stakeholders to improve understanding of disability inclusion and develop practical responses to exclusion.

5. Reducing Stigma and Stereotypes

Stigma, stereotypes and misconceptions about disability can create significant barriers to education, employment, entrepreneurship and skills development.

The 2026 call therefore supports initiatives designed to challenge misconceptions about the capabilities of persons with disabilities and encourage more inclusive attitudes and practices.

6. Legal, Policy and Institutional Frameworks

Projects may also contribute to strengthening legal, policy and institutional frameworks that promote disability-inclusive education, skills development, employment and economic participation.

This can involve working with relevant institutions and stakeholders to identify gaps and develop or strengthen approaches that support greater inclusion.

7. Partnerships for Economic Inclusion

The programme encourages collaboration among different stakeholders.

These can include:

Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs).

Civil society organisations.

Public institutions.

Employers.

Skills-development institutions.

Private-sector organisations.

Local authorities.

Other relevant development partners.

Partnership-based projects can help create sustainable pathways into employment, entrepreneurship and broader economic participation.

Grant Amount and Project Duration

Successful applicants can receive between:

€8,000 and €10,000 per project

The grant supports projects implemented over:

12 months

Applicants should therefore develop realistic project plans that can be delivered within the specified implementation period.

The proposed budget should clearly correspond to the project’s activities, expected results and implementation requirements.

Who Can Apply for the 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme?

The opportunity is not designed for individual applicants.

The eligible applicants are legally registered civil society organisations operating in Ghana.

According to the published eligibility requirements, eligible organisations include:

Legally registered and recognised civil society organisations in Ghana.

Civil society organisations affiliated with established networks or coalitions.

Organisations with a regional or district-level presence in Ghana.

Organisations working with local partners to implement projects.

Organisations with demonstrated experience in disability inclusion, economic empowerment, employability, skills development, livelihoods, entrepreneurship, education, human rights or closely related areas.

Organisations with adequate organisational, technical and financial capacity to manage and account for grant funding.

Organisations with appropriate governance, financial management and internal control arrangements.

Geographic Eligibility

The 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme is Ghana-specific.

Therefore, the primary geographic eligibility is:

Country: Ghana

The applicant organisation must be legally registered and operating in Ghana.

This means that an individual from another African country, Europe, Asia, North America or another part of the world cannot apply simply as an individual.

Likewise, an international organisation would need to satisfy the programme’s specific requirements concerning eligible operations and partnerships in Ghana.

What Kind of Organisations Are Particularly Relevant?

Organisations whose existing work relates to disability inclusion and economic empowerment may be particularly relevant to this call.

Relevant organisational experience may include:

Disability rights and inclusion.

Economic empowerment.

Employment and employability.

Vocational and technical skills development.

Entrepreneurship.

Livelihood development.

Inclusive education.

Human rights.

Community development.

Accessibility.

Social protection and inclusion.

Workplace inclusion.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate that they have the organisational capacity and relevant experience necessary to implement the proposed project successfully.

Priority for Disadvantaged Regions

The programme indicates that preference will be given to projects implemented in disadvantaged regions, with particular emphasis on Northern Ghana.

Applicants planning projects in underserved communities should therefore clearly explain the local context, the barriers faced by persons with disabilities and how the proposed intervention will respond to those challenges.

However, applicants should still ensure that their project meets all eligibility and programme requirements rather than assuming that geographic location alone guarantees funding.

Co-Financing Requirement

Applicants are required to include at least 10% co-financing in their project proposals.

Co-financing can demonstrate that the proposed project has support beyond the Dwabo grant and may contribute to the sustainability of the intervention.

Potential sources of co-financing could include contributions from partners, other donors, private-sector organisations or other eligible sources, subject to the programme’s rules.

Projects that benefit from co-financing involving other partners may receive favourable consideration.

Possible partners can include:

NGOs.

Private-sector organisations.

Local authorities.

Other donors.

Community organisations.

Relevant institutions.

Important Budget Requirements

Applicants should pay close attention to the programme’s financial requirements when preparing their proposals.

Administrative and Operational Costs

Administrative and operational costs must not exceed 8% of the global project budget.

This means that the majority of the requested funding should be directed towards the actual implementation of project activities and achievement of intended results.

Equipment Costs

Equipment expenditure is limited to 7% of the total budget.

Applicants should therefore avoid developing proposals in which most of the requested funding is dedicated to purchasing equipment.

The proposal should instead demonstrate how resources will contribute directly to the project’s objectives and beneficiaries.

Sitting Allowances and Honoraria

The published requirements state that proposals should not include sitting allowances or honoraria.

Applicants should take this restriction into account when preparing their budgets.

Projects That Are Not Eligible

Not every type of activity qualifies for funding under the 2026 Dwabo programme.

Applicants should carefully distinguish between a project that contributes to disability-inclusive economic participation and an activity that falls outside the scope of the call.

The following types of actions are listed as ineligible:

Individual Participation in Events

Projects concerned only or mainly with individual sponsorship for participation in:

Workshops.

Seminars.

Conferences.

Congresses.

are not eligible.

Standalone Events

Projects focused only on organising workshops, seminars, conferences or congresses are also not eligible.

The programme is looking for substantive projects that produce meaningful inclusion and economic participation outcomes rather than simply financing events.

Individual Scholarships

Projects concerned only or mainly with individual scholarships for studies or training courses are not eligible.

This is an important distinction because the Dwabo programme is a project grant for eligible organisations, not an individual scholarship programme.

Formal Education

Projects in the formal education sector are generally ineligible except in special circumstances.

Applicants should therefore ensure that an education-related project clearly fits within the programme’s broader disability inclusion and economic participation objectives.
