TITLE: TD Securities Women at TD 2026–2027 University Mentorship Program for Undergraduate Women in Canada

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The TD Securities Women at TD University Mentorship Program 2026–2027 is a career-development and mentorship opportunity designed to encourage undergraduate women to explore careers in capital markets and learn more about opportunities within TD Securities.

The program provides selected students with access to one-on-one mentorship with TD Securities leaders, group events, networking opportunities, job-shadowing experiences, and exposure to different areas of the capital markets industry. It is particularly designed for undergraduate students in their first or second year of university who are interested in building a future career in capital markets.

Successful participants will take part in a structured six-month mentorship experience running approximately from October 2026 to April 2027.

About TD Securities

TD Securities is the capital markets division of TD Bank and provides a broad range of financial products and services to corporate, government, and institutional clients.

Its areas of activity include:

Investment Banking

Corporate Banking

Capital Markets

Interest Rate Products

Currency Products

Derivative Products

Debt and equity underwriting and distribution

Strategic mergers and acquisitions advice

Trading and investment services

Through its global operations, TD Securities works with clients on financial and strategic needs while providing students and early-career professionals with opportunities to learn about the financial services industry.

The Women at TD University Mentorship Program is designed to give undergraduate students an opportunity to gain firsthand insight into this environment before making important decisions about their future careers.

What Is the TD Securities University Mentorship Program?

The TD Securities University Mentorship Program (UMP) is an initiative of the TD Securities Women at TD committee.

Its primary purpose is to encourage women at the university level to explore the world of capital markets and consider pursuing careers in this area.

Rather than being a traditional paid employment position, the program focuses on:

Career exploration

Professional mentorship

Networking

Leadership development

Exposure to capital markets

Understanding career paths within TD Securities

Preparation for future co-op and graduate opportunities

Selected students will be paired with TD Securities mentors who can provide guidance based on their professional experience.

The program can therefore help participants better understand what working in capital markets is like and what steps they can take during university to position themselves for future opportunities.

TD Securities Women at TD Mentorship Program 2026–2027 Benefits

Participants can gain several valuable professional and career-development benefits throughout the six-month program.

1. One-on-One Mentorship

Each selected mentee will be matched with a TD Securities mentor.

The mentor may be either a woman or a man working within TD Securities.

This relationship provides students with an opportunity to ask questions, seek career advice, discuss professional goals, and learn from someone with experience in the financial services industry.

2. Exposure to Capital Markets Careers

The program is specifically designed for students who want to learn more about careers in capital markets.

Participants can gain a better understanding of the different roles, teams, and career paths available within the industry.

This can be particularly valuable for students who are still deciding which area of finance they may want to pursue.

3. Networking Opportunities

Participants can develop professional relationships with TD Securities employees and other students.

Networking opportunities may help students learn about:

Different career paths

Recruitment processes

University-to-work transitions

Co-op opportunities

Graduate employment opportunities

Skills required in capital markets

4. Trading Floor Experience

Group events may provide participants with an opportunity to meet professionals from different product groups and tour the trading floor.

This can give students firsthand exposure to the environment in which capital markets professionals work.

5. Job Shadowing

Mentees may have opportunities to participate in job-shadowing experiences across various TD Securities groups.

Job shadowing can help students understand what professionals actually do in different areas of the organization.

6. Career Guidance

Participants can seek advice from TD Securities personnel about building a career in capital markets.

This can help students make more informed decisions about:

Academic choices

Extracurricular activities

Professional development

Networking

Internships and co-op positions

Long-term career planning

7. Exposure to TD’s Workplace Culture

The program can also give participants an opportunity to experience TD’s diverse and inclusive culture firsthand.

This provides students with insight into the organization’s working environment and professional expectations.

8. Potential Future Opportunities

Participation in the mentorship program may help students become more familiar with future opportunities at TD Securities, including potential summer co-op and post-graduate opportunities.

However, participation does not guarantee future employment or a paid position with TD Securities.

Mentorship Program Structure

The 2026–2027 program will select undergraduate students from various Canadian universities.

Approximately:

10–15 first-year students will be accepted.

15–20 second-year students will be accepted.

Selected participants will enter a structured mentoring relationship lasting approximately six months, from October 2026 to April 2027.

The formal mentorship relationship will conclude at the end of the six-month period. However, TD Securities encourages mentors and mentees to remain in contact after the formal program ends if both parties wish to continue the relationship.

Monthly Commitment

Applicants must be prepared to commit sufficient time and energy to the program.

Participants are expected to confirm their availability for:

Two one-on-one mentorship sessions per month

One group event per month

Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic and extracurricular schedules allow them to participate consistently.

Who Is Eligible for the TD Securities Women at TD University Mentorship Program?

The program has specific eligibility requirements.

Applicants must meet the following criteria:

1. First- or Second-Year Undergraduate Student

Applicants must currently be enrolled in their first or second year of undergraduate studies at a Canadian university.

The program is intended for students graduating in:

Spring 2028, or

Spring 2029

2. Identifies as a Woman

The opportunity is specifically intended for undergraduate students who identify as women, including transgender women.

3. Interest in Capital Markets

Applicants should have a genuine interest in pursuing a career in capital markets and an interest in TD Securities.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate that they have considered why capital markets appeals to them and how the mentorship program could support their career development.

4. Strong Academic Record

Applicants must demonstrate strong academic performance.

Academic records will be evidenced through the submission of an official or appropriate university transcript as part of the application.

5. Leadership Skills

Applicants should demonstrate leadership ability.

Leadership does not necessarily have to come from formal employment. Examples may include involvement in:

University clubs

Student organizations

Sports

Extracurricular activities

Community activities

Other leadership initiatives

Students should be able to demonstrate how they have taken initiative, influenced others, contributed to a team, or taken responsibility for achieving a goal.

6. Commitment to the Program

Applicants must be prepared to dedicate the necessary time and effort to participate in the mentorship program.

The monthly commitment includes two one-on-one mentorship sessions and one group event.

Who Cannot Apply?

Students should pay particular attention to the program’s year-of-study requirements.

The opportunity is not designed for:

Students outside their first or second year of undergraduate study

Students graduating outside the specified 2028 or 2029 graduation timelines

Students who do not identify as women

Students without an interest in capital markets

Students unable to commit the required time to the program

There is also an important restriction for returning participants.

If a student previously participated in the University Mentorship Program as a first-year student, they are not eligible to participate again as a second-year student.

What Documents Are Required?

Applicants must submit several materials as part of their application.

The required application materials include:

Resume

Transcript

Availability confirmation

Essay submission

Applicants should make sure that all required documents are uploaded in the appropriate attachment section of the application.

TD specifically states that applicants should submit all required documentation through the attachments section of the application process where the resume is uploaded.

Essay Requirements

Applicants are required to submit written responses as part of the application.

The essay component contains two parts.

Essay Question: Choose One

Applicants must answer one of the following questions in a maximum of 400 words:

Option A:

“Describe an experience that has shaped you as a leader.”

Option B:

“What experience made you interested in a career in capital markets?”

Applicants should choose the question that allows them to provide the strongest and most authentic response.

For the leadership question, applicants could discuss an experience that demonstrates initiative, responsibility, teamwork, problem-solving, resilience, or the ability to influence others.

For the capital markets question, applicants should explain what sparked their interest and how that experience influenced their career aspirations.

Mentorship Goals and Expectations

Applicants must also answer the following question in a maximum of 100 words:

“What are your goals and expectations of the mentoring program?”

A strong response should clearly explain what the applicant hopes to learn, the type of guidance they are seeking, and how the mentorship experience connects with their academic and professional goals.

Application Process

Students interested in applying should prepare all required documents before beginning the application.

The application process requires applicants to provide:

A current resume

Their university transcript

Confirmation of their availability

Their required essay responses

Their name and program of study

Applicants should ensure that all documents are attached correctly before submitting the application.

Application Deadline

The official application deadline stated in the opportunity is:

11:59 PM EST on Sunday, September 27, 2026.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

The job posting page currently displays an end date of September 28, 2026, while the detailed application instructions specify 11:59 PM EST on September 27, 2026. Applicants should therefore treat September 27, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST as the operative deadline.

Is the TD Mentorship Program Paid?

No.

The TD Securities University Mentorship Program is explicitly described as unpaid.

The purpose of the program is learning, mentorship, career development, and networking rather than paid employment.

Although participation may potentially lead to future paid opportunities with TD Securities, TD does not guarantee that participation will result in employment, a co-op position, or another paid opportunity.

Applicants should therefore view the program primarily as a professional development and networking opportunity.

Selection and Interview Process

TD Securities will review applications submitted by interested students.

Only qualified candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted for an interview.

The organization states that it will make efforts to communicate outcomes to applicants by email or phone.

Applicants should therefore monitor the contact information provided in their application after submitting their materials.

Why This Mentorship Opportunity Matters

For undergraduate students interested in finance, capital markets, investment banking, trading, corporate banking, or related fields, gaining exposure to professionals early in university can be valuable.

Many students begin university without a clear understanding of the different career paths available in financial services. A structured mentorship program can help bridge that knowledge gap by connecting students directly with professionals.

Through the TD Securities program, participants can learn about the industry while they still have time to develop relevant academic, extracurricular, networking, and professional experiences before graduation.

The opportunity may be particularly useful for students who want to understand what capital markets careers look like in practice rather than relying solely on classroom learning.

What Applicants Should Highlight

Students preparing their applications should consider demonstrating the following qualities:

Genuine interest in capital markets

Strong academic performance

Leadership experience

Initiative

Teamwork

Curiosity

Communication skills

Commitment to professional development

Clear career aspirations

Willingness to learn from mentors

Ability to commit to the program’s schedule

The application should provide evidence rather than simply listing these qualities.

For example, instead of simply stating that an applicant is a leader, the essay could describe a specific situation in which the applicant took responsibility, faced a challenge, made decisions, and achieved an outcome.

About TD Bank

TD is one of the major financial institutions in North America, serving more than 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States, and other markets.

The organization has more than 95,000 employees and operates across a broad range of financial services.

TD emphasizes career development, training, mentorship, inclusion, and opportunities for employees to develop their skills.

The organization’s stated values include Impact, Growth, and a Culture of Care, reflecting its focus on supporting customers, colleagues, and communities.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

TD states that it is committed to creating an inclusive workplace in which employees can bring their authentic selves to work and have equitable opportunities to grow.

The Women at TD mentorship initiative forms part of this broader commitment to supporting diverse perspectives and encouraging women to explore careers in areas such as capital markets.

Important Information for Applicants

Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully review the following points:

The program is for first- and second-year undergraduate students.

Applicants must identify as women, including transgender women.

Applicants must be enrolled at a Canadian university.

Applicants should be graduating in spring 2028 or 2029.

Applicants should have a strong academic record.

Applicants should demonstrate leadership skills.

Applicants must have an interest in capital markets and TD Securities.

Participation is unpaid.

Participants must commit to two one-on-one mentorship sessions and one group event each month.

The formal mentorship period is approximately October 2026 to April 2027.

Applicants must submit a resume and transcript.

Applicants must complete the required essay responses.

Previous first-year participants cannot participate again as second-year students.

Future employment or paid opportunities are not guaranteed.

The stated application deadline is 11:59 PM EST on September 27, 2026.

Conclusion

The TD Securities Women at TD 2026–2027 University Mentorship Program offers eligible undergraduate women an opportunity to gain early exposure to the capital markets industry while building professional relationships with TD Securities leaders.

Through structured mentorship, networking, job-shadowing opportunities, trading-floor exposure, group events, and career guidance, participants can develop a clearer understanding of capital markets and begin preparing for future co-op and graduate career opportunities.

For eligible first- and second-year undergraduate students in Canada who are academically strong, demonstrate leadership, and are genuinely interested in capital markets, this program can provide valuable professional exposure well before graduation.

Interested students should prepare their resume, transcript, availability confirmation, and essay responses carefully and submit their complete application by 11:59 PM EST on September 27, 2026.

TITLE: Global Mental Health Fellowship Program 2026 Cohort 5: Applications Open for Young Mental Health Changemakers Worldwide

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the Global Mental Health Fellowship Program 2026 (Cohort 5), an international virtual fellowship designed to create a space where young people can explore mental health, share perspectives, build practical skills, connect across communities and cultures, and translate their learning into meaningful action.

Under the theme “Strengthening Mental Health Through Lived Experiences,” the fifth cohort of the Global Mental Health Fellowship recognizes that people’s understanding of mental health is influenced by their environments, communities, relationships, observations, challenges, and experiences.

Rather than expecting applicants to already be mental health experts, the fellowship focuses on curiosity, willingness to learn, individual perspectives, and the potential of young people to contribute meaningfully to conversations surrounding mental health.

Applications opened on September 16, 2026, and interested candidates have until September 26, 2026 to submit their applications.

About the Global Mental Health Fellowship Program 2026

The Global Mental Health Fellowship Program provides young people with an opportunity to engage with mental health issues while developing the skills, perspectives, connections, and confidence needed to contribute to positive change.

Cohort 5 is founded on the understanding that every individual develops a unique perspective based on their experiences.

The communities people grow up in, challenges they encounter, people they interact with, situations they observe, and lessons they learn can all influence how they understand mental health and wellbeing.

Through the 2026 fellowship, Global MHF aims to create a platform where young people can bring these perspectives into meaningful conversations while learning from other participants from different communities and cultural backgrounds.

The program is designed not simply around discussion but around helping participants turn learning into action.

Theme of Global Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 5

The theme for the 2026 Cohort 5 program is:

Strengthening Mental Health Through Lived Experiences

Lived experiences can provide valuable perspectives on how mental health challenges are understood and addressed within different families, communities, cultures, and social environments.

The fellowship therefore values the perspectives that individuals bring to mental health conversations based on what they have experienced, witnessed, learned, or observed.

Importantly, however, applicants are not required to disclose traumatic, sensitive, or deeply personal experiences in order to apply for or participate in the fellowship.

Applicants are specifically encouraged to share only information they feel comfortable sharing.

This approach allows participants to contribute their perspectives without feeling compelled to reveal private experiences simply to demonstrate their suitability for the program.

What Is the Purpose of the Global Mental Health Fellowship?

The Global Mental Health Fellowship seeks to provide young people with an environment where they can learn, engage, connect, and develop their capacity to contribute to mental health advocacy and positive social change.

Cohort 5 creates opportunities for young people to:

Participate in meaningful conversations around mental health.

Develop practical skills that can support their growth as changemakers.

Learn from different perspectives and lived experiences.

Connect with other young people across communities and cultures.

Strengthen their understanding of mental health issues.

Translate knowledge and learning into meaningful action.

Develop their capacity to participate in mental health advocacy.

Contribute their individual perspectives and community insights.

Build relationships within a wider network of young people interested in mental health.

The program places considerable emphasis on learning through interaction, perspective-sharing, and cross-cultural engagement.

What Participants Can Gain from the Fellowship

Participants selected for the Global Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 5 can expect several important developmental opportunities.

1. Practical Skills Development

The fellowship is designed to equip participants with practical tools that can help them develop into effective changemakers.

Rather than requiring applicants to arrive with professional mental health experience, the program creates an environment where participants can develop relevant skills through learning and engagement.

These skills may support participants who want to become more active in mental health advocacy, community engagement, awareness initiatives, and related areas of social impact.

2. Access to a Global Network

Another important element of the fellowship is the opportunity to connect with people from different communities and cultural backgrounds.

Mental health experiences and attitudes can vary considerably depending on social, economic, cultural, and community contexts.

Connecting participants across these contexts can encourage broader conversations and expose fellows to perspectives beyond their immediate environments.

This international and cross-cultural network may also provide opportunities for continued learning, collaboration, and relationship-building.

3. An Inclusive Space for Different Perspectives

The fellowship aims to create an inclusive environment in which participants’ perspectives and voices are valued.

Applicants do not need to present themselves as experts.

Instead, the program is interested in understanding applicants’ perspectives, curiosity, experiences, aspirations, and the contributions they hope to make.

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant to young people who are still developing their understanding of mental health but have a genuine interest in learning and contributing.

4. Flexible Virtual Participation

The Global Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 5 is conducted 100% virtually.

This online structure provides greater flexibility for participants and makes it possible for young people to participate without relocating or travelling internationally.

Participants can therefore engage in the fellowship while managing other academic, professional, volunteering, or personal commitments.

The virtual format also supports the fellowship’s objective of connecting young people from different communities and cultural backgrounds.

Who Can Apply for the Global Mental Health Fellowship 2026?

The fellowship is targeted at young people who are interested in mental health, learning, advocacy, community engagement, and positive social change.

Applicants should generally meet the following eligibility conditions:

Be between 20 and 25 years old.

Have an interest in mental health and related conversations.

Demonstrate curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Be interested in developing practical skills.

Be willing to engage with different perspectives.

Have an interest in connecting with young people from different communities and cultures.

Be interested in translating learning into meaningful action.

Importantly, previous professional experience is not required.

This means young people should not automatically exclude themselves because they have never worked professionally in mental health, psychology, counselling, public health, or advocacy.

Passion, curiosity, perspective, and willingness to learn are central considerations for the fellowship.

Do You Need Mental Health Experience to Apply?

No prior experience is required.

This is one of the important features of the Global Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 5.

The fellowship is accessible to young people who may be at an early stage of their involvement with mental health advocacy or social impact.

Applicants therefore do not necessarily need professional qualifications in psychology, psychiatry, counselling, public health, medicine, social work, or another mental health-related discipline.

Instead, the fellowship seeks young people who demonstrate genuine interest, curiosity, and willingness to learn and contribute.

The Importance of Lived Experience

The 2026 cohort specifically recognizes the value of lived experiences and the perspectives they can bring to mental health conversations.

However, “lived experience” should not be interpreted as a requirement to disclose trauma or a mental health diagnosis.

Applicants are not required to disclose personal, traumatic, or sensitive experiences as part of their application or participation.

Candidates should only share information with which they are comfortable.

This distinction is particularly important because the application seeks to understand the individual behind the application—their perspective, curiosity, experiences, aspirations, and potential contribution—rather than requiring disclosure of sensitive personal information.

What Is the Fellowship Looking for in Applicants?

The application process is not designed around applicants having perfect answers.

Global MHF emphasizes that it wants to understand the person applying.

Applicants should therefore approach their responses thoughtfully and authentically.

In particular, candidates should consider communicating:

Their perspective on mental health and related issues.

Why mental health matters to them.

Their curiosity and willingness to learn.

What they have observed within their communities.

What they hope to learn through the fellowship.

How they would like to grow personally or professionally.

What they could contribute to conversations within the cohort.

How they may use their learning to create meaningful impact.

Applicants should avoid feeling that they need to manufacture dramatic experiences or present themselves as established mental health professionals.

The program explicitly recognizes that applicants are still learning and developing.

Why the Fellowship Focuses on Young People

Young people are important participants in conversations about mental health because they experience rapidly changing educational, professional, technological, cultural, and social environments.

Providing young people with practical skills and spaces for constructive dialogue can strengthen their capacity to participate in mental health advocacy and community action.

Through Cohort 5, participants can learn not only from structured fellowship activities but also from each other’s experiences and perspectives.

The resulting exchange can help participants develop a broader understanding of how mental health is experienced and discussed across different environments.

International and Cross-Cultural Learning

A particularly valuable dimension of the Global Mental Health Fellowship is its emphasis on connecting participants across different communities and cultures.

Mental health cannot always be understood through a single cultural or community perspective.

Attitudes toward seeking help, stigma, family support, community engagement, wellbeing, and mental health advocacy can differ substantially between societies.

Bringing young people together creates opportunities to understand these differences while identifying shared challenges and opportunities for positive action.

The fellowship therefore offers participants an opportunity to expand their perspectives while building relationships with peers interested in similar issues.

Global Mental Health Fellowship 2026 Program Format

The program is delivered 100% virtually.

This provides greater accessibility and allows selected participants to participate from their respective locations.

The online format can particularly benefit applicants who might otherwise face geographical or travel barriers to participating in an international fellowship.

Because the fellowship is virtual, candidates should consider their ability to participate consistently in online activities and engage constructively with other fellows.

Application Timeline

Applicants should take note of the official application period:

Applications Open: Wednesday, September 16, 2026

Application Deadline: Saturday, September 26, 2026

Applicants are encouraged not to wait until the final day to complete the application.

Submitting early can provide additional time to address any technical difficulties and allows candidates to review their responses carefully before final submission.

How to Apply for the Global Mental Health Fellowship 2026

Applications are being accepted through the official online application form.

Interested candidates should:

Review the fellowship information and eligibility requirements carefully.

Access the official Global Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 5 application form.

Complete all required sections of the application.

Respond thoughtfully to questions concerning their perspective, curiosity, experiences, goals, and potential contribution.

Share only personal information or experiences they are comfortable disclosing.

Review their responses for completeness and accuracy.

Submit the application before September 26, 2026.

Apply through the official application form:

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfb5L5Nng0wOzAdlME_HtUVIpqiouhVmViDuH-gkAd8vSGIjw/viewform

Important Advice for Applicants

Candidates should remember that the application is not an examination of how much they already know about mental health.

Applicants should focus on communicating their genuine motivation and perspective.

A thoughtful application can explain why the applicant cares about mental health, what they hope to learn, what they have observed in their community, and how participation in the fellowship could help them contribute more effectively.

Applicants should also respect their own privacy. The program explicitly states that candidates do not have to disclose traumatic or sensitive personal experiences.

Authenticity does not require revealing information that an applicant would prefer to keep private.

Why Consider the Global Mental Health Fellowship?

For young people interested in mental health, advocacy, community development, youth engagement, social impact, or related areas, the fellowship provides an opportunity to develop knowledge and practical capabilities within an international learning environment.

The combination of practical skills development, cross-cultural interaction, perspective-sharing, and virtual accessibility makes the program particularly relevant to emerging young changemakers who may not yet have extensive professional experience.

Because no previous experience is required, Cohort 5 can also provide an entry point for young people who want to begin contributing more actively to mental health conversations and initiatives.

Deadline

The deadline to apply for the Global Mental Health Fellowship Program 2026 (Cohort 5) is:

Saturday, September 26, 2026

Interested candidates should complete and submit the official application form before the deadline.

Conclusion

The Global Mental Health Fellowship Program 2026 (Cohort 5) provides young people with an opportunity to transform their perspectives, curiosity, community insights, and lived experiences into meaningful learning and action.

Built around the theme “Strengthening Mental Health Through Lived Experiences,” the fellowship recognizes that meaningful contributions to mental health conversations do not come exclusively from established professionals. Young people’s experiences, observations, questions, and perspectives can also contribute to improving how mental health is understood and addressed.

With no prior experience required and a fully virtual structure, the fellowship lowers important barriers to participation and creates opportunities for young people to develop practical skills while connecting across communities and cultures.

Applicants aged 20 to 25 who are passionate about mental health, curious to learn, and interested in contributing to positive change are encouraged to prepare thoughtful applications and submit them by September 26, 2026.

TITLE: AAU TV African Union Day 2023 Commemoration Show – May 25, 2023

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Theme; “Accelerating the Implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area

Register here – Meeting Registration – Zoom

Background

As part of our collective reflection on Africa’s progress and the need to embrace our unity, the AAU TV commemorates African Union Day with the aim to honor Africa’s heroes who contributed to Africa’s unity as well as celebrate the achievements of African unity while fostering a deeper sense of solidarity among African nations and diaspora communities. The program seeks to reflect on the overall theme of the African Union for 2023 which is “Accelerating the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)”.

According to the United Nations (UN), Africa has the youngest population in the world, with 70% under the age of 30. This proportion presents a remarkable chance for the continent’s advancement. However, the majority of Africa’s youth are not empowered and included in decision-making.

AfCFTA offers enormous prospects for economic development and job creation, particularly for young people. Hence, leveraging the potential of the youth is crucial for the successful implementation of the AfCFTA. Moreover, enhancing youth inclusivity ensures that the perspectives of young people, their aspirations, and innovative ideas are integrated into the policy framework, leading to more relevant and effective outcomes and contributing to the closing of the young unemployment gap, which remains a key concern across Africa.

This two-hour and thirty-minute programme will emphasize the importance of youth inclusion in the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) as well as assess Africa’s progress in implementing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) remains Africa’s flagship project of Agenda 2063 aimed at creating a single African market for goods and services facilitated by free movement persons, capital, investment to deepen economic integration, promote and attain sustainable and inclusive socio-economic development, gender equality, industrialization, agricultural development, food security, and structural transformation.

Objectives:

To celebrate Africa’s lifelong achievement after the establishment of the Organization of African Unity

Reflect on the African Union theme on “Accelerating the Implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area”.

Highlight the impact of youth inclusivity in implementing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

TITLE: Graduate Student Lunch Club

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The CTP Lunch Club meets most Fridays at 12:30 (provided that there are sufficient speakers).

About the Seminar
The seminars are designed for graduate students and should be accessible to all students. First year students are particularly encouraged to attend so that they may learn about research being performed in the CTP.

Email notification of the club will be sent to the ctp-all, ctp-postdocs and ctp-students email lists as appropriate. If you wish to speak, or have suggestions about speakers and/or possible workshop topics, please contact the organizers: Wenjie Gong, Angus Lowe, Richard Allen, Rachel Stein, Manu Srivastava

Friday, February 3
Stella Schindler, MIT
Title: Factorization Enabling Lattice Calculations of TMDs
Abstract: Transverse momentum distributions (TMDs) encode the three-dimensional momentum structure of quarks and gluons inside hadrons. Global fits to experimental data exhibit large uncertainties for non-perturbative parton momenta, a kinematic region where lattice QCD is typically well-positioned to provide complementary information. Unfortunately, TMD dynamics are dominated by the lightcone, which induces a so-called sign problem, an obstacle to numerics that is NP-hard in the general case. To circumvent this issue, lattice theorists typically project Wilson lines appearing in TMD matrix elements from a lightcone path onto an equal-time slice. We derive a factorization formula connecting the resulting lattice-calculable equal-time distributions (quasi-TMDs) to the TMDs that appear in cross-sections (Collins scheme). This formula holds at leading power to all orders in α_s, for all spins and parton flavors. The factorization establishes that lattice and physical TMDs share the same IR physics, and opens the path towards computing gluon TMDs.

TITLE: Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 at PNNL | Fully Funded Research Fellowship in the USA

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is now accepting applications from outstanding early-career scientists and engineers who are ready to pursue ambitious, independent research.

The prestigious fellowship provides selected researchers with full funding to undertake a major research project of their own conception at PNNL. Fellows have the opportunity to develop original research ideas, work with internationally recognised scientists, access advanced research capabilities, and contribute to discoveries addressing important scientific and national challenges.

The programme is designed for the next generation of scientists and engineers who want to push the boundaries of research and development and produce work with the potential for world-recognised impact.

What Is the Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship?

The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship is a postdoctoral research programme hosted by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory.

Named after renowned scientist Linus Pauling, the fellowship supports exceptional recent and upcoming PhD graduates in science and engineering.

Unlike a conventional postdoctoral position where researchers may primarily work on an established project, the Linus Pauling Fellowship allows successful candidates to propose and pursue a major research project of their own design.

Applicants are expected to develop a detailed and original research proposal explaining their research plans, objectives, methodology, and anticipated outcomes.

The fellowship therefore provides an opportunity for talented early-career researchers to demonstrate scientific independence while benefiting from PNNL’s research environment and expertise.

What Does the Fellowship Offer?

Selected Linus Pauling Fellows receive full funding to pursue their proposed research at PNNL.

The fellowship provides researchers with an opportunity to:

Develop and conduct a major research project of their own conception.

Work alongside internationally recognised researchers.

Access state-of-the-art scientific and technological capabilities.

Develop innovative approaches to complex research questions.

Advance scientific knowledge in their chosen field.

Contribute to research addressing pressing national concerns.

Build their scientific and professional networks.

Develop their independence as researchers.

Work within one of the United States’ leading national laboratory environments.

The programme is particularly suited to researchers who already have a strong research background and a clear vision for an ambitious postdoctoral project.

Research Areas

Applicants can propose research connected to PNNL’s mission areas.

The fellowship highlights four broad areas of research:

1. Scientific Discovery

Researchers interested in fundamental and applied scientific discovery can develop projects aimed at expanding knowledge and creating new scientific capabilities.

Projects may involve emerging scientific questions and approaches capable of generating significant discoveries.

2. Energy Resiliency

Energy is one of PNNL’s major research areas.

Researchers can explore topics related to energy systems, energy technologies, resilience, sustainability, and other challenges associated with securing and transforming energy systems.

3. Data Science and Computing

The fellowship also supports research involving data science and computing.

This area can be relevant to researchers developing advanced computational methods, data-driven approaches, modelling techniques, artificial intelligence applications, and other computational research aligned with PNNL’s mission.

4. National Security

PNNL conducts research addressing important national security challenges.

Applicants whose research interests align with this area may develop proposals addressing scientific and technological challenges relevant to national security.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship is intended for qualified recent and upcoming PhD graduates in science and engineering.

Applicants must have completed, or be on track to complete, a PhD in a science or engineering field related to the mission areas of PNNL.

The degree must be from an accredited college or university.

For the 2027 fellowship, qualified candidates must have completed their PhD within the last three years or prior to the start of the fellowship.

This makes the opportunity particularly suitable for early-career researchers who have recently completed doctoral studies or are approaching completion.

International Applicants

The fellowship is based at PNNL in the United States.

Applicants should note that all PNNL staff must be able to demonstrate the legal right to work in the United States.

Therefore, prospective international applicants should carefully review the employment and work-authorisation requirements before applying.

Eligibility should not be assumed solely based on academic qualifications.

What Makes the Fellowship Competitive?

The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship is designed for researchers who can demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions to science and engineering.

A strong application should therefore go beyond simply describing an existing research project.

Applicants are expected to present an original research proposal that demonstrates:

A clear and important research question.

Strong scientific reasoning.

Originality and innovation.

A well-defined research approach.

Potential scientific or technological impact.

Alignment with PNNL’s mission areas.

Clear anticipated outcomes.

The potential to advance research beyond existing approaches.

The ability to demonstrate an independent research vision is an important aspect of the fellowship.

Research Proposal

One of the central components of the application is the research proposal.

Applicants must submit a detailed proposal describing the research project they intend to undertake.

The proposal should communicate the central research idea clearly and explain how the proposed work could contribute to scientific or technological advancement.

Candidates should carefully consider the connection between their proposed research and PNNL’s research priorities.

Because the fellowship allows researchers to pursue projects of their own conception, applicants should use the proposal to demonstrate both their scientific expertise and their capacity for independent research.

Mentoring and Research Environment

Linus Pauling Fellows benefit from mentoring by internationally recognised researchers at PNNL.

This provides fellows with the opportunity to work in an environment where they can receive guidance while developing their own research programme.

The fellowship combines independent research with access to experienced scientists and advanced research infrastructure.

This can be particularly valuable for researchers seeking to transition from doctoral research into more independent scientific leadership.

About Pacific Northwest National Laboratory

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a U.S. national laboratory known for research and technological innovation in areas including energy, environment, science, and national security.

PNNL conducts multidisciplinary research aimed at addressing complex scientific and societal challenges.

The laboratory’s research environment gives fellows the opportunity to work with researchers from different scientific and engineering disciplines and use advanced capabilities to pursue ambitious projects.

Why Apply for the Linus Pauling Fellowship?

The fellowship can be an important opportunity for researchers who want to establish themselves as independent scientists or engineers.

Rather than simply joining an existing research programme, successful candidates can develop a significant research project based on their own scientific vision.

The fellowship can help researchers:

Strengthen their independent research profile.

Develop a major original research project.

Work with leading scientists.

Access advanced laboratory capabilities.

Expand their professional network.

Gain experience conducting research in a national laboratory.

Build a foundation for a long-term scientific career.

Contribute to research with potential global impact.

Application Deadline

Applications for the 2027 Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship are open until:

15 October 2026 at 4:00 p.m. Pacific Standard Time (PST).

Applicants should ensure that their complete application is submitted before the stated deadline.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should apply through the official PNNL careers portal.

Application Link: https://careers.pnnl.gov/jobs/11983?lang=en-us

Applicants should review the official vacancy and fellowship information carefully for the complete application requirements, required documents, and current instructions.

The official fellowship page is also available through PNNL:

https://www.pnnl.gov/projects/linus-pauling-distinguished-postdoctoral-fellowship

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Because the fellowship is designed for researchers with the potential to generate world-recognised discoveries, applicants should dedicate significant attention to their research proposal.

Develop an Original Research Idea

The project should demonstrate originality and address a meaningful scientific or technological question.

Demonstrate Alignment With PNNL

Explain how the proposed research connects to one or more of PNNL’s mission areas, including scientific discovery, energy resiliency, data science and computing, or national security.

Clearly Explain the Research Impact

Applicants should make it clear why the proposed research matters and what could change if the research is successful.

Present a Strong Research Plan

The proposal should provide a logical pathway from the research question to the anticipated outcomes.

Demonstrate Independence

The fellowship is an opportunity to establish an independent research identity. Applicants should demonstrate their ability to formulate and lead an ambitious research programme.

Review Eligibility Carefully

Candidates should confirm that their PhD timing, academic field, work authorisation, and other requirements satisfy the official fellowship conditions before submitting an application.

Important Information for Applicants

Applicants should rely on the official PNNL fellowship and careers pages for the most current requirements.

The opportunity is highly competitive, and meeting the basic eligibility requirements does not guarantee selection.

Candidates should also ensure that their proposal and supporting materials accurately represent their academic background, research achievements, and proposed work.

Conclusion

The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for recent and upcoming PhD graduates in science and engineering to pursue ambitious independent research at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory in the United States.

Selected fellows receive full funding to undertake a major research project of their own conception while benefiting from mentorship by internationally recognised researchers and access to PNNL’s advanced scientific capabilities.

With research opportunities spanning Scientific Discovery, Energy Resiliency, Data Science and Computing, and National Security, the fellowship is particularly suited to researchers with innovative ideas and the ambition to make significant contributions to their fields.

Qualified candidates should begin preparing their research proposal and supporting application materials early. Applications close on 15 October 2026 at 4:00 p.m. PST.

TITLE: Promoting Women in Science -WoHE 2019 Conference Communiqué

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Association of African Universities (AAU), with support from the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) and other partners, held its 2nd International Leadership Conference for Women in Higher Education (WoHE, 2019) in Nairobi, Kenya from 6-8 March 2019, under the theme “Promoting Women in Science to Address the 21st Century Challenges”.

This event brought together over 70 seasoned participants from countries across the continent, including Kenya, Nigeria, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Uganda, Sudan, Egypt, Burkina Faso, Mauritius, Tanzania and Cameroun.

Dr. Beatrice Ngenja, Head of the Education Division of the African Union Commission served as the keynote speaker for this event, whilst Professor Margaret Kobia, a Cabinet Secretary in Kenya, honoured the AAU WoHE 2019 conference with her presence and officially declared the conference open. In her address, she:

emphasized that women leaders have the power to move gender equality and women empowerment to the next level.

challenged women to reflect on what they were doing in schools, institutions, departments and ministries to transform their world.

challenged women to cultivate and nurture strategic networks for collaborative research to solve the current challenges hindering the progression of women in higher education.

articulated her conviction that the gender mainstreaming budget should be influenced by women.

encouraged women to be agents of peace.

thanked the AAU, sponsors and partners in the organisation of the event and said that this event came in the backdrop of problematic statistics of about 10% women leaders in education and a ratio of 5-1 ratio of men to women in higher education; a state of affairs that needed to be addressed.

encouraged higher education institutions across the continent to continue to place emphasis on gender responsive and equitable education as well as gender friendly leadership.

The communique and resolve of participants at the 2019 international Leadership Conference for Women in Higher Education, is presented here as follows;

We, the participants at the Association of African Universities 2nd International Leadership Conference for Women in Higher Education (AAU WoHE 2019) held in Nairobi, Kenya from 6 – 8 March 2019, under the theme Promoting Women in Science to Address the 21st Century Challenges, resolve and agree on the five (5) main categories as follows:

Addressing Africa’s Challenges: the Role of Women in Science

Current Developments on Women in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics in Africa

Breaking the Glass Ceiling – Policies, Strategies and Mechanisms to support Women in STEM

Resource Mobilization Strategies to support STEM research

Barriers to Female Participation in STEM fields

Narrative Summaries of Resolutions

Addressing Africa’s Challenges: the Role of Women in Science

Participants agreed on the following:

Actively bring together women in STEM to collaborate and cooperate in carrying out needs-oriented research.

Going out to schools to mentor young girls and bring them in to universities to undertake courses in the STEM fields.

Encourage young women to take up programmes in STEM disciplines such as climate change, engineering, technology in higher education to address the current continental and global challenges.

Need to create response mechanisms that promote women advancement guided by the pursuits set out in the African Union Agenda 2063.

Women scientists to rise and reverse threats to human security such as gender inequality and gender based violence as championed by the African Union Agenda 2063, through identifying challenges and seeking resources, whether social, intellectual and/or financial, to implement solutions.

Mentor women to become visible and instrumental in roles that bring solutions at institutional, departmental and ministerial level.

Encourage experienced women scientists to move up and take the position of role models to prove to young scientists that it is possible for women to lead ground breaking research that can proffer practical solutions to the world’s challenges.

Heed the call of the African Union to plan more events that create enabling environments for women’s advancement such as the WoHE 2019 conference.
2. Current Developments on Women in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics in Africa

Participants agreed on the following:

To encourage women in STEM to seek funding from organisations and institutions that support women in research such as the organisation for women Scientists in Developing Countries (OWSD), and the Forum for African Women Educationalists, among others.

To encourage the formation of active research networks across Africa.

To formulate research groups with a mixture of experienced and young STEM researchers.

To start innovation centres at schools to encourage young women scientists.

To share research findings with communities so that STEM is connected to the community, and innovations are communicated with the people.

To explore other sources of funding, including working with private sector to be self- sustaining.

To propose the creation of gender friendly environments at institutions such as child care/day care centres that allow women to have peace of mind as they pursue their work. This will ensure career progression and help seal the leaky pipeline.

Interface STEM with social science research to ensure there is no disconnect in development programming and that no-one is left behind as endeavoured by the African Union Agenda 2063.

Promote collaborations between STEM and Arts in an attempt to better link the outside world and the laboratory. This will attract more women to take up STEM fields of study.

Establish research teams such as the ones that were created during the speed networking sessions during the WoHE 2019 Conference, linking senior women scientists with younger researchers as well as Masters and PhD students.

3. Breaking the Glass Ceiling – Policies, Strategies and Mechanisms to support Women in STEM

Participants agreed on the following:

Implement policies that encourage women’s representation in leadership positions and ensure accountability for increasing women’s participation in creating the Africa we want as espoused by the African Union.

Advocate for the introduction of Diversity and Equality training as an examinable common undergraduate course to halt gender discrimination and engender inclusive mindsets.

Present an environment where women are not seen to be disproportionately disadvantaged in scientific careers compared to men through mentorship that presents STEM as an inviting field.

Institute mentorship programmes for STEM students and young women scientists to enable them take up, and progress in STEM careers thus stopping the leaky pipeline.

Institute mentor-mentee teams involving senior female scientists and upcoming STEM researchers with the purpose of providing the platform for sharing, learning, and deliberation on, important issues. Mentorship will instil confidence and ensure much needed continuity as indicated in the case study narratives.

Implement changes in policies that disadvantage older women in science, through provision for a more favourable age limit for funding applications and award competitions. This is against the reality that women catch up much later in research and studies due to family-related breaks and leave.
4. Resource Mobilization Strategies to support STEM research

Participants agreed on the following:

Promote gender equality in science and technology-based entrepreneurship and innovation activities.

Create policies that consider extending the age of women competing for research awards

Lobby for budgetary Allocation for Gender Responsive STEM Education.

Set up monitoring and evaluation mechanisms and employ a systems approach to ensure accountability for positive outcomes in HEIs.

Mentor young STEM scientists and innovators on how to apply for grant proposals and ensure competent and fully resourced participation in solution- oriented STEM research for the current 21st century STEM economies.

Institute needs-oriented research that solves current problems, improves livelihoods of all including girls and women.

Lobby for infrastructural support in terms of laboratories and equipment to facilitate STEM at all levels of education.

5. Barriers to Female Participation in STEM fields

Participants agreed on the following:

Institute and ensure a gender responsive leadership at all levels of institution.

Deliberately set up mentorship programmes that conscientize women on the challenges of work-family balance and strategies that can be employed to manage this complex situation.

Hold institutions accountable by ensuring STEM programmes are accompanied by adequately equipped laboratories. Ill-equipped laboratories discredit science as difficult and success in it as unachievable.

Ensure there is a gender dimension in policy designs and prioritize gender equality in STEM education policy- related designs through conscious and proactive female leadership.

Advocate for the establishment and implementation of Strategic Gender responsive STEM Education policy.

Strategize to attract and retain women in STEM in Higher education at all levels (including masters and PhD, through scholarships and awards).

Promote work life – balance and appropriate re-entry mechanisms to the STEM workforce after career break or family leave.

Lobby for flexible working hours in specific circumstances that demand the attention of women

Ensure gender equality in career progression for scientists and engineers – recruitment criteria and processes, opportunities in the work place; (mentor, expose and encourage women not to give up).

Respond and report sexual harassment and support girls and women in this regard.

Concluding Remarks

Prof Chacha Nyaigoti Chacha, who conducted the closing ceremony, thanked all participants for setting time aside to respond to the call sent out for the Women in Higher Education Conference and for honouring the invitation to come to Nairobi to contribute to the vibrant discussions and engagements. He indicated that all contributions were invaluable as they added critical insights to the discussion that culminated in implementable resolutions. Prof Chacha encouraged participants to work in close collaborative networks to ensure achievement of all the resolutions drawn at the three-day conference. He emphasized the need to mainstream resolutions into action. Most important was the need for gender responsive institutions, support for science infrastructure, interfacing STEM and Social Science research, mentorship and collaboration in research. He expressed his gratitude to the AAU and its funding partners for creating such a platform on engagement of women in higher education. If properly implemented, these key enablers would significantly advance the achievement of the African Union’s Agenda 2063, he said. In closing; Prof Chacha congratulated the AAU and its funding partners, especially Sida, for being pathfinders and instrumental advocates in the advancement of women in African higher education.

Dr Sindiso Zhou; Chief Rapporteur

TITLE: Georg Arnhold Senior Fellowship 2028 in Germany: €3,300 Monthly Stipend for Education for Sustainable Peace

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Leibniz Institute for Educational Media | Georg Eckert Institute (GEI) has announced the call for applications for the 2028 Georg Arnhold Senior Fellowship for Education for Sustainable Peace. The opportunity is designed for highly accomplished scholars and practitioners who wish to undertake an advanced research or practice-related project in peace education.

The fellowship includes a research stay of up to six months at the GEI in Brunswick, Germany. The selected candidate will receive a monthly stipend of €3,300, return economy airfare to Germany, access to specialist educational-media resources, academic mentoring, and support with administrative and publication-related matters.

The application deadline is 2 November 2026. The successful candidate may begin the fellowship in January 2028 at the earliest.

The opportunity is administered by the Leibniz Institute for Educational Media | Georg Eckert Institute, while the announcement has also been shared by the Global Campaign for Peace Education.

Georg Arnhold Senior Fellowship 2028: Key Facts

Detail
Information

Programme
Georg Arnhold Senior Fellowship 2028

Host institution
Leibniz Institute for Educational Media

Location
Brunswick, Germany

Research area
Education for sustainable peace

Main focus
Educational media and curricula at secondary-school level

Duration
Normally six months

Shorter duration
Possible in exceptional cases, with a minimum of three months

Monthly stipend
€3,300

Travel support
Return economy airfare to Germany

Working language
English

Earliest start date
January 2028

Application deadline
2 November 2026

Application method
Online application form

About the Georg Arnhold Program

The Georg Arnhold Program promotes research and practice related to education for sustainable peace. It is operated by the GEI in Brunswick, Germany, an institute that researches the production, content, and use of educational media within their social, political, economic, cultural, and historical contexts.

The program was established in 2013 by American benefactor Henry H. Arnhold in honour of his grandfather, Georg Arnhold, who was a German banker, patron of the arts, and committed pacifist.

The program has three principal objectives:

To connect academic research with practical peace-education work.

To encourage decolonial approaches to peace-education research and practice.

To make research findings and practical experiences freely available through open-access publications.

The fellowship is particularly relevant to projects that examine how education can contribute to peacebuilding, reconciliation, social justice, conflict prevention, and sustainable development.

Main Focus of the Fellowship

The 2028 fellowship focuses on education for sustainable peace, particularly educational media and curricula used at the secondary-school level. Educational media may include:

School textbooks

Curriculum frameworks

Teacher-training materials

Digital educational resources

Online learning tools

Educational games

Virtual-reality learning resources

Creative pedagogical approaches

Other forms of learning and teaching media

Applicants are expected to explain how their proposed project responds to the objectives of the Georg Arnhold Program. Projects may examine the contribution of educational media to peace and reconciliation, or investigate how textbooks and curricula can reproduce inequality, exclusion, stereotypes, or conflict.

The wider program also places importance on post-conflict and transitional societies, grassroots approaches, long-term peacebuilding, and the development of educational practices that can be adapted to different regional contexts.

Possible Project Directions

The call does not prescribe a fixed list of research topics. However, suitable applicants may consider projects related to:

Peace-oriented curriculum development

Conflict-sensitive education

Textbook narratives and historical reconciliation

Decolonising school curricula

Educational media in post-conflict societies

Digital tools for peace education

Teacher education for inclusive classrooms

Education, identity, inequality, and social cohesion

The role of games and virtual reality in peace learning

Comparative studies of educational media in different regions

Educational responses to displacement and forced migration

Curriculum reforms supporting human rights and democratic citizenship

Open-access educational materials for peacebuilding

Community-based and grassroots peace-education initiatives

These examples are intended to demonstrate possible areas of alignment. Applicants should develop an original project based on their own academic or professional expertise.

Financial Support and Fellowship Benefits

The selected Senior Fellow will receive a monthly stipend of €3,300 for a normal six-month fellowship period. At the published rate, six months would equal €19,800 in total stipend support, subject to the applicant’s personal tax position and other applicable costs.

The fellowship also includes:

Return economy airfare to Germany

Administrative assistance from program coordinators

Support related to publication work

Access to the GEI’s international library of educational media

Access to school textbooks, curricula, and digital educational resources

Discussions and mentoring with GEI experts

Opportunities to present research at GEI research colloquia

Access to “The Basement,” the GEI’s experimental digital media laboratory

Contact with researchers and practitioners working in peace education and educational-media research

Possible coverage of open-access fees for direct project outputs

“The Basement” may be particularly useful for projects involving games-based learning, virtual reality, robotics, digital media, or creative pedagogies.

Applicants should carefully prepare their financial plans. The official call specifically states that candidates are responsible for arranging their passport, visa where required, health insurance, and liability insurance. Accommodation, meals, local transportation, and other personal expenses are not separately listed as covered benefits in the call, so applicants should not assume that all living costs will automatically be paid.

Responsibilities of the Selected Fellow

The successful candidate will be expected to complete a substantial project in the area of education for sustainable peace. The project should preferably focus on educational media, curriculum development, or related peace-education practice.

The Fellow will also be expected to:

Contribute to the intellectual and conceptual design of the annual Georg Arnhold Program conference in collaboration with the program coordinator.

Present the project at a GEI research colloquium.

Spend the fellowship period at the GEI in Brunswick, Germany.

Participate in the daily academic and professional life of the institute.

Work primarily in English.

Complete and publish the project outcomes no later than one year after the fellowship ends.

Preferred forms of final output include:

Policy papers

Educational materials

Research papers

Curriculum resources

Practice-oriented publications

A substantial academic or professional publication

The fellowship is therefore not simply a funded period for private study. Applicants should demonstrate how their work will produce a useful and publishable contribution to peace education.

Application Requirements and Preparation

The initial application is submitted online. Applicants will be asked to describe their proposed project through guiding questions covering:

The main objectives of the project

The research or practice gap

The theoretical framework

The methodological framework

The expected outcomes

The relationship of the project to peace education

The project’s connection with the objectives of the Georg Arnhold Program

Applicants are advised to prepare both short and longer descriptions of their proposed project before starting the online form.

The official application form contains 22 questions and is available through the GEI online application portal.

Candidates who reach the final stage will be asked to submit:

A short curriculum vitae

A list of publications

A detailed project proposal

References

Evidence of impact in peace education

The full proposal must not exceed 25 pages, including references and evidence of impact. Evidence of impact may include highly cited publications, project websites, documented success stories, policy influence, educational implementation, or other verifiable achievements.

Selection Procedure

The selection process consists of several stages.

1. Online application

Applicants submit the initial online form and provide information about their background and proposed project.

2. GEI pre-selection

Academic experts at the GEI will review eligible candidates and suitable projects through a multi-stage internal process. Up to 10 applications may be forwarded to the Academic Advisory Board of the Georg Arnhold Program.

3. Shortlisting by the Academic Advisory Board

The Academic Advisory Board will select the three strongest candidates for the final stage.

4. Submission of full proposals

The three shortlisted candidates will be invited to submit a full application by email. This will include a short CV, publication list, detailed proposal, references, and evidence of impact. The proposal must be no longer than 25 pages.

5. Online interview and final selection

Each shortlisted candidate will participate in an online interview with the Academic Advisory Board. One candidate will ultimately be selected for the 2028 fellowship.

The main selection criteria are:

The candidate’s expertise and experience

Innovation in research or professional practice

The quality of the proposed project

The quality and usefulness of the proposed output

Alignment with the objectives of the Georg Arnhold Program

The candidate’s motivation to benefit specifically from a stay at the GEI

Mandatory AI-Use Disclosure Policy

The GEI requires applicants to disclose any use of artificial-intelligence tools during the research, writing, and application process.

Applicants must be prepared to disclose:

The name of every AI tool used

The tool’s proprietor

The software version

The prompts used

The dates on which the tools were used

Any prompt-engineering tools employed

The purpose and scope of the AI assistance

Use of AI during research design must be documented in the methodology section. AI use for brainstorming, research assistance, translation, text generation, or other purposes must be explained separately in the application.

AI-generated material must not be presented as original research. Applicants are also expected to use AI systems in ways that allow the results to be checked and verified by themselves and by other researchers.

Where an application has joint authors, the authors must clearly explain the scope and type of AI use. Responsibility for the application remains with the applicants.

Applicants should therefore maintain an AI-use record from the beginning of the preparation process. Concealing AI assistance could create a serious compliance problem.

International Scope and Location

The fellowship is intended to address education for sustainable peace in all regions of the world. The call does not identify a specific nationality, citizenship, race, ethnicity, or continent restriction.

The selected Fellow must be able to undertake an in-person research stay at the GEI in Brunswick, Germany. Applicants are responsible for obtaining any required visa and arranging the required insurance.

The earliest possible start date is January 2028. The final fellowship dates and duration will be agreed with the host institution.

Post-Fellowship Network

The official application information states that Fellows receive unlimited membership in the Georg Arnhold Network after completing the fellowship. Alumni may remain connected through program activities and may occasionally be invited to support the wider program, such as through peer review or dissemination of future calls.

This provides an opportunity to continue professional relationships with researchers, educators, policy specialists, and peacebuilding practitioners beyond the formal fellowship period.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should follow these steps:

Review the official fellowship information carefully.

Confirm that their professional or academic background is relevant to peace education.

Develop a focused project connected to education for sustainable peace.

Explain the project’s theoretical and methodological approach.

Show how the project addresses a genuine research or practice gap.

Demonstrate alignment with educational media, curricula, peacebuilding, or related areas.

Prepare short and extended project descriptions.

Review the GEI’s AI-use policy before using the application form.

Prepare evidence of publications, professional achievements, and practical impact.

Submit the online application before 2 November 2026.

Applications should be submitted through the official online application form.

For questions about the application process or project content, applicants may contact:

Katharina Baier

Georg Arnhold Program

Email: arnhold@gei.de

Telephone: +49 (0)531 59099-226

Important Deadline

The deadline to submit an application for the Georg Arnhold Senior Fellowship 2028 is:

2 November 2026

The official page does not state a specific submission time or time zone. Applicants should submit well before the deadline to avoid technical or documentation problems.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Georg Arnhold Senior Fellowship?

It is an advanced opportunity for experienced peace-education scholars and practitioners to complete a research or practice-related project at the Georg Eckert Institute in Germany.

How long is the fellowship?

The normal period is six months. In exceptional cases, a shorter period may be arranged, but the minimum period is three months.

Can practitioners apply without a PhD?

Yes. Practitioner applicants do not have to hold a PhD if they can demonstrate at least five years of advanced professional achievement in peace education or a closely related field.

Is the fellowship fully funded?

The fellowship provides a monthly stipend, return economy airfare, and administrative and publication support. Applicants must arrange their own passport, visa, health insurance, and liability insurance. Other living costs are not separately detailed in the official call.

Is the opportunity open to international applicants?

The call is international in scope and refers to all regions of the world. It does not state a specific nationality or citizenship restriction.

What language is used during the fellowship?

English is the working language of the fellowship and the host institute.

Can applicants use artificial intelligence?

AI use is not prohibited, but it must be fully disclosed. AI-generated content must not be presented as original research.

What happens after the project is completed?

Project outcomes should be published no later than one year after the fellowship ends. Preferred outputs include policy papers, educational materials, research papers, or a larger publication.

Conclusion

The Georg Arnhold Senior Fellowship 2028 offers an important platform for experienced peace-education researchers and practitioners to develop work with international relevance. Its combination of financial support, access to educational-media collections, expert mentoring, research facilities, and global networking makes it particularly suitable for applicants working on curricula, textbooks, digital learning, conflict-sensitive education, reconciliation, or decolonial approaches to peacebuilding.

Strong applicants should present a clearly defined project, demonstrate meaningful academic or professional impact, show practical relevance, and explain why the GEI is the right environment for their work. Those interested in applying should begin preparing their project descriptions and supporting evidence well before the 2 November 2026 deadline.
