TITLE: Community Values

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
This statement of values informs departmental policies and structures and applies to the MIT Physics community, including students, faculty, staff, and all those who choose to affiliate with the MIT Physics Department. The Department commits to ensuring that the entire community understands and strives to uphold the values in this document.

Our Physics Community Values stem from the basic principle that members of our community should treat each other with respect and decency at all times. In turn, we should not alienate, diminish or insult each other, either in word or deed.

Based on this principle, we believe that well-being, respect, inclusion, collaboration and mentorship are moral imperatives that are vital to scientific progress. These ideals are essential for excellence in teaching and research and guide our participation in the MIT Physics community.

Well-being

We support each other at all times and remember that we are not alone.

Mental and physical health are priorities above all else. Proactively addressing wellness is essential to everyone in our community. We look out for others who may be in distress or struggling and offer them compassion and understanding. Just as we treat others well, we must be compassionate with ourselves. Asking for support is brave and admirable no matter the circumstances. We strive to find a healthy balance between our professional and personal lives and proactively seek out any support that we need.

Respect

We value the multitude of ways to be a physicist and the many paths through our field and Department.

We are all respected as physicists, regardless of the problems we choose to study or our current level of mastery. No field of research is inferior; all areas of study are worthy of respect. Much of physics research is interdisciplinary. We value the richness that interdisciplinary research brings and recognize the worth of other research fields.

Our community includes an invaluable team of dedicated administrative and support staff members. We value the diverse strengths and experiences of all staff members and recognize them as an integral part of the Department.

Inclusion

We strive to speak and act in ways that support and include all members of our community.

We are informed and shaped by our identities and experiences. A diversity of identities and experiences is essential to bringing broad perspectives to our Department and academic mission. It is our responsibility to ensure that these diverse voices are included and heard. As individuals and as a community we constantly work to avoid all forms of discrimination, including explicit, implicit and/or unintended bias. We respect and validate other people’s identities and the language they use to describe themselves. Comments made with good intentions can still be hurtful and we strive to be aware of how our comments impact others.

Collaboration

Physics is a social endeavor and we proudly collaborate with others to advance the field.

When we collaborate, we take other people’s ideas seriously and recognize that they might understand concepts and approach problems differently. Exclusion or derision of others based on different points of view is not acceptable. Collaboration requires sharing knowledge and skills, and is based on appropriately acknowledging everyone’s intellectual contributions. Proper acknowledgement is crucial to all activities in the Department.

Mentorship

All physicists are here because of the mentorship we have received and continue to receive, and the mentorship we offer to others.

We all act as both mentors and mentees throughout our careers. Mentor-mentee relationships entail constructive feedback, active listening, responsiveness and a mutual respect and appreciation of each other’s efforts and time. Humiliation and degradation are unacceptable forms of interaction. Mentors should act with compassion, empathy and a strong belief in the potential of their mentees. Mentees should be communicative, ask questions and take initiative.

As members of our community, we uphold the principles of well-being, value, inclusion, collaboration and mentorship. We take an active responsibility in ensuring that everyone feels welcome and respected. We recognize that other people’s life experiences are not our own, but are valid in and of themselves. Given this, we realize that our actions may impact others in unintended ways even as we strive to treat each other with respect. We understand that we will make mistakes. When we do, we will work to correct them and educate ourselves. We take pride in being upstanding members of our community.

Established: Fall 2016
Updated: May 2018

TITLE: With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship 2027: Paid 13-Month Fellowship to Work in the U.S. Congress

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the 2027 With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship Program, a paid professional fellowship that gives experienced professionals an opportunity to work directly in the United States Congress in Washington, D.C.

Organized by the With Honor Institute (WHI), the program is designed for mid-career professionals interested in public service, Congress, national security, and cross-partisan collaboration. Selected fellows receive intensive congressional training before undertaking a full-time, year-long placement in the personal office of a participating member of the U.S. House of Representatives or U.S. Senate.

The fellowship provides participants with direct exposure to the legislative process while allowing them to contribute their existing professional expertise to congressional work. Military experience is welcomed but is not required for the 2027 program.

About the With Honor Institute

The With Honor Institute is a nonpartisan 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Washington, D.C. Its stated mission focuses on addressing political polarization and supporting more effective cross-partisan cooperation. The organization works with veterans and other servant leaders and emphasizes integrity, civility, and courage.

Its activities include public education, research and nonpartisan analysis, convening leaders from different sectors, and placing mid-career professionals in congressional offices through its Congressional Fellowship Program.

About the 2027 With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship

The Congressional Fellowship is a 13-month paid professional development and public-service program.

The fellowship begins with intensive congressional training in Washington, D.C. After completing the training component, fellows move into full-time placements with participating congressional offices for approximately one year.

The program is structured to give experienced professionals substantive exposure to the operations of Congress rather than simply providing an observational experience. Fellows become part of the congressional workplace and gain practical experience with the legislative process while contributing their professional knowledge to the offices where they are placed.

WHI describes the program as a mechanism for strengthening congressional office capacity while promoting cooperation across partisan lines through experienced, values-driven professionals.

What Will Fellows Do?

Selected fellows are placed in the personal offices of participating Members of Congress. The fellowship therefore provides participants with an opportunity to understand congressional operations from inside the legislative branch.

Depending on the office, assignments, professional background and needs of the congressional team, the experience may involve areas associated with legislative and congressional work.

The core value of the fellowship is the opportunity to combine a fellow’s previous professional expertise with practical congressional experience.

For professionals who have spent several years developing expertise outside Congress, the program provides a structured route into public service and legislative work.

Fellowship Duration

The 2027 Congressional Fellowship is described as a 13-month paid fellowship.

The structure consists broadly of two components:

Intensive congressional training in Washington, D.C.

A full-time, year-long placement in a participating U.S. House or Senate office.

This distinguishes the opportunity from shorter internships or academic fellowships. Participants should be prepared to make a substantial professional commitment to the program and to work full-time in Washington, D.C.

Who Is the Fellowship Designed For?

The fellowship primarily targets mid-career professionals.

For the 2027 intake, With Honor states that competitive candidates will generally bring approximately five years of professional experience.

The program is particularly relevant to professionals interested in areas such as:

Congress and the legislative process

Public service

National security

Public policy

Government

Cross-partisan cooperation

Democratic institutions

Leadership and public affairs

The official fellowship page specifically describes the program as being for mid-career professionals interested in Congress and national security.

Military Experience Is Not Required

Although With Honor Institute has a strong organizational focus on veterans and servant leadership, applicants should note an important point about the 2027 fellowship:

Military experience is welcomed, but it is not required.

This means qualified professionals without military backgrounds may also be considered.

The emphasis for the 2027 intake is on finding experienced, values-driven professionals capable of contributing meaningfully to public service and working constructively across political and ideological differences.

Professional Experience

Competitive applicants are expected to have around five years of professional experience.

This requirement reflects the mid-career nature of the program. Unlike many congressional internships intended primarily for university students or recent graduates, this fellowship seeks professionals who can bring established skills, professional judgment and practical experience into a congressional office.

Candidates from different professional sectors may therefore find the fellowship relevant, particularly where their experience can translate effectively into legislative or public-service work.

Skills Sought in Applicants

With Honor indicates that competitive applicants for the 2027 program should demonstrate several important professional attributes, including:

Strong written communication skills

Strong verbal communication skills

Sound professional judgment

Approximately five years of professional experience

Ability to work effectively with people who hold different ideological perspectives

Commitment to public service

Interest in bipartisan or cross-partisan collaboration

The ability to work across differences is particularly important because cross-partisan cooperation is central to the Institute’s stated mission.

Why the Fellowship Is Professionally Significant

Working inside a congressional office can provide participants with practical exposure to how federal policymaking operates.

Rather than studying Congress solely from an academic or external professional perspective, fellows work within congressional offices and encounter the legislative environment directly.

The program can therefore help participants develop deeper knowledge of:

Congressional processes and institutions

Legislative work

Policymaking

Public-service leadership

Congressional office operations

Political and ideological differences within policymaking

Professional communication in a legislative environment

Cross-partisan collaboration

WHI states that fellows gain substantive experience in the legislative process while contributing their existing professional expertise to Congress.

Full-Time Congressional Placement

Following the initial training period, fellows undertake a full-time placement lasting approximately one year.

Placements may be with participating offices in either chamber of Congress:

U.S. House of Representatives

or

U.S. Senate.

The program therefore offers direct institutional exposure to the federal legislative branch.

The exact responsibilities of an individual fellow can depend on the congressional office and its needs.

Training Component

Before entering their congressional placements, selected participants undertake intensive training in Washington, D.C.

This component is particularly valuable for professionals who possess significant expertise in another field but have not previously worked on Capitol Hill.

Training helps participants transition from their existing professional environment into the highly specialized working environment of Congress.

A Program for Experienced Professionals

One of the most distinctive characteristics of the With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship is its focus on people who already possess substantial professional experience.

Many public-service programs target students or individuals at the beginning of their careers. By contrast, WHI seeks mid-career candidates capable of transferring established expertise into congressional service.

This creates an opportunity for professionals considering a transition toward government, legislative affairs, national security, public policy or broader public service.

TITLE: Donor Profile: Riccardo Di Capua

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Why Riccardo ’72 ML and Raquel Di Capua support physics fellowships.

by Erin McGrath // MIT Physics Annual 2012

Riccardo had come to MIT some five years ago with a unique idea in mind. He wanted to sponsor half a dozen recent graduates for one year while they figured out the next step in their lives. The only conditions would be that candidates had graduated that year and would submit mid-term and year-end reports of what had been learned. There would be no other expectations. Initially, the idea did not resonate anywhere at MIT.

Riccardo and Raquel Di Capua
One day Dean of Science Marc Kastner, at the time Head of the Physics Department, got wind of what was going on and asked Riccardo if they could meet in the Lobby of Building 7. Walking briskly together through campus toward the Stata Center, Marc listened carefully to Riccardo and then made a suggestion. Instead of sponsoring half a dozen, nomadic recent graduates, going off to who knows where in the world and doing who knows what, the good intention could be put to a much better and more focused use. Marc pointed out that there are some graduate students who arrive at MIT to pursue a PhD in physics, but are still unsure which of the four physics subfields interested them most. Perhaps, funding this handful of students during their first year in graduate school in Course VIII would allow them the freedom to explore the department without the financial pressure to commit prematurely?

Why Course VIII? Because math and physics triggered my applying to MIT. Supporting fellowships in the Physics Department has been rewarding both intellectually and personally, and has led to active involvement in other areas at MIT.
Riccardo Di Capua ’72 ML

The idea would give immense flexibility to the undecided, while at the same time offering a measure of reassurance in that the recipients had already completed an undergraduate degree and been accepted to graduate school at MIT. Each year since that initial discussion and walk across campus with Marc, Riccardo and his wife Raquel have supported the physics graduate fellowship program.

The rewards have been intellectual as well as personal for Riccardo, and have led to active involvement in other areas at MIT. Most undergraduates come to MIT because they excelled at math and were fascinated by physics in school; it’s the math/ physics combination that triggers the application process for most. Riccardo was no exception, arriving from Colombia with all good intentions of majoring in Course VIII. Two hours in 8.01 showed a woeful lack of high school preparation, calling for a shift into the lower gears of 8.011 and 8.021, and, finally, stunting his physics career ambitions after 8.03. Course III became Riccardo’s new major.

Riccardo’s reconnection with Course VIII in later life rekindled a love for physics without the accompanying classroom stress. To this day, he maintains an active fascination with physics, reading avidly, and more recently downloading Course VIII OpenCourseWare onto his tablet computer to watch and learn while running on the treadmill. “How nerdy of me!”

On the personal side, Riccardo credits Marc with having opened doors to meeting countless graduate students, administrators, and faculty in the Department, including Professors Sara Seager and Eddie Farhi, and Department Head Edmund Bertschinger. Over the years, Riccardo and Raquel have hosted numerous MIT receptions in their home, with guests including alumni as well as MIT applicants. One memorable event featured Ed Bertschinger speaking on “Planets, Black Holes, and the Accelerating Universe.” It was a great opportunity for high school students in particular to be exposed to some of the fascinating scientific work being done at MIT.

This initial involvement with the Physics Department led Riccardo to a wider range of activities at MIT, including appointments as regional chair of the MIT Corporation Development Committee and Chair of the Annual Fund. Along the way, other strong friendships were formed throughout the Institute, building upon the close personal friendship forged earlier with Marc Kastner. Riccardo has enjoyed his relationship with his Di Capua Fellows, often meeting with them informally during campus visits and speaking with them at the annual Patrons of Physics Fellows Society Dinner. Riccardo has also become close with the development staff in the Physics Department and School of Science and has worked with Elizabeth Chadis and Erin McGrath for many years.

When asked, “Why Course VIII?” Riccardo replies, “Because math and physics triggered my applying to MIT. I think Dean Marc Kastner encapsulates the theme of the School of Science with the title of his popular lecture, “Amazing People Doing Amazing Things.” And nowhere is the title more vibrant, more exciting, and more magical than in the Physics Department!”

Towards The Next Generation of European Transnational Access

ACCESS2ACCESS will design a simpler, fairer, and more sustainable system for researchers to access scientific facilities across Europe. By bringing together 17 leading research organisations, the project addresses a concrete problem faced daily by researchers and facility managers: fragmented, opaque, and unequal access to Europe’s research infrastructures (Ris). A central element of the project is the development of an AI-assisted discovery tool, or “one-stop-shop”, that would allow any researcher to describe their scientific problem in plain language and be guided to the most relevant facilities and services across Europe.

The project is designed to be inclusive by default, ensuring that researchers from all scientific disciplines, career stages, and European countries, including Widening Countries will have the chance to shape the future of access to European RIs.

a comprehensive map of existing research infrastructure access schemes across Europe

an extensive analysis of stakeholder expectations from the new access scheme

a set of policy options for a future EU-wide access programme, including governance and funding models

an AI-assisted “one-stop-shop” discovery tool for research facility access

TITLE: How do manatees stay hydrated?

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
(Photo courtesy of The Ocean Agency)
For the manatee, hydration is life. But drinking underwater is not always an easy feat. In fact, for West Indian (Trichechus manatus) and African (Trichechus senegalensis) manatees, it’s often a test of creativity.

These two species, unlike their Amazonian relatives, migrate between warm freshwater and tepid saltwater. They move according to the seasons, avoiding low temperatures that may kill them. So, clever hydration strategies in any environment are a must-no matter how peculiar some appear.

Generally, manatees take advantage of every freshwater source. River mouths, which stream drinkable water into marine and estuarine environments, are important underwater oases for these gentle giants. Rainwater is another source of hydration. Thanks to the buoyancy of saltwater, fresh rain collects on the surface. Manatees then swoop up and vacuum it in. Sometimes they don’t wait for the rain to end. Instead, they float belly-up and open wide.

These freshwater pockets support manatees by allowing them to remain in marine and estuarine environments without having to spend time and energy migrating back to fresh water.

But neither river mouths nor wet seasons are fully reliable sources of hydration. So, they graze aquatic plants, some of which are highly concentrated with water or salt. And manatees are intuitive about what they consume. Studies have shown they actually avoid salty greens when already dehydrated-similar to how thirsty humans may go for fruit over chips. They instead snack on water-concentrated vegetation, also hydrating through it.

A West Indian manatee grazes on seagrass, an important source of freshwater. (Video courtesy of The Ocean Agency)

Physiology also plays a role. Like many other organisms, manatees can produce water through the metabolic breakdown of food. In other words, their bodies’ chemical reactions during digestion release H2O as a byproduct. This is the well-oiled machine of an age-old animal’s body-they can hydrate without even drinking.

And if a manatee is down on its luck, with no freshwater sources or water-concentrated foods, its unique physiology can keep it going a while longer. Though not routine, manatees’ kidneys can concentrate salt to the extent that their urine is saltier than the water around them. This is helpful when a manatee accidentally ingests saltwater, or when osmosis causes salt to seep into their skin. To exist in saline waters is to become saline oneself. That’s why the ability to minimize blood salt levels is an essential backup plan: it maintains homeostasis as well as possible, even when no freshwater is available.

If manatees strive for anything in life, it’s balance. While these “sea cows” are crafty in finding water, they must do so in moderation. Because sodium and chloride, though unhealthy in high concentrations, are still vital electrolytes for numerous bodily functions.

TITLE: PhD in Physics, Statistics, and Data Science

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Many PhD students in the MIT Physics Department incorporate probability, statistics, computation, and data analysis into their research. These techniques are becoming increasingly important for both experimental and theoretical Physics research, with ever-growing datasets, more sophisticated physics simulations, and the development of cutting-edge machine learning tools. The Interdisciplinary Doctoral Program in Statistics (IDPS) is designed to provide students with the highest level of competency in 21st century statistics, enabling doctoral students across MIT to better integrate computation and data analysis into their PhD thesis research.

Admission to this program is restricted to students currently enrolled in the Physics doctoral program or another participating MIT doctoral program. In addition to satisfying all of the requirements of the Physics PhD, students take one subject each in probability, statistics, computation and statistics, and data analysis, as well as the Doctoral Seminar in Statistics, and they write a dissertation in Physics utilizing statistical methods. Graduates of the program will receive their doctoral degree in the field of “Physics, Statistics, and Data Science.”

Selection

Doctoral students in Physics may submit an Interdisciplinary PhD in Statistics Form between the end of their second semester and penultimate semester in their Physics program. The application must include an endorsement from the student’s advisor, an up-to-date CV, current transcript, and a 1-2 page statement of interest in Statistics and Data Science.

The statement of interest can be based on the student’s thesis proposal for the Physics Department, but it must demonstrate that statistical methods will be used in a substantial way in the proposed research. In their statement, applicants are encouraged to explain how specific statistical techniques would be applied in their research. Applicants should further highlight ways that their proposed research might advance the use of statistics and data science, both in their physics subfield and potentially in other disciplines. If the work is part of a larger collaborative effort, the applicant should focus on their personal contributions.

For access to the selection form or for further information, please contact the IDSS Academic Office at idss_academic_office@mit.edu.

Required Courses

Courses in this list that satisfy the Physics PhD degree requirements can count for both programs. Other similar or more advanced courses can count towards the “Computation & Statistics” and “Data Analysis” requirements, with permission from the program co-chairs. The IDS.190 requirement may be satisfied instead by IDS.957 – Practical Experience in Data Analysis, if that experience exposes the student to a diverse set of topics in statistics and data science. Making this substitution requires permission from the program co-chairs prior to doing the practical experience.

Grade Policy

C, D, F, and O grades are unacceptable. Students should not earn more B grades than A grades, reflected by a PhysSDS GPA of ≥ 4.5. Students may be required to retake subjects graded B or lower, although generally one B grade will be tolerated.

Unless approved by the PhysSDS co-chairs, a minimum grade of B+ is required in all 12 unit courses, except IDS.190 (3 units) which requires a P grade.

Advising

Though not required, it is strongly encouraged for a member of the MIT Statistics and Data Science Center (SDSC) to serve on a student’s doctoral committee. This could be an SDSC member from the Physics department or from another field relevant to the proposed thesis research.

Thesis Proposal

All students must submit a thesis proposal using the standard Physics format. Dissertation research must involve the utilization of statistical methods in a substantial way.

FAQs

Can I satisfy the requirements with courses taken at Harvard?

Harvard CompSci 181 will count as the equivalent of MIT’s 6.867. For the status of other courses, please contact the program co-chairs.

Can a course count both for the Physics degree requirements and the PhysSDS requirements?

Yes, this is possible, as long as the courses are already on the approved list of requirements. E.g. 8.592 can count as a breadth requirement for a NUPAX student as well as a Data Analysis requirement for the PhysSDS degree.

If I have previous experience in Probability and/or Statistics, can I test out of these requirements?

These courses are required by all of the IDPS degrees. They are meant to ensure that all students obtaining an IDPS degree share the same solid grounding in these fundamentals, and to help build a community of IDPS students across the various disciplines. Only in exceptional cases might it be possible to substitute more advanced courses in these areas.

Can I substitute a similar or more advanced course for the PhysSDS requirements?

Yes, this is possible for the “computation and statistics” and “data analysis” requirements, with permission of program co-chairs. Substitutions for the “probability” and “statistics” requirements will only be granted in exceptional cases.

For Spring 2021, the following course has been approved as a substitution for the “computation and statistics” requirement: 18.408 (Theoretical Foundations for Deep Learning).

The following course has been approved as a substitution for the “data analysis” requirement: 6.481 (Introduction to Statistical Data Analysis).

Can I apply for the PhysSDS degree in my last semester at MIT?

No, you must apply no later than your penultimate semester.

What does it mean to use statistical methods in a “substantial way” in one’s thesis?

The ideal case is that one’s thesis advances statistics research independent of the Physics applications. Advancing the use of statistical methods in one’s subfield of Physics would also qualify. Applying well-established statistical methods in one’s thesis could qualify, if the application is central to the Physics result. In all cases, we expect the student to demonstrate mastery of statistics and data science.

TITLE: CEA-SAMEF gives back to society through health screening

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The African Center of Excellence in Maternal and Infant Health (CEA-SAMEF), hosted by the University of Cheikh Anta Diop, Senegal organized a health screening and awareness campaign for over 500 residents of Dakar. The event was organized in collaboration with the Institute of Social Pediatrics (IPS) Guédiawaye, Senegal on Saturday, September 1 2018. These residents were screened for various diseases and infections including; urinary tract infections in children, anemia in adolescents and children, breast and cervical cancer in women, among others. Coupled with the screening was a training session for health workers in preventive techniques and first aid care.

Again, on Monday, September 03, 2018, CEA-SAMEF launched another joint medical campaign in partnership with the Association of Student Surgeons and Dentists of Senegal (AECDS) in the Commune of Mboro. The campaign which provided free health screening for about five hundred (500) people including women and children was held at the Darou Khoudoss ICS health post in Dakar, Senegal. More than 35 doctors from all disciplines including dentists and pharmacist participated in this well meaning contribution to quality healthcare delivery.

The health screening also created awareness on the role of CEA-SAMEF in improving child and maternal health in Senegal. It also strengthened the partnership between the Center, the Institute of Social Paediatrics (IPS) and Association of Student Surgeons and Dentists of Senegal (AECDS). Moreover, participants were sensitized on adolescent health, nutritional status of women and children among other health related issues.

Based on the enormous impact of the health screening, efforts are being made to perpetuate the event and make it a statutory one for CEA-SAMEF.

The Africa Centre of Excellence in Maternal and Child Health (CEA_SAMEF) is one of the six Centres under the Africa Centre of Excellence(ACE) project funded by the World Bank. The Centre since its inception has awarded more than 10 PhD scholarships to deserving students and introduced 13 short courses to train health staff.

TITLE: Aspen Policy Academy AI Civic Action Accelerator 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 1, 2026

Applications are open for the Aspen Policy Academy AI Civic Action Accelerator 2026. The AI Civic Action Accelerator is a free, 6-session, part-time program that helps individuals and teams refine and advance promising policy solutions to civic artificial intelligence (AI) challenges. The accelerator will support early-stage projects that aim to strengthen the relationship between government, communities, and AI.

They are seeking practical, community-driven ideas that help governments tackle AI issues in society or use AI more effectively. For instance, projects may seek to improve public participation and civic engagement through AI; improve youth online safety; enable governments and AI to work together in more transparent, equitable, and effective ways; or propose new ways to handle AI automating jobs for certain sectors of the workforce.

Curriculum

During the AI Civic Action Accelerator, participants will learn the Policy Academy’s proven framework for achieving policy impact, workshop their own ideas with peers and expert Aspen Policy Academy instructors to refine them using this framework, and pitch a polished solution directly to a decisionmaker. Each 2-hour session will be split between instruction and hands-on workshopping. The instructional portion will cover the Academy’s policy impact framework, including lessons on scoping problems, identifying stakeholders, defining alternative solutions, developing relevant outputs, and creating an advocacy plan. The workshopping portion will focus on applying these lessons: Participants will complete assignments to advance their civic AI policy ideas and present them at each session for feedback from peers and Aspen Policy Academy instructors. By the end of the program, participants will have a concrete civic AI policy solution and deliverables, and will have pitched their solution to a real decisionmaker.

Benefits

This program offers you and your team free coaching from policy experts at the Aspen Institute to advance a policy idea, while learning and applying our framework for policy impact. By the end of the program, participants will have a concrete solution and a set of deliverables to pitch to a stakeholder. You’ll also gain insights from other cohort members and have ongoing access to opportunities and resources offered to Academy alumni.

TITLE: Global Fund Business & Consultancy Opportunities 2026: Apply for International Tenders, Consulting Contracts and Global Health Procurement Opportunities

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
About the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria

The Global Fund is an international financing partnership dedicated to accelerating progress against HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria while supporting stronger and more resilient health systems.

Rather than directly implementing most country programs itself, the Global Fund finances programs that are implemented through its partners and Principal Recipients. This distinction is important when reviewing its business opportunities.

The organization’s Business & Consultancy Opportunities page primarily covers procurement undertaken by the Global Fund itself, particularly requirements of its Secretariat. Principal Recipients administering Global Fund grants may conduct their own procurement processes separately in accordance with applicable grant requirements.

The Global Fund’s procurement activities are intended to support its organizational operations while helping ensure that resources ultimately contribute to effective global health interventions.

What Are Global Fund Business and Consultancy Opportunities?

The opportunities published through the platform are essentially competitive procurement exercises.

Depending on the requirement, the Global Fund may seek proposals from:

Individual consultants

Consultancy firms

Professional service providers

Companies

Contractors

Suppliers

Manufacturers

Technical organizations

Research organizations

Specialist agencies

Procurement service providers

Other qualified entities

The Global Fund’s Procurement Policy defines a supplier broadly as an external entity that may include an organization, individual contractor or service provider supplying goods, services or other support.

Consequently, applicants should not assume that every opportunity is intended for an individual consultant. Some tenders may require established companies or organizations capable of delivering substantial contracts.

What Types of Opportunities May Be Available?

The exact opportunities change throughout the year.

Potential procurement areas can include professional and technical services associated with the Global Fund’s operations and mission.

Depending on organizational requirements, opportunities may potentially cover areas such as:

Global health consulting

HIV-related technical services

Tuberculosis programs and expertise

Malaria-related technical services

Health-system strengthening

Procurement and supply-chain services

Public-health analysis

Data and analytics

Monitoring and evaluation

Independent evaluation

Research

Strategy development

Organizational consulting

Finance and accounting services

Audit and assurance

Risk management

Information technology

Digital systems

Communications

Knowledge management

Human resources consulting

Legal or regulatory support

Program management

Project management

Logistics

Procurement of goods

Health-product procurement

Pharmaceutical products

Diagnostic products

Other specialized technical or operational services

Actual eligibility and technical requirements are determined separately for each solicitation.

Global Fund Consulting Opportunities

Consultancy assignments represent an important component of the Global Fund’s external contracting activities.

The Global Fund’s careers information confirms that it engages both individual consultants and consultancy firms, with relevant opportunities published through the Business & Consultancy Opportunities section.

These assignments should not be confused with permanent employment vacancies.

Permanent and fixed-term staff vacancies generally appear through the Global Fund’s separate careers system, while consulting and supplier procurements are normally handled as contracting opportunities.

Consultants may therefore be engaged to deliver specific outputs, technical expertise, analysis, assessments, evaluations or other professional services under contractual terms defined in the relevant solicitation.

Global Fund Procurement Opportunities for Suppliers

Companies interested in doing business with the Global Fund should understand that procurement is governed by formal institutional rules.

The Global Fund states that it seeks value for money in the procurement of goods and services and publishes tenders as part of a transparent procurement process.

Its Procurement Policy applies to several areas, including:

Procurement of health products and related services through the Pooled Procurement Mechanism.

Procurement of goods and services financed through Global Fund operating expenses.

Certain other procurements financed through approved investments or funds.

Procurement of Local Fund Agent services.

This means the procurement framework covers both operational requirements and major elements of the organization’s health-product supply system.

Open Competition Is the Standard Procurement Approach

One of the most important aspects for prospective bidders is the Global Fund’s emphasis on competitive procurement.

Its Procurement Policy states that procurement should generally be based on effective competition and identifies open competition as the organization’s standard procurement method.

Effective competition may involve:

Publicly advertising procurement opportunities;

Inviting a sufficient number of prospective suppliers;

Ensuring bidders compete under equivalent conditions;

Receiving sufficient independent offers; and

Evaluating proposals against established requirements.

This approach is intended to provide a transparent and competitive environment for qualified suppliers.

Core Global Fund Procurement Principles

Prospective applicants should understand the principles against which Global Fund procurement is managed.

1. Value for Money

Procurement decisions are not necessarily based solely on selecting the lowest-priced offer.

The Global Fund defines value for money by considering the relationship among:

Price

Quality

Performance

Total cost of ownership

Technical suitability

Delivery requirements

Organizational capability

Environmental, social, sustainability and risk considerations may also be incorporated where relevant.

A bidder should therefore ensure that its proposal demonstrates overall value rather than simply offering a low financial price.

2. Effective Competition

Competitive procurement is intended to ensure multiple qualified suppliers have a fair opportunity to participate.

The organization seeks an adequate competitive environment and normally uses open competition as its standard approach.

3. Fairness, Impartiality and Integrity

The Global Fund requires bidders to be treated equally and proposals to be evaluated objectively against predetermined criteria.

Its Procurement Policy specifically emphasizes avoiding actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest.

4. Client-Centered Procurement

Procurement is also expected to meet the requirements of the internal Global Fund unit requesting the goods or services.

This means suppliers must closely understand the technical specifications and intended outcomes of each tender.

5. Sustainable Procurement

The Global Fund explicitly incorporates sustainability into its procurement framework.

Its policy states that sustainable procurement seeks to:

Reduce environmental impacts across supply chains;

Support fair and humane working conditions;

Promote social progress;

Support economic development; and

Contribute to the long-term well-being of communities.

6. Best Interests of the Global Fund

Procurement must ultimately support the organization’s mission, protect its assets and ensure responsible stewardship of its resources.

Ethical Requirements for Global Fund Suppliers

Ethical compliance is a major requirement for companies and consultants seeking contracts with the organization.

The Global Fund’s Code of Conduct for Suppliers applies broadly to bidders, suppliers, agents, intermediaries, consultants and contractors, as well as relevant representatives, employees, subcontractors and affiliates.

Suppliers are expected to participate in procurement processes honestly, fairly, transparently and accountably.

The organization prohibits practices including:

Corruption

Fraud

Collusion

Anti-competitive practices

Coercion

Misrepresentation

Improper payments

Undisclosed commissions

Other unethical procurement practices

Applicants should therefore ensure that every statement, qualification, reference, financial proposal and declaration contained in their bid is accurate.

Compliance With Laws

Suppliers and their representatives are required to comply with applicable laws and regulations in the countries where they conduct business, as well as relevant Global Fund rules and policies.

The Code of Conduct also includes provisions concerning matters such as:

Anti-corruption

Anti-money laundering

Fair competition

Responsible use of Global Fund resources

Disclosure of conflicts

Human rights

Labor standards

Environmental responsibilities

Child protection

Protection from sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassment

These requirements should be treated as substantive contractual obligations rather than formalities.

Record-Keeping and Audit Requirements

Companies that obtain Global Fund-financed contracts should also be prepared for accountability and audit requirements.

The Supplier Code of Conduct requires suppliers to maintain appropriate and complete financial and business records associated with Global Fund-financed contracts for at least five years after the final payment under the contract.

Suppliers are also expected to cooperate with the Global Fund, including its Office of the Inspector General, where access to relevant records, documents or personnel is reasonably requested.

This requirement is particularly relevant to larger consulting firms, contractors and suppliers managing financially significant contracts.

Conflicts of Interest

Potential suppliers must pay close attention to conflict-of-interest requirements.

The procurement framework seeks to ensure objective evaluation and prevent circumstances where a bidder could obtain an improper competitive advantage.

Suppliers should disclose relevant relationships or situations where required and carefully review the specific tender documentation before submitting their proposal.

Failure to properly address conflicts may jeopardize a bid or contract.

Can Suppliers Use the Global Fund Name or Logo?

Winning a Global Fund contract does not automatically authorize a supplier to use the organization’s name or logo for advertising.

The Supplier Code states that suppliers may not, without prior written consent, use the Global Fund’s name or logo in publicity or advertising, represent a business relationship as an endorsement of their products or services, or make statements on behalf of the Global Fund.

Companies should therefore obtain appropriate authorization before publicly promoting a contractual relationship.

Health Product Procurement Opportunities

The Global Fund is also a major procurer of medicines and health products.

Its Pooled Procurement Mechanism (PPM) aggregates orders from participating grant implementers to obtain competitive prices and delivery conditions from manufacturers and suppliers.

In 2025, the mechanism handled approximately US$1.02 billion in orders for implementing partners in 81 countries.

Products available through the mechanism include categories such as:

Antiretroviral medicines

Antimalarial medicines

Other essential medicines

Insecticide-treated mosquito nets

Viral load tests

Rapid diagnostic tests

Regular tenders for medicines and diagnostic products may also appear through the Business & Consultancy Opportunities section.

Important Information for Health Product Suppliers

Companies interested specifically in supplying medicines or health products should not rely exclusively on the general tender page.

The Global Fund advises potential health-product suppliers to:

Review its Procurement Policy.

Understand quality-assurance requirements applicable to their products.

Review relevant procurement and purchasing information.

Understand the Pooled Procurement Mechanism and wambo.org.

Review the Code of Conduct for Suppliers.

Review applicable procurement regulations.

The organization does not maintain a general list of automatically preselected suppliers for implementing partners.

Manufacturers must therefore satisfy the particular regulatory, quality and procurement conditions applicable to their products.

What Documents Should Applicants Read Before Applying?

The Global Fund explicitly advises prospective bidders to review key procurement documentation before submitting a proposal.

Important documents include:

Procurement Policy

Code of Conduct for Suppliers

Terms and Conditions for the Purchase of Goods and Services

Privacy Statement for the Global Fund Procurement Process

Travel Guidelines for Contractors

Applicants should not treat these documents as optional background reading.

They can establish important conditions relating to:

Ethical conduct

Contract administration

Financial arrangements

Confidentiality

Travel

Compliance

Reporting

Supplier obligations

Legal liability

Tender-specific conditions may supplement these general rules.

How to Apply for Global Fund Business and Consultancy Opportunities

The application procedure is not identical for every procurement.

The official Business & Consultancy Opportunities page directs applicants to the Global Fund’s Open Tenders platform.

Each individual solicitation contains its own:

Tender description

Terms of reference or specifications

Eligibility requirements

Required qualifications

Submission procedure

Technical documentation

Financial requirements

Deadline

Contact or clarification procedure

Applicants should therefore first identify a tender that matches their qualifications and carefully review the complete tender package before preparing a proposal.

View Global Fund Business & Consultancy Opportunities

Preparing a Competitive Proposal

Although tender requirements vary, applicants should generally prepare to demonstrate why they are technically and commercially capable of delivering the requested work.

A strong proposal may need to address areas such as:

Understanding of the Assignment

Demonstrate a clear understanding of:

The Global Fund’s requirements

Expected outputs

Relevant technical issues

Contract objectives

Deliverables

Technical Approach

Where required, explain:

Proposed methodology

Implementation approach

Work plan

Quality-assurance arrangements

Risk management

Project governance

Reporting arrangements

Relevant Experience

Applicants may need to demonstrate previous experience delivering similar assignments.

Evidence could include:

Comparable contracts

Client references

Case studies

Project summaries

Past performance

Demonstrated international experience

Personnel

Consultancy tenders may require CVs of proposed experts.

Applicants should ensure that each proposed team member clearly satisfies any mandatory:

Education requirements

Professional qualifications

Years of experience

Technical competencies

Language requirements

Financial Proposal

Price should be realistic and consistent with the technical methodology.

Because Global Fund procurement evaluates overall value for money rather than price alone, applicants should avoid compromising technical quality merely to submit the lowest possible price.

Evaluation of Proposals

The exact scoring methodology will be provided in the individual tender documentation.

However, the Global Fund’s overarching Procurement Policy permits consideration of:

Technical factors

Commercial factors

Organizational factors

Pricing

Environmental factors

Social considerations

Sustainability

Risk

Appropriate due diligence

Applicants should therefore respond directly to every evaluation criterion instead of submitting a generic corporate proposal.

Tender Review and Contract Award

The Global Fund’s procurement framework includes controls before contracts are awarded.

Its Procurement Policy states that procurement contracts are subject to a mandatory review process prior to award to confirm compliance with applicable policies and procurement rules. No award may be made before that review is completed.

This reflects the organization’s emphasis on transparency, accountability and procurement integrity.

Are These Opportunities Based in Geneva?

Many opportunities published through this particular portal primarily involve supplying goods or services to the Global Fund Secretariat in Geneva, Switzerland.

However, this does not necessarily mean every consultant must permanently reside in Switzerland.

Assignment location, travel requirements, remote-working arrangements and geographical eligibility can differ substantially from one tender to another.

Applicants should therefore consult the individual Terms of Reference rather than assuming an opportunity is either remote or Geneva-based.

Can International Applicants Apply?

The Global Fund Business & Consultancy Opportunities page does not establish one universal nationality restriction covering all tenders.

It states that open tenders are available for prospective suppliers to review and consider. The Supplier Code also covers a broad range of bidders, suppliers, consultants, contractors, organizations and representatives.

However, international eligibility must be determined tender by tender.

A specific procurement may impose requirements relating to:

Country registration

Geographic presence

Local expertise

Language

Tax registration

Professional licensing

Experience in certain regions

Ability to travel

Manufacturer authorization

Product regulatory approval

Applicants should therefore never interpret the general procurement page as guaranteeing eligibility for every nationality in every procurement.

Are There Opportunities for Applicants From Africa, Asia, Europe and Other Regions?

Potentially, yes, depending on the specific tender.

The Global Fund operates globally, and its procurement ecosystem includes international companies, consultants, manufacturers and service providers. But there is no blanket statement on the Business & Consultancy Opportunities page saying every tender is universally open to every country.

Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, Latin America, the Caribbean, the Middle East and Oceania should check the nationality, registration and location provisions of each individual procurement notice.

Application Deadline

There is no single overall deadline for Global Fund Business & Consultancy Opportunities.

This is an ongoing procurement portal.

Each open tender has its own closing date and submission time, which are stated within the individual solicitation documentation. The official page specifically directs applicants to the individual tender for submission instructions and contact information.

Applicants should therefore:

Open the current tender list.

Identify the relevant opportunity.

Check its exact closing date.

Note the applicable time zone.

Submit the complete proposal before the stated deadline.

Late submissions may not be accepted under tender-specific rules.

Important Difference Between Global Fund Tenders and Global Fund Jobs

Applicants should understand that this procurement portal is not the Global Fund’s ordinary employment vacancies page.

The organization maintains a separate recruitment system for staff vacancies. Its careers page specifically explains that consulting opportunities for consultants and consultancy firms are listed under Business & Consultancy Opportunities.

Therefore:

Permanent or temporary employment: Check Global Fund Careers.

Consultancy contracts, supplier opportunities and tenders: Check Business & Consultancy Opportunities.

This distinction is particularly important for applicants preparing CVs or proposals.

Why Consider Global Fund Business Opportunities?

Working with the Global Fund can provide experienced consultants and organizations with an opportunity to contribute specialized expertise to one of the world’s major global health financing institutions.

Potential benefits include:

Participation in international health initiatives

Exposure to complex global programs

Opportunities to work with international stakeholders

Experience with major institutional procurement systems

Potential long-term professional relationships

Opportunities for specialist consulting firms

Participation in health-product and supply-chain initiatives

Work contributing indirectly to the fight against HIV, tuberculosis and malaria

However, applicants should approach these opportunities as formal competitive procurements rather than guaranteed contracts.

Tips for Prospective Applicants

Before submitting a Global Fund tender, applicants should:

Read the complete Terms of Reference or technical specifications.

Confirm that all mandatory eligibility criteria can be satisfied.

Read the Procurement Policy.

Review the Supplier Code of Conduct.

Examine the applicable Terms and Conditions.

Prepare a proposal specifically tailored to the tender.

Demonstrate relevant experience with evidence.

Provide qualified personnel where required.

Address every evaluation criterion.

Ensure pricing is complete and commercially realistic.

Disclose potential conflicts where required.

Avoid unsupported claims about organizational capacity.

Confirm the deadline and applicable time zone.

Submit through the method specified in the tender.

Retain copies of all documents submitted.

Important Warning for Applicants

Applicants should use only official Global Fund procurement channels and verify all tender information against the official website.

A legitimate procurement process should include formal documentation defining the required goods or services, submission requirements and applicable conditions.

Prospective bidders should also remember that winning a Global Fund contract does not provide unrestricted permission to use the organization’s name or logo for advertising purposes.

Conclusion

The Global Fund Business & Consultancy Opportunities platform provides an important route for qualified consultants, businesses, manufacturers, contractors and professional service providers seeking to work with an internationally recognized global health financing organization.

Unlike a conventional job board, the platform operates as an ongoing competitive procurement system, with individual tenders covering different goods, consulting assignments and specialized services.

The Global Fund emphasizes transparency, effective competition, integrity, sustainability and value for money throughout its procurement activities. Applicants should therefore expect rigorous technical, ethical and contractual standards.

There is no universal application deadline. Each opportunity has its own closing date, technical requirements, financial requirements and submission procedure.

Prospective suppliers and consultants should regularly review the official portal, identify opportunities aligned with their expertise, carefully study all tender documentation and prepare compliant, evidence-based proposals.

Accra, Ghana, 16th June 2021 – Under the patronage of His Excellency, Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of the Republic of Ghana, the Association of African Universities (AAU), will be holding its 15th General Conference on July 5-8, 2021, virtually. | Download French Version HERE

The AAU, Africa’s apex continental Higher Education body with a membership of over 400 higher education institutions, convenes its General Conference – an assembly of representatives of all member institutions and key higher education stakeholders including policy makers, academics, researchers, development partner representatives and others, once every four years.

The 2021 General Conference, with the theme: “The Future of African Higher Education” will, among other things, provide an opportunity for African academics to share scientific and research information on the theme, as well as provide a platform for sharing best practices with policy makers, and strengthen networking among African higher education institutions.

The Conference also features statutory sessions which are specific to the Association, such as electing a new Governing Board from among the Vice Chancellors, Presidents and Rectors of the member universities; Assessing the activities implemented by the AAU in the past four years against the background of its Work Programme and Strategic Plan approved at the previous Conference and; Approving the plan of activities and budget estimates for the following four-year period.

The 15th General Conference coincides with the 21st Conference of Rectors, Vice Chancellors and Presidents of African Universities (COREVIP), which is also hosted by the AAU. The two events are jointly being held under the main theme with the following six (6) Sub-themes :

Sub-Theme 1: The Future of African Higher Education Post-COVID-19 ; Sub-Theme 2: Contributions of African Higher Education Institutions to Addressing the Challenges linked to the COVID-19 pandemic ; Sub-Theme 3: Contributions of African Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) in Achieving the Sustainable Development Goals; Sub-Theme 4: Funding of African Higher Education Institutions in the face of unpredictable Economy ; Sub-Theme 5: Mainstreaming e-learning and the digital divide and Sub-Theme 6: Contributions of the Diaspora to African Higher Education.

“Africa’s ongoing transformation, founded on strong economic growth, political will and favorable demographics, is ushering a new higher education landscape on the continent as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. The current environment beckons the higher education community to position itself as a beacon to accelerate this transformation from promise to reality and the 15th General Conference is a key step in this direction that will ultimately foster development of a cohesive and vibrant African higher education community as a driver of Africa’s development agenda”, said Prof. Ehile, Secretary General, AAU.

Being one of the biggest gatherings of Higher Education stakeholders on the continent, the AAU is encouraging all stakeholders both on the continent and beyond, including Africans in the Diaspora, to actively get involved by registering via the event registration link – https://tinyurl.com/AAUGC2021 . Participation in this conference is free of charge.

About the Association of African Universities

The Association of African Universities is an international non-profit, non-governmental organization created by African Universities to promote cooperation among them on the one hand, and between them and the international academic community on the other. Created in 1967, the AAU is the voice of higher education in Africa. AAU aims to improve the quality of African higher education, and to strengthen its contribution to Africa’s development by supporting the core functions of higher education institutions and facilitating critical reflection and consensus building on issues affecting higher education. Mission

The European Astrobiology Institute (EAI) is a consortium of European research and higher education institutions and organisations as well as other stakeholders aiming to carry out research, training, outreach and dissemination activities in astrobiology in a comprehensive and coordinated manner and thereby securing a leading role for the European Research Area in the field. The EAI is an Expert Board hosted and administered by the European Science Foundation.

As such, the EAI aims to:

Perform ground-breaking research on key scientific questions in astrobiology (which will be periodically reviewed) requiring a cooperative interdisciplinary approach

Disseminate high-quality results of such research efforts effectively across the scientific community

Provide interdisciplinary training for students and early career scientists in astrobiology

Engage in education in the field of astrobiology on all levels

Liaise with industry to foster collaborations on technological developments that are relevant to astrobiology research and beneficial to Europe as a whole

Coordinate the outreach activities of European astrobiologists to the general public, industry and all other relevant stakeholders

Act as an advisory body and provide high-quality expertise to European research organisations and decision makers on all aspects of astrobiology at the European level

Ensure the necessary financial means to carry out these activities through a coordinated approach to European funding agencies including Horizon programmes

TITLE: Obituary Kofi Annan 1938 – 2018

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
AAU MOURNS KOFI ANNAN

The Secretary General of the Association of African Universities (AAU) on behalf of the Governing Board and African Universities, expresses our profound shock at the passing of Ghana’s Nobel Peace Laureate and her finest international diplomat of all-time, Busumru Dr. Kofi Annan, which sad event occurred in the early hours of Saturday, August 18, 2018 in Berne, Switzerland. He was 80.

A highly respected global statesman, Kofi Annan led a life concentrated on the pursuit of a just and peaceful society. Born in Kumasi, Ghana, on 8 April 1938, Mr. Annan studied at the University of Science and Technology in Kumasi and completed his undergraduate work in economics at Macalester College in the United States in 1961 before undertaking his graduate studies in economics at the Institut universitaire des hautes études internationales in Geneva. As a 1971- 1972 Sloan Fellow at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Mr. Annan received a Master of Science degree in management.

Kofi Annan joined the UN in 1962, working for the World Health Organization in Geneva from where he rose through the ranks to the highest position of Secretary-General of United Nations for two terms, spanning 1997 to 2006.

The Association of African Universities extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family and commiserates with Ghana, Africa and the United Nations on this sad event. In compliance with the directive from the Government of Ghana, the flags of AAU would fly at half-mast for one-week beginning Monday 20th August, 2018 in honour of a man known for his humility, nobility and love for peace.

While mourning the passing of this global icon, the AAU pledges to uphold Kofi Annan’s virtues and celebrate him for living a life worth emulating. May his soul find eternal rest.

TITLE: Rhodes Business School partners with eLearnAfrica To Develop A Virtual Learning Environment (VLE).

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
PRESS RELEASE – Accra, Ghana (November 3, 2022) – Recognized as one of the leading business schools for its focus on sustainability and ethical leadership, Rhodes Business School has entered into a partnership with eLearnAfrica to develop a Virtual Learning Environment (VLE), to fulfil the School’s goal of enabling its AMBA accredited MBA to reach into Africa and beyond, like never before.

Professor Owen Skae, Director of Rhodes Business School, says that the eLearnAfrica-supported VLE will be launched and operational from 2024. “We have learnt two things from the pandemic. Returning to the old ‘business as usual model’ of ‘chalk and talk’ is not going to happen like it used to. At the same time, running Zoom or Teams sessions, and just displaying your power-point slides does not suffice. Students and lecturers want the best in both the virtual and the physical teaching world. That is key! The virtual mode provides convenience and flexibility. The physical mode provides immersion and human engagement that we still need. We know that our students still value the opportunity to come to Rhodes University, given that it is such a unique and special institution.”

The common denominator is having the necessary technology enablement to provide the best teaching and learning experience for students, whilst creating a virtual classroom environment for academic staff to deliver effectively and efficiently, regardless of the mode of delivery. “Getting the state-of-the-art VLE platform that was needed, required to partner with someone who knows what they are doing. Students need the right balance of synchronous and asynchronous interaction that only a top-class VLE can bring. That partner is eLearnAfrica”, says Skae.

The VLE will provide the full suite of synchronous and asynchronous teaching and learning applications to ensure that the Rhodes Business School MBA continues to be the transformative experience it is renowned for. The partnership with ELearnAfrica brings immersion, flexibility, and convenience.

The VLE-enabled MBA will allow the current six two-week block attendances (i.e. three blocks in Year 1 and three blocks in Year 2) to be reduced to one two-week block in each year (i.e. one block in each of Year 1 and Year 2), for the invaluable face-face synchronous delivery mode.

The Rhodes Business School’s essence is ‘Leadership for Sustainability’. Leadership and sustainability principles underline all subjects in the curriculum. Emphasis is placed on business continuity, and achieving a balance between economic, social, and environmental sustainability. The School applies its unique 4E (Economy, Ethics, Ecology, and Equity) model in its teaching and learning practice.

The Rhodes MBA is a coursework degree comprising 13 courses (made up of 12 core courses and 1 elective) and a mini-thesis of 15,000 words. The degree is offered on a part-time, modular basis over two years or on a full-time, modular basis over one and a half years.

About eLearnAfrica

In 2016, eLearnAfrica entered a partnership agreement with the Association of African Universities (AAU); one that would expand online learning opportunities for students enrolled in the AAU’s over 400 member institutions and other universities not yet under the umbrella of the prestigious AAU. The target was to make educational opportunities available to about 10 million African students. In pursuing this agenda, the AAU-eLearnAfricaLMS launched at the 15th Quadrennial AAU General Conference of African University Leaders, on 7th July 2021.

About Rhodes University

Rhodes University is a public research-intensive university located in Makhanda in the Eastern Cape Province of South Africa. It is one of four universities in the province. Established in 1904, Rhodes owes its unique character among South African universities to a combination of factors – historical, geographical, cultural and architectural. Its history is a chronicle of the people whose intellect, vision and courage created and sustained a university, often against seemingly insuperable odds. Successive generations of its alumni, imbued with their independence of thought, have had an influence on southern Africa and world affairs out of all proportion to their small numbers. It is known as the institution ‘Where leaders learn’. Rhodes Business School was founded in 2000.

TITLE: American Academy of Diplomacy Spring 2027 Program & Communications Internship: Gain Hands-On Experience in U.S. Diplomacy, Foreign Affairs and Nonprofit Communications

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the American Academy of Diplomacy Spring 2027 Program & Communications Internship, an opportunity designed for students and recent graduates who want practical exposure to diplomacy, foreign affairs, communications and nonprofit management.

Based at the American Academy of Diplomacy, an organization whose membership includes former senior ambassadors and career diplomats, the programme offers an unusual opportunity to work closely with a small professional team while learning more about how diplomacy, foreign-policy engagement and nonprofit organizations function in practice.

Rather than limiting the intern to one narrow area of work, the Academy plans to involve the selected candidate across a wide range of organizational responsibilities. These include managing social-media accounts, helping implement events and meetings, communicating with Academy members, updating website content, maintaining contact lists, supporting professional staff and creating an independent project.

The Academy particularly encourages applications from a student or recent graduate with continuing education goals who has an interest in the Foreign Service, communications, nonprofit management or the broader practice of American diplomacy.

The internship requires a commitment of 20 to 40 hours per week, depending on the candidate’s availability. Applicants must also be able to participate for a minimum of 13 weeks. Candidates who cannot commit to at least 13 weeks will not be considered.

The programme is unpaid, although academic credit may be possible depending on the requirements of the participant’s school or university. The Academy reviews applications on a rolling basis, meaning interested candidates are encouraged to apply before the final deadline rather than waiting until the last day.

Application deadline: End of day on November 2, 2026.

About the American Academy of Diplomacy

The American Academy of Diplomacy, commonly referred to as the Academy or AAD, is a nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening the resources and tools the United States brings to managing diplomatic challenges.

Its work is aimed at improving understanding of the importance of diplomacy and increasing the effectiveness of American engagement with the international community.

The Academy pursues this mission through activities such as:

Targeted outreach programmes

Policy proposals

Publications

Distinguished awards

Professional engagement

Discussions on diplomacy and foreign policy

An important feature of the organization is its membership. The Academy is composed of former senior ambassadors and career diplomats who bring extensive professional experience in the practice of diplomacy.

For an intern, this creates a professional environment that is quite different from a conventional university internship. The selected candidate may have opportunities to interact with people who have spent significant portions of their careers working directly on diplomatic negotiations, international relations, foreign-policy implementation and overseas representation.

About the Spring 2027 Program & Communications Internship

The Academy is specifically looking for an individual interested in two connected areas:

The practice of American diplomacy; and

The internal workings of a nonprofit organization.

Because the Academy is a relatively small organization, it states that an intern can become an integral part of its core team.

This matters because internships at larger institutions can sometimes separate interns from central organizational work. At AAD, the selected intern is expected to contribute directly to the Academy’s regular communications, programme and administrative activities.

The opportunity may be especially relevant for students considering careers in:

Diplomacy

Foreign Service

International affairs

Strategic communications

Public diplomacy

Foreign-policy organizations

Think tanks

Nonprofit management

Public policy

Government affairs

International relations

Digital communications

However, the Academy does not require applicants to be enrolled in one specific academic major.

What Will the Intern Do?

The internship combines communications, programme support, event assistance, digital content management and organizational administration.

Managing the Academy’s Social Media Accounts

One of the most significant responsibilities is helping manage the Academy’s social-media presence.

The Academy specifically prefers applicants who have previous organizational experience using platforms such as:

TikTok

Instagram

Experience with social-media analytics is also considered valuable.

The selected intern may therefore be involved in activities such as preparing posts, promoting Academy publications, distributing articles written by Academy members, publicizing events and helping analyze audience engagement.

This could be especially useful for someone interested in digital diplomacy, strategic communications or public affairs, where institutions increasingly rely on social media to communicate policy ideas and professional expertise.

Supporting the Distribution of Academy Members’ Published Work

The Academy notes that interns may assist with distributing articles written by its distinguished members.

This could provide experience in identifying appropriate digital channels, preparing concise promotional copy and presenting foreign-policy analysis to wider audiences.

The work may help the intern develop skills in:

Editorial promotion

Social-media writing

Audience engagement

Digital communications

Content distribution

For students interested in journalism or public diplomacy, this part of the placement could provide valuable experience in translating substantive foreign-policy content into accessible public communications.

Helping With Events and Meetings

The intern will also assist with the organization and implementation of Academy events and meetings.

This may involve helping professional staff prepare for:

Committee meetings

Board meetings

Public events

Member activities

Policy discussions

Other Academy programmes

The internship description specifically mentions assisting during committee and Board meetings as an example of the level of responsibility an intern may receive.

This means organizational ability and attention to detail will be important.

An intern may need to keep track of schedules, documents, participants, communications and follow-up tasks without constant supervision.

Communicating With Academy Members

The selected intern will interact with Academy members as part of regular organizational operations.

Because the Academy’s membership includes experienced diplomats and former ambassadors, communication needs to be accurate and professional.

The Academy explicitly expects a successful intern to be detail-oriented enough to handle tasks such as sending member emails without constant guidance.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate an ability to communicate professionally through:

Written correspondence

Digital platforms

Internal organizational communications

A strong command of written English is particularly important.

Updating the Academy Website

The intern will help update content on the Academy’s website.

The Academy indicates that front-end Wix development experience is preferred, although it is not listed as an absolute requirement.

Applicants who already have experience using Wix may therefore have an advantage.

Candidates who have worked with other content-management systems may also have transferable experience. Examples could include:

WordPress

Squarespace

Drupal

Other web publishing systems

The role does not appear to require advanced software development. The emphasis is on front-end website and content-management capability.

Managing Contact Lists

The intern will help manage organizational contact lists.

This can involve maintaining accurate information about:

Academy members

Event participants

Professional contacts

Mailing lists

Other institutional stakeholders

Although this may appear to be a simple administrative responsibility, accurate database management is essential in a membership organization.

The Academy therefore emphasizes the importance of being detail-oriented.

Supporting Professional Staff

The intern will provide broader support to the Academy’s professional staff.

Because the organization is small, interns may be exposed to several dimensions of nonprofit management at the same time.

This could help participants learn more about:

Programme coordination

Administrative systems

Institutional communications

Membership organizations

Foreign-policy programming

Event management

Digital outreach

This broad exposure may be particularly useful for students who are still determining which professional path within international affairs most interests them.

Create Your Own Project

Another notable component of the internship is the opportunity to create an independent project.

The Academy does not prescribe one specific project that every intern must complete.

This can potentially allow the selected participant to develop something that reflects both organizational priorities and their own professional interests.

Depending on discussions with the Academy, such a project could potentially involve subjects such as:

Digital communications

Diplomacy outreach

Social-media strategy

Membership engagement

Website content

Communications analytics

Foreign-policy resources

Applicants should not assume that any particular project will automatically be approved, but thinking about a possible contribution before applying could strengthen an interview or cover letter.

Mentorship and Professional Guidance

The Academy states that its Program and Finance Assistant will provide detailed guidance and constructive critique.

The purpose is to maximize the intern’s learning experience.

This means the programme is intended to have a developmental component rather than simply assigning administrative tasks without feedback.

A participant may therefore gain experience receiving professional critique and improving their work in areas such as:

Organization

Programme support

Professional judgment

20 to 40 hours per week

to the programme.

Candidates should therefore carefully consider their academic timetable before applying.

No employment is guaranteed.

The Academy specifically states that participating in the programme comes without an expectation of employment at the conclusion of the internship.

Applicants should therefore view this primarily as a learning and professional-development opportunity rather than a guaranteed pathway into a paid position at AAD.

Although the internship is unpaid, academic credit may potentially be available.
