TITLE: African Education Trust Fund (AETF) Committee meets with the AAU Secretary-General

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Thursday 10th March 2022

The Chairman of the African Education Trust Fund (AETF) Committee, Dr. Ekwow Spio-Garbrah, has led a three-member delegation comprising Dr. Jeannine Uwimana- Nicol (Snr Researcher, Faculty of Medicine & Health Sciences, Stellenbosch University, South Africa) and Prof. Goski Alabi (President of Laweh Open University, Ghana) to meet with the Secretary-General of the Association of African Universities (AAU), Prof. Olusola Oyewole at the AAU Secretariat in Accra, Ghana. Accompanying the delegation was Mr. Wendell Addy, Chairman of the African Private Sector Summit (APSS), the organisation mandated by the AAU and Pan African Chamber of Commerce to implement a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the two bodies which, among others, set up the AETF. The AETF was set up by the AAU and the Pan African Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PACCI) to transform tertiary education in Africa and scale up the skills set of the continent for the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

The exploratory visit, according to Dr. Spio-Garbrah, was to consult with the AAU on ideas to make the Committee’s task successful. He affirmed the open-mindedness of the Committee in taking on board all views garnered to structure the objectives of the Fund. It was in light of this that the AAU would be officially written to by the Committee to consider gender, linguistic and professional expertise in the future enlargement of the Committee’s membership.

Welcoming the delegation, Prof. Oyewole expressed his confidence in the Committee due to the quality, experience and expertise each member brings on board to the fundraising effort to support Africa’s development through education and the private sector. He advised the Committee to deliberate thoroughly on whether the Funds would be used to wholly support higher education, including technical and vocational education in Africa or include basic and secondary levels of education, for which the consent of African governments would have to be sought.

His postulation on the application of the Fund for higher education included supporting mentorship programmes for African academics through secondment to industry, support for annual African innovation fairs that showcase African inventions and innovations and postgraduate scholarships and research grants, among others.

Prof. Oyewole also shared his vision of harnessing African expertise through the establishment of an African brain bank through which databases of experts would be built for industry, policy makers and other stakeholders to tap into the skills bank of academics for synergetic relationships.

Wrapping up, the AAU Secretary General paid glowing tribute to Mr. Wendell Addy for his perseverance is seeing to the implementation of the MOU between AAU and PACCI which has led to the establishment of the AETF.

The meeting agreed to undertake a baseline survey on the critical skills need for the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) as well as to implement the other activities to be rolled out under the Fund, which like a baby in conception, would need to be resourced and housed when it is born. Prof. Oyewole offered AAU’s support to locate the Trust Fund at its Secretariat and in future have a full-time administrator for it when funding is secured. However, he advised against ownership of the Fund by either AAU or PACCI, which would betray the purpose of its establishment. All agreed that to ensure credibility and integrity, the AETF would require a higher level of management and proper governance, with the AAU Secretary-General advocating for the establishment of a 7-member Board to oversee it. He proposed the membership to include the AAU, PACCI, the APSS and the AETF Committee.

To ensure sustainability, it was also agreed that the relevance and impact of activities to be implemented must be felt and, as a private sector driven initiative, the AETF stood a better chance of sustainability unlike many funds established by wealthy individuals which go extinct with the demise of the philanthropists.

Dr. Ekwow Spio-Garbrah expressed his gratitude for the exchange of ideas to streamline the work of the Committee and promised more engagement with the AAU in other steps of the Committee’s tasks.

TITLE: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28: HK$344,400 Annual Stipend for International PhD Students in Hong Kong

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) 2027/28 is now accepting applications from outstanding prospective doctoral students from around the world who want to pursue full-time PhD studies at participating universities in Hong Kong.

Established by Hong Kong’s Research Grants Council (RGC) in 2009, the scheme was created to attract high-achieving researchers and talented doctoral students from around the world to Hong Kong’s universities. The programme is open to applicants regardless of their country of origin, prior work experience or ethnic background, making it a genuinely international doctoral fellowship opportunity.

For the 2027/28 academic year, the scheme will award 400 PhD fellowships. The current official scheme information lists an annual fellowship stipend of HK$344,400, together with an annual HK$14,400 conference and research-related travel allowance, with fellowship support provided for up to three years.

The application period for the 2027/28 intake runs from 1 September 2026 to 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time. Late initial applications will not be considered.

What Is the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme?

The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme is a competitive doctoral fellowship programme established by the Research Grants Council to attract talented researchers to Hong Kong.

The scheme supports students seeking admission as new full-time PhD students at participating Hong Kong universities.

Rather than restricting applications to applicants from a particular country or region, the scheme is designed to attract talented doctoral candidates internationally.

The programme is therefore relevant to prospective PhD students from:

Africa

Asia

Europe

North America

South America

Oceania

Other regions around the world

The official eligibility information states that applicants are considered irrespective of their country of origin, prior work experience and ethnic background.

What Makes the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme Special?

One of the major attractions of the HKPFS is the level of financial support available to successful fellows.

For the current fellowship information published by the Research Grants Council, each awardee receives:

HK$344,400 per year in fellowship stipend.

HK$14,400 per year for conference and research-related travel.

Fellowship support for up to three years.

Potential additional support from the chosen university if the PhD requires more than three years to complete.

For the 2027/28 academic year, 400 PhD fellowships will be awarded. Hong Kong universities normally begin their academic year in September.

The travel allowance is particularly valuable for doctoral researchers who need to attend academic conferences, present research findings or undertake research-related travel.

Who Can Apply for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship?

The scheme is open to individuals seeking admission as new full-time PhD students at one of the participating Hong Kong universities.

Applicants can come from any country or region, and the scheme does not restrict eligibility based on ethnic background or previous work experience.

However, applicants must satisfy the admission requirements of the university and specific PhD programme they choose.

In addition to meeting university admission requirements, applicants should demonstrate strong qualities in several areas.

These include:

Outstanding academic performance

Research ability or potential

Strong communication and interpersonal skills

Excellent leadership abilities

These characteristics form an important part of the fellowship’s selection process.

Academic Excellence Is a Major Selection Factor

The HKPFS selection process places particular emphasis on academic excellence.

However, academic results are not the only factor considered.

The selection panels also assess:

Research ability and potential.

Communication and interpersonal skills.

Leadership abilities.

This means that applicants should present themselves as well-rounded researchers rather than relying exclusively on academic grades.

A strong application should demonstrate both academic achievement and evidence that the applicant has the potential to become an independent and impactful researcher.

Research Ability and Potential

Research capability is another major component of the selection process.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate their potential to undertake doctoral-level research successfully.

This may be reflected through:

Previous research projects.

Undergraduate or master’s research.

Research publications.

Conference presentations.

Research-related work experience.

A well-developed proposed research direction.

Evidence of analytical and problem-solving abilities.

The selection process considers not only what applicants have already achieved but also their potential for future research.

Communication and Interpersonal Skills

The fellowship also considers communication and interpersonal skills.

Doctoral researchers frequently work with supervisors, research teams, academic institutions and researchers from different countries.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate that they can:

Communicate research ideas clearly.

Work effectively with others.

Participate in academic discussions.

Build professional relationships.

Present ideas to different audiences.

Leadership Abilities

Leadership is also one of the four major criteria used in the HKPFS assessment.

Applicants should consider how their academic, professional, research or community experiences demonstrate leadership potential.

Leadership does not necessarily mean holding a formal leadership position. Evidence of taking initiative, leading projects, contributing to research teams or creating meaningful academic or community impact can help demonstrate leadership potential.

Participating Universities

Applicants can apply for PhD programmes at the following eight participating universities:

1. City University of Hong Kong

City University of Hong Kong is one of the participating institutions where HKPFS applicants can pursue eligible doctoral programmes.

2. Hong Kong Baptist University

Hong Kong Baptist University is another participating university offering doctoral study opportunities under the scheme.

3. Lingnan University

Lingnan University is included among the eight participating institutions.

4. The Chinese University of Hong Kong

The Chinese University of Hong Kong participates in the HKPFS and offers doctoral programmes across a broad range of disciplines.

5. The Education University of Hong Kong

The Education University of Hong Kong is also part of the participating university network.

6. The Hong Kong Polytechnic University

The Hong Kong Polytechnic University participates in the scheme and provides PhD opportunities across multiple academic and research areas.

7. The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology is another participating institution.

8. The University of Hong Kong

The University of Hong Kong, one of the region’s major research universities, is also included in the scheme.

The Research Grants Council confirms that applicants can seek admission as new full-time PhD students at these eight universities.

How Many Universities Can You Apply To?

Applicants may choose a maximum of two programmes within one or two participating universities for their PhD study.

This means applicants should carefully research their preferred programmes before completing the initial HKPFS application.

Candidates should consider:

The university’s research strengths.

The specific PhD programme.

Potential supervisors.

Research facilities.

Programme requirements.

University-specific application deadlines.

The suitability of the programme for their proposed research.

HKPFS Application Process

Applying for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme involves more than completing the initial fellowship application.

Applicants must complete the HKPFS initial application and also submit full PhD admission applications to their selected universities.

Step 1: Identify Your Preferred PhD Programme

Applicants should first identify suitable PhD programmes at the participating universities.

Research the programmes carefully and ensure that you meet their specific admission requirements.

Step 2: Submit the HKPFS Initial Application

The initial application is submitted through the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme Electronic System (HKPFSES).

For the 2027/28 intake, the application system is open from:

1 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time

until:

1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time.

Step 3: Obtain Your HKPFS Reference Number

After submitting the initial application, applicants receive an HKPFS Reference Number.

This reference number is important because applicants must use it when communicating with the RGC and when submitting applications to their selected universities.

Applicants should save the confirmation email containing their reference number and login information.

Step 4: Submit Full Applications to the Universities

Completing the HKPFS initial application is not enough.

Applicants must also submit a full PhD admission application to the university or universities selected in their initial application.

The university applications must be submitted before the individual universities’ own deadlines.

The universities may have different application deadlines, so candidates should check each institution carefully.

An initial HKPFS application that is not followed by the required university application will be considered void and will not be processed further by the RGC.

University Admission Requirements Still Apply

Applicants should understand that receiving an HKPFS fellowship is separate from satisfying the admission requirements of the selected university and PhD programme.

Candidates must comply with the relevant university’s:

PhD admission requirements.

Application procedures.

Programme requirements.

Application deadlines.

Other applicable university regulations and policies.

Universities will normally conduct interviews as part of their assessment process.

Selection Panels

Shortlisted applications are assessed according to the applicant’s area of study.

The scheme has two major selection panels:

Sciences, Medicine, Engineering and Technology

This panel considers applications relating to scientific, medical, engineering and technological areas.

Humanities, Social Sciences and Business Studies

This panel considers research in humanities, social sciences and business-related areas.

The panels consist of experts in the relevant areas.

How Applicants Are Assessed

The four main selection criteria are:

1. Academic Excellence

The academic record of the applicant is a primary consideration.

Candidates should demonstrate strong academic performance and the ability to succeed at doctoral level.

2. Research Ability and Potential

Applicants should demonstrate their capacity and potential to conduct high-quality research.

3. Communication and Interpersonal Skills

The panels assess whether candidates can communicate effectively and work successfully with others.

4. Leadership Abilities

Applicants should demonstrate leadership potential through their academic, professional, research or other relevant experiences.

The RGC states that academic excellence is the prime consideration, while the other three areas are also taken into account.

What Happens If You Are Not Selected for the Fellowship?

Not being selected for the HKPFS fellowship does not necessarily mean that the applicant cannot pursue a PhD in Hong Kong.

Candidates who are not selected for the fellowship may still be accepted by the university for regular PhD admission.

In some cases, universities may offer successful university applicants a postgraduate studentship or other financial support.

Therefore, applicants should still submit their university applications even though fellowship selection is competitive.

Application Fee

The Research Grants Council does not charge an application fee for the HKPFS.

However, individual universities may charge their own application or processing fees.

Applicants should therefore check the fee requirements of each university to which they apply.

Important Application Rule: Submit Only One Initial HKPFS Application

Applicants should be particularly careful about the number of initial HKPFS applications they submit.

Only one initial application is accepted per applicant.

Submitting multiple initial applications can result in disqualification of all applications, even if a university subsequently nominates the applicant for the fellowship.

Applicants who accidentally submit multiple applications are advised to contact the RGC immediately before the application deadline.

Application Language

The initial HKPFS application must be completed in English, except for the field requiring an applicant’s name in Chinese where applicable.

Applicants should therefore ensure that the information provided in the initial application is clear, accurate and consistent.

Keep Your Information Consistent

The RGC cross-checks information submitted through the HKPFS system with information provided in university applications.

Applicants should therefore ensure that:

Personal information is accurate.

Academic information is consistent.

Research information is consistent.

University choices match the initial application.

Programme information is correct.

Supporting information does not conflict between applications.

Inconsistencies or incomplete information may result in an application not being considered.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28 is:

1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time (HKT).

The application period begins on 1 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time.

Late initial applications will not be considered.

If an awardee needs more than three years to complete the PhD, additional support may be available from the university where the student is enrolled.

Applicants requiring additional support should contact their chosen university directly for information about its policies and funding arrangements.

Expected Academic Experience

Successful fellows will become part of the research communities at their selected universities and pursue doctoral research under the academic supervision and requirements of their chosen programme.

Preparing a Competitive Application

Although the RGC identifies academic excellence as the primary consideration, applicants should also pay close attention to the other three assessment areas.

A strong candidate should aim to demonstrate:

TITLE: Longview Philanthropy COO / Director of Operations 2026 | Apply by 6 September

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Longview Philanthropy is inviting applications for a senior Chief Operating Officer (COO) or Director of Operations position to help the organisation rapidly scale its team, systems, and operations.

The opportunity is designed for an experienced operations leader who has successfully managed organisational growth and can build effective teams, processes, and functions in a fast-paced environment. Longview says candidates do not necessarily need previous experience in AI safety or philanthropy and expects strong applicants may come from rapidly scaling startups and technology companies.

About Longview Philanthropy

Longview Philanthropy advises major donors and makes grants in areas including AI safety and nuclear weapons policy. Its mission is to help the world navigate extreme risk and unlock an excellent future.

The organisation states that it directed more than $75 million to high-impact organisations in 2025 and expects its activities to grow substantially in 2026. Longview currently has offices in Berkeley, New York City, Washington DC, and London.

As Longview plans significant growth in 2027 and beyond, it is seeking a senior operations leader who can help the organisation scale while maintaining its effectiveness, agility, and high standards.

About the COO / Director of Operations Role

The successful candidate will be appointed as either:

Chief Operating Officer (COO), or

Director of Operations

The final title and scope will depend on the candidate’s experience. The role reports to Longview’s current COO, Katie Hearsum, as she transitions into another senior position, or to CEO Simran Dhaliwal.

The organisation is looking for someone who can operate at a senior leadership level, manage multiple operational functions, and build systems capable of supporting rapid organisational growth.

Key Responsibilities

Help Longview Double in Size

One of the central responsibilities is helping Longview significantly expand its workforce and organisational capacity.

The successful candidate will:

Design and execute an operations and hiring strategy to support the organisation’s growth.

Work with the Office of the CEO and leadership team to determine which functions need to be developed and when.

Own the operations organisational structure and hiring decisions.

Scope roles and help close strong candidates.

Maintain a high standard for excellence and organisational fit.

Build strong relationships between operations and other departments.

Ensure that regulatory requirements are appropriately managed across the US and UK entities.

Develop Operations Leaders

The COO or Director of Operations will manage and develop leaders responsible for several critical functions.

These currently include:

People Operations

Business Operations

Finance

Talent

Grants Management

The successful candidate will coach these leaders and help them navigate the challenges associated with a rapidly scaling organisation.

The role will also involve setting the standard for how operations functions across Longview, including promoting clear ownership, direct feedback, high-quality decision-making, and a mission-focused approach.

Build New Operational Functions

Longview is looking for a leader capable of expanding the scope of traditional operations functions.

For example, the successful candidate may be responsible for developing a finance function that handles both internal financial activities and investment of capital held by the organisation.

The role may also involve creating a recruiting function that not only supports Longview’s own hiring needs but also helps identify founders for new organisations that Longview’s grantmakers want to support.

Build Systems and Processes for Growth

Another major responsibility will be developing systems that allow Longview to grow without unnecessarily creating bureaucracy.

The successful candidate will:

Build simple and robust systems for planning and decision-making.

Determine when additional structure is useful and when it may become counterproductive.

Streamline routine operational activities.

Standardise processes where appropriate.

Automate operational work, including through AI.

Provide operational support that allows grantmakers and advisors to focus on specialised work.

Longview also states that it is open to tailoring the role for exceptional candidates and may consider a different scope or title where appropriate.

Ideal Candidate

Longview is looking for an experienced operations leader who has successfully guided organisations through rapid growth.

The ideal candidate is expected to be:

An experienced manager of managers.

Comfortable working across multiple operational functions.

Experienced in fast-paced environments.

Highly capable of prioritising competing demands.

Confident working through organisational ambiguity.

Interested in coaching and developing people.

Essential Experience

Candidates should ideally have experience in the following areas:

Experience Scaling Organisations

Applicants should have scaled operations at a fast-growing organisation, preferably at the 30-to-60-person stage or beyond, and understand the challenges and failure modes that can occur during organisational growth.

Managing Geographically Distributed Teams

Candidates should be comfortable managing teams and working effectively across different locations.

Managing Managers

Experience managing managers during periods of significant organisational growth is an important requirement.

Multiple Operational Functions

Candidates should have been responsible for at least three operational functions.

Longview’s current operational functions include People Operations, Business Operations, Finance, Talent, and Grants Management.

Critical Abilities

The successful candidate should demonstrate strong judgement and operational leadership.

Longview particularly values candidates who:

Know when processes create value and when they create unnecessary bureaucracy.

Can move quickly and prioritise effectively under pressure.

Are comfortable managing multiple competing priorities and changing deadlines.

Enjoy coaching and developing people.

Can tackle new problems without relying on an established playbook.

Are comfortable operating in ambiguous environments.

Communication and Collaboration Skills

Strong communication will be important in the role.

Candidates should be:

Exceptionally clear written and verbal communicators.

Comfortable adapting to Longview’s working style.

Able to prepare effective agendas and support memo-based decision-making.

Confident pushing back on colleagues when necessary, regardless of seniority.

Comfortable giving and receiving direct feedback.

Proactive in providing candid feedback.

Motivation and Organisational Fit

Longview wants candidates who are genuinely motivated by its mission.

Previous knowledge of AI safety or philanthropy is not required, but candidates should care about the problems Longview works on and understand how the organisation’s mission influences its decision-making.

The organisation is also looking for people who are:

Kind and conscientious.

Energised by fast-paced, lean working environments.

Comfortable taking ownership.

Committed to professional excellence.

Additional Experience That Would Be an Advantage

The following experience is considered useful but is not required:

Hands-on experience with grants management.

Non-profit compliance experience.

Experience working in regulated-industry operations.

Previous exposure to AI safety.

Previous experience in philanthropy.

Longview explicitly encourages strong candidates to apply even if they do not meet every qualification listed in the vacancy.

Salary and Compensation

The advertised total compensation depends on the position offered:

Director of Operations: $165,000–$264,000+

Chief Operating Officer: $220,000–$330,000+

These figures include base salary and a 10% unconditional pension/401(k) contribution.

Benefits

Longview provides a range of benefits, with specific benefits depending on the employee’s location.

Benefits for US Staff

US employees may receive:

100% employer-paid private health insurance through UHC.

Dental and vision coverage.

25 vacation days, plus public holidays and additional winter-break days.

Four months of fully paid family leave.

$3,000 annual professional development budget.

Well-being support of up to $200 per month for gym memberships and fitness classes.

In-office meals and a stocked office fridge at most US offices.

Benefits for UK Staff

UK employees may receive:

Private health insurance through Aviva.

25 days of holiday plus bank holidays and additional winter-break days.

Four months of fully paid family leave.

£5,000 annual well-being budget.

£2,400 annual professional development budget.

Equipment and support for establishing a productive work environment.

In-office meals and a stocked office fridge.

Benefits are subject to eligibility requirements and applicable waiting periods.

Location

Longview prefers candidates who can work in person at one of its offices in:

Berkeley, United States

Washington DC, United States

New York, United States

London, United Kingdom

The organisation states that it is able to sponsor visas in the United States and United Kingdom.

Start Date

The successful candidate is expected to start as soon as possible, with the exact start date to be agreed between Longview and the successful applicant.

Application Process

Longview plans to use a thorough but relatively fast recruitment process.

The process is expected to include:

An application form.

A paid strategy work task.

Interviews with leadership and direct reports.

Reference checks.

A paid two-day in-person work trial.

Longview states that the process may be tailored for individual candidates.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should complete the official Longview Philanthropy application form.

Apply here: Longview Philanthropy COO / Director of Operations Application

Candidates should ensure their application clearly demonstrates relevant experience in organisational scaling, operations leadership, management, hiring, systems development, and cross-functional collaboration.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

Sunday, 6 September 2026 — End of Day

Applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis, so interested candidates are encouraged to apply as early as possible.

Important Information for Applicants

This is a senior-level operations leadership position, rather than an entry-level or graduate opportunity.

Candidates should therefore carefully assess their experience against Longview’s expectations, particularly experience managing managers, overseeing multiple operational functions, and scaling organisations.

However, Longview states that most strong candidates will not have every qualification listed and encourages candidates who are uncertain about meeting every requirement to apply.

About Longview’s Work

Longview Philanthropy was founded in 2018 to advise major donors on reducing extreme risks.

The organisation has four departments:

Operations

Donor Advising

AI Grantmaking

Nuclear Grantmaking

Longview describes its team as collaborative and dedicated, with a culture centred on clear communication, professional development, direct feedback, ownership, excellence, and outcomes.

Conclusion

The Longview Philanthropy COO / Director of Operations opportunity is aimed at experienced operations professionals who can help a growing organisation scale its people, systems, processes, and functions while maintaining a high standard of effectiveness.

The successful candidate will play a central role in organisational growth, including managing operational leaders, expanding teams, developing new functions, improving systems, and supporting strategic decision-making.

With compensation of up to $330,000+ for the COO position, additional benefits, and opportunities to work across Longview’s offices in the United States or United Kingdom, the role represents a significant senior leadership opportunity for an experienced operations professional.

Candidates who have successfully scaled organisations and are motivated by Longview’s mission should consider applying before the 6 September 2026 deadline.

TITLE: UC Berkeley–Packard Foundation Philanthropy Fellow 2026: Apply for a $90,000 Professional Opportunity in Civil Society and Leadership

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The University of California, Berkeley, through the Haas School of Business and its Center for Social Sector Leadership (CSL), is inviting qualified professionals to apply for the Philanthropy Fellow, Civil Society and Leadership position with the David and Lucile Packard Foundation.

This full-time professional opportunity offers an exciting pathway for emerging leaders interested in philanthropy, civil society, nonprofit organizations, strategic grantmaking, social impact, research, evaluation, leadership, and international development. The successful candidate will work with the Packard Foundation’s Civil Society and Leadership team while receiving professional development, coaching, mentorship, and institutional support from UC Berkeley’s Center for Social Sector Leadership.

The position is based at the David and Lucile Packard Foundation in Los Altos, California, with the Foundation currently operating on a hybrid schedule in which staff work from the office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

The role provides an opportunity to gain practical experience in strategic philanthropy while contributing to research, evaluation and learning, strategy implementation, grantmaking, knowledge management, project management, and engagement with nonprofit organizations and other stakeholders.

Opportunity Overview

Position: Philanthropy Fellow, Civil Society and Leadership

Job ID: 88658

Reference Number: 5257C

Employer: University of California, Berkeley

Partner Organization: The David and Lucile Packard Foundation

Department: Haas School of Business / Center for Social Sector Leadership

Team: Civil Society and Leadership Initiative

Location: Los Altos, California, USA

Work Arrangement: Hybrid

Employment Type: Full-time

Hours: 40 hours per week

Salary: $78,435 to $90,000 per year

Application Materials: Resume and cover letter

First Review Date: September 22, 2026

Visa Sponsorship: Not a visa opportunity

About UC Berkeley

The University of California, Berkeley is one of the world’s leading public research universities. Founded in 1868, Berkeley has developed a global reputation for academic excellence, innovation, research, public service, and social impact.

The university describes its community as one built around openness, freedom, belonging, equity, and opportunity. Its faculty, students, researchers, and staff include internationally recognized scholars and leaders, and the institution has played a significant role in intellectual, economic, scientific, and social progress in California, the United States, and beyond.

For employees, Berkeley emphasizes continuous learning and professional development. Full-time staff employees receive support for professional growth, including paid professional development time and access to colleague communities and employee resource groups.

The Philanthropy Fellow position is situated within this broader environment of learning, leadership, innovation, and public impact.

About the Haas School of Business

The UC Berkeley Haas School of Business is the academic home supporting this fellowship partnership. Haas is known for a culture that encourages innovation, collaboration, leadership, and continuous learning.

The school’s workplace culture is organized around four defining leadership principles:

Question the Status Quo

Confidence Without Attitude

Students Always

Beyond Yourself

These principles are particularly relevant to the Philanthropy Fellow role because the position requires someone who can think strategically, work collaboratively, approach complex social challenges with curiosity, and contribute to initiatives designed to strengthen civil society.

Haas also supports flexible working arrangements, although specific arrangements depend on the responsibilities of each role and are determined in partnership with supervisors.

About the David and Lucile Packard Foundation

The David and Lucile Packard Foundation was established in 1964 by David and Lucile Packard. The Foundation works with people and communities to develop enduring solutions that contribute to just societies and a healthy, resilient natural world.

Over the years, the Foundation has supported organizations and leaders working across a range of important areas, including:

Science

Ocean and land conservation

Climate change

Women’s reproductive health and rights

Children, families, and communities

Civil society

Social justice

Community well-being

The Foundation’s work involves partnerships with organizations and leaders in the United States and internationally.

For someone seeking to build a career in philanthropy, nonprofit leadership, international development, or social impact, the opportunity provides exposure to how a major philanthropic institution works with grantees, partners, experts, and other stakeholders to address complex societal challenges.

About the Civil Society and Leadership Initiative

The Philanthropy Fellow will work within the Foundation’s Civil Society and Leadership (CSL) Initiative.

The Packard Foundation’s strategic framework recognizes civil society as an important component of achieving its broader goals and contributing to a just society. The CSL Initiative therefore focuses on strengthening civil society organizations, supporting resilient civil society ecosystems, and promoting a safe and thriving civic space.

The initiative operates under the Foundation’s Just Societies goal while supporting work connected to the Foundation’s other major goals and geographic areas of operation.

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant to professionals interested in questions surrounding:

Civil society development

Nonprofit organizations

Civic space

Social justice

Philanthropy

Organizational resilience

Strategic grantmaking

Public policy

Community development

Social impact

Evaluation and learning

International development

What Is the UC Berkeley–Packard Foundation Philanthropy Fellowship?

The partnership between UC Berkeley and the Packard Foundation is designed to strengthen the future of philanthropy and civil society by introducing recent graduates and emerging professionals from diverse academic and professional backgrounds to the philanthropic and nonprofit sectors.

The fellowship has two major objectives.

1. Developing the next generation of philanthropic leaders

The program provides participants with professional-level exposure to philanthropy and nonprofit work. Through direct involvement in Foundation activities, the Fellow can develop knowledge and skills that may support a future career in philanthropy, civil society, nonprofit leadership, social impact, policy, research, or related fields.

2. Bringing fresh perspectives to the Packard Foundation

The partnership also allows the Foundation to benefit from new ideas, skills, experiences, and perspectives brought by the Fellows.

The selected Fellow will join a cohort of four other fellows working across different Foundation areas, including environment and science, families and communities, and global reproductive health.

The fellowship cohort will participate in quarterly activities, creating additional opportunities for learning, collaboration, networking, and professional development.

Where Will the Fellow Work?

The Fellow will be based at the David and Lucile Packard Foundation in Los Altos, California.

The Foundation currently uses a hybrid work schedule, with staff attending the office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

The position therefore combines professional experience within a major philanthropic organization with the resources and support of UC Berkeley’s Center for Social Sector Leadership.

Key Responsibilities of the Philanthropy Fellow

The selected Fellow will have a broad range of responsibilities involving research, evaluation, strategy, grantmaking, project management, knowledge management, stakeholder engagement, and professional learning.

1. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning

The Fellow will support CSL’s monitoring, evaluation, and learning activities.

This may include:

Supporting research projects

Coordinating internal learning processes

Contributing to evaluation activities

Helping the team assess progress

Supporting strategic reflection

Contributing to the Foundation’s mid-strategy reflection for 2027–2028

This responsibility makes research, analytical thinking, organization, and the ability to interpret evidence particularly important.

2. Strategy Development and Implementation

The Fellow will work with the CSL team to help inform and refine organizational strategy.

Responsibilities may include:

Conducting research

Analyzing relevant information

Supporting strategic discussions

Facilitating team deliberations

Identifying relevant trends and issues

Contributing research that informs decision-making

The role therefore requires more than administrative ability. Applicants should be comfortable examining complex issues, identifying relevant evidence, synthesizing information, and communicating findings clearly.

3. Grantmaking Support

The Fellow will work with a Program Officer and Program Associate to support grantmaking within a CSL portfolio.

This provides an opportunity to gain practical exposure to how philanthropic organizations identify priorities, engage with organizations, develop grant-related materials, and support initiatives designed to strengthen civil society.

4. Project and Event Management

The Fellow will project-manage important initiatives and events for the CSL team.

Examples include supporting strategy sessions held during organizational retreats.

This requires strong organizational skills and the ability to coordinate multiple activities, deadlines, people, and deliverables.

5. Knowledge Management

Knowledge management is another important component of the position.

The Fellow will help maintain and improve the team’s knowledge-management infrastructure and identify efficient ways to store and analyze different types of information and data.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable working with information systems, organizing knowledge, identifying patterns, and developing streamlined processes.

6. Support for Program Officers

The Fellow will provide support to relevant program officers.

This can include:

Preparing materials for meetings

Preparing meeting agendas

Supporting grantee meetings

Supporting field convenings

Participating in meetings with grantees

Participating in site visits

Preparing meeting summaries

Managing follow-up actions

Supporting other program-related activities

These responsibilities require strong written communication, attention to detail, interpersonal skills, and the ability to work professionally with different stakeholders.

7. Stakeholder Engagement

The Fellow may interact with a broad range of individuals and organizations, including:

Foundation program staff

Evaluation staff

Grantees

Funding partners

Government agencies

Content experts

Civil society organizations

Other relevant partners

This exposure can provide valuable insight into how strategic philanthropy operates in practice.

8. Travel and Conferences

The role may involve travel to meet new and existing partners and to participate in conferences relevant to the Civil Society and Leadership Initiative and the Fellow’s professional development goals.

This means the position may provide opportunities to learn directly from organizations, practitioners, experts, and other professionals working in civil society and philanthropy.

9. Foundation-Wide and University Activities

The Fellow will also participate in Foundation-wide activities that are relevant to their work and professional objectives.

They will have opportunities to engage with both University and Foundation communities and participate in professional development opportunities related to their responsibilities.

10. Professional Learning and Growth

Professional development is an important part of the position.

The Fellow is expected to contribute positively to a team environment that promotes belonging and collaboration and to demonstrate the Haas School of Business leadership principles.

The successful candidate will also be expected to complete required training and take advantage of relevant learning opportunities.

Professional Development Benefits

One of the distinctive features of this opportunity is the professional development support attached to the fellowship.

The Fellow will receive support from the Center for Social Sector Leadership at UC Berkeley, including context about the philanthropic sector, access to resources, and personal coaching and supervision.

The fellowship also includes a professional development budget.

This budget can support activities such as:

Attending conferences related to philanthropy

Participating in civil society conferences

Taking relevant workshops

Attending seminars

Receiving professional career coaching

Developing specific skills

Building knowledge relevant to future career objectives

For early-career professionals, this additional development component can make the role particularly valuable because the position is designed not only around immediate responsibilities but also around long-term leadership development.

Required Qualifications

Applicants are expected to demonstrate a combination of education, professional experience, analytical ability, communication skills, and knowledge of civil society.

Educational and professional experience

Candidates should have:

At least two to three years of experience and/or graduate-level education in a related field.

At least two years of experience working in a full-time professional position.

A bachelor’s degree in a related area or equivalent experience and training.

Experience working in civil society organizations.

The wording of the requirements means applicants should carefully demonstrate how their education and professional background relate to civil society, philanthropy, nonprofit organizations, research, public policy, social impact, or another relevant field.

Strategic thinking and research

Candidates should be strong strategic thinkers and researchers.

They should be able to:

Conduct research

Analyze information

Understand studies

Interpret complex material

Identify relevant evidence

Synthesize findings

Apply research to practical decision-making

Understanding of civil society

Applicants should demonstrate awareness of current threats and challenges facing civil society.

This may include understanding issues affecting nonprofit organizations, civic space, social movements, community organizations, institutional resilience, governance, or other factors influencing the ability of civil society actors to operate effectively.

Knowledge management

Applicants should have experience or demonstrated ability in developing systems and practices for effective knowledge management.

This is important because the position involves working with multiple types of information and helping the team store, organize, retrieve, and analyze knowledge efficiently.

Communication skills

Excellent communication skills are required.

Applicants should be able to:

Write clearly

Communicate complex ideas

Structure analysis

Synthesize information

Prepare reports

Present findings

Communicate effectively with different stakeholders

Both oral and written communication are emphasized in the job description.

Interpersonal and teamwork skills

The role involves collaboration with Foundation staff, grantees, government agencies, experts, funding partners, and other stakeholders.

Applicants therefore need strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a team.

Initiative and project management

The successful candidate should demonstrate strong initiative and be capable of managing multiple tasks and projects across diverse subject areas.

The role involves balancing research, grantmaking support, meetings, events, knowledge management, stakeholder engagement, and professional development.

Judgment and decision-making

Candidates should be comfortable operating in ambiguous situations.

The position requires the ability to use judgment, make sound decisions, and move projects forward even when complete information may not be available.

Responsible use of artificial intelligence

Another notable requirement is the ability to creatively and ethically use artificial intelligence to support strategy and learning.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate that they understand how AI can be used responsibly to improve research, analysis, knowledge management, learning, and strategic work while maintaining appropriate ethical standards.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not listed as mandatory requirements.

Experience strengthening civil society

Applicants with experience working in organizations focused on strengthening civil society, enabling conditions, or threats affecting civil society may be particularly competitive.

International experience

Experience working internationally is preferred.

This could be especially relevant for applicants who have worked across countries, regions, international organizations, global nonprofits, development institutions, or cross-border civil society initiatives.

Language skills

High proficiency in conversational Spanish, French, or Bahasa Indonesian is preferred.

Applicants who possess one or more of these language skills should highlight them clearly in their application materials.

Graduate-level education

Graduate-level education or comparable experience in areas such as:

International development

Public policy

Public health

Social science

Law

Related disciplines

is preferred.

Salary and Benefits

The position is a 100% full-time career position, requiring approximately 40 hours per week.

The budgeted annual salary range is:

$78,435 to $90,000 per year.

The position is also eligible for UC Benefits.

The exact salary offered to a successful candidate will depend on factors including qualifications, experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, internal equity, and other organizational considerations.

The University notes that it is not typical for an individual to be offered compensation at or near the top of the posted range.

Is This a Visa Opportunity?

No.

The job description explicitly states:

This is not a visa opportunity.

International applicants should therefore carefully consider their existing authorization and eligibility to work in the United States before applying.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to submit:

A resume

A cover letter

Because the position emphasizes research, strategic thinking, civil society experience, communication, and professional judgment, applicants should ensure that their application materials clearly demonstrate these areas rather than simply listing general duties.

A strong application should make it easy for the hiring team to see the connection between the applicant’s background and the responsibilities of the Philanthropy Fellow position.

How to Strengthen Your Application

Candidates interested in this opportunity can consider emphasizing the following areas in their resume and cover letter:

Clearly explain your experience with civil society organizations, nonprofits, community organizations, social-impact initiatives, advocacy organizations, or related institutions.

TITLE: Nzalakanda-Noble Dabri Loic from the Republic of the Congo is OD Young Person of the Month – September 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Nzalakanda-Noble Dabri Loïc is a young social entrepreneur from the Republic of the Congo and Co-Founder of AquaPlay, an innovative platform using technology and gamification to transform environmental education and inspire action for ocean conservation. Driven by the belief that technology can do more than entertain, Loïc is working to make learning about marine ecosystems engaging, accessible and action-oriented, particularly for young people. Through AquaPlay, he is demonstrating how locally developed digital solutions can help build a new generation of environmentally conscious citizens.

Background and Work

Loïc’s work sits at the intersection of technology, youth engagement and environmental conservation. Growing up in the Republic of the Congo, a country rich in natural resources and home to coastal communities whose livelihoods are closely connected to the ocean, he became increasingly concerned about the limited understanding of marine biodiversity and environmental protection among many young people. At the same time, he observed how deeply technology, mobile devices and digital platforms were becoming embedded in the everyday lives of young people. Rather than seeing this growing digital engagement simply as a form of entertainment, Loïc began thinking about how technology could become a tool for education and social action. That thinking ultimately led to AquaPlay. AquaPlay transforms environmental education into an interactive experience. The platform combines learning with gamification to help users understand marine ecosystems while encouraging them to participate actively in protecting them. Through interactive challenges, marine species recognition activities, citizen reporting tools and a community platform, users can learn about biodiversity, identify environmental issues and become part of a wider community taking action for the ocean. At the centre of AquaPlay is a simple idea: environmental education becomes more powerful when people are not only told about a problem but are given practical and engaging ways to become part of the solution.

How It Started
The idea for AquaPlay grew from a question Loïc kept returning to:What if technology could be used not just to entertain young people, but to educate them and inspire environmental action? For Loïc, the disconnect between young people and environmental issues presented both a challenge and an opportunity. Although conversations around climate change, pollution and biodiversity are becoming increasingly visible globally, environmental information can sometimes feel distant from the everyday experiences of young people. Traditional approaches to environmental education may also struggle to compete with the interactive digital platforms that increasingly shape how young people communicate, learn and spend their time. Loïc wanted to bridge this gap. Together with his co-founder, he began developing AquaPlay as a platform where environmental learning could become interactive, practical and enjoyable. Instead of positioning young people merely as recipients of environmental information, AquaPlay encourages them to become learners, observers, reporters and active participants in protecting marine ecosystems.

Successes So Far
AquaPlay’s journey has already gained recognition within both the innovation and environmental communities. The project won second place at the Ocean Hackathon in Pointe-Noire, an innovation event bringing together participants to develop solutions to challenges facing the ocean. For Loïc and the AquaPlay team, the recognition provided important validation that a technology-driven approach to marine education and conservation could offer a meaningful response to environmental challenges. AquaPlay reached another major milestone when it was selected among the 12 global finalists of the Opportunity Desk Impact Challenge 2025. Being recognised on a global platform strengthened Loïc’s conviction that solutions developed by young African innovators can respond to local challenges while carrying relevance far beyond their immediate communities. But for Loïc, awards are not the ultimate measure of success. What matters most is AquaPlay’s potential to help young people see themselves differently: not simply as people inheriting environmental problems, but as individuals capable of contributing to their solutions. Each young person who learns about a marine species, reports an environmental concern, participates in a challenge or becomes more conscious of their relationship with nature represents another step towards the future AquaPlay is working to create.

Challenges and How They Were Faced
Building AquaPlay has not been without challenges. Like many young African innovators and social entrepreneurs, Loïc and his team have had to navigate limited funding opportunities, technical constraints and access to resources while attempting to develop an ambitious technology-based solution. There have been periods when progress has been slower than anticipated and when limited resources have required the team to rethink how they develop and grow the platform. Rather than allowing these constraints to stop the project, Loïc has tried to approach them as part of the innovation process. The experience has taught him the importance of persistence, adaptability and continuing to build even when ideal conditions do not exist. Each challenge has pushed the AquaPlay team to think differently about what is possible with the resources available to them. For Loïc, being a young innovator in Africa means learning to create within constraints while refusing to allow those constraints to define the scale of one’s ambition.

Plans for the Future
Loïc’s vision extends far beyond building a digital platform. His dream is to contribute to a generation of young Africans who understand the importance of biodiversity, recognise their responsibility towards the environment and have the knowledge and tools to develop solutions of their own. Through AquaPlay, he hopes to expand access to engaging environmental education while strengthening the connection between technology, citizen participation and conservation. The long-term ambition is to build a platform capable of reaching more young people and communities, deepening understanding of marine ecosystems and encouraging everyday environmental action. Loïc also sees enormous potential in placing young Africans at the centre of environmental innovation. Across the continent, young people are increasingly using technology to respond to challenges in education, healthcare, agriculture, finance and civic participation. He believes environmental protection should be part of that same innovation movement. Ultimately, AquaPlay is working towards a future where learning about the environment does not stop with awareness, but leads to participation and action. For Loïc, the journey is one learner, one community and one action at a time.

Words of Advice for Young Changemakers
Loïc’s journey is a reminder to young changemakers that meaningful ideas often begin with paying close attention to the problems around them. Do not assume that solutions must come from somewhere else. Look at the challenges within your own community and ask what you can contribute with the skills, technology and resources available to you. Challenges will come, particularly when building something new with limited resources.

TITLE: EBRD Internship 2026 in Brussels: Apply for a 6-Month Intern Position in Corporate Strategy

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is inviting applications for an Intern position based in Brussels, Belgium, offering an opportunity for qualified graduates and early-career professionals to gain practical experience within an international financial institution. The six-month internship is situated within the Corporate Strategy Division and will involve work related to European Union policies and initiatives, institutional communications, policy engagement, events, meetings, research, and coordination.

This EBRD internship provides an opportunity for an individual with an academic degree and some professional working experience to contribute to the work of the Bank’s EU Representative Office while developing professional experience in an international and multicultural environment.

The position may be particularly relevant to candidates interested in European Union affairs, international development, public policy, international organisations, communications, sustainability, finance, and institutional relations.

Overview of the EBRD Internship Opportunity

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is recruiting an Intern to support its team in Brussels. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of the Principal Manager and contribute to a range of policy, communication, event, meeting, administrative, and coordination activities.

According to the vacancy announcement, the internship has a duration of six months and is based in Brussels, Belgium.

Key Opportunity Details

Organisation: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD)

Position: Intern

Division: Corporate Strategy

Location: Brussels, Belgium

Office Country: Belgium

Office City: Brussels

Contract Type: Internship

Contract Length: 6 months

Requisition ID: 37050

Posting Date: 11 September 2026

Application Deadline: 25 September 2026

The vacancy is designed for an individual who can support the Brussels-based team across policy engagement, communications, events, meetings, outreach, and coordination activities.

About the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is an international financial institution that works across regions in which it invests. The organisation describes its approach as agile and innovative and highlights the opportunity for employees to work with experts from a wide range of professional sectors.

Working at the EBRD can expose interns and other employees to professionals operating across areas including finance, public policy, international development, government, the private sector, and institutional relations.

The organisation also places emphasis on values including:

Inclusiveness

Innovation

Trust

Responsibility

These values are reflected in workplace behaviours that include listening and speaking up, collaborating, acting decisively, and simplifying processes to increase impact.

For an intern interested in international organisations and development-related work, the environment can provide exposure to how an international financial institution interacts with policymakers, institutions, stakeholders, and other organisations.

Purpose of the EBRD Brussels Internship

The primary purpose of the position is to provide support to the Brussels team across several areas of work.

The intern will work under the supervision of the Principal Manager and assist with activities connected to EU policies and initiatives, communications, policy engagement, outreach, events, meetings, administration, and project coordination.

Because the role combines policy and communication responsibilities, applicants may benefit from having an interest in both the institutional and public-facing aspects of international development work.

The position can therefore provide practical exposure to how policy developments are monitored, analysed, communicated, and incorporated into institutional engagement.

Key Responsibilities of the EBRD Intern

The selected candidate will be expected to support the team in several areas.

1. Supporting Analysis of EU Policies and Initiatives

One of the key responsibilities will involve supporting the analysis of and engagement with European Union policies and initiatives.

This means the intern will contribute to the team’s understanding of relevant EU developments and help support engagement around policies and initiatives that may be relevant to the EBRD’s work.

This responsibility could provide valuable exposure to EU policymaking and the relationship between international financial institutions and European institutions.

2. Supporting Communication Activities

The intern will also support internal and external communication activities aimed at raising the profile of the EBRD and its EU Representative Office.

Communication responsibilities may involve helping the team communicate its activities, priorities, engagements, and work to relevant audiences.

This part of the position may be particularly relevant to graduates and early-career professionals with an interest in corporate communications, public affairs, institutional communications, digital communication, or international development communication.

3. Attending Relevant Events

The intern will have the opportunity to attend relevant events and report back to management.

This responsibility can provide exposure to professional events involving policymakers, institutions, development organisations, financial-sector stakeholders, and other relevant actors.

The ability to observe discussions, identify important developments, and communicate key information clearly will therefore be useful in this role.

4. Participating in Meetings

The intern may participate in internal and external meetings where appropriate.

This provides an opportunity to observe and contribute to professional discussions and gain insight into how an international organisation coordinates its work and engages with external stakeholders.

5. Supporting Policy Engagement and Communication Outreach

Another important component of the internship involves supporting the team with both policy engagement and communication outreach.

This combines two closely connected areas: understanding and engaging with policy developments while also helping communicate the organisation’s work and priorities.

Candidates who are comfortable researching information, preparing written materials, communicating professionally, and working with different stakeholders may find these responsibilities particularly relevant.

6. Administrative and Coordination Support

The intern will also provide occasional administrative and coordination support for other project activities.

Although these tasks may be secondary to the policy and communication responsibilities, they can be important for ensuring that projects and team activities are organised effectively.

Strong organisational skills, attention to detail, reliability, and the ability to manage changing priorities can therefore be valuable.

Academic and Professional Qualifications

The EBRD states that applicants should have a degree with some professional working experience.

The vacancy does not specify a single academic discipline in the information provided. Consequently, candidates from different educational backgrounds may potentially be relevant, particularly where their studies and experience align with the responsibilities of the role.

Relevant academic or professional interests may include areas such as:

European studies

International relations

International development

Public policy

Political science

Economics

Finance

Communications

Corporate communications

Public affairs

Development studies

Business

International organisations

Applicants should carefully review the official vacancy requirements before applying to determine whether their specific academic and professional background meets the employer’s criteria.

Professional Experience

The vacancy requires candidates to have some professional working experience.

The EBRD further notes that experience engaging with EU institutions or international organisations is a plus.

This means previous experience in these environments can strengthen an applicant’s relevance to the role, although the vacancy presents such experience as an advantage rather than as the stated core qualification.

Experience gained through employment, internships, professional assignments, project work, or other relevant professional settings may help demonstrate an applicant’s ability to operate in a structured organisational environment.

Candidates should focus their application materials on experiences that demonstrate their ability to:

Conduct research and analysis

Understand policy developments

Communicate professionally

Work with different stakeholders

Prepare or present information

Support events and meetings

Manage multiple tasks

Coordinate activities

Work independently

Adapt to changing priorities

Language Requirements

Fluency in English is required for the position.

Knowledge of French is an advantage.

Because the role is located in Brussels and involves engagement connected to EU institutions and initiatives, language capabilities can be particularly useful when communicating in a multicultural and international environment.

Applicants should clearly demonstrate their English-language proficiency and indicate any additional relevant language abilities in their application where appropriate.

Knowledge of EU Institutions and Development Policy

The EBRD is looking for candidates with knowledge of EU institutions and an understanding of development policy.

This requirement is particularly relevant because a substantial part of the internship involves supporting the team’s engagement with EU policies and initiatives.

Applicants should therefore be familiar with the role and functions of relevant EU institutions and have an understanding of broader development-policy issues.

A strong application should demonstrate genuine interest in the policy environment in which the EBRD operates rather than simply listing academic qualifications.

Ability to Work Independently

The successful candidate should be able to work independently while also understanding when it is appropriate to seek advice.

This is an important professional skill in an international organisation where interns may be given individual assignments while also working as part of a wider team.

Applicants can demonstrate this capability through examples of situations where they have:

Managed assignments independently

Met deadlines without constant supervision

Taken initiative on projects

Identified when additional guidance was needed

Communicated challenges promptly

Worked responsibly with confidential or important information

Ability to Work in a Multicultural Environment

The EBRD operates as an international organisation with employees and stakeholders from different professional, cultural, and national backgrounds.

The vacancy therefore requires candidates to be able to operate effectively in a multicultural environment with changing priorities.

Adaptability, cultural awareness, communication skills, collaboration, professionalism, and openness to different perspectives can all be valuable in such an environment.

Applicants should consider highlighting experiences that demonstrate their ability to collaborate with people from different backgrounds and adapt when priorities change.

What the EBRD Offers as a Workplace

The EBRD describes its workplace as providing varied, stimulating, and engaging work.

Employees can interact with experts working across the financial, political, public, and private sectors in the regions where the Bank operates.

This type of professional exposure can allow interns to understand how different sectors interact in the context of international development and investment.

The organisation also highlights several aspects of its working environment.

International and Diverse Professional Environment

The EBRD states that it embraces inclusion and celebrates diversity.

Its workforce includes people with different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. According to the organisation, this diversity contributes fresh ideas, energy, and innovation to its work.

For an intern, working in such an environment can provide an opportunity to develop cross-cultural communication and collaboration skills.

Hybrid Workplace

The EBRD describes its workplace as a hybrid environment, providing flexibility to teams and individuals.

The organisation says its approach is based on trust, flexibility, and connectedness.

Applicants should nevertheless review the official vacancy and any applicable employment information for the specific working arrangements associated with this internship.

Sustainability and Digital Transformation

The organisation states that sustainability, equality, and digital transformation are central elements of its environment.

These themes are increasingly important across international development and financial institutions, making exposure to them potentially valuable for candidates building careers in related fields.

Employee Wellbeing

The EBRD also states that its workplace prioritises employee wellbeing and provides a comprehensive suite of competitive benefits.

Specific benefits applicable to an intern should be confirmed from the official employment terms and vacancy information.

Diversity and Inclusion at the EBRD

Diversity is identified by the EBRD as one of its core values.

The organisation states that it seeks to ensure that people are treated with respect, given equal opportunities, and able to work in an inclusive environment.

The vacancy specifically encourages qualified candidates who are nationals of EBRD member countries to apply regardless of racial, ethnic, religious, or cultural background, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, socioeconomic background, or disability.

This is an important point for prospective applicants because eligibility is linked to nationality within the EBRD member-country framework.

Candidates should therefore verify that their nationality meets the EBRD’s applicable eligibility requirements before submitting an application.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This internship may be relevant to graduates and early-career professionals who have an academic degree and some professional working experience and who are interested in areas such as:

European Union affairs

International development

International organisations

Public policy

Development policy

Corporate strategy

Institutional relations

Public affairs

Strategic communications

International finance

Sustainability

Government and stakeholder engagement

Candidates who have previously engaged with EU institutions or international organisations may have particularly relevant experience because the EBRD identifies this background as an advantage.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should ensure that their application clearly connects their education and professional experience to the responsibilities described in the vacancy.

A strong application can demonstrate:

Academic preparation – Clearly state your degree and explain how your academic background relates to the position.

Professional experience – Highlight relevant professional experience rather than simply listing previous positions.

EU knowledge – Demonstrate your understanding of EU institutions, policies, and initiatives.

Development-policy awareness – Show familiarity with development-related issues and explain your interest in the field.

Communication skills – Provide evidence of experience supporting internal or external communications.

Research and analytical skills – Highlight assignments where you researched, analysed, summarised, or presented information.

International experience – If applicable, mention experience working with international organisations, EU institutions, multinational teams, or multicultural stakeholders.

Adaptability – Demonstrate that you can manage changing priorities while maintaining the quality of your work.

Independent working ability – Give examples of projects or assignments that you successfully handled with limited supervision.

Language skills – Clearly indicate your English proficiency and any French-language skills.

Important Dates

The EBRD published the vacancy on 11 September 2026.

The stated application deadline is 25 September 2026.

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and should not wait until the final day if they already have the necessary documents prepared.

Application Process

Interested candidates should apply through the official EBRD careers platform and review the complete vacancy details before submitting their application.

The official vacancy should be used to confirm all current requirements, application instructions, and any information concerning the recruitment process.

The EBRD also notes that because it receives a high volume of applications, it is unable to provide detailed feedback to candidates who are not shortlisted for further consideration.

An internship within an international financial institution can provide practical exposure to the relationship between policy, development, finance, communications, and institutional engagement.

For someone seeking a career in international organisations, public policy, European affairs, development, communications, or related fields, the responsibilities outlined in this vacancy provide exposure to several professional functions within one role.

The Brussels location is also significant because the city is a major centre for European institutional and policy activity. Working within the EBRD’s EU Representative Office can therefore place the intern in an environment where EU policy engagement and international development intersect.

The EBRD Intern position in Brussels offers a six-month opportunity for a qualified graduate or early-career professional to gain practical experience within the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development’s Corporate Strategy Division.
