TITLE: Africa Fundraising Incubator (AFI) Program 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: August 14, 2026

Applications are open for the Africa Fundraising Incubator (AFI) Program 2026. The Africa Fundraising Incubator – AFI (previously called the Africa Impact Fundraising Grant – AIFG) is a multi-stage capacity-building program designed by the New Africa Fund (NAF) to equip African organizations with the practical skills, resources, and institutional support needed to build sustainable funding pipelines, broaden their reach, and deepen their impact.

The program consists of the following:

Online Training: Selected organizations will receive specialized training in the foundational skills needed to run successful small-donor fundraising campaigns.

30-Day Challenge Month: Participants will put their new skills into practice by launching live fundraising campaigns, with the opportunity to receive up to $5,000 in matching funds from the New Africa Fund.

Fiscal Sponsorship: To reduce administrative barriers, all participating organizations will receive 12 months of free fiscal sponsorship.

In-Person Training in Kigali, Rwanda: Top-performing organizations will be invited to an all-expenses-paid, week-long, in-person boot camp focused on strengthening their fundraising and leadership skills. This training includes sessions in financial management, marketing, communications, grant writing, donor research, cultivation and retention, individual donor campaigns, and local fundraising strategies.

Benefits

Selected organizations will receive foundational training on individual donor campaigns.

Selected organizations will participate in a 30-day fundraising challenge, with up to $5,000 USD in matching funds available.

All participating organizations will receive 12 months of free fiscal sponsorship from the New Africa Fund, with the possibility of extension.

Top-performing organizations will be invited to a week-long intensive workshop in Kigali to deepen their fundraising expertise.

Additional performance-based fundraising opportunities will be provided as the program develops.

Eligibility

Only organizations registered in one of the 54 African Union member states are eligible to apply.

Application

Before you apply make sure you have collected the following documents to upload as PDFs:

Organization’s Registration Document

Most recent external audit. If no audit is available upload five months financial statements for all accounts.

Click here to apply

For more information, visit AFI Program.

TITLE: Chevening British Library Coptic Collections Fellowship 2027 (Funded)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: October 27, 2026

Applications are open for the Chevening British Library Coptic Collections Fellowship 2027. The Chevening British Library Coptic Collections Fellowship is co-funded by the British Library and the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. It is open to applications from mid-career professionals from Egypt, Palestine, and Sudan, who have a strong interest in Coptic manuscript heritage and cultural collections.

The British Library holds one of the world’s most significant collections of Coptic manuscripts, comprising hundreds of complete and fragmentary codices, as well as papyrus, parchment, and paper fragments documenting more than 1,500 years of Coptic history, theology, and literary culture. This internationally important collection provides unique insights into the history of Christianity, Egypt’s cultural heritage, manuscript production, and scholarly traditions.

The fellowship will take place at the British Library, where you will work closely with Dr. Michael Erdman, Head of Asian and African Studies (interim) to lead a research project. You will use your language skills, subject expertise, and professional experience to survey the British Library’s Coptic holdings, enhance catalogue records, investigate collection provenance, and develop new opportunities for public and community engagement.

Benefits

Each fellowship includes:

12-month period of project-based activity at the British Library

Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship

Return economy airfare

Allowance package for fellowship-related activities

Up to £1,000 for approved project-related expenses

Eligibility

Be citizens of Egypt, Sudan, or Palestine. Applicants should normally be resident in one of these countries, however citizens of these countries who are resident elsewhere in the Middle East and North Africa region in Chevening eligible, ODA-eligible countries (Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Syria, Tunisia, Yemen) may also apply. Applicants must demonstrate a clear intention to return to and contribute to their country of citizenship following the fellowship and must return there for at least one year after the fellowship ends.

Have a postgraduate level qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant area) at the time of application.

Have significant professional and/or academic research experience (at least five years).

Be currently employed or enrolled as a PhD candidate (your PhD must not be with a UK/EU or USA university).

Have excellent knowledge of Coptic (Sahidic or Bohairic), with knowledge of Arabic and/or Greek desirable.

Have good written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate research findings effectively.

Have experience of cataloguing and handling manuscript collections, with knowledge of manuscript description standards.

Have experience of provenance research and documentation, or a demonstrable interest in this area.

Have experience of working with heritage communities or delivering engagement activities related to cultural heritage collections.

Application

Applications are open until 27 October 2026, at 12:00 (UTC). The duration of this fellowship is 12 months.

Click here to apply

For more information, visit Chevening British Library Coptic Collections Fellowship.

TITLE: EMA Traineeship Programme 2027 in Amsterdam: Apply for Paid 10-Month Placements With a €2,049.77 Monthly Stipend

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Apply for the European Medicines Agency Traineeship Programme 2027 in Amsterdam. Explore eight placements, eligibility requirements, the €2,049.77 monthly stipend, application process and September 2026 deadline.

Applications are open for the European Medicines Agency Traineeship Programme, offering recent graduates and eligible university students an opportunity to complete a paid, ten-month placement at the Agency’s headquarters in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

The current opportunities cover pharmaceutical regulation, public health, law, information science, veterinary digital services, paediatric medicine safety, artificial intelligence, financial data analytics and process automation. Successful applicants will join the Agency on March 1, 2027, and remain in the programme until December 31, 2027.

EMA offers a monthly stipend of €2,049.77 for a full-time placement, a contribution toward travel costs when joining the Agency, professional mentorship, structured development activities and access to a multidisciplinary European working environment.

The deadline for all eight currently advertised placements is September 30, 2026, at 23:59 Central European Summer Time. Late applications will not be accepted.

EMA Traineeship Programme 2027 at a Glance

Programme detail
Information

Host organization
European Medicines Agency

Location
Amsterdam, the Netherlands

Current intake
March 1, 2027

End date
December 31, 2027

Duration
10 months

Full-time schedule
40 hours per week

Part-time options
80% or 50% when combined with qualifying university studies

Monthly stipend
€2,049.77 for full-time participation

Travel support
Contribution toward travel costs when joining EMA

Working arrangement
Office-based in Amsterdam with limited hybrid working

Current placements
Eight

Application deadline
September 30, 2026, at 23:59 CEST

Remote assessments
Mid-October to mid-November 2026

Decisions and offers
By the end of December 2026

Required English level
At least C1

Second-language requirement
At least B2 in another official EU language

Application method
Online through the EMA Careers Portal

About the European Medicines Agency

The European Medicines Agency is a decentralised agency of the European Union. It began operating in 1995 and is based in Amsterdam.

EMA is responsible for the scientific evaluation, supervision and safety monitoring of medicines within the European Union. It works with national regulatory authorities and scientific experts to ensure that medicines available in the European market are safe, effective and of appropriate quality.

The Agency’s responsibilities extend across human and veterinary medicines. Its work includes medicine development, scientific assessment, pharmacovigilance, regulatory guidance, public-health communication, access to information, legal support, innovation and the digitalisation of regulatory processes.

The traineeship programme allows eligible young professionals to understand how a major European public-health organization operates while contributing to practical projects under professional supervision.

Purpose of the EMA Traineeship Programme

The programme is designed primarily as a structured learning and professional-development experience. Trainees complete tasks that increase their technical knowledge, practical skills and understanding of the Agency’s work.

EMA welcomes young professionals because they can bring new perspectives, current academic knowledge and innovative ideas. In return, trainees receive practical exposure to the European medicines regulatory system and experience working in a multicultural EU institution.

The wider EMA traineeship programme covers areas such as:

Medicine regulation.

Life sciences.

Healthcare.

Chemistry.

Information technology.

Pharmaceutical law.

Human resources.

Finance.

Communications.

Public relations.

Data analysis.

Process improvement.

Artificial intelligence.

Stakeholder engagement.

Scientific information management.

Not every field is necessarily available during every application cycle. Candidates must apply for one of the placements listed on the live EMA Careers Portal.

What EMA Offers Successful Trainees

Ten-Month Placement in Amsterdam

The current intake will run from March 1 to December 31, 2027. EMA’s wider programme may also offer a separate October-to-July cycle, depending on the vacancies advertised.

The current placements are based at the Agency’s premises in Amsterdam. They should not be treated as fully remote opportunities.

Monthly Stipend

A full-time trainee will receive a monthly stipend of €2,049.77.

The amount is reduced proportionately for approved 80% or 50% part-time arrangements. EMA does not describe this stipend as a permanent employee salary, and applicants should consult the programme rules for any applicable administrative or financial conditions.

Travel Contribution

EMA provides a contribution toward travel expenses when the trainee joins the Agency. The programme page does not promise that every relocation or travel expense will be covered in full.

Full-Time and Part-Time Arrangements

A standard full-time traineeship involves 40 hours of work per week.

Part-time participation at 80% or 50% may be available when the placement is combined with eligible university studies, such as Erasmus+, a similar academic programme or doctoral studies. Applicants should confirm the permitted arrangement in the particular vacancy notice.

Hybrid Working

The current vacancies state that trainees may work remotely for up to 40% of their working time from within the Netherlands. Occasional teleworking from outside the Netherlands may also be permitted.

This arrangement does not convert the programme into an international remote placement. Trainees are expected to be based in the Netherlands and attend the Agency’s Amsterdam premises.

Individual Mentorship

Each trainee is assigned a mentor who is responsible for:

Helping establish individual learning objectives.

Supervising the trainee’s work.

Monitoring progress regularly.

Providing professional guidance.

Supporting the trainee throughout the programme.

Career and Professional Development

Trainees can benefit from:

Workshops and structured learning activities.

Meetings connected to the Agency’s work.

Information about EMA’s mission, functions and regulatory responsibilities.

Agency-wide competency-development opportunities.

Career reflection and professional guidance.

Exposure to experienced specialists.

Practical experience in an international and multidisciplinary environment.

What EMA Expects From Trainees

EMA expects applicants and selected trainees to demonstrate:

An open-minded approach to working in a multicultural setting.

Genuine interest in the Agency’s working methods.

Willingness to contribute new ideas and perspectives.

A proactive and responsible attitude.

Ability to work cooperatively with colleagues.

Curiosity and willingness to learn.

Strong professional communication.

Adaptability.

Research and analytical ability.

Commitment to personal learning and development.

The vacancy notices consistently identify communication, interpersonal ability, teamwork, adaptability, research, analysis and continuous learning as important behavioural competencies.

General Eligibility Requirements

Candidates must satisfy all general requirements and the academic conditions of their chosen placement.

Nationality Requirement

Applicants must enjoy full rights as citizens of:

A European Union Member State; or

Iceland;

Liechtenstein; or

Norway.

Nationality is a mandatory condition. Merely living, studying or working in an eligible country does not replace the citizenship requirement.

Academic Status Requirement

A candidate must fall into at least one of the following groups:

Recent university graduate

For the current vacancies, the applicant must have completed a relevant university degree of at least three years between September 30, 2025, and September 30, 2026.

Erasmus+ or similar university-programme student

The applicant may be completing a placement as part of Erasmus+ or another comparable academic programme.

Master’s student

A current master’s student can apply if they have already fully completed an earlier relevant university degree.

PhD student

A current doctoral student may apply when their education is relevant to the chosen placement.

The required field of study varies considerably among the eight available tracks. Candidates should not assume that possession of any university degree makes them eligible for every placement.

Language Requirements

Applicants must have:

A thorough command of English at a minimum of CEFR level C1.

Good knowledge of another official European Union language at a minimum of CEFR level B2.

C1 English generally means that the candidate can understand complex professional and academic material, communicate fluently and produce well-structured written work. B2 in a second official EU language indicates an independent working knowledge of that language.

Documentary Evidence

Candidates must be ready to provide evidence of nationality and academic eligibility in the application and during the interview stage.

Required evidence may include:

A passport or national identity document.

University degree certificates.

Academic records.

Evidence of graduation dates.

Erasmus+ or similar programme documentation.

Proof of current master’s or doctoral enrolment.

Translations of academic documents where required.

Failure to provide satisfactory evidence may result in disqualification.

Eight EMA Traineeship Placements Open for the March 2027 Intake

As of August 28, 2026, the EMA Careers Portal lists eight active traineeship opportunities. All have the same deadline, programme period, stipend and general nationality and language requirements, but their academic requirements and project responsibilities differ.

1. Supporting Stakeholder Engagement and Medicines Health Information

Selection reference: EMA/TR/11533

Department: Public and Stakeholders Engagement Department

Relevant degrees: Biomedical sciences, pharmacy, medicine, public health or social sciences

This placement focuses on improving stakeholder-engagement processes and examining how public enquiries are handled across the European medicines regulatory network.

EMA works with patients, consumers, healthcare professionals, academic institutions and the pharmaceutical industry. The selected trainee will help the Agency organize, collect and communicate information about these engagement activities more effectively.

Principal activities include:

Developing a standardized data-collection template.

Identifying the minimum information needed for stakeholder-engagement reporting.

Proposing a more efficient process for collecting information across EMA offices.

Examining possible digital tools for information collection.

Recommending a shorter, clearer and more structured reporting format.

Incorporating suitable visual elements into reports.

Surveying relevant authorities in the EU regulatory network.

Studying communication channels, workflows, response times, query categories and enquiry volumes.

Comparing practices across EU Member States.

Identifying examples of effective public-enquiry management.

Examining how enquiries move between EMA and national authorities.

Identifying inefficiencies or opportunities for better coordination.

Assessing potential uses of digital tools and artificial intelligence.

Preparing practical recommendations.

The placement can build experience in stakeholder engagement, survey design, qualitative analysis, professional communication, process mapping and multinational regulatory cooperation.

Desirable skills include project management, communications, stakeholder engagement, process improvement, analysis, organization and strong written English.

View the official stakeholder-engagement placement.

2. Analysis of EU Strategic and Legal Provisions Promoting Pharmaceutical Innovation

Selection reference: EMA/TR/11542

Department: Regulatory Science and Innovation Task Force

Relevant degrees: Biomedical sciences or medicine

The successful trainee will prepare a review of existing and forthcoming European legislation, regulations and strategies related to innovation in medicine development and regulation.

The project aims to identify European initiatives concerning innovation and competitiveness and assess how they can be translated into tangible, sustainable and meaningful regulatory outcomes.

The trainee will have opportunities to:

Examine existing and proposed EU legislation.

Review European strategies connected to pharmaceutical innovation.

Study initiatives affecting medicine development and competitiveness.

Engage with the European Medicines Regulatory Network and specialist experts.

Learn how EMA supports developers during the early stages of medicine development.

Understand key stages in medicine development.

Develop knowledge of regulatory science.

Examine evolving methods and technologies for evidence generation.

Strengthen scientific writing and presentation skills.

Translate complex legal, scientific and policy information into an accessible review report.

Competitive applicants should be able to demonstrate experience or ability in:

Scientific writing.

Literature reviews.

Policy analysis.

Analytical work.

Data visualization.

Synthesis of complex scientific or legal information.

Clear professional communication.

View the official pharmaceutical-innovation placement.

3. EMA Legal Department

Selection reference: EMA/TR/11532

Department: Legal Department

Relevant degree: Law

This placement provides broad exposure to the work of EMA’s Legal Department and its three principal areas:

Pharmaceutical Law and Support to Core Business.

Litigation.

General Affairs and Anti-Fraud.

The selected trainee may support projects involving general pharmaceutical legislation, requests for public access to documents, European Ombudsman enquiries, litigation and other legal matters affecting the Agency.

Possible responsibilities include:

Supporting Legal Administrators.

Attending relevant meetings.

Researching legislation and case law.

Preparing reports and legal notes.

Assisting with access-to-document matters.

Supporting litigation-related work.

Contributing to responses involving the European Ombudsman.

Examining legal issues connected to EMA’s regulatory responsibilities.

Communicating with internal stakeholders.

The placement is intended to improve the trainee’s knowledge of the legal framework governing EMA, legal research methods, internal procedures and professional legal communication.

Additional strengths include:

Knowledge of EU law.

Knowledge of EU pharmaceutical law.

Relevant academic, professional or previous placement experience.

Ability to draft formal documents in English.

View the official Legal Department placement.

4. Information Centre and EMA’s Public-Health Knowledge Base

Selection reference: EMA/TR/11539

Department: Information Centre

Relevant degree: Library and Information Science or a comparable discipline

This placement examines how scientific publishing and information-retrieval practices are changing and what those changes mean for access to medical, scientific and public-health information.

The trainee will explore emerging information tools, including artificial-intelligence-enabled solutions, that may help EMA staff discover, understand and use scientific literature more efficiently.

The project also involves supporting the visibility and strategic development of EMA’s Information Centre.

Activities and learning areas include:

Analysing changes in scientific publishing.

Exploring new publication formats and discovery platforms.

Reviewing AI-enabled literature-search and information tools.

Improving digital scientific literacy.

Supporting the implementation of the Information Centre’s strategy.

Communicating library and knowledge services to EMA staff.

Increasing internal engagement with the Information Centre.

Working with electronic databases and online subscriptions.

Learning about information-resource management software.

Developing knowledge-management skills.

Supporting collection management and cataloguing.

Conducting literature searches.

Assisting with document delivery.

Delivering live presentations.

Providing customer-oriented information services.

This track is particularly relevant to applicants interested in medical librarianship, information management, scientific literature and digital knowledge services.

View the official Information Centre placement.

5. Mobile Application for Veterinary Electronic Leaflets

Selection reference: EMA/TR/11543

Department: Veterinary Regulatory Affairs and Referrals Office

Relevant degrees: STEM, computer science, data science or a related field

EMA’s Union Product Database contains validated information about veterinary medicines authorized across the EU and EEA. Its public portal provides official information about authorized veterinary medicines in the EU’s official languages.

This project explores the development of a mobile application that could make electronic veterinary-medicine package leaflets accessible to veterinary professionals and members of the public.

The trainee’s responsibilities may include:

Gathering and consolidating source information.

Identifying the needs of different users.

Supporting the design of the application.

Developing technical components with EMA colleagues.

Testing usability with sample users.

Working with project stakeholders.

Presenting findings and progress.

Preparing project handover documentation.

Considering accessibility, transparency and consistency across EU and EEA countries.

Candidates can gain experience at the intersection of animal health, veterinary medicine regulation, public information and digital-product development.

Useful technical experience includes:

JavaScript or TypeScript.

Swift.

Kotlin.

Dart.

Flutter.

React Native.

Application programming interfaces.

Software development kits.

View the official veterinary mobile-application placement.

6. Development of Medicines for Children and Paediatric Pharmacovigilance

Selection reference: EMA/TR/11538

Department: Paediatric Medicines Office

Relevant degrees: Medicine, pharmacy or life sciences

Medicines used by children require careful safety monitoring during development and after authorization. Developers of new medicines must prepare Paediatric Investigation Plans explaining how their products will be researched and developed for children.

The selected trainee will support a project examining safety monitoring for paediatric medicines and how regulatory safety measures have changed over time.

Key tasks include:

Reviewing ongoing safety-monitoring procedures for medicines used by children.

Comparing historical and current safety measures.

Identifying trends and gaps.

Highlighting opportunities to strengthen paediatric pharmacovigilance.

Contributing to work supporting the assessment of Paediatric Investigation Plans.

Summarizing findings for internal discussions.

Supporting future regulatory improvements.

Contributing toward a possible scientific paper for a peer-reviewed journal.

The trainee can develop knowledge and experience in:

EU pharmacovigilance requirements.

Paediatric medicines regulation.

Medicine safety monitoring.

Risk-management approaches.

The full lifecycle of paediatric medicines.

Regulatory and scientific data analysis.

Evidence-based regulatory decision-making.

Medicine development for different paediatric age groups, including neonates.

Scientific and regulatory writing.

Familiarity with EU pharmacovigilance or paediatric regulatory frameworks, excellent written and spoken English, and strong analytical ability will strengthen an application.

View the official paediatric-medicines placement.

7. Leveraging Administration for Automation, AI and Digitisation

Selection reference: EMA/TR/11582

Department: Leveraging Administration for Automation, AI and Digitisation Office

Relevant degree: A university degree of at least three years meeting the current graduation or study requirements

This placement is connected to the Administration Division’s digitalisation working group. The trainee will contribute to an AI-driven project intended to simplify and improve administrative workflows.

The particular AI solution may be finalized during project planning, but the selected trainee is expected to participate throughout the development and implementation process.

Responsibilities include:

Supporting project planning and coordination.

Helping design, test and introduce an AI solution.

Gathering business requirements.

Converting operational needs into appropriate technical requirements.

Working with administrative and multidisciplinary teams.

Supporting data preparation.

Participating in model evaluation.

Monitoring solution performance.

Promoting effective adoption of the selected tool.

Recording project outcomes and lessons learned.

Preparing recommendations for future AI and automation projects.

Communicating technical progress to non-technical stakeholders.

The placement can provide experience in:

AI use cases in public administration.

Workflow automation.

User stories and acceptance criteria.

AI project lifecycles.

Testing and implementation.

Large language model-based assistants.

Bots and automation platforms.

AI documentation and governance.

Communicating technological benefits and limitations.

Applicants should have relevant knowledge of Python, including data cleaning, visualization and validation. The notice specifically refers to Pandas, NumPy, Plotly, Pydantic and regular expressions. Knowledge of Power BI is desirable.

View the official automation, AI and digitisation placement.

8. Data Analytics and Process Automation

Selection reference: EMA/TR/11545

Department: Financial Management Office

Relevant degree: A university degree of at least three years meeting the current graduation or study requirements

This placement focuses on converting raw financial information into useful insights and improving financial processes through analysis, visualization and automation.

EMA’s Financial Management Office uses data to support transparent administration, statutory reporting and informed decision-making. It is also seeking to reduce repetitive manual tasks through digital process improvement.

Principal responsibilities include:

Collecting financial data from multiple sources.

Structuring and analysing data.

Developing reports and visualizations.

Creating dashboards, including through Power BI.

Producing information for managers and decision-makers.

Supporting statutory reporting requirements.

Reviewing existing financial processes.

Identifying opportunities for improvement.

Designing and implementing automation solutions.

Using Power Automate and comparable digital tools.

Working with finance and procurement specialists.

Collaborating with data and process-improvement colleagues.

The selected trainee can develop experience in EU-agency financial management, data structuring, analytical reporting, dashboard design and process automation.

Applicants should ideally demonstrate:

Basic knowledge of data-analysis tools.

Basic knowledge of data-visualization tools.

Analytical and problem-solving ability.

Communication skills.

Teamwork.

View the official financial data and process-automation placement.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the official EMA Careers Portal.

Step 1: Review All Current Placements

Visit the EMA vacancies page and identify the placement that best matches your degree, academic background and technical skills.

Do not apply based only on the general programme description. Every vacancy contains specific degree and competency requirements.

Step 2: Create an EMA Candidate Profile

Applicants can create a candidate profile before selecting a vacancy. The profile can be used to pre-fill future applications and monitor application progress.

Step 3: Complete the Online Application

Select the relevant placement and complete every required part of the application form. Pay particular attention to the eligibility and pre-screening questions.

A negative response to a mandatory eligibility question may prevent the application from progressing.

Step 4: Substantiate Pre-Screening Answers

Candidates should describe relevant education, knowledge, projects and experience when answering pre-screening questions, even if the same information appears elsewhere in the application.

The selection team may evaluate the application primarily through these responses. Applicants should not assume that reviewers will infer eligibility from a CV or another section.

Step 5: Tailor the Application

The description of skills and motivation should be directly connected to the selected placement.

For example:

A legal applicant should emphasize EU law, pharmaceutical law, legal research and English drafting.

A public-health applicant should highlight stakeholder engagement, surveys, communication and process improvement.

A technical applicant should identify relevant programming languages, frameworks, APIs, automation platforms and data tools.

A life-sciences applicant should explain relevant knowledge of pharmacovigilance, medicine development or regulatory science.

An information-science applicant should discuss databases, literature searches, cataloguing and knowledge-management tools.

Step 6: Check Character Limits

EMA advises candidates to answer concisely and respect all character limits. Long but unfocused answers can be less effective than brief responses that directly demonstrate the required evidence.

Step 7: Proofread the Application

Review grammar, spelling, dates, degree information and language claims before submission.

Academic dates are especially important because the recent-graduate pathway applies only to degrees obtained within the specified period.

Step 8: Submit Before the Deadline

Candidates may update information in their application until the closing time. However, EMA cannot accept applications submitted after the deadline.

Applicants should submit early enough to manage possible technical problems.

Application Deadline

The deadline for all eight current placements is:

September 30, 2026, at 23:59 CEST

The deadline is stated in Central European Summer Time, not the applicant’s local time. Candidates applying from another time zone should convert the deadline carefully and submit well in advance.

What Happens After Submission?

Initial Application Assessment

EMA assesses applications against the eligibility requirements and placement-specific criteria. The general programme page states that this stage can take approximately two to three weeks.

Remote Assessment Period

For the March 2027 intake, remote assessments are expected to take place between mid-October and mid-November 2026.

Interview and Possible Written Test

Candidates whose profiles most closely match a placement may be invited to a short remote interview with the hiring manager.

Applicants may also be required to complete a written or other relevant assessment.

Documentary Verification

Shortlisted candidates must be able to prove their nationality, degree, graduation date and academic status. Missing or inconsistent documentation can result in disqualification.

Decisions and Offers

EMA expects to issue decisions and offers by the end of December 2026.

Successful candidates will receive a traineeship contract confirming the March 1, 2027 starting date and applicable programme conditions.

Practical Tips for a Strong EMA Application

Select the right placement

Apply where your academic background and technical knowledge closely match the published requirements.

Treat eligibility questions as decisive

Verify nationality, graduation dates, degree duration and language levels before beginning.

Use evidence rather than general claims

Instead of saying that you have analytical skills, describe a research project, data analysis, policy review, legal assignment or technical product that demonstrates those skills.

Connect your motivation to EMA’s work

Explain why medicine regulation, public or animal health, regulatory science, digitalization or EU administration interests you.

Address every placement-specific skill

Use the vacancy notice as a checklist and provide relevant evidence for as many requirements as possible.

Do not exaggerate language or technical proficiency

Candidates may be tested or questioned about the claims in their applications.

Prepare documentation early

Obtain degree certificates, enrolment evidence, identity documents and translations before the interview stage.

Prepare for a competency-based interview

Be ready to explain how you have demonstrated communication, teamwork, adaptability, analysis, research and learning ability.

Monitor email and spam folders

EMA communicates with candidates by email. Missing an assessment or interview invitation could end the application.

Use only the official portal

EMA states that it does not charge candidates to participate in recruitment or traineeship selection. Applicants should not pay intermediaries or respond to requests for money.

Official Application Link

Applications must be submitted through the EMA Careers vacancies portal.

Candidates should also read the official EMA traineeship overview before applying.

For recruitment-related questions, EMA lists the following contact details:

Email: recruitment@ema.europa.eu

Telephone: +31 (0)88 781 6000

Address: Domenico Scarlattilaan 6, 1083 HS Amsterdam, the Netherlands

Conclusion

The European Medicines Agency Traineeship Programme provides eligible graduates and university students with a valuable opportunity to gain practical experience inside an important European public-health and medicines-regulation institution.

The current March 2027 intake includes eight diverse placements spanning stakeholder engagement, pharmaceutical innovation, law, scientific information, veterinary application development, paediatric pharmacovigilance, artificial intelligence and financial data automation.

Successful trainees will receive a monthly full-time stipend of €2,049.77, a travel contribution, professional mentorship, structured learning opportunities and experience working in an international EU environment.

Eligibility is strict. Candidates must hold an eligible nationality, satisfy the relevant academic-status requirement, possess the required degree for their selected placement and demonstrate C1 English plus B2 knowledge of another official EU language.

Applications must be completed through the official EMA Careers Portal by September 30, 2026, at 23:59 CEST. Candidates should apply early, provide detailed evidence in the pre-screening questions and ensure that every eligibility claim can be supported with official documents.

TITLE: Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development 2027 at AUC: Graduate Diploma Tuition Funding in Public Policy and Public Administration

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The American University in Cairo is inviting eligible graduate applicants to consider the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development, commonly abbreviated as SFID. Designed for academically strong students, the opportunity provides substantial tuition and fee support for graduate-diploma study in public policy or public administration at AUC. The credits completed through either diploma can also count toward the university’s Master of Public Policy or Master of Public Administration degree.

This makes the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development at AUC particularly relevant to applicants who want advanced training in public policy, governance, public administration, institutional development, or related public-service fields. In addition to academic study, recipients undertake a structured weekly work commitment with AUC’s Public Policy HUB, connecting their coursework with policy research and practical engagement.

The fellowship is not open to every international applicant. AUC limits eligibility to Egyptian nationals and certain refugees residing in Egypt. Applicants must also meet the university’s graduate admission requirements and demonstrate an excellent academic record. Prospective candidates should therefore check both their nationality or refugee eligibility and their academic readiness before beginning the two-part application process.

Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development at a Glance

Detail
Information

Host institution
The American University in Cairo, Egypt

Official name
Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development (SFID)

Supported study
Graduate Diploma in Public Policy or Graduate Diploma in Public Administration

Future academic pathway
Diploma credits can count toward an MPP or MPA at AUC

Duration
Two semesters, subject to a satisfactory review after the first semester

Tuition coverage
Up to nine credits per semester

Additional covered fees
Student services and activities fees; medical service and health insurance fees

Study status
Full-time enrollment is required

Academic standard while funded
Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.2

Practical commitment
At least 12 working hours each week with the Public Policy HUB

Next application deadline
November 2, 2026, for the Spring 2027 fellowship cycle

Official information
AUC Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development page

What Is the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development?

The Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development is an AUC graduate funding opportunity for new students with excellent academic performance. Its central purpose is to cover the credit hours required for an eligible graduate diploma in public policy or public administration. AUC explains that the same credits can subsequently count toward the Master of Public Policy or Master of Public Administration, allowing the diploma to function as a meaningful step toward a related master’s degree rather than as an isolated short course.

The structure combines three important elements:

Graduate-level academic training: Recipients enroll full-time in one of the two approved graduate-diploma programs.

Financial support: The award covers tuition for a maximum of nine credits per semester and several mandatory university and health-related fees.

Applied policy experience: Fellows contribute at least 12 working hours per week to AUC’s Public Policy HUB.

The Public Policy HUB was created within AUC’s School of Global Affairs and Public Policy to help develop, test, refine, and communicate responses to public-policy challenges. It brings policy scholars and mentors together with emerging policy analysts and supports the production of policy research and briefs. Consequently, the weekly work requirement is a substantive part of the experience rather than a purely administrative condition. It can expose fellows to the process of turning policy ideas into structured analysis intended for policymakers and the wider public. More information about this initiative is available on the official Public Policy HUB page.

Eligible Graduate Programs and Degree Pathways

The fellowship is tied specifically to full-time study in one of the following AUC programs:

Graduate Diploma in Public Policy

Graduate Diploma in Public Administration

Applicants should not assume that the award can be transferred to an unrelated graduate program. The official fellowship terms identify only these two diploma routes.

An important feature is the relationship between the diplomas and AUC’s related master’s degrees. Credits earned while completing the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy can count toward the Master of Public Policy, while credits from the Graduate Diploma in Public Administration can count toward the Master of Public Administration. This arrangement may benefit candidates who want to build graduate credentials progressively, beginning with a diploma and later continuing toward a master’s degree.

However, fellowship coverage is limited to the stated two-semester award and the eligible diploma credit hours. The fact that credits can count toward a later master’s degree does not mean that the fellowship automatically finances the remainder of an MPP or MPA. Applicants planning to continue should separately investigate the academic transition requirements, remaining degree credits, future tuition, and any other funding opportunities.

Financial Coverage and Benefits

AUC lists the following costs as covered by the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development:

Tuition fees for up to nine credits per semester. Across the stated two-semester duration, this represents coverage of as many as 18 credits in total, provided the recipient remains eligible after the first-semester review.

Student services and activities fees. These are university fees connected with the services and activities available to enrolled students.

Medical service and health insurance fees. The award covers the health-related fees specifically named in the official terms.

The phrase “full coverage” on the AUC fellowship page refers to the credit hours needed to complete the eligible graduate diploma, within the maximum of nine funded credits per semester. Applicants should read that wording together with the detailed award list. The official page does not list a living allowance, monthly stipend, accommodation, meals, books, equipment, local transportation, visa costs, relocation expenses, or international travel as covered benefits. Candidates should not budget on the assumption that these unlisted costs will be paid.

This distinction matters. The award offers strong academic-cost support, but it should not be described as an all-expenses-paid package unless AUC later publishes additional coverage in an individual award letter or updated terms. Applicants should prepare a personal budget for any expenses not expressly included and seek written clarification from AUC when necessary.

Fellowship Duration and Continuation Conditions

The award lasts for two semesters. Continued funding for the second semester is not unconditional: AUC reviews the fellow’s academic performance after the first semester and requires satisfactory progress.

To retain the award, a recipient must maintain a minimum GPA of 3.2. This academic threshold should be treated as an ongoing condition, not simply an entry qualification. A fellow whose performance falls below the stated minimum may risk losing continued support.

Recipients must also remain full-time students in the approved public policy or public administration graduate-diploma program and complete the required Public Policy HUB work. Because the academic and work obligations run together, candidates should assess whether they can realistically manage a full-time graduate course load alongside at least 12 working hours every week.

Who Can Apply?

The official eligibility rules identify two nationality or status groups:

Egyptian nationals

Refugees residing in Egypt who are Yemeni, Palestinian, Syrian, or Sudanese applicants

The wording is specific. It does not announce eligibility for all nationalities, all refugees, all residents of Egypt, or all applicants from Africa or the Middle East. A refugee applicant must both reside in Egypt and fall within one of the four nationality groups named by AUC.

The fellowship is intended for new graduate degree-seeking students who satisfy AUC’s full graduate admission requirements. AUC also refers to continuing students in the context of retaining the award and maintaining the required GPA. Prospective applicants should therefore understand the primary applicant profile as a new graduate student seeking admission, while the continuation rule governs recipients after the award begins.

Academic and Admission Qualifications

Fellowship eligibility and admission to AUC are connected but distinct. A candidate must be admissible to the relevant graduate program, and an admission offer does not by itself guarantee fellowship selection.

At university level, AUC states that graduate applicants must hold an accredited bachelor’s degree and have an academic record sufficient for full or provisional admission. A specific department may impose additional or higher standards. Credentials must be submitted in English; documents issued in another language must be accompanied by an official English translation.

For master’s and graduate-diploma admission consideration, AUC’s current general checklist includes:

A completed online graduate application.

Payment of the application fee online.

Selection of up to two graduate programs for admission processing.

A statement of purpose of approximately 500 words for each program selected, explaining the applicant’s interest, relevant skills or experience, and long-term academic and professional objectives.

An updated curriculum vitae showing education and any work experience.

At least two online recommendation letters from people familiar with the applicant’s academic or professional background.

Official academic records, including the final detailed bachelor’s transcript and proof that the degree was completed. Depending on the case, an enrollment certificate or an equivalency certificate from Egypt’s Supreme Council of Universities may also be requested.

Satisfactory English-language proficiency results. AUC notes that accepted tests can include the TOEFL iBT, Academic IELTS, and specified Cambridge English examinations, while individual programs may require higher scores.

A clear valid national identity card for Egyptian applicants, or the information pages of a passport for international applicants and Egyptian dual nationals.

One recent passport-size photograph in electronic form.

Any additional requirements imposed by the selected program or requested for an individual case.

Applicants should use the official AUC graduate admissions page as the controlling source for the complete and most current checklist. They should also review the selected diploma’s program-specific requirements before submission. A strong academic record is particularly important because the fellowship description expressly targets new graduate students with excellent academic performance.

Responsibilities of Selected Fellows

Receiving the award creates continuing obligations. According to AUC, every fellow must:

Enroll full-time in the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy or Graduate Diploma in Public Administration.

Maintain a GPA of at least 3.2.

Complete a minimum of 12 working hours per week with the Public Policy HUB.

Respond to reporting requests from AUC by the deadlines communicated by the university.

Supply requested materials that may include photographs or information about academic progress for reporting purposes.

Attend fellowship meetings or events when requested by the relevant university units.

Candidates should consider these conditions before applying. The 12-hour weekly commitment is substantial, particularly when combined with full-time graduate study. It may provide valuable policy experience, but it also requires dependable scheduling, professional conduct, timely communication, and consistent academic performance.

Application Deadline for Spring and Fall 2027

The nearest published deadline is for the Spring 2027 fellowship cycle:

Application opens: October 7, 2026

Application deadline: November 2, 2026

AUC also publishes two application cycles for Fall 2027:

Cycle 1 opens: December 22, 2026

Cycle 1 deadline: January 17, 2027

Cycle 2 opens: April 6, 2027

Cycle 2 deadline: May 6, 2027

These dates come from AUC’s fellowship deadline page, which was last updated on August 23, 2026. Applicants should recheck the official AUC fellowship deadlines immediately before submitting because universities may revise application calendars.

The dates above concern the fellowship application cycle. Because AUC requires applicants to submit a graduate admission application as well as a fellowship application, candidates must also comply with any admission deadline applicable to their intended semester. Do not assume that finishing one form automatically completes the other process.

How to Apply for the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development

AUC describes a two-step application process. Both steps are essential.

Step 1: Submit the AUC Graduate Admission Application

Review the university’s graduate admission instructions and prepare the required documents. Then create an account or sign in through the AUC online application portal. Select the appropriate degree-seeking graduate-diploma program in public policy or public administration and complete every required section.

Before submission, confirm that:

The name and personal information on the application match the applicant’s official identity documents.

Academic transcripts and proof of degree completion meet AUC’s official-document rules.

Any document not issued in English has the required official translation.

The statement of purpose is tailored to the selected program.

Recommenders have enough time to submit their letters.

English-proficiency results will remain valid through the first day of registered classes, as required by AUC.

Step 2: Submit the Online Fellowship Application

After addressing the graduate admission process, complete the separate fellowship application through the link provided on the official SFID listing. AUC’s fellowship button currently directs users to its Banner portal.

Applicants should save confirmation pages or emails for both submissions. If the portals request different information, complete each form independently rather than assuming information transfers automatically between systems.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

The official page does not publish a detailed scoring rubric, so no applicant can guarantee selection. Nevertheless, candidates can present a clearer and more credible application by focusing on the qualities directly relevant to the fellowship’s stated design.

1. Demonstrate academic excellence with evidence

The fellowship specifically targets applicants with excellent academic records. Use the CV, transcripts, statement of purpose, and recommendations to show consistent achievement, analytical ability, research experience, strong writing, or other evidence of readiness for graduate study.

2. Explain why the chosen diploma fits the applicant’s goals

A generic statement is less useful than a focused explanation of why public policy or public administration is the appropriate field. Applicants should connect previous education, professional experience, volunteer work, research interests, or public-service ambitions to the diploma they select.

3. Show a credible interest in inclusive development

Candidates can explain the social or policy challenges they hope to understand and address. The strongest discussion will be specific, grounded in experience, and connected to realistic academic and professional goals rather than relying on broad claims.

4. Address readiness for the Public Policy HUB commitment

Because fellows must complete at least 12 working hours per week with the HUB, applicants should be ready to describe relevant strengths such as policy research, writing, data analysis, stakeholder engagement, communication, teamwork, or project coordination. They should also consider how they will balance this commitment with full-time study.

5. Choose recommenders strategically

The general graduate checklist requires at least two recommendations. Suitable referees should know the applicant’s academic or professional work well enough to give concrete examples of performance, judgment, reliability, and potential for advanced study.

6. Start before the application window closes

Official transcripts, English-language testing, translations, and recommendation letters can take time. Applicants should prepare these materials in advance and avoid treating the final day as the target submission date.

Important Clarifications Before Applying

Does the award fund a complete master’s degree?

The fellowship provides full coverage for the credit hours needed for the eligible graduate diploma, up to nine credits per semester for two semesters. Diploma credits may count toward an MPP or MPA, but AUC does not state that this award covers the remaining requirements of either master’s degree.

Is the fellowship open to applicants living outside Egypt?

The official eligibility statement includes Egyptian nationals and refugees residing in Egypt from Yemen, Palestine, Syria, and Sudan. Refugee applicants should therefore not assume eligibility if they live outside Egypt.

Can a refugee of any nationality apply?

Not according to the published criteria. AUC expressly names Yemeni, Palestinian, Syrian, and Sudanese applicants among refugees residing in Egypt.

Is a monthly stipend included?

AUC’s published award list does not mention a stipend or living allowance. The listed support consists of eligible tuition, student services and activities fees, and medical service and health insurance fees.

Is the award automatically renewed for the second semester?

No. The two-semester duration is subject to review after the first semester for satisfactory academic performance, and fellows must maintain at least a 3.2 GPA.

Is admission to AUC the same as receiving the fellowship?

No. Candidates must complete the graduate admission application and the separate fellowship application. Admission eligibility is a requirement, while fellowship selection is a distinct funding decision.

Where can applicants ask questions?

AUC directs fellowship inquiries to gradserv@aucegypt.edu. Questions about unusual residency documentation, refugee status evidence, program-specific admission requirements, or unlisted expenses should be sent to AUC before the deadline.

Final Application Checklist

Before submitting, candidates should confirm that they have:

Verified that they fall within one of the published nationality or refugee-status groups.

Selected the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy or Graduate Diploma in Public Administration.

Reviewed AUC’s general and program-specific graduate admission requirements.

Prepared an official bachelor’s transcript and proof of degree completion.

Arranged an official English translation for any credential not issued in English.

Prepared a focused statement of purpose of about 500 words for each selected program.

Updated their CV.

Requested at least two recommendation letters.

Confirmed the applicable English-proficiency requirements and test validity.

Completed the graduate admission application.

Completed the separate fellowship application.

Submitted both processes before their respective deadlines.

Planned for a full-time course load and at least 12 Public Policy HUB working hours each week.

Understood the minimum 3.2 GPA continuation requirement.

Budgeted for expenses not identified in the official award coverage.

Conclusion

The Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development at the American University in Cairo offers a focused route into graduate-level public policy or public administration study for academically excellent, eligible applicants. Its combination of tuition support, university fee coverage, health-related fee coverage, and practical work with the Public Policy HUB can help recipients develop both academic knowledge and applied policy experience.

Applicants should approach the opportunity with a precise understanding of its scope. The award supports up to nine credits per semester for two semesters, requires full-time diploma enrollment, demands at least 12 hours of HUB work each week, and depends on maintaining a minimum 3.2 GPA. It is restricted to Egyptian nationals and specified refugee groups residing in Egypt, and it requires both an AUC graduate admission application and a separate fellowship application.

For the Spring 2027 cycle, the fellowship application deadline is November 2, 2026. Prospective candidates should begin collecting academic records, recommendations, English-language evidence, and identity or residency documents well before the portal opens. All applicants should verify the current instructions and dates on AUC’s official website before submitting.

TITLE: TEEEM Foundation Community Impact Grant Program 2026: Apply for $5,000–$30,000 Grants for Nonprofits and Charitable Organizations Worldwide

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are officially open for the TEEEM Foundation Community Impact Grant Program 2026, a new international funding opportunity supporting nonprofit and charitable organizations that are creating sustainable, measurable and community-driven solutions.

The TEEEM Foundation is seeking organizations whose work improves lives and strengthens communities through areas such as education, youth development, health, essential needs, equality, empowerment, entrepreneurship, economic opportunity and community infrastructure. The Foundation emphasizes projects that are developed with communities rather than simply for them, and that demonstrate a credible path toward lasting impact.

Grant awards are generally available across three funding ranges:

$5,000–$10,000 for local and grassroots community initiatives.

$10,000–$20,000 for organizations seeking to expand successful programmes and increase their impact.

$20,000–$30,000 for larger or more transformational initiatives with the potential for sustained community change.

Organizations may request amounts outside these typical ranges, although the Foundation notes that awards can be funded either fully or partially depending on available resources and programme priorities.

The 2026 application period runs from 17 August to 1 November 2026.

Application deadline: 1 November 2026.

The official application document indicates that eligible applicants may include U.S. 501(c)(3) organizations as well as international NGOs, registered charities and organizations holding equivalent nonprofit documentation, reinforcing the programme’s stated global orientation.

About the TEEEM Foundation Community Impact Grant Program

TEEEM stands for the Empathy Equality Entrepreneurship Mission. The Foundation describes its grantmaking approach as an investment in organizations that combine empathy, equality, entrepreneurship, education and service with practical community-level action.

The Community Impact Grant Program is intended to support organizations that understand the communities they serve and are capable of developing solutions that are both responsive to immediate needs and sustainable over time.

This means TEEEM is not simply looking for projects that distribute resources once and end when the grant is exhausted. The Foundation places particular value on organizations that can demonstrate:

Sustainable and measurable community impact

Strong leadership

Responsible financial stewardship

Community-centered design

Educational opportunities

Youth development

Entrepreneurial or innovative approaches

Alignment with TEEEM’s wider mission and values

The Foundation’s public guidance repeatedly emphasizes the importance of community ownership, measurable outcomes and long-term sustainability.

Who Is TEEEM Looking to Fund?

TEEEM is seeking nonprofit and charitable organizations that can demonstrate the ability to turn community needs into practical, accountable and lasting programmes.

A strong candidate is likely to be an organization that does more than identify a problem. It should be able to explain:

What the community actually needs.

How local people have been involved in defining that need.

What solution the organization proposes.

Why that organization is capable of implementing the solution.

What measurable outcomes will result.

How the work will continue or create longer-term value after the grant period.

The application specifically asks organizations to explain how community members participate in planning, implementation and decision-making, making community engagement a central feature rather than an optional addition.

Three Levels of Funding Available

TEEEM has structured the Community Impact Grant Program around three typical award levels.

1. Community Grants: $5,000–$10,000

Community Grants are intended to support:

Local projects and grassroots initiatives.

This tier may be appropriate for organizations implementing smaller-scale but clearly defined community programmes.

A strong proposal at this level might involve a focused project serving a particular:

Community

School population

Youth group

Village

Neighborhood

Underserved population

The grant amount should be proportionate to the project’s scale and expected outcomes.

2. Growth Grants: $10,000–$20,000

Growth Grants are designed to help organizations:

Expand successful programmes and increase community impact.

This tier is likely to be particularly relevant to organizations that have already tested an approach and can demonstrate evidence that it works.

Applicants might use a Growth Grant to:

Reach more beneficiaries

Expand into additional communities

Strengthen programme delivery

Increase organizational capacity connected directly to the project

Scale an existing successful intervention

The strongest applicants should be able to show why additional funding will translate into additional measurable impact.

3. Transformational Grants: $20,000–$30,000

Transformational Grants support larger initiatives with the potential for:

Long-term, sustainable change.

These awards are intended for comparatively ambitious projects.

Organizations seeking funding at this level should be prepared to demonstrate:

Strong organizational capacity

Clear governance

Appropriate financial controls

Experience managing meaningful programmes

A detailed project budget

Credible monitoring arrangements

A clear sustainability plan

The amount requested should match both the proposed activities and the organization’s demonstrated ability to deliver them.

Can You Request More or Less Than the Published Grant Ranges?

Yes.

TEEEM explicitly states that organizations requesting amounts outside the three standard funding ranges may still be considered.

Awards may also be funded:

In full, or

In part

depending on the Foundation’s available resources and programme priorities.

Applicants should therefore request an amount based on genuine project need rather than artificially adjusting a budget simply to fit neatly into one tier.

However, every cost should be clearly linked to:

Project delivery

Expected outcomes

Sustainability

Community impact

What Does the TEEEM Foundation Fund?

The Community Impact Grant Program identifies six broad areas of support.

Education and Youth Development

TEEEM supports initiatives that expand:

Educational access

Educational opportunity

Youth leadership

Youth development

This can make the programme relevant to organizations working with:

Schools

Students

Out-of-school youth

Underserved learners

Young leaders

Communities facing educational inequality

The Foundation’s own mission has a strong education and youth-development component, making this one of the central themes of the grant programme.

Health and Essential Needs

TEEEM also funds work addressing fundamental community needs.

The Foundation specifically identifies:

Food security

Basic needs

Medical care

Community health

as relevant areas.

Organizations may therefore be a good fit if they are addressing problems that directly affect community well-being and quality of life.

The application materials similarly identify priorities such as improving access to medical care and supporting food security.

Equality and Empowerment

Another major funding priority is:

Equality and empowerment.

TEEEM identifies programmes supporting:

Underserved populations

Female empowerment

Gender equity

as examples of relevant work.

Organizations applying in this area should explain how the project changes opportunities, access or outcomes for the communities involved.

Entrepreneurship and Economic Opportunity

Entrepreneurship is central to TEEEM’s identity.

The Foundation is interested in innovative programmes that:

Build skills

Strengthen livelihoods

Expand economic opportunities

Use entrepreneurial approaches to social challenges

This creates potential relevance for organizations working in:

Skills development

Livelihoods

Employment preparation

Small enterprise development

Youth entrepreneurship

Women’s economic empowerment

The proposal should nevertheless remain clearly connected to measurable community impact rather than focusing only on business development.

Community Infrastructure

TEEEM also considers projects that strengthen the physical and social foundations communities need to thrive.

Its application materials specifically mention infrastructure alongside other priority areas such as:

Education

Healthcare

Food security

Female empowerment

Youth development

Economic opportunity

Applicants proposing infrastructure-related work should explain how the infrastructure solves a demonstrated community need and how it will be maintained after construction or installation.

Sustainable Community Impact

The sixth broad theme cuts across all other priorities.

TEEEM is seeking:

Community-led solutions with measurable outcomes, responsible financial stewardship and potential for lasting change.

This means sustainability should appear throughout the application.

It should not be treated as an isolated paragraph added at the end.

Strong proposals should connect:

Need → project activities → measurable results → community ownership → long-term impact.

Priority Consideration

The complete grant application explains that priority may be given to organizations demonstrating several characteristics.

These include:

Sustainable, community-driven solutions

Long-term impact

Empowerment of underserved populations

Equitable access to opportunities and resources

Educational opportunities

Youth leadership

Innovative and entrepreneurial approaches

Economic opportunity

Food security

Healthcare access

Female empowerment

Community infrastructure

Meaningful local engagement

Financial accountability

Measurable results

The Foundation therefore appears to be looking not simply for charitable activity, but for organizations combining strong values with good programme design and operational capacity.

What Does “Community-Driven” Mean?

TEEEM repeatedly emphasizes that successful organizations should create solutions with communities, not simply for them.

In practice, this means a proposal should explain how local people are involved.

Community participation might appear through:

Identifying the problem

Designing the intervention

Setting priorities

Implementing activities

Providing feedback

Monitoring results

Making decisions

Maintaining the project afterward

An application that treats community members only as passive beneficiaries may be less aligned with the Foundation’s stated approach.

What Does TEEEM Mean by Sustainable Impact?

The application specifically asks:

How will the project continue after TEEEM Foundation funding has been utilized?

Applicants may discuss areas such as:

Future funding

Community ownership

Capacity building

Long-term operational sustainability

The Foundation therefore wants applicants to consider what happens after the grant ends.

A strong sustainability plan could show that the award will help establish something that continues through:

Local ownership

New partnerships

Earned revenue

Future fundraising

Institutional adoption

Training

Community capacity

The correct strategy will depend on the project.

How Applications Will Be Evaluated

TEEEM publicly identifies five major evaluation considerations:

Mission Alignment

Organizational Capacity

Community Need

Sustainability

Anticipated Impact

These criteria provide applicants with a useful framework for preparing a competitive submission.

Mission Alignment

Applicants should explain why their work aligns with TEEEM’s values of:

Empathy

Equality

Entrepreneurship

Education

Service

Meaningful social impact

The application includes a specific section asking applicants to explain this alignment.

Organizational Capacity

The Foundation wants confidence that the organization can deliver what it proposes.

Applicants are asked to describe capacity through factors such as:

Experience managing similar projects

Key staff

Previous successes

Community partnerships

Organizational strengths

A compelling idea without sufficient implementation capacity may therefore be weaker than a realistic project supported by a capable organization.

Community Need

Applicants must clearly identify the issue they want to address.

The grant application asks questions including:

Who is affected?

Why does the problem matter?

What evidence supports the need?

Why is action required now?

Strong applicants should use credible data where possible rather than relying only on broad statements.

Sustainability

Applicants should explain how the project will continue or create enduring value after TEEEM funding has been spent.

The Foundation specifically asks about future funding, community ownership and capacity building.

Anticipated Impact

Impact should be measurable.

TEEEM’s application asks applicants to identify outputs and, where possible, estimated numbers.

Examples in the form include:

Students served

Families impacted

Wells constructed

Meals provided

Training sessions conducted

Organizations should select indicators appropriate to their own project rather than simply copying these examples.

Long-Term Outcomes

The application also distinguishes immediate outputs from longer-term outcomes.

Examples of longer-term change identified in the application include:

Increased educational achievement

Improved health

Greater economic opportunity

Increased community capacity

Improved quality of life

Applicants should demonstrate a logical relationship between project activities and the outcomes they expect.

Measuring Success

Applicants must explain how success will actually be measured.

TEEEM asks organizations to identify:

Indicators

Evaluation methods

Reporting tools

This means a proposal should avoid claims such as:

“Our project will empower thousands of people”

without explaining how empowerment will be measured.

Instead, applicants should identify concrete evidence they can reasonably collect.

Organizational Information Required

The application asks for detailed organizational information, including:

Organization name

Address

Website

Countries of operation

Year founded

Primary and secondary contacts

Tax-exempt status

Registration information

Banking arrangements

The tax-status options specifically include:

501(c)(3)

International NGO

Registered charity

Other qualifying status

This confirms that the programme is not structured exclusively for U.S.-based charities.

Do International Organizations Need a U.S. Bank Account?

The application asks whether the organization has a U.S.-based bank account capable of receiving grant funds.

However, answering “No” does not automatically end the application.

How grant funds would be received and administered if awarded.

250–500 words.

Expected impact

Why the organization is uniquely positioned to implement the project

This is one of the most important sections of the application because it gives reviewers a concise overview of the entire proposal.

Organizational Overview

Description

Existing programmes

Volunteer base

Board governance

Project Description

Goals

Objectives

Major activities

Timeline

Estimated completion dates

A good project description should make it easy for reviewers to understand exactly what will happen if funding is awarded.

Risk Management

Applicants are also asked to identify:

Anticipated challenges

How those risks will be addressed

Acknowledging realistic risks does not necessarily weaken an application.

In many cases, it demonstrates stronger planning.

Project Budget

Organizations must provide:

Amount requested from TEEEM

Total project budget

Other secured or pending funding

Detailed budget categories

Expense descriptions

Amount requested per category

Budget narrative

The budget narrative should explain how expenditure contributes to both project success and sustainability.

Other Funding Sources

Secured

Pending

This allows the Foundation to understand the complete financing structure of the proposed project.

Required Application Documents

Completed Community Impact Grant Application

Board of Directors list

Current organizational budget

Project budget

Photos or other supporting materials, optional

Reporting Requirements for Successful Organizations

Grant recipients will be expected to demonstrate accountability throughout implementation.

Required deliverables include:

Final Impact Report

Financial updates on grant expenditure

Notification of significant changes to the funded project

The full application additionally asks selected organizations to commit to:

Mid-year reporting

Final reporting

Financial accountability

Project updates

Milestone
Date

This suggests a relatively fast review process between the application deadline and award announcement.

How to Apply

The application process consists of three broad steps.

Step 1: Download and Complete the Application

Applicants should first download the TEEEM Foundation Community Impact Grant Application from the Foundation website.

The document contains the complete:

Eligibility requirements

Project questions

Budget sections

Reporting commitments

Required attachments

Step 3: Submit the Complete Application

A single PDF whenever possible.

Applications should be submitted electronically to:

Michelle Della Fortuna
Vice President of Finance & Strategy
TEEEM Foundation
michelle@teeem.org

by 1 November 2026.

How to Make a Strong Application

1. Demonstrate a Real Community Need

Avoid vague claims.

Use:

Data

Local evidence

Community consultation

Existing service gaps

to show that the project addresses a genuine need.

2. Explain Community Ownership

TEEEM strongly emphasizes solutions created with communities.

Explain:

Who participated in project design

Who will participate in implementation

Who makes decisions

3. Use Measurable Outcomes

Do not promise only abstract change.

Identify numbers and indicators where appropriate.

For example:

Instead of:

“Improve educational opportunity.”

Explain:

Number of students reached

Attendance changes

Skills gained

Completion rates

Learning outcomes

4. Connect the Budget to Outcomes

Every major expense should answer the question:

How does this expenditure help achieve the proposed impact?

A clear budget increases confidence in the organization’s financial stewardship.

5. Show Sustainability

Additional fundraising

Partnerships

Training

Earned income

TITLE: UNDP Responsible Digital Transformation: Impact Assessments for AI & Data Governance Course 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 19, 2026

Applications are open for the UNDP Responsible Digital Transformation: Impact Assessments for AI & Data Governance Course 2026. UNDP is launching Responsible Digital Transformation: Impact Assessments for AI and Data Governance, a 4-week online course designed to help public-sector professionals translate responsible AI principles into practice.

As governments accelerate digital transformation, the use of AI and data-driven systems in public services is rapidly expanding. These technologies are reshaping service delivery while introducing new challenges around fairness, transparency, accountability, and inclusion.

This course equips policymakers and practitioners to move beyond general principles and awareness, and apply practical impact assessment tools to real governance decisions involving AI, digital public infrastructure and data-driven public services. Building on UNDP’s Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA) methodology, the course guides participants through a structured process to scope a use case, identify risks and impacts, and develop mitigation and governance recommendations.

By the end of the course, participants will have developed a draft impact assessment and mitigation plan for a real-world digital or AI governance use case relevant to their institutional contexts.

Costs

With the generous support of the Global Gateway strategy of the European Union, this course is free for selected participants.

Eligibility

Participants should have a basic understanding of digital systems and AI, and ideally two or more years of experience in digital policy/transformation, ICT, or governance, dealing with various governance frameworks for digital systems. Those who have a strong interest in applying practical risk assessment tools are particularly encouraged to apply.

Important additional requirements:

Applicants must hold an undergraduate degree in a relevant field or have a minimum of three years of experience in the above-mentioned areas if they do not hold a university degree.

Possess a fluent level of English.

Complete the application questionnaire, provide a motivation letter and attach an up-to-date CV.

Government officials and policymakers from developing countries, particularly women, are encouraged to apply.
