TITLE: Press Release- Strengthening Recruitment, Development and Retention of Faculty in the East African Community: Carnegie Corporation of New York Funds Research to Address Data and Intervention Gaps

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
For immediate release | 29th July 2021 | Download a Copy of the Press Release Here

The Demographics of African Faculty (DAF) consortium today announces that it has secured $390,000 of funding from Carnegie Corporation of New York for a two-year research project focusing on understanding and addressing ‘faculty challenges’. The financial commitment is to enable a detailed study of the challenges that higher education institutions (HEIs) in the East African Community (EAC) face, with respect to faculty to student ratios and the composition of faculty, which directly affect the quality of education in the region.

The DAF initiative was established in 2018, to systematically analyse the staffing challenges in sub-Saharan Africa. This involved using administrative data and policy norms to describe the current context and project the future supply of and demand for faculty. The consortium is comprised of the Association of African Universities (AAU), Education Sub Saharan Africa (ESSA) and the Population Reference Bureau (PRB). Using funding received from The Mastercard Foundation, the DAF consortium undertook a pilot research project (DAF I) in Ghana, West Africa, in partnership with Ghana’s National Commission for Tertiary Education [NCTE – now restructured and renamed the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC)].

In 2020, the DAF consortium expanded to include the Inter-University Council for East Africa (IUCEA), an inter-governmental agency. The aim was to seek funding to extend and scale up the pilot study in Ghana by undertaking a new study in the East African Community (EAC). It is this new research project in the EAC (i.e. DAF II), that Carnegie Corporation of New York has agreed to fund. The implementing partners for DAF Phase II are IUCEA, AAU, ESSA and PRB.

Through this new DAF II project, the partners aim to strengthen the ability of higher education stakeholders to plan and implement evidence-informed responses targeted at improving the numbers and nature of quality faculty within Higher Education Institutions in the EAC.

“We believe that quality higher education for students in all countries in sub-Saharan Africa can only be achieved if there are enough qualified and skilled faculty. To make this happen, adequate planning for recruitment, development and retention of faculty is essential.” said Lucy Heady, Chief Executive Officer at ESSA. “Having accurate data is crucial in this planning process. Staffing projections must be based on actual figures and solutions to the faculty crisis must be driven by evidence.”

This project builds on existing efforts to improve the recruitment pipeline for future academics in the EAC. The DAF consortium will provide data required to propel stakeholders to take urgent steps towards achieving effective and globally competitive higher education systems.

“Within the East African Community, there is lack of comprehensive and consolidated data and insights on faculty across the region, which makes it challenging to plan for effective regional solutions.”, said Professor Mike Kuria, Deputy Executive Secretary of IUCEA. “As the lead member for the research and analyses, IUCEA will work closely with all stakeholders to ensure that DAF II achieves maximum impact for the benefit of young people and educators in member states – Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Uganda, and the United Republic of Tanzania.”

As part of their broader focus, DAF partners will collect and analyse data on current challenges with faculty and establish a methodology to project future supply and demand for faculty in the region. Collaborating to increase awareness of the faculty challenges among stakeholders, to facilitate buy-in for faculty development-related initiatives, to inform policy, strategic planning and resource allocation will also be prioritised. Most importantly, the partners will work with higher education stakeholders to co-develop solutions and make evidence-informed policy recommendations.

“AAU’s participation in this project is to complement our efforts at the continental level towards ensuring the provision of the requisite human resources needed to achieve the African Union’s Vision of Agenda 2063 and other global goals.” said Professor Ehile, Secretary General, AAU. “Addressing systemic and data gaps in the broad higher education ecosystem to build a strong, resilient, and quality education system across African is even more critical in this era of the COVID-19 pandemic.”

The DAF II project will also benefit from ongoing research by some consortium members on the impact that the COVID-19 pandemic has had on higher education. The findings will enable policymakers, Higher Education Institution leaders, the public and other stakeholders to better understand how to manage threats to HEIs resulting from or exacerbated by the pandemic.

“PRB is honoured to be a member of the partnership and looks forward to drawing on our rich research and demographic expertise to ensure that the consortium’s analyses are conducted with transparency and rigor.” said Jeff Jordan, President and Chief Executive Officer, PRB.

Claudia Frittelli – a Program Officer for Higher Education and Research in Africa, a key part of the International Program at Carnegie Corporation of New York said, “This initiative demonstrates the criticality of regional collaboration and transparency to strengthen Africa’s higher education sector. We look forward to seeing evidence-informed solutions implemented within the East African Community by its higher education stakeholders.”.

Carnegie Corporation of New York (the philanthropic funder) and the implementing partners (IUCEA, AAU, ESSA and PRB) are committed to strengthening quality faculty supply in the EAC through this DAF II research project. We also call on all stakeholders to join forces with us towards achieving an even greater impact in the East African Community and beyond.

TITLE: MOVE Fund 2026: Apply for Two-Year Grants of $40,000–$150,000 for Sport and Youth Development Coalitions

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The MOVE Fund 2026 is inviting eligible coalitions and collectives working at the intersection of sport, play, youth development, equity, and community systems to participate in its 2026 funding opportunity. The fund is designed to support collaborative groups seeking to strengthen sport-based youth development, advocate for increased investment in sport and play, and help create local sports systems that are more equitable, positive, and inclusive.

Eligible coalitions and collaboratives can apply for two-year operating grants ranging from $40,000 to $150,000. The opportunity is particularly relevant for organizations and collaborative groups that are working to use sport and play as tools for youth development and broader community change.

Applications for the MOVE Fund 2026 opened on August 24, 2026, and eligible applicants must submit their applications by September 16, 2026.

In addition to the funding opportunity, the MOVE Fund is hosting a MOVE Fund 2026 Webinar on September 2, 2026, where prospective applicants can learn more about the fund and its priorities.

MOVE Fund 2026 Opportunity Details

Opportunity: MOVE Fund 2026

Category: Grant

Grant Type: Two-year operating grant

Grant Amount: $40,000 to $150,000

Application Opening Date: August 24, 2026

Application Deadline: September 16, 2026

Webinar Date: September 2, 2026

Webinar Time: 8:30 PM Nairobi time

Application Structure: One application per coalition or collective

Lead Applicant Requirement: The lead organization must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status

What Is the MOVE Fund?

The MOVE Fund is focused on supporting collaborative efforts that recognize the role that sport and play can play in youth development and community transformation.

Rather than focusing exclusively on individual sports organizations, the fund is intended to support coalitions and collectives working together around broader systems-level goals. These collaborations may bring together organizations, community groups, youth development organizations, advocates, and other stakeholders seeking to improve how sport and play are supported and delivered within their regions.

The fund’s priorities center on three major areas:

Advocating for public and private investment in sport and play

Building the capacity of sport-based youth development organizations

Creating equitable, positive, and inclusive local sports systems

This makes the opportunity potentially valuable for collaborative initiatives that want to move beyond individual programs and contribute to longer-term changes within their local or regional sports ecosystems.

What Will the MOVE Fund Support?

The MOVE Fund will support coalitions and collectives whose work aligns with its stated priorities. Applicants should demonstrate how their collaborative efforts contribute to strengthening sport and play as important tools for youth development and community development.

1. Advocacy for Investment in Sport and Play

One of the key priorities of the MOVE Fund is supporting coalitions that advocate for increased public and private investment in sport and play.

This may be particularly relevant to collaborative groups working to influence:

Government investment in sports infrastructure and programming

Private-sector investment in sport and youth initiatives

Funding for community-based sports programs

Policies that improve access to sport and play

Investment in youth-focused sports development

Greater recognition of sport and play as tools for positive youth development

Community-level or regional strategies for strengthening sports ecosystems

Coalitions involved in advocacy should be able to demonstrate how their collective efforts can contribute to stronger investment and support for sport and play.

2. Capacity Building for Sport-Based Youth Development Organizations

The MOVE Fund also seeks to support work that builds the capacity of sport-based youth development organizations.

Capacity building can involve strengthening the ability of organizations to design, implement, manage, evaluate, and sustain programs that use sport and play to support young people.

Collaboratives working in this area may focus on strengthening organizational systems, improving leadership, developing partnerships, enhancing program quality, or building the long-term sustainability of organizations serving young people through sport.

The emphasis on capacity building means that the opportunity is not necessarily limited to organizations delivering sports activities. It can also be relevant to collaborative efforts aimed at strengthening the organizations and systems behind youth sports development.

3. Building Equitable, Positive and Inclusive Local Sports Systems

A third major priority is supporting coalitions that work to create local sports systems that are equitable, positive, and inclusive.

This recognizes that access to sport and play can be influenced by factors such as resources, community infrastructure, organizational capacity, inclusion, and opportunities available to young people.

Coalitions applying to the MOVE Fund should therefore consider how their work contributes to creating sports environments where young people and communities can participate meaningfully and benefit from positive sporting experiences.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Successful applicants can receive two-year operating grants ranging from $40,000 to $150,000.

The operating-grant structure is important because it indicates that the funding is intended to help support the broader work of eligible coalitions and collectives rather than being limited to a narrowly defined one-time activity.

Depending on the approved grant amount and the needs of the collaborative, funding could provide important support for activities related to advocacy, capacity development, coalition coordination, systems strengthening, and other work aligned with the MOVE Fund’s priorities.

Applicants should carefully review the fund’s official guidance and application requirements before determining the appropriate funding request.

Who Can Apply for the MOVE Fund 2026?

The opportunity is specifically designed for coalitions and collectives/collaboratives whose work aligns with the MOVE Fund’s priorities.

Importantly, the fund states that coalitions or collaboratives at various stages of development are encouraged to apply, provided that their work aligns with the fund’s priorities.

This means that an applicant does not necessarily have to be an established, highly developed coalition to be considered. Emerging and developing collaborative efforts may also be encouraged to apply if they can demonstrate alignment with the fund’s objectives.

Lead Organization Requirement

Although the opportunity is designed around coalitions and collectives, the application must be submitted through one lead organization.

The lead organization must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status designation.

This is a key eligibility requirement that prospective applicants should consider before beginning the application process.

Coalitions that do not themselves have the required nonprofit status may therefore need to identify an eligible lead organization that can formally submit the application on behalf of the collaborative.

One Application Per Collaborative

Only one application per collaborative or collective can be submitted.

This means that members of the same coalition should coordinate internally before submitting an application.

A coalition should avoid having multiple participating organizations submit separate applications for the same collaborative effort. Instead, the coalition should agree on its lead organization and coordinate the submission as a single collective application.

This makes internal planning and communication particularly important.

This can be particularly relevant to emerging partnerships that have begun working together but may not yet have the institutional maturity of long-established networks.

How to Prepare a Strong MOVE Fund Application

TITLE: KAUST Scholarship 2027 in Saudi Arabia: Fully Funded Master’s and PhD Scholarship for International Students

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The KAUST Scholarship 2027 offers an exciting opportunity for international students seeking to pursue fully funded graduate studies at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) in Saudi Arabia. The scholarship is available for students applying to eligible Master’s and PhD degree programs beginning in Spring 2027. Designed to support talented students pursuing advanced study and research, the KAUST scholarship provides comprehensive financial assistance, including tuition coverage, a monthly living stipend, accommodation, medical and dental coverage, and relocation support for international students. Applications for the Spring 2027 intake are currently open, and prospective applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their documents well before the deadline.

Application deadline: September 27, 2026.

KAUST Scholarship 2027 Overview

The KAUST Scholarship provides international graduate students with the opportunity to study at a research-intensive university in Saudi Arabia while undertaking advanced work in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and related research areas.

Here are the key details:

University: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)

Location: Saudi Arabia

Study level: Master’s and PhD

Intake: Spring 2027

Duration: Approximately 2 years for Master’s programs and 3–4 years for doctoral programs

Funding: Fully funded

Tuition: Fully covered

Monthly stipend: Provided

Accommodation: On-campus housing provided

Medical coverage: Included

Dental coverage: Included

Relocation support: Available for international students

Eligible applicants: International students from around the world

Application deadline: September 27, 2026

Application method: Online

About King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) was established in 2009 and has developed into a major research-focused university in Saudi Arabia.

The university places a strong emphasis on scientific research, innovation, technology and graduate education. Its academic environment is particularly focused on research areas associated with science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

KAUST’s research-oriented model makes it an attractive destination for students interested in developing advanced technical knowledge and contributing to research addressing scientific and technological challenges.

The university has also received international recognition for its research output. According to the information provided for this opportunity, KAUST was ranked 19th globally in the 2016 Nature Index Rising Stars recognition of universities experiencing rapid growth in high-quality research output and scientific publications.

What Is the KAUST Scholarship 2027?

The KAUST Scholarship is a comprehensive financial support package associated with admission to eligible graduate programs at KAUST.

Rather than requiring students to independently secure separate funding for tuition and living costs, admitted students are automatically considered for the scholarship according to the information provided.

This means that qualified applicants who are admitted to an eligible program can receive substantial financial support throughout their studies.

The scholarship is intended to allow graduate students to focus on their education and research without carrying the typical financial burden associated with international graduate study.

Master’s Programs at KAUST

The scholarship is available to students pursuing eligible Master’s degree programs.

The expected duration for Master’s studies is approximately two years.

During this period, students can undertake graduate-level coursework and research while becoming part of KAUST’s international academic and research community.

Students interested in Master’s study should carefully examine the specific admission requirements of their intended program because meeting the general scholarship conditions does not replace the academic requirements for admission.

PhD Programs at KAUST

The opportunity is also available to students seeking doctoral study.

KAUST’s PhD programs are research-intensive and generally require approximately three to four years, depending on the program, research requirements and individual academic progress.

Doctoral students can use their time at KAUST to develop specialised expertise, conduct original research and contribute to scientific knowledge in their chosen area.

Prospective PhD applicants should pay particular attention to identifying an appropriate research direction and demonstrating their academic and research preparation in their application.

Available Fields and Majors

The KAUST Scholarship is available across the academic subjects and research areas offered by the university.

The institution has a strong focus on:

Science

Technology

Engineering

Mathematics

Scientific research

Advanced technological research

Related interdisciplinary fields

Because the scholarship is tied to admission to KAUST graduate programs, applicants should review the programs currently offered by the university and select a field that matches their academic background, research interests and career objectives.

Applicants should also ensure that their previous academic qualifications satisfy the entry requirements of the specific program they select.

Financial Benefits of the KAUST Scholarship

One of the most significant features of the KAUST Scholarship is its comprehensive funding package.

According to the information provided, successful students can receive the following benefits.

1. Full Tuition Fee Coverage

The scholarship covers the student’s tuition fees for the eligible graduate program.

This can significantly reduce the financial cost of obtaining a Master’s or PhD degree abroad.

2. Monthly Living Stipend

Students receive a monthly stipend intended to help cover living expenses while studying at KAUST.

The stipend allows students to concentrate more fully on their studies and research without having to finance their everyday expenses entirely from personal savings.

3. On-Campus Accommodation

The scholarship includes access to on-campus housing accommodation.

This is particularly useful for international students relocating to Saudi Arabia because it reduces the difficulty and expense associated with finding private accommodation after arrival.

4. Medical Coverage

The financial package includes medical coverage, providing students with access to healthcare support during their studies.

5. Dental Coverage

Dental coverage is also included as part of the scholarship’s comprehensive support package.

6. Relocation Support

International students may receive relocation support, helping them manage some of the costs and practical challenges associated with moving to Saudi Arabia for their studies.

Taken together, these benefits make the opportunity particularly attractive to students who would otherwise find the cost of international graduate education difficult to manage.

Duration of the KAUST Scholarship

The expected duration depends on the level of study.

Master’s degree

The Master’s scholarship support is generally provided for approximately:

2 years

PhD degree

Doctoral scholarship support is generally provided for approximately:

3–4 years

The actual period of study and funding may depend on the student’s program, academic progress and applicable university requirements.

KAUST Scholarship Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy the admission requirements for the Master’s or PhD program they intend to study.

The provided requirements include the following:

Applicants must meet the entry requirements for their selected graduate program.

International students from any country can apply.

Applicants should be seeking admission for the Spring 2027 intake.

Applicants must satisfy the applicable English-language requirements unless exempt.

Applicants must provide three letters of recommendation.

GRE scores are not mandatory, although they may strengthen an application when available.

Because admission requirements can differ between programs, applicants should not rely exclusively on the general scholarship requirements. They should also review the requirements for their chosen KAUST degree program.

English Language Requirements

English-language proficiency is an important part of the application.

The information provided lists the following minimum scores:

TOEFL iBT: 79

IELTS: 6.0

Applicants should make sure that their test results satisfy the university’s applicable requirements before submitting their application.

Who may be exempt from English-language test requirements?

According to the provided information, TOEFL or IELTS scores are not required if the applicant received their degree from an accredited institution in one of the following countries:

United States

Canada

United Kingdom

Ireland

Australia

New Zealand

Applicants should nevertheless verify their individual circumstances and the current requirements applicable to their program before submitting the application.

Letters of Recommendation

Applicants are required to submit three letters of recommendation.

Recommendation letters can provide admissions reviewers with independent evidence of an applicant’s academic ability, research potential, intellectual maturity and suitability for graduate-level study.

Applicants should therefore select recommenders who know their academic or research work well and can provide specific, meaningful assessments of their abilities.

Where possible, applicants should approach potential referees well in advance of the application deadline.

Is the GRE Required?

The GRE is not mandatory according to the information provided.

However, GRE scores may be considered advantageous if an applicant has them available.

Applicants should therefore avoid delaying their application solely because they have not taken the GRE, while also considering whether submitting a valid score could strengthen their particular application.

Required Documents for the KAUST Scholarship

Prospective applicants should prepare the required documentation before beginning or completing their online application.

The provided list includes:

Academic Transcript

Applicants should submit their academic transcript.

The transcript must be presented in English.

It should accurately demonstrate the applicant’s academic history and qualifications.

Degree Certificate

A degree certificate is also required and should be presented in English.

Applicants should make sure that their submitted documents clearly demonstrate completion of their previous degree.

IELTS or English-Language Test Result

Applicants who are required to demonstrate English proficiency should prepare a valid IELTS or TOEFL result according to the university’s requirements.

Applicants from non-English-speaking countries should pay particular attention to this requirement.

However, the provided information indicates that applicants who received their degree from accredited institutions in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand are exempt from submitting TOEFL or IELTS scores.

Three Recommendation Letters

Applicants must provide:

Three letters of recommendation.

These should ideally come from individuals who can provide credible information about the applicant’s academic and research capabilities.

Current CV or Resume

A current curriculum vitae or resume should be included.

The CV should present the applicant’s academic background, research experience, publications, projects, awards, professional experience and other relevant achievements.

Valid Passport

International applicants should provide a valid passport.

Applicants should check the validity of their passport before submitting their application, particularly because an international move may require sufficient passport validity for visa and travel arrangements.

Passport-Size Photograph

A current passport-size photograph is also listed among the required documents.

Research Articles

Research articles may be included if available.

For research-focused Master’s and PhD applicants, publications or other evidence of research experience can help demonstrate preparation for graduate-level study.

Automatic Scholarship Consideration for Admitted Students

A notable feature of the opportunity is that, according to the provided information, all admitted students automatically receive the scholarship.

This means applicants do not need to compete for a limited number of separate scholarship awards after admission in the manner common to many external funding programs.

Instead, the scholarship is associated with admission to the eligible graduate program.

This makes the academic admission application especially important. Applicants should therefore focus on presenting a strong overall application that demonstrates their academic qualifications, research potential and suitability for their chosen program.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The KAUST Scholarship may be particularly relevant to students who:

Want to pursue a Master’s degree in a research-focused environment.

Are interested in pursuing a PhD abroad.

Have strong academic qualifications.

Want to develop advanced expertise in science, technology, engineering or mathematics.

Are interested in scientific research and innovation.

Need comprehensive financial support for graduate education.

Are prepared to relocate to Saudi Arabia.

Have research interests compatible with KAUST’s academic programs.

Meet the English-language requirements or qualify for an exemption.

Can provide three strong recommendation letters.

Are preparing for the Spring 2027 intake.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Meeting the minimum requirements does not necessarily guarantee admission. Prospective applicants should use the application to demonstrate why they are a strong fit for their chosen program.

1. Choose the right program

Start by identifying the KAUST graduate program that best matches your previous degree, research interests and long-term goals.

Your academic background should make sense in relation to the program you select.

2. Research the academic environment

Applicants should investigate the university’s research areas and identify the areas that align most closely with their interests.

This can help candidates develop a more focused application.

3. Prepare your academic documents early

Do not wait until shortly before the deadline to request transcripts, degree certificates and recommendation letters.

International applicants may need additional time to obtain official documents or translations.

4. Prepare your CV carefully

Your CV should clearly communicate your academic and research achievements.

Where applicable, include:

Research projects

Publications

Conference participation

Academic awards

Research experience

Internships

Relevant employment

Technical skills

Laboratory experience

Academic achievements

5. Secure strong recommendation letters

Contact your referees early and provide them with enough information about the program and your academic goals.

This gives them an opportunity to prepare detailed and relevant recommendations.

6. Check your English-language status

Determine whether you need IELTS or TOEFL before submitting the application.

If you are required to provide a test score, make sure your result meets the stated minimum.

7. Apply before the deadline

Do not leave the application until the final day.

Technical issues, missing documents or problems uploading files can prevent an otherwise qualified applicant from completing the application successfully.

Application Deadline for KAUST Scholarship 2027

The stated deadline for the Spring 2027 KAUST Scholarship is:

September 27, 2026.

Prospective applicants should ensure that all required application components are completed and submitted before the stated deadline.

Since the deadline is approaching, applicants should begin gathering documents, contacting referees and reviewing program-specific admission requirements as early as possible.

How to Apply for the KAUST Scholarship 2027

The application process is conducted entirely online.

Applicants should begin by reviewing the available graduate programs and identifying the program that best fits their academic and research background.

The general process involves:

Review KAUST’s Master’s and PhD programs.

Select the degree and academic area that matches your interests.

Review the admission requirements for the selected program.

Prepare your academic transcripts and degree certificates.

Prepare your CV or resume.

Arrange three recommendation letters.

Prepare your valid passport and passport-size photograph.

Prepare an English-language test result if required.

Include research articles or other relevant research evidence if available.

Complete the online application.

Upload the required supporting documents.

Review the application carefully.

Submit the application before September 27, 2026.

Applicants should use the official KAUST application portal and consult the university’s current instructions for the latest program-specific requirements.

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before submitting an application, prospective students should keep several points in mind.

First, being an international applicant does not by itself guarantee admission. Candidates must still satisfy the admission requirements for their chosen Master’s or PhD program.

Second, the scholarship is described as being automatically awarded to admitted students, making the overall academic application extremely important.

Third, applicants should pay attention to English-language requirements. While the provided information lists TOEFL iBT 79 and IELTS 6.0 as minimum scores, certain applicants may be exempt based on where they obtained their previous degree.

Fourth, recommendation letters are a required component of the application. Candidates should not wait until the final days before contacting potential referees.

Finally, applicants should check all documents carefully before submission to ensure that the application is complete.

Frequently Asked Questions About the KAUST Scholarship 2027

Is the KAUST Scholarship fully funded?

Yes. The opportunity is described as a fully funded scholarship providing comprehensive financial support, including tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation, medical and dental coverage, and relocation support for international students.

Who can apply for the KAUST Scholarship?

International students from any country can apply, provided they meet the admission requirements for their selected Master’s or PhD program.

What degree levels are covered?

The opportunity covers eligible Master’s and PhD programs.

When does the 2027 scholarship begin?

The provided opportunity is for students beginning their studies in Spring 2027.

What is the application deadline?

The stated deadline is September 27, 2026.

How long does the Master’s program take?

The provided information states that Master’s programs are generally supported for approximately two years.

How long does the PhD program take?

Doctoral programs are generally expected to take approximately three to four years, depending on the program and academic progress.

Do I need IELTS?

Applicants generally need to meet the stated English-language requirement unless they qualify for an exemption.

The provided minimum scores are IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 79.

Is the GRE compulsory?

No. The GRE is not mandatory according to the provided information, although a score may be advantageous if available.

How many recommendation letters are required?

Applicants must submit three letters of recommendation.

Do all admitted students receive the scholarship?

According to the information provided, all admitted students automatically receive the scholarship.

Can applicants from outside Saudi Arabia apply?

Yes. The opportunity is specifically open to international students from countries around the world.

Where will students study?

Successful applicants will study at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Saudi Arabia.

Final Checklist for Applicants

Before submitting your application, make sure you have considered the following:

Confirm that you meet the entry requirements for your selected program.

Confirm that your academic background matches the program.

Check the applicable English-language requirements.

Determine whether you qualify for an English-language test exemption.

Conclusion

The KAUST Scholarship 2027 is a significant opportunity for international students seeking fully funded Master’s or PhD study in Saudi Arabia. Through comprehensive financial support, the program is designed to allow admitted graduate students to concentrate on their academic development and research while studying at a research-intensive university.

The funding package includes full tuition coverage, a monthly living stipend, on-campus accommodation, medical and dental coverage, and relocation support for international students, making it an attractive option for students who want to pursue advanced education without the substantial financial burden normally associated with international graduate study.

The opportunity is open to international students from any country, while applicants must still satisfy the admission requirements of their chosen KAUST program. Candidates should also pay close attention to English-language requirements, recommendation letters and supporting documentation.

For students interested in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and related research areas, KAUST can provide an international research environment in which to develop advanced knowledge and contribute to scientific innovation.

Applications are open for the Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027. The Voqal Partners Fellowship is a six-month program for social justice changemakers ready to build and test a new idea. Each year, they select a small cohort of fellows and provide the funding, coaching, and community to move their work forward from concept to real-world experimentation.

This is a dream-stage and idea-stage fellowship. They are looking for people with a bold vision for the future—even if they’re still figuring out exactly how to get there. A cohort of peers: Eight fellows per year, learning alongside each other. Past fellows stay connected through an active alum network.

Eligibility

You must be 18 or older, based in the United States, and able to receive funds in the U.S. Voqal Partners does not offer visa sponsorship.

They are looking for community leaders who are part of the communities they work with — not outside them. They believe the people closest to a challenge are often closest to the solutions. They prioritize people with lived experience, who represent non-dominant cultures, and who are working to resource historically excluded communities.

TITLE: Fight Kids Cancer

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Co-funded Programmes

Image: from iStock © Choreograph

Fight Kids Cancer

Fight Kids Cancer (FKC) is a collaborative research programme supporting academic research for paediatric cancers, providing 10M€ funding per year.

Launched in 2019, the initiative was created to address the urgent need for innovation in the treatment of paediatric oncology. The programme supports clinical trials and translational research focused on improving survival rates, reducing treatment toxicity, and restoring young patients to full health. FKC prioritises interdisciplinary and collaborative research, particularly in areas with high unmet needs such as paediatric brain tumours, leukaemia, and solid tumours. It also aims to advance fundamental scientific knowledge and build scientific capacity across Europe. By encouraging cross-border collaboration, FKC fosters fostering synergies between leading paediatric oncology centers and supports long-term European collaboration.

In addition to its funding role, FKC has built a pan-European network of excellence in paediatric oncology, helping to build long-term scientific capacity and supporting the next generation of paediatric cancer researchers.

To date, FKC has supported 14 clinical trials and 32 translational research projects representing an investment of over 42 million euros across 6 years.

Funders

SCIANCE (AI in Science) will support the development of RAISE, a new European virtual institute designed to accelerate the adoption of AI in scientific research, and coordinate AI-enabled scientific research across Europe through a bottom-up approach. The project mobilises leading European scientific organisations and research infrastructures across five pilot areas – fundamental physics and astronomy, materials science, life science, earth sciences, and social sciences and humanities – together with AI research centres and e-infrastructures. TITLE: Donor Profile: George J. Elbaum

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
George J. Elbaum (AA ’59, SM AA, NU ’63, PhD NU ’67)
The Whiteman Fellowships

by Elizabeth Chadis, Development Officer // MIT Physics Annual 2003

George J. Elbaum (AA ’59, SM AA, NU ’63, PhD NU ’67) with his wife Mimi Jensen

George Elbaum had no intention of going on to graduate school upon completing his SB. Instead, he went to Los Angeles to work in aerospace. But when his employer, TRW, offered him a doctoral fellowship specifically for MIT, “I jumped at the chance.”

“The doctoral fellowship allowed me to select a thesis that was not funded but that interested me and resulted in three very exciting years of my life, so now I want to give this opportunity to some talented graduate students.”

George had been totally inactive as an alumnus—no contacts, clubs,or reunions since leaving the Institute.Then in 1998, an article on a philanthropic project in the local newspaper “awoke me to giving back.”

Physics is beautiful… freshman physics was my nemesis, I had an epiphany while reviewing undergrad physics for the doctoral exam. I said to myself in awe, ‘Physics is beautiful.’
George J. Elbaum (AA ’59, SM AA, NU ’63, PhD NU ’67)

Because he places such a high value on his MIT education, which “taught me to think analytically; it seemed natural to start giving back through MIT.” Since 1998, George has supported three graduate fellowships and two postdoctoral fellowships in the MIT School of Science. The Whiteman Fellowships, named after George’s mother, Pauline Whiteman, are highly prized by the recipients.

TITLE: Evaluating altimetry-derived surface currents on the south Greenland shelf with surface drifters

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Coquereau, A., & Foukal, N. P., 2023. Evaluating altimetry-derived surface currents on the south Greenland shelf with surface drifters. Ocean Science, 19(5), 1393-1411. https://doi.org/10.5194/os-19-1393-2023

The pathways and fate of freshwater in the East Greenland Coastal Current (EGCC) are crucial to the climate system. The EGCC transports large amounts of freshwater in close proximity to sites of deep open-ocean convection in the Labrador and Irminger seas. Many studies have attempted to analyze this system from models and various observational platforms, but the modeling results largely disagree with one another, and observations are limited due to the harsh conditions typical of the region. Altimetry-derived surface currents, constructed from remote-sensing observations and applying geostrophic equations, provide a continuous observational data set beginning in 1993. However, these products have historically encountered difficulties in coastal regions, and thus their validity must be checked. In this work, we use a comprehensive methodology to compare these Eulerian data to a Lagrangian data set of 34 surface drifter trajectories and demonstrate that the altimetry-derived surface currents are surprisingly capable of recovering the spatial structure of the flow field on the south Greenland shelf and can mimic the Lagrangian nature of the flow as observed from surface drifters.

TITLE: Mastercard Foundation Scholarships: What Sets the Programme Apart, Who Can Apply and How to Get Started

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
For many talented young Africans, the challenge is not a lack of ambition or academic ability, but access to the resources, networks and opportunities that can turn that potential into impact. The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program was created to help address that gap. Since its launch in 2012, the programme has developed into much more than a traditional university scholarship. Through partnerships with universities and organisations in Africa and internationally, it supports young people, particularly those who have faced barriers to education, to pursue higher education while developing their leadership capacity and preparing to contribute to their communities and the continent. Financial support can include tuition, accommodation, books and educational materials, alongside mentoring, counselling, leadership development and, where necessary, return travel. Importantly, however, the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is not administered through one universal application. Each partner institution determines its own programmes, eligibility requirements, selection process and deadlines. (Mastercard Foundation) Explore the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.

University of Edinburgh Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program 2027/2028
One of the major opportunities prospective applicants should currently be watching is the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Edinburgh. For the 2027/2028 academic year, Edinburgh is offering both on-campus and online postgraduate scholarship routes. The on-campus scholarship supports a one-year, full-time master’s degree and covers approved tuition, accommodation, travel, study materials and a living-cost stipend. Online scholars receive full approved tuition fees, an academic stipend to support access to a laptop and reliable internet, an opportunity to attend an in-person gathering, and participation in the University’s wider Climate Leadership Programme. (Global) What particularly sets Edinburgh’s programme apart is its emphasis on climate leadership. Applicants must demonstrate experience or ambition in addressing the climate crisis, and all Mastercard Foundation Scholars at Edinburgh participate in a Climate Leadership Programme. The University describes the wider programme as developing talented, entrepreneurial and compassionate African leaders equipped to contribute to sustainable transitions. (Global)

There is also considerable flexibility in how scholars can study. Eligible on-campus programmes include Africa and International Development, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Environment and Development, Food Security, Planetary Health, Sustainable Energy Systems, Climate Change Finance and Investment, Environmental Sustainability, Data, Inequality and Society, and Operational Research. Online options include programmes such as International Development, Global Food Security and Nutrition, One Health, Social Justice and Community Action, Digital Education and Data Science Technologies. (Global)

Who can apply to Edinburgh?
Applicants must be citizens or refugees of an African country and resident in Africa. They must have faced significant barriers in their education or early career and demonstrate both leadership and service within their communities. For 2027/2028, applicants must also be 35 or younger when the programme begins, meaning they must have been born on or after 1 January 1992. Master’s applicants should not already have completed a postgraduate degree. Applicants must also meet the academic requirements for their selected Edinburgh programme, generally equivalent to at least a UK upper-second-class bachelor’s degree. (Global) The University particularly encourages applications from women, people from refugee and displaced backgrounds, and people with disabilities, although belonging to one of these groups is not itself a requirement. You can read more here

What Sets the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program Apart?
There are thousands of scholarships available internationally, but several characteristics distinguish the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.
First, it is more than tuition funding. Depending on the partner institution, scholars can receive support for accommodation, living expenses, books, travel and other educational costs, alongside academic and psychosocial support. (Mastercard Foundation) Second, leadership and community impact matter alongside academic achievement. The programme is interested in what applicants have already done with the opportunities available to them and what they hope to contribute in the future. At Edinburgh, for example, selection considers academic merit, transformative leadership and community service, the quality of the applicant’s alignment with climate justice, potential impact in their home country and the barriers they have overcome. (Edinburgh University Registry Services) Third, the programme deliberately considers barriers to opportunity. Applicants are not assessed simply on whether they have accumulated the most prestigious experiences. Partner programmes can specifically seek talented people whose educational journeys have been affected by financial, social, personal or practical barriers. Fourth, scholars join a community rather than simply receiving an award. Leadership programmes, mentoring, coaching, professional development and scholar and alumni networks are integral to many of the partnerships. Finally, there is a strong emphasis on translating education into meaningful change. The scholarship is particularly relevant to applicants who can connect their academic ambitions with a credible vision for improving communities, institutions, industries or wider development outcomes.

Other Mastercard Foundation Scholarships to Watch
The University of Edinburgh is only one institution in the wider Scholars Program. Opportunities are offered through numerous partner institutions, and because every university manages its own recruitment process, deadlines can vary substantially. (Mastercard Foundation) Among the current opportunities applicants may encounter are programmes at the University of British Columbia, University of Toronto and University of Oxford, alongside Mastercard Foundation partnerships with institutions across Africa and elsewhere. This means applicants should not think of the programme as one annual scholarship competition. Instead, they should identify the Mastercard Foundation partner institutions that offer programmes aligned with their academic background and career goals and then follow those institutions individually.
You can find Mastercard Foundation partner institutions and where to apply here

How to Prepare a Strong Application
A strong Mastercard Foundation scholarship application should tell a coherent story. Academic achievement is important, but applicants should also demonstrate leadership, service, resilience and a clear sense of purpose. Instead of simply listing positions held, candidates should show what they actually changed, improved, created or contributed. An applicant who founded an initiative, for example, should explain the problem it addressed, what they personally did and what changed because of the intervention. Someone who has overcome substantial barriers to education should explain those circumstances truthfully while demonstrating how they responded to them. Applicants should also be able to answer three fundamental questions: Why this programme? Why this university? And what will you do with the opportunity? Generic statements about wanting to “change Africa” are unlikely to be as persuasive as a specific understanding of the problem the applicant wants to address, the skills they currently lack and how the selected degree can help close that gap. Edinburgh explicitly advises candidates to tailor their application to the individual institution rather than simply recycling the same Mastercard Foundation application across universities. Its application includes short essays exploring the applicant’s personal story, academic and leadership experience and future ambitions. (Global)

Start Preparing Before Applications Open
Prospective scholars should begin preparing long before the final application deadline. Academic transcripts and degree certificates should be ready, and applicants should review the precise eligibility requirements of both the scholarship and their intended degree. They should also think carefully about their leadership examples, community service, barriers they have overcome and the long-term impact they want to make. For Edinburgh applicants, preparation is particularly urgent because the first important dates are Sep. 15–24, not the November application deadline. Missing the mandatory information-session stage means an applicant cannot proceed to the 2027/2028 scholarship application. (Global) It is equally important to use official sources. There is no universal Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application, and deadlines vary by partner institution. The Foundation advises prospective scholars to check the application requirements of the specific partner they want to attend. (Mastercard Foundation)

More Than a Scholarship
Perhaps the most important thing to understand about the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is that it is designed as an investment in people, not simply degrees. The financial support can make an otherwise inaccessible university education possible. But the combination of education, leadership development, mentoring, community, professional networks and a strong expectation of social contribution is what distinguishes the programme. For young Africans who have demonstrated academic potential, overcome barriers and are already finding ways to serve or lead within their communities, the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program can provide something much bigger than funding. It can provide the education, community and platform from which their next chapter of impact begins.

As a Mastercard Foundation Scholar, I have shared several blogs based on my experience of the scholarship journey. If you are preparing to apply, you can read my guide on how to win the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program scholarship here. If you are wondering whether the scholarship is the right fit for you, read why the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program may be the best fit for you here. And if you have faced several rejections and are beginning to feel discouraged, I wrote something especially for you, which you can read here.

For more articles and scholarships, visit Opportunity Desk

TITLE: UN Women EmPower Bootcamp 2026: Apply for AI for Gender-Responsive Climate Action Training During Bangkok Climate Action Week

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
UN Women is inviting young people to register for the EmPower Bootcamp: AI for Gender-Responsive Climate Action, an intensive learning opportunity taking place as part of Bangkok Climate Action Week 2026.

The bootcamp will be held on 3 October 2026 and will bring together participants interested in understanding how artificial intelligence can be used to support climate action while also examining the gender, ethical, environmental and social implications associated with rapidly developing AI technologies.

Participants will be able to join either in person at Nextopia, Siam Paragon in Bangkok, Thailand, or online through Microsoft Teams, making the programme accessible to people who are unable to travel to Bangkok. The in-person component is limited to up to 50 participants.

The training is particularly relevant for young people interested in climate action, gender equality, responsible technology, artificial intelligence, digital innovation and sustainable development. Importantly, UN Women has indicated that applicants do not need previous programming or artificial-intelligence experience to participate.

Event Date: 3 October 2026

Time: 13:00–18:00 Bangkok time (UTC+7)

Venue: Nextopia, Siam Paragon, Bangkok, Thailand, with an online participation option through Microsoft Teams.

Registration Deadline: The official registration form does not state a specific closing date. Because in-person participation is limited and UN Women describes slots as limited, interested candidates should register as early as possible.

About the UN Women EmPower Bootcamp 2026

The EmPower Bootcamp: AI for Gender-Responsive Climate Action is designed to help young people develop a more practical and critical understanding of artificial intelligence and how emerging AI technologies can contribute to climate solutions.

Rather than treating AI only as a technical subject, the bootcamp approaches artificial intelligence through the interconnected lenses of:

Climate action

Gender equality

Responsible innovation

Ethics

Social inclusion

Environmental sustainability

Digital skills

The programme recognizes that AI can create new opportunities for climate action while also creating risks that need to be understood and managed.

The official registration form explains that participants will explore how artificial intelligence can support climate action that advances gender equality while critically examining its risks and limitations.

The learning format will include interactive sessions and practical exercises, meaning participants will not simply listen to presentations. They will actively engage with tools, concepts and project-development exercises throughout the bootcamp.

Why AI and Gender-Responsive Climate Action Matter

Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing the way governments, businesses, researchers, civil-society organizations and communities analyze environmental challenges and design potential climate solutions.

AI technologies can potentially support areas such as:

Climate-data analysis

Environmental monitoring

Early-warning systems

Energy management

Climate adaptation planning

Agriculture

Disaster-risk management

Sustainable transportation

Renewable-energy optimization

Climate communications

However, technological solutions are not automatically inclusive.

AI systems are developed using data, algorithms and assumptions created within existing societies. If gender inequality or social exclusion exists within those societies or datasets, technology can reproduce or even intensify those inequalities.

This is why gender-responsive approaches to artificial intelligence are increasingly important.

UN Women’s bootcamp encourages participants to think critically about both the potential benefits and potential limitations of AI, rather than treating technology as automatically neutral or beneficial.

What Participants Will Learn

The bootcamp will cover several interconnected subject areas.

According to the official registration form, the programme includes:

AI fundamentals

Gender bias

Ethical considerations

Prompt engineering

Custom GPTs

Practical applications of AI for climate work

Development of participants’ own project ideas

Each of these areas contributes to the broader objective of helping young people understand how AI can be applied responsibly to climate challenges.

Understanding AI Fundamentals

One of the first areas of focus will be the basic concepts underlying artificial intelligence.

This is particularly important because the programme is not limited to technology professionals.

UN Women’s public announcement states that no programming or previous AI experience is required.

This means the bootcamp can be relevant to participants from a wide variety of backgrounds, including:

Climate activism

Environmental studies

Gender studies

Sustainable development

Youth leadership

Civil society

Communications

Public policy

Education

Social entrepreneurship

International development

Community-based organizations

Participants will be introduced to AI concepts in a way intended to support later practical exercises.

Exploring Gender Bias in Artificial Intelligence

A major component of the programme will focus on gender bias in AI.

Artificial-intelligence systems are influenced by the data on which they are trained and by the way systems are designed and deployed.

Participants will therefore be encouraged to examine questions such as:

Whose experiences are represented in AI data?

Who may be excluded?

Can an AI system unintentionally reinforce gender stereotypes?

How can bias affect climate-related decisions?

How can developers and users identify potential bias?

What safeguards can make AI applications more inclusive?

UN Women’s public communication for the event specifically highlights the need to identify bias, risks and safeguards when working with AI.

For participants interested in climate justice, gender equality or technology governance, this is an especially important component of the training.

Ethical Considerations in AI

The bootcamp will also examine ethical questions surrounding artificial intelligence.

As AI becomes more widely used, responsible deployment requires more than simply asking whether a technology is technically capable of performing a task.

Participants will also need to consider:

Whether its use is fair

Whether its outputs may reinforce discrimination

Whether privacy is protected

Whether affected communities are represented

Whether vulnerable groups could face disproportionate risks

Whether technology is being used transparently and responsibly

The programme therefore encourages participants to evaluate AI critically rather than focusing exclusively on technological capability.

Prompt Engineering

Participants will gain practical exposure to prompt engineering.

Prompt engineering refers to the process of structuring instructions and questions given to generative-AI systems in order to obtain more useful, accurate or contextually appropriate results.

This element of the bootcamp can help participants understand how to interact more effectively with generative-AI tools.

For climate activists, researchers, students and civil-society organizations, stronger prompting skills can potentially support activities such as:

Generating ideas

Structuring research

Drafting communications

Exploring scenarios

Summarizing complex information

Developing project concepts

Creating educational materials

The bootcamp is therefore intended to provide practical digital skills alongside broader discussions of gender and ethics.

Building Custom GPTs and AI Assistants

Another practical topic included in the programme is custom GPTs.

UN Women’s announcement describes the bootcamp as an opportunity for participants to experiment with prompting and build an AI assistant.

This is significant because it moves the programme beyond theoretical discussion.

Participants will have an opportunity to explore how an AI tool can be adapted around a defined purpose or challenge.

For example, this kind of thinking could potentially be applied to:

Climate education

Community information

Environmental awareness

Youth engagement

Advocacy

Project planning

Climate adaptation

Gender-responsive outreach

The emphasis is not on becoming a software engineer during a five-hour session, but on understanding how accessible AI tools can potentially be configured and applied responsibly.

Practical Applications of AI for Climate Action

The bootcamp will explore practical ways in which artificial intelligence can potentially support climate work.

Participants will be encouraged to consider technology in relation to real climate challenges rather than treating AI as an abstract concept.

UN Women describes the programme as a hands-on exploration of how AI can support climate action while participants critically examine its wider implications.

This practical orientation makes the bootcamp particularly relevant to young climate advocates and emerging professionals who want to understand how AI might strengthen their existing work.

Develop Your Own AI and Climate Project Idea

One of the most important components of the bootcamp will be helping participants develop their own project idea.

The official registration page states that the programme will move from AI fundamentals and practical applications toward supporting participants in developing an individual project concept.

UN Women similarly describes this as developing a responsible AI × climate project idea.

This gives participants an opportunity to move from learning concepts toward applying them creatively.

A project idea could potentially relate to the participant’s:

Community

Organization

Climate campaign

University

Youth network

Research interest

Advocacy initiative

Environmental challenge

The programme therefore emphasizes active application rather than passive learning.

In-Person Participation in Bangkok

Participants can request to attend the bootcamp physically at:

Nextopia, Siam Paragon, Bangkok, Thailand

The session will take place from:

13:00 to 18:00 Bangkok time on 3 October 2026.

The registration form clearly states that the physical session can accommodate:

Up to 50 participants.

Because capacity is limited, submitting the registration form should be understood as registering interest, rather than an automatic guarantee of a physical place.

The official form itself asks applicants to indicate whether they prefer to participate in person or online.

Online Participation Through Microsoft Teams

Applicants unable to attend physically in Bangkok can select the:

Online via Microsoft Teams

option.

This makes the bootcamp significantly more accessible to interested young people located outside Thailand.

Online participation can be particularly useful for:

Students

Youth activists

Civil-society professionals

Climate advocates

Young professionals

Participants in other Asia-Pacific countries

Individuals unable to travel internationally

The form does not state that online participation requires travel to any physical venue.

Part of Bangkok Climate Action Week 2026

The EmPower Bootcamp is being delivered during Bangkok Climate Action Week 2026.

The official Bangkok Climate Action Week programme lists the EmPower Bootcamp on 3 October 2026 at 13:00 at Nextopia.

Bangkok Climate Action Week itself runs from 3 to 11 October 2026 and includes a wide variety of workshops, discussions, exhibitions and activities relating to climate action, sustainability, communities and environmental innovation.

By placing the bootcamp within this wider programme, participants attending physically in Bangkok will be engaging with a broader climate-action environment.

Who Is the Bootcamp Intended For?

UN Women describes the event as open to young people aged 35 and below.

The registration form collects applicants’ ages using the following categories:

Under 18

18–24

25–30

31–35

Over 35

However, UN Women’s public announcement explicitly states that the opportunity is open to young people aged 35 and below.

Accordingly, applicants aged 35 or younger should be regarded as the intended participant group.

No Programming Experience Required

A particularly important feature of the opportunity is that participants do not need previous coding, programming or AI experience.

UN Women specifically states:

No programming or previous AI experience required.

This significantly broadens accessibility.

A young climate activist with limited technical experience can therefore apply alongside someone with a technology or data background.

The programme is designed around learning, experimentation and responsible application rather than requiring participants to arrive with advanced technical expertise.

Applications from Individuals and Organizations

The registration form allows applicants to register either:

As an individual/activist

On behalf of an organization

Applicants registering on behalf of an organization are asked to provide the organization’s name.

This means participation is not limited exclusively to employees of NGOs, international organizations or formal institutions.

Independent activists and other individual applicants can also register.

Strong Focus on Inclusive Participation

UN Women explicitly encourages applications from groups that are frequently underrepresented in technology, climate action and decision-making.

The official form states:

Applications are strongly encouraged from young women, gender-diverse youth, persons with disabilities, and youth from ethnic minorities and/or Indigenous groups.

Applicants are offered the option to voluntarily self-identify as:

Gender-diverse

A person with a disability

None of the above

Prefer not to say

This information reflects the programme’s emphasis on inclusive participation.

Gender Eligibility

The registration form asks applicants how they identify and provides the following choices:

Woman

This demonstrates that the event is not restricted only to women.

However, young women and gender-diverse youth are specifically encouraged to apply.

Pakistan Is Included

What Information Is Required to Register?

The application process is relatively straightforward.

No CV or Academic Transcript Required in the Registration Form

Instead, the process focuses on basic participant information and preferred attendance format.

This makes the registration process considerably simpler than many international training programmes.

No Specific Degree Requirement

TITLE: Why Municipal Youth Participation? European Training Seminar 2026 in Budapest, Hungary

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Why Municipal Youth Participation? seminar is an international training and professional development opportunity designed for people working to strengthen youth participation in local and regional decision-making. The seminar will bring together 50 participants in Budapest, Hungary, to explore practical approaches to municipal youth participation and the implementation of the new European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life.

Organized by the Council of Europe Youth Department, within the framework of the Youth Revitalising Democracy project, together with the Democracy Reloading Partnership of Erasmus+ national agencies, the seminar will take place from 16 to 21 November 2026 at the European Youth Centre Budapest.

The training is particularly relevant for municipal youth policy officers, youth policy practitioners, locally elected political representatives, youth councils, and youth civil society organizations involved in developing or implementing local and regional youth participation policies.

Applications must be submitted by 15 September 2026 at 24:00 UTC.

Who Can Apply?

The seminar is primarily intended for:

Municipal youth policy officers and their local partners

Locally elected political representatives

Local youth councils

Youth civil society organizations

Youth leaders

Youth policy makers

Youth policy officers

Other practitioners involved in planning and implementing local or regional youth participation policies and practices

Applicants must generally:

Be resident and working in a Council of Europe member state, although exceptions may be possible when duly justified.

Be able to communicate independently in English.

Be actively engaged in youth participation policy or practice at the local or regional level.

Priority will be given to participants from countries participating in the Democracy Reloading Partnership, although participation is not exclusively limited to those countries.

No specific race, ethnicity, gender, or academic qualification requirement is stated in the provided information.

What Is the “Why Municipal Youth Participation?” Seminar?

The Why Municipal Youth Participation? seminar is designed to strengthen the capacity of local and regional actors to develop and implement meaningful youth participation policies.

Youth participation is an important part of democratic life because local and regional authorities make decisions that directly affect young people and their communities.

The seminar provides participants with an opportunity to learn about European standards for youth participation, exchange experiences with peers, explore practical tools, and examine examples of municipal youth participation in Budapest.

The event will bring together 50 participants for an intensive learning and exchange experience.

Who Organizes the Seminar?

The seminar is organized by the Council of Europe Youth Department as part of the Youth Revitalising Democracy project.

It is being organized in cooperation with the Democracy Reloading Partnership of Erasmus+ national agencies.

The Council of Europe is a major European intergovernmental organization focused on human rights, democracy, and the rule of law.

The cooperation between the Council of Europe and Democracy Reloading gives the seminar a particular focus on strengthening democratic participation at the local level.

Where and When Will the Training Take Place?

The seminar will take place in:

European Youth Centre Budapest
Budapest, Hungary

Dates

16–21 November 2026

Participants are expected to arrive on Monday, 16 November and can leave on Saturday, 21 November 2026.

The activity will therefore provide several days of face-to-face learning, discussion, networking, and practical exploration of municipal youth participation.

Main Aim of the Seminar

The central aim is to support local and regional municipalities in designing and implementing participative youth policies that align with the new European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life.

Participants will have the opportunity to explore how European-level standards can be translated into practical approaches within their own municipalities and communities.

The seminar is therefore not only about learning theoretical concepts. It is also focused on understanding how youth participation can work in practice at the local level.

The European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life

A major focus of the seminar is the European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life.

The Charter is described in the opportunity information as the key standard for youth participation at local and regional level.

The Charter was first adopted in 1992 and subsequently underwent a major revision during 2024–2025.

More than 400 stakeholders participated in the revision process.

According to the provided information, the revised Charter was adopted by the Congress of Local and Regional Authorities and the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe in 2026.

The Council of Europe and its partners at international, national, and local levels are taking measures to support implementation of the Charter’s provisions.

This seminar is part of that broader effort.

Why Is the European Charter Important for the Seminar?

The Charter provides a framework for youth participation at local and regional levels.

The seminar will help participants become familiar with its provisions and consider how those provisions can be implemented in their own local realities.

Participants can therefore explore questions such as:

How can young people participate meaningfully in local decision-making?

What mechanisms can municipalities use to involve young people?

How can local youth policies become more participatory?

How can youth councils and civil society contribute to local policymaking?

How can European standards be translated into practical municipal policies?

What approaches have worked in different communities?

The seminar provides a setting for participants to explore these issues collectively.

Objectives of the Seminar

The training has several specific objectives.

1. Understanding the New European Charter

Participants will become familiar with the provisions of the new European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life.

They will also explore ways to apply those provisions within their own local and regional contexts.

This means participants can move from simply knowing about the Charter to considering how it can inform practical youth participation policies.

2. Understanding Council of Europe Standards

Participants will learn about Council of Europe standards for local youth participation in democratic life.

This can help practitioners understand the broader European framework surrounding youth participation and democratic engagement.

3. Understanding Democracy Reloading

The seminar will introduce participants to the Democracy Reloading concept and its tools.

These tools are intended to support municipal youth participation in decision-making.

This component can provide participants with practical resources that they can potentially use within their own municipalities and youth policy work.

4. Sharing Experiences and Practices

Another important objective is peer learning.

Participants will have the opportunity to share their experiences and practices with other people working on youth participation.

This creates space for participants to learn not only from trainers but also from colleagues working in different countries and local contexts.

5. Learning From Budapest

Participants will also gain insight into practices of municipal youth participation in Budapest and its district municipalities.

This practical component allows participants to examine how youth participation operates in a real municipal environment.

What Will the Program Include?

The seminar will include several learning and practical components.

Introduction to Council of Europe Youth Participation Standards

Participants will be introduced to key standards developed by the Council of Europe concerning youth participation.

Democracy Reloading Concept and Tools

The program will introduce the Democracy Reloading approach and tools designed to support municipal youth participation.

Visits to Local Practices in Budapest

Participants will have the opportunity to visit local examples of municipal youth participation in Budapest.

Council of Europe and Democracy Reloading Resources

The seminar will present relevant tools and resources from both the Council of Europe and the Democracy Reloading Partnership.

Together, these elements combine theoretical learning, practical examples, peer exchange, and exposure to useful resources.

Youth leaders

Why Municipal Youth Participation Matters

Local governments make decisions concerning many aspects of young people’s lives.

Effective youth participation can provide mechanisms through which young people can contribute to decisions affecting their communities.

For youth policy practitioners, understanding how to create meaningful participation structures can therefore be an important part of developing effective local youth policies.

The seminar approaches this issue from a European perspective, using the Council of Europe’s standards and the new European Charter as important reference points.
