TITLE: Policy and Research Officer – DFAT Australian Embassy The Hague: International Law and Research Job Opportunity

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Australian Embassy in The Hague is seeking a highly capable and analytical professional to join the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) as a Policy and Research Officer – LE4. This is a 12-month non-ongoing position for a locally engaged staff member, supporting Australia’s engagement with major international legal, accountability and diplomatic institutions based in The Hague. The position provides an opportunity to contribute to Australia’s international policy interests, particularly in relation to the International Court of Justice (ICJ), International Criminal Court (ICC), international law, human rights, political affairs, accountability mechanisms and the ongoing international response to the July 2014 downing of flight MH17. Importantly, applicants must already have the legal right to live and work in the Netherlands. The Australian Embassy in The Hague cannot provide visa sponsorship or relocation assistance, and applications from individuals without an appropriate and valid Dutch residence and work permit will not be considered.

Opportunity Overview

The Policy and Research Officer will work within the Australian Embassy in The Hague and assist the Australian Government in advancing its interests across international organisations and institutions located in The Hague.

The role is particularly relevant to professionals with experience or qualifications in areas such as:

International relations

International law

Political affairs

Human rights

Policy research

Government and diplomacy

International organisations

Legal research and analysis

Accountability and justice mechanisms

The successful applicant will be engaged on a non-ongoing 12-month contract as a Locally Engaged Staff member.

The employment conditions for Locally Engaged Staff are governed by the laws of the Netherlands. The Fair Work Act 2009 does not apply to the employment of Locally Engaged Staff at Australia’s overseas diplomatic and consular missions.

About the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) is responsible for advancing the interests of Australia and Australians internationally.

Its responsibilities include strengthening Australia’s security, supporting Australia’s economic prosperity, delivering Australia’s overseas development assistance and helping Australian citizens travelling or living overseas.

DFAT provides foreign, trade and development policy advice to the Australian Government and works with other Australian Government agencies to coordinate Australia’s global, regional and bilateral interests.

Working at an Australian diplomatic mission therefore provides exposure to Australia’s international policy and diplomatic activities while supporting government priorities in a particular country or region.

About the Policy and Research Officer Position

The Australian Government is looking for a Policy and Research Officer to support Australia’s engagement with international organisations based in The Hague.

The Hague is home to a number of important international legal and accountability institutions, making this position particularly relevant to professionals interested in international law, diplomacy, international justice and government policy.

The successful candidate will assist with Australia’s engagement with institutions including:

The International Court of Justice (ICJ)

The International Criminal Court (ICC)

The Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH)

The Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA)

Other international legal and accountability bodies and institutions

The Officer will undertake research and analysis, prepare briefings and reports, monitor developments, support meetings and visits, develop professional networks and provide broader policy and administrative assistance to the Embassy.

MH17 Accountability Work

One of the significant areas of responsibility associated with this position is supporting Australia’s ongoing pursuit of accountability relating to the July 2014 downing of flight MH17.

The Officer will monitor and report on relevant legal developments and support Australia’s participation in ongoing accountability efforts and commemorative activities.

The role may also involve work on international law, political affairs, human rights and budget-related issues, depending on Australia’s priorities and the needs of the Embassy.

This makes the position particularly suitable for candidates who have a strong interest in international justice, accountability, international legal proceedings and Australia’s role in international institutions.

Key Responsibilities

The Policy and Research Officer will be responsible for a broad range of policy, research, representational and organisational duties.

1. Support engagement with international legal institutions

The Officer will support Australia’s engagement with the ICJ, ICC and other international legal and accountability organisations.

This may involve:

Conducting research and analysis

Preparing briefing materials

Providing administrative support

Supporting effective governance

Preparing information to advance Australian Government priorities

Monitoring institutional developments

Supporting Australia’s participation in relevant meetings and processes

The Officer must therefore be capable of understanding complex information and converting it into useful, accurate and concise material for government decision-makers and other stakeholders.

2. Monitor international developments

A key component of the role is monitoring developments that may affect Australia’s interests.

The successful candidate will research, analyse and report on developments in areas including:

International law

International politics

Accountability

Human rights

Hague-based international organisations

Other international policy issues relevant to Australia

The ability to identify important developments, understand their implications and communicate them effectively will be essential.

3. Represent the Australian Embassy

The Officer may be required to represent the Embassy at meetings involving international organisations based in The Hague.

These organisations may include the Hague Conference on Private International Law and the Permanent Court of Arbitration.

This responsibility requires strong interpersonal and representational skills, professionalism and the ability to communicate Australia’s interests appropriately in an international environment.

4. Support MH17-related accountability efforts

The successful candidate will monitor developments related to MH17 and assist with Australia’s participation in ongoing accountability activities.

Responsibilities may include:

Monitoring legal developments

Preparing reports and briefings

Supporting Australia’s participation in accountability processes

Assisting with commemorative activities

Communicating relevant developments internally

5. Build and maintain professional networks

The Officer will establish, maintain and develop a network of contacts capable of providing useful information and supporting Australia’s interests.

This requires strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work effectively with internal and external stakeholders.

6. Coordinate visits and briefings

The position may involve coordinating visit programs and managing briefings for Australian Government officials and high-level visitors.

The Officer must therefore be able to manage competing tasks, coordinate stakeholders and deliver accurate information within strict deadlines.

7. Provide broader Embassy support

The role may also include administrative, public diplomacy and policy support.

In emergency situations, the Officer may also be required to provide consular assistance.

This means applicants should be adaptable and comfortable working across different responsibilities in a small diplomatic mission.

Qualifications and Experience

Applicants should have a tertiary qualification in international relations, law or another relevant field, or an equivalent level of professional experience.

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

Strong research and analytical skills

Applicants should be able to conduct detailed research, evaluate information from different sources, identify relevant findings and produce accurate analysis.

Knowledge of international law is specifically relevant to the position.

Excellent communication skills

The role requires strong oral and written communication abilities.

Applicants should be able to prepare professional documents that present information in a logical, concise and persuasive manner.

English is essential, while Dutch is desirable.

Strong interpersonal and liaison skills

The Officer will interact with government officials, international organisations and other stakeholders.

Applicants should therefore be capable of establishing professional relationships, maintaining networks and communicating effectively with people from different organisations and backgrounds.

Strong organisational abilities

The successful candidate will need to manage several responsibilities simultaneously, meet tight deadlines and maintain accuracy while working under limited supervision.

Ability to work independently

Although the role involves working as part of a small team, applicants must be capable of taking initiative and completing tasks with limited supervision.

Security Clearance Requirements

This is a security-designated position.

The successful applicant must either already hold an Australian Government NV1 security clearance or have the ability to obtain one.

Applicants must also be willing to undergo the security checks required to obtain an Australian National Security clearance.

Importantly, the vacancy specifies that applications can only be considered from nationals of:

Australia

Canada

New Zealand

United Kingdom

United States

Applicants must be eligible for an Australian Government security clearance.

The position also specifies that candidates who hold dual Dutch nationality together with one of the listed nationalities are not eligible for the security clearance required for this position.

Applicants should carefully consider this requirement before applying.

Right to Live and Work in the Netherlands

A mandatory requirement for this position is an existing legal right to live and work in the Netherlands.

The Australian Embassy in The Hague:

Does not provide visa sponsorship

Does not assist with relocation

Will not consider applications without an appropriate and valid visa or permit

Requires successful applicants to meet Dutch legal requirements for employment

Any costs associated with taking up the position, including relocation expenses, are the responsibility of the successful candidate.

This requirement is particularly important for international applicants because meeting the nationality requirement alone does not automatically make someone eligible to apply.

Selection Criteria

Applicants must respond to each of the five listed selection criteria as part of their application.

Each response has a strict maximum of 250 words.

Applications may not be assessed if they are incomplete or if responses exceed the specified word limit.

Selection Criterion A: Communication

Applicants must demonstrate well-developed written and oral communication skills in English and Dutch for both traditional and digital platforms in a professional environment.

Candidates should provide examples demonstrating their ability to prepare written material that presents information logically, succinctly and persuasively.

Selection Criterion B: Research and Analysis

Applicants must demonstrate the ability to independently conduct high-quality, thorough and accurate research using a variety of sources, including data.

Candidates should demonstrate how they have analysed findings, monitored trends and presented research findings or reports to different internal and external stakeholders.

Selection Criterion C: Stakeholder Engagement

Applicants must demonstrate the ability to communicate and liaise effectively with internal and external stakeholders.

Relevant examples should show excellent interpersonal skills, the ability to establish effective stakeholder relationships and the capacity to build and maintain professional networks.

Selection Criterion D: Judgment and Problem-Solving

Applicants should demonstrate effective judgment, decision-making and complex problem-solving skills.

Candidates should provide examples showing their ability to use initiative and innovation when addressing challenges or developing solutions.

Selection Criterion E: Planning and Organisation

Applicants must demonstrate effective planning and organisational skills.

Examples should show the ability to manage multiple tasks and competing priorities, achieve required outcomes and meet tight deadlines while working with limited supervision.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because the application requires a response to five specific selection criteria, applicants should avoid submitting generic statements.

A strong application should use specific examples from previous professional, academic or relevant experience.

For each selection criterion, candidates should consider using a structured example that clearly explains:

The situation or context.

The task or responsibility they were given.

The actions they personally took.

The result or outcome achieved.

What the example demonstrates about their suitability for the position.

Candidates should also ensure that each response remains within the 250-word limit.

It is important to address every part of the criterion rather than simply describing general skills.

English and Dutch Language Skills

English is explicitly identified as essential for the position, while Dutch is desirable.

However, the selection criteria request evidence of written and oral communication skills in both English and Dutch.

Applicants should therefore carefully review their own language capabilities and demonstrate relevant professional communication experience where applicable.

Dutch language ability may be particularly useful when interacting with local stakeholders and navigating the Dutch professional environment.

Locally Engaged Staff at Australian Overseas Missions

The position forms part of Australia’s Locally Engaged Staff workforce.

Locally Engaged Staff support and complement Australian Public Service employees working at Australia’s overseas posts.

They provide valuable local and professional knowledge, skills, networks and continuity across Australia’s diplomatic missions.

Australian Government overseas posts operate in more than 100 locations around the world, and locally engaged employees make an important contribution to Australia’s international objectives.

The position therefore offers an opportunity to contribute directly to the work of an Australian diplomatic mission while working in an international environment.

Recruitment and Application Process

The Human Resources Section based at the Australian High Commission in London manages recruitment processes for Australian diplomatic missions and other Australian Government overseas positions across the European region.

Applicants should use the Apply button associated with the vacancy to submit their application.

Questions regarding the recruitment process can be directed to the Human Resources Section at the recruitment contact provided in the vacancy announcement.

Applicants should ensure that their application is complete and that every selection criterion has been addressed within the required word limit.

Inclusive Workplace

The Australian Embassy states that it is committed to providing an inclusive and diverse workplace in which employees are valued.

Applications are encouraged from people with diverse backgrounds who share the values of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

Candidates should therefore focus their applications on demonstrating relevant skills, experience, qualifications and their ability to contribute effectively to the role.

Important Points Applicants Should Know

Before applying, candidates should carefully consider the following requirements:

The position is a 12-month non-ongoing contract.

It is a Locally Engaged Staff position at the Australian Embassy in The Hague.

Applicants must already have the legal right to live and work in the Netherlands.

The Australian Embassy does not provide visa sponsorship.

The Embassy does not provide relocation assistance.

Relocation and other costs associated with taking up the position are the responsibility of the successful applicant.

Applicants must meet the specified nationality requirements for the security clearance.

Eligible applicants must be nationals of Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the United Kingdom or the United States.

Dual Dutch nationals who also hold one of the listed nationalities are stated to be ineligible for the required security clearance.

Applicants must be able to obtain an Australian Government NV1 security clearance.

Applicants must be willing to undergo the required security checks.

A tertiary qualification in international relations, law or another relevant field, or equivalent experience, is required.

Knowledge of international law is relevant to the position.

English communication skills are essential.

Dutch is desirable and is also referenced in the selection criteria.

Each selection criterion must be answered.

Each selection criterion has a strict 250-word limit.

Incomplete applications or responses exceeding the word limit may not be assessed.

Apply HERE

Deadline

No application deadline is provided in the information supplied for this vacancy.

Applicants should therefore check the official vacancy page and application portal for the current closing date before submitting an application, as recruitment timelines can change.

Why This Position Could Be Valuable for International Policy Professionals

This opportunity is particularly relevant to professionals seeking experience at the intersection of international law, diplomacy, policy research, international organisations and government affairs.

Working in The Hague can provide exposure to an international environment where major institutions dealing with international justice, arbitration, private international law and accountability are located.

The responsibilities also extend beyond desk-based research. The successful applicant may participate in meetings, represent the Embassy, develop professional networks, coordinate high-level visits and support Australia’s engagement with international institutions.

For a professional with the appropriate nationality, Dutch work authorisation, qualifications and security-clearance eligibility, the role could provide meaningful experience in Australia’s international policy and diplomatic environment.

About the Commonwealth Government of Australia

The Commonwealth Government of Australia employs staff overseas to support the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade and other Australian Government agencies at embassies, high commissions and consulates around the world.

These overseas employees contribute to Australia’s diplomatic, policy, consular and international objectives.

Locally Engaged Staff are an important part of this global workforce. Their knowledge, skills, networks and continuity help Australian diplomatic missions operate effectively in their host countries.

The Human Resources Section at the Australian High Commission in London manages local job vacancies across the European region, including various categories of employment and certain internship programs.

Learn more HERE

Privacy and Personal Data

Personal information provided during the recruitment process will be handled in accordance with the relevant privacy notice and applicable data protection laws.

Applicants should review the applicable privacy information before submitting personal details as part of their application.

Conclusion

The Policy and Research Officer – LE4 position at the Australian Embassy in The Hague offers an opportunity for an appropriately qualified and security-clearance-eligible professional to contribute to Australia’s international policy interests in one of the world’s most important centres for international law and justice. The successful candidate will support Australia’s engagement with institutions such as the International Court of Justice and International Criminal Court, monitor international legal and political developments, conduct research and analysis, prepare briefings, represent the Embassy at relevant meetings, support MH17 accountability activities and build relationships with international stakeholders. However, applicants should pay particularly close attention to the eligibility requirements. The position requires an existing right to live and work in the Netherlands, does not provide visa sponsorship or relocation assistance, and has specific nationality and security-clearance requirements. Candidates who meet these conditions and can demonstrate strong research, analytical, communication, stakeholder-management, judgment and organisational skills should prepare carefully structured responses to all five selection criteria, ensuring that every response remains within the strict 250-word limit. Because the supplied vacancy information does not state a closing date, prospective applicants should verify the official application portal for the current deadline and submit a complete application as early as possible.

TITLE: FASPE Journalism Fellowship 2027: Fully Funded Two-Week Ethics Programme for Journalism Students and Early-Career Journalists in Germany and Poland

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the 2027 FASPE Journalism Fellowship, a fully funded international programme for graduate students with journalism experience and early-career journalists who want to examine professional ethics, ethical leadership, responsibility, media power and the role of journalists in democratic society.

The Fellowships at Auschwitz for the Study of Professional Ethics (FASPE) Journalism programme brings a small cohort of approximately 13 to 16 Journalism Fellows to Germany and Poland for an intensive two-week programme combining seminars, historical site visits, interdisciplinary discussion and sustained reflection on the ethical responsibilities of journalists.

For the 2027 cycle, the Journalism Fellowship will take place from:

June 18, 2027 to July 2, 2027

Applications are open until:

January 3, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET

Two letters of recommendation are required separately and are due on:

January 10, 2027.

The Fellowship is fully funded. FASPE covers programme costs and related travel so that a candidate’s financial circumstances do not determine whether they can participate. Covered expenses include airfare to and from Europe, programme transportation in Germany and Poland, hotel accommodation, admission costs, programme materials, group meals and pocket money for meals not provided as part of the group programme. FASPE confirms that participants travelling from outside the United States can also have their travel to Berlin and return travel covered.

Importantly, applicants do not need to be U.S. citizens or U.S. residents. FASPE accepts eligible applicants regardless of citizenship or residence, although selected Fellows are responsible for arranging any visas they need; FASPE provides supporting documentation for visa applications.

About the FASPE Journalism Fellowship

FASPE is an intensive professional ethics programme that uses the history of professionals working in Germany and Europe during the Nazi period as a framework for examining ethical responsibility in contemporary professional life.

The Journalism Fellowship focuses particularly on the behavior, decisions and responsibilities of journalists.

Participants examine how German and international journalists:

Reported Nazi policies

Failed to report important developments adequately

Misrepresented events

Normalized dangerous developments

Used or failed to use their professional influence

Responded to political pressure

Navigated institutional and personal responsibility

FASPE then uses these historical examples to encourage Fellows to confront the ethical challenges journalists face today.

The programme is therefore unusual because it does not treat journalism ethics simply as a collection of professional rules.

Instead, Fellows are encouraged to ask more difficult questions about:

Personal responsibility

Professional identity

Institutional pressure

Moral judgment

Ethical leadership

Power

Accountability

Public trust

The consequences of professional decisions

FASPE Is Not a Holocaust Studies Programme

Prospective applicants should understand what the Fellowship is—and what it is not.

FASPE explicitly states that it is:

Not a Holocaust studies course

Not a genocide-prevention programme

The history of the Nazi period is central to the Fellowship, but it functions as an ethical framework through which participants examine their responsibilities in contemporary professional settings.

The objective is not simply to learn what happened historically.

Rather, Fellows are asked to consider questions such as:

What responsibilities does an individual journalist have inside a large institution?

When does professional compliance become ethical failure?

How can journalists recognize when apparently normal professional practices are contributing to wider harm?

How should journalists react when political, financial or institutional pressures influence reporting?

What is the relationship between legality and ethical responsibility?

When should journalists challenge their own organizations?

How should professional influence be exercised responsibly?

This makes FASPE particularly relevant to journalism students and early-career journalists interested in the relationship between media institutions and ethical decision-making.

2027 Programme Dates

The 2027 Journalism programme runs from:

June 18 to July 2, 2027.

Journalism Fellows travel during the same programme period as Fellows in:

Medicine

Clergy and Religious Leadership

This shared travel structure allows for interdisciplinary discussion among people preparing for very different professions.

FASPE also operates fellowship programmes in:

Business

Law

Design and Technology

Medicine

Clergy and Religious Leadership

Journalism

Each programme examines professional ethics through questions specific to that profession while also creating opportunities for Fellows from different fields to engage with one another.

Where Does the Fellowship Take Place?

The Fellowship is conducted primarily in:

Germany and Poland

Journalism Fellows spend approximately two weeks travelling through historically significant locations while participating in intensive seminars.

The programme uses what FASPE describes as the “power of place”—the idea that ethical questions can be understood differently when discussed in the locations where historical professional decisions had real consequences.

Programme activities include:

Daily seminars

Historical site visits

Profession-specific discussions

Interdisciplinary sessions

Shared meals

Informal conversations

Group activities

The combination of place, history and academic discussion is central to the Fellowship model.

How Many Journalism Fellows Are Selected?

Each year, FASPE Journalism generally selects:

13 to 16 Fellows

from a large applicant pool.

The relatively small cohort allows participants to engage in intensive discussion rather than attend a large lecture-style programme.

FASPE emphasizes that Fellows should be able to participate constructively in discussions involving difficult, controversial and emotionally demanding subjects.

The programme therefore looks not only at academic or professional achievements but also at the applicant’s ability to contribute meaningfully to a small intellectual community.

What Does the FASPE Journalism Fellowship Cover?

FASPE describes its Fellowships as:

Fully funded

so that financial ability does not affect participation.

The programme covers substantial travel and participation expenses.

Airfare

FASPE covers:

Round-trip economy-class airfare

for Fellowship travel.

Its FAQ specifies airfare from the United States to Europe, while also confirming that Fellows travelling from outside the United States can have their travel to Berlin and return travel covered.

This is especially important for international applicants.

Transportation in Germany and Poland

The Fellowship covers transportation associated with:

Group travel

Programme activities

Travel between programme locations

during the Germany and Poland portion of the programme.

Participants therefore do not need to finance normal group transportation connected with the Fellowship itinerary.

Hotel Accommodation

FASPE covers:

All hotel costs

associated with the programme.

Accommodation arrangements are made as part of the Fellowship structure.

Meals

The programme covers:

All group meals

and also provides:

Pocket money for non-group meals.

This makes the financial package considerably more comprehensive than a programme that covers only airfare and accommodation.

Admission Fees and Programme Materials

FASPE also pays for:

Admission fees associated with programme visits

Programme materials

Participants therefore do not need to pay separately for required historical-site admissions or core academic materials.

Who Can Apply for the FASPE Journalism Fellowship?

FASPE identifies three main eligibility pathways for Journalism applicants.

An applicant should generally fall into one of the following categories.

Category 1: Graduate Students With Journalism Experience

Applicants may be:

Enrolled in a graduate programme of any kind

Have some journalism experience

Plan to work as a journalist

The graduate programme does not necessarily need to be a journalism degree.

This means a candidate could potentially be studying another field at graduate level while developing a serious journalism career, provided they already have some journalistic experience and intend to work professionally as a journalist.

Journalistic experience may include work in:

A university newsroom

Student media

Professional media

Independent journalism

Other relevant settings

Category 2: Bachelor’s Graduates Working as Journalists

Applicants can also qualify if they:

Have completed an undergraduate degree

Are currently working as journalists

This pathway is particularly relevant to early-career reporters and other journalism professionals who entered the industry after completing university.

Category 3: Graduate-Degree Holders Working as Journalists

Applicants may also qualify if they:

Have completed a graduate degree

Are working as journalists

The degree itself does not appear to need to be exclusively in journalism, provided the candidate is professionally working in journalism and otherwise fits the programme’s early-career orientation.

Early-Career Requirement

FASPE seeks Journalism Fellows who are:

Preparing for or in the early stages of their careers.

Candidates generally should have:

No more than 10 years of total professional experience.

This is not designed primarily for highly established senior journalists with decades of professional experience.

The programme focuses on people who are still developing their:

Professional identity

Ethical framework

Leadership approach

Understanding of their role within journalism

Published Journalism Is Preferred

FASPE states that preference will be given to candidates whose journalism has been:

Published, or

Aired

by a:

Recognized news organization.

This is described as a preference rather than an absolute eligibility condition.

Applicants should therefore not necessarily exclude themselves because they do not have major national publication credits.

However, candidates with relevant published work should make it clearly visible in their application.

Types of Journalists FASPE Welcomes

FASPE seeks Journalism Fellows with diverse professional interests.

Potential candidates may be pursuing careers as:

Reporters

Editors

Photojournalists

Documentary journalists

Nonfiction writers

Broadcasters

Multimedia journalists

Other forms of journalistic storyteller

FASPE welcomes journalism conducted in:

Local contexts

National contexts

International contexts

The Fellowship is therefore not restricted to newspaper reporters or traditional print journalism.

What Qualities Does FASPE Look for?

Selection is not based solely on the prestige of an applicant’s newsroom or university.

FASPE seeks people at a formative stage of their professional lives who demonstrate characteristics such as:

Open-mindedness

Self-reflection

Leadership potential

Intellectual maturity

Emotional maturity

Capacity for respectful disagreement

Ability to participate in difficult conversations

Potential to influence their profession

FASPE evaluates candidates based on their:

Academic background

Personal experience

Professional experience

Leadership capacity

Potential contribution to the Fellowship

Potential contribution to the alumni community

No U.S. Citizenship Requirement

FASPE is based in the United States, but international applicants are welcome.

The programme explicitly states:

Applicants do not need to be American or reside in the United States.

Eligible candidates may apply:

Regardless of citizenship or residency.

This makes the Fellowship genuinely international.

Applicants may therefore potentially come from countries across:

Africa

Asia

Europe

North America

Latin America and the Caribbean

Middle East

Oceania

provided they meet the Journalism Fellowship eligibility requirements.

Visa Requirements for International Fellows

International applicants should understand that FASPE does not arrange visas on behalf of Fellows.

Selected participants are responsible for:

Making their own visa arrangements.

However, FASPE provides the necessary supporting documentation to assist selected Fellows with visa applications.

Candidates should therefore ensure that they are able to travel to Germany and Poland during the programme dates if selected.

No Religious, Racial or Gender Preference

Because FASPE’s historical curriculum includes the Holocaust and Nazi Germany, applicants sometimes assume the programme might prioritize candidates of a particular religious background.

FASPE explicitly says this is not the case.

There are no preferences based on:

Religion

Race

Ideology

Political background

Gender

Socioeconomic status

The organization also states that it welcomes applicants of diverse backgrounds and gender identities.

Selection is based on eligibility, professional and academic experience, leadership potential and the applicant’s capacity to contribute to the Fellowship.

What Journalism Ethics Topics Are Discussed?

The programme covers several major contemporary ethical challenges.

Journalistic Complicity and Misrepresentation

Fellows examine how German and international journalists participated in or enabled Nazi policy through:

Inadequate coverage

Misrepresentation

Professional compromise

The goal is not merely to assign historical blame.

Rather, participants ask what these cases reveal about contemporary journalists’ responsibilities when institutions or political systems begin to normalize harmful behavior.

Technology and Journalism

FASPE also examines:

The impact of technology on journalism.

This topic has become increasingly important as journalists work in an environment shaped by:

Social media

Artificial intelligence

Algorithmic distribution

Digital publishing

Platform economics

Rapid information circulation

Participants can consider how technological systems affect both professional practice and ethical responsibility.

Journalism and Electoral Politics

Another theme concerns the role of journalists in:

Electoral politics

Democratic accountability

Holding power to account

Journalists frequently have to balance:

Neutrality

Scrutiny

Public interest

Access

Fairness

Accountability

FASPE provides a space for Fellows to examine those tensions through an ethical rather than purely technical lens.

Advocacy Journalism

Participants examine:

The nature and propriety of advocacy journalism.

Questions can include:

Can a journalist advocate and still be fair?

What responsibilities come with taking a public position?

Does neutrality always serve the public?

When can advocacy undermine journalistic trust?

These questions are especially relevant in coverage involving:

Human rights

Climate change

Conflict

Social justice

Public health

Normalizing Aberrant Behavior

FASPE also examines how media coverage can:

Normalize aberrant behavior

through repetition, framing or treatment as ordinary political or social activity.

This raises important questions about:

Language

Headlines

Framing

False equivalence

Newsworthiness

Repetition

Context

Participants are encouraged to consider how routine journalistic practices can sometimes produce unintended ethical consequences.

Fake News and Accusations of Fake News

The Fellowship also addresses reporting in an environment where:

Disinformation is widespread

Journalists are regularly accused of producing “fake news”

Trust in media institutions may be weak

Fellows consider how journalists can maintain:

Accuracy

Verification

Independence

Transparency

Credibility

while operating within polarized information environments.

Access Journalism

Another ethical question concerns:

Access tactics

and the trade-offs involved in maintaining access to:

Politicians

Government officials

Institutions

Powerful sources

Journalists frequently face the possibility that aggressive scrutiny may reduce future access, while excessive accommodation may undermine independence.

FASPE encourages Fellows to examine where ethical responsibility lies when professional incentives conflict with public-interest reporting.

Interdisciplinary Learning

Journalism Fellows do not study entirely separately from other professional cohorts.

During the 2027 programme they travel alongside:

Medical Fellows

Clergy and Religious Leaders Fellows

Participants share:

Meals

Activities

Some seminars

This structure allows journalists to compare their ethical responsibilities with those of professionals in areas such as:

Medicine

Religion

Institutional leadership

FASPE believes this interdisciplinary element helps participants understand professional ethics beyond the assumptions of their own field.

The Fellowship Continues Beyond the Two-Week Programme

The FASPE experience does not end when participants return home.

Fellows become part of a lifetime alumni network that now includes more than 900 alumni across FASPE’s professional programmes.

FASPE supports continuing engagement through activities such as:

Alumni gatherings

Online education

Writing

Lectures

Symposia

Professional networking

Social networking

For emerging journalists, this network can create long-term connections with professionals who share an interest in ethical leadership.

Where Former Journalism Fellows Work

Former FASPE Journalism Fellows have gone on to careers as:

Editors

Reporters

Nonfiction writers

Photojournalists

Broadcasters

Other media professionals

FASPE emphasizes that Fellows frequently form long-lasting personal and professional relationships through their shared programme experience.

Connection With Columbia Journalism School

The FASPE Journalism programme was originally developed in consultation with faculty from:

Columbia Journalism School.

The programme has since developed its own international alumni network and interdisciplinary professional-ethics model.

How to Apply

FASPE requires all candidates to use its online application portal.

Apply for the 2027 FASPE Journalism Fellowship

Applicants should carefully review the application instructions before submitting.

Application Requirement 1: Online Form

Applicants must complete the online application form.

It requests basic information including:

Contact details

Educational institutions attended

Recommendation writers

References

Candidates should ensure that names and contact details are accurate, particularly because recommendation letters are handled separately through Submittable.

Application Requirement 2: Resume or CV

Applicants must submit a:

Resume or curriculum vitae

The document should include:

Educational history

Employment history

Honors

Awards

Publications where applicable

Journalism candidates should make relevant experience particularly easy to identify.

This could include:

Newsroom positions

Freelance work

Internships

Student journalism

Publications

Broadcast work

Documentary projects

Reporting awards

Application Requirement 3: Academic Transcripts

Applicants must provide transcripts from institutions of higher education where they spent significant periods of study.

FASPE accepts:

Electronic transcripts

Scanned hard-copy transcripts

Unofficial transcripts

However:

Screenshots of online transcripts are not accepted.

Applicants do not normally need to submit transcripts for brief experiences such as:

A single semester abroad

One summer course

What If You Are a First-Year Graduate Student?

Applicants in the first year of a programme may not yet have grades available.

In that situation, FASPE allows the applicant to provide a letter from the relevant dean confirming:

Enrollment in the degree programme

Good academic standing

Ideally, current courses

A general admissions letter or registrar letter that does not identify the degree programme is not sufficient.

Application Requirement 4: Journalism Short Essays

Journalism candidates must respond to:

Programme-specific short essay questions.

These questions are intended to give FASPE insight into the applicant’s:

Motivation

Professional identity

Ethical thinking

Capacity for reflection

Leadership potential

Ability to engage with difficult questions

The current How to Apply page provides the Journalism short-essay materials for the 2027 cycle.

Applicants should take these essays seriously.

The Fellowship is built around discussion and self-examination, so reflective writing may be just as important as demonstrating professional accomplishments.

Application Requirement 5: Two Letters of Recommendation

Applicants need:

Two recommendation letters

from:

Academic faculty, or

Professional references

For students, FASPE generally prefers recommendations from academic faculty who have taught the candidate in their current or most recent graduate programme.

However, recommendations can also come from:

Previous graduate faculty

Undergraduate professors

Professional supervisors

Employers

particularly for early-career professionals.

Recommendation Letter Deadline

An important detail is that recommendation letters have a later deadline than the main application.

Applicant deadline: January 3, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET

Recommendation deadline: January 10, 2027

Letters must be submitted:

Directly by the recommenders through Submittable.

Applicants should therefore enter referee information early enough to give recommenders adequate preparation time.

What FASPE Wants Recommenders to Address

FASPE says recommendation letters can usefully discuss areas including:

Academic work

Relevant professional experience

Experiences that would enrich discussions about professional ethics

Participation in discussion

Written and verbal communication

Responses to intellectually or emotionally intense situations

Ability to work and travel in small groups

Leadership potential

Professional strengths and weaknesses

Candidates should therefore select recommenders who know them meaningfully rather than choosing only the most prestigious person available.

How FASPE Selects Fellows

FASPE evaluates candidates using a combination of:

Academic background

Professional experience

Personal experience

Leadership potential

Capacity for self-reflection

Potential contribution to discussions

Potential contribution to the alumni network

The Fellowship is especially interested in applicants who are willing to question their own assumptions and participate respectfully in challenging conversations.

Preparing a Competitive FASPE Journalism Application

1. Demonstrate Real Journalism Commitment

If you are still studying, explain why journalism is not simply an extracurricular interest.

Show evidence such as:

Reporting

Student media

Freelance publication

Newsroom experience

Documentary work

Broadcast work

and explain where you want your journalism career to go.

2. Do Not Treat the Ethics Essays Like Generic Personal Statements

FASPE is specifically about professional ethics.

The strongest responses are likely to engage seriously with:

Ambiguity

Responsibility

Professional pressure

Personal vulnerability

Institutional power

Avoid writing only that ethics is “important.”

Explain how ethical conflicts actually arise in journalism.

3. Be Willing to Examine Your Own Vulnerabilities

A programme centered on ethical leadership is likely to value applicants who can identify the circumstances under which they themselves might make poor professional decisions.

For example:

Pressure to publish quickly

Desire for access

Career ambition

Organizational loyalty

Political assumptions

Fear of professional consequences

Self-reflection is stronger than presenting yourself as someone who would never make an ethical mistake.

4. Highlight Published Work Clearly

Because FASPE gives preference to applicants whose journalism has been published or broadcast by recognized news organizations, include relevant work prominently.

Provide clear information about:

Outlet

Date

Role

Type of journalism

where appropriate.

5. Choose Recommenders Who Can Discuss How You Think

A useful FASPE recommendation is not merely:

“This candidate received excellent grades.”

A stronger referee can discuss:

How you respond to disagreement

How you think through difficult problems

Your judgment

Your leadership potential

How you operate in groups

6. Show That You Can Participate in Difficult Dialogue

FASPE explicitly seeks Fellows capable of discussing controversial and emotionally difficult issues:

Responsibly and respectfully.

Your application should show intellectual confidence without presenting yourself as unwilling to reconsider your assumptions.

Key Details at a Glance

Programme: FASPE Journalism Fellowship

Year: 2027

Programme dates: June 18–July 2, 2027

Locations: Germany and Poland

Duration: Approximately two weeks

Number of Journalism Fellows: Around 13–16

Primary focus: Professional ethics and ethical leadership in journalism

Target applicants: Graduate students with journalism experience and early-career journalists

Career stage: Generally no more than 10 years of professional experience

Funding: Fully funded

Airfare: Covered

Programme transportation: Covered

Hotels: Covered

Admission fees: Covered

Programme materials: Covered

Group meals: Covered

Pocket money for non-group meals: Provided

Citizenship restriction: None

Application platform: Submittable

Main application deadline: January 3, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET

Recommendation deadline: January 10, 2027

Official FASPE Journalism Fellowship information

FASPE 2027 application instructions

Conclusion

The FASPE Journalism Fellowship 2027 offers journalism students and early-career journalists an unusual opportunity to spend two intensive weeks in Germany and Poland examining some of the most difficult ethical questions confronting the profession.

Rather than functioning as a conventional journalism skills course, the Fellowship focuses on the deeper responsibilities associated with being a journalist. Participants examine the conduct of journalists during the Nazi period and use those historical cases to explore contemporary questions involving media power, political accountability, technology, advocacy journalism, misinformation, professional access and the normalization of harmful behavior.

Approximately 13 to 16 Journalism Fellows are selected each year. Eligible applicants generally include graduate students with journalism experience who plan to enter the profession, Bachelor’s graduates currently working as journalists, and graduate-degree holders working as journalists. FASPE generally seeks candidates with no more than ten years of professional experience.

The Fellowship is particularly accessible because it is fully funded. FASPE covers airfare, programme transportation, hotels, admission costs, materials, group meals and pocket money for meals outside organized group activities. International applicants are also eligible for travel support.

There is no U.S. citizenship or residency requirement, and FASPE explicitly welcomes eligible applicants regardless of nationality. It also states that there are no preferences based on race, religion, ideology, political background, gender or socioeconomic status.

The 2027 Journalism programme will run from June 18 to July 2, 2027.

Applications must be submitted through Submittable by:

January 3, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET

and the two required recommendation letters must arrive by:

January 10, 2027.

For emerging journalists interested not simply in how to report, but in what responsibilities come with the power to report, the FASPE Journalism Fellowship offers a distinctive opportunity for professional reflection, international learning and long-term engagement with an interdisciplinary community of ethical leaders.

TITLE: Kickoff Meeting of the Climate Change and Health Innovation Hub for West and Central Africa (CHINNOVA) – Partners Converge with a Focus on Strengthening Health Systems’ Resilience to Climate Change

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
A two-day kickoff meeting for the Climate Change and Health Innovation Hub for West and Central Africa (CHINNOVA) project took place from January 27th to 28th, 2025. CHINNOVA is a 4.8 million Canadian Dollar project funded by the International Development Research Centre (IDRC), Canada, and the UK Foreign Commonwealth Development Office. The project is being implemented from 2025-2028 by a consortium led by the Association of African Universities, in partnership with the West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adapted Land use (WASCAL), Institut Pasteur de la Côte d’Ivoire (IPCI), and the University of Omar Bongo (Université Omar Bongo) in Gabon.

The kickoff meeting was organized by the Association of African Universities (AAU) at its headquarters in Accra, Ghana, in collaboration with WASCAL, IPCI, and Omar Bongo University (UOB). The event marked the formal launch of the CHINNOVA project, where participants clarified their roles and responsibilities, establishing a collaborative framework essential for successful project implementation.

Notable representatives from the organizing partner institutions attended the meeting, including the Principal Investigator and Director of Research and Programmes at the Association of African Universities (AAU), Prof. Frederick Ato Armah; the Director of WASCAL Competence Center in Ouagadougou, Prof. Kehinde Ogunjobi; and Dr. Andre Offianan and Dr. Seyni Salack, both from WASCAL. The Institut Pasteur de la Cote d’Ivoire (IPCI) was represented by its Director of Research, Dr. Soumahoro Man-Koumba, Dr. Coulibaly Julien Kalpy, and Dr. Tuo Karim. Prof. Aba’a Ibrahim, a researcher and Core Team Member, represented the University of Omar Bongo (Universite Omar Bongo) and Central Africa at the meeting. Prof. Doku Teye, a core team member of CHINNOVA and the Director at the Directorate of Research Innovation and Consultancy at the University of Cape Coast (UCC), attended the meeting, along with other team members from the AAU’s Secretariat who play various roles on the project.

The meeting commenced with a welcome address by Ms. Nodumo Dhlamini, Director for ICT, Communication, and Knowledge Management at the AAU, who provided an overview of the Association’s history and its integral role in facilitating higher education collaboration across Africa. Prof. Armah outlined the CHINNOVA project’s target to strengthen resilience in health systems to climate change through improving data availability, fostering interdisciplinary and inter-sectoral collaborations, and building the capacity of the health workforce.

Throughout the two-day meeting, participants engaged in substantive discussions covering critical topics related to the implementation of the project’s activities. These discussions were aimed at laying a strong foundation to foster the achievement of results and impact on the target beneficiaries and stakeholders. Participants deliberated on enhancing the availability and interoperability of climate and health data, with a particular emphasis on integrating gender equality and inclusion into health systems. They also discussed plans to address existing knowledge gaps through targeted training and capacity-building initiatives.

Discussions encompassed micro, meso, and macro-level considerations for the project, examining the project’s implications at various scales. The meeting also discussed the explicit roles and responsibilities for each partner institution regarding project execution, data collection, knowledge management, and monitoring and evaluation. Emphasis was placed on the composition of effective knowledge management strategies, including data storage, sharing, and usage, underscoring the significance of open access to data and publications.

A framework for monitoring and assessing the progress and impact of the project was outlined, emphasizing a commitment to continuous learning and adaptive management. Additionally, procedures for financial reporting, budget allocation, and auditing were reviewed to ensure transparency and accountability concerning the project resources.

The CHINNOVA kickoff meeting was a resounding success, achieving several key outcomes. Participants collectively developed a shared understanding of the project’s goals, objectives, and implementation strategies. A collaborative framework was established, clearly outlining the roles and responsibilities of each partner institution. The attendees also reviewed the detailed work plan for 2025, specifying key activities, timelines, and deliverables. The meeting facilitated networking among partners and stakeholders, laying the groundwork for stronger collaborations towards the achievement of the project’s goals.

TITLE: Call for Papers – 2023 Conference of Rectors, Vice-Chancellors & Presidents of African Universities (COREVIP 2023) by the Association of African Universities

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Note: Authors of selected papers will be funded to participate in this conference . Deadline for submission extended to March 10, 2023

Theme: Advancing Excellence in African Higher Education

African higher education has recorded phenomenal growth in the last decades creating opportunities for millions of students—and in the process, building capacities for national, social and economic advancement. The sector, which is currently estimated to enroll some 20 million students however still needs to scale up, as the enrollment rate for the sector continue to remain in single digits in many countries.

The expansion however brought about numerous nagging issues pertaining particularly to quality and excellence. Despite massive financial injection, the sector remains one of the most, if not the most financially challenged in the world with implications for every facet of the higher education landscape.

Consequently, the narrative on African higher education has been disproportionately exhibited in a deficit mode, typically highlighting it in a crisis and defective mode—permanently. This phenomenon has relentlessly pushed the debates and dialogues to focus on challenges and problems, instead of focusing on what has been achieved so far and dampening the opportunities for success and excellence.

Despite the challenges and issues that have confronted the sector, some pockets of excellence—typically at institutional or departmental levels—have been well recorded. Some meagre body of knowledge, experience and perspectives on how these entities have overcome—and even thrived exists, creating an opportunity for a more nuanced narrative in advancing African higher education.

The AAU’s year 2023 COREVIP will seek to focus specifically on excellence and successful initiatives, interventions and outcomes in African higher education by highlighting the key enabling elements within the sub-themes outlined below: The proposed sub-themes include, but not limited to:

Doctoral education

African Higher Education has witnessed massive expansion in the last decade opening up unprecedented opportunities for access. This trend is anticipated to continue and potentially increase more rapidly in the foreseeable future. Doctoral education resides centrally in this phenomenal development and its role in advancing excellence in African higher education cannot be overemphasized. Accordingly, efforts are underway to strengthen the doctoral education landscape in the continent which faces a plethora of challenges. The upcoming AAU Conference intends to extensively explore and propose relevant interventions and recommendations for the advancement of excellence in doctoral education in Africa.

Institutional differentiation

Despite the phenomenal expansion that the African higher education has witnessed, only little can be said about its differentiation. The new institutions have tended to copycat existing institutions in their form, content and culture—falling under a very strong spell of institutional isomorphism. This has undermined efforts of institutional and program diversity as well as establishing centers of excellence that are paramount in national higher education systems. The Conference will undertake a robust dialogue and analysis to advance institutional differentiation, among others, re-calibrate institutional mission and revisit existing (and dominating) modalities of delivery (by capitalizing on virtual/distance learning), in pursuit of excellence in higher education systems.

Partnership/cooperation and internationalization

Research and academic collaboration, as a phenomenon of internationalization, have taken center stage in promoting quality and advancing excellence. Institutional vigor, status and reputation are now measured in terms of the scope and magnitude of international partnerships and academic cooperation. Student mobility, academic exchange, joint research and program development have emerged as key aspects in advancing academic excellence. The Conference will explore the challenges of promoting internationalization, for instance rankings, and academic partnerships and advance relevant and appropriate approaches to foster it.

University-industry linkages

The importance of university-industry linkages has been well established in advancing multi-disciplinary research, public-private partnership, innovation, entrepreneurship and excellence. Of recent, entrepreneurship and public-private partnerships have garnered robust support, among others, to expand employment and job creation opportunities—key aspects of development in the continent. While the contributions of university-industry linkages in advancing excellence and relevance has long been well understood, this particular path to excellence has not been fully exploited for a number of reasons. The Conference, while identifying the impediments, will propose relevant and practical interventions to address it.

Funding and financing

The massive expansion of the higher education sector in Africa has not been matched with commensurate resources. The sector, which is striving to address a deficit in access, equity, quality, and excellence needs to scale up and diversify its sources of funding. It is well established that developing countries need to invest one percent (1%) of their Gross Domestic Product (GDP) towards research, yet, most countries are to pursue that in a more sustainable, strategic, and equitable manner. In countries where public funding for the sector has reached a threshold, multiple avenues of generating both public and private resources have been sought. As key to the advancement of excellence and quality in higher education, the Conference will deliberate on how African countries and their higher education institutions need to navigate the chronic challenges of financing the sector in the aftermath of post-Covid 19 and the global economic, social and political upheavals.

Role of intellectual diaspora

Africa has a huge untapped capital in the intellectual diaspora. The human, financial and technical potential of the intellectual diaspora in advancing African higher education has been well recognized, recently. The Carnegie Corporation of New York’s African Diaspora initiative in advancing higher education in the continent through the diaspora, is one case in point. Based on the lessons learned and experiences acquired—from such organizationally supported and also privately steered initiatives — the Conference will vigorously explore this emerging trend in advancing excellence in African higher education.

Deadline for submission of abstracts: Extended to 10th March, 2023

Deadline for submission of full papers: 15th May 2023

Interested individuals are invited to submit an abstract, of not more than 500 words, by 25th February, 2023 at https://event-mgt.aau.org/event/73/

TITLE: Call for Abstracts & Papers – Association of African Universities’ 16th Quadrennial General  Conference, 21-25 July, 2025 |Rabat, Morocco

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Introduction

As Africa strives to address socio-economic challenges and achieve sustainable growth, the transformation of the continent’s higher education institutions (HEIs) to drive innovation, address sustainable development goals (SDGs), and empower future generations becomes increasingly critical. Transforming Africa’s higher education institutions (HEIs) is no longer optional; it is an urgent imperative to address the continent’s socio-economic challenges and realize the vision of Africa’s Agenda 2063. By fostering innovation, driving sustainable development goals (SDGs), and equipping future generations with relevant skills, HEIs can catalyze Africa’s sustainable growth and prosperity.

The current challenges in higher education in Africa underscore the urgent need for comprehensive reforms and innovative approaches across the continent. The integration of innovation and entrepreneurship to enhance curriculum relevance; investment in research infrastructure; establishment of collaborative research networks; harnessing of digital technologies, particularly the expansion of e-learning platforms and incorporation of ICT in teaching and learning; introduction of industry-driven curriculum to strengthen university-industry linkages; and the establishment of technology transfer offices and business incubation hubs within HEIs are some of the known strategies that act as catalysts for higher education to drive innovation, economic growth, and sustainable development in Africa.

Conference Details and Objectives

The Association of African Universities (AAU), the apex organization for higher education in Africa, is organizing its 16th Quadrennial General Conference (QGC) in Rabat, Morocco, from July 21st to 25th, 2025. This flagship event is proudly hosted by two esteemed Moroccan AAU member institutions: Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P), host of the General Conference—and Mohammed V University (UM5), host of the AAU Governing Board Meeting.

Under the broader theme Shaping the Future of Higher Education for Innovation and Sustainable Development of Africa, this conference is set to achieve three main objectives, namely:

Enhancing access and equity in higher education to reduce barriers to entry and improve retention rates;

Fostering research and innovation ecosystems by providing funding and support for innovative projects that address local and regional challenges; and

Integrating Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into curricula and institutional practices to ensure that education contributes to sustainable societal transformation.

Sub-themes

Proposals are encouraged to address various forms of narratives under the nine (9) sub-themes supporting the main theme, namely:

• Sub-theme 1 – Policy, Governance and Advocacy for Transforming Higher Education

• Sub-theme 2 – Artificial Intelligence and Technology-driven Teaching and Learning in Higher Education Institutions

• Sub-theme 3 – Curricula Re-engineering and smooth Credit Transfer System

• Sub-theme 4 – Collaborative Research and Capacity Building

• Sub-theme 5 – Climate Change, Green Energy and Blue Economy

• Sub-theme 6 – Entrepreneurship Skills and Competencies

• Sub-theme 7 – Funding Infrastructural Development in Higher Educational Institutions

• Sub-theme 8 – Indigenous Knowledge and Preservation of Environment Through Culture

• Sub-theme 9 – Contribution of Higher Education to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)

Please access the Conference Concept Note for further information on the conference subthemes.

Call for Submissions:

This call for submissions represents a significant opportunity to contribute to the transformation of higher education in Africa. By addressing the critical issues outlined in the sub-themes, we can collectively shape a future where higher education serves as a catalyst for innovation, sustainable development, and the overall betterment of the African continent. The AAU invites researchers, educators, policymakers, practitioners, and stakeholders from across the African continent and beyond to submit their abstracts, papers, and case studies addressing the above sub-themes.

Submissions should provide innovative insights, practical solutions, and actionable recommendations that will shape the future of higher education for the innovation and sustainable development of Africa. We look forward to your valuable contributions and engagement in this crucial dialogue.

Submission Guidelines:

Submissions should clearly articulate the narrative type, thematic focus, proposed presentation modality, and relevance to the conference theme. Submissions should include a brief bio of the presenter(s) and contact information.

Abstracts should be between 150 and 300 words (see Call for Papers for further details on the

Conference website).

Full papers should not exceed 6,000 words.

All submissions must be in English or French.

Submissions should include the author’s name, affiliation, and contact information.

Deadline for abstract submission: Friday 28th March 2025 at 16:30 GMT.

Submissions should be sent to: https://indico.aau.org/event/1/abstracts/

Notification of successful abstracts: By Friday, 18th April 2025

Deadline for submission of full papers: Friday 13th June 2025 @ 16:30 GMT

Evaluation Criteria:

Submissions will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

• Relevance to the theme and sub-themes.

• Originality and innovation.

• Clarity of objectives and methodology.

• Practicality and applicability of recommendations.

• Contribution to the advancement of higher education in Africa.

Important Dates:

• Abstract Submission Deadline: Friday 28th March 2025

• Notification of Decision: By Friday 18th April 2025

• Conference Dates: 21st– 25th July 2025

Note: We are committed to hosting a high-quality conference that brings together experts from Africa and around the world. While we are unable to provide funding for paper presenters this

year, we have worked to keep conference registration fees as low as possible. Successful presenters will be responsible for their own conference travel expenses.
