TITLE: CERV-2026-DAPHNE: EU Grants to Prevent and Combat Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The European Union has opened the CERV-2026-DAPHNE Call for Proposals, a major funding opportunity under the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values (CERV) Programme designed to support organisations working to prevent and combat gender-based violence and violence against children.

With an estimated €21 million total budget, the call will support projects addressing victim protection and support, prevention of gender-based violence, child protection systems, implementation of European legal frameworks, and financial and capacity-building support for grassroots civil society organisations.

What Is the CERV-2026-DAPHNE Call?

The CERV-2026-DAPHNE call is part of the European Union’s broader effort to protect fundamental rights, promote equality and strengthen societies’ ability to prevent and respond to violence.

The Daphne strand of CERV specifically focuses on combating violence, including gender-based violence and violence against children. The 2026 call seeks projects that address different forms of violence through prevention, victim and survivor support, stronger child-protection systems, policy implementation and support to civil society.

The European Commission highlights that gender-based violence remains closely connected to gender inequality and can have significant social, human and economic consequences. The 2026 call also places particular emphasis on emerging forms of violence, including online and technology-facilitated violence.

The call is aligned with several EU policy frameworks, including the EU Gender Equality Strategy 2026–2030, the EU Strategy on the Rights of the Child, the Istanbul Convention and the EU Directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence.

Five Funding Priorities Under CERV-2026-DAPHNE

Applicants should carefully select the priority that most closely matches their organisation’s expertise and proposed project because one proposal can address only one of the five topics.

1. Supporting Intermediary Organisations and Grassroots Civil Society Organisations

Topic: CERV-2026-DAPHNE-REGRANTING

The first priority focuses on organisations that can act as intermediaries and provide financial support and capacity building to smaller grassroots civil society organisations working on gender-based violence and/or violence against children.

The objective is not simply to fund one organisation’s activities. Instead, successful intermediary organisations will be expected to create mechanisms through which funding and capacity-building support can reach smaller and grassroots organisations.

Particular attention is given to organisations operating in:

Remote areas

Rural communities

Underserved communities

Areas where grassroots organisations have limited access to funding

Settings where smaller civil society organisations have limited institutional capacity

Activities can address areas such as:

Domestic violence

Sexual violence

Gender-based cyberviolence

Violence against children

Victim protection

Victim-centred services

Access to justice

Medical and psychological support

Capacity building

Organisational development

Community-level prevention

For this priority, applicants must demonstrate recent experience in CSO capacity building and experience in awarding and managing grants in the relevant fields. The call requires at least three years of recent proven experience in implementing CSO capacity-building activities related to gender-based violence and/or violence against children.

Funding under Priority 1

Minimum requested grant: €1 million

Maximum requested grant: €2.5 million

Project duration: 36 months

Regranting: Mandatory

Application: Single applicant or consortium

Geographical scope: National or transnational

Click HERE to read more and apply.

2. Protecting and Supporting Victims and Survivors of Gender-Based Violence

Topic: CERV-2026-DAPHNE-PROTECTION

The second priority focuses on improving protection and support for victims and survivors of gender-based violence.

Projects can seek to strengthen services that help victims and survivors access appropriate support, protection and justice.

Potential areas of work include:

Victim support services

Survivor-centred approaches

Domestic violence services

Sexual violence support

Access to justice

Psychological and psychosocial support

Medical support

Protection mechanisms

Trauma-informed services

Support for children affected by domestic violence

Services for people facing multiple or intersecting forms of discrimination

The call encourages applicants to develop integrated approaches rather than isolated interventions.

Funding under Priority 2

Grant range: €200,000–€600,000

Duration: 12–24 months

Application: Consortium of at least two applicants

Scope: National or transnational

Public authority involvement: Recommended

Click HERE to read more and apply.

3. Preventing Gender-Based Violence

Topic: CERV-2026-DAPHNE-PREVENTION

The third priority focuses on preventing gender-based violence before it occurs and addressing the social, cultural and structural factors that contribute to violence.

Projects under this priority can focus on prevention strategies, awareness, education, behavioural change, community engagement, research, communication and other approaches that contribute to reducing gender-based violence.

Potential areas may include:

Prevention campaigns

Awareness-raising

Community education

Gender equality initiatives

Prevention of domestic violence

Prevention of sexual violence

Prevention of online gender-based violence

Addressing harmful social norms

Training professionals

Improving prevention systems

Community-based interventions

Research and evidence generation

Digital safety and prevention

The call places significant importance on integrating gender and non-discrimination considerations into project design.

Funding under Priority 3

Grant range: €200,000–€600,000

Duration: 12–24 months

Application: Consortium of at least two applicants

Scope: National or transnational

Public authority involvement: Recommended

Click HERE to read more and apply.

4. Supporting the EU Directive on Violence Against Women

Topic: CERV-2026-DAPHNE-CONVENTION-DIR

The fourth priority is specifically focused on supporting implementation of the Council of Europe Convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence, commonly known as the Istanbul Convention, as well as the EU Directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence.

This priority is particularly relevant for organisations working on:

Policy reform

Legislative implementation

Public administration

Legal systems

Gender-based violence policy

Domestic violence prevention

Victim protection

Training of relevant professionals

Awareness raising

Monitoring and evaluation

Research

Implementation of legislation

Institutional capacity building

Important eligibility distinction

For Priority 4, the lead applicant must be a public authority at national, regional or local level.

Co-applicants can include:

Public entities

Private non-profit organisations

Private for-profit organisations

International organisations

Funding under Priority 4

Grant range: €200,000–€600,000

Duration: 12–24 months

Application: Single applicant or consortium

Lead applicant: Public authority

Scope: National or transnational

Click HERE to read more and apply.

5. Strengthening Integrated Child Protection Systems

Topic: CERV-2026-DAPHNE-CHILDREN

The fifth priority focuses on strengthening integrated systems for protecting children from violence.

The European Commission promotes a coordinated, child-centred approach in which different sectors and institutions work together rather than operating separately.

Projects may address:

Child protection systems

Prevention of violence against children

Child-centred services

Cross-sectoral collaboration

Child safeguarding

Child participation

Prevention of child sexual abuse

Prevention of bullying and cyberbullying

Protection against domestic violence

Mental health and psychosocial support

Referral systems

Early identification and reporting

Monitoring and evaluation

Coordination between government agencies and civil society

Protection of children in vulnerable situations

The call recognises that violence against children can occur both offline and online and can include physical or mental violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation and sexual abuse.

Funding under Priority 5

Grant range: €200,000–€600,000

Duration: 12–24 months

Application: Consortium of at least two applicants

Scope: National or transnational

Public authority involvement: Mandatory

Organisations whose projects involve children must also have an appropriate child protection policy covering the required safeguarding areas.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Who Can Apply?

This is an important point: CERV-2026-DAPHNE is not an individual grant opportunity.

It is designed primarily for organisations and institutions, rather than individuals applying in their personal capacity.

Eligible applicants generally need to be legal entities, including public or private bodies, established in an eligible country. International organisations can also participate, and the call contains specific rules for entities without separate legal personality and other types of participants.

For priorities 2, 3 and 5, applications must generally be submitted by a consortium of at least two eligible applicants.

For Priority 1 and Priority 4, applications can be submitted either by a single applicant or by a consortium, subject to the specific requirements of the priority.

National or International Projects

Projects under all five priorities can be either:

National, or

Transnational

However, the consortium requirements differ by priority.

For organisations considering a transnational application, the partnership should provide clear added value rather than simply satisfying a formal requirement.

The European Commission specifically expects partnerships to demonstrate complementary expertise and an appropriate distribution of responsibilities and resources.

Key Areas That Could Make a Strong Proposal

A competitive application should go beyond describing the problem.

A strong proposal should clearly demonstrate:

A clearly defined problem

Evidence-based needs assessment

A clearly identified target population

A strong connection to one of the five priorities

A realistic intervention model

Strong organisational capacity

Appropriate partners

Clear roles and responsibilities

Measurable outputs and outcomes

A credible monitoring and evaluation system

A realistic budget

A strong sustainability plan

A dissemination and communication strategy

Alignment with EU values and policy priorities

The proposal should also demonstrate how its results can continue to generate impact beyond the period of EU funding. This is particularly important because Impact accounts for 20 of the 100 available evaluation points.

Important Compliance Requirements

Applicants should also pay close attention to compliance.

Organisations must have sufficient financial and operational capacity to implement the project.

The European Commission may assess:

Financial statements

Revenue

Deficits

Dependence on EU funding

Previous project experience

Staff qualifications

Technical resources

Organisational capacity

Organisations can also be excluded for serious issues such as certain financial, legal, tax, social-security, professional misconduct, fraud, corruption or other exclusion circumstances.

Application Process

Applications must be submitted electronically through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.

Paper applications are not accepted.

Applicants should:

Identify the most appropriate CERV-2026-DAPHNE priority.

Carefully review the eligibility requirements.

Confirm that the organisation and proposed partners are eligible.

Register the relevant entities in the Participant Register.

Develop the project concept.

Identify appropriate partners where a consortium is required.

Prepare the needs assessment.

Develop the methodology and work plan.

Establish measurable objectives and indicators.

Prepare the detailed budget.

Prepare CVs and supporting organisational documents.

Complete the application forms through the Submission System.

Upload the required supporting documents.

Review the proposal against the evaluation criteria.

Submit before the deadline.

The Commission states that beneficiaries and affiliated entities must be registered in the Participant Register before submitting the proposal and will undergo legal-entity validation.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity may be particularly relevant for eligible organisations such as:

Non-profit civil society organisations

NGOs

Women’s rights organisations

Organisations working on gender equality

Organisations working on gender-based violence

Organisations supporting survivors

Child protection organisations

Organisations working on violence prevention

Public authorities

Local and regional authorities

Research and policy organisations

International organisations

Organisations with expertise in child protection

Organisations working on digital violence and online safety

Organisations providing psychosocial or victim support

Organisations with experience in advocacy and policy implementation

However, eligibility depends on the specific priority, the applicant’s legal status, country of establishment, consortium requirements and other conditions.

Important Advice Before Applying

Applicants should not begin by writing the proposal.

The stronger approach is to first determine which of the five priorities is the best fit.

For example:

An organisation funding and strengthening grassroots CSOs may consider Priority 1.

A survivor-support organisation may consider Priority 2.

A prevention and awareness organisation may consider Priority 3.

A public authority working on implementation of relevant legislation may consider Priority 4.

A child protection organisation working on integrated systems may consider Priority 5.

The proposal should then be built around the selected priority rather than trying to make one project fit multiple priorities.

The Commission explicitly states that each proposal must address only one of the five topics.

Conclusion

The CERV-2026-DAPHNE Call for Proposals represents a substantial European Union funding opportunity for organisations working to prevent and combat gender-based violence and violence against children.

With an estimated €21 million available, the call provides funding across five major areas: grassroots civil society support through regranting, victim and survivor protection, prevention of gender-based violence, implementation of European frameworks on violence against women, and integrated child protection systems.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to organisations with demonstrated experience, strong partnerships, clear project designs and the operational and financial capacity to implement substantial interventions.

Applicants should carefully select the appropriate priority, verify their country’s eligibility, build a strong and appropriately sized partnership where required, develop an evidence-based needs assessment, prepare a realistic lump-sum budget and demonstrate measurable long-term impact.

The current deadline listed on the Funding & Tenders Portal is 5 November 2026 at 17:00 Brussels time. Because the call document still contains the earlier 3 November date, applicants should rely on the live Portal for the latest submission status and verify the deadline immediately before submitting.

TITLE: Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program 2026: Visiting Research Opportunity at Harvard University for Urban Problem-Solving and City Leadership

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program is inviting applications from researchers whose work aligns with the mission of the Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard University. The program supports rigorous, policy-relevant research focused on urban problem-solving and city leadership, with the aim of strengthening both academic scholarship and practical approaches to challenges facing cities.

Selected applicants will be appointed as Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars and will have the opportunity to spend either one semester or one full academic year in residence at the Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard University.

The program is designed to provide scholars with protected time to advance a specific research project while also participating in the intellectual community of the Center and contributing to selected academic activities.

Application Deadline: October 28, 2026

About the Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program

The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program is a new visiting scholar initiative of the Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard University.

The program seeks to build a lasting and collaborative community of researchers whose work can contribute to the practice of urban problem-solving and city leadership.

The program is particularly interested in research that can help cities and city leaders strengthen their capacity to:

Drive performance

Lead innovation

Deliver results for residents

Develop effective policies

Strengthen organizational capabilities

Use evidence and data effectively

Collaborate across sectors

The program therefore provides an opportunity for researchers to pursue rigorous research while engaging with a community focused on translating knowledge into better urban governance and outcomes.

What Is the Bloomberg Center for Cities?

The Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard University supports research and learning focused on helping cities and city leaders improve their ability to deliver results.

The Center’s interests extend across different dimensions of city leadership, management, organizational performance, innovation, evidence-based policymaking, data, artificial intelligence, and cross-sector collaboration.

The Visiting Scholars Program is intended to contribute to this broader mission by bringing researchers into the Center’s intellectual community for a dedicated period of research.

Research Areas of Interest

The Bloomberg Center for Cities supports research addressing significant questions related to urban problem-solving and city leadership.

Areas of particular interest include, but are not limited to:

1. Mayoral Leadership and Management Strategies

Research may examine how mayors and other city leaders manage organizations, implement priorities, lead change, and deliver results.

Applicants working on leadership and management approaches within cities may find alignment with this area of interest.

2. High-Performing Staff and Teams

Another area of interest is understanding the conditions that enable high-performing staff and teams.

Research could examine organizational environments, management practices, leadership approaches, or other factors that contribute to effective public-sector teams.

3. Organizational Capabilities for Innovation

The program is also interested in research examining how organizations develop the capabilities needed to innovate.

This can include questions surrounding organizational structures, leadership, management, processes, and other conditions that support innovation in city government.

4. Evidence-Based Policy Solutions

The Center is interested in evidence-based policy solutions and the capacity required to implement and deliver them.

This creates an opportunity for researchers to examine not only which policies work, but also the institutional and organizational capabilities needed to put those policies into practice.

5. Data and Artificial Intelligence

The use of data and artificial intelligence to strengthen decision-making is another area of particular interest.

Researchers may explore how data and AI can support better decision-making in urban environments.

6. Cross-Sector Collaboration

The program also highlights effective approaches to cross-sector collaboration.

Research in this area may examine how governments, organizations, communities, and other actors can work together to address complex urban challenges.

These areas are not presented as an exhaustive list. The broader focus is on research that advances understanding and practice in urban problem-solving and city leadership.

Program Structure

The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program is designed primarily to provide scholars with protected time for research.

During their residency, selected scholars will focus primarily on advancing the research project described in their application.

The residency can last for either:

One semester, or

One full academic year

This flexibility allows selected scholars to participate in the program for a period that fits the scope of their research and individual circumstances.

Research Focus During the Residency

The central purpose of the residency is to give scholars dedicated time to develop their proposed research.

The research project should be clearly defined in the application and should address a meaningful challenge related to urban problem-solving or city leadership.

While research will be the primary focus, scholars will also be expected to contribute to the intellectual life of the Bloomberg Center for Cities through a limited number of structured activities.

Activities and Expectations for Visiting Scholars

In addition to their research, Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars will participate in several activities during their residency.

Research Seminar

Scholars will be expected to host one research seminar per semester.

The seminar should focus on the scholar’s ongoing research or related themes.

This provides an opportunity to share research with members of the Center’s intellectual community and receive discussion and feedback.

Student Study Group

Scholars will also be expected to convene a student study group connected to their research.

The study group will:

Meet twice per month

Include monthly office hours

Facilitate discussion related to the scholar’s research

The study group is intended to facilitate discussion rather than function as formal classroom instruction.

Harvard Community Event

Each scholar will also organize one event, such as a talk or panel, that is open to the broader Harvard community.

This provides another opportunity for scholars to share ideas and engage with the wider university community.

Housing and Financial Support

The program provides housing near Harvard University for participating scholars.

In addition, financial assistance is available to help scholars dedicate sustained time to their proposed research project.

Depending on an individual scholar’s circumstances, financial support may be used to facilitate:

Course buyout

Other arrangements that allow the scholar to step back from regular academic obligations

Dedicated time to focus on the proposed research

The purpose of this support is to help selected scholars create sufficient protected time to advance their research during the residency.

Visa Support

The Bloomberg Center for Cities anticipates being able to sponsor visas for selected scholars, subject to:

Institutional policies

The individual scholar’s circumstances

International applicants should therefore consider the applicable visa and institutional requirements as part of the residency planning process.

Who Can Apply?

The program invites applications from researchers whose work aligns with the mission of the Bloomberg Center for Cities.

Applicants may come from:

Different disciplinary backgrounds

Different career stages

The program therefore does not restrict applicants to a single academic discipline, provided their research aligns with the Center’s mission and interests.

Academic Requirement

Applicants must hold a:

Doctoral degree (Ph.D. or comparable terminal research degree).

This is a core eligibility requirement for the program.

Current Academic or Research Appointment

At the time of application, applicants must also hold a current faculty or research appointment at one of the following:

A degree-granting university, or

A recognized research institution

Therefore, holding a doctoral degree alone is not sufficient. Applicants must also have a current qualifying faculty or research appointment when they apply.

Research Proposal Requirements

Applicants must submit a proposal describing the specific research project they intend to pursue during their residency.

The proposal is a central part of the application and should clearly explain the research project and its relevance to urban problem-solving and city leadership.

The proposal should address several important components.

1. Urban Problem or City Leadership Challenge

Applicants should clearly identify the urban problem or city leadership challenge their research will address.

The problem should be significant and connected to the broader mission of the Bloomberg Center for Cities.

2. Research Questions

The proposal should explain the specific research question or questions that the project will examine.

Applicants should also identify the theory or theories underpinning the work.

3. Research Design and Methodology

Applicants should describe the research design and methodological approach they intend to use.

This should demonstrate how the research questions will be investigated.

4. Significance for Research and Practice

Applicants should explain why the project matters to both:

The relevant research field, and

The practice of urban problem-solving

The program is particularly interested in work that can contribute not only to scholarship but also to real-world urban challenges.

5. Outputs and Potential Impact

The proposal should also identify the types of outputs envisioned and the potential impact of the research.

Applicants should therefore consider what their research could produce and how those outputs could contribute to scholarship and urban practice.

Selection Process

After applications are submitted, applicants may be invited to participate in an interview with members of a selection committee.

Following the selection process, successful applicants will be formally appointed as Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars.

The selection process therefore considers both the submitted application and, where applicable, the interview stage.

Selection Criteria

Applications will be evaluated based on several key criteria.

Clarity and Significance of the Research Problem

The selection committee will consider how clearly the applicant identifies the research problem and the significance of the issue being studied.

Strength of the Research Design

The quality and strength of the proposed research design will also be considered.

Applicants should clearly explain how their proposed methodology will address their research questions.

Contribution to Scholarship and Practice

The program will assess the potential contribution of the proposed research to:

Academic scholarship

The practice of urban problem-solving

This reflects the program’s emphasis on research that can have relevance beyond academia.

Alignment With the Bloomberg Center for Cities

Applications will also be evaluated based on their alignment with the mission and thematic interests of the Bloomberg Center for Cities.

Applicants should therefore clearly demonstrate how their proposed research connects with the Center’s focus on urban problem-solving and city leadership.

Program Timeline

The application timeline provided for the Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program is:

Stage
Date

Application Launch
September 16, 2026

Application Deadline
October 28, 2026

Notice of Selection
February

Applicants should complete and submit their application by October 28, 2026.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Prospective applicants should ensure that their application clearly connects their research with the program’s focus.

1. Define the Urban Challenge Clearly

Start by identifying the specific urban problem or city leadership challenge your research addresses.

2. Develop Clear Research Questions

Make sure the research questions are specific and directly connected to the problem you identify.

3. Explain the Research Methodology

Clearly describe how you intend to conduct the research and why the proposed methodology is appropriate.

4. Demonstrate Relevance to Urban Practice

Explain how the research could contribute to practical urban problem-solving, rather than focusing exclusively on its academic contribution.

5. Show Alignment With the Center

Connect your proposed project to relevant areas of interest at the Bloomberg Center for Cities, such as:

City leadership

Organizational performance

Innovation

Evidence-based policy

Data and AI

Cross-sector collaboration

6. Explain Potential Outputs

Identify what you expect the research to produce and how those outputs could potentially contribute to research and practice.

7. Consider the Residency Commitment

Applicants should consider whether a one-semester or full-year residency is appropriate for their research project and professional circumstances.

Click HERE to read more.

Why the Program May Be Valuable for Researchers

The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program combines several components that can support researchers working on urban challenges.

These include:

Protected time dedicated primarily to research

Residence at Harvard University’s Bloomberg Center for Cities

Access to an intellectual community focused on urban problem-solving

Housing near Harvard University

Financial assistance to support sustained research time

Opportunities to engage with students

Opportunities to organize research discussions and events

Potential visa sponsorship for selected scholars, subject to institutional policies and individual circumstances

Opportunities to connect academic research with practical urban leadership challenges

The program’s structure is particularly focused on creating an environment where scholars can advance a specific research project while contributing to a wider intellectual community.

Application Deadline

The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program application deadline is October 28, 2026.

Applications opened on September 16, 2026.

Prospective applicants should allow sufficient time to develop their research proposal, review their eligibility, and prepare the required application materials before the deadline.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The Bloomberg Harvard Visiting Scholars Program offers researchers an opportunity to spend one semester or one full academic year in residence at Harvard University’s Bloomberg Center for Cities, with protected time to advance a research project focused on urban problem-solving and city leadership.

The program welcomes researchers from different disciplinary backgrounds and career stages, provided they meet the core eligibility requirements of holding a Ph.D. or comparable terminal research degree and a current faculty or research appointment at a degree-granting university or recognized research institution.

Successful applicants will focus primarily on their proposed research while also contributing to the intellectual community through research seminars, student study groups, and a Harvard community event.

Researchers whose work addresses issues such as mayoral leadership, high-performing teams, organizational innovation, evidence-based policy, data and artificial intelligence, or cross-sector collaboration may find particular alignment with the Center’s areas of interest.

With applications closing on October 28, 2026, eligible researchers interested in advancing policy-relevant research on cities and urban leadership should review the program requirements and prepare their application before the deadline.

TITLE: World Bank Group Global Program on GovTech & Public Sector Innovation 2026 (Fully-funded)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: October 2, 2026

Applications are open for the World Bank Group Global Program on GovTech & Public Sector Innovation 2026. The World Bank, the Republic of Korea’s Ministry of the Interior and Safety (MOIS), and the National Information Society Agency (NIA) invite government institutions worldwide to apply for the GovTech Bootcamp on AI in Governance and Public Administration.

This initiative targets government institutions in low- and middle-income countries that are developing, piloting, or deploying AI-enabled solutions to strengthen public administration, service delivery, transparency, efficiency, and citizen engagement.

Participants will learn directly from practitioners who design, operate, and scale Korea’s public AI systems, engage with Korean and World Bank experts, and develop practical implementation roadmaps for their own AI initiatives. Following the bootcamp, participating teams will be able to receive follow-up support and technical feedback to help advance their initiatives, depending on the strength and viability of their proposals and the expert advice provided during the program.

Benefits

Up to five government teams will be selected to participate in a fully funded, five-day technical bootcamp in Seoul.

Eligibility

Open to government agencies from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), as classified by the World Bank’s income group methodology. The applying institution must be developing, piloting, or deploying an AI tool or application for the public sector that addresses a specific governance or administrative challenge.

Upper-middle-income countries are classified as LMICs under the World Bank’s income group methodology and are therefore eligible to apply.

Only government institutions may apply. The proposal must be led by and submitted on behalf of a government agency with direct institutional authority over the initiative.

Multiple agencies from the same country may submit separate proposals. However, only one team per country will be selected for the bootcamp.

Prior participation in World Bank programs does not disqualify an applicant.

Proposals at the concept, prototype, pilot, or deployment stage are all eligible. However, proposals that demonstrate concrete institutional backing and a specific, actionable plan will be prioritized over purely conceptual submissions.

Application

Information sessions for prospective applicants will be offered across three time zones. Applicants will be asked to describe the public sector challenge being addressed, the proposed AI solution, technical and data readiness, institutional support, implementation risks, learning objectives, and planned next steps following the bootcamp.

Applicants may also submit supporting materials, such as endorsement letters, technical diagrams, policy documents, budget commitments, or other relevant documents.

TITLE: Press Release – University of Namibia to co-host the 2023 Association of African Universities’ 22nd Conference of Rectors, Vice Chancellors and Presidents of African Universities (COREVIP)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Accra, Ghana and Windhoek, Namibia, 16th March 2023 – The Association of African Universities (AAU) in collaboration with the Republic of Namibia and the University of Namibia (UNAM) will be hosting the 22nd edition of the AAU’s Conference of Rectors, Vice Chancellors and Presidents of African Universities (COREVIP) from 4th – 7th July 2023, in Namibia.

The COREVIP is an assembly of the Chief Executive Officers of AAU member institutions or their representatives. It is held once every two years with the purpose of collectively examining themes identified as common concerns and priorities for the development of higher education in member institutions and Africa in general, making recommendations primarily to members, as well as to the Governing Board of the Association, and to the Secretariat, and acting as a mid-term forum for taking stock of the implementation of the decisions of the previous AAU General Conference and recommending corrective actions.

This year’s biennial event will assemble the leadership of higher education institutions, as well as other senior members of the university community, higher education policymakers, researchers, development partners and funding agencies as well as other stakeholders – from Africa and beyond – to collectively deliberate on issues of common concerns and priorities to the higher education community in Africa.

Holding under the overall theme: “Advancing Excellence in African Higher Education”, the Conference seeks to sharply focus on excellence and successful initiatives, interventions and outcomes in African higher education by highlighting the key enabling elements within the sub-themes. These are: 1. Doctoral Education; 2. Institutional Differentiation; 3. Partnership/Cooperation and Internationalisation; 4. University-Industry Linkages; 5. Funding and Financing, and 6. Role of Intellectual Diaspora.

The concept note for COREVIP is available in all the four official languages of the Association of African Universities – English, French, Arabic and Portuguese.

“With attendees joining from diverse backgrounds and countries, the 22nd COREVIP provides an unparalleled learning and networking platform to its participants. It is a golden opportunity for higher education stakeholders to expand their knowledgebase, identify new frameworks and strategies, discover innovative approaches, contribute to shaping Africa’s higher education sector and form new relationships while strengthening existing ones.”– said Prof. Olusola Oyewole, Secretary General of the AAU.

“In a globally competitive and digital age where research and innovation are critical for economic and social advancement, the 22nd COREVIP unravels the barriers that inhibit knowledge dissemination, networking and collaboration, while ensuring that higher education institutions in Africa are well placed to play a pivotal role as hubs for research excellence. This conference will endeavour to engage all key stakeholders and advocate for evidence-based and innovative approaches that address real problems confronting our continent” – said Prof. Dr. Kenneth Kamwi Matengu, Vice Chancellor of the University of Namibia and President of the Pan- African Universities.

All stakeholders are invited to visit the event website and register to participate in this conference via this link: https://events.aau.org/corevip/

Individuals and institutions from the academic, industry and development partner communities with aligned vision of promoting higher education advancement and excellence, and who wish to hold a side event, exhibit, sponsor the event, and or book a speaking slot, should contact: ransford@aau.org or ndarko@aau.org for further information.

Conference Organising Institutions

Association of African Universities (AAU) www.aau.org/ – Main Organiser

The Association of African Universities (AAU) is the apex higher education organization in Africa and represents the voice of Africa’s higher education on regional and international bodies. Established in Rabat (Morocco) in 1967, the AAU currently has a membership of over 400 institutions of higher learning across all the linguistic and geographic divides of Africa. Its headquarters is in Accra, Ghana and it currently has two regional offices – East Africa Regional Office (hosted by the University of Khartoum in Sudan) and the North Africa Regional Office (hosted by the Al Azhar University in Egypt), as well as a Country Office in Abuja, Nigeria.

The AAU supports African universities to deliver quality higher education and, as its niche, creates platforms for networking among its members. The Association enjoys a unique capacity for convening most of the higher education community in Africa to reflect and consult on key issues affecting education on the continent. The thrust of its base is the nimble deploying of advocacy, commissioning of studies, and acting and becoming the clearing house and intelligence arm for these higher education institutions on the continent.

The AAU operates in four languages namely, English, French, Arabic and Portuguese. It endeavours to raise the quality of higher education in Africa and strengthen its contribution to Africa’s development by fostering collaboration among its member institutions; providing support to their core functions of teaching, learning, research, and community engagement; and facilitating critical reflection on, and consensus-building around, issues affecting higher education and the development of Africa.

University of Namibia www.unam.edu.na/ – Host

The University of Namibia (UNAM) is the primary institution of tertiary education in Namibia, established by an Act of Parliament on 31August 1992. With 12 campuses located across the country, UNAM is a community-based institution recognised for its academic excellence, exceptional research and community development projects. The University has a diverse student body from 40 countries around the world and has grown rapidly to support a student population of over 25,000. UNAM offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes across various educational platforms, from natural to social sciences.

According to a study conducted by international expert Guillermo Lemarchand, titled Science and Technology & Information Platform for Namibia, UNAM is the leading contributor to new knowledge in the country. The University’s programmes are designed to ensure that each student is fully prepared for their chosen course of study, making UNAM increasingly becoming the university of choice for many citizens of the world. This is evidenced by its level of ranking among African higher education institutions, with The Times Higher Education World University Rankings of 13 October 2022 placing UNAM at 501-600.

UNAM’s alumni have also achieved success, with many recommended for promotion to associate or full professorship by international academic peers around the globe. To date, UNAM has graduated over 55,000 students who are serving the country in various sectors of the economy, with many occupying prominent positions in government, the private sector, and even worldwide.

TITLE: Global Futures Scholarships 2027 at the University of Manchester: More Than £6 Million in Funding for International Students

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The University of Manchester is offering a major scholarship opportunity for international students planning to begin undergraduate or master’s studies in September 2027. Through the Global Futures Scholarships 2027, the University is providing more than £6 million in scholarship awards, with more than 350 partial merit-based scholarships available for eligible international students.

The scholarships are designed for international students who intend to study full-time and on campus at the University of Manchester in Manchester, United Kingdom. Applicants must first secure an offer of admission for an eligible course beginning in September 2027 before they can apply for the scholarship.

Global Futures Scholarships 2027: Overview

The Global Futures Scholarships provide international students with an opportunity to receive financial support towards their studies at one of the UK’s major universities.

For the 2027 entry cycle, the University of Manchester states that it is offering:

More than £6 million in scholarship awards.

More than 350 partial merit-based scholarships.

Scholarships for both undergraduate students and master’s students.

Opportunities for eligible students from a specified list of countries.

Scholarships for students beginning their studies in September 2027.

The scholarship is particularly relevant to international applicants who are preparing applications to the University of Manchester and are seeking financial support for their studies.

What Are the Global Futures Scholarships?

The Global Futures Scholarships are international student scholarships offered by the University of Manchester for students entering eligible undergraduate and postgraduate taught master’s programmes.

For 2027 entry, the University describes the awards as partial merit-based scholarships. This means the scholarships are intended to provide financial support based on merit, rather than representing a full scholarship covering every cost associated with studying in the United Kingdom.

The University has allocated more than £6 million to the scholarship programme for international students starting their studies in September 2027.

Because the programme covers multiple countries and regions, the exact award amount, eligibility requirements and application deadline are not necessarily identical for every applicant. The University specifically advises applicants to consult the scholarship information for their country because the award level, eligibility criteria and application deadlines differ by region.

Who Can Apply for the Global Futures Scholarships 2027?

The opportunity is open to eligible international students who meet the University’s requirements.

According to the University of Manchester, applicants must satisfy the following fundamental conditions:

Be living in one of the countries covered by the scholarship.

Hold an offer from the University of Manchester.

Have an offer for a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester.

Be applying for a programme that starts in September 2027.

Complete the scholarship application process after receiving the relevant invitation from the University.

The scholarship is available to applicants at both undergraduate and master’s level, although the precise requirements may vary according to the applicant’s country and level of study.

Applicants should not assume that meeting the general scholarship conditions automatically guarantees eligibility, because the University indicates that individual country profiles contain specific criteria.

Scholarships Available for Undergraduate and Master’s Students

One of the important features of the Global Futures Scholarships 2027 is that the programme covers more than one level of university study.

The University states that there are more than 350 partial merit-based scholarships available for undergraduate and master’s students entering in 2027.

Undergraduate applicants

International students seeking to begin an undergraduate programme at the University of Manchester in September 2027 may be eligible to apply, provided they satisfy the applicable country-specific requirements and have an offer for an eligible full-time, on-campus course.

Applicants should therefore begin by researching suitable undergraduate programmes, checking their academic admission requirements and submitting their university application.

Master’s applicants

The scholarship also provides opportunities for eligible international students planning to begin master’s-level study in September 2027.

Master’s applicants must similarly hold an offer for an eligible full-time, on-campus course at the University of Manchester and satisfy the conditions applicable to their country.

The supplied scholarship information also notes that Taiwan is listed for postgraduate taught master’s only, making it important for applicants from each country to read their specific country profile carefully.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The Global Futures Scholarships are described by the University of Manchester as partial merit-based scholarships. The university’s 2027 announcement confirms that the overall scholarship programme has a value exceeding £6 million, with more than 350 awards available.

However, the supplied general scholarship page does not provide one universal scholarship amount for every recipient.

This is because the University states that the level of award differs by region. Applicants therefore need to consult the country-specific scholarship profile to determine the amount applicable to their particular country and programme.

Consequently, prospective applicants should not assume that every Global Futures Scholarship recipient will receive the same financial award.

Merit-Based Nature of the Scholarship

The Global Futures Scholarships are identified as partial merit-based scholarships.

Applicants should therefore pay attention not only to the admission requirements for their intended programme but also to the scholarship’s country-specific eligibility and selection requirements.

A strong university application should clearly demonstrate the applicant’s academic preparation and suitability for the chosen course. However, applicants should rely on the specific criteria provided by the University for their country when determining what information is required for the scholarship application.

Study Location: Manchester, United Kingdom

Successful applicants will study at The University of Manchester, located in Manchester, United Kingdom.

The scholarship requires students to hold an offer for a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester.

This means that the scholarship is not presented as an opportunity for online or part-time study under the general eligibility conditions provided on the scholarship page.

The University of Manchester is located on Oxford Road in Manchester, UK.

For international students, studying in Manchester can also provide an opportunity to experience a major UK city while undertaking university-level education in a global academic environment.

How to Apply for the Global Futures Scholarships 2027

The application process begins with applying for an eligible programme at the University of Manchester.

Step 1: Identify an eligible course

Applicants should first research the University of Manchester’s undergraduate or master’s programmes and identify a course that corresponds with their academic background and future study plans.

The scholarship requires the applicant to have an offer for a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester.

Step 2: Apply for admission to the University of Manchester

The next step is to submit an application for admission to the University.

Importantly, the scholarship is not presented as a standalone application that applicants can complete before obtaining university admission. The University states that applicants must hold an offer of a study place for a course beginning in September 2027.

Step 3: Receive an offer of study

Applicants must receive an offer for an eligible course beginning in September 2027.

Once an applicant has an appropriate offer, they can proceed to the scholarship application stage if they meet the other requirements.

Step 4: Complete the scholarship application

The University states that eligible offer-holders will be sent an online scholarship application form by email.

Applicants should therefore monitor the email address used during their university application process and carefully check messages from the University of Manchester.

Step 5: Check the country-specific deadline

One of the most important points for applicants is that there is no single universal deadline stated on the general Global Futures Scholarship page supplied here.

Instead, the University explains that application deadlines differ according to region.

Applicants should therefore check the scholarship profile for their specific country rather than relying on a deadline published for another country.

Deadline: Varies by country/region.

The University of Manchester states that the application deadlines differ for each region and directs applicants to their country-specific scholarship profiles for the applicable deadline.

Students should check the relevant country profile as soon as possible after reviewing their eligibility and receiving their university offer.

What Applicants Should Check Before Applying

Before beginning the scholarship application process, prospective students should carefully review the following:

1. Country eligibility

Confirm that you are living in one of the countries listed by the University for the Global Futures Scholarships.

2. Academic level

Determine whether your intended programme is at undergraduate or master’s level and whether the scholarship is available for that level in your country.

3. University admission

You must hold an offer from the University of Manchester for an eligible course.

4. Mode of study

The general scholarship requirement specifies a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester.

5. Programme start date

The course must begin in September 2027.

6. Country-specific requirements

Applicants should review the scholarship profile for their country because the award value and eligibility conditions differ by region.

7. Scholarship deadline

Check the deadline associated with your country rather than relying on information from another country.

8. Scholarship application invitation

Eligible offer-holders will receive information about the online scholarship application form by email.

Why Applicants Should Pay Attention to the Country Profile

The country profile is one of the most important parts of the Global Futures Scholarships application process.

Although the general scholarship page provides an overview of the programme, the University explicitly states that award levels, eligibility criteria and application deadlines differ by region.

For this reason, two applicants from different eligible countries may not necessarily have exactly the same scholarship conditions.

Applicants should therefore avoid relying exclusively on general scholarship information found on third-party websites, social media pages or scholarship blogs. The country-specific information provided by the University should be used when confirming the requirements that apply to an individual application.

Contact Information

Applicants who need additional information about the Global Futures Scholarships can contact the University of Manchester’s International Office.

The scholarship page provides the following contact email:

international@manchester.ac.uk

The University also provides an International Team that offers support and guidance to international students.

Official Scholarship Information

Applicants should always verify the latest requirements, country-specific eligibility conditions, scholarship value and deadline directly with the University of Manchester before submitting an application.

Visit HERE for more information about the Global Futures Scholarships 2027 at the University of Manchester.

Conclusion

The Global Futures Scholarships 2027 provide a significant funding opportunity for eligible international students seeking to study at the University of Manchester. For the September 2027 intake, the University is offering more than 350 partial merit-based scholarships, with the total value of awards exceeding £6 million.

The opportunity is open to eligible students at undergraduate and master’s level from a specified group of countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and other regions. However, eligibility is country-specific, and applicants must meet the applicable requirements for their country.

A key requirement is that applicants must have an offer for a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester beginning in September 2027. Eligible offer-holders will subsequently be invited to complete an online scholarship application.

Because scholarship amounts, eligibility requirements and deadlines vary by region, prospective applicants should carefully review the country-specific scholarship information and ensure that they meet the requirements before applying. The general scholarship page does not provide one universal deadline; instead, applicants must check the deadline applicable to their country.

TITLE: FRIAS Senior Fellowship Programme 2027/2028

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 18, 2026

Applications are open for the FRIAS Senior Fellowship Programme 2027/2028. The Freiburg Institute for Advanced Studies (FRIAS) is the international research college of the University of Freiburg. It brings together scholars from Freiburg and around the world, offering temporary fellowships that allow researchers to focus entirely on their projects within a vibrant community of diverse cultural and academic backgrounds. FRIAS provides exceptional support to help fellows succeed.

For the academic year 2027/28, FRIAS is offering individual Senior Fellowships to researchers from any nationality and discipline based in Freiburg, Germany and abroad. The programme offers access to the resources, networks, and academic community of the University of Freiburg, enhancing your research through new perspectives and collaborative opportunities.

Fellowship

Depending on their situation, selected applicants will either receive a fellowship contract with the University of Freiburg or other compensation.

Fellows receive a research cost contribution and travel costs for the inbound and the outbound journey (if applicable).

Eligibility

Applicants must hold a completed doctoral degree plus a minimum of eight years of post-doctoral experience.

Applicants must have 10 peer-reviewed publications since 1 January 2020.

Applicants must have at least six months’ research or study experience at academic institution(s) in a country different from the country of their first academic degree by the time of application.

Fellowships will be awarded to individuals with challenging and innovative research projects of top academic quality through a highly competitive, strictly merit-based selection process (expected success rate: ~5% of eligible applications).

Applications are welcome from any discipline that can be supported at the University of Freiburg. FRIAS encourages applicants to learn more about the University of Freiburg’s research strengths and areas of focus.

Application

Information on the candidate and project (abstract, Layman’s abstract to communicate the research project to a general public, ethical issue table, motivation statement) must be filled into the online application form.

Additionally, the following attachments are required to be uploaded to the application portal:

Project proposal (max. 3000 words including footnotes, headers, footers, and bibliographical references, 4 graphs) PDF, for mandatory structure refer to the application manual)

CV in tabular form (PDF, mandatory template available in the application portal)

Publication list (PDF): Applicants must provide a list of publications that may not exceed 15 publications in total. 10 of those publications must be published after 1 January 2020 and must be peer-reviewed (Mandatory template available in the application portal)

Copy of the PhD diploma (PDF)

Letter of support (PDF): identifying a host laboratory in Freiburg where the research project can be carried out; only applicable to experimental scientists

Experiment sketch and timetable (PDF): only applicable to experimental scientists, who are required to submit a sketch and timetable of the experiments they wish to conduct in Freiburg

TITLE: Skills & Innovation Academy Ghana 2026: GIZ Opens 5-Day Employability Training for Graduates in Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the Skills & Innovation Academy 2026, an intensive five-day professional development programme designed to help graduates strengthen their technical and soft skills and improve their readiness for the world of work.

The current application round targets graduates based in four regions of Ghana:

Greater Accra

Bono

Northern Region

Upper West Region

The Academy is an initiative of Invest for Jobs – Special Initiative “Decent Work for a Just Transition”, an initiative of Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. GIZ Ghana’s current call describes the programme as an intensive five-day technical and soft-skills training aimed at improving participants’ employability.

The application deadline is:

23 September 2026

Interested candidates can submit their applications through the official registration form.

Apply for the Skills & Innovation Academy 2026

About the Skills & Innovation Academy

The Skills & Innovation Academy is a short, intensive employability training initiative designed to help graduates strengthen the practical skills needed to transition more effectively into employment.

The current September 2026 call invites graduates from Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West who want to upgrade their skills and improve their employability. Participants will take part in five days of technical and soft-skills training focused on preparing them for the demands of the workplace.

The programme is particularly relevant to graduates who may already have academic qualifications but want additional practical preparation before entering or progressing in the labour market.

It reflects a wider challenge facing many young graduates: completing formal education does not always mean that a person has had sufficient opportunities to develop the practical, interpersonal and workplace skills employers expect.

The Academy therefore seeks to help bridge the space between:

Academic learning and employment

Technical knowledge and workplace application

Qualifications and job readiness

Graduate potential and employer expectations

Who Is Behind the Skills & Innovation Academy?

The Academy is linked to Invest for Jobs – Special Initiative “Decent Work for a Just Transition.”

The initiative is supported by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development of Germany, BMZ, and implemented by GIZ. The current call was published by GIZ Ghana.

GIZ is Germany’s international cooperation agency and works with governments, private-sector institutions, civil society and other partners on programmes connected to areas such as:

Employment

Economic development

Skills

Governance

Sustainability

Private-sector development

Innovation

Within Ghana, the Skills & Innovation Academy fits particularly closely with employment and workforce-development objectives.

What Is Invest for Jobs?

Invest for Jobs is associated with the German development cooperation initiative focused on supporting decent employment and sustainable economic development.

For graduates, programmes supported under this framework may be particularly valuable because they focus not only on education in the abstract, but on the transition into actual economic and professional opportunities.

The Skills & Innovation Academy therefore emphasizes practical preparation for work rather than purely academic instruction.

What Does the Programme Offer?

The current call describes the Academy as an:

Intensive 5-day technical and soft-skills training programme.

Its central objective is to equip participants with practical skills that can help them function more effectively in the workplace and compete for employment opportunities.

The programme combines two broad areas:

1. Technical Skills

Technical skills are the practical or job-related capabilities people need to perform professional tasks.

The exact technical modules for the September 2026 cohort are not listed in the public announcement provided by GIZ Ghana.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that a specific technology, profession or vocational field is guaranteed unless it is stated in the registration form or communicated directly by programme organizers.

The important point from the current call is that technical training forms part of the five-day programme.

2. Soft Skills

Soft skills refer to the interpersonal and professional behaviours that help employees function successfully in organizations.

These can generally relate to areas such as:

Communication

Teamwork

Professionalism

Problem-solving

Workplace behaviour

Adaptability

Collaboration

Self-management

However, the current public call does not publish a detailed list of the September cohort’s exact soft-skills modules.

Applicants should therefore rely on the current registration materials for the definitive curriculum.

Why Soft Skills Matter for Graduates

Employers often evaluate candidates on more than academic qualifications.

A graduate may have strong academic knowledge but still need to develop the ability to:

Communicate clearly

Collaborate with colleagues

Manage responsibilities

Present ideas professionally

Adapt to workplace expectations

Solve practical problems

Demonstrate initiative

This is one reason short employability programmes can be useful during the transition between education and work.

The Skills & Innovation Academy specifically positions itself around strengthening employability through both technical and interpersonal development.

The Academy Is Focused on Practical Employability

The wording of the current call is important.

GIZ Ghana does not describe this as a theoretical academic course. It says the training is intended to equip participants with practical skills for the world of work.

That means the Academy should be particularly relevant to individuals who want to become more workplace-ready.

Potential participants may include graduates who are:

Searching for their first job

Preparing for employment

Trying to strengthen their professional profile

Looking to build practical skills after graduation

Seeking to improve confidence in professional environments

Preparing to transition into a new career area

Programme Duration

The Skills & Innovation Academy lasts:

Five days

The training is described as intensive, meaning participants should expect a concentrated learning schedule rather than a long-term part-time programme.

Applicants should ensure that they can commit to the programme once selected.

The current public announcement does not specify the exact training dates or daily schedule, so selected participants should rely on instructions from GIZ or the implementing team.

Is This a Job?

No.

The Skills & Innovation Academy is a training and employability development programme.

Applicants should not interpret participation as:

A job offer

Guaranteed employment

An internship

A paid position

Its purpose is to strengthen participants’ skills and employability.

The public call does not state that completion automatically results in placement with an employer.

Is This a Scholarship?

No.

The opportunity is not advertised as an academic scholarship.

Participants are not applying for:

University tuition

A degree

Research funding

Academic study abroad

Instead, they are applying for a short professional skills-development programme.

Is There a Stipend or Financial Allowance?

The current September 2026 public call does not state that participants will receive a stipend, transport allowance, accommodation allowance or cash payment.

It also does not publicly specify:

Training fee

Accommodation provision

Meals

Transport support

Certificate

Employment guarantee

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that these benefits are included unless the registration form or organizers confirm them.

This is especially important when promoting the opportunity: it should not be described as “fully funded” based solely on the currently published announcement.

Current Target Regions

The September 2026 call specifically targets graduates in:

Greater Accra

Greater Accra is Ghana’s main administrative and economic centre and includes Accra and its surrounding metropolitan areas.

Graduates living in this region form one of the target groups for the current round.

Bono Region

Graduates in the Bono Region are also invited to participate.

Northern Region

The current programme expands access to graduates in Northern Ghana through inclusion of the Northern Region.

Upper West Region

Graduates based in Upper West are also among the target participants.

The geographical targeting is therefore not nationwide in the current announcement.

A Region-Based Programme Model

The Skills & Innovation Academy appears to use different regional application rounds.

For example, an earlier GIZ Ghana round in June 2026 targeted applicants in:

Greater Accra

Eastern Region

Volta Region

and described eligibility for that particular round as SHS graduate or higher.

The current September round is different: it specifically names:

Greater Accra

Bono

Northern

Upper West

and simply refers to applicants as graduates.

Applicants should therefore follow the requirements of the current September 2026 call, rather than assuming that every criterion from an earlier regional round automatically applies.

What Academic Qualification Is Required?

The current public announcement asks:

“Are you a graduate in the Greater Accra, Bono, Northern & Upper West…”

However, it does not publicly define the precise educational level meant by “graduate” in the current call.

For example, the announcement does not explicitly state whether the September round requires:

SHS completion

Diploma

HND

Bachelor’s degree

University degree

Any post-secondary qualification

An earlier 2026 round explicitly said SHS graduate or higher, but the current September announcement does not repeat that exact wording.

Therefore, applicants should complete the official form and follow the current eligibility questions rather than assuming a specific tertiary degree is compulsory.

Is There an Age Limit?

The current Skills & Innovation Academy announcement does not state an age limit.

It does not publicly specify:

Minimum age

Maximum age

A youth age bracket such as 18–35

Therefore, an age restriction should not be added to promotional material unless it appears in the current application form.

Is Work Experience Required?

The current call does not state a minimum work-experience requirement.

Applicants are therefore not publicly required to have:

One year of experience

Two years of experience

Prior professional employment

Previous internship experience

The programme is presented around strengthening graduate employability, which suggests that it is particularly relevant to people at an early stage of their careers.

What Fields of Study Can Apply?

The current announcement does not restrict participation to one academic field.

It does not state that candidates must be graduates of:

STEM

Business

Engineering

IT

Humanities

Social sciences

or another specific discipline.

The wording is broad: graduates seeking to improve their skills and employability.

Applicants from different academic backgrounds may therefore consider applying, unless the registration form contains additional track-specific requirements.

What Participants Could Gain

Although the current call does not publish an exhaustive list of outputs, the programme is designed to improve participants’ readiness for employment.

Potential professional value includes:

Stronger Workplace Skills

Participants can develop a better understanding of the behaviours and practical abilities needed in professional environments.

Improved Technical Capacity

The programme includes technical-skills training alongside soft skills.

Greater Employability

The Academy is explicitly marketed as an opportunity to upgrade skills and improve employability.

Professional Development

A concentrated skills programme can help graduates identify areas requiring further development before applying for jobs.

Why Employability Training Matters

The transition from education into employment can be difficult, particularly where graduates have limited opportunities to gain workplace experience.

Common challenges can include:

Limited practical experience

Lack of familiarity with workplace expectations

Difficulty translating qualifications into job-ready skills

Weak interview preparation

Limited professional networks

Insufficient soft-skills training

Programmes such as the Skills & Innovation Academy seek to strengthen the practical side of graduate preparation.

How to Apply

Applications are submitted through the official online registration form.

Apply for the Skills & Innovation Academy 2026

Candidates should provide accurate information and carefully review all questions before submitting.

The public call also notes that applicants can register through the QR code displayed on the programme flyer.

Application Deadline

The deadline is:

23 September 2026

GIZ Ghana’s current public announcement confirms this closing date.

Applicants should consider submitting early in case they experience:

Connectivity problems

Form errors

Missing documents

Last-minute technical difficulties

How to Prepare Before Applying

1. Review Your Educational Information

Have accurate details of your:

Educational institution

Qualification

Field of study

Graduation status

ready before beginning.

2. Be Clear About Your Employment Goals

If the form asks why you want to join, avoid generic answers such as:

“I want to gain skills.”

Instead explain:

What career area you want to enter

What skills you currently lack

Why the programme would help you

How you intend to use the training

3. Explain Your Employability Gap

A strong response might identify a practical challenge such as:

Limited professional experience

Weak digital skills

Limited workplace exposure

Need for stronger communication skills

Difficulty transitioning from school to employment

Then explain how training could help address it.

4. Demonstrate Commitment

A five-day intensive programme requires active participation.

If asked about availability, applicants should ensure they can attend the full programme.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity may be especially relevant if you:

Have recently graduated

Are searching for employment

Want to strengthen your practical skills

Want stronger workplace readiness

Live in one of the targeted regions

Can commit to an intensive five-day programme

Key Information at a Glance

Programme: Skills & Innovation Academy 2026

Country: Ghana

Organizer/Implementer: GIZ Ghana

Initiative: Invest for Jobs – Special Initiative “Decent Work for a Just Transition”

Supporting ministry: German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)

Duration: 5 days

Training focus: Technical and soft skills

Purpose: Improve practical skills and employability

Target participants: Graduates

Regions: Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West

Deadline: 23 September 2026

Application method: Online registration

Application link:
Skills & Innovation Academy registration form

The current call does not publicly state a stipend, job guarantee, accommodation package, participation allowance, age restriction or precise academic degree threshold.

Conclusion

The Skills & Innovation Academy Ghana 2026 offers graduates in Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West an opportunity to spend five intensive days strengthening practical technical and soft skills for the workplace.

The programme is part of Invest for Jobs – Special Initiative “Decent Work for a Just Transition,” supported by Germany’s BMZ and implemented by GIZ. Its emphasis is firmly on employability: helping graduates strengthen the competencies needed to transition more effectively from education into professional environments.

The current call does not promise employment, a stipend or an internship. It should instead be understood as a short professional-development and skills-training opportunity.

Applicants should also pay attention to the regional eligibility. The September 2026 round specifically names graduates located in Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West, and should not automatically be promoted as open to every region of Ghana.
