TITLE: WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027 for Young Ugandan Environmental Leaders – 9-Month Fully Funded Leadership Programme

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027, an intensive nine-month virtual leadership development programme designed to support young Ugandans who are actively contributing to conservation, climate action, environmental education, sustainable development, or community transformation.

Organised by WWF International in collaboration with the Amano So Global Mentorship Network, the fellowship provides emerging environmental leaders with access to mentorship, expert-led workshops, peer learning, strategic leadership development and an international network of young changemakers.

The programme is particularly suitable for young people who are already taking action in their communities and want to strengthen their ability to create meaningful and lasting impact for nature, people and sustainable development.

About the WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027

The WWF-Amano Fellowship is a nine-month virtual leadership development programme created to help emerging conservation and environmental leaders develop the knowledge, confidence, networks and practical leadership skills required to advance positive change.

The fellowship combines several areas of development, including:

Conservation awareness

Leadership development

Strategic thinking

Emotional resilience

Mentorship

Peer learning

Community engagement

Environmental advocacy

One of the major advantages of the programme is its virtual format. Fellows can participate in the programme while continuing their existing employment, education, businesses, conservation activities or community initiatives.

Rather than requiring participants to leave their ongoing work, the fellowship is designed to complement what they are already doing.

What Is the Aim of the WWF-Amano Fellowship?

The programme is focused on developing a new generation of environmental leaders who can contribute to biodiversity conservation and sustainable development at the community level.

Many environmental challenges require strong leadership beyond technical knowledge. Young people working in conservation and community development may need to understand how to build partnerships, influence decision-makers, communicate effectively, develop strategies and maintain resilience when working on complex environmental issues.

The WWF-Amano Fellowship seeks to strengthen these abilities by bringing together young changemakers for a structured learning and mentorship experience.

Through the programme, fellows can develop the capacity to:

Strengthen their leadership abilities.

Improve their strategic thinking.

Build professional and personal networks.

Learn from experienced conservation professionals.

Exchange ideas with other young environmental leaders.

Better understand conservation and sustainable development challenges.

Increase their ability to influence environmental initiatives and policies.

Develop approaches for creating measurable community impact.

Fellowship Duration and Format

The WWF-Amano Fellowship will run for nine months.

The programme will be conducted online, allowing participants to remain active in their existing professional, academic or community activities.

The virtual programme is expected to involve activities such as:

Mentorship meetings

Group mentoring sessions

One-on-one coaching

Expert-led workshops

Guest speaker sessions

Peer discussions

Knowledge-sharing activities

Other online learning and leadership development activities

Participants will therefore need access to a reliable internet connection and sufficient time to participate consistently.

Key Benefits of the WWF-Amano Fellowship

Selected fellows will have access to several leadership and professional development opportunities.

1. Group Mentoring

Participants will take part in group mentoring with experienced conservation professionals. These sessions provide opportunities to learn from individuals with practical experience in environmental and conservation work.

2. Personalised One-on-One Coaching

The programme also provides personalised coaching, allowing fellows to receive more focused guidance as they develop their leadership capabilities.

3. Expert-Led Workshops

Fellows will participate in interactive workshops led by experienced environmental leaders and professionals.

These sessions are intended to strengthen practical knowledge and expose participants to different approaches to conservation, leadership and sustainable development.

4. International and Regional Networking

The fellowship brings together young changemakers from Uganda, Africa and beyond.

This provides an opportunity to establish relationships with other people working on environmental and community issues and potentially develop future collaborations.

5. Peer Learning

Participants will have opportunities to share experiences, challenges and solutions with fellow environmental leaders.

Peer learning can be particularly valuable because participants may be working on different environmental challenges and can learn from approaches being used in other communities.

6. Leadership Development

The programme focuses strongly on developing leadership capabilities, including strategic thinking, confidence, resilience and the ability to influence positive change.

7. Greater Conservation Knowledge

Fellows can strengthen their understanding of conservation and sustainable development issues and explore approaches that can be applied within their own communities.

8. Stronger Professional Networks

Participants can build social and professional capital that may help them engage more effectively with conservation initiatives, community organisations and environmental policy processes.

9. Practical Community Impact

The fellowship is designed for people who are already involved in creating positive change. The knowledge, mentorship and networks gained through the programme can therefore be applied to existing or future community and environmental initiatives.

Who Is the WWF-Amano Fellowship Looking For?

The programme is intended for young Ugandan environmental and community leaders aged 21–30.

Applicants should be people who are already demonstrating a commitment to environmental or community-based action rather than individuals with no previous involvement in these areas.

The programme particularly welcomes applicants who are contributing to areas such as:

Nature conservation

Biodiversity protection

Climate advocacy

Environmental education

Sustainable entrepreneurship

Community development

Environmental awareness

Conservation-related initiatives

Other activities contributing to positive environmental or community change

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered for the WWF-Amano Fellowship, applicants should meet the following requirements.

Age

Applicants must be 21 to 30 years old.

Nationality

The fellowship is specifically open to young Ugandans.

Demonstrated Environmental or Community Engagement

Applicants should have evidence that they have been involved in conservation, environmental activities, climate advocacy, environmental education, sustainable entrepreneurship or related community initiatives.

The fellowship is therefore aimed at emerging leaders who are already doing work that contributes to positive change.

Evidence of Impact

Applicants are expected to demonstrate how their work, project or initiative has contributed to positive environmental or community outcomes.

This could include involvement in projects, advocacy activities, education initiatives, conservation programmes, community mobilisation or other relevant work.

English Language

Applicants must have strong spoken and written English skills because programme activities will be conducted in English.

Time Commitment

Fellows must be able to dedicate approximately 5–8 hours per month to fellowship activities.

This may include:

Mentor group meetings

Expert workshops

Guest speaker sessions

Peer discussions

Other fellowship activities

Internet Access

Because the fellowship is delivered virtually, applicants should have reliable internet connectivity that allows them to participate in online meetings, workshops and other programme activities.

Who Is Particularly Encouraged to Apply?

The programme highlights the importance of supporting diverse and emerging environmental leaders.

In particular, the fellowship encourages applications from:

Individuals from local communities involved in conservation.

Individuals from Indigenous communities with demonstrated conservation involvement.

Young women working in environmental and conservation fields.

Applicants from underserved or marginalised communities.

Early-career emerging environmental leaders.

Mid-career emerging leaders who meet the age and other requirements.

The key consideration is that applicants should be able to demonstrate genuine involvement and positive impact in conservation, environmental action or community development.

What Kind of Experience Can Strengthen an Application?

Applicants should be able to demonstrate practical involvement in environmental or community activities.

Relevant experience may include participation in:

Conservation projects

Climate action campaigns

Environmental education programmes

Community environmental initiatives

Sustainable businesses or entrepreneurship

Biodiversity-related activities

Community awareness campaigns

Environmental advocacy

Youth-led environmental initiatives

Projects addressing local environmental challenges

Applicants should focus on demonstrating what they have done, the role they played and the impact their work created.

How to Apply for the WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027

Interested applicants are required to prepare a one-page brief about themselves.

The brief should highlight the applicant’s:

Background

Leadership experience

Conservation involvement

Environmental activities

Community engagement

Relevant achievements or impact

The application should clearly provide the following information:

Full name

Date of birth

Email address

Telephone number

Evidence of conservation, environmental or community engagement experience

Applicants should ensure that their information is clear, accurate and easy to review.

Where to Submit the Application

Applications should be submitted by email to:

recruitment@wwfuganda.org

Applicants should ensure that their application reaches the organisation before the stated deadline.

WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027 Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

16 September 2026

Applicants are encouraged to prepare and submit their applications early rather than waiting until the final day.

Since the application requires evidence of previous conservation, environmental or community engagement, applicants should allow enough time to prepare a clear one-page profile and supporting information.

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Young Environmental Leaders

Environmental leadership requires more than simply understanding environmental problems. Young leaders often need the ability to mobilise communities, communicate ideas, build partnerships, influence policies and develop practical solutions.

The WWF-Amano Fellowship combines leadership development with conservation awareness, mentorship and networking.

For a young Ugandan already working on environmental or community issues, the programme could therefore provide an opportunity to strengthen existing capabilities while remaining engaged in ongoing activities.

The emphasis on strategic thinking, emotional resilience and peer learning can also help participants approach complex environmental challenges with greater confidence and a broader perspective.

Learn more about this opportunity HERE

Application Preparation Tips

Before submitting an application, prospective applicants should consider the following:

Clearly explain your impact

Do not simply list environmental activities you have participated in. Explain what you actually contributed and what changed as a result.

Highlight leadership

The fellowship is a leadership development programme, so applicants should demonstrate examples of taking initiative, leading activities, mobilising people or helping to solve community problems.

Keep the one-page profile focused

Because the application requires a one-page brief, applicants should prioritise their strongest and most relevant experiences rather than attempting to include every activity they have ever undertaken.

Demonstrate your environmental commitment

Make the connection between your experience and conservation, climate action, environmental education, sustainable entrepreneurship or community development clear.

Check your contact information

Ensure that your full name, email address and telephone number are correct so that the organisers can contact you if necessary.

Apply before the deadline

Applications must be submitted by 16 September 2026. Early submission is recommended.

Conclusion

The WWF-Amano Fellowship 2027 provides an important leadership development opportunity for young Ugandans already working to create positive environmental and community change.

Through its nine-month virtual format, the programme combines conservation awareness with leadership development, strategic thinking, emotional resilience, mentorship, expert workshops and peer learning. Fellows can remain active in their studies, employment, businesses or community initiatives while developing new skills and expanding their professional networks.

The fellowship is particularly relevant to young conservationists, climate advocates, environmental educators, sustainable entrepreneurs and community changemakers who can demonstrate genuine involvement and positive impact.

TITLE: Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026: Attend the One Young World Summit in Cape Town

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026, an exciting opportunity designed to recognise and support young South Africans who are actively contributing to positive change in their communities and across the country.

Offered through a partnership between Brand South Africa and One Young World, the Play Your Part Bursary will enable six outstanding young South Africans to participate in the One Young World Summit 2026, taking place in Cape Town, South Africa, from 3–6 November 2026.

The opportunity is specifically aimed at young active citizens who are already making meaningful contributions to South African society. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to participate in one of the world’s prominent gatherings of emerging young leaders, engage with a diverse leadership community and gain access to development opportunities that extend beyond the Summit itself.

Applications opened on 11 August 2026 and interested candidates must submit their applications by 16 September 2026.

About the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026

The Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026 has been created to support young South Africans who demonstrate the values of active citizenship through tangible contributions to their communities and society.

The bursary is connected to Brand South Africa’s wider mission of strengthening the country’s reputation, competitiveness and sense of national participation.

Brand South Africa is the official marketing agency of South Africa. Its mandate includes building South Africa’s brand reputation and improving the country’s global competitiveness.

Through coordinated and proactive marketing and communications strategies, the organisation works to position South Africa as a competitive investment destination while simultaneously encouraging South Africans, both within the country and abroad, to participate actively in building a better society.

A central part of this work is the Play Your Part initiative.

What Is the Play Your Part Initiative?

Play Your Part is a nationwide initiative developed to inspire, empower and celebrate active citizenship in South Africa.

The initiative is based on the principle that building a stronger country is a collective responsibility and that contributions to society can take many different forms.

Rather than limiting active citizenship to formal organisations or large-scale projects, Play Your Part encourages participation from across South African society, including:

Individuals;

Businesses and corporations;

Non-governmental organisations;

Government institutions;

Schools;

Faith communities; and

Other community groups and organisations.

Participants are encouraged to contribute whatever resources they can towards creating a better future. Contributions may include their:

Time;

Money;

Professional or personal skills;

Knowledge;

Resources; or

Goods.

At its core, Play Your Part seeks to demonstrate the impact that can be achieved when people actively care for their communities, fellow citizens and the environment.

The partnership with One Young World extends this mission by identifying young people who are already putting these principles into practice and providing them with an international leadership development opportunity.

Six Young South Africans Will Receive the Bursary

A total of six bursaries are available through the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026.

The bursaries have been divided geographically to ensure opportunities for both Cape Town-based candidates and young leaders elsewhere in South Africa.

The six places are allocated as follows:

Three bursaries are reserved for candidates based in Cape Town.

Three bursaries are available to applicants from across South Africa.

Successful candidates will participate in the One Young World Summit 2026 alongside other emerging leaders and changemakers.

About the One Young World Summit 2026

The One Young World Summit 2026 will take place from 3–6 November 2026 in Cape Town, South Africa.

The Summit brings together young leaders and provides a platform for participants to connect, exchange ideas, discuss important global and local challenges, and strengthen their capacity to create positive change.

For recipients of the Play Your Part Bursary, participation is intended to be more than attendance at a single event. Successful applicants will also gain access to leadership development opportunities and the wider One Young World community.

This makes the bursary particularly relevant to young South Africans who are already demonstrating leadership through community service, social initiatives, civic participation or other activities that benefit society.

What Does the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary Cover?

Successful applicants will receive support to participate in the One Young World Summit 2026.

The bursary includes the following:

1. Access to the One Young World Summit 2026

Recipients will receive access to the One Young World Summit 2026, scheduled for 3–6 November 2026 in Cape Town, South Africa.

This gives successful candidates the opportunity to participate in the Summit’s activities and engage with the wider One Young World community.

2. Travel and Accommodation Where Required

The bursary provides travel and accommodation as required for eligible successful candidates.

However, an important exception applies to applicants who are already based in Cape Town.

Travel and accommodation will not be provided for candidates based in Cape Town.

Applicants should therefore take this condition into consideration when applying.

3. Catering During the Summit

Selected participants will receive catering during specified periods of the Summit.

The package includes:

Dinner on 3 November 2026;

Lunch and dinner on 4 November 2026;

Lunch and dinner on 5 November 2026; and

Lunch and dinner on 6 November 2026.

4. Access to the One Young World Global Leadership Programme

Bursary recipients will also receive access to the One Young World Global Leadership Programme.

This component adds a leadership development dimension to the opportunity and is particularly relevant to candidates seeking to strengthen their ability to contribute effectively to their communities and wider society.

5. Access to Action Accelerator

Successful candidates will receive access to Action Accelerator, a One Young World programme connected to supporting leadership and action.

For young people already developing initiatives or contributing to community projects, this provides an additional opportunity to build on the work they are currently undertaking.

6. Lifetime Membership of the One Young World Ambassador Community

One of the longer-term benefits of the bursary is lifetime membership in the One Young World Ambassador Community.

This means that the value of the opportunity extends beyond the four-day Summit in Cape Town.

Successful participants will become part of the wider One Young World community after the Summit, creating opportunities for continued engagement with other young leaders and changemakers.

Who Is Eligible for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026?

The bursary has specific eligibility requirements, and candidates should review them carefully before submitting an application.

Age Requirement

Candidates must be between 18 and 30 years old at the time of the One Young World Summit 2026.

Applicants who will still be under the age of 18 at the time of the Summit cannot be accepted.

Candidates should therefore calculate their age based on the Summit dates rather than only their age at the time they submit their application.

Nationality or Residency Requirement

Applicants must be a:

South African national; or

Resident of South Africa.

The opportunity is therefore specifically focused on young people connected to South Africa through nationality or residency.

Commitment to Active Citizenship

Candidates must demonstrate a genuine commitment to active citizenship and contributing to positive change in South Africa.

The bursary is not simply based on academic qualifications or professional achievements. Applicants are expected to demonstrate that they are already actively contributing to their communities or society.

Evidence of Community or Social Contribution

Applicants should be able to demonstrate a track record of using one or more of the following to benefit their community or society:

Time;

Money;

Skills; or

Goods.

This requirement reflects the philosophy behind the Play Your Part initiative: positive change can come from different forms of contribution.

Applicants should therefore consider the practical impact they have already made and how their actions have benefited other people, their community or South African society more broadly.

Understanding of Issues Affecting South Africa

Candidates must demonstrate an understanding of key local and/or global issues facing South Africa.

This means applicants should be able to connect their active citizenship or community involvement to broader challenges and opportunities affecting the country.

What Type of Candidate Is the Bursary Looking For?

The Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary is particularly suited to young people who are not simply interested in leadership as a concept but are already demonstrating it through action.

Strong applicants are likely to be able to show clear evidence of how they have contributed to positive change.

This contribution could potentially take different forms, provided it demonstrates the required commitment to active citizenship.

Applicants should therefore think carefully about questions such as:

What have I personally done to contribute to positive change?

Who has benefited from my actions?

What problem or social challenge have I attempted to address?

What resources, skills, time or goods have I contributed?

What measurable or meaningful difference has my contribution made?

What important issues affecting South Africa do I understand particularly well?

How could participation in the One Young World Summit strengthen my ability to continue creating positive change?

Candidates who can communicate their answers clearly may be better positioned to demonstrate alignment with the purpose of the bursary.

Why Young South African Changemakers Should Consider Applying

The Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary offers more than access to an international leadership gathering.

It creates an opportunity for young South Africans already contributing to their communities to expand their leadership exposure and become part of a wider community.

For successful applicants, the opportunity includes:

Participation in the One Young World Summit 2026;

Exposure to a wider community of young leaders;

Access to leadership development programming;

Participation in Action Accelerator;

Lifetime membership of the One Young World Ambassador Community;

Travel and accommodation support where applicable; and

An opportunity to represent the spirit of active citizenship in South Africa.

The bursary may therefore be especially valuable for community leaders, social changemakers and other young people who are already turning ideas into meaningful action.

Important Dates for Applicants

Prospective applicants should take note of the following dates:

Applications opened: 11 August 2026

Application deadline: 16 September 2026

One Young World Summit: 3–6 November 2026

Summit location: Cape Town, South Africa

Applicants are encouraged not to wait until the final day to prepare and submit their applications.

Application Deadline

The official application deadline for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026 is 16 September 2026.

Applications submitted after the stated deadline may not be considered, so prospective candidates should ensure that they complete the application process on time.

How to Apply for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026

Interested candidates should apply through the official One Young World application portal for the Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary.

Before starting the application, candidates should carefully review the eligibility criteria and think about how they will demonstrate their record of active citizenship.

Applicants should be prepared to communicate clearly:

Their commitment to positive change in South Africa;

Their record of contributing time, money, skills or goods;

The impact of their activities on their community or wider society;

Their understanding of issues affecting South Africa; and

How their experiences align with the values of the Play Your Part initiative.

https://www.oneyoungworld.com/scholarship/brand-south-africa-play-your-part-bursary

Application portal:

https://apply.oneyoungworld.com/scholarship/form/brand-south-africa-play-your-par

Candidates interested in learning more about Brand South Africa can also visit:

https://www.brandsouthafrica.com/

Important Note for Cape Town Applicants

Applicants based in Cape Town should pay particular attention to the funding arrangements.

Three of the six bursaries are specifically reserved for candidates based in Cape Town. However, travel and accommodation are not provided for Cape Town-based candidates.

The remaining three bursaries are open to applicants from across South Africa, with travel and accommodation provided as required.

Candidates should understand these arrangements before submitting their application.

Conclusion

The Brand South Africa Play Your Part Bursary 2026 provides an important opportunity for young South Africans who are already demonstrating that active citizenship can create meaningful change.

Through the partnership between Brand South Africa and One Young World, six young people will be selected to participate in the One Young World Summit 2026 in Cape Town from 3–6 November 2026.

Beyond access to the Summit, successful candidates will benefit from leadership development opportunities, Action Accelerator and lifetime membership in the One Young World Ambassador Community. Travel and accommodation will also be supported where required, although this support does not apply to successful candidates based in Cape Town.

Most importantly, this opportunity is designed for young people who can demonstrate action. Applicants should have a track record of contributing their time, money, skills or goods towards improving their communities or society and should understand important issues affecting South Africa.

Young South African citizens and residents aged 18–30 who meet the criteria and are actively contributing to positive change are encouraged to consider applying.

Applications close on 16 September 2026.

Interested candidates should review the official requirements carefully and submit their applications through the One Young World application platform before the deadline.

TITLE: WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme 2026–2027: Call for Young Researchers and Professionals in Trade and Gender

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The World Trade Organization (WTO) has opened nominations for the second edition of the WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme, a global initiative designed to support the next generation of researchers and professionals working at the intersection of international trade, gender equality and women’s economic empowerment.

Running from 12 October 2026 to 30 June 2027, the programme offers young talent an opportunity to strengthen their expertise through mentoring, capacity building, applied learning and international networking. Participants will have opportunities to engage with global experts, WTO Members and other stakeholders working on trade and gender issues.

The programme is particularly relevant for young researchers whose academic or professional work already addresses trade and gender, as well as those seeking to incorporate these issues into their current research or policy work.

About the WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme

The Youth Talent Incubator Programme was developed from the momentum generated by the World Trade Congress on Gender, which was first held at the WTO in December 2022. The Congress brought together leading experts working on trade and gender research and created opportunities for researchers and policymakers to exchange knowledge and establish partnerships.

The initiative subsequently contributed to the Youth Trade Summit on Gender, held in November 2023, which brought together 50 young professionals from academic institutions, research centres, think tanks and government authorities from around the world.

The Summit gave young researchers and early-career professionals opportunities to interact with WTO member delegations, senior researchers and international stakeholders on topics including women’s economic empowerment and the relationship between gender and international trade.

The first Youth Talent Incubator Programme was launched in July 2024. Over an eleven-month period, participants developed their knowledge and professional skills through mentorship, applied policy research, training and networking. The outcomes of that programme were presented to the WTO Informal Working Group on Trade and Gender in December 2025.

Building on these achievements, the second edition will run from 12 October 2026 to 30 June 2027.

What the Programme Focuses On

The WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme is built around three main pillars:

1. Mentoring

Participants will benefit from engagement with experienced researchers, experts and professionals in the trade and gender field.

Mentoring is intended to help young participants develop their ideas, strengthen their professional direction and deepen their understanding of how trade and gender issues are addressed in research and policymaking.

2. Capacity Building

The programme provides opportunities for participants to strengthen their technical knowledge and professional skills related to trade and gender.

This is particularly valuable for young researchers and professionals who want to connect academic research with practical policy challenges and evidence-based solutions.

3. Networking

Participants will have opportunities to build connections with global experts, WTO Members and other international and regional stakeholders.

The networking component can help participants expand their professional networks and become more connected to the global trade and gender community.

Why Trade and Gender Matter

The programme comes at a time when governments, international organisations and other public and private stakeholders increasingly recognise the relationship between women’s economic empowerment, international trade and sustainable development.

Improving women’s participation in international trade requires not only policy action but also strong research and evidence. Researchers play an important role by examining existing challenges, identifying inequalities and developing evidence-based approaches that policymakers can use.

The WTO has progressively integrated gender considerations into its work since 2017 through political commitments, technical policy work, research, capacity building and practical trade-policy tools.

In 2020, the WTO Informal Working Group on Trade and Gender was established. According to the call, the group now represents more than 80% of WTO membership and has become the main platform within the WTO for discussions on trade and gender.

The WTO’s work in this area has continued to develop through successive Ministerial Conferences. At the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference in March 2026, the Informal Working Group achieved several member-led outcomes, including:

A joint statement on strengthening the global trading system through women’s economic empowerment.

An achievements tracking compendium documenting gender-responsive trade initiatives since 2020.

A new initiative, developed with the Informal Working Group on MSMEs, to create a compendium on empowering women to trade through digitalisation.

Additional practical policy tools to support women’s economic empowerment through trade.

These developments demonstrate the growing importance of researchers and young professionals who can contribute evidence, ideas and policy recommendations to the global trade and gender conversation.

Who Is the WTO Seeking to Nominate?

The WTO Gender Research Hub is seeking nominations for young researchers and young professionals working in relevant academic, research and government environments.

Potential nominees may come from:

Universities and academic institutions

Research foundations

Research centres

Think tanks

Policy research organisations

Government institutions

Other relevant research and policy settings

The programme is designed for young researchers in academia and research institutions, as well as young professionals working in government.

Learn more HERE

Eligibility and Nomination Criteria

Candidates must satisfy the programme’s nomination requirements.

Age

Applicants must generally be 20 to 35 years old.

The call also notes that the age limit may be relaxed in exceptional circumstances. This may apply to nominees who demonstrate outstanding initiative or who have taken a career break. Candidates seeking such an exception should explain their circumstances in their motivation letter.

Interest or Current Work in Trade and Gender

Candidates must demonstrate current work relating to trade and gender, or show a clear interest in incorporating trade and gender issues into their existing work.

This means applicants should be able to demonstrate a genuine connection to the subject rather than simply expressing a general interest in international development.

Motivation Letter

Candidates must provide a motivation letter explaining their interest and suitability for the programme.

A strong motivation letter should clearly communicate the candidate’s existing work, professional or research interests and reasons for wanting to engage more deeply with trade and gender issues.

Institutional Endorsement

Candidates must be formally endorsed by their academic or research institution.

The call specifically refers to institutions such as think tanks, research foundations and centres and policy research settings.

This is important because the programme is not structured as an entirely individual application. The candidate must be nominated and endorsed through an eligible academic or research institution.

How the Selection Process Works

The call for nominations is directed to academic and research institutions.

Nominations may be submitted by legal representatives of eligible institutions through the designated online nomination form.

Up to 35 nominees will ultimately be selected by the Chair of the WTO Gender Research Hub to participate in the second edition of the Youth Talent Incubator Programme.

Selected applicants are scheduled to receive notification of the outcome by email on 1 October 2026.

Programme Format and Cost

The programme will be conducted entirely online, making it accessible to selected participants without requiring relocation to Geneva or another physical programme location.

Importantly, the programme is cost-free for participants.

This online format can be particularly valuable for young researchers and professionals who are working or studying while participating in the programme.

Programme Dates

The second edition of the WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme will run from:

12 October 2026 to 30 June 2027.

The selected participants will therefore have an extended period to engage with mentoring, capacity-building and networking activities.

Application Deadline

The deadline for nominations is 24 September 2026 at 23:59 CET.

The WTO states explicitly that the deadline will not be extended, so eligible institutions and potential nominees should begin the nomination process well in advance.

Important Point About the Application Process

Potential candidates should note that the call is specifically seeking nominations from academic and research institutions.

Therefore, an eligible young researcher or professional should not assume that simply submitting an individual application will satisfy the requirements. Candidates should work with their university, research centre, think tank, foundation or relevant institution to secure the required formal endorsement.

Institutions should ensure that the nomination is submitted through the appropriate online form before the deadline.

Contact Information

For questions concerning the Youth Talent Incubator Programme or the nomination process, applicants and institutions can contact the WTO’s Trade and Gender Office at:

trade-gender@wto.org

Additional information about the programme is available through the WTO website.

How to Prepare a Strong Nomination

Although meeting the eligibility criteria is essential, candidates can strengthen their prospects by preparing a clear and convincing nomination.

Consider the following:

Clearly demonstrate your connection to trade and gender. Explain your current research, professional work or academic interests and how they relate to these themes.

Show evidence of commitment. Where possible, highlight research projects, publications, policy work, academic activities or professional experiences related to gender, trade, women’s economic empowerment or related policy issues.

Write a focused motivation letter. Explain why participation in the Youth Talent Incubator Programme is important for your research or career development.

Approach your institution early. Because institutional endorsement is required, do not wait until the final day to begin discussions with your university, research centre, think tank or other eligible institution.

Demonstrate future potential. Explain how the knowledge, mentoring and networks gained through the programme could contribute to your future research, professional work or policy engagement.

Connect your work to broader policy challenges. Strong candidates should be able to demonstrate an understanding of why gender-responsive trade policies matter for sustainable development and women’s economic empowerment.

APPLY HERE

Why This Opportunity Is Valuable

The WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme provides a distinctive opportunity for emerging researchers and professionals to develop within an international policy environment.

Participants can potentially gain:

Exposure to international trade and gender policy discussions.

Mentorship from experienced experts.

Capacity-building opportunities.

Greater understanding of the relationship between trade and gender.

Opportunities to engage with WTO Members and international stakeholders.

International professional networking.

Experience connecting research with policy.

A platform for contributing young people’s perspectives to global discussions.

Participation in a global community focused on advancing gender-responsive trade policy.

The programme can therefore be particularly relevant to individuals considering careers in international organisations, public policy, trade policy, gender equality, economic development, research, academia and international relations.

Visit HERE to learn more about the WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme.

Conclusion

The WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme – 2nd Edition represents an important opportunity for young researchers and professionals seeking to deepen their engagement with the relationship between international trade and gender equality.

With its three pillars of mentoring, capacity building and networking, the programme is designed to help develop the next generation of trade and gender experts while strengthening connections between research and policymaking. The entirely online and cost-free format further makes the programme accessible to selected participants from different professional and academic environments.

Young researchers and professionals who meet the criteria should begin working with their eligible academic or research institutions as soon as possible, particularly because institutional endorsement is required and the nomination deadline is 24 September 2026 at 23:59 CET.

TITLE: Press Release – The University of Nigeria, Nsukka Launches a New Online Master’s Degree in Public Administration

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Accra, Ghana (June 7, 2022) – A new Online Master’s Degree in Public Administration (MPA) has been launched by the University of Nigeria, Nsukka in line with its target of ensuring a functional, globally competitive, and responsive higher education which meets the needs of society.

The Master’s in Public Administration, which will commence September 2022, is an intensive 24- month program that will emphasize the evaluation of the theories that inform debates about the management of public services. It is offered by the University of Nigeria, Nsukka on the AAU-eLearnAfrica Learning Management System, a premier online learning platform by the e-Learn Africa and Association of African Universities, which is championing the transformation of online education in Africa.

The Online Master’s Degree in Public Administration is targeted at all stakeholders including African civil servants and leaders in development. The MPA seeks to equip current leaders and students with advanced theories in public policy for sustainable development. Studying the Online Master of Public Administration will provide students with the ability to apply the latest theoretical knowledge to their careers in real-time and offer the opportunity for students to build a practical understanding of public management and governance.

All interested students are invited to join the online Masters in Public Administration Program to deepen their knowledge and to access the numerous opportunities offered by the Program, for their advancement and generally for the advancement of their countries and Africa.

About the University of Nigeria, Nsukka

The University of Nigeria is a top federal-controlled public university located in Southeastern Nigeria. It is commonly referred to as UNN. The University was founded in 1955 and on October 7, 1960, was formally opened for academic operations. It has three campuses – Nsukka (the main campus), Enugu, and ItukuOzalla, all in Nigeria. UNN has 17 Faculties, and 102 academic Departments and offers 106 undergraduate programs, 211 postgraduate programs.

About The AAU-eLearnAfrica Learning Management System

In 2016, eLearnAfrica entered a partnership agreement with the Association of African Universities (AAU); one that would expand online learning opportunities for students enrolled in the AAU’s over 400 member institutions and other universities not yet under the umbrella of the prestigious AAU. The target was to make educational opportunities available to about 10 million African students. In pursuing this agenda, the AAU-eLearnAfricaLMS was birthed and launched at the 15th Quadrennial AAU General Conference of African University Leaders, on 7th July 2021.

The internships are available across three teams: Economics and Political Section (EPS), National Security and Foreign Policy Section (NSFP), and the Communications and Engagement Team. Applicants can indicate their preferred team during the application process.

About the British Embassy France Internships

The British Embassy in Paris is part of the UK’s global diplomatic network and represents British political, economic and consular interests overseas. Interns will work alongside experienced professionals and contribute to projects, events, policy work and international engagement involving the UK and France.

The programme is designed for motivated students and graduates interested in areas such as:

Diplomacy and international relations

European and EU affairs

Public policy

Political and economic affairs

Migration and borders

National security

Communications and public diplomacy

International engagement

Applicants from different academic and professional backgrounds are encouraged to apply, with emphasis placed on motivation, potential and skills.

Available Internship Teams

1. Economics and Political Section (EPS)

The Economics and Political Section works with French government institutions, academia, businesses and civil society organisations to strengthen cooperation between the UK and France.

The section covers:

Bilateral and Political Affairs

Economic, Social and Sustainability Policy

European Affairs

Science and Technology

The successful intern will work within the European Affairs team during a period in which the UK is seeking to strengthen its relations with France, the European Union and wider European partners.

Responsibilities may include:

Monitoring and analysing political, EU and economic developments

Conducting research on priority policy issues

Drafting briefings, reports and policy updates

Supporting strategic engagement with French stakeholders

Assisting with Embassy events, ministerial visits and diplomatic engagements

Providing administrative and project support

This placement is particularly suited to candidates interested in research, current affairs and the relationship between policy decisions and international relations.

2. National Security and Foreign Policy Section (NSFP)

The National Security and Foreign Policy Section focuses on major international challenges and works closely with French institutions and international partners. Its areas of work include:

Foreign and Development Policy

Migration and Borders

National Security

Interns will support work that helps UK decision-makers understand French perspectives on foreign policy, migration and security matters.

Possible responsibilities include:

Researching and analysing French policy developments

Preparing reports and briefings

Supporting strategic stakeholder engagement

Working with think tanks and policy experts

Assisting with Embassy events and high-level meetings

Working with colleagues across the FCDO, Ministry of Defence, Cabinet Office and wider UK Government network

The placement is particularly relevant for candidates interested in international relations, global affairs, security and public policy.

3. Communications and Engagement Team

The Communications and Engagement Team works across France to communicate UK priorities to different audiences and support public diplomacy.

The team includes:

Media and press relations

Ministerial and VIP visits

Public diplomacy

Outreach programmes

Cultural engagement

Flagship events

The successful intern will primarily support the Europe Regional Programme Fund, helping coordinate projects that advance UK priorities and strengthen UK-France relations.

Responsibilities may include:

Supporting programme and project management

Monitoring project delivery, outcomes and financial compliance

Maintaining programme records and documentation

Supporting governance meetings

Working with external partners, media organisations and stakeholders

Assisting with public diplomacy events

Supporting media monitoring and reporting

Contributing to social media and communications activities

Supporting high-level visits and diplomatic engagements

Eligibility and Requirements

Applicants should demonstrate the following:

Excellent written and spoken French and English, with a minimum C1 CEFR level

An internship agreement known as a “Convention de stage”

Interest in Europe/EU affairs, migration, communications and/or UK-France relations

Interest in politics and working in an international environment

Ability to work effectively as part of a team

Drive, enthusiasm and the ability to deliver

Strong research and problem-solving skills

Ability to work independently and find creative solutions

Excellent communication skills

Strong organisational and attention-to-detail skills

Flexibility to support wider Embassy priorities

Confidence using Microsoft Office

Candidates must also currently hold an independent right to live and work in France and be able to maintain that right throughout the contract.

Internship Details

Organisation: British Embassy in France

Location: Paris, France

Position: Intern

Number of vacancies: 3

Duration: 5 months

Start date: 2 November 2026

Working arrangement: Full-time

Working hours: 35 hours per week

Salary: €1,000 gross per month

Additional condition: Meal contribution

Application deadline: 2 September 2026

The position also allows some flexible and remote working, although the jobholder is expected to work from the office at least 60% of the week and more frequently when required.

Application Requirements

Applications must be submitted in English and must clearly indicate all nationalities held by the applicant. Successful candidates will undergo professional background checks and security clearance.

Applicants should also note that the position requires the successful candidate to provide documentation for security and background checks, including identification, recent criminal-record documentation for relevant countries of residence, proofs of address and references.

The British Embassy states that the internship is locally recruited and governed by applicable French employment conditions. It is not an entry point into the UK’s Diplomatic Service.

Important Application Information

The application deadline is 2 September 2026 at 23:55, using the time zone of the country where the vacancy has arisen. Applicants are advised to allow sufficient time to complete and submit their applications before the deadline.

Applicants should also ensure that their application authentically reflects their own experiences. The Embassy states that AI tools may only be used for limited tasks such as formatting consistency and keyword relevance, while personal narratives and responses must genuinely reflect the applicant’s own professional journey and achievements.

Applications for Country Based Staff positions with the British Government must be submitted through the official tal.net recruitment platform. The Embassy warns that applications submitted through other websites will not be received.

Conclusion

TITLE: The Association of African Universities participates in a stakeholder engagement forum to strengthen data collection and management in African higher education for evidence-based policy making

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
A two-day stakeholder engagement forum focused on providing the platform to explore opportunities for enhancing the collection, consolidation, and management of secure quality data to boost evidence-based policy making in higher education and research was organised in Entebbe, Uganda, from September 1-2, 2022.

Hosted by the Inter Universities Council for East Africa (IUCEA) a consortium member of the Demographics of African Faculty Project (DAF II), the forum brought together key higher education stakeholders from the seven East African Community (EAC) member states – Democratic Republic of Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, Uganda, and Tanzania. Specifically, participants were persons/technical staff responsible for data management and research from the councils and commissions for higher education; persons/technical staff responsible for data management in higher education and research from the ministries of education; technical officers from the commissions for science, innovation, and technology; relevant research organizations involved in data and policy research and the DAF II Research Consortium partners among others.

The Demographics of African Faculty consortium consist of the Association of African Universities (AAU), the IUCEA, the Education Sub-Saharan Africa and the Population Reference Bureau (PRB). The project seeks to systematically analyse the staffing challenges in sub-Saharan Africa – with a first phase conducted in Ghana in 2018, while the second phase (DAF II) which is currently ongoing and funded by the Carnegie Corporation of New York, is focusing on strengthening the ability of higher education stakeholders to plan and implement evidence-informed responses targeted at improving the numbers and nature of quality faculty within Higher Education Institutions in the East African Community. As a consortium partner to the DAF II project, the Association of African Universities’ (AAU), participated in the Entebbe forum in line with its role in the project. AAU’s multi faceted role under DAF II include working with the partners in conducting the background research, facilitating stakeholder engagements, disseminating project findings to stakeholders in the EAC and beyond through multiple digital and non-digital channels among others.

Officially opening the two-day stakeholder forum, the honourable minister of state for higher education of the Republic of Uganda, Dr. John Chrysestom Muyingo reiterated the need to strengthen collaboration among key players – government, higher education institutions and the private sector to foster quality generation, management, and utilisation of data for planning purposes.

Additionally, the forum featured remarks and keynote presentations on important topics by various institutions, including the IUCEA; the East African Science and Technology Commission (EASTECO); the African Population and Health Research Centre (APHRC) and the African Centre for Technology Studies (ACTs).

The forum also provided the platform for the EAC country researchers engaged under the DAF II project to share the preliminary country status and data collection insights related to the nature of the faculty challenges with the participants, for their input. This engagement session and involvement of the stakeholders was important in ensuring that high quality research findings to foster accurate projections and insights for effective decision making is produced by the DAF II project.

Again, the event featured a presentation on ‘the attributes and aspirations of IUCEA’s Higher Education Management Information System (HEMIS), and engaged stakeholders for input towards ensuring a robust and effective system which serves the needs of stakeholders in the EAC and beyond.

Following a presentation by the DAF II consortium, another discussion item that featured prominently at the forum was on ‘the Impact of Covid-19 on Teaching Models and the Supply and Demand of Faculty in the East African Community’.

In a highly participatory manner, the forum also created the very important platform for participants to engage with key issues and to work in groups on the thematic focus and themes of importance to the forum’s objective.

The two-day stakeholder engagement forum ended on a positive note with a refreshed commitment by all participating stakeholders and institutions to deepen collaborations to accelerate the strengthening of data management in higher education and research for the benefit of the East African Community.

NVIDIA Research

Artificial intelligence

Parallel computing

Machine learning

Graphics

Robotics

Computing systems

Emerging technologies

NVIDIA Developer Forums

The NVIDIA Developer Forums allow developers and technical professionals to interact with other members of the NVIDIA community.

Students can use such communities to:

Learn from technical discussions

Engage with GPU specialists

Explore developer problems

Improve their technical knowledge

Understand how NVIDIA tools are used in practice

Why Consider an NVIDIA Early Talent Opportunity?

NVIDIA’s early-career programs can be especially attractive to students interested in working at the intersection of research, engineering and commercial technology.

Key reasons applicants may consider these programs include:

1. Real project experience

Interns are employees and may contribute directly to projects instead of participating only in classroom-style exercises.

2. Exposure to advanced technologies

Participants can work with technologies connected with artificial intelligence, GPUs, accelerated computing, networking, robotics, autonomous systems and other technical areas.

3. Professional networking

Students may interact with experienced engineers, researchers, managers, other interns and professionals across various teams.

4. Career development

Internships can provide practical experience that strengthens future applications for graduate employment.

5. Multiple education levels are supported

NVIDIA has opportunities for undergraduate students, master’s students, MBA students, PhD candidates and new graduates.

6. Potential long-term career pathway

Internships represent an important source of NVIDIA’s new college graduate and early-career hiring.

7. Research and engineering opportunities

Candidates can explore both research-focused and product-focused career paths.

Find Your Perfect Fit

Where Are NVIDIA Early Talent Opportunities Located?

NVIDIA recruits internationally, but the availability of positions varies over time.

The opportunities included in the supplied careers information were located in countries and territories such as:

China

Taiwan

Israel

Germany

Additional vacancies may be available in the United States and other NVIDIA locations depending on current recruitment needs.

Applicants should never assume that every vacancy accepts applicants from every country.

Instead, candidates should review each job posting carefully for:

Work location

Immigration requirements

Work authorization requirements

Visa sponsorship information

Education requirements

Language requirements

Onsite or remote expectations

Application Deadline

There is no single universal application deadline for NVIDIA’s Early Talent Programs.

NVIDIA recruits for internships and new graduate opportunities throughout the year, and individual vacancies may open or close according to hiring needs.

For this reason, candidates are encouraged to apply as early as possible when they find a suitable role.

Some job advertisements may close after enough applications have been received or once the position has been filled.

Applicants should therefore check the individual vacancy for the most accurate deadline information.

How to Apply for NVIDIA Internships and Graduate Opportunities

Applications should be submitted through NVIDIA’s official careers platform.

Applicants can follow these general steps:

Visit NVIDIA’s university recruiting or careers page.

Open the list of internship and new college graduate positions.

Filter vacancies based on job category, location and career level.

Select a position that matches your academic background and interests.

Read the full job description carefully.

Confirm that you meet the education, technical, language and location requirements.

Prepare an updated resume in the required language.

Highlight relevant technical projects, internships, research or open-source contributions.

Complete the online application form.

Upload the required documents.

Submit the application through NVIDIA’s official careers system.

Monitor your application account and email for any communication from NVIDIA.

Applicants should tailor their resume to the specific job rather than using a completely generic application.

What Applicants Should Include in Their Resume

Depending on the role, a strong application may highlight:

Degree program and university

Expected graduation date

Relevant coursework

Programming languages

Research experience

Academic projects

Technical projects

Previous internships

GitHub portfolio

Open-source contributions

Publications

AI or machine learning experience

Cloud computing experience

Linux knowledge

Hardware experience

Leadership experience

Relevant certifications

Candidates should focus most strongly on experience that directly matches the vacancy they are applying for.

Equal Opportunity and Accessibility

NVIDIA states that it is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering an inclusive environment.

The company also offers reasonable accommodations upon request for applicants with disabilities.

Candidates who need support during the recruitment process can use NVIDIA’s official accommodation and human resources channels.

Important Advice Before Applying

Before submitting an application, candidates should pay close attention to the requirements of each individual position.

In particular:

Do not assume all NVIDIA internships have the same qualifications.

Check whether the role requires undergraduate, master’s, MBA or PhD enrollment.

Verify whether the position requires full-time availability.

Check whether the job is onsite, hybrid or otherwise location-specific.

Review the expected internship duration.

Confirm whether you possess the required programming or technical skills.

Check whether English or another language is required.

Review local work authorization and immigration conditions.

Apply early when a suitable opportunity appears.

Use only NVIDIA’s official recruiting platform when submitting an application.

APPLY NOW

Official Application Links

NVIDIA University Recruiting:

https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/about-nvidia/careers/university-recruiting/

NVIDIA Open Internship and New College Graduate Positions:

https://jobs.nvidia.com/careers?filter_job_type=intern%20%28fixed%20term%29%2Cnew%20college%20graduate

Applicants should use the official job portal to identify current vacancies because the number and location of available opportunities can change regularly.

Conclusion

The NVIDIA Early Talent Programs provide university students, MBA candidates, PhD researchers and recent graduates with opportunities to begin or accelerate careers in some of the world’s most important areas of emerging technology.

Through internships, Ignite, MBA pathways, PhD opportunities and the New College Graduate Program, participants can potentially work on real projects connected with artificial intelligence, software engineering, GPU computing, robotics, autonomous systems, networking, hardware engineering, deep learning and high-performance computing.

A major feature of NVIDIA’s early-career approach is that interns are treated as employees who contribute directly to meaningful work. Students can therefore combine academic knowledge with industry experience while collaborating with professionals developing real technologies and products.

Because NVIDIA recruits across multiple disciplines, countries and educational levels, eligibility differs substantially from one position to another. There is also no single application deadline for the entire university recruitment program.

Students and recent graduates who are interested in NVIDIA should regularly monitor the official careers platform, identify opportunities that match their qualifications and apply as early as possible when suitable vacancies become available.

For ambitious candidates interested in AI, computing, engineering and advanced technology, NVIDIA’s internship and early-career ecosystem offers a significant opportunity to gain practical experience, strengthen technical capabilities and potentially build a long-term career within one of the world’s leading computing companies.

TITLE: SEDarc ESRC PhD Studentships 2027 in the UK | Fully Funded Doctoral Opportunities

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The South East Doctoral Training Arc (SEDarc) is offering Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC)-funded PhD studentships for September 2027 entry, providing opportunities for talented researchers in the social sciences to undertake doctoral study at one of six participating universities in London and South East England.

The studentships are open to UK and international students and include UK tuition fees and a stipend at the UKRI rate. For successful overseas applicants, the SEDarc institutions will cover the difference between UK home and international tuition fees, except for the University of Reading.

The SEDarc deadline is 29 January 2027 at 16:00 GMT, although applicants must first complete the institutional application process, and each participating university has its own deadline and procedure.

Participating Universities

Students can be based at one of six higher education institutions:

University of Kent

Kingston University

University of Reading

Royal Holloway, University of London

University of Surrey

University of Sussex

SEDarc also works with non-higher-education partner organisations to strengthen the research and training opportunities available to doctoral students.

SEDarc Research Pathways

SEDarc’s doctoral training model combines advanced research skills training, placements and an individual research project within one of five interdisciplinary, challenge-led pathways:

Living Sustainably

Healthy Thriving Communities

Inclusive Economic Growth

Secure, Effective, & Trusted Institutions

Transformative Technologies for Society

These pathways provide a framework for research addressing major social, economic, environmental, institutional and technological challenges.

Funding and Benefits

The standard SEDarc PhD lasts 3.5 years full-time, including a three-month placement, or the part-time equivalent.

The funding package covers:

UK tuition fees

A UKRI-rate stipend

Three-month placement

Research and skills training

Individual doctoral research

For eligible students without a relevant social-science Master’s degree, potential funding for an approved Master’s course within the SEDarc consortium

The UKRI has not yet announced the 2027/28 tuition fee and stipend rates.

For reference, the 2026/27 rates were:

UK tuition fees: £5,238

UKRI stipend: £21,805

London-weighted stipend: £23,805 where applicable

The 2027/28 figures may therefore differ.

Funding for International Students

SEDarc accepts international applications.

For successful overseas applicants, the SEDarc institutions will cover the difference between UK home tuition fees and international tuition fees.

However, an important exception applies: the University of Reading does not cover this difference.

International applicants should therefore carefully check the financial arrangements of their chosen institution before applying.

Ring-Fenced Scholarships

SEDarc is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion throughout the doctoral journey.

The programme states that it will reserve up to three ring-fenced scholarships for eligible home students from certain Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic groups.

Applicants interested in these ring-fenced studentships should review the specific eligibility criteria published by SEDarc.

Who Can Apply?

The SEDarc PhD studentships are open to:

UK students

International students

Applicants working across the social sciences

Prospective PhD researchers who meet the academic requirements of their chosen institution and programme

Applicants who do not already hold a Master’s degree in the social sciences may also be eligible for funding to undertake an approved Master’s course within the SEDarc consortium.

Eligibility for this additional Master’s funding depends on the relevant requirements.

How to Apply

Applicants cannot apply directly to SEDarc without institutional nomination.

Students must first be nominated by one of the six SEDarc universities.

The application process therefore involves:

Choose one of the six participating SEDarc institutions.

Identify a suitable doctoral research area and SEDarc pathway.

Contact the SEDarc administrator at your chosen university.

Follow that institution’s application process and deadline.

Complete the institutional stage of the application.

Obtain nomination from the university.

Submit the SEDarc studentship application by the SEDarc deadline.

Because the six universities have different institutional deadlines and procedures, applicants should contact their chosen university as early as possible.

University Contacts

Kingston University: hssce-research@kingston.ac.uk

Royal Holloway, University of London: esrcdtp@rhul.ac.uk

University of Kent: kentgrc@kent.ac.uk

University of Reading: doctoralstudentshipsofficer@reading.ac.uk

University of Surrey: doctoralcollege@surrey.ac.uk

University of Sussex: pgr-scholarships@sussex.ac.uk

Application Deadline

The SEDarc studentship application deadline is:

29 January 2027 at 16:00 GMT

Applicants should note that this is the SEDarc deadline. The university they choose will have its own earlier institutional deadline and application process.

Applicants should therefore not wait until January 2027 before contacting their chosen institution.

Important Funding Notice

SEDarc’s ESRC Doctoral Training Partnership is subject to a mid-term review in 2026.

According to the programme information, the number of studentships may be revised depending on the findings of the review.

Allocations for the 2027 cohort are expected to be confirmed around January 2027.

Conclusion

The SEDarc ESRC PhD studentships provide funded doctoral study opportunities for UK and international researchers in the social sciences, with placements, research training and interdisciplinary research pathways forming part of the programme.

Students can apply through one of six participating universities: Kent, Kingston, Reading, Royal Holloway, Surrey or Sussex.

The standard PhD is 3.5 years full-time and includes a three-month placement. Funding covers UK tuition fees and provides a UKRI-rate stipend, while arrangements for international tuition fees vary by institution.

The main SEDarc application deadline is 29 January 2027 at 16:00 GMT, but applicants must first meet the separate institutional deadline and nomination requirements of their selected university.

Discover more on the OFY Webpage.

TITLE: University of Notre Dame Fully Funded PhD in Sustainable Development 2027: Full Tuition, 12-Month Stipend and Research Funding in the USA

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the University of Notre Dame Ph.D. in Sustainable Development for Fall 2027, a fully funded, interdisciplinary doctoral programme designed for scholars seeking to address major global challenges involving climate change, environmental governance, development policy, inequality and human well-being.

Based within the Keough School of Global Affairs at the University of Notre Dame in the United States, the doctoral programme combines advanced academic training, rigorous quantitative and qualitative research methods, interdisciplinary mentorship, engaged scholarship and policy-relevant research.

The programme is STEM-designated and is intended to prepare scholars whose work can contribute both to academic knowledge and to real-world policymaking and practice.

The PhD places particular emphasis on major sustainable development questions such as:

Climate change mitigation

Climate adaptation

Environmental governance

Development policy

Poverty and inequality

Human well-being

Global development

Governance

Sustainable institutions

Policy design

Evidence-based decision-making

The programme is influenced by the University of Notre Dame’s tradition of Catholic social teaching and Pope Francis’ Laudato Si’, with a particular commitment to improving human well-being, protecting vulnerable populations and safeguarding the natural environment.

Admitted doctoral students receive comprehensive financial support including:

Full tuition scholarship

A 12-month living stipend

Health insurance subsidy

Up to $4,000 for conference presentations and professional development

Most students complete the PhD in approximately five years, although individual timelines may vary depending on prior academic preparation, research progress and the nature of the dissertation project.

Applications for the Fall 2027 intake must be submitted by:

December 1, 2026

Apply:
https://gradengage.nd.edu/apply/

About the University of Notre Dame Ph.D. in Sustainable Development

The University of Notre Dame’s Ph.D. in Sustainable Development is designed for students who want to undertake rigorous research on some of the most significant economic, environmental, political and social challenges facing the world.

Rather than treating sustainable development as a narrowly environmental field, the programme takes a broad interdisciplinary approach.

Students investigate relationships among:

Human development

Environmental sustainability

Institutions

Governance

Economic systems

Political behavior

Climate change

Public policy

Development interventions

This approach recognizes that sustainable development challenges rarely fit neatly inside one discipline.

For example, climate adaptation may involve:

Political institutions

Public finance

Community behavior

Environmental science

Governance

Development economics

Social vulnerability

Likewise, poverty reduction may require researchers to understand not only economic outcomes but also political institutions, social structures, behavioral decision-making and environmental pressures.

The programme therefore trains students to work across disciplinary boundaries while developing deep research expertise in their chosen field.

A STEM-Designated Sustainable Development PhD

One particularly important feature of the programme is its designation as a:

STEM-designated doctoral programme

This reflects the programme’s strong emphasis on:

Research methods

Evidence

Data

Analysis

Empirical investigation

Policy evaluation

Students receive training in both:

Quantitative methods

Qualitative methods

Decarbonization

Public institutions

Environmental regulation

Political support for climate policy

Infrastructure

Development and emissions

Climate vulnerability

Community adaptation

Infrastructure

Agricultural systems

Water security

Migration

Development planning

A sustainable development perspective can help connect climate impacts with wider issues involving inequality, governance and human well-being.

3. Environmental Governance

Environmental governance examines how societies make decisions about natural resources, environmental protection and sustainability.

Research could involve:

Environmental institutions

Resource governance

Government regulation

Local communities

International environmental agreements

Accountability

Conservation

Forest governance

Water management

Students can investigate both formal institutions and informal systems through which environmental decisions are made.

Education

Health

Social protection

Inequality

Economic development

Governance

Institutional reform

International development assistance

Development interventions

Improving human well-being

and particularly with communities experiencing vulnerability.

This means sustainable development is approached not only as a technical or environmental challenge but also as an ethical and social challenge.

Research may therefore examine questions such as:

Who benefits from development?

Who bears environmental costs?

How do policies affect marginalized communities?

How can economic progress be made more equitable?

Catholic social teaching

and Pope Francis’ encyclical:

Laudato Si’

Human dignity

Social justice

Environmental responsibility

Poverty

Sustainable development

Care for the planet

Keough School of Global Affairs

at the University of Notre Dame.

Global policy

International affairs
