TITLE: Pennsylvania Apprenticeships on the Move Grant 2026: Apply for Up to $249,999 to Expand Workforce Apprenticeship Programs

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, through the Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry (L&I), has announced the Apprenticeships on the Move: Advancing Pennsylvania’s Workforce Grant, a major workforce development funding opportunity designed to strengthen apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship pathways across the state.

Through this Notice of Grant Availability (NGA), approximately $4 million in state funding is available to eligible organizations seeking to develop new Registered Apprenticeship or Registered Pre-Apprenticeship programs or expand existing registered programs in Pennsylvania.

Eligible applicants may request up to $249,999 to support projects that respond to employer workforce needs, build stronger talent pipelines, expand access to quality training, address barriers to employment, and create pathways into sustainable careers.

The initiative is particularly focused on high-priority sectors including agriculture, energy, life sciences, manufacturing, robotics and technology, education, healthcare, and skilled trades.

Applications for the Pennsylvania Apprenticeships on the Move Grant are due by October 2, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Time. The anticipated grant performance period will run from May 1, 2027, through April 30, 2030.

Pennsylvania Apprenticeships on the Move Grant Overview

The Apprenticeships on the Move initiative is intended to support Pennsylvania’s long-term workforce and economic development objectives by increasing the number, accessibility, and effectiveness of Registered Apprenticeship and Registered Pre-Apprenticeship opportunities.

The program recognizes that employers across Pennsylvania are facing increasing demand for skilled workers while also dealing with retirements, workforce shortages, competition for talent, and the loss of institutional knowledge.

The grant therefore seeks to fund innovative approaches that connect employers, workforce organizations, education providers, labor organizations, community-based organizations, and other stakeholders to create sustainable workforce pipelines.

Under the opportunity, organizations can propose either:

Development of a new Registered Apprenticeship or Registered Pre-Apprenticeship program, or

Expansion of an existing Registered Apprenticeship or Registered Pre-Apprenticeship program.

Projects must operate within Pennsylvania and address workforce development needs in one or more of the eligible industry sectors identified by L&I.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Approximately $4,000,000 has been allocated for the Apprenticeships on the Move initiative.

Eligible applicants may request:

Up to $249,999 per application

Funding amounts aligned with the actual scope and needs of the proposed project

Funding for eligible activities associated with developing or expanding apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship programs

The exact amount awarded will depend on the funding requested, the quality and competitiveness of applications, available funds, and the evaluation conducted by L&I.

Pennsylvania may also provide additional funding during the grant period if funds become available through deobligation of other awards. Supplemental funding is not guaranteed and will depend on factors such as grantee performance, demonstrated need, ability to spend additional funds effectively, and continued alignment with the objectives of the grant.

The grant is 100% state funded.

What Is the Main Purpose of the Apprenticeships on the Move Grant?

The central purpose of this grant is to strengthen Pennsylvania’s workforce by supporting apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship programs that respond directly to employer and labor-market needs.

The initiative seeks to:

Develop new Registered Apprenticeship programs.

Develop new Registered Pre-Apprenticeship programs.

Expand existing registered apprenticeship programs.

Expand existing registered pre-apprenticeship programs.

Strengthen talent pipelines in high-demand industries.

Increase access to apprenticeship opportunities.

Help employers address workforce shortages.

Provide individuals with skills and workplace experience.

Support pathways to industry-recognized credentials.

Address barriers preventing individuals from entering apprenticeship pathways.

Increase participation among historically underserved and underrepresented populations.

Encourage collaboration between employers, education providers, labor organizations, workforce boards, and community organizations.

Strengthen Pennsylvania’s long-term economic development priorities.

Applicants are expected to demonstrate a clear connection between their proposed project and Pennsylvania’s workforce and economic development priorities, including Governor Shapiro’s Ten-Year Strategic Plan for Economic Development and the Pennsylvania Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Combined State Plan.

Who Can Apply for the Grant?

The opportunity is intended for organizations that can serve as sponsors or intermediaries for new or existing registered apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship programs in Pennsylvania.

Eligible organizations may include:

Businesses

Community-based organizations

Economic development organizations

Industry associations

Labor organizations

Local education agencies

Local workforce development boards

Nonprofit organizations

Postsecondary institutions

Public libraries

STEM ecosystems

If an applicant is not the actual program sponsor, the application must provide significant evidence demonstrating that the program sponsor is an involved partner in the proposed project.

The organization must also have the capacity to coordinate and manage the project, administer the financial aspects of the grant, collect and report performance information, and work with an evaluator.

Two Types of Projects Can Be Funded

1. Development of a New Registered Apprenticeship or Pre-Apprenticeship Program

Organizations may apply to establish a new apprenticeship or pre-apprenticeship program that has not yet been registered at the beginning of the grant performance period.

The proposed program must ultimately be registered with the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

Awardees will have up to one year from the contract start date to finalize registration or demonstrate progress toward registration.

Grantees will be expected to establish and maintain communication with representatives of the Pennsylvania Apprenticeship and Training Office (ATO), which serves as the State Apprenticeship Agency (SAA), as they develop and register the program.

Organizations that fail to make adequate progress toward registration may have funds deobligated.

2. Expansion of an Existing Registered Program

Organizations may also apply to expand an existing Registered Apprenticeship or Registered Pre-Apprenticeship program that was already registered before the start of the grant performance period.

For purposes of this grant, expansion means an increase in the number of participants enrolled in the program.

Expansion does not include adding a new occupation to the existing program.

Organizations seeking to expand an existing program must ensure that the program sponsor remains compliant with applicable federal and Pennsylvania laws, regulations, policies, standards, and approved program standards.

Eligible Industry Sectors

The proposed apprenticeship or pre-apprenticeship program must operate within at least one of the sectors identified by Pennsylvania L&I.

Eligible sectors are:

Agriculture

Projects may address workforce needs associated with agricultural occupations and the broader agricultural economy.

Energy

Programs may develop talent pipelines for energy-related occupations and emerging workforce requirements in the energy sector.

Life Sciences

Organizations working to develop skilled talent for life sciences industries may submit proposals within this sector.

Manufacturing

Manufacturing remains a major focus of Pennsylvania’s workforce development strategy, and eligible projects may address skills shortages and talent pipeline needs within the sector.

Robotics and Technology

Programs focused on robotics, technology, and related occupations may qualify where they demonstrate clear workforce demand.

Education

Education-sector apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship initiatives may be eligible where they respond to identified workforce needs.

Healthcare

Healthcare workforce development projects may qualify under the healthcare sector.

Skilled Trades

The skilled trades category includes, but is not limited to:

Construction

Electrical work

HVAC

Steamfitting

Fiber optics

Telecommunications

Applicants must identify the applicable sector or sectors in their application and demonstrate how the proposed project addresses workforce development needs within those sectors.

Applications proposing programs outside the eligible sectors will be considered ineligible.

What Is a Registered Apprenticeship?

Registered Apprenticeship is a structured workforce development model that combines employment, training, mentorship, technical education, and recognized credentials.

According to the grant announcement, Registered Apprenticeships have five key components:

A paid job

On-the-job training

Related technical instruction

Mentorship

Credentials

This combination allows participants to gain practical work experience while developing technical and occupational skills.

For employers, apprenticeship programs can provide a structured way to develop and retain skilled workers. For participants, apprenticeships provide a pathway to earn wages while learning and working toward industry-recognized credentials.

What Is a Registered Pre-Apprenticeship?

Registered Pre-Apprenticeship programs are designed to prepare individuals for entry into Registered Apprenticeship programs.

The grant identifies five core components of a registered pre-apprenticeship:

An established connection to at least one existing Registered Apprenticeship program.

Approved training and curriculum.

Hands-on learning through appropriate program designs and approaches.

An opportunity to earn an industry-recognized credential.

Access to support services and career counseling.

Pre-apprenticeship can therefore serve as an important bridge between education, workforce preparation, and formal apprenticeship.

Why Is Pennsylvania Investing in Apprenticeships?

Pennsylvania is experiencing workforce challenges driven by several factors.

Employers are facing shortages of skilled workers, increased competition for talent, and the retirement of experienced workers.

As experienced employees leave the workforce, organizations can lose decades of technical knowledge and operational expertise.

Registered Apprenticeship programs can help address this challenge by combining experienced-worker mentorship with structured training for new employees.

This allows organizations to facilitate knowledge transfer while preparing the next generation of workers.

Apprenticeships also provide workers with opportunities to earn wages while acquiring skills and credentials, making them an important pathway into family-sustaining careers.

Pennsylvania has historically used apprenticeship models in areas such as construction, manufacturing, and industrial occupations. The Commonwealth is now seeking to expand apprenticeship opportunities into sectors such as healthcare, education, agriculture, energy, life sciences, robotics, technology, and telecommunications.

What Should Successful Projects Demonstrate?

Applicants must clearly demonstrate that the proposed program responds to a real workforce need.

A strong application should provide evidence such as:

Labor market information

Employer demand

Workforce shortage data

Talent pipeline gaps

Economic development information

Information about the occupations being targeted

The number of apprentices or pre-apprentices expected to be served

Information about the geographic area to be served

Evidence of employer involvement

Evidence of stakeholder partnerships

The applicant must also explain how the project contributes to Pennsylvania’s broader workforce and economic development goals.

Priority Areas That Can Strengthen an Application

The grant provides priority consideration for proposals demonstrating certain characteristics.

Previously Unfunded Programs

Priority may be given to new initiatives that have not previously received funding, including initiatives developed by existing Registered Apprenticeship or Pre-Apprenticeship sponsors.

On-the-Job Learning, Related Technical Instruction and Supportive Services

Priority consideration may be given to:

Registered Apprenticeship programs using grant funds to support on-the-job learning, related technical instruction, and supportive services.

Pre-Apprenticeship programs using grant funds to support paid work experience, related technical instruction, and supportive services.

Applicants seeking this priority must reflect the relevant expenses in the applicable budget categories.

Group Apprenticeship Models and Multi-County Programs

Priority may be given to group Registered Apprenticeship models or pre-apprenticeship programs operating physically across multiple counties.

For multi-county pre-apprenticeship replication, the program must have physical operations in at least three counties.

Historically Underserved and Underrepresented Populations

Applicants are encouraged to develop diverse talent pipelines that expand apprenticeship access for groups that have historically been underrepresented or underserved.

These may include:

Women

People of color

Individuals with disabilities

Veterans

Individuals from underserved or unserved communities

Individuals who speak English as a second language

Justice-impacted or adjudicated populations

Individuals experiencing multiple barriers to employment

Applicants should explain how their programs will identify and address barriers to education, training, and employment.

Accessibility

Priority consideration may also be given to projects that design, create, adjust, or upgrade physical and digital environments and services to improve accessibility for apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship participants.

Labor Union Collaboration

Applications demonstrating meaningful collaboration with labor unions can receive priority consideration.

The labor union must either be the applicant or provide a letter of commitment explaining its specific role in the project.

Potential involvement could include:

Serving as an affiliated Registered Apprenticeship sponsor.

Supporting curriculum development.

Supporting a Registered Pre-Apprenticeship program.

Providing continuing support after the grant period.

Addressing Barriers to Apprenticeship Participation

A major component of the opportunity is the expectation that projects address barriers that prevent people from entering or completing apprenticeship pathways.

Applicants should consider barriers such as:

Transportation challenges

Basic skills deficiencies

Socioeconomic limitations

Program waitlists

Program choice restrictions

Workplace accessibility challenges

Other barriers to education and employment

Projects that provide meaningful solutions to these challenges can strengthen access to apprenticeship opportunities.

Required Program Outcomes

Applicants are expected to propose measurable participant and program outcomes.

For new Registered Apprenticeship programs, the desired outcome is that 80% of participants either remain active apprentices or successfully complete the program.

For group apprenticeship models, the same 80% target applies to participants.

For Registered Pre-Apprenticeship programs, applicants must establish targets for completion and transition into the affiliated Registered Apprenticeship program.

At least 30% of pre-apprentices who complete the program must matriculate into the affiliated Registered Apprenticeship program.

The same 30% matriculation requirement applies to eligible pre-apprenticeship programs being replicated across multiple counties.

Expansion projects are similarly expected to focus on participation, completion, retention, and progression into apprenticeship.

Performance Metrics

L&I will work with successful applicants to establish performance metrics during the grant period.

Applicants should propose measurable outputs and outcomes covering areas such as:

Participant enrollment

Participant demographics

Continued participation

Program completion

Employer engagement

Training provider engagement

Apprentice and pre-apprentice participation

Transition from pre-apprenticeship into apprenticeship

Credentials obtained

Participant wages

Program impact

Partnership activities

Projects should also track the average wage of apprentices at the time of program completion.

Grantees are expected to maintain secure, confidential, accurate, and complete participant records for verification and compliance purposes.

Grant Evaluation Criteria

Applications will be reviewed through an initial eligibility review followed by a merit-based evaluation.

To be considered for funding, an application must achieve at least 70% of the total available score, equivalent to 84 out of 120 points.

The evaluation structure is:

Evaluation Area
Points

Project Design and Management Plan
25

Performance Outcomes
15

Impact and Sustainability
15

Stakeholder Engagement and Partnership
15

Other Selection Factors/Priority Considerations
35

Budget and Budget Justification
15

Total
120

This scoring structure makes it important for applicants to address every evaluation category directly and provide evidence rather than relying on general descriptions.

Project Design and Management Plan

This section is worth 25 points.

Applicants should clearly explain:

The workforce need being addressed.

The population to be served.

Employers involved.

Occupations targeted.

Geographic area covered.

Relevant labor market information.

Employer demand.

Workforce shortages.

Talent pipeline gaps.

The number of apprentices or pre-apprentices to be served.

How traditionally underserved populations will be reached.

How the project aligns with Pennsylvania’s WIOA Combined State Plan.

How the project aligns with Pennsylvania’s economic development priorities.

The implementation timeline.

Cohort start and completion dates.

Key milestones.

Registration steps.

Long-term sustainability.

Potential for scaling and replication.

Applicants must use the required timeline template in Appendix D.

Performance Outcomes

This category is worth 15 points.

Applicants must describe their intended outcomes and explain how those outcomes will be measured.

The application should include:

Goals

Services

Expected outcomes

Number of people to be served

Performance indicators

Enrollment targets

Completion targets

Employer engagement

Training provider engagement

Participant retention

Wage outcomes

The Goals and Outcomes Table in Appendix E must be used as required.

Impact and Sustainability

This category is worth 15 points.

Applicants should explain how the project will contribute to the broader goals of the Apprenticeships on the Move initiative.

They should identify:

Credentials participants will receive.

Expected impact on participants.

Expected impact on employers.

Impact of partnerships.

Data tracking and reporting capacity.

Recruitment metrics.

Participation metrics.

Completion and accomplishment metrics.

Long-term sustainability.

Applicants must also complete the Sustainability Plan in Appendix F.

The sustainability strategy should explain how the apprenticeship or pre-apprenticeship program will continue after the grant period ends.

Stakeholder Engagement and Partnerships

This section is worth 15 points.

Applicants should identify the organizations and stakeholders involved in the proposed project and clearly define their roles.

Potential partners may include:

Employers

Workforce development organizations

Educational institutions

Community-based organizations

Labor organizations

Economic development organizations

Workforce boards

Training providers

Applications should explain the responsibilities of each partner and demonstrate that the applicant has the capacity to coordinate the partnership effectively.

Key personnel should also be identified by name, along with their roles and contributions to the project.

Sector Diversity

Pennsylvania is also seeking diversity among funded sectors.

No more than three awards may be made to applications supporting the same industry sector, even where projects serve different geographic areas.

Applicants should therefore clearly identify the sector or sectors their project supports and explain how their proposal responds to workforce needs in that sector.

Budget Requirements

The proposed budget must be directly connected to the project narrative.

Applicants should provide:

Detailed budget line items.

Requested funds.

Leveraged funds.

Costs by category.

Quantities.

Unit costs where applicable.

Detailed justification for expenditures.

Explanation of how expenditures support project activities and deliverables.

Costs that are not discussed in the proposal should not appear in the budget.

Administrative costs may not exceed 10% of the total amount requested.

The budget must cover the entire performance period from May 1, 2027, to April 30, 2030.

Reimbursement-Based Funding

Applicants should understand that this grant does not operate as an upfront lump-sum payment.

Grant expenses are reimbursed after they have been incurred and documented.

Monthly invoices must be supported by appropriate documentation.

Organizations should therefore have sufficient financial and administrative capacity to manage expenses, maintain records, and submit invoices properly.

Awardees must document expenses consistently with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.

Supporting documentation may include evidence such as:

Invoices

Competitive bidding documentation

Time records

Payroll documentation

Other appropriate expenditure records

Employee time charged to the grant must accurately reflect the actual amount of time spent working on grant activities.

Important Restriction for New Programs

Organizations developing new Registered Apprenticeship or Pre-Apprenticeship programs should pay particular attention to the registration requirement.

New programs cannot invoice for:

On-the-Job Training (OJT)

Related Technical Instruction (RTI)

Supportive services

before the new apprenticeship or pre-apprenticeship program has been approved.

These expenses must be incurred after program approval.

Pennsylvania SAP Vendor Identification Number

Applicants are required to have a Pennsylvania SAP Vendor Identification Number.

The number can be obtained at no cost through the applicable Pennsylvania vendor registration process.

Applicants should begin this process early because obtaining the vendor number may take up to two weeks.

An organization may submit its application before receiving the number if necessary, but a grant will not be awarded without documentation of the required Pennsylvania Vendor Identification Number.

Applicants unable to meet this requirement at the time of award may have to relinquish the award.

Fiscal Agent Requirements

A fiscal agent is an organization that accepts responsibility for managing grant funds on behalf of the grantee.

The fiscal agent may be a business, school, workforce organization, or another eligible organization capable of managing the financial requirements of the award.

The fiscal agent is responsible for areas such as:

Fiscal accounting

Invoicing

Payments

State and federal tax reporting

Financial documentation

Audit requirements

A fiscal agent must also obtain employee dishonesty/theft insurance of at least $100,000.

Organizations that can manage the fiscal responsibilities themselves may serve as their own fiscal agents.

Where Local Workforce Development Boards apply as a region, the region must designate a single LWDB as the lead applicant and fiscal agent.

Application Package Requirements

Applicants must download and complete the official application documents provided by Pennsylvania L&I.

The application package must include several components.

1. Application Form

The Application Form must:

Be completed in full.

Be no more than one page.

Be saved as a single file.

Follow the required naming convention: ApplicantName_App_Form.

2. Project Summary Cover

The Project Summary Cover must not exceed three pages.

It should include:

Applicant name

Fiscal agent name

Vendor ID number

Unique Entity Identifier, where applicable

Project title

Project county

Project service area

Municipality

House and Senate districts served

Project partners

Brief project summary

Project point of contact

Contact information

3. Project Narrative

The Project Narrative is a central part of the application and may be up to 10 pages, excluding the Goals/Outcomes Table, Timeline, and Sustainability Plan attachments.

The narrative should address:

Project Design and Management Plan

Project steps

Performance Outcomes

Impact and Sustainability

Stakeholder Engagement and Partnership

Other Selection Factors and Priority Considerations

Applicants should structure the narrative so that evaluators can easily identify how each evaluation criterion has been addressed.

4. Timeline

Applicants must complete the required timeline template.

The timeline should show:

Implementation steps

Dates

Milestones

Cohort schedules

Registration activities

ATO engagement

Expected outcomes

Key benchmarks

For new programs, the timeline should specifically demonstrate the steps toward registration.

5. Goals and Outcomes Table

Applicants must complete the Goals and Outcomes Table in Appendix E.

The table should clearly identify the project’s goals, services, participant targets, and expected outcomes.

6. Sustainability Plan

Applicants must submit a sustainability plan explaining how the apprenticeship or pre-apprenticeship program will continue after the grant ends.

The plan should demonstrate that the project is designed for long-term impact rather than temporary implementation.

7. Letters of Support

Applicants must submit one to three unique letters of support.

Letters should demonstrate meaningful partner commitment and strong cross-sector collaboration.

They should describe:

The partner’s role.

Responsibilities.

Nature of the commitment.

How the organization will contribute to project implementation.

Applicants are encouraged to establish partnerships across areas such as education, workforce development, business, economic development, and community services.

8. Grant Financial Reporting Package

The Grant Financial Reporting Package must be submitted as a single Excel file.

It should include:

Requested funds

Leveraged funds

Expenditures by category

Line items

Budget justification

The budget will form the financial basis for the grant and reimbursement payments.

9. Local Workforce Development Board Notification

Applicants that are not LWDBs must notify their regional Local Workforce Development Board of their application.

A copy of the notification email must be included in the application package.

The requirement does not apply to LWDB applicants.

10. Worker Protection Certification

Applicants must complete the EO 2021-06 Worker Protection Certification Form.

The certification relates to compliance with Pennsylvania’s:

Unemployment Compensation Law

Workers’ Compensation Law

State labor laws

Workforce safety laws

Application Formatting Requirements

Applications must follow the required formatting specifications.

The main application documents should be:

Single-spaced

8.5 by 11 inches

Formatted with one-inch margins

Written in 11-point Calibri font

Submitted as PDF files, except for the Budget Form

Numbered with page numbers in the footer

Applications may not contain hyperlinks.

Applicants must also ensure that they do not include proprietary or sensitive business information.

Incomplete applications or applications that fail to meet the specified requirements will not be reviewed or scored.

Evaluators will review only the specified number of pages even if an application exceeds the permitted length. Letters of Support and the Budget Form do not count toward the applicable page limit.

How to Submit the Application

Completed application packages must be submitted electronically by email to the Pennsylvania Apprenticeship and Training Office Grants resource account: ATOGrants@pa.gov

The application must be submitted no later than: October 2, 2026, at 4:00 PM ET

Late applications will not be accepted.

Applicants should ensure that the email subject line follows the required grant naming instructions. The Notice specifies the application subject as:

“Apprenticeships on the Move: Advancing Pennsylvania’s Workforce”

Applicants should retain the automatic email confirmation received after submission.

If an applicant does not receive the automatic response, the applicant should forward the sent email to the ATO Grants Resource Account and provide the grant name, submission date and time, name, and telephone number.

Applicants may also contact the L&I Apprenticeship and Training Office at (717) 787-6997 if they do not receive an automatic confirmation.

Important Grant Timeline

Applicants should take note of the following dates:

August 12, 2026: Notice of Grant Availability released.

August 26, 2026 at 9:00 AM ET: Bidder’s Conference.

September 8, 2026 at 4:00 PM ET: Deadline for submitting questions.

October 2, 2026 at 4:00 PM ET: Application deadline.

May 1, 2027: Anticipated performance period start.

April 30, 2030: Anticipated contract end date.

Questions must be submitted to ATOGrants@pa.gov with the subject line “Question- Apprenticeships on the Move.”

Questions submitted after the deadline will not be answered.

Grant Award and Notification Process

Funding will be awarded competitively based on the availability of funds and the quality of submitted applications.

L&I expects to notify applicants by email within 30 days following the award determination.

Applicants whose proposals are not selected may request a feedback call within 30 days of receiving their denial notification.

Feedback requests must be submitted by the authorized representative using the appropriate email subject line.

Successful applicants will be required to enter into a Workforce Grant Agreement with L&I unless they already have an applicable grant agreement in place.

Reporting and Monitoring Requirements

Successful grantees will have substantial reporting responsibilities.

Grantees will be required to submit program and fiscal progress reports:

Monthly

Annually

At the conclusion of the project

Final closeout reports must generally be submitted within 60 days after the end of the performance period, or within 60 days of full expenditure, whichever occurs first.

Grantees may also be required to:

Participate in routine calls with L&I.

Share project progress.

Discuss best practices.

Receive technical assistance.

Participate in third-party evaluation.

Collect participant information.

Maintain appropriate records.

Submit additional performance data when requested.

Organizations must ensure that personally identifiable information is adequately protected and handled in accordance with applicable Commonwealth data protection requirements.

Allowable and Unallowable Costs

Grant funds must support the objectives and activities of the Apprenticeships on the Move initiative.

Allowable costs may include eligible project activities and administrative costs, subject to the grant requirements.

Administrative costs may not exceed 10% of the amount requested.

Examples of unallowable costs include:

Pre-award costs

Building construction

Lobbying services

Costs unrelated to direct performance of the award

Other expenses not aligned with the approved grant proposal

Pre-award costs are incurred at the applicant’s own risk and will not be reimbursed.

L&I can also disallow expenses that do not align with the approved grant proposal or Notice of Grant Award.

How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Proposals

Because the grant uses a competitive merit-based evaluation, applicants should develop their proposals around the scoring criteria rather than simply describing their organization.

A strong proposal should:

Clearly identify a genuine workforce problem.

Support the problem statement with labor-market and employer-demand evidence.

Identify the specific occupations and sector being targeted.

Clearly define the population and geographic area to be served.

Demonstrate meaningful employer participation.

Build strong cross-sector partnerships.

Explain how the project will increase apprenticeship participation.

Address barriers to entry and completion.

Establish measurable participant targets.

Provide realistic completion and retention goals.

Demonstrate a clear pathway from pre-apprenticeship into Registered Apprenticeship where applicable.

Explain how participants will obtain credentials.

Provide a detailed implementation timeline.

Demonstrate a credible path toward program registration where a new program is proposed.

Include a realistic and well-justified budget.

Demonstrate long-term sustainability.

Explain how project data will be collected, protected, analyzed, and reported.

Address priority considerations wherever applicable.

Secure strong letters of support from committed partners.

Ensure every required application component is complete and correctly formatted.

Key Considerations for New Apprenticeship Programs

Organizations proposing new programs should begin registration-related planning early.

The application should explain:

The occupation to be supported.

Why the occupation is appropriate for apprenticeship.

The workforce need.

Employer demand.

Proposed training structure.

Related technical instruction.

On-the-job learning.

Mentorship.

Credentials.

Program partners.

Registration milestones.

Engagement with the Apprenticeship and Training Office.

Applicants should verify whether their proposed occupation is apprenticeable through the relevant apprenticeship resources.

If an occupation is not already recognized as apprenticeable, applicants should use the applicable apprenticeability process and ensure compliance with Pennsylvania apprenticeship requirements.

Long-Term Sustainability

Sustainability is a major part of the evaluation.

Applicants must explain how the program will continue after the grant period.

A credible sustainability plan could demonstrate how partnerships, employer participation, training infrastructure, funding sources, program operations, and participant recruitment will continue beyond the grant.

The objective is to establish apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship systems that remain useful to employers and workers after grant funding has ended.

Why This Grant Matters for Pennsylvania’s Workforce

The Apprenticeships on the Move initiative represents an effort to connect workforce development directly with employer demand.

Instead of treating workforce training as a standalone activity, the initiative encourages collaboration among businesses, educational institutions, workforce boards, community organizations, labor organizations, and other stakeholders.

By combining paid work experience, technical instruction, mentorship, support services, and recognized credentials, apprenticeship programs can help individuals transition into skilled occupations while giving employers a structured mechanism for developing talent.

The initiative also places significant emphasis on expanding access for populations that have historically experienced barriers to employment and apprenticeship participation.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Pennsylvania Apprenticeships on the Move Grant 2026.

Conclusion

The Pennsylvania Apprenticeships on the Move: Advancing Pennsylvania’s Workforce Grant provides a significant opportunity for organizations across Pennsylvania to develop and expand Registered Apprenticeship and Registered Pre-Apprenticeship programs.

With approximately $4 million available and individual applicants able to request up to $249,999, the initiative is designed to support projects that address workforce shortages, strengthen talent pipelines, expand access to quality careers, and align workforce development with Pennsylvania’s economic priorities.

Eligible organizations can propose new programs or expand existing registered programs in agriculture, energy, life sciences, manufacturing, robotics and technology, education, healthcare, and skilled trades.

The strongest proposals will be those that clearly demonstrate employer demand, establish measurable outcomes, build strong partnerships, address barriers to participation, support underserved populations, provide a realistic implementation and sustainability strategy, and directly respond to the grant’s evaluation criteria.

Organizations interested in applying should begin preparing their application materials well before the deadline, particularly because the application requires multiple documents, partner letters, a detailed project narrative, a timeline, a sustainability plan, a detailed budget, and other supporting documentation.

The application deadline is October 2, 2026, at 4:00 PM ET, and late applications will not be accepted.

Prospective applicants should carefully review the official Notice of Grant Availability and all required application templates before submitting their proposal to ensure full compliance with Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry requirements.

TITLE: EBID Young Professionals Recruitment Programme 2026: Apply for the ECOWAS Bank Young Professionals Programme

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
EBID Young Professionals Recruitment Programme 2026

Opportunity
EBID Young Professionals Recruitment Programme

Organisation
ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID)

Target group
Young professionals / graduates

Age limit
Less than 30 years at recruitment

Qualification
Master’s degree or equivalent

Eligible applicants
Citizens of ECOWAS Member States

Location
Lomé, Togo

Contract
Two-year fixed-term contract

Probation
Six months

Potential outcome
Conversion to open-ended contract if performance is satisfactory

Application format
Paper/hard-copy application

Deadline
October 30, 2026

The ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID) has announced its Young Professionals Recruitment Programme, seeking to recruit high-calibre young graduates from universities and other tertiary institutions of learning in the West African sub-region and the diaspora.

The programme is designed for young professionals who will not be more than 30 years of age at the time of recruitment. Successful candidates will be appointed as Young Trainee Professional Staff under a two-year fixed-term contract.

About the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID)

The ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID) is an international financial institution owned by the fifteen Member States of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

The ECOWAS Member States are Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Côte d’Ivoire, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone and Togo.

The headquarters of EBID is located in Lomé, Togolese Republic. The mission of EBID is to work towards the emergence of an economically strong, industrialized and prosperous West Africa that is fully integrated within the region and world economy in order to take advantage of the opportunities offered by globalization.

EBID Young Professionals Recruitment Programme 2026

The EBID Young Professionals Programme is designed for high-calibre young professionals who will not be more than 30 years old at the time of recruitment.

Selected candidates will be appointed as Young Trainee Professional Staff under a two-year fixed-term contract.

Candidates will undergo a six-month probationary period, during which either party may terminate the relationship without prior notice. Where the performance of the Young Trainee Professional Staff is satisfactory during the probationary period, the appointment will be converted into an open-ended contract, meaning successful candidates can become permanent members of staff of the Bank.

During the appointment, Young Trainee Professional Staff will be posted to different departments on a rotational basis. This is intended to familiarize them with the activities of the Bank, integrate them into teams and enable them to make positive contributions.

Trainee Professional Staff will also work under the supervision of senior staff to become acquainted with the various Departments, Policies and Programmes of EBID.

EBID Young Professionals Programme Eligibility Criteria

Citizens of ECOWAS Member States who meet the following criteria are invited to apply:

Be less than 30 years of age at the time of recruitment.

Hold a Master’s degree or equivalent qualification in fields related to the activities of the Bank.

Be able to work in a team and under pressure within a multicultural environment.

Have strong analytical and organizational skills, with the ability to plan and determine priorities.

Have good research skills for obtaining pertinent information, including banking analysis, statistics and monitoring competitive trends, from external sources, electronic databases and other media admitted for professional purposes.

Have good knowledge of office automation systems, including Excel, Word, Access and PowerPoint.

Be fluent in English, French or Portuguese, with a working knowledge of one of the other two languages.

Eligible Fields of Study

The required Master’s degree or equivalent qualification may be in fields related to EBID’s activities, including:

Asset/Liabilities Management

Audit

Communication and Marketing

Finance

Engineering

Business Administration

Law

Accounting

Economics

Information Technology (IT)

Human Resources

Infrastructure

Private Sector Operations

Public Sector Operations

Risk Management

Language Services

Other areas relevant to the activities of the Bank.

EBID Young Professionals Salary and Conditions of Service

According to the recruitment advertisement, young professionals will be posted to departments in response to specific needs and will not be recruited to fill vacant positions.

Throughout the duration of their appointment, they will be considered Professional staff of the Bank. Their conditions of service will correspond to grade P1-1 in the EBID staff classification and salary scale.

Various allowances will be added to the salary, including:

Post adjustment allowance

Housing allowance

Transport allowance

Family grant, where necessary

Young professionals will also be admitted into the Bank’s pension scheme during their appointment.

They will further be entitled to insurance cover against death and permanent disability, total and permanent disability, temporary occupational disability, partial permanent disability, personal accident and sickness.

EBID Recruitment Criteria and Selection Procedure

Shortlisted candidates will be invited for written and oral tests at the headquarters of the Bank in Lomé.

Candidates will be tested for:

Technical skills

Potential

Personality and level of motivation

Computer skills

Good verbal communication and writing skills in not less than two of the three working languages of the Bank.

Documents Required for EBID Young Professionals Application

Interested candidates who meet the eligibility criteria should submit their application dossier to the Bank in paper form.

The application dossier should comprise:

A detailed curriculum vitae;

Copy of qualifications obtained;

Copy of national identity card or passport;

Copy of birth certificate;

A letter of motivation indicating:

Reasons for participating in the programme;

Areas of competence/interest;

Relevant experience; and

Career prospects.

EBID Young Professionals Programme 2026 Application Deadline

Interested candidates should submit their hard-copy application dossiers no later than October 30, 2026.

Applications must be submitted in a sealed envelope marked “2026 Young Professionals Recruitment Programme” and addressed to:

ECOWAS BANK FOR INVESTMENT AND DEVELOPMENT (EBID)
128, Boulevard du 13 janvier
B.P. 2704, Lomé – Togo
Tel: +228 22 21 68 64

Important Note

Only shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview. EBID reserves the right to withdraw the notified vacancies or offer a position at a lower grade.

How to Apply for the EBID Young Professionals Programme 2026

Eligible applicants should prepare the required application dossier in paper form, including their detailed CV, qualifications, national identity card or passport, birth certificate and motivation letter.

The complete application should be placed in a sealed envelope marked:

“2026 Young Professionals Recruitment Programme”

and submitted to the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID), 128 Boulevard du 13 janvier, B.P. 2704, Lomé – Togo, no later than October 30, 2026.

TITLE: UN Junior Professional Officer Programme 2026 | Three Positions Open

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The United Nations Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme 2026 is inviting applications from qualified young professionals for three JPO positions within the United Nations system.

The current call features opportunities in Political Affairs in New York, Humanitarian Affairs in East Jerusalem, and UN System Coordination in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire. All three positions are funded by Belgium and have an initial one-year contract that may be renewed annually for a maximum period of three years. (FPS Foreign Affairs)

The application deadline for all three positions is 18 September 2026 at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (New York). (FPS Foreign Affairs)

About the UN Junior Professional Officer Programme

The Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme is a United Nations training initiative that provides young professionals with an opportunity to gain practical experience within UN organisations, funds, programmes, and offices involved in development and international cooperation.

Through the programme, JPOs work within UN organisations connected to Belgium’s international development cooperation policy. Depending on the position, assignments can be based in partner countries, regional offices, or headquarters.

JPOs receive professional training and guidance from senior staff members and can become involved in areas including:

Programme design

Programme formulation

Programme implementation

Programme monitoring

Programme evaluation

Policy and coordination work

Development and humanitarian activities

The Belgian government currently funds JPO positions across 18 UN organisations, funds, programmes and offices, including UNDP, UNICEF, WFP, FAO, UNHCR, WHO, UNFPA, UN Women, UNEP, IOM, OHCHR and OCHA.

Current JPO Opportunities

Three positions are currently available under the 2026 Belgian JPO call.

1. JPO in Political Affairs – Support to UN Reform

Organisation: United Nations Executive Office of the Secretary-General (EOSG), Office of the Under-Secretary-General for Policy, UN80 Secretariat

Location: New York, USA

Field: Political Affairs / UN Reform

The position focuses on supporting work related to UN reform and political affairs within the UN80 Secretariat.

Eligibility and Qualifications

Applicants must:

Hold Belgian citizenship.

Be 32 years old or younger as of 31 December 2026.

Be born on or after 1 January 1994.

Hold an advanced university degree, such as a master’s degree or equivalent, in:

Political Science

International Relations

International Humanitarian Law

Human Rights

Social Sciences or another related field.

Have at least two years of relevant professional experience in political affairs, development and/or humanitarian work.

Have relevant experience with governments, international organisations, NGOs or research institutes.

Experience with the UN or other international or non-governmental organisations is considered an advantage. Strong research, analytical and writing skills, as well as organisational abilities, are also preferred.

Language Requirements

Fluent English is required.

Knowledge of French is desirable, while knowledge of another official UN language is an advantage.

Important Experience Requirement

Applicants’ work experience within the UN organisation to which they are applying must not exceed one year, including internships, UN Volunteers and consultancies. Relevant internships and volunteering may be counted at 50%.

2. JPO in Humanitarian Affairs

Organisation: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), Operations and Advocacy Division, Country Office in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt)

Location: East Jerusalem

Field: Humanitarian Affairs

This position is focused on humanitarian affairs and supports work related to humanitarian operations and advocacy.

Eligibility and Qualifications

Applicants must:

Hold Belgian citizenship.

Be 32 years old or younger as of 31 December 2026.

Be born on or after 1 January 1994.

Hold an advanced university degree, such as a Master’s degree, in:

Political or Social Science

International Relations

Public Administration

Law

Economics

Engineering

Earth Sciences

A related field.

Have at least two years of relevant professional experience in humanitarian affairs, emergency preparedness, crisis or emergency relief management, rehabilitation, development, or related areas.

Have experience in information analysis.

Experience working with international humanitarian agencies, the UN system, or in the occupied Palestinian territory context is considered desirable.

Language Requirements

Fluency in English is required.

Knowledge of Arabic is an advantage.

As with the other positions, work experience within the UN organisation to which the candidate is applying must not exceed one year, including internships, UNV and consultancies.

3. JPO in Coordination – UN System Coordination

Organisation: United Nations Resident Coordinator System (RCS), Resident Coordinator Office (RCO)

Location: Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire

Field: UN System Coordination

This position focuses on coordination within the UN Resident Coordinator System and provides an opportunity to contribute to cooperation and coordination across the UN system.

Eligibility and Qualifications

Applicants must:

Hold Belgian citizenship.

Be 32 years old or younger as of 31 December 2026.

Be born on or after 1 January 1994.

Hold a Master’s degree or equivalent advanced degree in:

Development

International Relations

Political Science

Economics

Management

A related field.

Have at least two years of professional experience in a relevant field.

Language Requirements

Fluency in French is required.

Knowledge of other official UN languages, particularly English, is an advantage.

General Eligibility Requirements

Although the three positions have different academic and professional requirements, the current Belgian-funded JPO call has several common eligibility conditions.

Belgian Citizenship

The current vacancies explicitly state that candidates must hold Belgian citizenship.

The Belgian Foreign Affairs website explains that most Belgian-funded JPO positions are reserved for Belgian nationals. A limited number of positions may be reserved for candidates from Belgium’s partner countries, but this must be specifically indicated in the relevant vacancy announcement. (FPS Foreign Affairs)

Therefore, applicants should not assume that every Belgian-funded JPO position is open to applicants from all countries.

Age Requirement

Candidates must be 32 years old or younger on 31 December 2026.

For the current positions, this means candidates must have been born on or after 1 January 1994.

Master’s Degree

A master’s degree or equivalent advanced university degree is required, although the acceptable field differs according to the position.

Professional Experience

The current positions generally require a minimum of two years of relevant professional experience.

Applicants should make sure that their experience is directly related to the responsibilities and subject area of the position for which they are applying.

UN Experience Limitation

For the current positions, professional experience within the specific UN organisation to which the applicant is applying should not exceed one year, including internships, UN Volunteers and consultancies.

Relevant internships and volunteering may be counted at 50%.

How the JPO Programme Works

JPOs work within participating UN organisations and receive professional training from experienced senior staff.

They may contribute to different stages of programme and policy work, including:

Defining programmes.

Formulating programmes.

Implementing programmes.

Monitoring programmes.

Evaluating programmes.

This allows young professionals to gain experience within the UN system while developing practical knowledge in international development, humanitarian affairs, policy, coordination and related fields.

Contract Duration

The initial JPO appointment is for one year.

Subject to a positive performance evaluation, the appointment may be renewed annually, up to a maximum total period of three years.

Salary and Employment Conditions

JPOs receive the international status of the UN organisation that recruits them.

Their salary is paid in US dollars and is based on the United Nations salary scales.

Belgium also contributes toward the pension component through the Belgian National Social Security Office or the United Nations pension fund, as applicable.

At the end of the JPO contract, there are no special placement facilities provided by Belgium’s Directorate-General for Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid. However, the experience and knowledge gained through the programme can improve participants’ prospects for progressing within international organisations.

Application Process

Applications must be submitted directly to the relevant UN organisation through the application system indicated in the vacancy announcement.

Candidates should consult the full job description before applying because the current Belgian Foreign Affairs page only displays the vacancy information during the application period.

The current vacancies direct applicants to the UNDESA recruitment website and its eRecruitment system.

Application portal: UNDESA JPO Application Portal

Applicants should select the appropriate position and follow the instructions provided by the UN recruitment system.

Application Documents and Selection

The Belgian Foreign Affairs guidance explains that shortlisted candidates may be required to provide copies of their:

University degree(s)

Employment certificates

Identity card or passport

The initial preselection is based on the candidate’s Personal History/CV and Cover Letter.

Shortlisted candidates are interviewed online.

Tips for Preparing Your Application

The Belgian Foreign Affairs department provides several recommendations for applicants.

Read the Vacancy Carefully

Study the required qualifications and responsibilities before completing the application.

Use Relevant Keywords

The department recommends using keywords appearing in the vacancy and making them clearly visible in the application.

Be Specific

Avoid vague descriptions of your experience.

Instead, provide concrete examples of relevant work and the results you achieved.

Provide Accurate Dates

When completing your application, provide accurate information, including the month and year where requested.

Avoid Unnecessary Acronyms

Write out abbreviations and acronyms rather than assuming that the selection panel will understand them.

Make Your Motivation Precise

Because the JPO selection process is described as highly competitive, applicants should ensure that their motivation clearly demonstrates why their background matches the specific position.

Application Deadline

The deadline for all three current Belgian-funded JPO positions is:

18 September 2026 at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (New York).

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. Applicants will receive confirmation that their application has been received, and only shortlisted candidates will subsequently be contacted.

Current Positions at a Glance

Position
Organisation
Location
Key Field
Deadline

JPO in Political Affairs – Support to UN Reform
UN Executive Office of the Secretary-General
New York, USA
Political Affairs / UN Reform
18 Sept. 2026

JPO in Humanitarian Affairs
OCHA

Humanitarian Affairs
18 Sept. 2026

JPO in Coordination – UN System Coordination
UN Resident Coordinator System
Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire
UN Coordination
18 Sept. 2026

The positions all have an initial one-year duration, renewable annually up to three years.

Who Can Apply?

Category of people who qualify: Young professionals who hold Belgian citizenship, are no older than 32 at the end of 2026, possess a relevant master’s degree or equivalent advanced degree, and have at least two years of relevant professional experience.

The precise academic background, work experience and language requirements depend on the JPO position selected.

Eligible nationality: The three current vacancies are specifically for Belgian citizens.

Conclusion

The UN Junior Professional Officer Programme 2026 provides an opportunity for qualified young Belgian professionals to gain practical experience within the United Nations system.

The current call offers three positions spanning political affairs and UN reform, humanitarian affairs, and UN system coordination, with placements in New York, East Jerusalem, and Abidjan.

The programme provides structured professional experience, exposure to international organisations, senior-level mentorship, and the opportunity to contribute to UN programmes and policy work. Successful JPO appointments begin with one year and can potentially be extended to a maximum of three years following positive evaluations.

Eligible candidates should carefully match their academic qualifications and professional experience to the specific vacancy and submit their application before 18 September 2026 at 6:00 PM Eastern Time.

In France

The Institut des Hautes Etudes Scientifiques is a foundation officially recognized as being in the public interest according to French law. Any donation made by a French tax resident to IHES provides tax benefits to the donor:

For individuals

Income tax: 66% of donations made by individuals to the Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques are tax deductible, provided they do not exceed 20% of the donor’s taxable income.

If gifts exceed the 20% income limit, the donor may defer the tax deduction on the excess amount over the next five years.

“Impôt sur la fortune immobilière”: 75% of the gifts made to certain not-for-profit organizations such as IHES, up to a limit of 50 000€, are tax deductible for donors who pay this tax.

For companies

Payments made by companies to the Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques result in a reduction in their corporate or income tax of 60% of the gift value. The limit beyond which it is no longer tax deductible is 0.5% of the company’s turnover.

If the payments exceed 0.5% of turnover, or if the company is in deficit, it may defer tax deductibility over five years.

TITLE: Request for Proposals: Deepening Knowledge and Implementation of Research Ethics in the African Context

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
About the SGCI

The Science Granting Councils Initiative (SGCI) is a multi-donor Initiative with Phase 2 (SGCI-2: 2020-2023) supported by Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida), United Kingdom’s Department for International Development (DFID), Canada’s International Development Research Centre (IDRC), South Africa’s National Research Foundation (NRF) and the German Research Foundation (DFG).

The overall goal of the SGCI-2 Research Management project is to fortify the capability of Science Granting Councils in explicit areas of research management, namely research excellence (particularly the knowledge and use of tools such as Research Quality Plus framework), research ethics, emerging scientific practices (especially open data, open access and citizen science) Good Financial Grant Practice (GFGP) benchmarking exercise and development of online grant management systems (including databases of peer reviewers).

The Association of African Universities (AAU) and the African Academy of Sciences (AAS) are the consortium partners for the SGCI-2 Research Management project. Both AAU and AAS are two continental higher education bodies with experience in research management. The AAU has participated in the SGCI-1 as part of the “Theme 3” Consortium. The SGCI-1 provided the AAU with invaluable experiences and lessons of working with and being part of activities taking place at the level of national science systems.

The SGCI-1 experiences and lessons learnt have been brought to bear on the SGCI-2 and are helping strengthen the capacity of Science Granting Councils to effectively and efficiently play their essential roles in research, knowledge and innovation.

Why the focus on strengthening knowledge and implementation of Research Ethics in the African context among SGCs

As part of the second phase of SGCI (SGCI-2) inception phase activities, the Initiative Management Team (IMT) interviewed 13 of the 15 SGCI Councils to better understand their individual research and capacity strengthening interests and priorities. Twelve (12) SGCI Councils identified Research Ethics as a high priority training need. SGCs in Sub Saharan Africa are not at the same level of maturity in terms of developing, implementing and enforcing research ethics practices. Kruger et al. (2014) In their contribution to a book on ‘Research Ethics in Africa’ mapped the status of research oversight systems and practices in Africa and reported that research initiatives in Africa had not automatically been complemented by advances in ‘health research oversight systems and functional ethical review committees. They decried that this had left the continent exposed to potential exploitative research funded by resource rich countries. Against this backdrop, there is need to build functional research regulatory frameworks in Africa through strengthening research ethics committees and adherence to national laws and guidelines. The SGCI-2 project work area on Research Ethics seeks to support national/regional studies aimed at deepening knowledge and implementation of research ethics in the African context. This work will be implemented in close partnership with participating Councils. The lessons from these studies will be used to refine and strengthen the implementation of research ethics codes.

Specifically, activities in this work area will include:

Identification and selection of themes for the national and regional studies.

Activities to support research, information gathering and knowledge sharing.

Publication of the national and regional studies including on factors that promote the involvement of women in research management.

The national and regional studies will be based upon using a participatory process to; prioritize the thematic areas for these studies; reviewing studies done in SGCI-1 of this project – e.g. the baseline studies; identifying the experts/consultants who will participate in other planned project activities. It is expected that this action will lead to two (2) published national studies and one (1) regional study including one on gender transformative approach, as well as a study on the review of the Research Ethics oversight systems and practices in selected SGC countries.

The Scope of Work

The AAU-AAS are seeking a consultant to undertake national and regional studies aimed at deepening knowledge and implementation of Research Ethics in the African context.

The consultant will be asked to perform the following tasks:

Identification and selection of themes for the national and regional studies

Identify consulting partner to co-implement and deliver on work area and work with AAU to develop ToRs and contract.

Identify the target SGCs and individuals for the studies

Conduct stakeholders’ meeting to identify and select themes for national and research studies.

Participate in project-wide activities to support, research, information gathering and knowledge sharing

Identify target SGCs and Individuals for the studies.

Facilitate on-line communication, surveys, documentation, as well as in-person desk study, conversations

Conduct a desk review of existing literature in the selected thematic areas

Develop data collection tools for the national and regional studies, pretest tools and implement surveys

Deliverables:

Publish two (2) national studies and one (1) regional study including one on gender transformative approach, as well as a study on the review of the Research Ethics oversight systems and practices in selected SGC countries.

Profile required and Submission of proposals

Consultant profile:

The consultant we are looking for should fulfill the following requirements:

(a) Deep knowledge of the research ethics landscape on the African Continent

(b) Broad understanding of the regulatory frameworks of Science Granting Councils in Sub Saharan Africa, including existing standards and best practice guidelines for the conduct of science, technology and innovation.

(c) Excellent project management skills in an international work environment.

(d) Excellent skills in conducting high level stakeholder meetings

(e) Demonstrated skills in conducting Research Ethics studies in Sub Saharan Africa.

Proposal Submission Guidelines:

Proposals from bidders should include the following elements:

a) A cover letter introducing the submission;

b) An overview of the consultant, including similar past experience, names, bios and detailed CVs of the consultant(s) who will be involved in this project, outlining the relevant skills and experience;

c) Three references from organizations with whom you’ve worked on similar projects outlining these past project deliverables and results;

d) An overview of the consultant’s understanding of this engagement;

e) Overview of the consultant’s proposed project plan, deliverables, timelines, milestones and outcomes;

f) Proposed budget for the provision of the services, broken down by deliverable and timeline. The Prices quoted should be inclusive of all taxes and delivery costs, must be in USD and shall remain valid for (120) days from the closing date of the tender;

h) Consultant(s) are encouraged to include any additional information they believe demonstrates added value for the AAU-AAS within the scope of this assignment.
