TITLE: AIAS-AUFF Fellowships 2027–2029: Fully Funded Research Fellowship at Aarhus University in Denmark

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies (AIAS) at Aarhus University in Denmark has opened applications for the AIAS-AUFF Fellowships 2027–2029, offering up to 10 fellowship opportunities for talented, curiosity-driven researchers from around the world.

The fellowship is designed for researchers across all academic and research disciplines who are interested in pursuing innovative, interdisciplinary research in an international and collaborative academic environment. Successful fellows will join AIAS in Aarhus, Denmark, where they will have access to an intellectually stimulating research community, office space, academic activities, conferences, workshops, and relevant research environments across Aarhus University.

The AIAS-AUFF Fellowship is particularly suited to researchers who want to develop their research independently while also engaging with scholars from different disciplines and exploring opportunities for collaboration at Aarhus University.

The fellowship starts on 1 September 2027 and lasts for 23 months. Applicants must have between 2 and 10 years of research career experience after completing their PhD by the application deadline.

Who Can Apply for the AIAS-AUFF Fellowship?

The AIAS-AUFF Fellowship is an international opportunity open to researchers of any nationality. The call welcomes applications from researchers working in all research disciplines and areas, making it suitable for applicants from different academic and professional research backgrounds.

To qualify, applicants must meet several key requirements:

They must be curiosity-driven researchers with a strong interest in developing their research.

They must have 2 to 10 years of career experience after completing their PhD by the application deadline.

They can come from any nationality.

They can apply from any country or continent, provided they satisfy the fellowship’s eligibility requirements.

Their research must demonstrate an interdisciplinary dimension, either through an interdisciplinary research project or a clear interdisciplinary research interest.

Applicants should have, or identify, relevant opportunities for collaboration at Aarhus University.

They must satisfy the fellowship’s mobility requirement concerning previous residence or main work activity in Denmark.

Importantly, the source does not specify any race, ethnic-group restriction, or continental limitation. Instead, it explicitly states that applications are welcomed from researchers of any nationality and from all research disciplines.

About the AIAS-AUFF Fellowships

The AIAS-AUFF Fellowship is hosted by the Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies (AIAS), an institute within Aarhus University that brings researchers together across disciplines, academic seniority and nationalities.

The fellowship provides researchers with an opportunity to step away from the routine demands of their everyday research environment and dedicate substantial time to developing their research in a stimulating academic setting.

AIAS describes itself as an environment for intellectual exploration, bringing together excellent researchers who want to advance their work through interdisciplinary, international and collaborative engagement.

The fellowship is therefore not limited to researchers working in a particular subject area. Instead, it encourages applications across research fields and themes, creating opportunities for researchers to encounter different methodologies, perspectives and approaches to academic inquiry.

Why Apply for the AIAS-AUFF Fellowship?

There are several reasons why researchers may find the AIAS-AUFF Fellowship particularly valuable.

1. Join an international research community

Fellows become part of an international academic community at AIAS, where researchers from different disciplines and countries interact and exchange ideas.

This environment can expose fellows to new approaches to research and create opportunities for intellectual collaboration beyond their immediate academic specialization.

2. Develop interdisciplinary research

Interdisciplinary research is a central feature of the fellowship.

AIAS encourages researchers to cross traditional academic boundaries and engage with scholars working in other research areas. This can help fellows develop new research questions, identify alternative methodologies and explore connections between disciplines.

The fellowship is therefore particularly relevant for researchers whose work naturally intersects with multiple academic fields.

3. Access Aarhus University’s research environment

Fellows will be affiliated with relevant research environments at Aarhus University.

This provides an opportunity to connect their work with established academic communities, research departments and research hubs within the university.

Applicants are specifically expected to identify relevant collaboration possibilities at Aarhus University as part of their application.

4. Participate in academic activities

AIAS fellows can participate in a range of academic activities, including

Academic training activities

Conferences

Workshops

Institute events

Collaborative activities with researchers from different disciplines

Fellows are also welcome to join, organize and contribute to events and activities at AIAS.

5. Work in a stimulating academic environment

AIAS aims to provide an environment where researchers can focus on developing their work while engaging with colleagues from different academic backgrounds.

The institute’s interdisciplinary structure is intended to encourage discussion, creativity and the exchange of ideas.

6. Strengthen academic and career development

The fellowship offers a career-empowering environment in which fellows can develop important competencies for academic development.

The source also highlights tailored activities designed to support researchers in developing skills and perspectives that can contribute to their longer-term academic careers.

Research Areas and Disciplines

One of the major advantages of the AIAS-AUFF Fellowship is its broad disciplinary scope.

The fellowship welcomes applications from all research disciplines. AIAS operates as an interdisciplinary platform that connects researchers across Aarhus University, including different departments and research hubs.

This means the opportunity is not restricted to a particular field such as social sciences, engineering, medicine, humanities, natural sciences or technology.

Researchers should instead focus on demonstrating the quality and relevance of their proposed research while explaining how their work can benefit from an interdisciplinary environment and potential collaboration at Aarhus University.

AIAS emphasizes that its fellows work across different research areas and themes, helping to create an environment where academic boundaries can be crossed and new ideas can emerge.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements before beginning their applications.

PhD and career experience requirement

Applicants must have between 2 and 10 years of career experience after completing their PhD by the fellowship application deadline.

This is an important requirement because the fellowship is specifically intended for researchers who have already established themselves in the post-PhD stage of their careers but are still within the specified career-experience window.

Nationality requirement

There is no nationality restriction stated in the call.

Researchers from any nationality are encouraged to apply.

Consequently, the opportunity is open internationally rather than being limited to researchers from Denmark, Europe, Africa, Asia, North America, South America, Oceania or any other specific region.

Interdisciplinary requirement

Applicants should have an interdisciplinary research project and/or interdisciplinary research interest.

This means applicants should be able to demonstrate how their research connects with ideas, methods, perspectives or expertise beyond a single academic discipline.

Collaboration requirement

Applicants should have, or identify, relevant collaboration possibilities at Aarhus University.

Prospective applicants should therefore familiarize themselves with relevant research environments at the university and consider where meaningful academic connections could be developed.

Mobility requirement

Applicants must also satisfy AIAS’s mobility requirement.

Under this requirement, applicants must not have resided or carried out their main work activity in Denmark for more than 12 months during the two years immediately preceding the application deadline.

This condition should be carefully considered by anyone who has recently lived or worked in Denmark.

What Does the Fellowship Provide?

Successful AIAS-AUFF fellows will receive several forms of support during their fellowship.

Salary

Fellows receive a salary based on seniority.

The employment conditions and wages are regulated through Danish collective union agreements.

This means the fellowship is structured as an employment-based research fellowship rather than simply an unpaid academic residency.

Relocation travel costs

The fellowship provides coverage for relocation travel costs, helping successful candidates move to Denmark for the fellowship.

Relocation assistance

In addition to relocation travel costs, fellows receive relocation assistance.

This can help researchers transition to their new academic environment in Aarhus.

Office space

Fellows are provided with office space at AIAS, giving them a dedicated environment in which to conduct their research and participate in institute activities.

Academic activities

Fellows can participate in AIAS’s academic training activities, conferences and workshops.

They can also engage with events and activities hosted by the institute and contribute to the academic community.

Affiliation with Aarhus University research environments

Fellows will be affiliated with relevant research environments at Aarhus University.

This affiliation can facilitate engagement with researchers and academic communities connected to their area of research.

Fellowship Duration and Start Date

The AIAS-AUFF Fellowships will begin on:

1 September 2027

The fellowship duration is

23 months

The opportunity is therefore designed to provide fellows with an extended period in which to pursue their research, collaborate with other scholars and participate in the academic life of AIAS and Aarhus University.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the AIAS-AUFF Fellowships 2027–2029 is

3 November 2026 at 12:00 noon CET

Applicants should ensure that their online application is completed and submitted before the stated deadline.

The call opened in August 2026, followed by an evaluation and selection period running from November 2026 to February 2027.

Applicants are expected to receive the outcome of the selection process in March 2027, while successful fellows will begin their fellowships on 1 September 2027.

AIAS-AUFF Fellowship Application Timeline

The official timeline is as follows:

Call opens: August 2026

Application deadline: 3 November 2026 at 12:00 noon CET

Evaluation and selection: November 2026 to February 2027

Applicants receive answers: March 2027

Fellowships begin: 1 September 2027

Applicants should pay particular attention to the deadline and time zone because applications submitted after the closing time may not be considered.

How to Apply for the AIAS-AUFF Fellowship

Applications must be submitted online through the GrantOne application system.

Applicants should consult the official Guide for Applicants before preparing and submitting their application. The guide contains detailed information about:

Application requirements

The structure of the online application system

Selection criteria

The selection process

Other relevant instructions for applicants

Because the fellowship places emphasis on interdisciplinary research and collaboration possibilities at Aarhus University, applicants should carefully develop their research proposal and clearly demonstrate why AIAS and Aarhus University are an appropriate environment for their work.

Application portal: GrantOne

Official call: AIAS-AUFF Call for Fellowships 2027–2029

Applicant guidance: AIAS-AUFF Guidelines 2027–2029

APPLY HERE

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Although the source does not prescribe additional application strategies beyond its stated requirements, prospective applicants can use the fellowship’s eligibility criteria to guide their preparation.

Demonstrate interdisciplinary relevance

Because interdisciplinary research is explicitly required, applicants should clearly explain the interdisciplinary dimension of their project or research interests.

The proposal should make it easy for reviewers to understand how different disciplines, perspectives or methodologies contribute to the research.

Identify collaboration opportunities at Aarhus University

Applicants are expected to have or identify relevant collaboration possibilities at Aarhus University.

It is therefore important to consider which research environments, departments, researchers or research hubs could be relevant to the proposed work.

Clearly position your post-PhD experience

Applicants should ensure that their application clearly establishes that they fall within the required 2–10 years of post-PhD career experience by the application deadline.

Review the official application guide

Before submitting an application, candidates should carefully read the official Guide for Applicants to understand the application structure, requirements, selection criteria and selection process.

Allow sufficient time for submission

Because the deadline is fixed at 12:00 noon CET on 3 November 2026, applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications.

About Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies

The Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies brings researchers together across disciplines, academic seniority and nationality.

AIAS offers fellowships to excellent researchers from different academic disciplines, allowing them to pursue cutting-edge research in conditions intended to support high-quality academic work.

The institute’s interdisciplinary environment is built around the idea that interaction with researchers from different fields can introduce new perspectives and approaches.

Through daily encounters with colleagues from diverse research disciplines, fellows may gain fresh insights into their own research, explore different methods and develop new research questions and ideas.

About Aarhus University

The AIAS-AUFF Fellowship is hosted at Aarhus University in Denmark.

The Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies is located on the university’s campus in Aarhus, providing fellows with access to an academic environment that connects international scholars with researchers across the university.

The institute’s location within Aarhus University supports its role as an interdisciplinary platform and enables fellows to interact with research communities beyond their immediate field.

Visit HERE for more information about the AIAS-AUFF Fellowships 2027–2029.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the AIAS-AUFF Fellowship fully open to international applicants?

Yes. The call states that applications are welcomed from researchers of any nationality.

Which academic disciplines are eligible?

The fellowship welcomes applications from all research disciplines and research areas.

How many fellowships are available?

The call offers up to 10 AIAS-AUFF Fellowships.

Conclusion

The AIAS-AUFF Fellowships 2027–2029 provide an opportunity for talented post-PhD researchers from around the world to spend 23 months pursuing research within an international, interdisciplinary and collaborative academic environment at Aarhus University in Denmark.

With up to 10 fellowships available, the programme welcomes researchers from all research disciplines and any nationality who have between 2 and 10 years of post-PhD career experience, meet the mobility requirement, demonstrate interdisciplinary interests and can identify relevant collaboration opportunities at Aarhus University.

The fellowship provides a salary based on seniority, relocation travel costs, relocation assistance, office space and opportunities to participate in academic training, conferences and workshops. Fellows also become affiliated with relevant research environments at Aarhus University.

Researchers interested in applying should carefully review the official application requirements and Guide for Applicants and ensure that their applications clearly address the interdisciplinary and collaborative dimensions of their proposed research.

The application deadline is 3 November 2026 at 12:00 noon CET, with the fellowships scheduled to begin on 1 September 2027.

Area of Physics

High Energy and Particle Theory

Research Interests

Ben Lehmann’s research is dedicated to understanding the nature and properties of dark matter.

Until recently, all signs pointed to a scenario in which dark matter is associated with new particle physics near the weak scale. But new experimental results have seriously challenged the most promising benchmark models, suggesting that the dark matter particle and its interactions could instead lie anywhere in an enormous parameter space.

Ben’s work focuses on probing this vast space by connecting dark matter particle physics to novel experimental and observational tools, including condensed matter systems, cosmological surveys and gravitational waves.

Biographical Sketch

Ben grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area, and has been a long-time resident of the region. He went from a local high school to Stanford University, where he received a B.S. with honors in physics and an M.S. in mathematics. Ben then traveled down the coast to the University of California, Santa Cruz, for his Ph.D.

Beyond research, Ben is passionate about mentoring students and engaging in outreach to the wider community. He has taught everywhere from elementary schools to correctional facilities. Ben also enjoys singing, hiking, and a good loaf of challah.

TITLE: Call for Youth Participants to the 2026 United Nations Youth Townhall

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 7, 2026

Applications are open for the United Nations Youth Townhall 2026. Young people are driving change around the world — from climate action and peacebuilding to technology, education, human rights and entrepreneurship. At the same time, many young people still face barriers to participating in decisions and processes that shape their lives and futures.

The first-ever UN Youth Townhall will bring over 1,000 participants together in Heidelberg, Germany, to build intergenerational trust, strengthen connections and create new opportunities for collaboration.

Convened by the United Nations Youth Office together with partners, the Townhall will bring young people, governments, the United Nations, civil society, the private sector and others into one space. At its core, the Townhall seeks to:

Strengthen inclusion and diversity — broadening participation in global youth engagement by reaching young people and communities too often excluded from international spaces and processes.

Reduce fragmentation across the ecosystem — creating stronger connections and collaboration between the many actors working across the global youth agenda.

Shape a collective path forward — enabling stakeholders to transform dialogue into commitments, build partnerships, and agree on actionable measures to accelerate progress on youth priorities, their participation in decision-making and global cooperation.

Funding

A limited number of funding opportunities are available for young people.

Eligibility

Young people, organizations, institutions and partners from around the world are invited to join for the UN Youth Townhall;

Applicants should be ideally between 18-35 years of age;

Selection will consider gender balance, geographical representation and youth from underrepresented and marginalized groups. Preference will be given to applicants engaged in a grassroots organization who have had limited or no prior engagement with the UN.

Application

Completing the application will take approximately 30-45 minutes. Submit it by 7 September 2026, midnight ET.

Click here to apply

For more information, visit UN Youth Townhall.

TITLE: YSEALI Academic Fellows Program 2027: Fully Funded Five-Week Exchange Programme in the United States

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative Academic Fellows Program 2027, commonly known as YSEALI AFP, is inviting eligible young leaders from Southeast Asia to apply for a fully funded academic exchange programme in the United States.

Sponsored by the U.S. Department of State, funded by the U.S. Government, and administered by the Maureen and Mike Mansfield Center at the University of Montana, the programme is designed to strengthen leadership skills, encourage cross-cultural understanding, and build lasting connections between the United States and Southeast Asia.

The five-week programme brings undergraduate students and recent graduates to a U.S. college or university for an intensive experience combining academic learning, leadership development, community service, field visits, cultural activities, and professional networking.

The 2027 application cycle covers both the Spring 2027 and Fall 2027 cohorts. Interested applicants must submit their applications before the official deadline.

Overview of the YSEALI Academic Fellows Program

The Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative is a U.S. Government initiative that supports emerging leaders across Southeast Asia. Its Academic Fellows component focuses on young people who demonstrate leadership potential, community involvement, academic interests, and a commitment to strengthening relationships between Southeast Asia and the United States.

The programme does not only focus on classroom learning. It provides participants with opportunities to:

Explore important regional and global issues.

Learn about U.S. society, institutions, culture, and values.

Develop leadership and problem-solving skills.

Engage in community service.

Build relationships with fellow young leaders.

Gain practical exposure through academic field experiences.

Develop ideas that can benefit their communities after returning home.

Establish long-term connections with U.S. participants and YSEALI alumni.

The programme’s broader goal is to foster a network of young leaders who can collaborate across national borders to address shared challenges.

Programme Details

Programme name: Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative Academic Fellows Program

Abbreviation: YSEALI AFP

Programme year: 2027

Duration: Approximately five weeks

Location: United States

Format: In-person academic exchange

Funding: Fully funded by the U.S. Government

Host institutions: U.S. colleges and universities

Application deadline: October 12, 2026, at 20:00 WIB

Spring 2027 expected dates: April 1–May 5, 2027

Fall 2027 expected dates: September 16–October 20, 2027

Official application platform: Submittable

The programme website states that there will be one application cycle for both the Spring and Fall 2027 cohorts. Applicants will not have a separate later opportunity to apply specifically for the Fall 2027 cohort.

What Does the Fully Funded Programme Cover?

Selected YSEALI Academic Fellows participate at no cost to themselves. According to the programme’s official FAQ, the U.S. Department of State covers costs associated with international travel, the visa, and basic living expenses in the United States.

The programme’s funding and support include the following:

1. International Travel Support

Selected Fellows receive support for international travel connected to the programme. Round-trip airfare is arranged for travel to the United States at the beginning of the programme and departure at the end.

Participants should note that the programme does not permit fellows to extend their official travel dates for personal travel, family visits, or other private reasons.

2. Visa Support

Selected participants receive assistance related to the U.S. J-1 exchange visitor visa process. The programme prepares the relevant documentation, including the DS-2019 form, which is used to begin the J-1 visa application process.

The official programme information states that:

Visa fees are covered or waived for selected programme participants.

Applicants must be eligible to receive a U.S. J-1 visa.

Participants must follow the instructions provided by the programme and the relevant U.S. Embassy or Consulate.

Visa approval remains subject to the applicable procedures and requirements.

Applicants do not need to have a valid passport at the time of application. However, selected Fellows must have a passport from an eligible YSEALI country before travelling to the United States.

3. Basic Living Costs

The programme covers basic living expenses in the United States during the official exchange period. This allows selected participants to focus on academic activities, leadership development, community service, and cultural learning without paying programme participation fees.

4. Academic Learning and Leadership Development

Fellows participate in an intensive academic residency at a U.S. university or college. The academic component introduces participants to relevant themes, U.S. institutions, policy approaches, and practical examples connected to their selected area of interest.

5. Community Service Activities

Community service is an important part of the programme. Fellows participate in activities that encourage them to engage with local communities, understand social issues, and explore how civic participation can contribute to positive change.

6. Academic Field Experience

The programme includes academic field experiences that allow participants to connect classroom discussions with real-world institutions, organizations, communities, and initiatives.

These experiences are intended to broaden participants’ understanding of the United States and demonstrate how different sectors address social, economic, environmental, and security-related challenges.

7. Closing Workshop

The five-week programme concludes with a closing workshop. This provides Fellows with an opportunity to reflect on what they have learned, share experiences, discuss future plans, and consider how they can apply their knowledge after returning home.

8. Cross-Cultural Networking

Participants meet other young leaders from Southeast Asia and interact with U.S. citizens through the programme’s activities and reciprocal exchange component. These relationships can become valuable sources of collaboration, professional support, and cross-border learning.

YSEALI Academic Fellowship Themes

Applicants can express interest in one or more of the programme’s four major themes. The official programme website identifies the following areas:

1. Liberty and Freedom

The Liberty and Freedom theme examines ideas connected to freedom of speech, liberty, self-governance, civic engagement, public advocacy, and individual rights.

Participants may explore:

Freedom of speech and expression.

Civic participation.

Public advocacy campaigns.

Self-governance.

The relationship between individual rights and social development.

How citizens and groups have influenced U.S. history, government, and society.

The role of open debate in innovation and public life.

The theme also considers how liberty and civic freedoms relate to economic stability and societal development.

2. Natural Resources

The Natural Resources theme explores the management, protection, and sustainable use of natural resources. It examines how agriculture, fisheries, energy, minerals, water, and other resources affect economic development and community well-being.

Possible topics include:

Agriculture and sustainable farming.

Fisheries management.

Energy security.

Critical minerals.

Supply chain resilience.

Natural disaster preparedness.

Mining and rare earth minerals.

Water and waste management.

Environmental sustainability.

The relationship between natural resources and economic prosperity.

This theme may be particularly relevant to applicants interested in environmental policy, climate resilience, agriculture, natural resource governance, sustainability, or community development.

3. Economic Prosperity

The Economic Prosperity theme focuses on the systems, institutions, and practices that contribute to economic growth and opportunity.

Topics may include:

Business models.

Entrepreneurship.

Technological innovation.

Labour market practices.

Monetary policy.

Financial literacy.

Investment and fundraising.

Organizational development.

Strategic business planning.

Corporate governance.

Supply chain management.

Strategic trade policies.

Technology and artificial intelligence frameworks.

Regulation and economic development.

Applicants with interests in entrepreneurship, business, economics, finance, innovation, employment, technology, or inclusive economic growth may find this theme relevant.

4. Peace and Security

The Peace and Security theme explores policies, institutions, and practices related to local, regional, and international peace and security.

Potential topics include:

Peacebuilding and conflict prevention.

Public policy and peacemaking.

Disaster preparedness and response.

Cybersecurity.

Public health security.

Human trafficking.

Drug trafficking.

Transnational crime.

Online scams.

Border security.

Regional and international cooperation.

The theme may appeal to students and young professionals interested in peacebuilding, international relations, public policy, security studies, governance, disaster management, public health, or human rights.

Applicants who are interested in more than one theme may be asked to rank their preferences in the application. However, selected Fellows will be assigned to a theme, and applicants cannot request a specific U.S. institute.

Who Can Apply for the YSEALI Academic Fellows Program?

The programme has specific eligibility requirements. Applicants should carefully review each condition before beginning their application.

Age Requirement

Applicants must generally be between 18 and 25 years old by October 12, 2026, which is the application deadline.

The programme notes that exceptional applicants over the age of 25 may be considered if they meet all other eligibility requirements. Applicants who are younger than 18 by the application deadline are not eligible, even if they will turn 18 before the programme begins.

Citizenship Requirement

Applicants must be citizens of one of the following eligible countries:

Brunei

Cambodia

Indonesia

Malaysia

Philippines

Singapore

Thailand

Timor-Leste

Vietnam

For the 2027 U.S.-based Academic Fellows Program, citizens of Myanmar and Laos are not eligible because of current visa restrictions. This restriction is based on citizenship and does not change based on the applicant’s country of residence.

Residency Requirement

Applicants must also be physically residing in an ASEAN member state as of October 12, 2026, and must remain resident in an ASEAN member state through the start of their selected fellowship.

Being a citizen of an eligible country is therefore not sufficient by itself. Applicants must meet both the citizenship and residency requirements.

Academic Requirement

Applicants must meet one of the following academic conditions:

Be enrolled as a full-time undergraduate student.

Be enrolled as a part-time undergraduate student.

Be enrolled as a graduate student.

Have graduated with an undergraduate degree within the last four years.

The programme is intended for young people who are at the beginning stages of their academic, professional, or leadership careers.

English-Language Requirement

The fellowship is conducted entirely in English. Applicants must be proficient in:

Reading English.

Writing English.

Speaking English.

Applications must also be submitted in English. Applications submitted in another language will not be evaluated.

Applicants who are deaf should be proficient in American Sign Language, according to the programme’s FAQ.

U.S. Citizenship and Residency Restriction

Applicants must not be:

U.S. citizens.

U.S. permanent residents.

Green card holders.

This restriction also applies to dual citizens who hold U.S. citizenship or permanent residency.

Previous YSEALI Participation

Applicants must not be alumni of the YSEALI Academic Fellows Program. Previous participation in the Academic Fellows programme makes an applicant ineligible for this particular opportunity.

U.S. Government Employment Restriction

Applicants must not be employees of the U.S. Government or immediate family members of U.S. Government employees.

J-1 Visa Eligibility

Applicants must be eligible to receive a U.S. J-1 visa. Selected participants will be guided through the relevant visa documentation and application process.

Desired Qualifications

Meeting the technical eligibility requirements does not automatically guarantee selection. The programme also identifies qualities and experiences that can strengthen an application.

Strong applicants are expected to demonstrate some combination of the following:

1. Interest in a Fellowship Theme

Applicants should demonstrate interest, knowledge, or relevant experience connected to one or more of the four fellowship themes:

Liberty and Freedom.

Natural Resources.

Economic Prosperity.

Peace and Security.

This interest may be demonstrated through academic work, professional experience, volunteering, community service, student leadership, research, advocacy, entrepreneurship, or other relevant activities.

2. Leadership Potential

Applicants should demonstrate leadership qualities and the potential to contribute positively to their university, workplace, organization, or community.

Leadership does not necessarily mean holding a formal title. It may include:

Organizing a community initiative.

Leading a student association.

Coordinating volunteers.

Supporting a social enterprise.

Conducting community research.

Advocating for a public issue.

Developing a local solution to a shared challenge.

Mentoring other young people.

Participating in civic or development activities.

3. Interest in the United States and Southeast Asia

Applicants should express a genuine interest in learning about the United States and building relationships between the United States and Southeast Asia.

The programme seeks participants who are open to cross-cultural learning and willing to engage respectfully with people from different backgrounds.

4. Commitment to Full Participation

The YSEALI Academic Fellows Program is intensive. Selected Fellows must be prepared to participate fully in:

Academic sessions.

Community service.

Field experiences.

Workshops.

Cultural activities.

Site visits.

Networking activities.

Other scheduled programme components.

The official FAQ states that Fellows cannot take time off for personal travel, schoolwork, employment, or other private matters during the programme. Full participation is required.

5. Commitment to Return Home

Applicants should demonstrate a commitment to returning to their home country after the programme and applying the leadership skills, knowledge, and relationships gained through the fellowship.

Applicants should be able to explain how the experience may benefit:

Their local community.

Their country.

Southeast Asia.

Their professional or academic field.

Cross-border cooperation.

Relationships between Southeast Asia and the United States.

6. Limited Prior U.S. Experience

The programme particularly encourages applicants who have little or no prior study or travel experience in the United States.

This does not mean that every applicant with previous U.S. experience is automatically disqualified. However, applicants with limited prior exposure to the United States may align more closely with this desired qualification.

Programme Structure and Participant Experience

The YSEALI Academic Fellows Program combines several components rather than relying exclusively on academic lectures.

A typical fellowship experience includes:

Academic residency: Fellows study their selected theme at a U.S. host institution.

Community service: Participants engage in activities that connect academic learning with community needs.

Academic field experience: Fellows visit or interact with institutions and organizations relevant to the programme theme.

Cultural learning: Participants gain a deeper understanding of U.S. society, culture, history, and institutions.

Leadership development: Fellows strengthen communication, collaboration, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

Closing workshop: Participants reflect on their learning and consider future applications.

Reciprocal exchange component: The programme includes a component through which Americans travel to Southeast Asia, supporting continued cross-cultural engagement.

The programme is designed to encourage relationships that continue beyond the five-week exchange.

Important Information About Travel and Participation

Applicants should understand that the fellowship is a structured exchange programme rather than a general tourism or personal travel opportunity.

Selected Fellows are expected to:

Attend all required activities.

Participate fully in academic and cultural sessions.

Follow programme rules and travel arrangements.

Travel on the dates arranged by the programme.

Remain engaged throughout the official fellowship period.

Return home at the end of the programme.

The programme does not permit participants to bring family members to the United States as part of the fellowship. Personal travel extensions are also not permitted under the programme’s stated rules.

Learn More HERE.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027 YSEALI Academic Fellows Program is:

October 12, 2026, at 20:00 WIB

Applicants should confirm the equivalent deadline in their local time zone and avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their application.

The programme does not offer extensions after the deadline. Applicants should also note that submissions are final and cannot be edited after they have been submitted.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should follow these steps:

Step 1: Review the Eligibility Requirements

Confirm that you meet the programme’s age, citizenship, residency, academic, English-language, and visa requirements.

Step 2: Review the Fellowship Themes

Read about the four available themes and identify the areas that best match your academic interests, leadership experience, professional goals, or community work.

Step 3: Prepare Your Application Information

Prepare clear information about:

Your academic background.

Your community or leadership experience.

Your professional interests.

Your interest in the selected fellowship themes.

Your interest in the United States and Southeast Asia.

Your plans after completing the programme.

How you intend to apply the fellowship experience in your community.

Step 4: Submit the Online Application

Applications must be submitted through the official Submittable application platform. The programme states that only applications submitted through the official online platform will be considered. A downloadable application form may be available for reference, but it is not a substitute for the online submission.

Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline

Complete and review the application carefully before submitting it by October 12, 2026, at 20:00 WIB.

Get the Application Information HERE and Apply HERE.

Application Tips

Applicants can improve the clarity and strength of their applications by following these recommendations:

Connect Your Experience to a Theme

Do not simply state that you are interested in a theme. Explain how your studies, work, volunteering, research, or community involvement connect to it.

For example, an applicant interested in Natural Resources could discuss experience in climate action, environmental education, sustainable agriculture, water management, or community conservation.

Demonstrate Leadership with Evidence

Use specific examples of what you have done. Explain:

The challenge you identified.

The action you took.

The people or groups you worked with.

The outcome of your efforts.

What you learned from the experience.

Explain Your Community Impact

The programme values applicants who intend to apply their learning after returning home. Describe a realistic way you could use the knowledge, networks, or skills gained during the fellowship.

Show Cross-Cultural Openness

Explain how you would contribute to and learn from a diverse group of participants. Avoid presenting the exchange only as an opportunity for personal travel or career advancement.

Review Eligibility Carefully

Pay close attention to the citizenship and residency requirements. Applicants must be both citizens of an eligible country and residents of an ASEAN member state under the programme’s definition.

Proofread Before Submission

Applications must be submitted in English, and submissions are final. Check your responses for clarity, accuracy, grammar, and completeness before submitting.

Official Application and Programme Links

Official programme website: YSEALI Academic Fellows Program

Application information and online application: Apply for YSEALI Academic Fellows Program

Fellowship themes: YSEALI Institute Themes

Frequently asked questions: YSEALI AFP FAQ

Programme contact: ysealiafp@umontana.edu

Conclusion

The YSEALI Academic Fellows Program 2027 offers eligible young leaders from Southeast Asia an opportunity to participate in a fully funded, five-week academic and cultural exchange in the United States. Through academic study, community service, field experiences, leadership development, and cross-cultural networking, the programme seeks to prepare participants to contribute to their communities and strengthen relationships across Southeast Asia and the United States.

Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements, identify the fellowship theme that best matches their experience, prepare thoughtful responses, and submit their applications before the October 12, 2026, at 20:00 WIB deadline.

Because the programme covers both Spring and Fall 2027 cohorts in one application cycle, eligible applicants should not wait for a later Fall 2027 call before applying.

Discover more global Fellowship and Asian opportunities on Opportunities for Youth (OFY).

TITLE: Funding

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
A budget of €10.2M (2022)

Support from the French Public Authorities

The French Ministry in charge of research has supported IHES since 1964. Today, the Ministry for Higher Education and Research awards the Institute an annual grant, representing about a third of its budget.

As part of the Choose France for Science program, Zhongkai Tao, Assistant Professor of Mathematics, receives funding from the French government, administered by the National Research Agency (ANR) under the France 2030 initiative, reference “ANRS-25-CFFS-0012”.

Four permanent researchers are affected to the French National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS), which pays for their salaries and funds a number of scientific events every year. Other institutional partners, such as Paris-Saclay University, the Jacques Hadamard Mathematical Foundation (FMJH), the CARMIN project and the French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Comission contribute to funding part of the Institute’s scientific activity.

Funding from the European Research Council (ERC)

Current projects funded by the European Research Council are:

– FourIntExP (Fourier interpolation and universal optimality of the A2 lattice): led by Principal Investigator Danylo Radchenko, this project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation program, under grant agreement #101078782.

– GravitaS (The gravitational S-matrix: from theory to experiment): led by Principal Investigator Julio Parra Martinez, this project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation program, under grant agreement #101221094.

An international network

This network was created in the 1970s, when the Institute started to broaden its funding sources by looking abroad:

The Swiss Academy of Sciences (since 1973)

Max-Planck Gesellschaft, Germany (since 1975)

The Belgian Science Policy Office (since 1976)

Gifts and donations

In the late 1990s, under Jean-Pierre Bourguignon’s directorship, IHES set up a department dedicated to fundraising and an endowment fund. Gifts, donations, and asset revenues from the endowment fund now make up for around 34% of its operations.

Make a gift

Funding from the Simons Foundation

The Simons Foundation is the institute’s most important donor. For twenty years, from the beginning of the fundraising activities undertaken by IHES in the 2000s, and until 2025, the Simons Foundation gave more than €25m to IHES.

In 2021, James and Marilyn Simons, the co-founders of the Simons Foundation, pledged another 25m€ to support IHES over ten years: this is a record gift both for the Institute and for fundamental research in France.

Depending on the Institute’s needs, these funds will be used to finance doctoral and post-doctoral fellowships, as well as one or more prestigious position(s) for a talented young scientist with an outstanding track record, as well as allow leading researchers to spend long sabbaticals at the Institute.

This grant will also allow IHES to continue to develop initiatives to promote diversity and inclusion in mathematics and theoretical physics, by raising awareness of these issues within the scientific and mathematical communities as well as at the Institute itself. It will also contribute to the financing of projects that promote the dissemination of science and knowledge to the general public.

A significant portion of the donation, given more specifically by the Simons Foundation International, will also strengthen the Institute’s endowment to ensure its financial independence and stability over the long-term.

The Simons Foundation also funds specific projects, the Simons Collaborations, carried out by some of its permanent professors:

Simons Collaboration on the Nonperturbative Bootstrap, led at IHES by Slava Rychkov;

Simons Collaboration on Perfection in Algebra, Geometry, and Topology whose principal investigator at IHES is Dustin Clausen;

Programme Overview

The rapid growth of Universities in Africa has come along with complex procurement and contract management requirements. Effective and efficient procurement and contract management is at the heart of institutional continuous growth and development. Consequently, it is important that University staff involved in Procurement and Contract Management have the requisite skills the tasks demand. Universities which have engaged skilled procurement and contract management professionals to manage their growth, all need to ensure the skills of such professionals are constantly sharpened in line with current developments in that field. This training, being organised by the Association of African Universities will ensure, contract and procurement staff are consistent with the standards to manage the vital activities of the university.

Contract and Procurement administrators

Team leaders and members in procurement environment

Contract Managers

Project team members

Administrators of purchasing and procurement activities

Expected Outcomes

On completion of the course, you will be able to:

Establish procurement needs of the university or project;

Procure goods and services through developing requests, receiving and selecting offers and administering contracts;

Understand the values and principles of the university and value diversity;

Develop and monitor service to clients through developing, implementing and reviewing client service strategies;

Gather and effectively analyse information from a range of sources;

Apply the required processes, support the implementation of policy and encourage compliance with legislation;

Effectively use a range of advanced workplace communication strategies;

Identify and treat risks; and

Procurement lifecycle

Supplier selection criteria

TITLE: Workshop on Research Leadership, Transparency, Communication, Partnerships and Collaboration

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Cairo, Egypt –July 15 -18, 2019

The Association of African Universities (AAU) in collaboration with the Al-Azhar University, Egypt, is inviting stakeholders to its 4th Workshop on Research Leadership, Transparency, Communication, Partnerships and Collaboration from July 15 -18, 2019.

Research is fundamental for Africa because it is an important source of new knowledge and provides solutions to pressing challenges. There is a need to strengthen Research Leadership so that more resources can be channeled to strengthen research and support African researchers to conduct relevant research.

Universities in Africa continue to be challenged to focus on relevant, transparent and demand driven research. If universities are going to do this effectively they must have the capacities to engage communities, follow research ethical norms, work with industry and manage multi-stakeholder relationships. This has an impact on how universities work and how they position themselves to respond to pressing societal problems.

Significant financial and human resources are also spent conducting research. However, because of ineffective communication of research findings by researchers – the intended beneficiaries of the research don’t always get to know about it. It is crucial that researchers develop skills to effectively communicate research findings for impact and uptake by its most needed stakeholders. There is a plethora of emerging research communication tools that researchers could employ.

Also, Scholarly publication in a peer-reviewed journal is central to the research communication and dissemination process. However, the process of publishing in peer-reviewed journals remains a daunting task for researchers and academics in Africa (Tarkang & Bain, 2019). This is partly due to the fact that the skills, ethics and norms that govern academic research in Africa do not reflect the transparency, openness and reproducibility culture required by these journals. To meet this rising demand of research transparency, it is essential for researchers to appreciate the concept of research transparency, reproducibility, and openness as well as raise their awareness on common academic and policy research misconducts allowing them to produce reliable, trustable and publishable research outputs.

Further, Strategic Partnerships and Collaboration are key for universities in the 21st century and beyond. In this regard, African Universities need to learn how to nurture, identify and strengthen mutually beneficial partnerships. They need to understand how they can position themselves / brand themselves to attract beneficial collaborations. No university can exist as an island and be able to succeed in its objectives. Therefore, building capacities for key staff in universities to advance strong partnerships and collaborations is equally fundamental to the success of African universities.

The workshop will focus on:

1. Developing the Research Leadership Skills of Researchers

2. Building capacities for Demand Driven Research Approaches

3. Discussing strategies for disseminating Research findings and Enhancing Researchers’ Online

Visibility

4. Sensitizing participants on various academic research misconducts (ethical issues) as well as the

lack of sharing and openness in research.

5. Exposing participants to best practices for research Transparency, Reproducibility and

Openness.

6. Developing capacities for strategic Partnerships and Collaboration

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

1. This workshop targets the following participants from universities in Africa and from the Africa

Centres of Excellence:

2. Research Directors from higher education institutions

3. All researchers in higher education institutions (both public and private)

4. Academic Staff – Deans, professors, lecturers

5. Vice-Chancellors

5. Research consultants

6. Researchers from National Research Councils and Science Granting Councils

7. Directors of Departments from the Ministries of Higher Education, Science, Technology, etc

STYLE OF WORKSHOP DELIVERY

The objectives of the workshop will be achieved through lead lectures, skills practice activities, guided feedback, and intensive participant interaction over carefully selected cases and other materials in a process facilitated by experienced Resource Persons.

DATE AND VENUE:

July 15 -18, 2019

Al-Azhar University, Cairo, Egypt

WORKSHOP FEES

This is a fee-based workshop – we will charge US$400 for AAU member institutions and US$500 for Non-AAU member institutions. The registration fees cover the facilitators’ costs, workshop materials and conference package including certificates, tea/coffee and lunch for the four days of the workshop.

Participants are responsible for other costs such as flight, accommodation and upkeep

CERTIFICATION

All participants who undergo the training course will be awarded certificates of participation by the AAU at the end of the workshop.

TITLE: Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship 2027–28: Fully Funded PhD Scholarship with £27,036 Annual Stipend

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Imperial College London is inviting applications from outstanding undergraduate and Master’s students for the President’s PhD Scholarships 2027–28. This prestigious scholarship provides exceptional candidates with the opportunity to undertake a fully funded doctoral research programme at one of the world’s leading research institutions.

The Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship offers comprehensive financial support for up to 3.5 years of PhD study, including full tuition-fee funding, an annual living-cost stipend of £27,036, an annual consumables allowance and access to specialist professional development opportunities.

The scholarship is open to talented applicants from the United Kingdom and around the world, with no restrictions on nationality. Applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and promising research potential.

About the Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship

The President’s PhD Scholarship is designed to attract and support exceptional doctoral researchers who have the academic ability, intellectual curiosity and research potential to make a meaningful contribution to their chosen fields.

The scholarship allows successful candidates to undertake a research project of their choosing under the supervision of an excellent academic supervisor at Imperial College London.

In addition to financial support, scholars become part of a wider community of President’s PhD Scholars and gain access to cohort-building activities, professional development programmes and research-related opportunities.

The scholarship is particularly suitable for applicants who want to pursue advanced research in areas such as:

Engineering

Medicine

Natural sciences

Computing

Climate and environmental research

Materials science

Biotechnology

Data science

Public health

Energy

Artificial intelligence

Mathematics

Physics

Chemistry

Other doctoral research disciplines offered by Imperial College London

Applicants must check the availability of their intended PhD programme and confirm whether their proposed department can support their application.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The President’s PhD Scholarship provides extensive financial support for the duration of the funded study period.

Each scholarship provides support for 3.5 years of doctoral study, subject to the applicable scholarship conditions.

1. Full Tuition-Fee Funding

Successful scholars receive full funding for their PhD tuition fees.

This means that the scholarship is designed to remove the financial burden of tuition fees during the funded period of study.

The scholarship is therefore particularly valuable for international applicants who may otherwise face substantial doctoral tuition costs.

2. Annual Living-Cost Stipend

Scholars receive an annual stipend of:

£27,036 per year

This is the stated 2027–28 stipend rate and is intended to assist with living expenses during the PhD programme.

The stipend may help scholars meet costs such as:

Accommodation

Food

Local transportation

Personal expenses

Study-related living costs

Other day-to-day expenses

The stipend is not described as a salary. It is financial support intended to help doctoral researchers manage their living costs while undertaking their studies.

3. Annual Consumables Fund

Scholars receive a consumables fund of:

£2,000 per year for the first three years of study

This funding is intended to support research-related consumables and expenses associated with the candidate’s doctoral work.

Depending on the research discipline, consumables may include materials, laboratory supplies, research resources or other approved items required for the research project.

Applicants should consult their department for details about how the consumables fund can be used within their specific research area.

4. Professional Development and Research Opportunities

President’s PhD Scholars receive access to a programme of bespoke opportunities and events delivered by the Early Career Researcher Institute, also known as the ECRI.

These opportunities are designed to support the broader development of doctoral researchers beyond their immediate research projects.

They may help scholars strengthen areas such as:

Research communication

Academic presentation

Professional development

Career planning

Leadership

Research impact

Collaboration

Transferable skills

Academic and non-academic career preparation

5. Access to Wider Postgraduate Support

Scholars can also access the broader range of postgraduate support available at Imperial College London.

This includes support services for:

International students

Students with disabilities

Academic development

Personal wellbeing

Researcher development

Student life

Career development

The scholarship therefore combines financial support with academic, professional and personal development resources.

Duration of the Scholarship

The President’s PhD Scholarship provides funding for:

3.5 years of PhD study

For the 2027–28 academic year, funded places have the following permitted start-date range:

Earliest start date: 1 August 2027

Latest start date: 1 November 2027

Applicants should ensure that their proposed PhD programme and department can accommodate a start date within this period.

Who Can Apply?

The scholarship is open to high-performing applicants from:

Imperial College London

The United Kingdom

Other countries worldwide

The scheme has no nationality restrictions. Applications are welcomed from international candidates, although applicants should be aware that some departments may be unable to support international students.

The scholarship is available for both:

Full-time PhD study

Part-time PhD study

The scheme is intended for new PhD applicants. Current registered Imperial College London PhD students are not eligible to be considered for a President’s PhD Scholarship.

Academic Eligibility Requirements

The scholarship is highly competitive and has higher-than-usual eligibility requirements.

Applicants must generally demonstrate outstanding academic achievement through one of the following routes.

Route 1: First-Class Undergraduate or Integrated Master’s Degree

Applicants may qualify if they hold, or expect to receive:

A first-class undergraduate degree or equivalent; or

A first-class integrated Master’s degree or equivalent.

Candidates who have only completed a single undergraduate degree or an integrated Master’s degree must generally meet the first-class or equivalent requirement.

Route 2: Distinction in a Standalone Master’s Degree

Applicants may also qualify if they hold, or expect to receive, a distinction in a standalone Master’s qualification.

This route allows applicants who may not have achieved a first-class undergraduate degree to demonstrate academic excellence through outstanding Master’s-level performance.

Candidates who have demonstrated exceptional performance at Master’s level may therefore be considered even if their undergraduate results do not meet the first-class requirement.

Applicants Awaiting Final Results

Applicants who have not yet received their final qualifications may still be considered if they can provide evidence that they are likely to achieve the required academic standard.

Any offer of a PhD place may be conditional upon the applicant obtaining the predicted qualifications.

International applicants should contact the relevant Imperial College London Admissions team to confirm how their qualifications compare with the scholarship’s academic requirements.

Departmental Special Cases

Imperial College London may consider applicants who do not meet the advertised academic criteria in special circumstances.

A department may nominate a candidate as a special case where there are extenuating circumstances explaining why the applicant did not obtain the required grades but where the candidate otherwise demonstrates the calibre expected for the scholarship.

Examples of evidence that may support a special-case application include:

Exceptional marks in research project modules

Strong performance during research placements

Outstanding research experience

Evidence of significant research ability

Other circumstances that affected academic performance

Applicants who believe they may qualify under this provision should contact their proposed department directly before applying.

Alternate Academic and Career Pathways

Imperial College London also encourages applications from candidates with non-traditional academic or career pathways.

Applicants who have not followed a conventional educational or professional route may still be considered if they demonstrate strong research potential.

This may include candidates who have:

Taken a career break

Changed academic disciplines

Entered higher education through an alternative route

Developed significant professional or research experience outside a traditional academic pathway

Experienced circumstances that affected their academic progression

The key consideration is whether the applicant can demonstrate the ability and potential to undertake high-quality doctoral research.

Other Eligibility Conditions

In addition to the academic requirements, applicants must meet the following conditions:

The application must be for a new PhD programme.

Applicants must have contacted an academic supervisor at Imperial College London.

The proposed supervisor must have agreed to supervise the applicant’s research project.

Applicants must meet the admission requirements of their chosen department.

Applicants must select the President’s PhD Scholarship option in the funding section of the online application.

Applicants must submit all required supporting documents.

Applicants must provide appropriate academic references.

Applicants must meet any additional requirements set by their chosen department.

Although there are no nationality restrictions, some academic departments may be unable to support international candidates.

Requirement to Secure an Imperial Supervisor

Before applying, candidates must make contact with a potential supervisor in an academic department at Imperial College London.

The supervisor must agree to supervise the proposed research project.

This is an important requirement because the scholarship is connected to a specific PhD research application and departmental review process.

Applicants should therefore:

Identify a department that offers a PhD related to their research interests.

Review the department’s research areas and academic staff.

Identify a potential supervisor whose research aligns with their proposed project.

Contact the prospective supervisor professionally.

Share a clear summary of their research interests and proposed project.

Confirm whether the supervisor is available and willing to supervise the research.

Imperial College London also states that supervisors are limited to supervising one President’s PhD Scholar at any given time. Applicants should therefore review the university’s information about unavailable supervisors before finalizing their application.

How to Apply for the President’s PhD Scholarship

There is no separate scholarship application form for the President’s PhD Scholarship.

Instead, applicants must apply for admission to a PhD programme at Imperial College London through the university’s online admissions system.

The department will then put eligible candidates forward for scholarship consideration based on academic merit and research potential.

Before you apply, please review the President’s PhD Scholarships – Unavailable Supervisors page for more information.

Step 1: Identify a Suitable PhD Programme

Applicants should first identify a doctoral programme and department that align with their academic background and research interests.

The selected department must offer a suitable PhD research opportunity and be able to consider the applicant for admission.

Step 2: Contact a Potential Supervisor

Applicants must contact a potential academic supervisor at Imperial College London who has agreed to supervise their proposed research.

This should be done before submitting the PhD application.

Step 3: Prepare the Required Documents

Applicants should prepare the necessary documents for the PhD admission application.

These may include:

Academic transcripts

Degree certificates, where available

Personal statement

Research proposal

Academic references

Evidence of English-language proficiency, where required

Curriculum vitae, where required

Other documents requested by the department

Applicants should carefully review the specific requirements of their chosen department because additional documents may be required.

Step 4: Submit the PhD Admission Application

Applicants must submit their application for admission through Imperial College London’s online postgraduate admissions system.

The scholarship is considered through the PhD admission application rather than through a separate scholarship form.

Step 5: Select the Scholarship Option

Within the online application form, applicants must select the President’s PhD Scholarship option in the funding section under the additional questions tab.

Failing to select the relevant funding option may prevent the application from being considered for the scholarship scheme.

Additional Application Instructions for 2027–28

Imperial College London provides specific instructions for applicants seeking consideration for the 2027–28 President’s PhD Scholarship.

Personal Statement and Research Proposal

Under the supporting documents section, applicants should submit a two-page document structured as follows:

First Page: Personal Statement

The first page should explain:

Why the applicant wants to study at Imperial College London

Why the applicant is applying for the President’s PhD Scholarship

The applicant’s academic and professional motivations

Relevant achievements

Supporting information not included elsewhere in the application

Any additional information that strengthens the application

Applicants are encouraged to write in the first person.

Second Page: Research Proposal

The second page should present the applicant’s research proposal.

The proposal should clearly communicate the intended research direction and demonstrate the applicant’s research potential.

A strong research proposal should generally explain:

The research topic

The central research problem

The research question or questions

The proposed objectives

The significance of the research

The proposed methodology or approach

The potential contribution of the research

Why the research is suitable for the chosen department

How the project aligns with the proposed supervisor’s expertise

Applicants may submit an updated version of the statement if required after submission, particularly if their department shortlists them for scholarship consideration.

Detailed Research Proposal

The research proposal section within the application may be used to provide a more detailed document if the applicant’s department requires one.

Candidates should check the specific research proposal requirements of their department before preparing the final version.

Academic Referees

Applicants will be asked to provide the names of two academic referees.

These should be individuals who can provide an academic reference in support of the application.

Suitable referees may include:

A personal tutor

A thesis supervisor

A lecturer familiar with the applicant’s academic work

A research project supervisor

Another academic who can assess the applicant’s research ability

Applicants should not list their proposed PhD supervisor as one of the two academic referees.

Selection Process

The President’s PhD Scholarship selection process involves multiple stages.

A total of:

50 scholarship places

are available.

Stage 1: Departmental Review

Candidates who meet, or are predicted to meet, the eligibility criteria will first be reviewed by the department to which they have applied.

Departments will assess applicants and select a shortlist of candidates to be presented to the College Selection Panel.

Stage 2: Faculty and College-Level Review

Shortlisted candidates will be reviewed through the university’s wider selection process.

A faculty allocation stage may score and rank candidates from departmental shortlists and make initial offers to the most promising applicants.

Faculty Vice-Deans for Research may present candidates and provide justifications for offers to the College Selection Panel.

The College Selection Panel may also make additional offers through a strategic allocation for candidates applying through alternate academic or career pathways.

Final Decision

The final scholarship decision is made by the College Selection Panel.

The panel includes senior university representatives, including:

The Vice-Provost for Research

The Director of the Graduate School

Faculty Vice-Deans for Research

Successful candidates will receive written confirmation of the scholarship.

Any PhD offer may be conditional upon the applicant achieving the predicted qualifications stated in the application.

Applicants who are not selected for the President’s PhD Scholarship will automatically be considered for a standard PhD place.

How Applicants Are Assessed

Candidates are assessed based on academic excellence and research potential.

Academic Excellence

Academic excellence may be assessed through:

Previous academic results

University transcripts

Relative class position

Academic awards

Distinctions

Other evidence of exceptional academic performance

Applicants should ensure that their academic records clearly demonstrate their ability to succeed in a demanding doctoral research environment.

Research Potential

Research potential may be assessed through:

Previous research experience

The applicant’s interest in discovery

The proposed research plan

The potential contribution of the proposed research

The quality and clarity of the research proposal

The departmental statement

Performance during an interview, where applicable

Applicants should demonstrate not only that they have performed well academically but also that they have the intellectual curiosity, independence and research ability required for PhD-level study.

Visit HERE for more information about the Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship.

Applicants should pay close attention to the relevant deadline and notification date.

The university also encourages applications from people from all backgrounds, recognizing the importance of diversity and representation in higher education and research.

However, prospective international applicants should note that some departments may not be able to support international candidates. Applicants should confirm departmental support and admission requirements before applying.

Is There a Race or Ethnicity Requirement?

There is no stated race or ethnicity restriction for the President’s PhD Scholarship.

Imperial College London encourages applications from people from all backgrounds.

Full-Time and Part-Time Study Options

The scholarship applies to both:

Full-time PhD study

Part-time PhD study

Applicants should check whether their intended department and research programme permit part-time study and whether the proposed research can be completed within the scholarship’s funding conditions.

Why This Scholarship Is a Strong Opportunity

The Imperial College London President’s PhD Scholarship is particularly attractive because it combines full tuition support with a substantial annual stipend and additional research-development resources.

For successful candidates, the scholarship can provide:

Access to a globally recognized research institution

Full tuition-fee funding

A £27,036 annual stipend at the 2027–28 rate

A 3.5-year funding period

Access to professional development opportunities

Support from an academic supervisor

Membership in a community of President’s PhD Scholars

Opportunities to develop research networks and transferable skills

The scholarship may be especially valuable for students who have strong academic records but require financial support to pursue doctoral research at an international institution.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

Because the scholarship is highly competitive, applicants should prepare their applications carefully.

1. Start Early

Applicants should begin the process well before the deadline.

Contacting a potential supervisor, preparing a research proposal and obtaining references can take considerable time.

2. Identify the Right Department

Applicants should select a department that closely matches their research interests and academic background.

A strong departmental fit can help demonstrate that the proposed research is realistic and appropriately supported.

3. Find a Suitable Supervisor

The proposed supervisor should have research expertise relevant to the applicant’s proposed project.

Applicants should review the supervisor’s research interests, publications, current projects and research group before making contact.

4. Develop a Focused Research Proposal

The research proposal should be clear, specific and academically compelling.

Applicants should avoid overly broad topics and should explain the problem, research questions, methodology and expected contribution in a structured manner.

Applicants should give referees sufficient time to prepare detailed and relevant references.

8. Confirm International Eligibility

Although the scholarship has no nationality restrictions, international applicants should confirm that their qualifications meet Imperial’s requirements and that their proposed department can support international candidates.

Frequently Asked Questions

Yes. The scholarship provides full tuition-fee funding, an annual stipend, a consumables fund and access to professional development opportunities for up to 3.5 years.

How much is the annual stipend?

The stated stipend for 2027–28 is £27,036 per year.

How many scholarships are available?

There are 50 scholarship places available.

Can international students apply?

Yes. Applicants from around the world can apply, and there are no nationality restrictions. However, some departments may be unable to support international candidates.

Can current Imperial PhD students apply?

No. The scheme is open only to new PhD applications. Current registered Imperial PhD students are not eligible.

Is there a separate scholarship application form?

No. Applicants must apply for admission to a PhD programme through Imperial College London’s online admissions system and select the President’s PhD Scholarship option in the funding section.

Do applicants need a supervisor before applying?

Yes. Applicants must have contacted a potential Imperial academic supervisor who has agreed to supervise their proposed research project.

Can part-time PhD students apply?

Yes. The scholarship applies to both full-time and part-time study.

What is the first application deadline?

The first deadline is 2 November 2026 at 23:59 UK time.

Are there later application rounds?

Yes. Additional deadlines are:

11 January 2027 at 23:59 UK time

1 March 2027 at 23:59 UK time
