TITLE: Data Ethics & Protection Webinar Series

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Association of African Universities (AAU), the University of Nottingham (UoN) and the Ethical Data Initiative (EDI) are joining forces to campaign for the inclusion of Data Ethics in Data Science education on a global scale.

The campaign will begin with a series of informative shows to be aired on AAU TV. The AAU TV network was established in 2018 to deliver news and information on important higher education-related issues on the African Continent such as advancements in education policy, STEM innovation and important research findings. The Ethical Data discussions will explore pressing ethical questions inherent in digital technology, data collection and data-driven research; highlighting the need for training digital practitioners in the ethics of their craft.

Webinar Series 1: Data Ethics Issues in Higher Education

Date & Time: May 23, 2023 at 09:00 GMT (10:00 in London)

Description

We are living in a digitally transformed society. Data drives problem-solving and better decision-making. While the digital revolution has transformed the way we live, solving many issues; it has also given rise to numerous questions and challenges which affect everyone. What governance policies and frameworks are needed to make sure digital technologies and opportunities are available for everyone and there are no monopolies created? How do we make sure there are proper governance mechanisms in place to embed values in all data ecosystems?

This webinar will look into key research questions on:

Who owns the data? Who benefits from my data?

With data capitalism becoming an increasingly recognised concept, how do we avoid the pitfalls of feudalism and colonialism in this new landscape?

With the increase in data intensive research, and focus on data law and ethics in general, do you think it is time that data ethics should become an integral part of the education curriculum in schools and universities? Why?

How can we build capacity for Data Ethics in universities and industry?

Registration Link: https://rb.gy/3yq7o

Speakers/ Discussants:

William G. Cantah, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Data Science and Economic Policy, and the Coordinator of the Centre for Data Archiving, Management, Analysis and Advocacy (CDAMAA) at the Department of Data Science & Economic Policy, School of Economics, University of Cape Coast.

Edward Ombui, the Dean, School of Science & Technology at the Africa Nazarene University, Kenya

Samba NDIAYE, Dept. of Mathematics and Computer Science, Faculty of Science and Technologies, Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar, Senegal

Special Remarks will be given by:

Olusola Bandele Oyewole, Secretary-General of the Association of African Universities (AAU) and

Juliet Thondlana, UNESCO Chair in International Education and Development; Professor of International Education and Development at Nottingham University; and Coordinator of the AAU Office in the UK

The webinar will be moderated by Amanda Chukwudozie [Programme and Project Manager (Policy), Nottingham University].

Dissemination

The Data Ethics webinar series will be streamed live on AAU TV (which transmits via satellite to 22 countries in West and North Africa and 8 countries in southern Europe), AAU YouTube channel and via Zoom.

For further information, please contact Ransford Bekoe on ransford@aau.org and aautv@aau.org

TITLE: Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship 2026: $45,000 Stipend for Doctoral Candidates to Conduct Research at the Smithsonian

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship 2026 offers an exciting research opportunity for doctoral candidates enrolled at participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities to undertake dissertation-related research at the Smithsonian Institution. The fellowship is designed for advanced doctoral students who have completed their coursework, have been admitted to doctoral candidacy, and have fulfilled all degree requirements except the completion of their dissertation. Selected fellows can conduct research and scholarship at the Smithsonian under the guidance of an appropriate Smithsonian adviser, with the goal of strengthening and advancing their doctoral thesis. The fellowship provides a stipend of $45,000 per year, along with a research allowance of up to $5,000 per year. Fellowship appointments can last from 3 to 12 months, with stipends prorated for periods shorter than one year. Applications for the 2026 competition must be submitted by October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) through the Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program application system.

Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship 2026 Overview

The Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship brings together doctoral research communities from participating Big Ten universities and the Smithsonian Institution.

The program is intended to help advanced doctoral candidates access Smithsonian research resources, collections, expertise and scholarly networks that can contribute substantially to their dissertation research.

Key details at a glance

Program: Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship

Host institution: Smithsonian Institution

Participating universities: Big Ten Academic Alliance member institutions

Duration: 3 to 12 months

Stipend: $45,000 per year

Research allowance: Up to $5,000 per year

Application deadline: October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET

Eligible applicants: Currently enrolled doctoral candidates at participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities

Citizenship: Open to both U.S. citizens and non-U.S. citizens

Application language: English

Application platform: Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program (SIFP)

What Is the Big Ten Academic Alliance?

The Big Ten Academic Alliance is a consortium of research universities that was established in 1958.

The alliance enables its member institutions to collaborate on academic and administrative initiatives designed to strengthen their educational and research missions. Through collaboration, the universities share expertise, leverage resources and create opportunities for students and faculty.

The alliance also seeks to support initiatives that contribute to the broader common good by encouraging collaboration and innovation across its member institutions.

The Smithsonian Fellowship is one example of this collaborative approach, providing eligible doctoral candidates with an opportunity to conduct research within the Smithsonian environment while advancing their dissertation work.

Universities Participating in the Program

The current Big Ten Academic Alliance institutions participating in the fellowship include:

University of Illinois

Indiana University

University of Iowa

University of Maryland

University of Michigan

University of Oregon

University of Washington

Michigan State University

University of Minnesota

University of Nebraska-Lincoln

Northwestern University

Ohio State University

University of California, Los Angeles

Pennsylvania State University

Purdue University

Rutgers University-New Brunswick

University of Wisconsin-Madison

University of Southern California

University of Chicago

The University of Chicago participates in the program as an affiliate.

Students should verify their university’s current participation and consult their campus Big Ten Academic Alliance fellowship contact before preparing an application.

Purpose of the Smithsonian Fellowship

The primary purpose of the program is to support advanced doctoral research.

The fellowship targets students who have reached a particularly important stage of their doctoral programs: they have completed their coursework and advanced to doctoral candidacy, but have not yet completed their dissertation.

At this stage, access to specialised research collections, laboratories, archives, experts and other academic resources can be extremely valuable.

The program allows eligible doctoral candidates to identify an appropriate adviser at the Smithsonian and conduct research or scholarship that contributes to the development and completion of their dissertation.

Rather than being a general graduate scholarship, the fellowship is therefore closely connected to a candidate’s existing doctoral research.

Research Areas Covered by the Fellowship

Applicants must propose research that will be conducted at the Smithsonian in an eligible research area.

The program covers a broad range of disciplines, allowing doctoral candidates from different academic backgrounds to develop research projects that align with Smithsonian expertise and resources.

Eligible areas include:

1. Animal Behavior, Ecology and Environmental Science

Research can focus on animal behavior, ecology and environmental science, including research with an emphasis on tropical environments.

This area may be particularly relevant to doctoral candidates researching biodiversity, ecosystems, species behavior, environmental change and related scientific questions.

2. Anthropology

The fellowship supports research in anthropology, including:

Archaeology

Cultural anthropology

Linguistics

Physical anthropology

Doctoral candidates conducting research involving human societies, cultures, languages, archaeological evidence or human biological variation may find this research area particularly relevant.

3. Earth Sciences and Paleobiology

Applicants can also propose research involving Earth sciences and paleobiology.

This area provides opportunities for researchers whose doctoral work focuses on Earth’s history, geological processes, fossils, ancient life and related scientific questions.

4. Evolutionary and Systematic Biology

The program supports research in evolutionary and systematic biology.

This may include doctoral research focused on evolutionary relationships, biological diversity, classification and the study of organisms and their development over time.

5. Folklife

Folklife is another eligible area of research.

Doctoral candidates whose work examines cultural traditions, everyday practices, community knowledge and related forms of cultural expression may be able to develop research projects within this area.

6. History of Science and Technology

Research concerning the history of science and technology is also eligible.

This may be relevant to doctoral candidates studying the development of scientific knowledge, technological change, scientific institutions, inventions and the relationship between science, technology and society.

7. History of Art

The fellowship supports history of art research, with particular emphasis on areas including:

American art

Contemporary art

African art

Asian art

Twentieth-century American crafts

Decorative arts

Doctoral candidates whose dissertations involve art history or related scholarly research may benefit from access to Smithsonian collections, expertise and resources.

8. Materials Research

Materials research is included among the eligible research areas.

This provides opportunities for doctoral candidates whose research involves the study, properties, development or application of materials.

9. Molecular Biology

The fellowship also supports molecular biology research.

This can be relevant to doctoral research involving biological molecules, cellular processes, genetics and related areas of molecular science.

10. Social and Cultural History of the United States

Applicants can also propose research focused on the social and cultural history of the United States.

This may include research examining American communities, social developments, cultural change, historical experiences and other aspects of the country’s social and cultural development.

Who Is Eligible for the Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship?

Eligibility is relatively specific because this fellowship is intended for doctoral candidates enrolled at participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities.

Applicants must be currently enrolled at one of the eligible Big Ten Academic Alliance member universities.

In addition, candidates must satisfy specific doctoral-stage requirements.

Doctoral requirements

By the time the fellowship appointment begins, applicants must have:

Completed all coursework required for their doctoral program.

Been admitted to doctoral candidacy.

Satisfied all doctoral requirements except completion of the dissertation.

This means the fellowship is designed for advanced doctoral candidates who are already at the dissertation stage rather than students who are just beginning their doctoral programs.

Citizenship and Nationality Eligibility

The fellowship is open to both U.S. citizens and non-U.S. citizens.

Therefore, citizenship does not appear to be restricted to applicants from the United States.

However, applicants must still meet the central institutional eligibility requirement: they must be currently enrolled at one of the participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities and satisfy the doctoral candidacy and coursework requirements.

For international doctoral candidates, this is an important distinction. Being a non-U.S. citizen does not automatically prevent participation, provided the applicant meets the program’s other eligibility conditions.

English Language Requirement

Applicants whose native language is not English are expected to have the ability to write and converse fluently in English.

All application materials must be presented in English.

$45,000 annual stipend

For fellowship appointments shorter than 12 months, the stipend is prorated according to the length of the appointment.

Interdisciplinary research opportunities

The wide range of eligible research fields makes the program relevant to doctoral candidates working across science, humanities, social sciences, anthropology, environmental research, art history and other disciplines.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Although meeting the eligibility requirements is essential, candidates should also focus on developing a clear and well-supported application.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate the connection between the applicant’s doctoral research and the Smithsonian environment.

Step 1: Confirm your university eligibility

Step 2: Confirm your doctoral status

Ensure that you will have completed all coursework, been admitted to doctoral candidacy and satisfied all requirements except the dissertation by the time the fellowship begins.

Clearly explain what you intend to accomplish during the fellowship.

Your proposal should make it easy for reviewers to understand:

The significance of the research

Why the Smithsonian is an appropriate place to conduct the work

What resources or expertise you need

What you expect to accomplish during the fellowship

Step 4: Identify a suitable Smithsonian adviser

Research the Smithsonian’s relevant scholars, scientists, curators and research resources to identify potential advisers whose expertise aligns with your dissertation.

Step 5: Connect the research to Smithsonian resources

Explain why conducting the research at the Smithsonian is important.

A convincing proposal should demonstrate that the Smithsonian environment offers meaningful resources, collections, expertise or facilities that will strengthen the dissertation.

TITLE: PRESS RELEASE – African Centers of Excellence converge in Djibouti from 18th to 27th February 2019

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
For
immediate release

African Centers of Excellence converge in Djibouti from 18th
to 27th February 2019 to strengthen research, development programmes
and innovations

Djibouti, 14 February 2019. The first Africa
Higher Education Centers of Excellence (ACE I) project was launched in Western
and Central Africa by the World Bank in 2014 to support higher education
sectors specializing in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM),
agriculture and health. In 2016, the second ACE project (ACE II) was launched
in Eastern and Southern Africa. The ACEs are an innovative regional response to
make higher education more relevant to Africa’s development.

As part of ACE I, 22 centers
have been financed by the World Bank for a total amount of US$165 million.
These are currently being implemented in universities in Benin, Burkina Faso,
Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Gambia, Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal and Togo and are
producing excellent results. ACE II has 24 centers across Ethiopia, Kenya,
Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia for an amount of US$148
million. Based on the successes of ACE I and it being in its final year of
implementation, the World Bank and the
French Development Agency (AFD) in collaboration with the African governments,
have conditionally identified 44 ACEs (26 new ones and 18 from ACE I); 5
Emerging Centers; and 5 Colleges and Schools of Engineering for funding through
a new phase called “ACE IMPACT” (pending both World Bank and AFD Boards
of Directors approvals). The new project will be implemented in universities in
12 countries, all nine participating countries under ACE1 with three additional
countries including Djibouti, Guinea and Niger. ACE Impact will strengthen
post-graduate training and applied research in existing fields and support new
fields that are essential for Africa’s economic growth.

From 18 to 27 February
2019, the centers and their partners will meet in Djibouti for the inaugural
ACE Impact workshop (a Bootcamp) to provide the platform for the centers to obtain
guidance on project preparation, exchange information on their respective
programs, build networks and forge partnerships to ensure the successful
implementation of the project. It will also create an opportunity for the new
ACEs to interact and learn from the existing centers. The ACE I centers will
also have the opportunity to discuss ongoing activities and progress, share
experiences and strengthen their impact on the continent’s development
challenges, as they work towards the closing of the ACE I project.

The event will be officially launched on Wednesday, February 20, 2019 at the Kempinski Hotel in Djibouti, starting at 8:30 am, while the rest of the activities will take place at the University of Djibouti.

TITLE: Call for Submission of Success Stories: SEADE Project

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Background

Over the past years, Africa has received increased interest and experienced various activities in the digital and innovation scene, reflecting a growing recognition of its immense potential for socio-economic transformation. This has led to many funded initiatives and projects aimed at gathering knowledge, developing digital tools, products, and services, and facilitating partnerships between Europe and Africa.

Against this backdrop of collaboration and innovation, the Strengthening the Europe-Africa Digital Ecosystem Through Increased Research & Innovation Cooperation (SEADE) Project was established as a beacon of concerted efforts to deepen and broaden digital cooperation between Europe and Africa.

To drive meaningful digital cooperation across borders, through leveraging knowledge reservoirs, and harnessing the insights and methodologies honed from past projects and initiatives, the SEADE Project is excited to announce a call for submissions of success stories related to past innovation projects. Through joint efforts while integrating the best practices and lessons learned from past experiences, this call for success stories aims to chart a path toward sustainable and inclusive digital progress. This involves addressing the digital gaps, improving digital proficiency, and fostering sustainable development across both the European Union and Africa.

Objectives

The goal of this call for submission is to showcase and celebrate the successful outcomes and impactful stories from funded research & innovation (R&I) projects and initiatives with a focus on digital tools, technologies, approaches, and transformations, among other areas. By highlighting these success stories, we aim to:

Inspire collaboration: Demonstrate the potential for successful cooperation between Europe and Africa in the field of research and innovation.

Share best practices: Disseminate valuable insights and lessons learned to facilitate knowledge exchange and replication of successful models.

Recognize achievements: Acknowledge the contributions and dedication towards advancing the goals of fostering digital transformation.

Learn from failures: Identify pitfalls and failings of initiatives and projects to understand what works and doesn’t work in R&I efforts.

Themes

Submissions are invited across various thematic areas including but not limited to:

Digital Inclusion: Success stories demonstrating efforts to bridge the digital gap and promote inclusive access to digital technologies and resources.

R&I Collaboration: Examples of successful partnerships and initiatives between European and African institutions, leading to impactful R&I outcomes.

Capacity Building: Stories showcasing capacity-building activities, training programs, and initiatives aimed at enhancing digital skills and competencies.

Entrepreneurship and Startups: Case studies highlighting successful digital entrepreneurship ventures and startups resulting from cross-continent collaborations.

Policy Impact: Demonstrations of policy advocacy efforts and interventions that have influenced digital policy frameworks and fostered an enabling environment for innovation.

Market Success: R&I initiatives that have effectively bridged the gap between research endeavors and market success. This includes facilitating the transfer of knowledge, supporting the development of economic growth through innovative products or services, creating opportunities within the employment market, etc.

Submission Guidelines

Interested applicants are encouraged to submit success stories adhering to the following guidelines:

Each submission should include a narrative outlining the project/initiative background, objectives, methodologies, achievements, challenges faced, and lessons learned. Visual aids such as photos, videos, and infographics are welcome to supplement the narrative.

Submissions should be concise yet comprehensive.

Entries must be submitted in digital format and may include supplementary multimedia materials.

Submissions are accepted in English, with translations provided for non-English entries if necessary.

Submission Process

Interested applicants are to make their submissions via the link https://www.research.net/r/RnISS24 by 28th June 2024.

Successful stories will be showcased through various channels including SEADE publications, digital platforms, and events organized by the project consortium, enhancing recognition and networking opportunities within the research and innovation community; furthermore, they will be recognized with an award as part of the project’s first event, with all selected submissions having the opportunity for widespread visibility and dissemination.

We eagerly anticipate receiving your inspiring success stories.

The Young Professionals Recruitment Programme

The programme is designed for high calibre young professionals who will not be more than thirty (30) years at the time of recruitment. The selected candidates will be appointed as Young Trainee Professional Staff in the Bank under a two (2)-year fixed term contract. The candidates will observe a probationary period of six (6) months during which each party may terminate the relationship without prior notice. However, where the performance of the Young Trainee Professional Staff is deemed to be satisfactory during the probationary period, their appointment shall be converted into an open-ended contract which means they will be permanent members of staff of the Bank.

During their appointment, the Young Trainee Professional Staff will be posted to different Departments on a rotational basis to make them familiar with activities of the Bank and integrate them into a team where they will make positive contributions. Furthermore, the Trainee Professional Staff will work under the supervision of senior staff in order to become acquainted with the various Departments, Policies and Programmes of the Bank.

Benefits

Various allowances (post adjustment allowance, housing and transport allowance, family grant where necessary) will be added to the salary.

During the period of their appointment the young professionals shall be admitted into the Bank’s pension scheme. The young professionals shall also be entitled to insurance cover against: death and permanent disability, total and permanent disability, temporary occupational disability, partial permanent disability, personal accident and sickness.

Eligibility

The citizens of ECOWAS Members States who fulfill the following criteria are invited to apply:

Less than 30 years of age at the time of recruitment;

Master’s degree or equivalent qualification in fields related to activities of the Bank in particular, Asset/Liabilities Management, Audit, Communication and Marketing, Finance, Engineering, Business Administration, Law, Accounting, Economics, IT, Human resources, Infrastructure, private sector operations, public sector operations, Risk Management, Language Services or a qualification in any other area that is relevant to the activities of the Bank;

Ability to work in a team and under pressure within a multicultural environment;

Analytical and organizational skills, ability to plan and determine priorities;

Good research skills for obtaining pertinent information (banking analysis, statistics, monitoring competitive trends etc.) from external sources in particular, electronic data bases and other media admitted for professional purposes.

Good knowledge of office automation systems (Excel, Word;
Access and Power Point);

Fluent in English/French/Portuguese with a working knowledge of one of the other two languages.

Conditions of service

In conformity with the rules governing the programme, the young professionals concerned shall be posted to Departments in response to specific needs. They shall not be recruited to fill vacant positions. However, throughout the duration of their appointment, they shall be considered as Professional staff of the Bank. Furthermore, their conditions of service shall correspond to those for grade P1-1 in the EBID staff classification and salary scale.

Recruitment Criteria and Procedure

Shortlisted candidates shall be invited for written and oral tests at the headquarters of the Bank in Lome. Candidates shall be tested for:

Technical skills,

Potentials,

Personality and level of motivation,

Computer skills,

Good verbal communication and writing skills in not less than two

(2) of the three (3) working languages of the Bank.

Application dossier

Interested candidates who meet the criteria listed above should forward their application dossier to the Bank in paper form. The dossier will comprise:

A detailled curriculum vitae;

Copy of qualifications obtained;

Copy of national identity card or passport;

Copy of birth certificate;

A letter of motivation indicating reasons for participating in the programme, areas of competence/interest, relevant experience and career prospects.

Interested candidates should submit no later than October 30, 2026, their hard copies application dossiers in a sealed envelope marked “2026 Young Professionals Recruitment Programme” addressed to:

ECOWAS BANK FOR INVESTMENT AND DEVELOPMENT (EBID)
128, Boulevard du 13 janvier, B.P. 2704, Lomé – Togo.
Tel: +228 22 21 68 64

N.B.: Only shortlisted candidates will be invited for interview. EBID reserves the right to withdraw the notified vacancies or offer position at a lower grade.

TITLE: Pulitzer Center Local Letters for Global Change Contest 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: November 1, 2026

Applications are open for the Pulitzer Center Local Letters for Global Change Contest 2026. Make your voice heard this fall by writing a letter to a local elected representative that explains the global issue you want them to prioritize, shows how it connects to your local community, and proposes a solution. Through this contest, students can practice global citizenship, civic action, and persuasive writing, all while exploring the underreported issues that matter to them through Pulitzer Center news stories.

The Pulitzer Center wants to read and share your letters: tell them, and the world, what’s most important to you.

Prizes

They will select one first place winner and up to four finalists for each issue category. First place winners will receive:

$300 to support global community engagement in your classroom (prize distributed to your class teacher)

Publication of your letter, photo, and bio on the Pulitzer Center website

Finalists will receive:

$75 to support global community engagement in your classroom (prize distributed to your class teacher)

Publication of your letter, photo, and bio on the Pulitzer Center website

All entrants will be invited to participate in a Pulitzer Center town hall event, held virtually in November, to share their solutions with other students from around the world.

Eligibility

They welcome entries from all current K-12 students across the globe. Letters may be written in English and/or Spanish.

Letters should address a topic within one of the Pulitzer Center’s five focus issues:

Climate and Environment (Includes climate change, pollution, extractive industries, and more)

Global Health (Includes health inequities, food security, mental health, water and sanitation, and more)

Human Rights (Includes racial justice, gender equality, migration and refugees, Indigenous rights, and more)

Information and Artificial Intelligence (Includes technology and society, misinformation, and more)

Peace and Conflict (Includes war, conflict, and peacebuilding efforts)

Application

Go to the Suggested Stories tab above and choose a story that gives you new information about an issue that matters to you. (All eligible stories are available here)

Write a one-page letter to a local decisionmaker that answers the following questions:

What issue do you want the local decisionmaker to address?

Why is this issue important globally? (Remember to cite evidence from the Pulitzer Center-supported story! You are encouraged to cite additional sources throughout your letter, too.)

Why is this issue important to your local community, and/or to you personally?

Why are you writing to this person? What power and/or responsibility do they have?

What do you want this person to do? Offer a solution, and cite evidence that your solution will be effective.

You do not have to answer the questions in this order, but your letter should answer all five questions. For support writing your letter, use this graphic organizer, or see the Resources for Teachers and Students tab above.

Submit your letter using the contest entry form. It will request some basic personal and contact information; the name and contact information for one of your teachers; and you can copy/paste your letter directly into the form.

After submitting your letter to the Pulitzer Center, consider mailing or emailing your letter to the decisionmaker directly.

For more information, visit Pulitzer Center Local Letters for Global Change Contest.

TITLE: Apply as a Sponsored Participant – Writing Workshop and Mentorship Programme

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Addressing Female STEM Lecturers’ Underrepresentation in Leadership in Technical Universities in Ghana

A British Council Gender Equality Partnerships Project

Introduction

Under the Gender Equality Partnerships Project, the Ho Technical University, the University of Nottingham, and the Association of African Universities invite female STEM lecturers at Ghanaian Technical Universities to participate in a two-day Writing Workshop to be held in Accra, Ghana, on Tuesday 13th and Wednesday 14th May 2025, followed by a 10-month Mentorship Programme designed to directly address participants’ challenges in securing leadership positions due to limited research output.

The aims of the writing workshop are outlined below:

to equip participants with the skills to improve their research writing, navigate the publication process and disseminate their research;

to provide a platform for participants to connect with peers, engage in mentorship and access international collaborations;

to elevate the participants’ confidence and improve leadership skills.

The Writing Workshop and Mentorship Programme draws on the collaborative partnership between Ho Technical University in Ghana (HTU), the Association of African Universities (AAU) and the University of Nottingham (UoN), and forms part of a larger qualitative, interdisciplinary study, co-designed and led by female scholars, that seeks to contribute valuable insights for promoting gender equity in STEM leadership. You can read more about the project here.

The British Council Gender Equality Partnerships will sponsor thirty female STEM lecturers at Ghanaian Technical Universities to participate in this workshop and the subsequent 10-month mentorship programme. This sponsorship includes:

Participation/Registration Fees (workshop training materials, and certificates)

Accommodation for three nights (during the workshop)

Local transportation, refreshments and meals

If you are a female STEM academic at a Technical University in Ghana seeking to advance your research career and enhance your leadership trajectory, we encourage you to apply and contribute to a more equitable future for women academics in STEM in Ghanaian Technical universities.

Eligibility Criteria

Applicants must be working at a Technical University in Ghana.

Applicants must be working in a STEM field.

Applicants should (1) have completed their PhD; (2) be nearing PhD completion or (3) be at earlier stages of their doctorate, provided they have collected their research data.

Note that a strong writing sample is required from all applicants.

Application Instructions and Submission Process:

Please follow these instructions carefully to complete your application. Note that incomplete applications will not be considered.

Fill out this form with all the required information – https://forms.office.com/e/p1n3D9vSvX

Ensure all information provided is accurate and complete.

The form requires applicants to:

– Provide a writing sample and tentative publication plan. Note that these documents are requested for the purposes of reviewing applications only. Your submission is confidential and will be deleted after the selection process is completed.

Submit a Writing Sample: Provide a 500 – 1,000 writing sample based on empirical data intended for publication, either authored or co-authored. This could be an excerpt from your doctoral thesis, a conference paper, or part of a draft journal article. If you have already published an article, this can be submitted too if based on empirical data.

Submit a Tentative Publication Plan: Provide a 1 to 2-page outline of a potential research paper based on empirical data. This plan should include a working title, a concise description of the research topic, research questions, a summary of the methodology and findings, and a timeline for completion of the draft.

Important Information:

The application deadline is Friday, 4th April 2025.

The organisers will review all applications and select the strongest 30 candidates to be sponsored to participate in this workshop. The selection results will be shared with all applicants by the end of April.

If you have any questions regarding the application process, please contact Dr Alicia Bowman at Alicia.Bowman@nottingham.ac.uk

We look forward to receiving your application.

All the best

TITLE: Advancing AI in Europe: From Foundations to Real-World Applications

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Inclusive Science | News | Project News

A Gathering in Brussels will bring leading voices from academia, industry, and public policy to address the most pressing challenges and opportunities shaping the future of artificial intelligence in Europe.

ENFIELD Project Final Conference

7-8 July 2026, 09:00-18:00 CEST

Palais des Académies, Brussels, Belgium

Participation Free

On the 7th and 8th of July 2026, the Palais des AcadÈmies in Brussels will host the Final Conference of the ENFIELD Project, a flagship Horizon Europe Network of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence. Titled Advancing AI in Europe: From Foundations to Real-World Applications, this two-day event brings together leading voices from academia, industry, and public policy to confront the most consequential challenges shaping the future of AI on the continent.

The conference arrives at a defining moment for European AI governance. With the EU AI Act entering its enforcement cycle and the AI Continent Action Plan setting out Europe’s ambitions for technological sovereignty, the need for a coherent, evidence-based dialogue between researchers, industry, and regulators has never been greater. ENFIELD’s Final Conference is designed to serve precisely that forum – translating years of collaborative research into actionable insight for practitioners and policymakers alike.

“Europe does not simply need more AI. It needs AI that is trustworthy, sustainable, and genuinely aligned with the values and strategic interests of its citizens. ENFIELD’s work has been to turn those principles into verifiable, deployable outcomes.” – Georgios Spathoulas, Technical Coordinator, NTNU.

This two-day conference will include keynote speeches, panel discussions, demonstrations and networking sessions designed to connect participants. The programme opens on Day 1 with a keynote from Rod Evans, NVIDIA‘s Vice President for Supercomputing, HER Cloud, and AI for Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Drawing on over 30 years of experience in the IT sector, Rod Evans will address the challenges related to AI infrastructure, focusing on energy constraints and sustainability of data centers. Day 2 opens with a keynote by Virginia Dignum, Professor of Responsible Artificial Intelligence at Umea University and one of the world’s foremost authorities on AI ethics and governance. A member of expert groups at UNESCO, the OECD, and the United Nations High-Level Advisory Body on AI, Dignum will examine the tension between innovation imperatives and the demands of human-centric regulation.

Further sessions will address data quality and explainability, Edge AI and robustness, EU AI Act compliance for industry, AI literacy and workforce development, and EU AI sovereignty. The conference will conclude with the formal presentation of ENFIELD’s strategic outcomes and roadmap, and its alignment with Europe’s broader ambitions for a competitive, responsible and sovereign AI ecosystem.

All sessions are free to attend, and demonstrations of research results will be presented throughout both days. Registration for the event is open here. Follow the latest news and information on the website: enfield-project.eu/final-conference.

Register here

About the ENFIELD Project

ENFIELD: European Lighthouse to Manifest Trustworthy and Green AI is a Horizon Europe funded Network of Excellence coordinated by the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU). The project brings together research institutions and industry partners across Europe to advance AI along four research pillars: Green AI, Adaptive AI, Human-Centric AI, and Trustworthy AI, to develop AI solutions that address challenges in sectors such as Healthcare, Energy, Manufacturing, and Space, while promoting sustainability and ethics. Promoted by 30 leading research institutions, businesses, and public sector representatives from 18 countries, the project builds a vibrant AI community of the brightest minds from across Europe. ENFIELD network will deliver over 75 unique AI solutions, 180 high-impact publications, strategic documents and extensive outreach efforts. Within the project, the European Science Foundation (ESF) leads the implementation of an analytical framework to monitor and assess ethics and gender dimensions across all project activities.

TITLE: College of Research Associates

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Join ESF’s

Strengthening science through collaborative expertise and review

In order to streamline our peer review process and ensure the continued high quality and responsiveness of our services, ESF recruits Research Associates on an ongoing basis across all scientific disciplines.

Research Associates collaborate with ESF remotely (home-based), on a consultancy basis and on a limited-time project basis. This includes supporting our Research Quality Assessment & Grant Evaluation team by :

Identifying scientific peers in order to assess research projects proposals and fellowships applications;

Providing quality check of peer-review reports;

Performing other related tasks as appropriate (ie: supporting review panels and their Chairs)

Selected Research Associates will receive appropriate training and mentoring as well as recognition for projects satisfactorily completed, in the form of a certificate delivered by ESF. They will learn more as to how successful award applications are written and how selection processes work.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible to join our College of Research Associates, you will need to fulfill certain criteria. We seek individuals who have direct knowledge of the academic sector including early-career researchers (advanced doctoral or postdoctoral researchers) with research expertise in a variety of disciplines:

Humanities

Social Sciences

Physics, Engineering and Material Sciences

Chemistry

Mathematics

Computer Sciences

Life Sciences

Earth Sciences

Environmental Sciences

Biomedical Sciences

Research Associates need to be active researchers in their field (academia or R&D) as testified by a recent publication record or other recent research outputs.

As a Research Associate you are required to invoice your services to ESF, as you would collaborate with ESF on a consultancy basis.

Frequently asked questions

What availability must I have to work as a Research Associate?
Expand
Time commitment is flexible depending on your availability. According to the number of hours you can be available on a month, we will allocate a certain number of research proposals to you.

How long does it take to work on a research proposal
Expand
In average a Research Associate spends 3h-4h per research proposal. This time involves reading the proposal, identifying Experts Reviewers, doing the quality check of their assessments and validating them on our online platform.

How many experts are to be identified?
Expand
For each proposal allocated, Research Associates need to provide between 4 to 6 Experts. This number allows us to secure at least 2 Expert evaluators per research proposal.

Annual publication of reviewers’ names on the ESF website (unless opted-out) for members having provided a review

Certificate of recognition awarded to members having provided a review (upon request).

What does the quality check of research proposals involve?
Expand
The quality check involves reading the assessment provided by an Expert Reviewer in order to make sure the Expert complied with the guidelines provided. This is not a second evaluation on the scientific point of view. The quality check also involves a brief proofreading to correct any typo mistakes, and takes in average 15-20 minutes.

Where are the expert evaluators to be found?
Expand
ESF provides access to internal and external databases of scientist across all scientific disciplines. We mainly rely on our Community of Experts, that gathers more than 10K scientists who have already agreed to collaborate with ESF on grant evaluation missions. Research Associates are also welcomed to suggest Experts from their network that comply with the Expert criteria provided.

What is the timeline of a grant evaluation mission?
Expand
A grant evaluation mission lasts between 2 to 4 months and follows three stages:

Research Associates identify Expert evaluators

Expert Reviewers evaluate research projects

Expert Reviewers upload their assessments on the online platform and Research Associates can then proceed to do the quality check and validation of their assessment reports.

When can I expected to be contacted once my application has been approved?
Expand
As soon as we have a grant evaluation mission involving research proposals in your field of expertise, we will contact you with more details about the number of research proposals allocated to you and dates involved. Upon your availability, we will establish a consultancy contract accordingly.

Training

Prior to any concrete work engagement with us, selected Research Associates will be provided with:

Documents and information describing the processes that they could be assigned to work on

Appropriate training/briefing on these processes.

More information about our Peer Review and grant evaluation processes can be found in the European Peer Review Guide (Integrating Policies and Practices into Coherent Procedures) published by ESF in 2011.

Applications

Please note that this is a Consultancy role and that selected candidates are required to provide invoices for consultancy services.

During the period covered by the consultancy contract, Research Associates cannot act as reviewers for any of the grant evaluation activities implemented by ESF.

We welcome your applications via the form hereafter. Applications will be processed by our HR and scientific teams and you shall expect a response within 2 months.

ESF will not discriminate, nor allow its staff to discriminate, against any member of staff or applicant for employment or ex-employee on the basis of gender (including in cases of pregnancy or maternity); age; ethnic, national or social origin; religion or belief; sexual orientation; disability; political opinion; social or economic condition or health.

TITLE: NGA Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field: Paid U.S. Federal Internship Applications Open

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field, a paid opportunity for eligible college and university students interested in government contracting, procurement, acquisition management, finance, business administration, supply chain management, public administration, law, and related fields.

The internship provides selected students with practical exposure to the full lifecycle of U.S. government acquisitions while working within the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, commonly known as NGA.

Positions are available in Springfield, Virginia, and St. Louis, Missouri, and the advertised annual salary range across the applicable NGA pay bands and locations is $27,108 to $101,097. The internship is not telework eligible, and participants should expect to work at their assigned NGA location.

The application window opened on August 31, 2026, and closes on September 30, 2026. NGA states that vacancy announcements close at 11:59 p.m. EDT on the closing date, so applicants should submit their complete online applications before that time.

About the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency

The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency is both a U.S. intelligence agency and a combat support agency. It is responsible for providing geospatial intelligence, commonly known as GEOINT, to support U.S. national security, defense, intelligence, navigation, and other government missions.

NGA describes itself as a world leader in providing timely, relevant, accurate, and actionable geospatial intelligence. Its work supports the U.S. Intelligence Community and Department of Defense and involves the analysis and integration of imagery, geospatial information, data, and intelligence.

The agency is headquartered in Springfield, Virginia, and also maintains major facilities in Missouri and other locations. Approximately 14,500 civilian, military, and contractor personnel work across NGA locations and supporting assignments worldwide.

For students, an NGA internship therefore provides more than general workplace experience. Interns operate within a national-security environment and gain exposure to professional processes used by a major U.S. federal intelligence and defense-support organization.

About the Summer 2027 Contracts Career Field Internship

The Summer 2027 College Internship in the Contracts Career Field is particularly relevant to students interested in how the federal government purchases goods and services and manages complex contractual relationships.

NGA explains that its Contracts Career Field helps procure the supplies and services required for the agency to accomplish its global mission.

Interns can gain practical exposure to the functions performed by Contract Specialists, professionals responsible for planning acquisitions, evaluating proposals, negotiating agreements, awarding contracts, and ensuring contractors comply with contractual terms and conditions.

The internship can therefore be highly relevant to students considering careers in:

Government procurement

Federal contracting

Acquisition management

Supply chain management

Business administration

Finance

Public administration

Contract management

Pre-law or legal studies

Commercial management

Vendor and supplier management

Government operations

Defense acquisition

Public-sector financial and commercial management

What Interns Will Learn

The internship is structured to expose students to the full lifecycle of government acquisitions.

Although individual assignments will depend on NGA’s operational and mission requirements, interns may gain experience in several important areas.

1. Acquisition Planning

Interns may learn how government agencies identify procurement requirements and develop plans for acquiring necessary goods and services.

This can involve understanding customer requirements, determining acquisition approaches, reviewing market information, and considering the most appropriate procurement strategy.

2. Development of Acquisition Strategies

Students may assist or observe professionals developing strategies for acquiring products and services.

An acquisition strategy considers issues such as requirements, procurement methods, competition, timelines, risks, contract structure, and expected outcomes.

For students interested in supply chain management or procurement, this exposure can provide an important understanding of how large public-sector acquisitions are planned.

3. Vendor Proposal Evaluation

Interns may learn how proposals submitted by vendors are evaluated.

Proposal evaluation is a central component of government contracting because federal agencies must select contractors using defined procedures and evaluation criteria.

Students can therefore gain exposure to structured commercial evaluation and government decision-making processes.

4. Contract Negotiation and Award

The internship can provide insight into how government Contract Specialists negotiate with vendors and award contracts.

Contract negotiations may involve issues such as pricing, contractual terms, deliverables, schedules, compliance requirements, and responsibilities.

This experience can be particularly valuable to students studying business, finance, procurement, public administration, or law.

5. Contract Administration

Awarding a contract is only one part of the procurement lifecycle.

After award, government agencies must ensure that contractors fulfill their obligations.

Interns may learn how contracts are administered to ensure compliance with applicable contractual terms and conditions.

Internship Locations

The announcement identifies vacancies in two locations:

Springfield, Virginia

and

St. Louis, Missouri

The USAJOBS announcement shows one vacancy in each location.

The opportunity is not telework eligible, meaning applicants should be prepared to work physically at the assigned location.

Relocation expenses are also listed as not reimbursed, so candidates who live outside these areas should carefully consider potential temporary housing, relocation, transportation, and living costs.

Salary for the NGA Summer 2027 Internship

USAJOBS publishes an overall annual salary range of:

$27,108–$101,097 per year

The applicable pay scale is listed as IA 01–02.

Because federal pay differs by pay band and geographic locality, compensation varies according to the location and the level at which the candidate is appointed.

Published 2026 ranges associated with this particular recruitment include:

Springfield / Washington, D.C. Locality

Band 1: $30,249–$75,059 annually

Band 2: $57,736–$101,097 annually

St. Louis Locality

Band 1: $27,108–$67,264 annually

Band 2: $51,740–$90,597 annually.

Applicants should understand that these are pay-band ranges rather than a guarantee that every intern will receive the maximum salary. Actual compensation will depend on NGA’s placement determination and the candidate’s applicable qualifications.

Who Should Consider the Contracts Career Field?

NGA specifically identifies several academic areas that align strongly with the Contracts Career Field.

Students majoring in the following subjects may find the internship particularly relevant:

Business Administration

Supply Chain Management

Finance

Pre-Law

Public Administration

These are examples of suitable majors rather than the only educational backgrounds mentioned in the broader student eligibility requirements.

Students interested in procurement, commercial operations, government contracting, business analysis, strategic problem-solving, financial management, public-sector administration, or acquisition policy may also find the professional experience especially valuable.

Mandatory Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should review the mandatory requirements carefully because failure to satisfy even one core condition can make an application ineligible.

Minimum Age

Applicants must be at least:

18 years old at the time of application.

Current Student Status

Candidates must currently be enrolled at least part-time in an accredited two-year or four-year college or university program.

Eligible levels include:

Associate degree

Bachelor’s degree

Graduate degree

Postgraduate degree

Applicants must have an anticipated graduation date of October 2027 or later.

Students who are expected to graduate before October 2027 are generally not eligible unless they have already been accepted into and enrolled in a subsequent qualifying degree program.

This requirement is important because the internship is designed specifically for individuals who will continue to hold qualifying student status.

GPA Requirement

Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of:

3.0 or higher

The GPA must appear on the most recent transcript uploaded with the application.

Freshmen who do not yet have an established college GPA may initially provide appropriate enrollment documentation, but they will later need to demonstrate that they achieved at least a 3.0 GPA for the relevant semester.

NGA states that offers may be rescinded if the required GPA is not subsequently achieved or verified.

Proof of Current Enrollment Is Mandatory

Although the USAJOBS required-documents summary displays “None,” the detailed vacancy instructions explicitly state that applicants must upload proof of current enrollment.

Applicants should therefore follow the more specific instruction in the announcement.

Students are required to provide their most recent unofficial transcript, showing:

Date

University information

GPA

Freshmen may submit a letter of enrollment from their university instead of a transcript where appropriate.

Failure to provide this proof of enrollment can result in disqualification.

Applicants who are ultimately accepted will also be required to provide an official transcript to NGA Student Programs after completion of the relevant semester.

Communication Skills Requirement

Applicants need experience providing clear verbal updates or explanations of routine information.

This experience may have been acquired through:

University presentations

Group projects

Employment

Volunteer activities

Student organizations

Academic research

Internships

Professional or community activities

Candidates should make sure their NGA resume provides specific examples rather than merely stating that they possess “good communication skills.”

Problem-Solving and Data-Gathering Experience

Candidates are also expected to demonstrate experience identifying and gathering information needed to resolve routine problems.

This competency could potentially be demonstrated through coursework, research projects, employment, student activities, internships, or other relevant experiences.

Applicants should emphasize situations in which they:

Identified a problem

Determined what information was required

Collected or analyzed relevant information

Reached a conclusion

Recommended or implemented an appropriate solution

The announcement specifically instructs applicants to use concrete examples and outcomes when demonstrating their qualifications.

Artificial Intelligence Knowledge

The current USAJOBS posting also identifies experience explaining fundamental artificial intelligence concepts and/or technologies used for routine tasks among the qualification criteria.

Students who have used or studied AI applications should therefore consider demonstrating their knowledge clearly and accurately in their application where relevant.

Examples could include academic exposure to:

Generative AI

Machine learning fundamentals

AI-enabled research tools

Data analytics

Automation

Responsible use of AI

AI-assisted business processes

Applicants should not exaggerate their expertise. The strongest approach is to provide a genuine example showing that they understand basic AI concepts and can explain them clearly.

U.S. Citizenship Requirement

One of the most important eligibility restrictions is that U.S. citizenship is required.

Because NGA operates in the intelligence and national-security environment and the internship requires access eligibility for highly classified information, international students who are not U.S. citizens should not assume they qualify merely because they are studying at a U.S. university.

The vacancy specifically identifies U.S. citizenship as a condition of employment.

Security Clearance Requirement

Applicants must be capable of obtaining and retaining a:

Top Secret security clearance with Sensitive Compartmented Information access, commonly referred to as Top Secret/SCI.

The security process is an important aspect of employment with NGA.

Selected candidates are also subject to a Counterintelligence Polygraph examination and drug testing.

Maintaining the required security eligibility is not simply an initial hiring requirement. Employees who require SCI access must continue to satisfy applicable security requirements throughout their NGA service.

Drug Testing

The announcement states that designated or random drug testing is required.

Applicants must therefore be prepared to comply with federal and NGA drug-testing requirements as a condition of employment.

Security Financial Disclosure

Employees holding SCI access while under NGA cognizance may be required to submit an annual Security Financial Disclosure Report, SF-714.

The purpose of this requirement is to support continuing assessment of eligibility for access to sensitive national-security information.

Failure to comply may affect continued access to classified information or secured facilities.

Work Schedule and Travel

The USAJOBS announcement identifies the work schedule as full-time.

Travel is listed as:

Not required

Telework is also listed as:

Not eligible

Relocation expenses are:

Not reimbursed.

Students considering the position should therefore plan carefully for the practical requirements associated with spending the internship period in Springfield, Virginia, or St. Louis, Missouri.

Federal Employment Classification

The position falls under occupational series:

0099 – General Student Trainee

and is within the Excepted Service.

The applicable pay bands are IA 01–02.

The announcement also notes that NGA operates under the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System, or DCIPS, for relevant civilian positions.

Important Note About the Appointment Description

Applicants may notice an apparent inconsistency in the USAJOBS announcement.

The position is repeatedly described by NGA and related postings as the Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field, and the duties are expressly framed as an internship.

However, the USAJOBS overview currently displays the appointment type as “Permanent.”

Candidates should therefore rely on the official NGA application process for final confirmation of the precise appointment mechanics and employment duration rather than assuming that the “Permanent” field converts the Summer 2027 internship into an indefinite regular position.

Resume Requirements

Applicants must use the NGA resume builder.

The vacancy specifically states that resumes must be limited to:

Two pages.

This is an important instruction. Applicants should not simply upload a lengthy general-purpose resume without checking NGA’s prescribed process.

A strong resume should directly address the mandatory qualification criteria and use specific examples demonstrating relevant experience.

Candidates should highlight:

Educational enrollment

GPA

Expected graduation date

Presentation and communication experience

Problem identification

Data gathering and analysis

AI knowledge or experience

Business or procurement exposure

Leadership

Academic projects

Relevant employment

Internships

Volunteer experience

Quantifiable achievements

NGA advises applicants to demonstrate the level and complexity of work they have performed and to include specific examples and results.

Is a Cover Letter Required?

A cover letter is not mandatory, but NGA recommends submitting one.

Applicants are given the option to attach a cover letter during the online application process.

Because this is a competitive intelligence-community internship, a focused cover letter can help an applicant explain why the Contracts Career Field aligns with their academic studies and career plans.

A strong letter could address:

Interest in NGA’s mission

Interest in federal acquisitions

Relevant academic background

Problem-solving capabilities

Communication skills

Interest in public service

Understanding of government contracting

Career goals

The letter should complement the resume rather than simply repeat it.

How Candidates Will Be Evaluated

NGA uses a multi-stage applicant evaluation process.

First, applications are reviewed against the mandatory qualification criteria.

Candidates who meet those requirements may then be evaluated by an expert or panel of experts using additional qualification criteria to identify the best-qualified applicants.

Those considered best qualified may subsequently be invited to participate in an interview process.

Meeting the minimum requirements therefore does not guarantee selection.

Veterans’ Preference

As a Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System position in the Excepted Service, applicable veterans’ preference procedures may apply.

External applicants claiming veterans’ preference must appropriately identify their eligibility in accordance with the vacancy instructions and applicable Department of Defense procedures.

Equal Employment Opportunity

NGA states that applicants will be considered without regard to factors including:

Race

Color

Religion

Sex

National origin

Age

Marital status

Disability

Sexual orientation

The agency also provides a process for requesting reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities during the recruitment and hiring process.

How to Apply for the NGA Summer 2027 Internship

Applications must be submitted electronically through NGA’s online recruitment process.

NGA states clearly that only electronic submissions will be accepted.

Applicants should:

Review the entire USAJOBS announcement carefully.

Confirm that they satisfy the U.S. citizenship requirement.

Confirm that they will be at least 18 when applying.

Confirm qualifying college or university enrollment.

Verify that their graduation date is October 2027 or later, unless continuing into another eligible program.

Ensure that their GPA is at least 3.0.

Obtain an up-to-date unofficial transcript showing enrollment details and GPA.

Prepare a targeted two-page resume using the NGA resume builder.

Consider preparing a focused cover letter.

Complete all questions in the NGA online application.

Upload the required enrollment evidence.

Review the entire application before submitting.

Submit before the September 30, 2026 deadline.

Applicants can subsequently follow the status of their application through NGA’s online application system.

Application Deadline

The application period for the NGA Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field is:

Opening date: August 31, 2026

Closing date: September 30, 2026

The NGA announcement states that applications close at:

11:59 p.m. EDT on the closing date.

Applicants are strongly advised not to wait until the final hours because transcript uploads, resume preparation, account issues, or technical problems could prevent timely submission.

Why Students Should Consider This Opportunity

This internship can provide valuable exposure to an area of the federal government that is rarely experienced through ordinary university coursework.

Federal acquisitions involve large-scale purchasing, regulatory requirements, vendor relationships, financial analysis, negotiation, risk management, strategic planning, and contract administration.

Students selected for the Contracts Career Field may therefore develop transferable professional skills relevant to careers in:

Federal government

Defense

Intelligence

Procurement

Finance

Consulting

Supply chain management

Contract management

Public administration

Commercial management

Working inside NGA also provides exposure to an organization operating at the intersection of national security, intelligence, technology, data, and government administration.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

Competition for federal intelligence-community internships can be significant, so candidates should avoid submitting a generic application.

Applicants should carefully map their experience against each mandatory qualification.

For example, instead of writing:

“Good communication skills”

a candidate could explain that they presented findings from a semester-long research project to a class of 30 students and answered questions about the methodology and conclusions.

Instead of stating:

“Good problem-solving skills”

the applicant could describe a project in which they identified missing data, collected information from several sources, evaluated alternatives, and produced a recommendation.

Students should also ensure that their graduation date and GPA can be immediately verified from their submitted documentation.

Most importantly, applicants should be accurate and truthful throughout the process because the role involves a high-level federal security investigation.

Conclusion

The NGA Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field offers eligible U.S. college and university students an opportunity to gain paid, practical experience inside one of the United States’ principal intelligence and combat-support agencies.

With positions available in Springfield, Virginia, and St. Louis, Missouri, students can gain exposure to government acquisitions, procurement strategy, proposal evaluation, contract negotiation, contract award, and contract administration.

The internship is particularly relevant to students studying Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Pre-Law, Public Administration, and related disciplines.

Applicants must satisfy strict eligibility requirements, including being at least 18 years old, a U.S. citizen, currently enrolled at least part-time in an accredited degree program, maintaining a GPA of at least 3.0, and generally having a graduation date of October 2027 or later. Candidates must also be able to obtain and maintain the required Top Secret/SCI security clearance and comply with applicable polygraph and drug-testing requirements.

The application deadline is September 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EDT.

Students who meet the requirements should prepare their transcript and targeted two-page NGA resume early and submit through the official online application system well before the deadline.
