TITLE: ChangemakerXchange Programme Lead Job 2026: Global Responsible Tech and AI Programme Management Opportunity in Berlin

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
ChangemakerXchange is inviting experienced programme and project management professionals to apply for the Programme Lead position, a hands-on role focused on delivering a global programme supporting young changemakers working to build a fairer, more sustainable future for artificial intelligence and the digital world.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to professionals with strong experience in programme management, project coordination, stakeholder engagement, corporate partnerships, impact measurement, and responsible technology or AI. The successful candidate will coordinate activities across four regional cohorts and work directly with more than 50 changemakers, local hosts, facilitators, and corporate partners.

The position is based in Berlin, Germany, and is offered as a 12-month contract, with the expected contract period running through the end of October 2027 or one year from the successful candidate’s start date.

ChangemakerXchange Programme Lead Job 2026

ChangemakerXchange is seeking an experienced Programme Lead to take responsibility for the end-to-end delivery of a global programme supporting young people using technology and AI to create positive social and environmental impact.

The programme brings together changemakers working across a broad range of responsible technology issues. These include developing alternative AI infrastructure, protecting indigenous and local knowledge, addressing algorithmic bias, reducing the environmental impact of hardware and data centres, defending digital rights, promoting fair labour conditions within AI systems, and applying technology to social and environmental challenges.

The Programme Lead will coordinate the initiative across Europe, MENA, the United States and Asia Pacific, with approximately 12 selected changemakers expected in each regional cohort.

The role therefore presents an opportunity for an experienced programme manager to work at the intersection of global programme delivery, responsible AI, technology, social innovation, youth leadership, stakeholder management and impact measurement.

About the Programme

The programme is designed to support young changemakers who are working towards a fairer and more sustainable future for AI and the wider digital world.

Rather than focusing exclusively on technical AI development, the programme encompasses a broad range of social, environmental and ethical questions surrounding technology.

Areas represented within the programme include:

Alternative AI infrastructure.

Preservation of indigenous and local knowledge.

Tackling algorithmic bias.

Reducing the environmental footprint of technology hardware.

Addressing the environmental impact of data centres.

Defending digital rights.

Promoting fair labour conditions for people involved in AI systems.

Using AI and technology to generate social impact.

Using technology to address environmental challenges.

Supporting changemakers developing responsible approaches to the digital economy.

The programme will operate through four regional cohorts:

Europe

Middle East and North Africa (MENA)

United States

Asia Pacific

Each region is expected to have approximately 12 selected changemakers, meaning that the Programme Lead will work directly with more than 50 changemakers overall.

The programme builds on ChangemakerXchange’s earlier AI programme, which was delivered across Europe, Latin America and MENA during 2025–2026.

What Will the Programme Lead Do?

This is described by ChangemakerXchange as a very hands-on project management role. The successful candidate will be responsible for coordinating the programme across all four regional cohorts while working with local hosts, facilitators, participants and the corporate partner supporting the initiative.

The role involves several major areas of responsibility.

1. Programme Delivery

The Programme Lead will take ownership of the programme’s delivery from beginning to end.

Responsibilities include:

Managing the selection process for programme participants.

Coordinating programme kick-offs.

Organising group sessions.

Coordinating in-person gatherings.

Supporting capacity-building activities.

Managing the overall programme timeline.

Ensuring activities are delivered consistently across regions.

Keeping the programme on schedule and within budget.

The successful candidate will therefore need to be highly organised and comfortable managing multiple activities simultaneously across different geographic locations.

2. Project Planning, Timelines and Budgets

A major component of the role is developing and managing detailed project plans across the four regions.

The Programme Lead will be expected to:

Establish project timelines.

Coordinate programme milestones.

Manage budgets.

Track implementation progress.

Identify potential delivery challenges.

Keep activities within agreed timelines and financial parameters.

Establish processes that allow the programme to operate smoothly across different locations.

This makes previous experience managing complex or multi-region programmes particularly valuable.

These may include systems for:

Participant tracking.

Scheduling.

Programme coordination.

Reporting.

Monitoring progress.

Collecting programme information.

Supporting communication among regional teams.

The Programme Lead will serve as the central coordination point between the organisation and these regional teams.

Key responsibilities include:

TITLE: ERC Advanced Grant – Arithmetic of Automorphic Motives (AAMOT project)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Principal Investigator : Michael HARRIS

Duration: 1 year

Description

The primary purpose of this project is to build on recent spectacular progress in the Langlands program to study the arithmetic properties of automorphic motives constructed in the cohomology of Shimura varieties. Because automorphic methods are available to study the L-functions of these motives, which include elliptic curves and certain families of Calabi-Yau varieties over totally real fields (possibly after base change), they represent the most accessible class of varieties for which one can hope to verify fundamental conjectures on special values of L-functions, including Deligne’s conjecture and the Main Conjecture of Iwasawa theory. Immediate goals include the proof of irreducibility of automorphic Galois representations; the establishment of period relations for automorphic and potentially automorphic realizations of motives in the cohomology of distinct Shimura varieties; the construction of p-adic L-functions for these and related motives, notably adjoint and tensor product L-functions in p-adic families; and the geometrization of the p-adic and mod p Langlands program. All four goals, as well as the others mentioned in the body of the proposal, are interconnected; the final goal provides a bridge to related work in geometric representation theory, algebraic geometry, and mathematical physics.­

Eligibility criteria

Candidates holding a PhD in Mathematics.

The selection will be based o­n the excellence of previous scientific achievements and the quality of the scientific project.

Contract details:

Each postdoctoral fellow will receive a net salary of 2100€ (including full health insurance and social coverage). He/she will be offered free housing in the IHES nearby residence and free access to the cafeteria for lunch.

The postdoctoral fellow will be requested to write a report at the end of the year on his/her scientific accomplishment comparing it with the initial Project and describing the perspectives.

Applications should be submitted online and include the application form duly completed, a CV, a list of publications, a description of research project and future plans as well as 2 or 3 letters of recommendation

The internship will provide an opportunity to contribute to UNDP’s work on risk intelligence, preparedness, anticipation, and the use of digital and AI-powered technologies for disaster risk reduction. UNDP works with governments and partners at international, national, and local levels to reduce disaster risks, strengthen resilience, and promote development that is risk-informed and sustainable.

The Early Warning & Preparedness Internship forms part of this broader effort. The intern will contribute to activities involving risk intelligence, early warning, preparedness, anticipation, digital innovation, and artificial intelligence applications for disaster risk reduction.

TITLE: Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship 2027–28: NIH-Supported Global Health Research Fellowship for U.S. and LMIC Scholars

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship 2027–28 is now accepting applications from emerging health researchers interested in advanced, mentored training in global health research. Supported by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) through the Fogarty International Center (FIC), the fellowship provides a 12-month research training experience designed to prepare the next generation of researchers and health professionals to address major and emerging global health challenges.

The GHES Fellowship brings together a consortium of leading U.S. universities, including Yale University, Stanford University, the University of California, Berkeley, and the University of Arizona, together with partner institutions in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

The program offers research training opportunities across 15 countries, providing fellows with the opportunity to work within international research environments while receiving mentorship from experienced global health researchers.

For scholars seeking to develop a career in global health research, epidemiology, public health, medicine, disease prevention, health systems, environmental health, or related fields, the GHES Fellowship provides an opportunity to gain specialized research experience, strengthen academic and professional networks, and contribute to research addressing population health challenges.

What Is the Global Health Emerging Scholars Fellowship?

The Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship is a 12-month, NIH-supported, mentored global health research training program.

The fellowship is designed to improve population health by developing researchers who can conduct rigorous research and contribute to solutions for pressing health challenges around the world.

The program is part of the Global Health Program for Fellows and Scholars/Launching Future Leaders in Global Health Research Training Program (LAUNCH), which is sponsored by the Fogarty International Center and collaborating institutes and centers at the NIH.

The fellowship year typically runs from July through June and provides participants with opportunities to undertake research training through a network of partner institutions in 15 LMICs.

Rather than focusing solely on classroom-based education, the program emphasizes mentored research training. Fellows are connected with experienced faculty members and research institutions whose work aligns with their research interests.

This structure allows participants to develop their research skills while gaining experience in international and multidisciplinary global health settings.

GHES Fellowship 2027–28 Application Deadline

The application for the 2027–28 GHES Fellowship year is currently open.

Deadline: October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

Applicants are encouraged to review the eligibility requirements carefully before submitting an application, particularly because eligibility requirements differ between U.S.-based applicants and applicants from LMICs.

Who Is the GHES Fellowship Designed For?

The fellowship is intended for emerging researchers at the predoctoral and postdoctoral levels.

There are three major applicant categories:

U.S. postdoctoral scholars

U.S.-based doctoral or professional students

Postdoctoral scholars based in eligible low- and middle-income countries

The precise requirements depend on the applicant’s academic status, citizenship or residency, institutional affiliation, and doctoral or professional qualifications.

U.S. Postdoctoral Fellowship Eligibility

U.S.-based postdoctoral applicants may be eligible if they meet the program’s requirements.

Applicants must generally:

Be a U.S. citizen or U.S. resident.

Provide a green card number where required for the application.

Have completed a qualifying doctoral degree within the past five years or be on track to complete the doctoral degree by June 2027.

Obtain endorsement from appropriate GHES mentors.

Have research interests that align with the expertise of available GHES mentors.

Applicants may come from any U.S. academic institution, rather than being restricted exclusively to Yale University, Stanford University, UC Berkeley, or the University of Arizona.

However, applicants who are not already affiliated with one of the consortium universities must obtain approval from the GHES Program Manager before applying.

Such applicants are expected to provide information including:

Their curriculum vitae.

A description of their research interests.

Potential GHES mentor(s) whose research aligns with their interests.

An NIH biosketch where required.

Information demonstrating that they have contacted potential mentors.

The doctoral degrees considered for eligibility include, among others:

PhD

MD

DVM

DrPH

PharmD

Applicants should carefully confirm whether their specific degree and academic status meet the current eligibility requirements.

U.S. Doctoral Student Fellowship Eligibility

The GHES program also provides opportunities for eligible U.S.-based doctoral and professional students.

Applicants in this category must generally:

Be a U.S. citizen or U.S. resident.

Be enrolled at UC Berkeley, the University of Arizona, Yale University, or Stanford University, or establish an appropriate affiliation with one of these institutions for the fellowship.

Be advanced-candidacy doctoral students or eligible professional students.

Professional students may include students pursuing degrees such as:

MD

DDS

DVM

PharmD

Other qualifying professional degrees.

Professional students must generally have completed at least three years of professional schooling.

The program is therefore particularly relevant to advanced doctoral and professional students who are preparing to develop research careers in global health.

LMIC Postdoctoral Fellowship Eligibility

The GHES Fellowship also welcomes eligible postdoctoral scholars from low- and middle-income countries.

For this category, applicants must generally:

Be a citizen of a low- or middle-income country as defined by the World Bank.

Have received a qualifying doctoral degree within the previous five years.

Be affiliated with one of the GHES partner LMIC institutions.

Obtain endorsement from appropriate GHES mentors.

Have research interests that align with the available research training opportunities and mentors.

Qualifying doctoral degrees can include:

MBBS

MMed

PhD

Other qualifying doctoral or professional degrees.

Importantly, the LMIC postdoctoral category requires a doctoral or professional degree. A master’s degree alone does not meet the stated requirement for this category.

Countries and Regions Represented by the GHES Network

The GHES consortium operates through collaborations involving institutions in 15 LMICs.

The network spans multiple geographical regions, including:

Africa

Latin America

The Caribbean

South and Southeast Asia

The Middle East

Eastern Europe

Oceania

This international structure gives fellows access to research environments addressing health issues in different populations and geographic contexts.

The program’s partner-site model is particularly important because applicants are expected to identify research sites and mentors that align with their proposed research interests.

Why the GHES Fellowship Is Important for Global Health Researchers

Global health challenges increasingly require researchers who can work across disciplines, institutions, countries and health systems.

The GHES Fellowship is structured around this need by combining:

Advanced research training

International collaboration

Faculty mentorship

Institutional partnerships

Population-health research

Cross-country research experience

Fellows have the opportunity to develop the skills necessary to contribute to evidence-based approaches to global health problems.

The program also places participants within established research networks, allowing them to learn from researchers and institutions working directly on health challenges in diverse settings.

What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying

Prospective applicants should not treat the application as simply a general fellowship application. A strong understanding of the program’s eligibility rules and research-site structure is essential.

Before applying, applicants should consider the following:

1. Confirm your applicant category

Determine whether you are applying as:

A U.S. postdoctoral scholar

A U.S. doctoral or professional student

An LMIC postdoctoral scholar

Each category has different requirements.

2. Verify your academic qualification

Applicants should confirm that their degree meets the program’s requirements.

For LMIC postdoctoral applicants in particular, a master’s degree alone is not sufficient according to the stated eligibility criteria.

3. Identify an appropriate research site

Applicants should review the available GHES research sites and identify the location that best corresponds with their research interests.

4. Identify potential mentors

Mentorship is central to the fellowship.

Applicants should therefore investigate the research interests of available GHES faculty members and identify mentors whose expertise aligns closely with their proposed area of research.

5. Contact the appropriate program representative

Applicants who are not already affiliated with one of the core consortium institutions may need to obtain eligibility confirmation from the GHES Program Manager before proceeding.

Providing a CV, research-interest statement and information about the relevant research site and potential mentor can help the program determine whether the applicant is eligible.

Application Process

The GHES application is hosted through the Yale University Global Health Emerging Scholars program.

Applicants should begin by carefully reviewing the program’s eligibility and application information.

For applicants seeking clarification, the Stanford GHES information recommends providing:

A curriculum vitae.

A short description of research interests.

The research site and faculty member with whom the applicant’s research interests are aligned.

Any questions about eligibility or the application.

Questions can be directed to Yosefa Gilon, GHES Stanford Program Manager, at the email address provided by the program.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours before the deadline to resolve questions about eligibility, institutional affiliation or potential mentorship.

Who Can Apply for the GHES Fellowship?

Applicants must satisfy the specific academic, citizenship/residency, institutional affiliation, degree and mentorship requirements applicable to their category.

The program is therefore not a general scholarship open to all students worldwide. Eligibility is structured around specific academic and professional stages and, for LMIC applicants, participation in the GHES partner-site network.

The eligibility criteria provided do not specify a race or ethnic-group restriction.

Geographic eligibility, however, is important.

TITLE: European Union Press and Information Officer Job in Switzerland 2026: Salary, Requirements, Responsibilities and How to Apply

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The European Union Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein has announced a new employment opportunity for an experienced communications, media, public relations or international affairs professional. The position is for a Press and Information Officer (m/f/x) within the Political, Press and Information Section of the EU Delegation in Bern, Switzerland. This opportunity is particularly relevant for professionals with substantial experience in media relations, strategic communication, digital communications, public diplomacy, journalism, public relations and event management who also have strong knowledge of German, French and English. The position is offered as a Local Agent Group I role under a fixed-term employment contract of two years, with the possibility of renewal subject to budgetary availability and operational considerations. The successful applicant is expected to begin work on 1 March 2027.

Press and Information Officer Job Opportunity at the EU Delegation

The European Union is an economic and political partnership made up of 27 European countries and plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development assistance and cooperation with global organizations. Outside the European Union, it is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations known as EU Delegations. These Delegations perform functions comparable in some respects to embassies and represent the EU in relations with governments and other stakeholders. The EU Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein is based in Bern, Switzerland. It works closely with the embassies and consulates of the 27 EU Member States and represents the European Union in dealings with the Swiss government on matters falling within the EU’s responsibilities. The advertised Press and Information Officer will become part of the Delegation’s Political, Press and Information Section. The role combines press relations, public diplomacy, social media, digital communication, event management, strategic communication and a smaller policy component.

Position Details

The position provides an opportunity to work directly within a diplomatic environment and contribute to the communication and public diplomacy activities of the European Union in Switzerland and Liechtenstein.

Key details include:

Position: Press and Information Officer (m/f/x)

Group: Local Agent Group I

Section: Political, Press and Information Section

Location: EU Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein, Bern, Switzerland

Contract: Fixed-term employment contract

Contract duration: Two years

Renewal: Possible, subject to budgetary availability and operational considerations

Probationary period: Three months

Expected start date: 1 March 2027

Working arrangement: Full time

Working hours: 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday

Additional requirements: Occasional evening and weekend work and travel for work missions

The successful candidate will work under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the Political, Press and Information Section. The role involves providing expertise and assistance in social media, digital communication and public relations.

What Will the Press and Information Officer Do?

The Press and Information Officer will have a central role in representing and communicating the activities, policies and values of the European Union in Switzerland and Liechtenstein.

The successful applicant will act as the EU Delegation’s spokesperson and will advise the Ambassador on communication-related matters. The position will also serve as a key point of contact between the Delegation and journalists and media organizations.

The officer will contribute significantly to the Delegation’s overall press, communication and visibility strategy while managing its digital presence and developing content for social media, websites and video platforms.

Another major component of the position is public diplomacy. This includes organizing events, engaging stakeholders and developing outreach activities designed to strengthen awareness and understanding of the EU, its activities and its values.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

Approximately 85% of the position’s time will be dedicated to press, communication and public diplomacy, while approximately 15% will be dedicated to policy-related work.

1. Press, Communication and Public Diplomacy

The largest part of the position focuses on communication and public diplomacy.

Public Relations and Media

The Press and Information Officer will be responsible for:

Maintaining and developing professional relationships with local and international journalists.

Working with media organizations and government press agencies.

Preparing and distributing press releases, press reviews and articles for publication.

Preparing interviews and speeches for the Head of Delegation.

Developing and implementing public diplomacy strategies designed to improve perceptions and understanding of the EU in Switzerland and Liechtenstein.

Preparing speeches, briefings and other information materials for the media.

Monitoring local and European media.

Preparing media reports.

Managing requests from journalists and coordinating responses with appropriate internal stakeholders.

Organizing media coverage during official missions and events.

Collaborating with EU Headquarters services and strategic communications task forces to maintain consistent messaging and communication strategies.

This means the successful applicant will need to be comfortable working in a fast-paced media environment where accuracy, speed, diplomacy and strong judgment are essential.

2. Social Media and Digital Communication

Digital communication is another major component of the role.

The officer will lead the Delegation’s digital and social media strategy and will be responsible for managing and producing content for relevant social media platforms and the Delegation’s website.

Responsibilities include:

Developing informative, engaging and accurate digital content.

Creating and implementing digital communication plans.

Developing social media campaigns.

Managing cross-posting activities.

Supporting livestreaming and event coverage.

Monitoring social media analytics and performance.

Recommending improvements to strengthen digital communication.

Improving the Delegation’s online visibility.

Coordinating digital campaigns with external service providers.

Candidates therefore need more than conventional writing or journalism skills. The position requires practical understanding of modern digital communications, social media strategy, analytics, web publishing and multimedia communication.

3. Event Management and Public Outreach

The successful applicant will also lead or coordinate public diplomacy and outreach activities.

This includes:

Preparing public diplomacy events.

Organizing public outreach activities.

Supporting high-level visits and site visits.

Working on events involving the Ambassador and other EU officials.

Coordinating with cultural, academic and diplomatic partners.

Strengthening the impact of public diplomacy activities.

Organizing cultural and visibility events that promote EU values and activities.

This aspect of the position makes event management and stakeholder engagement important areas of expertise.

4. Strategic Support and Administration

The Press and Information Officer will also:

Support the preparation of reports and strategic documents.

Assist with internal and external communication plans.

Support planning and management of the Delegation’s press and information budget.

Assist with procurement and contract management.

Policy Responsibilities

Although the majority of the position focuses on communication and public diplomacy, approximately 15% of the officer’s time will be dedicated to policy.

The policy component includes monitoring, policy analysis and reporting concerning EU-Switzerland cooperation in EU programmes, including areas such as:

Erasmus+

Research

Innovation

Science

Culture

Candidates who understand European affairs, EU institutions and EU-Switzerland relations may therefore have an advantage when demonstrating their suitability for the position.

Salary and Benefits

The vacancy states that the base salary will depend on the candidate’s relevant and verified employment experience, with the salary typically starting from CHF 10,343.

The position also comes with a competitive benefits package, subject to applicable conditions. The stated benefits include:

Personal leave days

Public holidays

A retirement savings plan

Health insurance, including accident insurance

Partial reimbursement of LAMal-related costs

The expected start date for the successful candidate is 1 March 2027.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements before submitting an application because the vacancy specifically states that applicants must verify that they satisfy all conditions. The position requires a combination of academic qualifications, professional experience, language proficiency and legal authorization to live and work in Switzerland.

Minimum Educational Requirement

Applicants must hold a university degree in a field relevant to the position.

Relevant fields include:

Political science

Communication

International relations

Media

Journalism

Public relations

Related fields

Professional Experience

Relevant experience may include:

Media

Online publishing

Public relations

Communication

Events

Similar professional areas

Language Requirements

Applicants must have excellent C1-level knowledge of German, French and English.

This is particularly important because the role involves communication with journalists, government stakeholders, diplomatic partners, EU institutions and the wider public.

Right to Work in Switzerland

This requirement is especially important for international applicants. The vacancy does not state that the position is universally open to candidates who would require unrestricted sponsorship or authorization to work in Switzerland.

Additional Qualifications That Can Strengthen an Application

The vacancy also identifies assets and selection criteria that may help candidates earn points during the selection process.

These include:

A postgraduate degree in political science, communication, international relations, media, journalism, public relations or a related field.

Experience working in a diplomatic mission.

Experience working for a development agency.

Experience in a multicultural international environment.

Experience working with European Union policies and procedures.

These are presented as assets rather than the basic minimum requirements, meaning candidates should distinguish carefully between mandatory eligibility conditions and additional experience that can strengthen their application.

Skills Required for the Position

The successful candidate should have a broad combination of strategic communication, digital, analytical, writing and interpersonal skills.

Important skills include:

Translating complicated policy issues into language suitable for traditional and social media.

Developing communication strategies and plans.

Maintaining a good professional network within Swiss media.

Understanding local and European cultural interaction.

Understanding EU institutions, history and priorities.

Understanding EU-Switzerland relations.

Strong knowledge of digital media and communication techniques.

Knowledge of graphic and layout editing and design tools.

Knowledge of web publication tools.

Excellent writing skills.

Ability to prepare concise and clear notes.

Ability to communicate effectively and clearly, both orally and in writing.

This combination demonstrates that the role is designed for an experienced communications professional who can move comfortably between strategic planning, media engagement, digital production, public speaking and policy communication.

Personal and Behavioral Qualities

Beyond academic and professional qualifications, the EU Delegation is looking for someone who can operate effectively in a demanding diplomatic environment.

The vacancy highlights the following qualities:

Ability to multitask.

Ability to work under time pressure.

Proactive approach to work.

Ability to take appropriate action without constant prompting.

Flexibility when responding to new requests.

Ability to build and maintain professional relationships.

Initiative and good workload organization.

Confidence speaking before large audiences.

Service-oriented mindset.

Professional attitude and appearance.

Willingness to learn and develop new competencies.

High levels of integrity, confidentiality and responsibility.

Working Environment

However, candidates should be prepared for occasional atypical working hours, including evenings and weekends. The position also involves travel for work missions.

The job is primarily office-based and does not involve specific or unusual physical requirements.

The officer will work closely with colleagues within the Political, Press and Information Section and other parts of the organization.

The role also requires regular cooperation with:

EU Headquarters

Cultural partners

Academic partners

Diplomatic partners

External service providers

Journalists and media organizations

Other relevant stakeholders

The cover letter should demonstrate the candidate’s suitability for the position and should clearly connect their professional experience and qualifications to the responsibilities described in the vacancy.

18 September 2026 at 24:00 CET.

Because the application requires multiple documents and the CV must contain detailed employment information, candidates should avoid waiting until the final day to prepare and submit their applications.

TITLE: Migration Policy Institute Associate Policy Analyst 2026: Apply for a Global Migration Policy Career with Worldwide Remote Work Considered

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Migration Policy Institute (MPI) is accepting applications for a full-time Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program, offering an opportunity for experienced researchers and policy professionals to contribute to international migration research, comparative policy analysis, policy advising, high-level convenings, and influential publications.

The position is based out of MPI’s Washington, D.C. office in the United States, but there is a particularly important provision for international applicants: remote work from anywhere in the world may be considered for the right candidate. For candidates based in the United States, the advertised starting salary is $62,000 to $67,000 per year, with final compensation depending on skills and experience. Arrangements for internationally based remote employees will be determined according to their location, experience, and applicable local employment regulations.

The role sits within MPI’s Global Program, which works across some of the most consequential migration-policy issues confronting governments and societies today. Its work includes demographic change, labor markets, refugee protection, climate-related migration, international cooperation, legal migration pathways, social cohesion, and migration governance.

Applications must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday, September 30, 2026. MPI is reviewing applications on a rolling basis and specifically encourages interested candidates to apply as early as possible.

About the Migration Policy Institute

The Migration Policy Institute is an independent, nonpartisan, evidence-informed think tank focused on immigration, migration, and immigrant integration policy.

Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Washington, D.C., MPI conducts research and policy analysis intended to improve how governments and institutions respond to migration. Its work combines empirical research, policy development, data analysis, dialogue, and the creation of practical approaches to complex migration questions.

MPI works on migration issues at local, national, and international levels and examines both voluntary and forced migration. Its research spans subjects including immigration systems, refugee and asylum policy, labor markets, migration and development, integration, education, enforcement, borders, and international governance.

In addition to its Washington operations, MPI has a sister organization, Migration Policy Institute Europe, headquartered in Brussels, Belgium. MPI Europe focuses particularly on migration, integration, and asylum policy within the European context.

About the Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program Position

The current vacancy is for a:

Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program

This is a full-time position designed for a professional who already has substantive research and policy experience and is ready to take an active intellectual role within MPI’s international work.

The successful candidate will support the Global Program through rigorous empirical research and comparative policy analysis. Rather than functioning only as a research assistant, the Associate Policy Analyst will have opportunities to contribute ideas, participate in team strategy, help shape research methods, write publications, work on policy projects, support high-level meetings, and gradually develop an independent public research profile.

MPI describes the Global Program as a highly collaborative team in which staff members are expected to contribute intellectually from the beginning. As analysts develop their expertise, there may be opportunities to co-author policy briefs, opinion pieces, and longer research publications, and eventually to single-author or lead-author some policy briefs.

What Does MPI’s Global Program Do?

MPI describes its Global Program as a policy laboratory that develops innovative, evidence-based, and politically feasible approaches to migration-policy challenges around the world.

The program combines several forms of work:

Comparative international research

Policy design

Direct policy advice

Government engagement

International cooperation

Research on migration trends

Stakeholder dialogue

Private policy convenings

Development of practical recommendations

The Global Program also seeks to anticipate how major structural changes—including demographics, economic transformation, climate change, and technology—could influence migration and migration policy in the future.

Its work involves governments and institutions across numerous regions, including Europe, North America, Central and South America, Africa, and the Asia-Pacific region. It also works with institutions at the European Union and United Nations levels.

Geographic Scope of the Role

The Global Program already has established portfolios of work in:

Latin America

East Africa

Europe

It is also developing or expanding work in:

South Asia

Southeast Asia

Middle East

North Africa

Australia

This international scope is one reason MPI prefers candidates with knowledge of international migration policy and expertise concerning at least one country outside the United States. Experience relating particularly to Africa, Latin America, or Europe is highlighted as desirable.

Major Migration Issues the Successful Candidate Could Work On

The position is deliberately broad rather than being restricted to a single migration-policy specialty.

Examples provided by MPI include research concerning:

Demographic Change and Labor Markets

Population aging, demographic transitions, skills shortages, workforce mobility, and labor-market change are increasingly connected with migration policies.

An Associate Policy Analyst may contribute to research examining how migration can interact with these demographic and economic developments.

Refugee Protection

The role can involve questions concerning the future of refugee and humanitarian-protection systems.

MPI’s Global Program is examining how protection mechanisms can respond to increasing displacement while remaining politically and institutionally sustainable.

Climate-Related Migration

Climate change is increasingly influencing patterns of mobility and displacement.

The Global Program examines connections between migration, resilience, development investments, and climate pressures, making climate-related mobility one of the areas relevant to the position.

Legal Migration Pathways

Migration systems must increasingly respond to technological change, demographic pressures, and evolving skills requirements.

MPI’s Global Program has identified the design of legal pathways in this changing environment as one of its major areas of work.

Public Trust and Social Cohesion

The Global Program also examines how migration systems interact with public confidence, political debate, social cohesion, and rapidly changing societies.

International Migration Governance

Another major area involves international cooperation and the governance of migration.

MPI examines how governments can coordinate migration policies, respond to crises, and create workable mechanisms for international collaboration.

Five Major Pillars of MPI’s Global Program

MPI identifies five principal pillars for the Global Program:

Rethinking humanitarian protection systems

Designing legal migration pathways in response to technological and demographic change

Strengthening public trust and social cohesion around migration

Using development investments to harness migration’s potential and strengthen climate resilience

Rethinking international cooperation and improving migration governance

These areas indicate the range of research questions that an Associate Policy Analyst may encounter while working within the program.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be expected to perform substantial analytical and research responsibilities rather than routine administrative work.

Conduct In-Depth Policy Analysis

The Associate Policy Analyst will conduct detailed research and interpret evidence in ways that produce clear policy findings and practical recommendations.

The role also includes helping to develop methodologies for new research projects.

Draft Research Publications

Writing forms a major component of the position.

The successful candidate will draft and edit materials such as:

Background notes

Analytical reports

Policy briefs

Research materials

Short-form analysis

Longer research publications

Candidates must therefore be capable of producing precise and accessible policy writing under tight deadlines and with relatively limited supervision.

Contribute to MPI Publications

The Associate Policy Analyst will contribute to and co-author MPI publications.

As the successful candidate develops expertise and experience within the organization, there may also be opportunities to lead or independently author policy briefs.

For researchers hoping to build a stronger publication record in international migration policy, this is a significant professional-development component of the role.

Fundraising and Grant Management

The successful applicant will also support senior staff members with fundraising and grant-management activities.

Responsibilities can include:

Contributing to grant proposals

Assisting with grant reporting

Researching potential funding opportunities

Supporting broader project-development activities

This means the role requires more than academic research ability. Candidates should also be comfortable working within the operational and funding structures of a nonprofit research organization.

Supporting High-Level Policy Roundtables and Meetings

MPI regularly brings together policymakers, researchers, government officials, and other stakeholders.

The Associate Policy Analyst will help organize high-level roundtables and private meetings.

Tasks may include:

Developing meeting agendas

Preparing concept notes

Communicating with participants

Briefing speakers

Supporting substantive preparation for policy discussions

This gives the successful candidate exposure to the practical side of policy engagement in addition to desk-based research.

Potential Media Engagement

MPI also states that, over time and with appropriate support, the successful candidate may engage with the news media.

This could provide an opportunity to develop experience communicating research findings beyond specialist academic and policy audiences.

Opportunity to Develop Your Own Research Ideas

One notable feature of the position is that the new analyst is not expected merely to execute work designed entirely by senior staff.

MPI states that team members are able to participate in strategy discussions and develop their own research ideas.

As expertise develops, candidates may move from supporting research toward co-authoring and potentially leading policy publications.

For researchers seeking to build an independent policy profile, this intellectual participation may be particularly valuable.

Required Academic Qualification

MPI lists the following principal qualification:

A master’s degree combined with three to five years of direct relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

This wording is important.

It means the advertised profile is not necessarily limited exclusively to candidates who follow one rigid educational route. MPI explicitly allows an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Applicants without the precise master’s-plus-experience combination would therefore need to demonstrate that their alternative background provides equivalent professional preparation.

Professional Experience Required

Candidates should generally have approximately:

3–5 years of direct relevant experience

when applying with a master’s degree.

Relevant experience could reasonably include work involving migration policy, international development, policy research, refugee policy, labor migration, demographic research, comparative public policy, policy analysis, or related fields, provided the experience demonstrates the capabilities requested by MPI.

Applicants should avoid assuming that unrelated professional experience will automatically satisfy the requirement.

Strong Research and Analytical Skills

A major requirement is the ability to conduct sophisticated research and analyze substantial volumes of information.

Candidates should be capable of collecting, organizing, interpreting, and synthesizing information from sources including:

Primary sources

Secondary sources

Surveys

Fieldwork

Large bodies of research evidence

MPI is looking for candidates who can move from collecting information to producing meaningful analytical conclusions.

Quantitative Analysis Is an Advantage

Experience conducting original quantitative analysis using statistical programming software is listed as an advantage.

However, MPI explicitly states that this capability is not required.

Applicants with skills in statistical analysis, quantitative research, programming, or data visualization should therefore highlight those capabilities, but candidates should not automatically disqualify themselves simply because their experience is predominantly qualitative.

Migration Policy Expertise

Candidates should understand international migration trends and policies.

MPI particularly prefers candidates with substantive knowledge relating to one or more countries outside the United States, with expertise concerning Africa, Latin America, or Europe highlighted as especially relevant.

This requirement aligns directly with the Global Program’s comparative international mandate.

A candidate with strong migration-policy expertise concerning South or Southeast Asia, MENA, Australia, or another relevant region could also be relevant given the program’s expanding geographic portfolio, though the official vacancy specifically emphasizes Africa, Latin America, and Europe among preferred areas of expertise.

Writing and Communication Skills

Strong written and oral communication ability is essential.

Candidates must be capable of taking complex empirical findings and communicating them clearly to policy and professional audiences.

MPI also describes the following capabilities as advantages:

Public-speaking confidence

Data visualization

Presenting evidence effectively

Explaining data clearly to different audiences

Because the position involves research publications, policy meetings, potential media engagement, and interaction with stakeholders, communication ability is central rather than secondary to the role.

Ability to Manage Multiple Projects

The successful candidate must be highly motivated, proactive, and capable of managing multiple assignments simultaneously.

MPI’s Global Program works across numerous countries, projects, funding arrangements, and policy themes. The candidate must therefore be able to:

Prioritize competing assignments

Maintain attention to detail

Meet deadlines

Switch between different kinds of work

Operate in a fast-paced environment

Adapt as projects evolve

Intellectual Curiosity

MPI also places explicit emphasis on curiosity.

Candidates should be willing to read widely and incorporate ideas, approaches, and methodologies from other policy fields into migration research.

The position therefore favors people who can move beyond a narrow specialty and connect migration with broader demographic, economic, political, environmental, technological, and social developments.

Salary for U.S.-Based Candidates

For an Associate Policy Analyst based in the United States, MPI advertises a starting salary range of:

$62,000–$67,000 per year

Final salary will be determined based on the candidate’s skills and experience.

It is important to state this precisely: the advertised $62,000–$67,000 range is specifically identified for a candidate based in the United States.

International remote applicants should not assume that this exact salary range automatically applies to them.

Benefits

MPI states that it provides a benefits package for full-time U.S.-based employees.

The vacancy page does not provide a detailed itemized list of those benefits.

For international remote appointments, compensation, benefits, and employment arrangements will instead be reviewed according to:

Candidate location

Experience

Applicable local employment laws and regulations

Is This a Remote Job?

Potentially, yes.

The primary position is based out of Washington, D.C., but MPI explicitly states:

Remote work worldwide will be considered for the right candidate.

This makes the vacancy particularly relevant to qualified migration-policy professionals outside the United States.

However, “considered” should not be interpreted as a guarantee that MPI can employ a candidate in every jurisdiction. The organization states that remote employment conditions will be determined according to local employment regulations and the candidate’s location.

Can Applicants Outside the United States Apply?

The vacancy does not impose a U.S.-only application restriction, and MPI explicitly says that worldwide remote work may be considered.

Accordingly, suitably qualified candidates outside the United States can consider applying.

This could potentially include applicants based in:

Africa

Asia

Europe

North America

South America

Australia/Oceania

Middle East

The decisive issues will be whether the applicant meets the professional requirements and whether a workable employment arrangement can be established under the laws applicable to their location.

Applicants should not interpret the worldwide-remote language as an unconditional promise of employment from every country.

Application Documents Required

Applicants must submit three main documents:

Cover letter

Resume

Short writing sample

Each file should be labeled using the applicant’s last name.

Special 1,000-Word Writing Sample Requirement

The writing sample is a particularly important part of the application.

Applicants must prepare approximately:

1,000 words on an immigration policy of their choice.

This provides candidates with an opportunity to demonstrate their analytical approach, command of evidence, understanding of migration policy, and ability to communicate complex policy questions concisely.

A strong writing sample should ordinarily demonstrate:

A clearly defined policy issue

Accurate use of evidence

Analytical reasoning

Understanding of policy trade-offs

Clear structure

Concise professional writing

Appropriate recommendations or implications where relevant

These are practical application suggestions, rather than an additional official scoring rubric published by MPI.

MPI Allows AI Tools — But Disclosure Is Required

One unusual and important detail in the vacancy announcement concerns artificial intelligence.

MPI explicitly states that applicants may use AI tools when preparing the writing sample, but they must disclose how those tools were used.

Candidates who use AI should therefore provide transparent disclosure rather than submitting AI-assisted material without explanation.

Since the purpose of the writing sample is to demonstrate the applicant’s analytical and writing capability, candidates should also ensure that the final submission accurately reflects their own knowledge, reasoning, and professional judgment.

Email Subject Line

Applicants should use the following position title in the email subject line:

Associate Policy Analyst – Global Program

They must also include a line explaining how they heard about the position.

Where to Send the Application

Applications are submitted by email.

The official careers page displays the recruitment email through protected website formatting. Independent reproductions of the same vacancy identify the recruitment address as:

hr@migrationpolicy.org.

Applicants should nevertheless verify the address directly on MPI’s official careers page immediately before submitting their materials.

Application Deadline

The final application deadline is:

Wednesday, September 30, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

MPI states that applications will be assessed on a rolling basis, meaning review can begin before the final deadline.

Candidates are therefore encouraged to apply early rather than assuming that submitting immediately before the deadline provides the same practical advantage as an earlier application.

What Happens After Applying?

MPI states that because it expects a large volume of applications, only candidates being considered for the position will be contacted.

The organization also asks candidates not to make phone calls or send separate inquiries to MPI staff regarding the application.

A separate listing reproducing the vacancy indicates that interviews are expected during October 2026 and that the start date is flexible but intended to occur before the end of 2026. Because these dates come from an external vacancy listing rather than the main MPI careers page, applicants should treat MPI’s own communications as controlling.

Application Strategy for Potential Candidates

Candidates should tailor their applications carefully to the actual responsibilities of the role.

A competitive cover letter should clearly demonstrate the connection between the applicant’s experience and MPI’s Global Program.

For example, rather than stating “I have strong research skills,” an applicant could explain that they designed a comparative research project, analyzed survey or administrative data, produced a policy report, and presented findings to government or international stakeholders.

How to Strengthen the Cover Letter

Because the position is relatively specialized, a generic cover letter is unlikely to communicate the candidate’s fit effectively.

Applicants can consider structuring their letter around:

Who Would This Position Be Most Relevant For?

The position is particularly relevant to mid-early-career professionals who already have substantive policy or research experience.

TITLE: University of Rochester Political Science Professor Job 2027: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Position in Political Methodology

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The University of Rochester is inviting applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Political Science specializing in political methodology. The position is based in Rochester, New York, and is expected to begin on July 1, 2027.

The opportunity is offered through the Department of Political Science within the University’s School of Arts & Sciences. It is particularly suited to scholars whose methodological research addresses substantive questions in politics and political economy.

Candidates from political science and related disciplines, including statistics, computer science, and economics, are encouraged to apply, provided their research aligns with the position’s methodological and substantive focus.

About the Position

The Department of Political Science at the University of Rochester is seeking a scholar for a tenure-track faculty appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor.

The successful candidate will join the department as a political methodology scholar whose research connects methodological innovation with substantive questions in politics and political economy.

The position provides an opportunity for an early-career academic to develop a long-term research and teaching career within a university environment.

The appointment is scheduled to begin:

July 1, 2027

The position is based in:

Rochester, New York, USA

The listed salary range is:

$120,000–$140,000

What Is Political Methodology?

Political methodology is an area of political science concerned with developing and applying research methods to understand political phenomena.

Researchers in this field may work with statistical methods, computational approaches, causal inference, research design, data analysis, mathematical modelling and other quantitative or qualitative approaches.

For this particular position, the University of Rochester is interested in candidates whose methodological research does not exist independently from substantive political questions.

Instead, candidates should demonstrate how their methodological research can be used to investigate important questions relating to politics and political economy.

This makes the position particularly relevant to researchers who combine methodological expertise with substantive interests in political science.

Research Focus

Applicants should have methodological research interests that address substantive questions in:

Politics

Political economy

Political behaviour

Political institutions

Related areas of political science

The department welcomes candidates whose research demonstrates strong methodological expertise while making meaningful contributions to understanding political or economic processes.

Applicants from related disciplines may also be considered, particularly where their methodological work connects clearly with political science.

Academic Background

The position is open to candidates who hold a PhD or are ABD in political science or a related discipline.

The advertisement specifically identifies several related fields, including:

Statistics

Computer science

Economics

Other relevant disciplines

Candidates from these fields should be able to demonstrate that their methodological research addresses substantive questions relevant to politics and political economy.

PhD and ABD Candidates

Applicants do not necessarily need to have completed their PhD at the time of application because the position also welcomes candidates who are ABD (All But Dissertation).

However, applicants should have the appropriate doctoral-level academic background in political science or a related field.

Candidates should ensure that their academic and research profile demonstrates a strong fit with the department’s focus on political methodology.

Salary

The advertised salary range for the position is:

$120,000–$140,000

The final salary may depend on factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, experience and the University’s applicable compensation policies.

Location

The position is located in:

Rochester, New York

Rochester is home to the University of Rochester and provides the academic environment in which the successful candidate will undertake their teaching and research responsibilities.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The University of Rochester will consider all applications received by September 15, 2026.

Importantly, the department states that it will continue accepting applications after September 15, 2026.

Applicants are therefore encouraged to submit their applications by the September 15 priority date rather than waiting until after the stated date.

Priority application date: September 15, 2026

Required Application Documents

Applicants are required to submit several documents as part of their application.

1. Cover Letter

The cover letter should introduce the candidate and explain their suitability for the position.

Applicants should use the letter to demonstrate their academic background, research interests and alignment with the Department of Political Science.

2. Curriculum Vitae

Candidates must submit an up-to-date CV detailing their academic qualifications, research experience, publications, teaching experience and other relevant professional achievements.

3. Research Statement

A research statement is required.

This document should communicate the candidate’s research agenda, methodological expertise, scholarly contributions and future research plans.

Candidates should make the connection between their methodological research and substantive questions in politics or political economy clear.

4. Teaching Statement

Applicants must also submit a teaching statement.

The statement should provide information about the candidate’s teaching experience, approach to teaching and potential contribution to the department’s academic programmes.

5. Three Confidential Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must arrange for three confidential letters of recommendation to be submitted.

These letters should provide an independent assessment of the candidate’s academic and research capabilities.

6. Writing Sample

A writing sample must also be included in the application.

Candidates should select a piece of scholarly work that demonstrates the quality of their research, analytical abilities and methodological expertise.

How the Application Process Works

The University of Rochester is using Interfolio’s Faculty Search system to manage applications for this position.

Applicants who apply through Interfolio will receive a free Dossier account.

This allows candidates to submit their application materials through the platform, including confidential recommendation letters, without being charged for the dossier service.

TITLE: Cairo hosts the Maiden 2019 African Universities Olympics

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Teams, coaches and spectators from 27 African countries, 17 African universities and the 5 regions of Africa thronged Cairo this week to participate in the African Universities Olympics organised by the Association of African Universities, Al-Azhar University and All Africa Students Union – supported by the Arab Republic of Egypt.

Thursday 14th March 2019 will remain imprinted on the minds of many – this is the day when the maiden 2019 African Universities Olympics event was officially opened during an electrifying, superbly organized and glamorous ceremony held at the Main Sports Stadium of the Military College in Cairo, Egypt. The 3,500-seater indoor stadium was packed to capacity and the mood was that of jubilation, excitement and expectancy.

The opening ceremony featured the Egyptian National Anthem, AAU Anthem, the African Olympics Song, parading of the participating nations, Olympics touch relay show, military music band show, percussion show, and sports shows by Physical Education students from Al-Azhar University and Helwan University. Congratulatory speeches were made by the President of the Parliament of International Students, the Secretary General of the All Africa Students Union (Mr Peter Kwasi Kodjie), representative of the Ministry of Youth and Sports in the Arab Republic of Egypt (Dr Amal Gamal), AAU Secretary General (Prof Etienne E. Ehile) and the President of Al-Azhar University (Professor Mohamed El-Mahrasawy). Professor Yousuf Amer the Vice President of Al-Azhar University raised the championship flag whilst the President of Al-Azhar University declared the African Olympics officially launched.

The Olympics will run from the 15-18 March 2019. The sports categories include football, basketball and athletics. The athletics events cover 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, 1500m, 4*100m, triple jump, high Jump, long jump, shot put throw, discus throw and javelin throw. The events are featuring male and female teams / competitors.

The 27 countries that are represented at the maiden event are Algeria, Benin, Burundi, Cameroon, Chad, Comoros, Cote d’Ivoire, Egypt, Eritrea, Gabon, Ghana, Lybia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia

In an interview with Mr Kwesi Acquah Sam who coordinated the logistics from the Association’s side and Prof Amany El-Sharif who coordinated the logistics from Al-Azhar University’s side, they indicated that the benefits of the African Universities Olympics are envisaged to be manifold. Some of the expected positive outcomes include:

Increased cooperation across the African continent among African Youth through the building of networks during and after the Olympics events

Improved self-discipline and self-esteem of the young African people

Promotion of tolerance of diverse cultures and religious affiliations

Promotion of language learning

Improved Physical health

Increased teamwork and problem-solving skills

Reduction of pressure and stress – hopefully reducing cases of drug abuse and depression

The African Universities Olympics enjoys the patronage of the President of the Arab Republic of Egypt, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi who was recently appointed the Chair of the African Union Commission. The African Universities Olympics is a key strategy for promoting the integration of the continent through sports – and this is in-line with the African Union Agenda 2063’s aspiration of “an integrated continent, politically united, based on the ideals of Pan Africanism and the vision of Africa’s Renaissance”.

TITLE: AfriQAN Forum 2023: Advancing Excellence in African Higher Education through Digital Transformation

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The African Quality Assurance Network (AfriQAN) Forum took place at the Serena Hotel in Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania, from 28th to 30th November 2023. Organized by the African Quality Assurance Network and hosted by the Tanzania Commission for Universities, this important event attracted over 100 participants from 18 different countries across Africa and beyond.

Distinguished attendees at the forum included CEOs and representatives of quality assurance agencies, members of quality assurance networks, representatives of quality assurance regional organizations, stakeholders from higher education institutions, lecturers, and representatives of the flagship initiative, the Harmonization of African Higher Education Quality Assurance and Accreditation (HAQAA 3) Initiative.

The Minister of Education, Science, and Technology of Tanzania, Prof. Adolf Mkenda graced the opening ceremony. The forum encompassed a series of technical sessions, which featured keynote presentations and engaging panel discussions. Under the theme “Potentials of Quality Assurance in Advancing Excellence in Higher Education in the Digital Era,” this year’s forum served as a dynamic platform for in-depth discussions and exchange of experiences on pivotal issues, such as online teaching and learning, quality assurance in doctoral education, and research methodologies.

In her address, Prof. Maria Luisa Chicote, President of AfriQAN, warmly welcomed participants, emphasizing the forum’s significance as a collective commitment to fostering academic excellence. She underscored its role in bridging institutional divides, transcending geographical boundaries, and uniting teams under a shared goal—the relentless pursuit of unparalleled quality in higher education.

Prof. Frederick Armah, the Director of Research and Programmes, who represented the Secretary-General of the Association of African Universities, acknowledged the widespread institutional digital transformation across the continent. He underscored the differences in the pace and extent of readiness, integration, and transformation in the various subregions of Africa. Prof. Armah said that higher education institutions and quality assurance agencies are making deliberate efforts to transform their procedures, frameworks, and systems to ensure that their engagements and initiatives resonate with the digital aspirations of 21st century HEIs. He urged AfriQAN to lead transformative initiatives, positioning itself to address the diverse needs of stakeholders within the teaching, research, and innovation ecosystem.

Expressing gratitude, Prof. Adolf Mkenda, Tanzania’s Minister of Education, Science, and Technology, commended the collaborative efforts of the Tanzania Commission for Universities and AfriQAN in coordinating the event. He emphasized the significance of such gatherings and encouraged collaboration within and across African countries to share resources and expertise. While acknowledging progress, he challenged participants to maintain educational quality amidst rising student numbers and expanding universities. The Minister called on the Association of African Universities and other stakeholders to facilitate collaborative initiatives that harness the rich potential within the African continent.

AfriQAN and the forum participants expressed their appreciation to Tanzania for its commitment to higher education and lauded the country for its exceptional hospitality throughout the event. The forum concluded on a note of optimism, setting the stage for continued advancements in African higher education through collaboration, innovation, and digital transformation.

TITLE: Fulcrum Fellowship 2026 | Leadership Fellowship for Community Investment Leaders

The Fulcrum Fellowship 2026 is now accepting applications for a 13-month leadership development programme designed for experienced leaders working to strengthen community investment, capital, policy and practice.

Applications close on October 15, 2026.

About the Fulcrum Fellowship

The Fulcrum Fellowship is designed for established leaders who have significant responsibility within their organisations and are working on challenges where access to capital can contribute to community-level change.

Collaborative problem-solving

Personalised leadership coaching

Systems-thinking exercises

Five multi-day in-person seminars

Monthly virtual coaching sessions

Group learning sessions

Peer networking

Leadership development

Strategies for community investment and capital deployment

The programme is designed to connect fellows with peers who are addressing complementary challenges in different communities and sectors.

CCI’s Capital Absorption Framework

A central component of the Fulcrum Fellowship is the Center for Community Investment’s Capital Absorption Framework.

Fellows use the framework and related systems-thinking tools to better understand how capital moves through communities and how different structures influence the ability of communities to access and use capital.

Through this work, fellows develop strategies for advancing community-defined priorities and addressing systemic barriers that affect opportunity.

In-Person Seminars

April 13–15, 2027

October 26–28, 2027

Fellows can also develop relationships with peers who may continue collaborating beyond the programme.

The Fulcrum Fellowship is designed to help participants strengthen their ability to:

Move capital toward community-defined priorities

Apply systems-thinking approaches to complex challenges

Develop stronger leadership strategies

Reconsider existing approaches to community investment

Work collaboratively across sectors

Build relationships with other leaders

Strengthen organisational capacity

Develop practical strategies for community-level change

Fellows also become part of a network of leaders working to influence the broader community investment ecosystem.

What Organisations Gain

The benefits of the programme extend beyond individual fellows.

Participants can bring new leadership approaches, strategies and relationships back to their organisations.

The programme is intended to help fellows develop sharper strategies, stronger networks and leadership tools that can be applied to their organisations and communities.

The Fulcrum Fellowship is designed for experienced leaders with meaningful authority within their organisations and a strong network of colleagues and partners with whom they can work.

Applicants should demonstrate experience and an established commitment to community-focused work.

Climate resilience

Housing and community development

Creative placemaking

Philanthropy

Finance

Fellows should be open to reconsidering and reframing existing strategies in order to accelerate progress and deepen their impact.

Develop Leadership Self-Awareness

Applicants should be interested in developing greater self-awareness and personal effectiveness as leaders.

October 15, 2026

Through coaching, peer learning, systems thinking and five in-person seminars in Berkeley, California, fellows will have opportunities to strengthen their leadership practice and develop strategies for moving capital toward community-defined priorities.

TITLE: Fulbright-Nehru International Education Administrators Award

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Fulbright-Nehru International Education Administrators Award provides opportunities for U.S. university administrators to attend meetings with representatives of Indian universities, private-sector agencies and organizations and selected government agencies. U.S. administrators will have the opportunity to familiarize themselves with program designs, organizational structures, quality assurance procedures and credit and degree expectations in Indian higher education. Participants will gain first-hand knowledge of a cross-section of Indian institutions and meet with high ranking university administrators and public sector officials who play key roles in the planning and administration of higher education in India. The seminar aims to achieve a balance of topical discussion, knowledge sharing, experiential excursions and exposure to societal/cultural facets of India.

Seminar locations will include highly respected universities and colleges in New Delhi and some other major cities (to be determined) and visits to research institutes and non-governmental organizations that lend themselves as sites for higher education collaborations and exchanges between the U.S. and India.

Number of Awards: Approximately 12

Duration: Two weeks

Award Length and Period

Seminar expected to take place in October/ November 2027, but please note this is tentative and therefore subject to change.

Eligibility: Applicants must have had at least five years of experience in the field. A Ph.D. is not required or expected for this program. Individuals without prior professional connections to India and whose home institutions do not have an established partnership or affiliation with Indian institutions of higher learning will be given priority.

Applicants must be international education administrators (for example, foreign student advisors, study abroad advisors and foreign student admissions) or senior-level university administrators (deans, vice presidents, provosts and presidents) in strategic positions of decision-making with substantial responsibility for enhancing the international dimension of their institutions and who wish to build capacity of their faculty and students by enhancing study abroad (especially to ‘non-traditional’ destinations) and expanding opportunities for international collaborations through faculty exchanges, collaborative research projects or pursuit of innovative curricular design. The award includes round-trip air travel, travel within India, lodging and meals. Grantee spouses and dependents cannot be accommodated during the seminar. OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
