4. PwC Assurance Remote Team Member Programme

The Assurance Remote Team Member, or RTM, programme reflects PwC’s efforts to integrate technology and remote working into the audit and assurance environment.

The programme was established through Remote Team Member Centres in Wuhan and Chengdu to provide high-quality audit services to clients while working remotely with engagement teams.

The RTM model combines traditional audit experience with information technology, standardized processes, flexible resource scheduling, and digital applications.

This approach is designed to improve audit efficiency, process quality, and delivery capacity while supporting PwC’s broader digital transformation.

Key Features of the PwC RTM Programme

1. Flexibility

The remote working model is designed to reduce unnecessary business travel and inefficient overtime.

It also aims to improve audit quality and delivery through flexible resource planning while helping employees achieve a better work-life balance.

2. Team Stability

The RTM model maintains a permanent team of partners.

This allows employees to benefit from ongoing coaching, stronger professional relationships, and greater efficiency through consistent teamwork.

3. Standardisation

The programme integrates audit processes and procedures using a relatively standardized approach.

Standardization is intended to improve audit quality while maintaining the integrity and consistency of audit processes.

4. Digitalisation

Technology plays an important role in RTM.

Participants work with PwC’s digital tools as part of the audit process. These tools are intended to improve audit efficiency and contribute to the transformation of traditional auditing into more technology-enabled and intelligent audit practices.

5. Professional Growth

RTM also provides opportunities for learning and career development.

Senior Associates can take on responsibilities that involve managing and coaching team members, allowing them to strengthen project management and multitasking skills.

Associates are organized by industry, which can give them broader exposure to industry-specific accounting knowledge and practical experience.

6. Diversity of Services

The RTM initiative also aims to expand beyond traditional audit services by drawing on audit experience and industry knowledge to develop more diversified services based on industry research and insights.

5. PwC Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme

The PwC Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme is designed for undergraduate students who want to gain professional experience while completing their university education.

The programme is described as a fast-track opportunity for students interested in building careers in the accounting profession.

Participants receive both formal and on-the-job training similar to PwC graduate recruits. They can also gain exposure to a broad range of projects and work with experienced managers involved in professional development and talent development.

Who Can Apply?

The programme is open to:

Year 2 undergraduate students.

Students studying accounting.

January–May 2028.

These employment periods take place while participants continue completing their four-year undergraduate degrees.

Successful apprentices who meet the required performance standard can have their careers fast-tracked by returning as Year 2 Associates after graduation.

6. PwC Internship Programme

PwC also offers internships for students who want to gain professional experience before graduating.

The internship programme provides an opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals, experience PwC’s organizational culture, explore career interests, and prepare for future professional employment.

The source states that PwC has two internship intakes per year: Summer and Winter, with opportunities available across different lines of service.

The internship can provide students with:

Practical workplace experience.

Exposure to different lines of service.

An opportunity to explore career aspirations.

7. PwC LEAP Programme

The LEAP programme is another early-career opportunity focused on developing future talent.

Rather than being limited to technical professional training, LEAP places emphasis on creativity, relationships, problem-solving, insight, agility, and leadership.

Participants, known as LEAPers, are invited to take part in leadership and business training events and may also have the opportunity to contribute to campus recruitment activities and initiatives that promote the PwC brand.

What Skills Does PwC LEAP Focus On?

The programme highlights several capabilities that are increasingly important in modern professional environments:

Creativity.

Relationship building.

Problem-solving.

Insight.

Agility.

Leadership.

The programme is designed around the idea that professional success requires more than technical knowledge. It also requires the ability to collaborate, adapt, influence, solve problems, and contribute to organizational initiatives.

With several programmes available, students and graduates should select an opportunity based on their current academic status and career objectives.

If You Graduated in 2025, 2026, or 2027

The General Graduate Programme may be relevant because PwC specifically welcomes graduates from these years and accepts applicants with bachelor’s degrees or above from all majors.

The Deals—Edge programme is another option for graduates interested in developing a career in Deals and professional advisory services.

If You Are Studying in the United States or Canada

Why PwC Student and Graduate Opportunities Are Valuable

Early-career opportunities can provide more than a first job. They can help students and graduates build the professional foundation necessary for long-term career development.

PwC’s programmes combine several elements that can be particularly valuable at the beginning of a career.

Application Tips for PwC Student and Graduate Opportunities

1. Select the Correct Programme

Do not apply randomly across programmes. Start by identifying whether you are a graduate, undergraduate student, accounting student, or student studying overseas.

2. Check Your Graduation Year

Graduation year is an important eligibility factor for several programmes.

For example, General Graduate and Deals—Edge specifically identify 2025, 2026, and 2027 graduates, while the internship opportunity identifies graduates of 2028 and beyond.

3. Prepare Your Academic Information

Applicants should have accurate information about their academic achievements and degree history because the application process asks for academic background.

4. Prepare Your Professional Background

Even where extensive professional experience is not required, applicants should prepare information about internships, projects, leadership activities, volunteering, extracurricular activities, and other experiences that demonstrate relevant capabilities.

5. Prepare for Online Assessments

Several of the programmes include an online assessment. Candidates should therefore be prepared to complete assessment stages after submitting their applications.

6. Prepare for Interviews

Some pathways include meetings with PwC, interviews, virtual interviews, or PwC Superday activities. Applicants should be prepared to explain their motivation, academic background, skills, career interests, and reasons for wanting to join PwC.

7. Highlight Transferable Skills

Students and graduates should demonstrate skills such as:

Communication.

Teamwork.

Problem-solving.

Leadership.

Adaptability.

Analytical thinking.

Relationship building.

Digital skills.

Professional curiosity.

These capabilities are particularly relevant because the different programmes emphasize collaboration, leadership, problem-solving, technical development, and professional growth.

PwC Student and Graduate Opportunities 2026: Key Takeaways

PwC provides multiple pathways for students and recent graduates rather than offering a single early-career programme.

The General Graduate Programme is designed for recent graduates and provides structured training, career coaching, and work-buddy support.

The China Sourcing Initiative provides a route for eligible students in the United States and Canada seeking Associate opportunities in Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong SAR, or Macau SAR.

The Deals—Edge programme focuses on developing graduates into future Deals advisers through international development opportunities, rotations, technical learning, professional learning, and potential professional qualifications.

The Assurance Remote Team Member programme combines audit expertise with remote working, standardized processes, digital tools, and professional development.

The Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme provides Year 2 accounting students with an opportunity to gain substantial work experience while completing their degrees.

The PwC Internship Programme enables students to gain workplace exposure before graduation and may provide a pathway toward graduate recruitment for strong performers.

The LEAP programme focuses on future talent development through leadership, creativity, relationships, problem-solving, agility, and business training.

Rather than relying solely on academic qualifications, the programmes provide opportunities to develop practical workplace experience, technical knowledge, leadership capabilities, professional relationships, and industry exposure. TITLE: President of the Association of African Universities participates in the inauguration and investiture of UNISA’s first female Vice Chancellor

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The President of the Association of African Universities (AAU), Professor Bakri Osman Saeed received a kind invitation from Professor Puleng LenkaBula, the new Principal and Vice-Chancellor of the University of South Africa (UNISA), to participate in her inauguration ceremony.

The celebration, which was hosted on Thursday, 2 September 2021 at the UNISA Muckleneuk Campus, was themed ‘Reclaiming Africa’s Intellectual Futures’. It was well attended by stakeholders and high-profile personalities including the university’s patron, Dr. Thabo Mbeki, the former president of the Republic of South Africa. Virtual speeches were also received from the President of the Republic of South Africa and the Minister of Higher Education.

Prof. Bakri Osman Saeed, the President of the AAU addressed the audience virtually on behalf of the Association of African Universities. He congratulated Professor LenkaBula on her remarkable achievement as a first black woman to become a Vice Chancellor in South Africa and the first woman Vice Chancellor for UNISA since its establishment 148 years ago. It is worth noting, that the University of South Africa is a full member of the Association of African Universities. Prof. Saeed outlined the role of the AAU in serving higher education in Africa guided by its strategic plan for the period 2021 – 2025, and the AAU’s commitment to work with all stakeholders towards improving the quality of Africa’s higher education.

The Association of African Universities once again congratulates Prof. Puleng LenkaBula on her appointment, as it falls in line with the AAU’s vision of women and young girls’ equal participation in top leadership positions in academic institutions in Africa.

AAU’s Effort in Promoting Women’s Equal Participation in Leadership

The Association has been undertaking a number of activities to promote and encourage women in academia to aspire to occupying top leadership positions in their institutions, including the following:

Organization of the WoLPHE Conference and other key events focusing on promoting the empowerment of women in academia: The AAU has been organizing its flagship Women in Leadership Positions in Higher Education Conference (WoLPHE) over the years. This event has been hosted in Ghana, Kenya and Nigeria. It is a key platform provided by AAU for the discussion of innovative and creative ways of empowering women, especially young women in higher education to reach their full potential and aspire to the topmost leadership positions in their chosen fields. Aside WoLPHE, the AAU has been hosting other key events focusing on this area, for instance, a high-level panel discussion was hosted during the African Academic Diaspora Home-coming event hosted by the AAU North American Office, in collaboration with the government of Ghana. Again, the AAU has been partnering with other institutions to host gender focused events on March 8th to celebrate the International Women’s Day.

Research and Commissioned Studies: The AAU continues to undertake studies related to the important subject of women in various fields including STEM. For instance, in 2019, the AAU commissioned a study which investigated and evaluated the proximate determinants that influence the participation of women in Science in Africa, titled ‘African Women in STEM – Paradigms and Limitations’. The study and findings can be accessed here https://aau.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Women-in-Science-October-2019-final-2.pdf

The development of a Tool Kit on Mainstreaming Gender in Higher Education in Africa: As far back as 2006, the Working Group on Higher Education (WGHE) of the Association for the Development of Education in Africa (ADEA), which was hosted by the AAU, decided to fund the development of a Toolkit for Mainstreaming Gender in Higher Education in Africa in response to a felt need and to catalyse the Gender Core Program of the Association of African Universities.

Partnerships and continuous engagement with key institutions involved in the promotion of gender in Higher Education in Africa: The AAU has a good working relationship with various organisations across the continent who implement initiatives focused on gender and the promotion of the advancement of women in particular, such as the Forum for African Women Educationist (FAWE), the African Union Centre for Women and Girls Education in Africa (AU/CEIFFA), The Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World (OWSD) among others.

Establishment of the African Women in Higher Education Network (WoHEN): The AAU has recently established this key network, which is focusing on several issues, including addressing unfair practices that affect women from achieving their potential in higher education. This is to be done through advocacy, education, and research programmes. WoHEN, was launched in July 2021, during the AAU’s 15th Quadrennial General Conference of African University Leaders. Interested persons can submit their details via this link to join – http://eepurl.com/hDw5Sv

Continuous advocacy among African Universities to prioritise gender mainstreaming and women empowerment: Being cognizant of gender imbalances in African Higher education, the AAU continuous to advocate for the prioritization of gender mainstreaming, through the various platforms and channels available to the Association.

The AAU wishes Prof. Puleng LenkaBula the very best in her new role and is optimistic that her appointment will inspire confidence in many young women in academia to aspire to the topmost leadership positions in their institutions.

TITLE: AfricaLics PhD Visiting Fellowship Programme (VFP) 2027

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: October 2, 2026

Applications are open for the AfricaLics PhD Visiting Fellowship Programme (VFP) 2027. The AfricaLics VFP aims to support African PhD students working in Innovation and Development by strengthening their academic and research capabilities, improving the quality of their dissertations, and preparing them for careers in academia, the private sector, or government and policymaking.

The AfricaLics VFP does this by increasing the mobility and level of exposure of the selected PhD students to international knowledge and research on innovation and development. The programme forms part of the broader AfricaLics efforts to contribute to the development of a vibrant research community in Africa in this emerging and highly multidisciplinary field.

Benefits

Return flight costs from your nearest international airport (economy class) to Johannesburg and accommodation in Johannesburg will be covered by AfricaLics through the Sida-supported RCS project.

A travel insurance is issued together with the ticket and serves as health insurance during the fellowship period. The medical insurance provided under the travel insurance usually only covers minor ailments that occur during your stay. Successful candidates who have a medical condition, are advised to check if their own health insurance works in South Africa and, if not, ensure they upgrade their insurance in advance of their study visit.

Living costs during the study visit to UJ are normally covered through a stipend amounting to approximately $600 per month. This amount should cover all costs while in Johannesburg related to living expenses and travel around Johannesburg including to and from UJ campus.

Costs for participation in joint courses and mentorship fees will be covered by AfricaLics. A small amount of funds is also available for students to participate in a short-course that is deemed important for their PhD studies and not normally available in their home country.

The AfricaLics RCS project will also cover costs related to the two face-to-face meetings between students, home supervisors and mentors.

If AfricaLics agrees to fund the three-month study visit to Johannesburg, the scholarship will only cover costs related to the student’s visit. Any costs related to accompanying spouses, children, or others will not be covered. The scholarship does not cover the costs of any additional travel in South Africa that the student may wish to undertake unless as part of selected and approved VFP activities.

Eligibility

Applicants for the AfricaLics PhD visiting fellowship programme should:

Be working actively on a subject relevant to innovation and development.

Be enrolled as a PhD student at a university in Africa.

Have preferably completed their first year of studies by December 2026

Have a background (BSc, MSc etc.) in Economics, Sociology, Political Science, Science and Technology Policy, Geography, History or Development Studies. Applicants may also work within the STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) subjects or even manufacturing, but from a social science perspective.

Possess adequate literacy in English (documentation may be requested).

Selection Criteria

The students are selected through a rigorous assessment process using the following criteria:

Focus and relevance: The application should demonstrate clear relevance to Innovation and Development studies in Africa and to the emerging AfricaLics research agenda. Applicants should provide a clear justification for their research and specify their research questions.

A well-elaborated explanation of the theoretical and conceptual framework rooted in innovation and development studies and with a clear explanation on how this framework relates to the research questions.

Methodological clarity and rigor (application shows intention to address all research questions with adequate methods; data sources and data collection methods are clearly explained and relevant for the research).

Application

Submit a brief application of one page/500 words explaining your background, motivation for applying and expected outcomes of participation in the AfricaLics PhD visiting fellowship programme.

The following documents must be submitted with the application:

Brief outline of current PhD project, including PhD training plans (max. 5 pages)

Curriculum Vitae – CV (including PhD courses attended so far)

Letter of support from the main PhD supervisor confirming that the PhD student will have completed her/his upgrade/probation by the end of December 2025 OR reasons why the student is deemed suitable for inclusion in the fellowship programme if this is not the case.

Letter of support from the University Administration at the university where the PhD student is enrolled

Copies of academic certificates (copies of Bachelor and Master Certificates as a minimum)

One writing sample (article or chapter) from current PhD program

Applicants are NOT expected to submit a copy of their passport when applying for the PhD visiting fellowship programme. Successful candidates will be asked to handle any visa issues that may be relevant with support from the AfricaLics Secretariat and UJ. Collection of personal data will be kept to a minimum, and information received will be stored safely and will not be used for any other purposes.

TITLE: Global Equity in Open Access Publishing- Workshop Series on Practical Mechanisms & Action Plans to Remove Barriers for Readers & Authors

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Viewpoints and contributions from Africa and Europe

Authors, globally, publish a large proportion of their research articles in scholarly journals that charge fees for open access. With fee-based open access publishing growing rapidly, there is increasing concern around equity.

It is important to identify the financial barriers that authors encounter and hear the challenges they face, particularly in resource-limited contexts, in order to develop actionable plans and practical mechanisms that ensure no author is limited in their opportunity to publish their accepted articles via open access in the journals of their choice. For example:

How can discounts and waiver programs be adjusted to enable more equitable access to open access publishing for authors, as a short-term strategy?

What actions could foster open access publishing fees that are differentiated globally?

What can funders, ministries and research administrators do to understand just how much money they are directing, collectively, to scholarly publishing? How can the global community assess the distribution of such funds and their impact, particularly for researchers in different resource contexts?

This workshop will be an opportunity for those who fund and produce research, including scientists and scholars, research administrators, libraries and library consortia, university leadership, science councils and grant funders, and ministries of research and education, to better understand the current tensions in the scholarly communication landscape and explore immediate and long-term actions they each can take to ensure open access publishing is delivered in accordance with these principles:

Fees associated with open access publishing services should be fair, reasonable, transparent, and globally equitable;

Scholarly communication is part of the research process and, as such, costs for open access publishing services should ultimately be borne by research funders and institutions;

Spending on scientific publishing should enable global open access by both readers and authors.

The first in a global relay, this workshop will be held in European and African time zones. The outcomes will be integrated with those of two additional and incremental workshops in early 2023 featuring viewpoints and contributions from the Asia-Pacific region and the Americas, with the aim of defining and promoting global practices and action lines in pursuit of the principles above.

Setting and timing

The 2-part workshop will be held online via Zoom and will include both plenary sessions and breakout discussions supported with virtual collaboration tools.

Date: November 21 and 22, 2022

Time: UTC 09:00 – 12:00 (UTC-1 08:00 to 11:00 / UTC+4 13:00 – 16:00)

Participation

This edition of the workshop series is dedicated to those who fund and produce research in the many regions of Africa and Europe. We welcome participation from a broad range of stakeholders, including scientists and scholars, research administrators, libraries and library consortia, university leadership, science councils, grant funders and ministries of research and education.

TITLE: Freedom Prize 2027 International Jury: Apply to Join a Global Youth Jury in Normandy, France

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Freedom Prize 2027 International Jury is inviting young people from France and around the world to apply for the opportunity to become one of 24 young international jury members responsible for identifying three individuals or organisations whose work represents an outstanding fight for freedom.

Open to young people aged 15 to 25, this unique youth participation opportunity offers applicants the chance to contribute to an international selection process, examine issues surrounding freedom and human rights, exchange perspectives with young people from different backgrounds, and participate in deliberations in Normandy, France.

The opportunity is particularly suitable for young people who are passionate about freedom, human rights, justice, peace, equality, civic engagement, advocacy, social change, and global issues.

Importantly, applicants do not need to have served on a jury before or possess a particular academic or professional background. The organisers state that the jury is open to both experienced and novice candidates and that particular attention will be given to applicants’ motivation and the diversity of profiles represented on the jury.

Applications for the international jury are open from June 4 to September 30, 2026.

What Is the Freedom Prize?

The Freedom Prize is an initiative that gives young people aged 15 to 25 the opportunity to identify and support inspiring individuals or organisations involved in exemplary struggles for freedom.

The programme is built around three major stages:

The “Our Freedom Prize 2027” call for proposals

The international jury deliberations

The international online vote to select the laureate

The international jury plays a particularly important role because its 24 members will review proposals submitted through the Freedom Prize nomination process and collectively select three nominees.

Young people worldwide will then have the opportunity to vote online for one of these three nominees.

The eventual laureate will receive an endowment of €25,000 to support their ongoing fight for freedom.

Apply to Become a Member of the Freedom Prize 2027 International Jury

The international jury will consist of 24 young people between the ages of 15 and 25.

The organisers aim to make the jury representative of international youth and reflective of different cultural, geographical, and generational perspectives.

The jury will include young people representing three broad geographical levels:

Normandy

Other regions of France

Other countries around the world

This international composition is intended to bring different experiences, viewpoints, cultures, and understandings of freedom into the deliberations.

As a result, applicants from countries outside France are strongly relevant to the international dimension of the programme.

What Will International Jury Members Do?

Being selected for the Freedom Prize international jury is more than simply attending an event in France.

Jury members will actively participate in a structured process involving research, analysis, discussion, argumentation, individual reflection, and collaborative decision-making.

During the deliberations, members will examine proposals submitted through the “Our Freedom Prize 2027” call for nominations.

These proposals will identify individuals or organisations involved in significant struggles for freedom.

The jury’s responsibility will be to carefully consider these proposals and determine which fights are particularly representative of the concerns and aspirations of young people in relation to freedom in 2027.

Key responsibilities include:

Studying proposals submitted through the Freedom Prize call for nominations

Researching the individuals and organisations presented in the proposals

Analysing the different causes and struggles represented

Reflecting individually on the proposals

Participating in collaborative discussions

Presenting and defending arguments

Comparing different perspectives and points of view

Developing shared criteria for evaluating the different proposals

Participating in the final selection of three nominees

At the end of the deliberation process, the 24 jury members will collectively select three individuals or organisations whose fight they consider particularly representative of a fight for freedom in 2027.

These three nominees will then proceed to the public voting stage.

Three Key Stages of the Freedom Prize 2027

The Freedom Prize 2027 is structured around three major phases.

1. “Our Freedom Prize 2027” Call for Proposals

The first stage invites young people aged 15 to 25 from France and around the world to nominate an inspiring individual or organisation committed to a fight for freedom.

Applicants use an online form to present their nominee and explain why the person or organisation deserves recognition.

According to the opportunity information, the call for nominations will remain open until January 12, 2027.

For applicants to the international jury, completing this nomination form is a requirement. The form becomes available from September 1, 2026, and it can be submitted after the jury application if necessary.

This means prospective jury members should ensure that they complete the additional nomination requirement even if they initially submit their jury application before the nomination form becomes available.

2. International Jury Deliberations

The second stage involves the 24-member international jury meeting in Normandy.

The formal deliberation period is scheduled for February 15–19, 2027, while the broader jury stay in Normandy is scheduled for Sunday, February 14 through Saturday, February 20, 2027.

Applicants should therefore plan to be available for the entire February 14–20 period, rather than only the formal deliberation dates.

During this stage, jury members will meet, prepare for their responsibilities, study the proposals, exchange ideas, and ultimately select the three nominees for the Freedom Prize 2027.

The deliberations are facilitated by the International Institute for Human Rights and Peace.

A Chairperson will also participate in the process, helping guide the reflections and sharing their own testimony concerning freedom and commitment.

3. Online Vote for the Freedom Prize 2027

After the international jury selects three nominees, the process moves to an international online voting stage.

The voting period is scheduled for March 22 to April 30, 2027.

Young people aged 15 to 25 from around the world will be able to vote for their preferred nominee from the three individuals or organisations selected by the international jury.

The nominee receiving the winning support will become the Freedom Prize 2027 laureate.

The laureate will receive an endowment of €25,000 intended to support their ongoing fight for freedom.

The award ceremony is scheduled to take place in Caen, France, in June 2027.

International Jury Meeting in Normandy, France

One of the most significant aspects of this opportunity is the opportunity for selected jury members to meet physically in Normandy.

The international panel will meet in Normandy from Sunday, February 14 to Saturday, February 20, 2027.

Applicants must confirm that they are available during these dates before submitting their application.

The stay will allow jury members to:

Meet other young people from different backgrounds

Prepare for their responsibilities

Participate in the jury deliberations

Discuss different perspectives on freedom

Conduct research and analysis

Exchange ideas and arguments

Work collectively toward the selection of the three nominees

This makes the programme both a decision-making opportunity and an international youth exchange experience.

Travel, Accommodation, Food and Visa Costs Covered

Selected jury members will not be expected to personally finance the main costs associated with attending the February meeting in Normandy.

According to the opportunity information, the organisers will cover:

Transportation

Accommodation

Catering

Visa costs

This is an important benefit for international applicants, particularly those travelling from outside France.

Applicants should carefully follow any instructions provided by the organisers concerning travel arrangements, visa documentation, and other logistical requirements after selection.

Eligibility Requirements for the Freedom Prize 2027 Jury

Applicants should carefully review the eligibility conditions before applying.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be between 15 and 25 years old on February 19, 2027.

This is an essential requirement.

Being within the age range when applying is not enough if the applicant will no longer meet the age requirement on February 19, 2027.

Prospective applicants should therefore calculate their age on the specified date before submitting the application.

Worldwide Eligibility

The opportunity is open to young people from around the world.

The jury is deliberately designed to include young people representing different geographical areas, cultures, and generations.

The programme specifically refers to participation from:

Normandy

Other parts of France

Other countries around the world

Therefore, the opportunity is not restricted to applicants living in France.

Young people from African countries, Asian countries, European countries, countries in North and South America, Oceania, and other parts of the world can potentially apply, provided they satisfy the other eligibility requirements.

Language Requirements

Applicants must be able to express themselves orally and in writing in either French or English.

Applicants can choose either language.

No other language will be used for exchanges with the organisers or during the jury deliberations.

Therefore, applicants should be comfortable communicating, discussing ideas, presenting arguments, and participating in group conversations in either English or French.

Applicants do not need to demonstrate proficiency in both languages if they can adequately communicate in one of the two accepted languages.

No Specific Academic or Professional Background Required

One of the most inclusive aspects of the opportunity is that there is no requirement for a specific educational or professional background.

The jury welcomes candidates with different experiences and profiles.

You do not necessarily need to be:

A university student

A human rights professional

An activist

A researcher

A lawyer

A political science student

A journalist

A member of an organisation

An experienced youth leader

The organisers explicitly state that the jury is open to experienced and novice candidates.

This means that someone without previous experience in a similar programme can still apply.

The emphasis is instead placed on the applicant’s motivation and the overall diversity of the jury.

Previous Freedom Prize Jury Members Cannot Reapply

There is one specific restriction concerning previous participation.

A person who has already been a member of the Freedom Prize jury in a previous edition cannot stand for the jury again.

This condition is designed to help provide opportunities to new young people and maintain diversity among jury members.

Mandatory “Our Freedom Prize 2027” Nomination

Applicants for the international jury must also complete the “Our Freedom Prize 2027” call for nominations form.

The nomination involves proposing an individual or organisation that is engaged in a fight for freedom.

Importantly, the nomination form will be available from September 1, 2026.

The organisers indicate that the nomination form can be completed even if it is submitted after the jury application.

Applicants should therefore make sure they do not overlook this additional requirement.

A strong nomination should clearly identify the person or organisation being proposed and explain the importance and impact of their work in relation to freedom.

How Are International Jury Members Selected?

Selection is conducted by the organisers of the Freedom Prize.

The information provided in the application form will be considered when determining who is selected.

The organisers are particularly interested in ensuring diversity of profiles within the international jury.

This includes diversity in areas such as:

Geography

Culture

Generation

Experience

Personal background

Perspectives and viewpoints

The programme does not require applicants to have participated in similar initiatives before.

Instead, motivation is given particular attention.

The organisers may also conduct telephone interviews with applicants before making the final selection.

Applicants should therefore provide thoughtful and genuine responses throughout the application form and be prepared to discuss their motivation if contacted.

What Makes a Strong Applicant?

Although the organisers do not require a particular educational or professional background, applicants should demonstrate genuine interest in the purpose of the Freedom Prize.

A strong application could communicate:

Why freedom matters to you

Your understanding of freedom and human rights

Your interest in social or civic issues

Your ability to listen to perspectives different from your own

Your willingness to engage in constructive debate

Your ability to analyse information critically

Your interest in learning from other young people

Your ability to work collaboratively

Your motivation for joining the international jury

What perspective or experience you could contribute to a diverse international jury

Applicants should avoid presenting themselves simply as people looking for an opportunity to travel to France.

The jury has an important responsibility, so the application should demonstrate a genuine understanding of the role and its purpose.

Preparatory Work Before Travelling to France

Being selected does not mean that jury members can simply wait until February to participate.

Before travelling to Caen and Normandy, each international jury member agrees to:

Participate in preparatory video conferences

Complete preparation work remotely

Familiarise themselves with the jury’s responsibilities

Prepare for the deliberation process

Applicants should therefore be able to commit time to the programme before the physical meeting in February 2027.

This remote preparation is an important part of the overall experience.

Application Process

The application is structured into several sections.

Applicants are asked to complete the following stages:

Presentation

Contact details

Languages

Application

Resume/CV

The application form allows candidates to choose between English and French.

Applicants should carefully complete each section and ensure that the information supplied is accurate and consistent.

A resume/CV must be attached at the end of the application.

Because motivation is an important consideration in the selection process, applicants should give serious attention to their written responses rather than treating the application as a simple registration form.

What Should You Prepare Before Applying?

Prospective applicants can prepare the following materials and information in advance.

1. An Updated CV

Your CV should clearly present relevant aspects of your background, interests, education, work, volunteering, leadership, community activities, projects, advocacy, or other experiences.

Because there is no required professional background, applicants should not assume that they need an extensive CV.

2. Your Motivation

Think carefully about why you want to become a member of the Freedom Prize international jury.

Consider:

Why are you interested in freedom?

Why do you want to participate in the selection process?

What perspectives can you contribute?

How do you approach disagreement?

What would you like to learn from other young people?

Why is international youth participation important?

3. Language Ability

Choose the language in which you can communicate most confidently: English or French.

4. Availability

Make sure you can commit to the required preparatory activities and the February 2027 stay in Normandy.

5. Your Freedom Prize Nomination

From September 1, 2026, make sure you complete the required “Our Freedom Prize 2027” nomination form.

Important Dates for the Freedom Prize 2027

The following dates are important for applicants:

International jury applications open: June 4, 2026

“Our Freedom Prize 2027” nomination form available: September 1, 2026

International jury application deadline: September 30, 2026

Nomination call deadline: January 12, 2027

Jury stay in Normandy: February 14–20, 2027

Formal jury deliberations: February 15–19, 2027

Online Freedom Prize vote: March 22–April 30, 2027

Freedom Prize award ceremony: June 2027

Freedom Prize 2027 Jury Application Deadline

The application must be validated online no later than Wednesday, September 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Paris time, France.

Applications or confirmations submitted after the deadline will not be considered.

Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their forms.

Because the deadline is expressed in Paris time, international applicants should account for the time difference between France and their country when submitting their application.

What Happens After You Apply?

The organisers will assess applications based on the information provided.

The selection process is intended to create a diverse international jury rather than simply select applicants according to a single academic or professional criterion.

Some applicants may also be contacted for a telephone interview before the final selection.

Successful candidates will then participate in the preparatory activities and ultimately travel to Normandy for the February 2027 jury meeting.

Data Protection and Privacy

The application form also contains important information concerning the processing of applicants’ personal data.

The data collected is processed by the Normandy Region to assist with the organisation of the Freedom Prize.

The information may be shared with the organisers of the event and will be stored for ten years after the event.

Applicants are informed of their rights under the European data protection framework and French data protection legislation.

These rights include the ability to:

Access personal information

Request correction of personal information

Request deletion of personal information

Object to the processing of personal information

For matters relating to data protection, applicants can contact the Data Protection Officer at dpo@normandie.fr.

Applicants should also review the applicable rules and data-processing information before submitting the form.

Questions and Application Support

Applicants who experience difficulties completing the application or who have questions about participation can contact the Freedom Prize organisers.

The contact email provided for enquiries is:

prixliberte@normandie.fr

A text version of the application form is also available upon request for applicants who require it.

Why Young People Should Consider Applying

The Freedom Prize international jury offers young people an opportunity to take part in a meaningful international decision-making process.

Rather than simply attending a conference, jury members will have a direct role in evaluating proposals and identifying the three candidates who will proceed to the final public vote.

The experience can provide exposure to:

International youth participation

Human rights and freedom issues

Research and analysis

Argumentation

Collaborative decision-making

Cross-cultural dialogue

Public-interest advocacy

Leadership and civic engagement

International networking

Critical thinking

Group deliberation

For young people interested in international development, human rights, diplomacy, public policy, social change, advocacy, journalism, law, politics, peacebuilding, or community leadership, the experience may also provide valuable personal and professional development.

A Unique International Youth Experience

The international jury is designed around the idea that young people should have a meaningful role in determining which freedom-related struggles deserve international recognition.

The programme brings together 24 young people from different geographical and cultural backgrounds and gives them a shared responsibility.

Rather than requiring everyone to have identical experiences or opinions, the organisers are looking for diversity.

This makes the ability to listen, analyse, discuss, question assumptions, and work with people who have different perspectives particularly important.

The jury members will collectively determine which three causes are most representative of a fight for freedom in 2027.

Their decision will then shape the final stage of the Freedom Prize.

Official Application and Further Information

Applicants should review the official Freedom Prize information and rules before submitting their application.

Official website: https://prixliberte.normandie.fr/en

Applicants should ensure that they understand all participation requirements, particularly the age requirement, language requirement, February availability, previous-jury restriction, CV requirement, and mandatory “Our Freedom Prize 2027” nomination.

More global opportunities visit OFY Website HERE

Conclusion

The Freedom Prize 2027 International Jury offers young people aged 15 to 25 from around the world an opportunity to take an active role in an international process focused on freedom, human rights, commitment, and social change.

The selected jury will consist of 24 young people, bringing together different geographical, cultural, and generational perspectives. Members will study nominations, conduct research and analysis, exchange arguments, compare viewpoints, and collectively select three individuals or organisations whose fight for freedom they believe is particularly representative of young people’s concerns in 2027.

The opportunity does not require a specific degree, profession, or previous jury experience. Instead, the organisers place particular importance on applicants’ motivation and the diversity of profiles represented in the jury.

Selected members will participate in preparatory activities before travelling to Normandy, where they will take part in the February 2027 programme. Transportation, accommodation, catering, and visa costs will be covered by the organisers, making the opportunity accessible to selected participants from different parts of the world.

If you are between 15 and 25 on February 19, 2027, can communicate confidently in English or French, are interested in freedom and social issues, and are prepared to contribute thoughtfully to an international youth jury, this could be a valuable opportunity to consider.

Application deadline: Wednesday, September 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Paris time, France.

Applicants should submit their applications well before the deadline and remember to complete the required “Our Freedom Prize 2027” nomination form, which becomes available on September 1, 2026.

TITLE: Redefining Higher Education in Africa – AAU Secretary General calls for urgent actions as he addresses the QS Forum in Morocco

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Secretary General of the Association of African Universities (AAU), Prof. Olusola Bandele Oyewole, participated in the inaugural edition of the QS Africa Forum, held at the Rabat – Morocco’s Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) in Morocco, from September 1-2, 2022. The event was organized in partnership with Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), a British firm behind one of the world’s higher education ranking mechanisms.

The Forum created the platform for stakeholders to discuss solutions towards addressing the myriad of challenges facing higher education in Africa, the continent’s potential in the sector, and its achievements thus far. While underscoring the many challenges confronting Africa’s higher education in its quest to advance knowledge and contribute to addressing the continent’s critical developmental needs, speakers at the event exuded a sense of optimism for the future and a clear understanding of the steps and initiatives to take to reach the desired endgame – the Africa We Want.

Making a presentation at the forum in Morocco, Prof. Olusola Oyewole, the Secretary General of the Association of African Universities stressed the urgent need to redefine Africa’s higher education system, stating that Africa’s current education system remains fashioned or programmed after colonial legacies which is more teacher-centered, bringing about more downsides than benefits.

Prof. Oyewole put the spotlight on the current state of education in Africa – as regards the low percentage of global research undertaken by the continent, the low uptake of research outputs, low skill and competence of learners, and little to no collaboration between universities and industries. He also spoke on the major challenges facing higher education in Africa which included funding, quality, relevance and employability of graduates, among others, while prescribing possible solutions to overcoming these hurdles .

Prof. Oyewole called for collaboration, networking, and inter-regional cooperation among universities in Africa which will in turn promote excellence, digitalization, lifelong learning, and the increase in access to education through distance education. He also spoke about some strategies to implement at the institutional and continental levels which include re-defining the curricula in African institutions to ensure it has a special focus on skills acquisition and entrepreneurship, promotion of industry-academia linkages, a renewed focus on research, and research focused on addressing local challenges, among others.

Focusing on the African Research, Innovation and Development Network (AfRID Network) anchored by the AAU and to be inaugurated soon, Prof. Oyewole mentioned that quality research is an essential tool for driving Africa’s development. According to him, for research to be relevant, it must lead to innovation and have scientific and societal value.

Other speakers at the event included – Amr. Adly, president of Egypt Japan University of Science & Technology, Amine Bensaid, President of Morocco’s Al Akhawayn University (AUI) and the QS Chief Commercial Officer Jason Newman.

Article Written By: Ms. Naomi Darko, AAU Communications Services

TITLE: Press Release: First Pan African Heritage World Conference  to be held in August, 2021

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Pan African Heritage World, and its partners will be hosting the first Pan African Heritage World Conference from August 5-7, 2021. The event has adopted a hybrid format and will take place both online (virtually) and onsite at the premises of the Association of African Universities in Accra, Ghana.

The Minister of Education of the Republic of Ghana, Dr. Yaw O. Adutwum, will deliver the keynote address at the Conference on the theme – ‘ Building Bridges among Africans worldwide through Scholarship, Culture, Technology and Innovation’. Participants at the conference will include Pan African visionaries and innovators, scholars and educators, religious and spiritual leaders, entrepreneurs, activists, technologists and Pan African student organizations and institutions from around the world.

Among the many speakers at the conference are Professor Molefi Kete Asante of Temple University, USA, Dr Runoko Rashidi, historian and public lecturer, and Professor Maulana Karenga, professor of African Studies and founder of the Kwanzaa Festival. Others include Emeritus Professor Kofi Asare Opoku of Ghana, Emeritus Prof Rupert Lewis of Jamaica, Emeritus Professor Iva Carruthers of California, Mr. Onyekachi Wambu of AFFORD-UK, and Dr Aurola Vergara-Figueroa of Colombia. Professor Toyin Falola of University of Texas at Austin, and Dr. Sheila Walker, Cultural Anthropologist, USA, will also be speaking at the conference. Interested participants are invited to visit events.pahw.org to register for the conference.

The Conference follows the groundbreaking sod cutting which commenced the construction of the Pan African Heritage World Museum to be completed in December 2022 and commissioned in Ghana in July 2023. The Heritage Museum complex will provide the opportunity to unlearn and relearn the history, culture, ideals and civilization of Africa from mankind’s creation till the present. The first living museum of its kind in Africa, the complex includes the Pan African Heroes Park, the Palaces of African Kingdoms, the African Herbal Plant Village and a host of experiential programmes and activities.

The Museum project is endorsed by the African Union Commission, the Association of African Universities, UNESCO, the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP), and other international organizations.
