TITLE: Global Advocacy Champions 2026–2027: WAGGGS Leadership and Advocacy Programme for Young Women

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the World Association of Girl Guides and Girl Scouts (WAGGGS) Global Advocacy Champions 2026–2027 programme, a global leadership and advocacy opportunity designed to equip young Girl Guides and Girl Scouts with the knowledge, skills and networks needed to influence change.

The programme provides young women with an opportunity to strengthen their advocacy capabilities, promote gender equality and represent the voices of girls and young women at local, national and international levels.

Selected participants will become part of a global network of young women working to influence change. Through the programme, Champions will have opportunities to participate in advocacy activities, support their WAGGGS Member Organisations, develop and lead projects in their communities, and engage in international spaces.

The 2026–2027 cohort will also include young women participating in the Girl-led Action on Climate Change programme, creating an additional connection between youth leadership, advocacy and climate action.

Application deadline: 30 September 2026.

About the Global Advocacy Champions Programme

The Global Advocacy Champions programme is an initiative of WAGGGS that was launched in 2018.

The programme is designed around the idea that young women and girls should have meaningful opportunities to participate in conversations and decisions affecting their lives and communities.

Rather than focusing only on learning advocacy concepts in a classroom environment, the Global Advocacy Champions programme combines skills development, practical advocacy, networking and opportunities to engage in international spaces.

According to WAGGGS, the programme enables participants to:

Strengthen their advocacy skills.

Champion gender equality.

Represent the voices of girls and young women.

Participate in advocacy at local, national and international levels.

Engage in global advocacy opportunities.

Support their WAGGGS Member Organisations.

Lead projects in their communities.

Build relationships with other young women working for change.

Develop communication and public-speaking capabilities.

Engage with WAGGGS priority issues.

This combination of leadership development and practical advocacy makes the programme particularly relevant to young women who want to move beyond simply participating in youth initiatives and develop the capacity to influence policies, institutions and communities.

What Is WAGGGS?

The World Association of Girl Guides and Girl Scouts (WAGGGS) is a global organisation representing Girl Guides and Girl Scouts around the world.

Its work focuses on supporting girls and young women to develop the skills, confidence and opportunities necessary to become active citizens and leaders.

The Global Advocacy Champions programme forms part of this wider approach by creating opportunities for young women within the Girl Guiding and Girl Scouting movement to develop advocacy skills and engage with issues that affect girls, young women and their communities.

For applicants, this means the Global Advocacy Champions programme is not simply a general youth leadership programme. It is connected specifically to the international Girl Guiding and Girl Scouting movement and provides participants with opportunities to contribute to advocacy through that network.

What Is the Global Advocacy Champions 2026–2027 Programme?

The Global Advocacy Champions 2026–2027 network brings together young women who are interested in advocacy, leadership and gender equality.

Selected Champions will form part of a global network and will be expected to use the knowledge, skills and opportunities gained through the programme to contribute to advocacy in their own contexts.

The programme is designed to create a link between three levels of engagement:

Community-level action

National-level advocacy

International advocacy

This structure gives participants opportunities to connect their experiences in their communities with wider conversations taking place nationally and internationally.

Who Are Global Advocacy Champions?

Global Advocacy Champions are young Girl Guides and Girl Scouts who are selected to participate in WAGGGS’ global advocacy network.

They are expected to contribute to advocacy efforts while also developing their own leadership and communication skills.

The programme is intended for young women who want to:

Speak up on issues affecting girls and young women.

Promote gender equality.

Develop stronger advocacy strategies.

Communicate effectively with different audiences.

Participate in policy and international discussions.

Support advocacy work within their Member Organisations.

Develop initiatives within their communities.

Connect with other young women around the world.

The programme therefore places participants in both a learning and action-oriented environment.

Main Focus of the Global Advocacy Champions Programme

Advocacy Skills

A central purpose of the programme is to strengthen participants’ ability to advocate effectively.

Advocacy involves more than raising awareness. It can include communicating evidence, engaging decision-makers, building public support, developing messages, forming partnerships and encouraging changes in policies or practices.

Through the Global Advocacy Champions programme, participants will receive opportunities to develop their understanding and practical ability in advocacy.

Gender Equality

Gender equality is another major focus.

Participants will be equipped to champion issues affecting girls and young women and to contribute to efforts aimed at creating more equitable opportunities and outcomes.

This can involve representing girls’ voices, engaging communities, supporting campaigns and participating in discussions around policies and programmes affecting young women.

Communication

Effective advocacy depends heavily on communication.

The programme includes development opportunities in communications, helping participants improve their ability to communicate ideas, advocacy messages and priorities to different audiences.

This can be particularly useful for young women who are involved in campaigns, youth organisations, community initiatives or public-facing leadership roles.

Public Speaking

Public speaking is specifically identified by WAGGGS as one of the areas covered through training and development opportunities.

Participants may therefore have opportunities to strengthen their confidence and effectiveness when speaking before groups, organisations, policymakers and other stakeholders.

WAGGGS Priority Issues

The Global Advocacy Champions will also receive development opportunities related to WAGGGS’ priority issues.

This allows participants to connect their advocacy work with broader areas of concern within the global Girl Guiding and Girl Scouting movement.

Benefits of Becoming a Global Advocacy Champion

The programme offers several forms of professional, leadership and advocacy development.

1. Advocacy Training

Selected Champions will receive training designed to strengthen their advocacy knowledge and skills.

This can help participants better understand how to identify issues, develop advocacy objectives, communicate effectively and engage relevant stakeholders.

2. Communications Development

Participants will have opportunities to improve their communication abilities.

Effective communication is essential for advocacy because Champions may need to communicate with communities, organisations, decision-makers, media audiences and international stakeholders.

3. Public Speaking Development

The programme includes public-speaking development.

This can help participants become more confident when presenting ideas, representing organisations and speaking about issues affecting girls and young women.

4. International Advocacy Opportunities

One of the notable features of the programme is the opportunity to engage in international advocacy spaces.

WAGGGS specifically highlights opportunities for Champions to engage in global spaces such as the United Nations Commission on the Status of Women.

This can provide exposure to international discussions surrounding gender equality and related issues.

5. Global Networking

Selected Champions will join a global network of young women working to influence change.

Being part of such a network can allow participants to:

Exchange experiences.

Learn from advocates in different countries.

Build professional and advocacy relationships.

Identify opportunities for collaboration.

Share approaches to addressing common challenges.

Develop international solidarity around issues affecting girls and young women.

6. Supporting Member Organisations

Champions will have opportunities to support their WAGGGS Member Organisations.

This creates a connection between individual leadership development and the wider work of the Girl Guiding and Girl Scouting movement.

Participants can potentially apply their advocacy knowledge within their national or local organisational contexts.

7. Leading Community Projects

The programme also provides opportunities for Champions to lead projects in their own communities.

This is an important practical element because it allows participants to translate learning and advocacy skills into action.

Community projects can provide opportunities to identify local challenges, engage stakeholders and develop responses based on the needs of girls and young women.

8. Leadership Development

Through training, networking, advocacy and practical project work, participants can strengthen their leadership capabilities.

The programme is particularly relevant to young women interested in developing themselves as advocates and community leaders.

Participation in the UN Commission on the Status of Women

WAGGGS specifically identifies the UN Commission on the Status of Women (CSW) as an example of a global space where Champions may have opportunities to engage.

The Commission on the Status of Women is an important international forum focused on gender equality and the advancement of women and girls.

For a young advocate, exposure to such a space can provide insight into how international policy discussions take place and how civil society and youth voices can contribute to those conversations.

Participation in an international advocacy space can also help Champions understand how local concerns can be connected to national and global policy discussions.

Applicants should, however, distinguish between an opportunity to engage in such spaces and a guarantee of attendance at every international event. The WAGGGS announcement describes these as opportunities available to Champions rather than guaranteeing participation for every individual.

Global Advocacy Champions and Climate Action

The 2026–2027 cohort will also include young women participating in the Girl-led Action on Climate Change programme.

This creates an additional dimension to the cohort by connecting youth-led climate action with the wider Global Advocacy Champions network.

Climate change increasingly affects communities, livelihoods, education, health and the wellbeing of children and young people.

Including young women involved in girl-led climate action can therefore help strengthen connections between advocacy, gender equality and environmental issues.

For applicants interested in climate advocacy, this aspect of the 2026–2027 cohort may provide an opportunity to connect their interests with wider youth leadership and advocacy work.

Who Can Apply for the Global Advocacy Champions Programme?

The WAGGGS announcement states that the programme is for Girl Guides and Girl Scouts aged 18–30.

The opportunity is therefore targeted at young women within the Girl Guiding and Girl Scouting movement who are interested in developing their advocacy and leadership abilities.

The key eligibility information explicitly provided in the announcement is:

You must be a Girl Guide or Girl Scout.

You must be between 18 and 30 years old.

You should be interested in advocacy and influencing change.

You should be willing to represent the voices of girls and young women.

You should be interested in gender equality and relevant WAGGGS priority issues.

You should be prepared to engage in a global network of young women.

You should be willing to support advocacy work and potentially lead projects in your community.

The full Terms of Reference should be reviewed for additional eligibility requirements, responsibilities, time commitments and the Member Organisation endorsement process.

Geographic Eligibility

The programme is presented by WAGGGS as a global network.

The announcement does not identify a specific continent or list of countries from which applicants can apply. Instead, it refers broadly to Girl Guides and Girl Scouts participating in the WAGGGS movement.

Therefore, applicants should not assume that the programme is restricted to Europe, Africa, Asia, the Americas, the Pacific or another particular region based solely on the announcement.

The precise country and organisational eligibility requirements should be confirmed through the Official Terms of Reference and the relevant WAGGGS Member Organisation endorsement process.

Member Organisation Endorsement

An important element of the application process is the Member Organisation endorsement process.

WAGGGS specifically directs applicants to read the Terms of Reference for information about this process.

This is important because applicants should not treat the programme as a completely independent individual application where organisational endorsement is irrelevant.

Prospective applicants should therefore review the requirements early and determine:

Whether they are connected to an eligible WAGGGS Member Organisation.

What endorsement is required.

Who within their organisation is authorised to provide or confirm the endorsement.

Whether there are internal deadlines before the global application deadline.

What supporting information their Member Organisation may require.

Starting this process early can help applicants avoid delays close to the application deadline.

What Kind of Candidate Is This Programme Looking For?

Although the announcement does not provide a detailed candidate profile beyond the stated eligibility, the programme’s structure provides a clear indication of the type of interests that are relevant.

Applicants may find the programme particularly relevant if they have experience or interests in areas such as:

Youth advocacy

Gender equality

Girl-led initiatives

Community development

Human rights

Public speaking

Communications

Campaigning

Policy engagement

Climate action

Youth participation

Leadership development

Community projects

International advocacy

Applicants should focus on demonstrating authentic engagement rather than simply listing advocacy-related terms.

For example, an applicant involved in a community project can explain the issue addressed, the role they played, the people involved and what they learned.

Similarly, someone involved in a gender-equality campaign can explain their advocacy activities and how they contributed to raising awareness, engaging stakeholders or supporting change.

What Will Global Advocacy Champions Do?

Selected Champions will have a range of opportunities and responsibilities associated with advocacy and leadership.

These include:

Representing Girls and Young Women

Champions will contribute to representing the perspectives and voices of girls and young women at different levels.

This requires participants to listen to the concerns of their communities and communicate those concerns effectively in wider advocacy spaces.

Engaging in Advocacy

Champions will participate in advocacy opportunities and use their developing skills to influence discussions around relevant issues.

Supporting Member Organisations

Champions will have opportunities to contribute to the advocacy work of their WAGGGS Member Organisations.

Leading Community Projects

Champions will be able to lead projects within their communities, providing an opportunity to turn learning into practical action.

Participating in a Global Network

Champions will join other young women working to influence change around the world.

The network element is important because advocacy often becomes more effective when individuals and organisations are able to share knowledge, coordinate activities and learn from different contexts.

Application Deadline

Applications for the Global Advocacy Champions 2026–2027 programme close on 30 September 2026.

Applicants should therefore begin the application and Member Organisation endorsement process as early as possible.

The WAGGGS announcement specifically directs applicants to the full Terms of Reference for information on eligibility, responsibilities, time commitment and the application and Member Organisation endorsement process.

Interested candidates should first read the official Terms of Reference carefully.

TITLE: Intensified currents associated with benthic storms underneath an eddying jet

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Chen, S.-Y. S., Marchal, O., Gardner, W., & Andres, M. (2024). Intensified currents associated with benthic storms underneath an eddying jet. Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans, 129(7), e2024JC020963. https://doi.org/10.1029/2024JC020963

Figure provided by Sean Chen

Benthic storms are episodes of intensified near‐bottom currents capable of sediment resuspension in the deep ocean. They typically occur under regions of high surface eddy kinetic energy (EKE), such as the Gulf Stream. Although they have long been observed, the mechanisms responsible for their formation remain poorly understood. In this study, we use an ocean circulation model to simulate the baroclinic instability of a surface current like the Gulf Stream, and to explore the effects of this instability on the abyssal flows near the bottom in an idealized zonal channel (panel a: domain and initial condition). We find that the unstable surface-intensified jet develops meanders and evolves into alternating, deep‐reaching cyclones and anticyclones (panel b, i-ii: normalized relative vorticity near surface and bottom, respectively). Simultaneously, EKE increases near the bottom due to the convergence of vertical eddy pressure fluxes, leading to near‐bottom currents comparable to those observed during benthic storms (panel b, iii: vertical section of EKE). The intensity of deep currents varies strongly with distance from the bottom, which creates turbulence and a well‐mixed layer adjacent to the deep seabed. In deep cyclones, particles from near the bottom can be transported upward through the entire well‐mixed layer (panel c, i-iv: initial particle positions; lateral particle distribution after 30 days; vertical distribution of particles after 30 days). Overall, our study shows that the physical environment near the bottom may exhibit a strong response to the instability of surface currents, which may have a potentially significant impact on the transport of fine sediment from the seafloor.

Transformative leadership

The approach to tackling the climate crisis is grounded in the Mastercard Foundation’s vision of Transformative Leadership, defined as “the act of engaging others in an ethical manner to generate positive and lasting change.”

The Climate Leadership Programme emphasises the importance of justice, inclusion and community.

The programme particularly encourages applications from young women, young people with disabilities, and young people with refugee and displaced status who are uniquely positioned to apply their experiences to create inclusive approaches.

Key skills

Entrepreneurial skills

Climate leaders are alert to innovative solutions and shifts in perspective that go beyond gradual improvements. Whether they aim to be an entrepreneur in a literal sense — running their own business or social enterprise — or leading change within an organisation, scholars will develop the ability to identify creative opportunities and implement game-changing solutions.

Values and justice

Transformative leaders seek change for the greater good, not just themselves. Addressing climate change and other multi-dimensional challenges involves understanding systemic injustice. Networks

TITLE: CRG Undergraduate and Master’s Fellowships 2026/2027: 10 Funded Research Opportunities in Barcelona

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Centre for Genomic Regulation (CRG) in Barcelona, Spain, is offering 10 fellowship opportunities for undergraduate and MSc students for the 2026/2027 academic year. The opportunities are designed for motivated students who want to gain hands-on research experience in an international scientific environment and develop skills relevant to future scientific and research careers.

The CRG brings together international research teams working across genomics, molecular biology, computational biology, biotechnology, biomedical sciences, evolution and other related disciplines.

Importantly, students from all nationalities can apply. Each project will remain open until the right candidate is found, so applicants are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

CRG Undergraduate and Master’s Fellowships 2026/2027

These fellowships provide students with the opportunity to join a CRG research group and contribute to a specific scientific project while receiving supervision and practical training.

The projects cover a wide range of cutting-edge research areas, including:

Proteomics and mass spectrometry

Regulatory genomics and diabetes

Single-cell genomics and evolution

Systems and synthetic biology

Chromatin folding and genome organisation

Cell fate engineering and neuronal diversity

Machine learning and genomics

Evolutionary biology

Computational biology and health genomics

Cancer genomics and immunogenicity

Fellowship Benefits

Selected students will receive:

€700 gross per month for up to four months.

Travel support for a return ticket:

Up to €1,000 for non-European flights.

Up to €400 for European flights.

Hands-on experience in an international research laboratory.

Training in advanced experimental, computational and analytical techniques.

Access to CRG’s research environment, scientific seminars, core technologies and training activities.

The fellowship must take place during the 2026/2027 academic year.

Available Research Projects

1. Proteomics – Development of LC-MS/MS Workflows

This Master’s-level project focuses on developing robust workflows for proteoform characterization in liquid biopsies. Students will gain experience in sample preparation, protein digestion, peptide clean-up, LC-MS/MS, experimental design, quality control and data analysis.

It is particularly suitable for students in biochemistry, biotechnology, molecular biology, biomedical sciences or related fields.

2. Regulatory Genomics and Diabetes – CRISPRi Screening

This undergraduate project investigates CRISPR interference screening in human pancreatic beta cells, with applications to understanding and improving potential treatments for Type 1 diabetes.

Students will receive training in molecular cloning, lentiviral production, cell culture and single-cell sequencing workflows.

3. Single-Cell Genomics and Evolution

This computational project compares methods for integrating genome-wide expression data across developmental trajectories.

Applicants should have a background in life sciences, with an interest in genomics, bioinformatics or computational biology. Basic Bash/Linux, R and Python skills are expected.

4. Systems and Synthetic Biology – CpG Organisation and Longevity

This four-month computational project examines the relationship between CpG spatial organisation and mammalian longevity using comparative genomics and statistical modelling.

It is suitable for BSc or MSc students interested in bioinformatics, computational biology, genomics, evolution or ageing research.

5. Reprogramming and Regeneration – Chromatin Folding

Students will investigate how depletion of TOP2A or TOP2B affects chromatin organisation in human cells using Optical Reconstruction of Chromatin Architecture (ORCA).

The project is suitable for motivated undergraduate students interested in molecular biology, cell biology, microscopy or quantitative biology. Previous ORCA or advanced programming experience is not required.

6. Cell Fate Decoding and Engineering

This project investigates neuronal diversity and cell fate engineering using transcription factors, molecular cloning, lentiviral vectors and mammalian cell culture.

Students from different backgrounds can apply, as training will be provided. Motivation, curiosity and willingness to learn are particularly important.

7. Probabilistic Machine Learning and Genomics

This Master’s-level computational project combines protein language models, protein folding, human genetics and machine learning to investigate the mechanisms behind missense genetic variants.

Applicants should have a background in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, physics, mathematics or a related quantitative discipline. Python programming experience is expected.

8. Systems and Synthetic Biology – Genotype-Phenotype Maps

This project uses computational approaches to investigate how environmental changes influence genotype-phenotype relationships and evolutionary simulations.

It is particularly suited to students with backgrounds in physics, computer science, biology or bioinformatics who are interested in interdisciplinary research.

9. Computational Biology and Health Genomics

Students will analyse structural variants identified through long-read sequencing and investigate their potential effects on gene regulation.

Applicants should have skills in Python and Bash/command line, alongside knowledge of molecular biology, statistics and genomics.

10. Evolutionary Processes Modeling and Cancer

This computational project explores how genetic and evolutionary factors influence the immunogenic potential of cancer-associated mutations.

Students interested in computational biology, evolution or cancer genomics are encouraged to apply. Experience with Python or similar programming languages and large datasets is preferred.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is open to:

Undergraduate students

MSc/Master’s students

Students from all nationalities

Students currently enrolled in an official university undergraduate or MSc programme

Students whose university can sign a learning agreement with CRG

Motivated students interested in scientific research and willing to develop new skills

Applicants must be new recruits and cannot already be students at CRG.

There is no requirement for applicants to have extensive previous research experience for every project. Several projects provide training, and requirements vary according to the individual research project.

Application Requirements

Applicants should review the available projects and contact the relevant project supervisor and group leader directly.

Applications should include:

Motivation letter

Curriculum Vitae (CV)

Reference letter

University transcripts

The selection will depend on the capacity of the relevant research group and the requirements of the ongoing project

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Deadline

There is no single fixed application deadline. According to CRG, each fellowship project will remain open until the right candidate is found. Applicants are therefore encouraged to apply early.

The fellowships must be undertaken during the 2026/2027 academic year.

How to Apply

Students should identify the research project that best matches their academic background and interests, carefully review its requirements, and send the required application documents directly to the listed project supervisor and group leader.

The publication date of the 2026/2027 fellowship opportunities is August 6, 2026.

Conclusion

The CRG Undergraduate and Master’s Fellowships 2026/2027 offer an excellent opportunity for students from around the world to gain practical experience in a leading international research environment. With projects spanning genomics, biotechnology, computational biology, cancer research, diabetes, evolution, proteomics and molecular biology, students can select a research area closely aligned with their academic and career interests.

Because projects remain open until suitable candidates are selected, interested students should identify a suitable project and submit their application as early as possible.

TITLE: Invitation to Participate in a DAF-EAC Research for Impact Webinar: High-level stakeholder engagement session for the dissemination of research findings on the Demographics of African Faculty (DAF) – Lessons from the East African Community (EAC) | Wednesday 3rd May 2023| 11:00am-12:30pm GMT

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The AAU, as a partner of the Demographics of African Faculty – East African Community (DAF EAC), Consortium is inviting higher education stakeholders (from all regions of the continent) to join a stakeholder dissemination webinar, being organised under the theme: Research for Impact: High-level stakeholder engagement session for the dissemination of research findings on the Demographics of African Faculty – Lessons from the East African Community on Wednesday 3rd May 2023.

The Demographics of African Faculty in the East Africa Community (DAF-EAC) is a project undertaken by a consortium comprised of the Inter-University Council of East Africa (IUCEA), Association of African Universities (AAU), Education Sub Saharan Africa (ESSA ) and the Population Reference Bureau (PRB). DAF EAC follows the initial study on Demographics of African Faculty in Ghana, which provided important demographic data and identified challenges concerning faculty in the country. DAF-EAC seeks to assess the status of higher education faculty in the East Africa region in terms of numbers, distribution by gender and areas of study. Specifically, the project comprises four components, which include background research, analysis of current and future faculty demand, stakeholder engagement and dissemination of project findings, and co-creation of solutions to address the faculty challenges. The study was funded by the Carnegie Corporation of New York, and focuses on six partner states of the East African community, namely Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

The two-year project also focuses on studying the challenges that higher education institutions face, with respect to faculty to student ratios, and the composition of faculty, which directly affect the quality of education. It aimed at increasing the ability of higher education stakeholders to plan and implement evidence informed responses to improve the numbers of quality faculty within higher education institutions – using the case of the East African Community.

The webinar being organised will provide the platform to share insights on the research findings of this two-year research with stakeholders in the higher education space while creating room for them to discuss the project’s outputs and developments. It is envisaged that participants will be well equipped with information which will help them better plan for quality faculty in their own institutions.

The Webinar is scheduled to take place on Wednesday 3rd May 2023 from 11:00 am – 12:30 pm GMT.

The registration link is made available here: https://us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/tZcrdOuupzouGtBdaL8B-gy7lXZI-6uni5FD

We look forward to your participation in this webinar as we believe that your participation will make a significant contribution to the success of the event.

About the Fellowship

The Africa Early Childhood Network (AfECN) is a registered Kenya-based, non-profit professional network established in 2015 to serve as a platform for championing and promoting excellence and collaboration in ensuring positive early childhood outcomes in Africa. AfECN achieves this mission by advocating for protectionof children’s rights, influencing policy and practice, strengthening partnerships, and sharing experiences and knowledge in Early Childhood Development (ECD) on the African continent. AfECN has identified five areas needing improvement to make progress towards large-scale equitable access to early child development programmes in sub-Saharan Africa: advocacy, networking, knowledge generation and dissemination, practice, and leadership.

In 2017, AfECN began implementing a mentorship programme to strengthen ECD research capacity in Africa by supporting early-to-mid-career African scholars (Research Fellows) who can work at the intersection of research, practice and policy to advance early childhood development in the region. Specifically, the aim is to develop capacity in the region for culturally and contextually relevant research to support the level of program implementation necessary to produce high-quality early childhood outcomes. At the same time, AfECN Research Fellows participate in disseminating their work through policy briefs, peer-reviewed articles as well as presentations at conferences, seminars and workshops.

AfECN also nurtures the combined capacity of a network of research universities across Africa to support scholarship on early childhood development policy generation and programming. To accomplish these goals, AfECN facilitates a regional research network that will promote collaborative relationships across universities and between early career scholars and well-established senior scholars for the purpose of enhancing knowledge generation, management, and dissemination.

AfECN activities to improve research capacity are being led by a Regional Research Technical Team (RRTT) comprised of accomplished ECD scholars and researchers in the continent. AfECN is currently in the process of recruiting the 3rd Cohort which is planned to have four (4) junior research fellows. TITLE: A hotspot and mechanism of enhanced bottom intrusion on the southern New England shelf

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Chen, K. (2024). A hotspot and mechanism of enhanced bottom intrusion on the southern New England shelf. Environmental Research Communications, 6(7). https://doi.org/10.1088/2515-7620/ad61c7

(a), (d): Composite mean bottom currents (black vectors) and salinity (color) for different stages of the bottom intrusion relative to the maximum salinity anomaly at the Block Trough (the rectangular box): 6 days and 2 days prior to the time of maximum anomaly. Spatial mean bottom velocity vector (within the rectangular box) is shown with magnitude amplified by five times for better visualization. Mean wind stress in the region is shown in blue vectors. (b), (e): Same as (a), (d) but for bottom pressure gradient force with magnitude in color and directions in gray vectors. (c), (f): Estimates of the bottom flow using pressure gradient, stress divergence, and acceleration terms within the trough. The light gray dots represent the geostrophic balance, i.e., using the first term to infer bottom flow. The darker gray represents the contribution of the pressure gradient and stress divergence. The black dots represent the consideration of the additional acceleration term, i.e., all three terms below the x-axis. Color-coded Root Mean Square Difference (RMSD) values are shown. Major balance is between pressure gradient, Coriolis, and bottom stress, with pressure gradient being the driving term. Image provided by Ke Chen.

Understanding the occurrence of open ocean water intrusions onto continental shelves holds both scientific significance and societal relevance, as such intrusions can significantly disrupt marine ecosystems and fisheries. Chen (2024) uses high-resolution numerical modeling to investigate the spatiotemporal occurrence and mechanisms of highly anomalous bottom intrusions on the southern New England shelf. Based on multi-year numerical simulations, the study identifies a hotspot of cross-isobath bottom-intensified intrusions at a topographic trough offshore of the Block Island, i.e., Block Trough. The examination of multiple events reveals a robust mechanism for locally enhanced bottom intrusions: persistent upwelling-favorable winds create an intensified pressure gradient field at the trough, driving the intrusions a considerable distance onshore.

Given the results’ implications for the marine environment and fisheries management, the study raises a key prediction question: can these events be predicted based on wind conditions alone? While realistic simulations show a connection between highly anomalous waters on the shelf and wind forcing, the correlation between wind stress anomalies and bottom salinity anomalies at the site of the enhanced intrusion is only modest. This suggests the need to incorporate additional environmental factors to develop more deterministic models for predicting subsurface conditions on the shelf.

TITLE: Register now to take the Sustainable Water Management in Agriculture course

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Course Name: Sustainable Water Management In Agriculture

Duration: 6 weeks

Target group:

OVERVIEW OF THE COURSE

Water is considered as the most critical resource for sustainable agricultural development worldwide. Irrigated areas will increase in forthcoming years, while fresh water supplies will be diverted from agriculture to meet the increasing demand of domestic use and industry. Irrigated agriculture represents 20 percent of the total cultivated land and contributes 40 percent of the total food produced worldwide. Irrigated agriculture is, on average, at least twice as productive per unit of land as rainfed agriculture, thereby allowing for more production intensification and crop diversification. However, the efficiency of irrigation is very low, since less than 65% of the applied water is actually used by the crops. The sustainable use of irrigation water is a priority for agriculture in arid areas and globally. This course teaches the improvements that are possible by adaptations in irrigation application, soil and plant practices, water pricing, reuse of treated wastewater, farmers’ participation in water management and capacity building.

As defined by the UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science, Open Science is a movement aiming to make science more open, accessible, efficient, democratic and transparent. The Open Access/Open Science workshops targeting research leadership in AAU member regions and universities is proposed with the objective of creating awareness and education on the importance and best practice of Open Access/Open Science. The desired outcome is engagement and buy-in by the academic community on the adoption of Open Science. TCC Africa and PLOS are the supporting partners in this initiative.

Outcome

• Effective adoption of Open Science and Open Access practice among members

• Increased education and awareness on Open Science and Open Access in the AAU member academic community

Objective of the workshops

• To create and embrace open science and open access in the respective member academic communities

• To understand the current developments on open science, challenges faced in their respective academic communities and opportunities on open science and open access

• To reduce the push back on the adoption of Open Science and Open Access by early career researchers.

• To create awareness on how Open Science aids in higher education institutions competitiveness

TITLE: Strengthening Relations Between African Universities and the Private Sector

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
AAU Secretary General meets the Africa Private Sector Summit representatives

The Association of African Universities (AAU) has reaffirmed its commitment to work closely with Africa’s private sector to promote economic transformation of the continent and contribute towards achieving the Africa we want, as targeted by the African Union’s Agenda 2063.

In a meeting held between the AAU and the Africa Private Sector Summit (APSS) representatives on 6th October 2021, the two parties acknowledged that economic transformation cannot materialize without the institutions that produce the requisite skill set and human resources – higher education institutions.

Strategically positioning higher education to make it relevant to industry has been a key priority of the AAU. Earlier in March 2021, the Association signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Pan African Chamber of Commerce and Industry to promote the continental integration of Africa through education, trade, and investment under the Regional Economic Communities (RECs) trade agreements and the Africa Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

In the Memorandum of Understanding, a special Africa Education Trust Fund (AfETF) to support African Universities and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions to meet the professional manpower skill set demands of the continent is expected to be launched.

The AAU has been an advocate for effective university-industry linkages in view of the synergies such collaborations build for socio-economic development. The AAU has, over the years of its existence, deployed advocacy tools through its programmes with member universities, conferences and capacity building workshops, to make higher education more responsive to the overtures from the private sector.

The Chairperson of the APSS, Mr. J Wendell Addy used the meeting with the AAU to extend an invitation to all universities in Africa and other stakeholders to participate in the upcoming hybrid Africa Private Sector Summit holding on October 19 -22, 2021 in Accra, Ghana and also virtually.

For his part, the Secretary General of the AAU, Prof. Olusola Bandele Oyewole reassured the meeting and stakeholders of the Association’s commitment to working with the private sector to ensure that academia has a strong presence and plays a critical role in the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) agenda. “The AAU will also play its expected roles as outlined in the MoU signed with the Pan African Chamber of Commerce and Industry for the benefit of our member institutions and stakeholders” Prof. Oyewole added.

TITLE: African Academic and Heritage Fair 2022, by the AAU TV

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
All African higher education stakeholders are being invited to join the AAU TV and its mother organisation, the Association of African Universities (AAU) as we host the maiden edition of the African Academic and Heritage Fair 2022, scheduled for 25th May, 2022.

Acknowledging the role of Africa’s cultural renaissance in the achievement of the African Union’s Agenda 2063 (The Africa We Want), and as AAU’s audiovisual mouthpiece in supporting the implementation of the Agenda, the AAU TV is rolling out the African Academic Heritage Fair with the objectives of:

Mobilizing expert knowledge and thoughts on African education and cultural heritage through carefully selected topics in tandem with the themes of the African Union Day; and

Promoting African heritage through storytelling, culture, arts, music, songs, food, and other forms of engagement that tell the continent’s narrative through the past and present to secure and shape the future.

Celebrating African heroes and heroines, both living and the dead to revive the spirit of Pan-Africanism as espoused by the earlier generation of ancestors.

The broad theme of this year’s AUD is Strengthening Resilience in Nutrition and Food Security on the African Continent, and the AAU TV is empaneling a team of experts to deliberate on the topic, The Role of Higher Education in Strengthening Agro-Food Systems, Health and Social Protection Systems towards Socio-Economic Development.

The celebration will also be marked by cultural displays, poetry recital, exhibitions and a competition, “Know Your Continent Quiz” which will reward excellence in knowledge of African history and the AU’s Agenda 2063. The ultimate winner of the quiz will be branded “The AAU TV African Heritage Ambassador, 2022”.

The Genesis & Current State – African Academic Heritage Fair

The AAU TV had, prior to the declaration of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, celebrated two previous Africa Days with studio discussions, presentations and portrayal of African history and thought. This year, the TV Unit is formalizing the celebrations under an exciting and new initiative dubbed the African Academic Heritage Fair. This will be an annual event on the calendar of the AAU TV that will be dedicated to promoting both the chosen theme of the year’s AUD as well as promoting the renaissance of African literature, debate, exhibition, music, and other art forms through the intervention of the educational sector.

Education and culture are intertwined and their symbiotic relationship makes them the bedrock of socio-economic development in any society. African universities, by their role as knowledge generators and disseminators, have a role to play in preserving the continent’s cultural heritage and societal norms against invading foreign cultures. The continent’s current academic curricula are overtly Westernized and hit by the neglect of the use of local indigenous systems as case studies. The medium of instruction from the basic to the tertiary levels of education has not been indigenized enough to preserve the purity of the African language as a legacy for generations. Restoring Africa’s heritage cannot be dictated by external sources. It must be generated from within through concerted efforts in which academia plays a vital role as convener.

Full-time

Fit with the proposed project

Fit with the supervisor

Career objectives

Draft research proposal

before the commencement deadline.

TITLE: STARLIGHT 2.0: Strategic Litigation for Rights in Europe | Applications Open

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Across Europe, democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights continue to face significant pressure. The EU Charter of Fundamental Rights provides an important legal framework for protecting these rights, but its potential as a tool for strategic litigation remains underused.

STARLIGHT 2.0 – Strategic Litigation for Rights in Europe is now accepting applications from legal professionals who want to strengthen their ability to use the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights to pursue systemic change and improve rights protection across Europe.

The programme brings together legal training, practical skills development, mentorship, legal clinics and networking opportunities to help participants turn strategic litigation into a tool for lasting impact. The programme is delivered by Democracy Reporting International, the Hertie School and the Hungarian Helsinki Committee, with support from the European Commission’s CERV programme.

About STARLIGHT 2.0

STARLIGHT 2.0 is designed for legal professionals who already have experience in litigation and want to develop stronger knowledge and practical strategies for using the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights in strategic cases.

The programme focuses on how litigation can go beyond resolving individual cases and contribute to broader changes in law, policy, institutional practice and rights protection.

Participants will learn from experienced academics, practitioners and litigators while working with peers from across EU Member States. The programme also includes legal clinics and mentorship to help participants apply what they learn to real-world cases.

What the STARLIGHT 2.0 Programme Offers

The programme combines several forms of professional learning and collaboration.

Practical Legal and Skills Training

Participants will take part in in-person training sessions designed to strengthen both their legal knowledge and practical professional skills.

The programme’s 2026–2027 cohort includes:

In-person Charter training

Skills training

Online legal clinics

Mentorship

Peer learning

Networking with other legal professionals

The in-person Charter training is scheduled for 9–11 November 2026, while the skills training is scheduled for 1–3 March 2027.

Expert Guidance

Participants will learn from experienced academics, legal practitioners and strategic litigators with expertise in using the EU Charter and pursuing rights-based litigation.

The programme is designed to connect participants with people who have practical experience in developing litigation strategies and using legal cases to achieve systemic change.

Legal Clinics and Mentorship

Participants will have opportunities to work through real-life cases and develop legal strategies with support from experts and mentors.

The legal clinics are an important part of the programme because they allow participants to apply knowledge from the training to practical litigation challenges.

European Network

STARLIGHT 2.0 also provides participants with an opportunity to connect with legal professionals from across Europe.

The programme aims to build a growing community of practitioners who can share knowledge, strategies and best practices while working to strengthen fundamental rights protection. The first cohort included lawyers from NGOs, National Human Rights Institutions and law firms across the EU.

Two Thematic Streams

Applicants can participate in one of two thematic areas.

Democracy and Rule of Law

This stream focuses on strategic litigation related to:

Democracy

Rule of law

Fundamental rights

Civic space

Democratic institutions

Systemic rights violations

Participants explore how strategic litigation can influence law, policy and public debate.

Asylum and Migration

The second stream focuses on legal issues involving:

Asylum

Migration

Fundamental rights

Protection of migrants and refugees

Strategic litigation

Applicants should select the stream that most closely aligns with their professional interests and experience.

Who Can Apply?

The STARLIGHT 2.0 call is open to legal practitioners working in EU Member States.

Eligible applicants include legal professionals working in:

Law firms

Civil society organisations

Legal clinics

National Human Rights Institutions

Applicants should have at least two years of relevant professional experience.

The programme is intended for experienced legal professionals who are interested in using strategic litigation to strengthen democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should meet the following requirements:

Be a legal practitioner working in an EU Member State.

Work in a law firm, civil society organisation, legal clinic or National Human Rights Institution.

Have at least two years of relevant professional experience.

Have an interest in strategic litigation and fundamental rights.

Be interested in using the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights in practical litigation.

Be prepared to actively participate throughout the programme.

The available information does not indicate that the programme is limited to lawyers working in a particular academic specialisation. Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their current legal work connects to the programme’s thematic areas.

Scholarships and Financial Support

Selected participants will receive scholarships covering the training fees and accommodation in Berlin for the three-day in-person legal and skills workshops.

However, travel costs are self-funded.

This means participants will need to arrange and finance their own travel to and from Berlin, while the programme covers the specified training fees and accommodation.

Programme Timeline

The current STARLIGHT 2.0 cohort will run from:

October 2026 to July 2027

Key in-person training dates include:

Charter Training:

9–11 November 2026

Skills Training:

1–3 March 2027

The programme also includes online clinics, mentorship and additional engagement during the programme period.

Why Strategic Litigation Matters

Strategic litigation can be used to pursue changes that extend beyond the outcome of an individual legal case.

A carefully selected case can potentially influence:

Legal interpretation

Government policy

Institutional practice

Protection of fundamental rights

Public debate

Implementation of court decisions

STARLIGHT 2.0 is designed to help legal professionals understand how to identify cases with broader potential and develop litigation strategies that can contribute to systemic change. (DevelopmentAid)

What Participants Can Gain

Through the programme, participants can develop:

Stronger Knowledge of the EU Charter

Gain a deeper understanding of how the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights can be used in strategic litigation.

Practical Litigation Skills

Learn approaches for developing and pursuing cases with potential for broader impact.

Expert Mentorship

Receive guidance from experienced legal practitioners and academics.

Case-Based Learning

Apply programme knowledge to real-life cases through legal clinics.

Professional Network

Connect with other legal professionals working on fundamental rights and strategic litigation across Europe.

Skills for Systemic Impact

Learn how litigation can contribute to changes beyond individual cases, including changes to law, policy and public debate.

Who Is This Opportunity Best Suited For?

STARLIGHT 2.0 may be particularly relevant to legal professionals working on:

Human rights

Fundamental rights

Democracy

Rule of law

Civic space

Asylum

Migration

Strategic litigation

Legal advocacy

Rights protection

It is especially relevant to practitioners who want to strengthen their ability to use the EU Charter as part of their litigation strategy.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the current cohort is:

20 September 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and carefully review all programme requirements before applying.

How to Apply

Interested legal professionals should apply through the official STARLIGHT 2.0 application process.

The programme information and application details are available through the official programme organisers.

Programme information: Democracy Reporting International — STARLIGHT 2.0

Applicants should review the official call carefully before submitting their application.

Application Tips

1. Demonstrate Your Relevant Experience

Clearly explain your legal experience and show how it relates to strategic litigation, fundamental rights, democracy, rule of law, asylum or migration.

2. Explain Your Motivation

Be specific about why you want to participate and how the programme will strengthen your professional work.

3. Choose the Appropriate Stream

Consider whether your experience and interests are more closely aligned with Democracy & Rule of Law or Asylum & Migration.

4. Highlight Your Litigation Work

Where applicable, describe relevant cases, legal research, advocacy or litigation experience that demonstrates your interest in systemic rights protection.

5. Consider Your Travel Arrangements

Although training fees and accommodation in Berlin are covered through scholarships, travel is self-funded. Applicants should plan accordingly.

Conclusion

STARLIGHT 2.0 – Strategic Litigation for Rights in Europe provides legal professionals across EU Member States with an opportunity to strengthen their ability to use the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights as a tool for strategic litigation and systemic rights protection.

The programme combines legal training, practical skills development, online legal clinics, mentorship and professional networking. Participants can choose between the Democracy & Rule of Law and Asylum & Migration streams while working with experienced practitioners and peers from across Europe.

Selected participants receive scholarships covering training fees and accommodation in Berlin, although travel costs remain the responsibility of participants.

Legal practitioners with at least two years of relevant experience who are working in law firms, civil society organisations, legal clinics or National Human Rights Institutions in EU Member States are encouraged to consider applying before the 20 September 2026 deadline.

High-quality independent research

University-level teaching

Interdisciplinary collaboration

Academic service

Public engagement and outreach

Research addressing important contemporary challenges

2. Teaching

Teaching is another important component of an academic career. Applicants should demonstrate their ability to contribute effectively to university education and explain how their teaching interests and approaches complement their academic expertise.

3. Service

Academic service can include contributions to departments, universities, professional organizations, scholarly communities, or other relevant groups. Applicants should consider how their past or proposed service activities demonstrate their willingness to contribute to the broader academic community.

4. Outreach and Public Engagement

The program also encourages applicants to consider how their expertise can reach audiences beyond traditional academic settings. Where relevant, candidates can highlight outreach, community engagement, knowledge-sharing, public scholarship, or other activities through which their work contributes to society.

Eligible Academic Fields and Departments

The fellowship is open across a broad range of disciplines in the humanities, arts, sciences, and professions. Because eligibility can depend on the departments participating in a particular fellowship cycle, prospective applicants should consult the official Michigan Society of Fellows information and the relevant departmental requirements before preparing and submitting an application.

Are interested in developing their university teaching experience.

Want to participate in a collaborative and intellectually diverse academic environment.

Instead of focusing exclusively on completing research, fellows can use the fellowship period to develop several dimensions of their professional profile simultaneously.

The fellowship provides an environment in which early-career researchers can continue developing their scholarly work and advancing their research agendas.

TITLE: Climate Caucus Programs & Policy Senior Manager 2026: Fully Remote Climate Policy Role Paying $75,000–$80,000 Per Year

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Climate Caucus is accepting applications for a Programs & Policy Senior Manager, a full-time, fully remote position for an experienced professional with a strong background in climate policy, policy research, programme management, stakeholder engagement and community-focused climate action.

The successful candidate will help lead research and community programmes that support local climate leadership across Canada. The position combines policy analysis with programme development and implementation, making it particularly relevant to professionals who want to work at the intersection of climate change, local government, public policy, advocacy, research and community engagement.

Climate Caucus describes the position as a highly generative role for a motivated individual with considerable experience in policy development and analysis. The successful candidate will be expected to manage complex and multi-year initiatives, lead policy research, develop strategic relationships with stakeholders and contribute to programmes designed to strengthen local climate leadership.

The position is fully remote, is offered on a full-time contract, and comes with a stated annual salary range of $75,000–$80,000. The currency is not specified in the information provided, so applicants should confirm this directly in the official vacancy notice.

In addition to salary, the position includes benefits such as flexible scheduling, paid time off, healthcare benefits and an annual $1,200 wellness allowance.

The application deadline is August 28, 2026.

About Climate Caucus

Climate Caucus works to strengthen climate leadership at the local level in Canada.

The organization’s work focuses on helping communities, leaders and decision-makers advance practical responses to climate change through stronger policy, programmes, research, collaboration and engagement.

Local governments and community leaders occupy an important position in climate action because many climate-related decisions are implemented at municipal, regional and community levels.

These may include areas such as:

Climate adaptation

Emissions reduction

Land-use planning

Infrastructure

Public transportation

Buildings

Community resilience

Energy

Environmental policy

Local economic development

Climate-related public engagement

The Programs & Policy Senior Manager will help support this broader climate leadership ecosystem.

About the Programs & Policy Senior Manager Position

The Programs & Policy Senior Manager is a senior-level role combining two major areas of responsibility:

Programme leadership and management

Climate policy research and analysis

The position also includes a substantial stakeholder-engagement component.

This means the successful candidate should not only be capable of producing strong climate-policy research but should also be comfortable managing programmes, coordinating relationships, planning multi-year work and translating research into practical action.

The job is therefore particularly suitable for someone who understands both policy and implementation.

Fully Remote Working Arrangement

The vacancy is described as:

Fully remote

This means the successful candidate will not be required to work permanently from a traditional central office under the arrangement described in the supplied announcement.

Remote work can offer greater flexibility, but senior remote positions also require strong self-management.

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate skills such as:

Independent work

Time management

Digital collaboration

Remote team communication

Project coordination

Accountability

Strategic planning

Because Climate Caucus operates in the Canadian climate-policy environment, prospective applicants should also review the full vacancy notice to confirm whether there are any geographic residence, time-zone or Canadian work-authorization requirements.

The information supplied here does not specify these conditions.

Employment Type

The position is:

Full-time

and is described as a:

Contract position

Applicants should consult the formal job advertisement for any additional information regarding the contract term or renewal arrangements, because the material provided does not specify a fixed contract end date.

Salary

The stated salary range is:

$75,000–$80,000 per year

The provided announcement does not explicitly identify the currency.

Because the organization operates across Canada, applicants may reasonably expect the official posting to clarify the applicable currency, but this should be verified directly rather than assumed.

Additional Benefits

The position also comes with a benefits package.

The supplied vacancy information identifies:

Fully remote work

Flexible scheduling

Paid time off

Healthcare benefits

$1,200 annual wellness allowance

These benefits make the role potentially attractive to experienced professionals seeking both meaningful climate-policy work and flexible employment arrangements.

Main Responsibilities

The Programs & Policy Senior Manager will work across several interconnected areas.

1. Managing Climate Programmes

One of the most important responsibilities is managing climate-related programmes.

This is likely to involve coordinating projects from planning through implementation and monitoring.

Senior programme management commonly requires the ability to:

Develop programme plans

Establish priorities

Coordinate activities

Manage timelines

Monitor progress

Support partners

Identify challenges

Adjust implementation strategies

Maintain communication across teams

The role appears particularly focused on programmes supporting local climate leadership across Canada.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate not simply that they understand climate change, but that they can turn climate priorities into structured and manageable programmes.

2. Managing Multi-Year Projects

The position also involves responsibility for multi-year projects.

Long-term initiatives require a different management approach from short, one-off activities.

Applicants may need experience with:

Long-term strategic planning

Project milestones

Annual work plans

Performance indicators

Partner relationships

Budget awareness

Risk management

Reporting

Programme evaluation

A strong candidate should be able to show that they can maintain momentum and strategic direction over extended periods.

3. Leading Research

Research is another significant part of the position.

The successful candidate will be expected to lead research that informs Climate Caucus programmes and policy work.

Policy research can involve:

Reviewing legislation

Examining government policies

Analyzing climate strategies

Comparing approaches across jurisdictions

Reviewing academic and policy literature

Synthesizing evidence

Identifying emerging climate-policy trends

Producing recommendations

The exact research portfolio will depend on the organization’s priorities.

4. Policy Analysis

The announcement particularly emphasizes policy development and analysis.

This suggests that the successful applicant should have substantial professional experience examining public-policy issues.

Strong policy analysis involves more than summarizing a government document.

Candidates should be able to assess questions such as:

What problem is a policy attempting to solve?

What evidence supports the approach?

Who is responsible for implementation?

What are the likely impacts?

Which stakeholders are affected?

What barriers could limit implementation?

How could the policy be improved?

What alternatives exist?

How can recommendations be translated into practical action?

Applicants with previous experience producing policy briefs, recommendations, reports or submissions may therefore be particularly well aligned with the position.

5. Policy Development

The role is also relevant to candidates who have participated directly in developing policies or policy proposals.

Policy development can involve:

Defining problems

Consulting stakeholders

Gathering evidence

Developing options

Assessing implications

Drafting recommendations

Supporting decision-makers

Monitoring policy implementation

Because Climate Caucus works with local climate leadership, the successful candidate may need to understand how climate-policy decisions operate at multiple levels of government.

6. Building Strategic Stakeholder Relationships

The Programs & Policy Senior Manager will also be responsible for building and maintaining relationships with important stakeholders.

Climate action often requires coordination across many types of organizations and institutions.

Relevant stakeholders could potentially include:

Local elected officials

Municipal governments

Climate organizations

Community organizations

Researchers

Policy experts

Environmental organizations

Civil society

Government representatives

Partner networks

The supplied vacancy information does not list a complete stakeholder map, so applicants should consult the official job advertisement for details.

However, relationship-building is clearly an important part of the position.

Why Stakeholder Engagement Matters

Local climate policy often depends on collaboration.

An excellent policy recommendation may have limited impact if decision-makers, communities and implementing organizations are not engaged.

The Senior Manager therefore needs to be capable of:

Building trust

Maintaining professional relationships

Understanding different interests

Facilitating dialogue

Communicating complex ideas clearly

Supporting collaboration

Navigating disagreement

This combination of policy knowledge and interpersonal skill is likely to be central to success in the role.

Supporting Local Climate Leadership

The central purpose of the position is to contribute to stronger local climate leadership across Canada.

Local leadership is essential because climate impacts are experienced directly within communities.

Municipalities and local decision-makers may be responsible for areas including:

Transportation

Urban planning

Building standards

Infrastructure

Waste management

Emergency preparedness

Community resilience

Land use

Local energy initiatives

A Senior Manager working in this field needs to understand that climate action is not simply a national-policy issue.

Implementation frequently occurs at the community and municipal level.

What Does a “Generative Role” Mean?

The announcement describes the opportunity as a generative role.

Although the supplied vacancy text does not formally define this term, the wording suggests Climate Caucus is looking for someone who can do more than execute predefined tasks.

The successful candidate may be expected to:

Develop ideas

Identify opportunities

Shape programmes

Generate policy insights

Develop new approaches

Strengthen partnerships

Help determine strategic direction

Candidates should therefore demonstrate initiative and independent thinking.

Ideal Professional Profile

The vacancy is particularly suitable for someone with considerable experience in:

Policy development

Policy analysis

Programme management

Research

Climate action

Stakeholder engagement

Because this is a Senior Manager position, applicants should expect the employer to look for evidence of meaningful professional experience rather than only academic knowledge.

Relevant Professional Backgrounds

The role could potentially be relevant to professionals coming from areas such as:

Climate policy

Environmental policy

Government

Municipal policy

Public policy

Environmental NGOs

Climate advocacy

Research organizations

Think tanks

Community programmes

Sustainability

Public administration

Programme management

The supplied announcement does not specify a required university degree, academic discipline or minimum number of years of experience.

Applicants should therefore consult the complete job posting for those details.

Skills That Could Strengthen an Application

Based on the responsibilities described, strong candidates are likely to benefit from skills in several areas.

Climate Policy Knowledge

Applicants should understand the policy environment surrounding climate action.

Knowledge could include:

Climate mitigation

Climate adaptation

Local climate governance

Climate resilience

Environmental regulation

Municipal climate policy

Research Skills

Strong research skills may include:

Policy research

Literature reviews

Evidence synthesis

Comparative analysis

Report writing

Research design

Programme Management

Applicants should be comfortable coordinating complex projects.

Relevant skills can include:

Planning

Scheduling

Monitoring

Coordination

Problem solving

Reporting

Strategic Thinking

Senior-level positions require the ability to consider long-term organizational goals rather than focusing exclusively on immediate tasks.

Communication

Strong writing and verbal communication will likely be important.

The Senior Manager may need to communicate with both specialists and non-specialists.

Relationship Management

The successful candidate should be able to develop productive relationships across a diverse stakeholder network.

Flexible Scheduling

The role includes flexible scheduling.

For experienced professionals, flexibility can support better management of:

Work responsibilities

Personal commitments

Remote collaboration

Different meeting schedules

Applicants should remember, however, that flexibility does not necessarily mean unrestricted working hours.

The successful candidate may still need to participate in meetings and stakeholder activities scheduled according to organizational and partner requirements.

Paid Time Off

The benefits include:

Paid time off

The exact number of paid days is not specified in the information supplied.

Applicants should consult the official employment conditions for detailed information.

Healthcare Benefits

The vacancy also includes:

Healthcare benefits

The supplied announcement does not describe the precise coverage.

Candidates should therefore review the full employment package during the recruitment process.

Annual Wellness Allowance

The position includes a stated:

$1,200 annual wellness allowance

This benefit may support employee wellbeing-related expenses under the organization’s relevant policies.

The eligible uses of the allowance are not specified in the supplied information.

Why This Position May Appeal to Climate Professionals

The Climate Caucus Programs & Policy Senior Manager position offers the opportunity to combine several forms of professional impact.

The successful candidate can work across:

Policy

Research

Programme management

Climate leadership

Community engagement

Strategic partnerships

This combination can be particularly appealing to professionals who do not want to choose between research and practical programme implementation.

The role also provides an opportunity to contribute to climate action at the local level, where many environmental decisions have direct effects on communities.

Application Deadline

Applications close on:

August 28, 2026

Interested candidates should not wait until the final day to prepare their materials.

Given the seniority of the position, applicants should take time to tailor their CV and other materials to the role’s key themes:

Climate policy

Programme management

Policy development

Research

Strategic partnerships

Local climate leadership

How to Apply

Interested candidates should email their resume and a personalized cover letter explaining their motivation and suitability for the role to jobs@climatecaucus.ca.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

1. Lead With Climate Policy Experience

Do not make recruiters search through several pages of your CV to understand your relevance.

Clearly highlight:

Climate policy

Environmental policy

Local government

Climate programmes

Sustainability

near the beginning of the application.

2. Demonstrate Policy Analysis

Avoid simply listing “policy analysis” as a skill.

Provide examples of:

Policies you analyzed

Reports you produced

Recommendations you developed

Governments or organizations you advised

3. Quantify Programme Management Experience

Where possible, include concrete indicators such as:

Number of projects managed

Programme duration

Number of partners

Number of communities

Geographic coverage

Budget responsibility

4. Highlight Multi-Year Project Experience

The role specifically mentions multi-year initiatives.

Show that you can maintain strategy, partnerships and delivery across long timelines.

5. Demonstrate Stakeholder Management

Describe your experience working with:

Government

Civil society

Community leaders

Policy experts

Research institutions

Environmental organizations

6. Show Independent Thinking

Because the role is described as generative, provide examples of times you:

Designed a programme

Developed a new initiative

Identified a policy opportunity

Created a research agenda

Built a new partnership

7. Tailor Your Cover Letter

A generic climate-sector cover letter may be less effective.

Explain specifically:

Why local climate leadership matters to you

Why Climate Caucus fits your experience

How your policy expertise connects with programme management

What you would bring to the organization

Important Information at a Glance

Organization: Climate Caucus

Position: Programs & Policy Senior Manager

Employment: Full-time

Work arrangement: Fully remote

Salary: $75,000–$80,000 annually, as stated in the vacancy information

Wellness allowance: $1,200 annually

Additional benefits: Flexible scheduling, paid time off and healthcare benefits

Focus: Local climate leadership across Canada

Key responsibilities: Programme management, policy research, policy analysis and strategic stakeholder relationships

Deadline: August 28, 2026

Application link: https://lnkd.in/dQWRCWRv

Conclusion

The Climate Caucus Programs & Policy Senior Manager 2026 opportunity is a strong option for experienced climate and public-policy professionals interested in helping strengthen local climate leadership across Canada.

The fully remote, full-time position combines climate-programme management with research, policy analysis, project leadership and strategic stakeholder engagement.

The successful candidate will be expected to manage climate programmes and multi-year initiatives, lead policy research and analysis, and build relationships that can support stronger community-level climate action.

The position offers an annual salary of $75,000–$80,000 as stated in the vacancy announcement, alongside flexible scheduling, paid time off, healthcare benefits and a $1,200 annual wellness allowance.

Because this is a senior-level role, candidates should demonstrate substantial experience rather than relying solely on academic credentials. Strong applications should clearly communicate measurable accomplishments in policy analysis, programme management, climate action, research and stakeholder engagement.

Applications close on August 28, 2026.
