TITLE: Results for Development (R4D) Program Officer, Scaling Innovation Practice Job in Abuja, Nigeria 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Results for Development (R4D) is hiring a Program Officer, Scaling Innovation Practice, in Abuja, Nigeria, offering an exciting opportunity for experienced professionals interested in global development, technology innovation, science and technology, innovation ecosystems, responsible artificial intelligence, and public policy.

The full-time position will support R4D’s Scaling Innovation Practice and contribute to the delivery of an upcoming programme funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO). The programme focuses on strengthening Nigeria’s science, technology and innovation (STI) ecosystem through partnerships, research-to-enterprise activities, and responsible artificial intelligence research.

The position is based in Abuja, Nigeria, and operates under a hybrid working arrangement combining remote and in-office working days. It is a full-time role of 40 hours per week and is initially offered on a fixed-term basis through 31 March 2027, with the possibility of an extension subject to funding.

For professionals with experience in managing complex programmes, working with innovation ecosystems, engaging government and development partners, conducting research, and translating technical evidence into practical programmes, this R4D vacancy provides an opportunity to contribute directly to major innovation initiatives in Nigeria.

About Results for Development

Results for Development, commonly known as R4D, is a global nonprofit development organisation that works with change agents around the world to develop stronger systems capable of improving people’s lives.

R4D works alongside stakeholders including government officials, civil society leaders and social innovators. Its approach combines expertise in areas such as health, education and nutrition with analytical research, implementation support, practical decision-making and peer-learning networks.

Rather than focusing solely on identifying development problems, R4D works with partners to determine how development objectives can be achieved and how effective systems can become sustainable over the long term.

The organisation describes its workplace as collaborative, creative and entrepreneurial, with diversity, equity and inclusion playing an important role in both its organisational culture and mission.

About R4D’s Scaling Innovation Practice

Innovation can play a major role in addressing complex global development challenges. Across areas including health, education, agriculture and finance, new approaches and technologies have contributed to significant improvements in people’s lives.

R4D’s Scaling Innovation Practice works with partners to help identify, test, strengthen and scale promising solutions while supporting broader innovation systems.

The practice engages a diverse range of actors at the global, regional and country levels. Its work includes helping partners overcome both supply-side and demand-side barriers that can prevent innovations from achieving greater impact.

The team also works to strengthen innovation ecosystems by identifying and addressing gaps, weaknesses and inefficiencies that may prevent innovation from developing or scaling successfully.

Stakeholders involved in this work can include:

Social entrepreneurs

National and subnational governments

Civil society organisations

Development agencies

Researchers and research institutions

Innovation ecosystem organisations

Other development and technical partners

R4D’s Scaling Innovation Practice also contributes to international thought leadership through global innovation initiatives. These include the International Development Innovation Alliance (IDIA), which connects innovation departments from leading development agencies, and the Million Lives Collective, a global multi-stakeholder network supporting proven innovations and their further scale-up.

About the R4D Program Officer Opportunity in Nigeria

R4D is recruiting a Program Officer to join its Scaling Innovation Practice in Abuja.

The successful candidate will support the delivery of an upcoming UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office-funded science, technology and innovation programme in Nigeria.

The programme requires full-time engagement at least until the end of March 2027 and is designed around three complementary workstreams intended to strengthen Nigeria’s science, technology and innovation ecosystem.

1. UK-Nigeria Science and Technology Cluster Partnership

The first workstream focuses on a UK-Nigeria Science and Technology Cluster Partnership.

The Program Officer will contribute to activities such as researching priority sectors, examining international good practices for science and technology cluster models, supporting ecosystem diagnostics, and assessing opportunities that could generate mutual benefits for Nigeria and the United Kingdom.

2. Research-to-Enterprise Pilot

The second workstream is a Research-to-Enterprise Pilot involving selected research institutions.

This area of work will explore approaches for connecting research more effectively with enterprise, including research commercialisation and knowledge transfer.

The Program Officer will contribute research, analysis and technical input to help understand which international models and practices could be relevant to the Nigerian context.

3. Responsible AI Research Initiative

The third workstream focuses on responsible artificial intelligence research.

The initiative will connect Nigerian and UK-based researchers around priorities associated with Nigeria’s national AI agenda. The successful candidate may therefore contribute to research and stakeholder engagement involving responsible AI governance and related innovation policy issues.

Together, the three workstreams place the successful applicant at the intersection of science, technology, innovation, research commercialisation, entrepreneurship and responsible AI.

What the Program Officer Will Do

The Program Officer will take responsibility for significant elements of the Nigeria programme while working as an integral member of R4D’s broader Innovation team.

R4D operates a matrixed resourcing structure, meaning team members may contribute their expertise across different programmes and projects. As a result, the successful candidate may also have opportunities to contribute technical knowledge relating to innovation scaling, innovation ecosystems, innovation policy and practice to other programmes within R4D’s portfolio.

The organisation is specifically looking for someone who is entrepreneurial, strategic and highly organised.

Candidates should be comfortable managing multiple projects and working with geographically dispersed teams, funders, contracts and partnerships while maintaining strong standards for risk management and deliverable quality. Experience in technology innovation, innovation ecosystem strengthening, responsible AI, or science and technology policy is required for the position.

Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities of the R4D Program Officer are divided into four major areas.

1. Project and Programme Management

The successful candidate will support and lead important elements of programme delivery.

Responsibilities include:

Leading significant components of the UK-Nigeria Science and Technology Cluster Partnership and Research-to-Enterprise Pilot.

Researching priority sectors.

Reviewing international good practices relating to cluster models and research-to-enterprise approaches.

Supporting the innovation ecosystem diagnostic process.

Developing and implementing individual workplans aligned with wider programme timelines.

Ensuring innovation activities are delivered on time and to a high standard.

Producing high-quality programme deliverables with appropriate senior guidance.

Supporting data collection for the programme’s monitoring, evaluation and learning strategy.

Collecting relevant stakeholder and innovation ecosystem information.

Identifying and proactively managing risks and programme issues.

Proposing practical options for resolving challenges.

Contributing to and taking ownership of funder progress reports and updates.

Supporting procurement, budgeting and resourcing processes.

Contributing to internal evaluations of programme and project progress.

Technical Research and Analysis Responsibilities

The Program Officer will also provide substantive technical and analytical input across the programme’s three workstreams.

This will include conducting rapid research and stakeholder mapping relating to priority sectors being considered for the UK-Nigeria Science and Technology Cluster.

The successful applicant will be expected to produce evidence-based briefs explaining potential sector opportunities and the possible mutual benefits for Nigeria and the United Kingdom.

Other technical responsibilities include:

Reviewing draft innovation ecosystem diagnostics.

Providing substantive input based on international good practices and lessons relating to cluster models.

Examining research-to-enterprise approaches.

Reviewing international evidence concerning research commercialisation.

Exploring knowledge-transfer approaches.

Reviewing responsible AI governance models that may be relevant to Nigeria.

Developing technical and analytical reports, tools and frameworks.

Contributing new knowledge and approaches relating to innovation ecosystems.

Supporting work relating to research commercialisation and responsible AI.

The successful candidate may lead the development of technical and analytical products across the programme’s three workstreams, with some senior-level support.

Partner and Stakeholder Engagement

Relationship management will be another major component of the position.

The Program Officer will establish and maintain collaborative relationships with partners and stakeholders throughout the innovation ecosystem.

These may include:

Government ministries

Government agencies

Research institutions

Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises

Innovation ecosystem organisations

Downstream delivery partners

Researchers

Private-sector stakeholders

Other programme partners

The Program Officer will need to communicate technical information clearly and develop impactful content suitable for audiences such as government officials, research institutions and private-sector stakeholders.

The role will also involve supporting and, in some instances, leading stakeholder workshops and convenings across the programme’s three workstreams.

Responsibilities can extend to workshop logistics, facilitation and documentation.

Another important element will be supporting engagement with the UK-based Nigerian research diaspora community as part of the responsible AI research initiative.

Contributing to R4D’s Wider Innovation Strategy

The successful candidate will not be limited exclusively to day-to-day programme implementation.

They will also contribute to strengthening R4D’s Scaling Innovation Practice.

Potential responsibilities include:

Producing thought-leadership materials.

Developing or improving methods and tools used by the Innovation Practice.

Supporting operational improvement initiatives.

Contributing to recruitment activities when required.

Supporting business development.

Contributing to funding proposals.

Writing sections of proposals.

Representing R4D and the Innovation Practice at meetings.

Participating in conferences and relevant events.

Contributing to R4D’s internal networks.

Supporting organisational improvement initiatives.

Qualifications and Experience Required

Applicants must meet substantial academic and professional experience requirements.

R4D states that candidates should have either:

A Master’s degree plus at least three years of relevant experience; or

A Bachelor’s degree plus at least five years of relevant experience.

Ideally, the qualification should be in a relevant discipline such as:

Global development

Public policy

Science and technology

Innovation

Another relevant field

However, R4D indicates that candidates with other qualifications providing an equivalent level of professional experience may also be considered.

Essential Professional Experience

Beyond academic qualifications, applicants need relevant programme and technical experience.

Essential requirements include experience in programme and project management within areas such as:

Global development

Innovation

Science and technology

Related ecosystem-based programmes

Candidates must also have experience working in technology innovation, scaling innovation and/or strengthening innovation ecosystems.

Applicants should demonstrate excellent writing, communication and presentation capabilities. This includes experience producing high-quality outputs and facilitating engagement with senior-level or multi-stakeholder audiences, both virtually and in person.

R4D is also seeking candidates who have experience working effectively in matrixed environments involving multiple programmes, teams or workstreams.

Relationship Management and Donor-Funded Programme Experience

Candidates should be able to demonstrate experience developing and managing relationships with diverse development stakeholders at both country and global levels.

These stakeholders may include:

Government actors

Think tanks

Innovation ecosystem organisations

Technical partners

Development partners

Experience managing components of donor-funded programmes is also essential.

R4D specifically mentions FCDO-funded programmes or equivalent experience, including coordinating with partners, subcontractors or implementing organisations.

Skills and Personal Qualities R4D Is Looking For

The organisation is seeking candidates who understand innovation and scaling processes as well as innovation ecosystems.

Applicants should demonstrate that they are:

Strategic and creative problem-solvers.

Highly collaborative and approachable.

Comfortable working closely with colleagues.

Highly organised.

Detail-oriented.

Professional and reliable.

Able to prioritise competing responsibilities.

Capable of working across multiple projects and workstreams.

Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment.

Able to exercise good judgement.

Capable of working independently.

Effective contributors within teams.

Willing to operate in environments that may sometimes involve ambiguity.

Candidates must also be willing to travel occasionally according to project needs. R4D estimates that travel could amount to a maximum of approximately three to four weeks per year.

Legal Right to Work in Nigeria

An especially important eligibility requirement is that all applicants must already be legally authorised to work in Nigeria.

Prospective applicants should carefully consider this condition before applying, particularly those applying from outside Nigeria.

The vacancy information does not indicate that visa sponsorship or relocation assistance will be provided. Candidates should therefore not assume that sponsorship is available unless R4D confirms this separately.

Highly Desirable Qualifications and Experience

In addition to the essential criteria, R4D identifies several qualifications and areas of experience that would strengthen an application.

These include:

A professional qualification in project or programme management.

Experience using innovation methodologies.

Experience with user-centred design.

Experience with agile methodologies.

Experience with adaptive learning.

Experience working directly with innovators or entrepreneurs.

Experience working with other actors within innovation ecosystems.

These criteria are described as highly desirable rather than essential, meaning candidates should distinguish them from the mandatory requirements when assessing their suitability.

Salary for the R4D Program Officer Position

The vacancy lists a potential salary of NGN 13,330,000, with actual compensation dependent on experience and other compensable factors.

R4D states that it seeks to provide equitable and consistent starting salaries for new hires based on the responsibilities and qualifications associated with each position.

The organisation also notes that the broader salary range is intended to provide opportunities for future career and earnings growth.

R4D Employee Benefits

15 days of paid sick leave

Location: Abuja, Nigeria

Why This Opportunity Could Be Particularly Relevant for Innovation Professionals

Donor-funded programme management

Important Points to Consider Before Applying

In particular, candidates should ensure that they:

Have relevant programme or project management experience.

Can demonstrate experience in technology innovation, scaling innovation and/or innovation ecosystem strengthening.

APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The Results for Development Program Officer, Scaling Innovation Practice opportunity in Abuja, Nigeria provides an opportunity for experienced professionals to contribute to the development and implementation of major science, technology and innovation initiatives.

Working within R4D’s Scaling Innovation Practice, the successful candidate will contribute to an FCDO-funded programme built around three important areas: the UK-Nigeria Science and Technology Cluster Partnership, a Research-to-Enterprise Pilot, and a responsible AI research initiative connecting Nigerian and UK-based researchers.

TITLE: Terms of Reference: A Study on the Factors that Affect Female Participation in Science in African Universities

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) in collaboration with the Association of African Universities (AAU) is calling on seasoned researchers to conduct studies on factors that affect female participation in science in African universities.

I. Introduction

Sida is a government agency working on behalf of the Swedish parliament and government, with the mission to reduce poverty in Africa and the world at large. Through it work and cooperation with others, it contributes to implementing Sweden’s Policy for Global Development (PGU). The Association of African Universities (AAU) is an international non-governmental organization (INGO) with headquarters in Accra, Ghana, set up in November 1967 by universities in Africa to promote cooperation among themselves and between them and the international academic community. The AAU collaborates with a number of international organizations and development partners in an effort to fulfil its mandate to the African higher education community.

II. Objectives of the Assignment

Africa’s progress is challenged by a myriad of problems ranging from lack of employment for its youth, the existence of tropical diseases, weak entrepreneurial drive and low levels of university-industry linkages, among others. It is widely accepted, that Science and Technology do have a key role to play in overcoming the continent’s

developmental challenges. However, studies have revealed that though the number of women in science and engineering is growing, men continue to outnumber women, especially at the upper levels of these professions (AAUW, 2010). With only 24% of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) occupations being filled by women, various barriers, ranging from culture, implicit bias and subtle stereotyping to wilful ignorance and blatant discrimination have been identified as contributing factors (Pierce, Margo, 2013). Africa needs to ensure that its human resource – both men and women, are fully engaged in the STEM fields in solving its developmental challenges, and thus should make significant investment into women in STEM to increase their contribution to solving the continent’s challenges. Therefore, AAU is calling on seasoned African scholars to conduct studies on the topic: Factors that Affect Female Participation in Science in African universities. The study should seek to identify empirically those factors, social, economic, political, cultural, etc. that influence female participation in science programmes in African universities.

III. Coordination and Responsibilities

* This study will be implemented under the supervision and guidance of the AAU Director of Research & Academic Planning / Programme Coordinator.

TITLE: Stevens Initiative AI Ignite Lab 2026: AI and Social Impact Program for Young People in the U.S. and UAE

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Stevens Initiative AI Ignite Lab is a pilot program designed to prepare young people in the United States and United Arab Emirates for future careers by combining artificial intelligence, human-centered design, cross-cultural collaboration, digital storytelling, and community-based action.

The program brings together participants between the ages of 18 and 24 from both countries to explore how AI and emerging technologies can be used to address real-world challenges and create positive social impact in their communities.

Through a structured four-week virtual Learning Lab, an intensive two-day Ideas Lab, team collaboration, and a final Day of Action, participants will move from learning about AI and design approaches to developing and implementing practical ideas in their own communities.

The program is intended to help participants develop practical skills that can be applied beyond the program, including AI-supported problem-solving, design thinking, communication, collaboration, leadership, and project development.

What Is the Stevens Initiative AI Ignite Lab?

The AI Ignite Lab is an experiential learning program that connects young people from the United States and the United Arab Emirates.

Rather than focusing only on technical AI knowledge, the program combines technology with human-centered approaches to help participants understand the needs of their communities and develop solutions that respond to real challenges.

The program brings together several areas of learning:

Artificial intelligence and emerging technology

Human-centered design

Cross-cultural collaboration

Digital storytelling

Social impact

Problem-solving

Communication

Leadership

Project development

Participants will work with peers from another country, giving them the opportunity to learn from different perspectives and understand how communities in different cultural contexts approach challenges and opportunities.

How the AI Ignite Lab Works

The program is structured around several connected stages.

Participants first develop their knowledge and skills through the virtual Learning Lab. They then move into an intensive Ideas Lab where they work on turning ideas into concrete plans.

Following this, participants refine their projects with their teams before implementing their plans during the Day of Action.

The program concludes with a virtual celebration where participants return to the full cohort to reflect on their experiences and share what they accomplished.

The Learning Lab is intended to give participants the tools they need to move from identifying community needs to thinking about possible technology-supported solutions.

Artificial Intelligence

Participants will explore AI and emerging technologies and consider how they can be applied to real-world challenges.

The emphasis is not simply on learning about technology but on understanding how technology can potentially contribute to social impact.

Design Thinking

Human-centered design is another important part of the program.

Participants will learn approaches for understanding community needs and developing ideas that are relevant to the people and communities they are intended to serve.

Cross-Cultural Collaboration

Because participants come from the United States and the United Arab Emirates, cross-cultural collaboration is an important element of the experience.

Participants will work alongside people from another cultural context, allowing them to exchange ideas and perspectives while developing their projects.

Social Impact

The program encourages participants to think about how AI and emerging technologies can be used to address challenges within their communities.

The project refinement period is important because participants will be moving from planning to actual implementation.

Participants are expected to emerge from the AI Ignite Lab with practical experience that can contribute to their future academic and professional development.

TITLE: Pitch Perfect Africa 2026: CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship Opportunity for African Health Entrepreneurs

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026, a competitive pitching opportunity designed to support early-stage entrepreneurs developing innovative solutions to health-related challenges across Africa.

Now in its second year, Pitch Perfect Africa provides selected ventures with an opportunity to present their innovations to experienced judges, strengthen their investment readiness, gain valuable pitching experience, and compete for financial support to further develop their work.

The 2026 edition will select six H2i Level 2 ventures to participate in the virtual pitch competition. From these finalists, three ventures will each receive a CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship, providing financial support for the continued development of their ventures.

The program is designed and implemented by the Health Innovation Hub (H2i) under the Africa Health Collaborative, in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation.

What Is Pitch Perfect Africa 2026?

Pitch Perfect Africa is a pitch competition created specifically to provide early-stage ventures within the H2i community with access to funding, pitching opportunities, mentorship-oriented learning, and investment-readiness development.

The initiative recognizes that early-stage health ventures often need more than financial resources to grow. Entrepreneurs also need to be able to clearly communicate their problem, solution, target market, competitive advantage, milestones, and team to potential investors, customers, partners, and other stakeholders.

Through the competition, participating ventures get the opportunity to practice these skills in a competitive environment while presenting their innovations to a panel of expert judges.

The Africa edition of Pitch Perfect was introduced to the H2i African venture community in 2025 and is continuing in 2026.

What Does Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 Offer?

The competition provides selected ventures with several valuable opportunities for development.

1. Opportunity to Pitch to Expert Judges

Six eligible H2i Level 2 ventures will be selected to pitch their innovations to a panel of expert judges.

This provides entrepreneurs with an opportunity to communicate their venture to an experienced audience and receive exposure through a formal pitch competition.

2. CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship

Three of the six ventures selected to pitch will be awarded an Innovation Fellowship worth CAD $5,000 each.

The funding is intended to support the continued development of the winning ventures and their work.

Applicants should note that fellowship payments may take approximately three to four months after the competition to be processed.

3. Investment-Readiness Development

Pitch Perfect Africa is not simply about winning funding. The competition is also intended to help early-stage ventures become better prepared to engage with potential investors and other stakeholders.

Through the pitch preparation process, entrepreneurs can strengthen their ability to explain:

The problem their venture is addressing

Their proposed solution

Their value proposition

Their target market

Their competitors

Their business or venture milestones

Their team

Their broader opportunity for growth

These are important areas for entrepreneurs seeking customers, partnerships, investment, or additional funding.

4. Pitching Experience

For early-stage entrepreneurs, the ability to deliver a clear and convincing pitch can be just as important as having a strong idea.

Pitch Perfect Africa gives participating ventures a structured environment in which they can practice presenting their work, communicating their value, and responding to an expert audience.

Who Can Apply for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026?

The eligibility requirements for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 are specific.

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

Current H2i Level 2 Venture

Applicants must be a current H2i Level 2 HENT venture that was onboarded by its lead mentor by August 31, 2026.

The organizers state that this requirement has no exceptions.

H2i Level 2 ventures are described as ventures in the Discovery stage of H2i’s four-level venture development model.

Therefore, this is not an open competition for every health entrepreneur in Africa. Applicants must already meet the specified H2i Level 2 venture requirement.

Previous Winners Are Not Eligible

Ventures that have previously won Pitch Perfect Africa cannot apply again.

However, past finalists who did not win are welcome to reapply.

Ventures Outside the H2i Community

Entrepreneurs and ventures that are not currently part of the H2i community are encouraged to join the H2i community as a client company.

Joining the H2i community can provide access to:

Mentorship

Programs

Venture development support

Future opportunities

However, simply being interested in the program does not mean a venture automatically qualifies for the 2026 competition. The specific H2i Level 2 eligibility requirement must be met.

Who Is This Opportunity Designed For?

Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 is designed for early-stage health entrepreneurs and health-focused ventures within the H2i African venture community, particularly ventures at the Level 2 Discovery stage.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to entrepreneurs who:

Are developing health-focused innovations

Are currently recognized as eligible H2i Level 2 HENT ventures

Want to strengthen their venture’s pitch

Want to improve investment readiness

Are preparing to communicate their innovation to investors, customers, partners, experts, and judges

Are interested in competing for financial support to continue developing their work

The program is specifically connected to H2i’s African venture community and is designed for African health innovation ventures within the H2i ecosystem.

Therefore, the source supports describing this as an Africa-focused opportunity for eligible H2i ventures, rather than claiming that every health entrepreneur from every African country can independently apply.

Benefits

Each fellowship provides:

Approved return travel from the Fellow’s home country to the in-person bootcamp in Accra, Ghana including, accommodation, travel, and catering.

Approved return travel from the Fellow’s home country to the in-person Capstone Week in London, UK including accommodation, travel, and catering.

Reimbursement of the standard visa application fee.

Eligibility

Be of at least graduate level

Be a citizen of or have been granted refugee status by an eligible low or middle income Commonwealth country

Be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country

Be fluent in written and spoken English

Not have undertaken a Commonwealth Professional Fellowship within the last five years (at the time of taking up the award)

Be available to undertake the fellowship from the prescribed start date (16 November 2026)

Be available to attend the Bootcamp in Accra, Ghana (estimated 25 January – 4 February 2027)

Demonstrate evidence of innovation, in terms of product, service, business model or approach to addressing a market need;

Have progressed beyond the idea, prototype, and pilot stages;

Have been actively operating their business for at least twelve months and be able to demonstrate meaningful progress;

Have a product or service that is available to customers;

Have demonstrated customer demand through paying customers and evidence of ongoing customer adoption (such as repeat purchases, contract renewals, recurring revenue, or sustained usage);

Operate through a sustainable business model and is not primarily dependent on donations, philanthropy, or grant funding;

TITLE: LSHTM Research Fellow and Fully Funded PhD Studentship Opportunities 2026–2027: Data Science, Statistics, Epidemiology and Maternity Inequalities

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) and the NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium (MDC) are offering exciting opportunities for researchers and aspiring doctoral scholars interested in data science, statistics, epidemiology, public health, health inequalities and maternity research.

These opportunities provide applicants with the chance to contribute to major research programmes focused on improving health outcomes, addressing inequalities and using large-scale routinely collected healthcare data to generate evidence that can influence policy and practice.

There are two closely related opportunities to consider. The first is for Research Fellows in Data Science, Statistics or Epidemiology at LSHTM, while the second is a funded PhD studentship under the NIHR Inequalities Challenge: Maternity Disparities Consortium.

Both opportunities are particularly relevant to candidates with strong quantitative research skills who are interested in using advanced analytical methods and large datasets to tackle important public health challenges.

1. LSHTM Research Fellow in Data Science, Statistics or Epidemiology

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine is recruiting two Research Fellows to join the Department of Health Services Research & Policy.

The successful researchers will work within the DELTA core function of the NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium, a major national programme designed to improve maternity and neonatal outcomes across the United Kingdom and reduce inequalities before, during and after pregnancy.

The position presents an excellent opportunity for researchers who want to develop or advance a career in big data research, healthcare analytics, epidemiology, statistics or health services research.

About the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine

LSHTM is internationally recognised for its work in public health, tropical medicine, epidemiology, health policy and global health research.

Its mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide through research, education, partnerships and the translation of evidence into policy and practice.

Researchers joining LSHTM can therefore expect to work in an academically strong environment where research findings can contribute to real-world health and policy decisions.

2. What the Research Fellow Role Involves

The Research Fellows will be involved in analysing routinely collected linked national datasets covering mothers and babies in England.

This means the researchers will have the opportunity to work with large-scale healthcare data and conduct sophisticated analyses to better understand maternity outcomes and disparities.

The role is particularly suited to someone who wants to develop expertise in:

Data science

Statistics

Epidemiology

Healthcare data analysis

Health services research

Large observational studies

Routinely collected healthcare data

Linked national datasets

Quantitative research

Public health research

Maternity and neonatal outcomes

Health inequalities

The successful candidate may come from a background in large observational healthcare studies, although experience analysing clinical trials may also be relevant.

The position is therefore not restricted exclusively to applicants whose previous research has focused on maternity care. Candidates with strong methodological and quantitative research experience may also be suitable.

3. Research Fellow Positions and Working Arrangement

There are two positions available.

The posts are:

Based in the Department of Health Services Research & Policy

Located in London

Available full-time or part-time

Between 17.5 and 35 hours per week

Equivalent to 0.5–1.0 FTE

Fixed-term until 31 May 2028

One position is available immediately, while the second position is scheduled to become available from 1 September 2026.

This flexibility may make the opportunity particularly attractive to researchers who are looking for either a full-time research career or a part-time research appointment.

4. Research Fellow Salary and Benefits

The salary is on the LSHTM Grade 6 salary scale:

£45,728 to £51,872 per annum pro rata, inclusive of London Weighting.

Because the positions can be part-time, the salary is paid on a pro-rata basis depending on the individual’s FTE appointment.

Additional benefits include:

30 working days of annual leave per year, pro rata for part-time staff

Discretionary Wellbeing Days

Access to the Pension Scheme

Employment under LSHTM terms and conditions of service

The opportunity to work within a leading public health research institution

Experience working with large-scale linked national healthcare datasets

Exposure to major national research programmes

The role could therefore provide valuable experience for researchers seeking to build a long-term career in academic research, health data science, epidemiology, statistics or public health.

5. Who Should Consider the Research Fellow Position?

The role is particularly appropriate for applicants with strong expertise in data science, statistics or epidemiology.

The successful applicant is expected to have a postgraduate qualification, with a doctoral degree ideally preferred, in a relevant field.

Candidates with experience in analysing large observational healthcare datasets would be especially relevant, although applicants with experience analysing clinical trial data may also be considered.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate strong quantitative and analytical capabilities and an interest in using research evidence to understand healthcare outcomes and inequalities.

6. NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium PhD Studentship

The second opportunity is part of the NIHR Inequalities Challenge: Maternity Disparities Consortium.

The Consortium is offering up to 13 funded PhD studentships across a range of projects hosted by universities within the Consortium.

The programme is designed to develop the next generation of researchers capable of addressing persistent inequalities in maternity and neonatal health.

The studentships are particularly focused on strengthening research capacity in methodological areas where additional expertise is needed.

These areas include, but are not limited to:

Health economics

Statistics

Trial design

Digital research

Data science

Implementation science

Co-production methods

Quantitative research

Health inequalities research

The PhD programme is therefore broader than maternity clinical research alone. Applicants with methodological expertise who can apply their skills to maternity inequalities are encouraged to consider the opportunity.

7. About the Maternity Disparities Consortium

The NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium is a UK-wide collaboration involving:

Universities

NHS trusts

Local councils

Charities

Industry partners

Researchers

Communities

Other organisations working to improve maternity outcomes

The Consortium aims to improve outcomes for women and babies before, during and after pregnancy while developing a new generation of research leaders.

Its capacity development programme focuses on building long-term research expertise and strengthening the workforce required to deliver sustainable improvements in maternity health.

Particular emphasis is placed on research capacity in underrepresented disciplines, professions and underserved communities.

8. The Featured PhD Research Project

One of the available projects is titled:

“Developing a unified conceptual and measurement framework of maternity inequalities to inform policy using routinely collected national data.”

The project is based at LSHTM and is identified by the project code:

D1.2_LSHTM

The research will investigate how different forms of disadvantage contribute to inequalities in maternity outcomes.

The project recognises that maternity inequalities can be influenced by multiple interacting factors rather than by a single characteristic.

While existing UK research has extensively examined factors such as ethnicity and area-based deprivation, there is comparatively less research examining other determinants and how multiple disadvantages interact.

The project therefore aims to develop better ways of identifying and measuring these factors using routinely collected national data.

9. Why This Research Matters

Understanding maternity inequalities requires more than identifying which groups experience poorer outcomes.

Researchers also need to understand:

What causes these inequalities

Which factors contribute to disadvantage

How different disadvantages interact

Which populations experience multiple forms of disadvantage

How inequalities influence access to maternity services

How inequalities affect health outcomes

Which interventions could reduce these inequalities

Which policies are most likely to benefit populations experiencing the greatest disadvantage

At present, routinely collected national datasets do not always contain standardised or reliable measurements for all relevant determinants of disadvantage.

The proposed PhD will therefore attempt to improve how these factors are measured and analysed.

This could help researchers and policymakers identify vulnerable populations more accurately and design interventions that are better targeted to their circumstances.

10. Main Aim of the PhD Project

The overall aim is to develop a conceptual and measurement framework for maternity inequalities.

The framework will seek to provide a better understanding of:

Individual-level determinants of disadvantage

Household-level determinants

Place-based determinants

Relationships between different determinants

Mechanisms through which disadvantage affects maternity outcomes

The accumulation of multiple disadvantages

Interactions between different forms of disadvantage

The research will combine theoretical approaches with data-driven methods and applied studies using routinely collected national datasets.

11. Research Objectives

The PhD project has three major research objectives.

Objective 1: Conduct a realist review and framework synthesis

The first stage will involve a comprehensive review of existing evidence.

The researcher will conduct a realist review and framework synthesis to identify determinants of inequality and develop an understanding of the plausible pathways through which these factors influence maternity outcomes.

This will help establish the theoretical foundation for the project.

Objective 2: Develop standardised measurement and coding frameworks

The second objective involves developing standardised and validated coding frameworks that can be used to measure determinants of disadvantage in routinely collected national datasets.

The project will use data science methods to improve the identification and measurement of factors that may currently be poorly captured.

Particular attention will be given to under-researched factors including:

Disability

Neurodivergent conditions

Language needs

Interpreter requirements

Migration status

Mental health conditions

Gender-based violence

Food insecurity

Housing insecurity

This component could involve significant data management, coding, statistical analysis and methodological development.

Objective 3: Apply the frameworks to maternity research

The third objective will involve applying the newly developed frameworks in up to three studies.

These studies may examine:

How different determinants accumulate

How multiple forms of disadvantage interact

The relationship between disadvantage and maternity outcomes

Family outcomes

The potential effects of interventions on different populations

How advanced statistical methods can be used to model intervention effects

This stage will allow the researcher to demonstrate how the framework works in practical research settings.

12. Expected Impact of the PhD

The project is expected to contribute to maternity health equity research by combining theory-driven and data-driven approaches.

The research could help demonstrate both the strengths and limitations of routinely collected healthcare data when conducting equity-focused research.

A major intended outcome is to improve the identification of populations experiencing multiple or intersecting forms of disadvantage.

Better measurement could ultimately help researchers and policymakers:

Identify populations at increased risk more accurately.

Understand the mechanisms behind maternity inequalities.

Design more targeted interventions.

Evaluate policies aimed at reducing inequalities.

Improve the evidence available to national studies.

Support the development and scaling of effective interventions.

Strengthen maternity health policy.

Apply the resulting methodological approaches beyond maternity care.

Potentially adapt the methods for use in other countries and healthcare systems.

The project’s impact therefore extends beyond the immediate maternity research setting.

13. Funding Package for the PhD Studentship

The PhD studentships provide substantial financial support.

Successful students will receive:

Full tuition fees

Research and training allowance

This can provide valuable additional support for activities required during the doctoral research.

14. Duration and Start Date

The PhD programme is scheduled to begin in:

January 2027

The duration can be:

Up to 3 years full-time, or

Up to 4 years at 0.8 WTE part-time, where this arrangement can be agreed.

Students will be required to meet the regulations and registration requirements of their host university.

15. International Students Can Apply

International applicants are welcome to apply for the PhD studentships.

However, there is an important financial condition for international candidates.

The studentship covers full home tuition fees at the relevant UK rate, but international applicants must secure alternative funding to cover the difference between UK and overseas tuition fees.

International candidates must also be prepared to provide proof of funding for international fees and immigration costs before their interview if they are shortlisted.

This is an important consideration for applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, Latin America, the Caribbean, Oceania and other regions outside the UK.

Applicants should therefore carefully assess the total cost of overseas tuition and immigration requirements before submitting an application.

16. Eligibility Requirements for the PhD

Applicants should meet the essential eligibility criteria.

Academic qualification

Applicants must normally hold:

A First-Class or Upper Second-Class Honours degree, equivalent to a UK 2:1 or above, in a relevant subject.

Relevant disciplines may include:

Statistics

Applied Mathematics

Data Science

Computer Science

Or a similar quantitative or methodological discipline

An overseas qualification equivalent to the required UK academic standard is acceptable.

Master’s degree

A Master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field is recommended.

While the information describes the Master’s as recommended rather than an absolute essential requirement, applicants should assess their academic profile against the specific requirements of the host institution.

Research experience

Applicants should have relevant previous research experience.

This experience may relate to either:

The substantive research area, or

The methodological area.

Therefore, applicants do not necessarily need to have previously specialised in maternity research if they can demonstrate strong methodological expertise and explain how their background can contribute to research on maternity inequalities.

Quantitative research skills

Applicants should have strong quantitative research skills and experience analysing complex datasets.

Experience with routinely collected data would be particularly advantageous.

Commitment to maternity inequalities

Applicants should demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to tackling maternity inequalities.

This is particularly important because the project is designed to address disparities in health outcomes and access to care.

Communication

Applicants should demonstrate excellent:

Written communication skills

Verbal communication skills

Academic communication

Research communication

Independence and teamwork

Candidates should be:

Highly motivated

Able to work independently

Able to work effectively as part of a team

Capable of planning and managing their own workload

17. Who Is Particularly Encouraged to Apply?

The NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium states that it particularly encourages applications from people who are passionate about maternity health equity and who can contribute relevant methodological knowledge and experience.

The programme specifically encourages applications from:

People from underrepresented ethnic backgrounds

People with disabilities

Neurodivergent people

People with long-term health requirements

Candidates of all genders

Candidates of all ages

Candidates of all beliefs

Applicants with experience in a broad range of research methodologies

Applicants should not assume that they are unsuitable simply because their previous academic discipline is not explicitly labelled “maternity research.”

If the connection between their academic background and maternity inequalities is not immediately obvious, applicants are encouraged to clearly explain that connection in their cover letter.

26. Why Routinely Collected Data Is Central to These Opportunities

One of the most important themes running through both opportunities is the use of routinely collected healthcare data.

Routine data can provide researchers with information about very large populations and can allow researchers to examine health outcomes across different demographic, geographic and social groups.

However, such datasets can also have limitations.

Some important characteristics may be incompletely recorded, inconsistently coded or difficult to identify.

This is particularly important when studying health inequalities.

For example, researchers may need better ways of identifying:

Disability

Neurodivergence

Language barriers

Migration status

Mental health conditions

Experiences of gender-based violence

Food insecurity

Housing insecurity

The proposed PhD therefore addresses an important methodological challenge: improving the ability of researchers to measure complex and intersecting forms of disadvantage using existing national data.

27. A Major Opportunity for International Researchers

The PhD programme is particularly noteworthy for international applicants because the Consortium explicitly states that international students are welcome to apply.

However, international applicants should understand the financial arrangement before applying.

TITLE: Schuman Challenge 2027: EU-U.S. Academic Competition for Undergraduate Students

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Schuman Challenge is an annual academic competition organized by the Delegation of the European Union to the United States for undergraduate students enrolled at colleges and universities across the United States. The competition gives students the opportunity to conduct original research, develop practical policy recommendations on transatlantic issues, and present and defend their ideas before a panel of judges.

Registration for the 2027 edition is now open.

The Schuman Challenge is designed to encourage undergraduate students to engage with major issues affecting relations between the European Union and the United States. Through research, teamwork, policy analysis, public speaking and critical thinking, participants are challenged to examine a specific topic selected by the EU Delegation and develop actionable recommendations.

For students interested in international relations, political science, diplomacy, European studies, foreign policy, international security, economics, technology, public policy and transatlantic affairs, the Schuman Challenge provides an opportunity to apply academic knowledge to a real-world policy question.

About the Schuman Challenge

The Schuman Challenge is the annual foreign affairs contest organized by the European Union Delegation to the United States.

The competition focuses on EU-U.S. relations and asks participating undergraduate teams to develop policy recommendations addressing a specific topic announced by the EU Delegation.

Rather than simply writing an academic paper, participants must be prepared to present, explain and defend their recommendations before judges.

What Participants Are Expected to Do

Each participating team is expected to:

Conduct original research on the competition topic.

Examine relevant evidence and sources.

Develop actionable policy recommendations.

Prepare a 10-minute presentation.

Present the proposal to a panel of judges.

Participate in a 10-minute question-and-answer session.

Defend the team’s recommendations and respond to questions from the judges.

The competition therefore combines academic research, policy analysis, teamwork, public speaking, critical thinking and communication skills.

Schuman Challenge 2027 Registration

Registration for the 2027 edition of the Schuman Challenge is now open.

The competition is organized specifically for undergraduate students at U.S. colleges and universities. Each participating institution can enter one team consisting of three to four undergraduate students.

Prospective participants should carefully review the official registration requirements and any updated competition guidance before registering.

2027 Application Deadline

The official page provided states that registration for the 2027 edition is open, but it does not currently state a specific closing deadline.

Applicants should therefore monitor the official registration page and the EU Delegation’s Schuman Challenge webpage for updates regarding the application deadline, competition topic and detailed 2027 requirements.

How the Schuman Challenge Works

The competition is structured around several stages that give participating teams the opportunity to progress from an online preliminary round to an in-person competition in Washington, D.C.

1. University or College Registration

The Schuman Challenge operates on a university and college team basis.

Only one team from each university or college can compete.

Each team consists of three to four undergraduate students.

Students interested in participating should therefore coordinate with their institution and determine how their university or college will organize its team.

2. Preliminary Round

The preliminary round takes place online in a live format.

Participating teams present their proposals to a panel of three judges.

The preliminary rounds are held on multiple dates.

During this stage, teams are expected to demonstrate their understanding of the assigned issue, explain their recommendations clearly and respond effectively to questions from the judges.

3. Semi-Final Round in Washington, D.C.

Fifteen teams qualify from the preliminary round and are invited to participate in the semi-final stage.

The semi-final takes place in person at the EU Delegation’s office in Washington, D.C.

The selected teams present their proposals to EU officials and experts.

Semi-finalist teams receive a travel stipend and accommodation in Washington, D.C., according to the competition information.

4. Final Round

Three teams progress from the semi-final stage to the final round.

The final round also takes place in Washington, D.C.

The finalist teams present their proposals and compete for the opportunity to become the winning team of the Schuman Challenge.

The Schuman Challenge Presentation Format

Each team gives a 10-minute presentation followed by a 10-minute question-and-answer session with the judges.

Visual aids may be used during the presentation.

This means participants need to be able to communicate complex policy issues in a clear and structured manner while also responding to questions under pressure.

The presentation should demonstrate the team’s understanding of the issue, the evidence supporting its position and the practical nature of its recommendations.

Research Requirements

Participants are expected to conduct original research, cite sources and prepare policy proposals based on credible evidence.

Teams Should Be Prepared To:

Identify the central policy challenge.

Research the existing EU-U.S. relationship relating to the issue.

Examine relevant evidence and existing policies.

Identify challenges, gaps or opportunities.

Develop an actionable policy recommendation.

Support their proposal with credible sources.

Prepare a structured presentation.

Anticipate questions from the judges.

Defend their recommendations during the Q&A session.

The Winning Team’s Prize

The winning team receives a four-day Victory Tour of Brussels, the headquarters of the European Union.

During the Victory Tour, the winning students have the opportunity to visit EU institutions and engage with officials and organizations involved in European policymaking.

The winning team also has the opportunity to present its winning policy proposal to EU officials.

What the Victory Tour Can Include

The prize provides the winning students with opportunities to:

Visit European Union institutions.

Meet or engage with EU officials.

Visit relevant organizations and think tanks.

Present their winning policy proposal.

Gain exposure to European policymaking.

Learn more about EU-U.S. relations and transatlantic cooperation.

The 2026 Schuman Challenge

The 2026 edition of the Schuman Challenge took place on April 7–8, 2026, at the EU Delegation’s office in Washington, D.C.

The 2026 competition focused on the future of EU-U.S. cooperation on security.

The competition topic asked students to develop a policy proposal analyzing the current state of EU-U.S. cooperation on security and proposing an initiative or policy that could strengthen the partnership in the coming years.

2026 Competition Areas

Teams were required to consider two of four areas:

Defense

Economy, trade and energy

Technology and digital

Arctic cooperation

The topic was connected to the 250th anniversary of the signing of the U.S. Declaration of Independence and the evolution of the transatlantic relationship.

2026 Participation and Results

The 2026 edition involved universities from across the United States.

According to the EU Delegation:

34 universities participated in the preliminary rounds.

The participating universities represented 20 U.S. states and Washington, D.C.

15 teams advanced to the semi-final round.

Three teams advanced to the final round.

2026 Final Results

Macalester College, Minnesota

Patrick Henry College, Virginia

Stanford University, California

Macalester College won the 2026 competition.

The winning team developed a proposal called the “Atlantic Cable Infrastructure Program.” The proposal focused on cooperation between the European Union and United States to monitor, maintain and defend transatlantic cable systems using new technology.

The second- and third-placed teams were also commended for their policy proposals.

Skills Students Can Develop

The Schuman Challenge provides participants with an opportunity to develop practical skills that can be useful in academic, policy, diplomatic and professional environments.

Research Skills

Students conduct original research and use credible sources to support their recommendations.

Policy Analysis

Participants examine complex international issues and develop practical policy proposals.

Public Speaking

Each team must deliver a 10-minute presentation before judges.

Critical Thinking

Participants need to analyze the assigned issue and respond to questions about their recommendations.

Teamwork

Teams consist of three to four students, requiring participants to coordinate research, writing, presentation preparation and responses.

Communication

Students must explain complicated international policy issues in a clear and understandable manner.

International Affairs

The competition provides students with exposure to issues involving EU-U.S. relations, foreign affairs and transatlantic cooperation.

Who Should Consider This Opportunity?

The Schuman Challenge may be particularly relevant to undergraduate students interested in fields such as:

Political Science

International Relations

International Affairs

Diplomacy

European Studies

Foreign Policy

Security Studies

International Economics

Technology Policy

Public Policy

Government

International Development

Strategic Studies

However, the competition is not limited to one specific academic discipline. The key requirement is that participants meet the official eligibility requirements and can contribute effectively to their university’s team.

Important Eligibility Information

The Schuman Challenge is specifically designed for undergraduate students from U.S. colleges and universities.

Each university or college may enter only one team.

Teams consist of three to four undergraduate students.

Geographic Eligibility

The official competition description identifies undergraduate students from colleges and universities in the United States as the target participants.

Students studying at universities outside the United States should not assume that they are eligible simply because they are undergraduate students.

The competition is therefore not presented as an open worldwide opportunity for undergraduate students.

Benefits of Participating

Participating in the Schuman Challenge can provide students with several valuable experiences, including:

Opportunity to conduct original policy research.

Experience developing actionable policy recommendations.

Opportunity to present before judges and experts.

Exposure to EU officials and experts.

Experience participating in an academic foreign affairs competition.

Travel opportunity for qualifying teams to Washington, D.C.

Travel stipend and accommodation for semi-finalist teams.

Opportunity for the winning team to travel to Brussels.

Opportunity to visit EU institutions.

Opportunity to present to EU officials.

Development of teamwork and leadership skills.

Development of public speaking and presentation skills.

Exposure to transatlantic policy issues.

How to Prepare for the Schuman Challenge 2027

Students and universities interested in participating can begin preparing by taking the following steps.

Step 1: Form a Team

Identify three or four eligible undergraduate students who can work effectively together.

Step 2: Coordinate With Your University

Since only one team can represent each university or college, students should communicate with the relevant department, faculty, international affairs office or university administration about participation.

Step 3: Follow the Official 2027 Topic

The competition topic is determined by the EU Delegation. Teams should carefully study the official 2027 instructions once the topic and competition guide are available.

Step 4: Conduct Original Research

Use credible academic, governmental and institutional sources to understand the issue and the existing EU-U.S. relationship.

Step 5: Develop an Actionable Policy Proposal

Teams should develop a practical proposal rather than simply describing a problem.

Step 6: Prepare for Questions

Judges will have the opportunity to question participants, so teams should anticipate possible challenges to their recommendations.

Step 7: Practice the Presentation

The 10-minute presentation limit means teams should practice extensively to ensure that their most important arguments are presented clearly within the allotted time.

Conclusion

The Schuman Challenge 2027 is an academic competition that gives undergraduate students at U.S. colleges and universities an opportunity to engage with important issues concerning the European Union and the United States.

The competition combines original research, policy analysis, teamwork, public speaking and the development of actionable recommendations. Participants begin with an online preliminary stage, while successful teams can progress to an in-person competition in Washington, D.C.

Fifteen teams advance to the semi-final stage, three teams reach the final, and the winning team receives a four-day Victory Tour of Brussels, where students can visit EU institutions and present their winning proposal to EU officials.

With registration for the 2027 edition now open, eligible undergraduate students and U.S. universities can begin preparing their teams.

TITLE: Press Release – The Association of African Universities (AAU) signs a Memorandum of Understanding with the China Association of Higher Education (CAHE) to promote China-Africa Universities Collaboration

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Accra, Ghana and Peking, China 17 November 2022 – The Association of African Universities (AAU), and the China Association of Higher Education (CAHE), have signed a five-year Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to collaborate in areas of mutual interest for the benefit of higher education institutions and other stakeholders within their respective regions.

The MOU, signed by Prof. Olusola Bandele Oyewole on behalf of the AAU and Mr. Jiang Enlai on behalf of CAHE, on November 15, 2022, seals an agreement spearheading the collaborative efforts of the two strategic partners, and paves the way for the implementation of a rich portfolio of activities and initiatives aimed at addressing the pressing needs of higher education institutions.

The key focus areas of the agreement include the establishment of a China-Africa Consortium of Universities Exchange Mechanism targeted at bringing together universities, educational institutions and research institutions of both sides for regular cooperation and annual strategic meetings; the formation of a research network between China and Africa to compile and publish guidelines on higher education in China and Africa; and the promotion of scholarships and grants for African students to pursue postgraduate studies in China.

A high-powered delegation from the Chinese side, comprising Mr. Du Yubo (President, CAHE), Mr. Zhang Daliang (Deputy President, CAHE), Mr. Zhou Yu (Deputy President, CAHE), Mr. Jia Peng (Deputy Director of Department of International Cooperation and Exchange, Ministry of Education, China), and Mr. Yang Zhou (Director of Asia and Africa Branch, Department of International Cooperation and Exchange, MOE, China), were present for the MoU signing ceremony. Also present were Mr. Jiang Enlai (Deputy President and Secretary-General, CAHE), Mr. Hao Qingjie (Deputy Secretary-General, CAHE), Ms. Gao Xiaojie (Director, Department of Academic and Exchange Affairs, CAHE) and Prof. Peng Yi (Foreign Affairs, Department of Academic and Exchange Affairs, CAHE).

The AAU delegation was led by Professor Bakri Saeed Osman (President, AAU), Professor Olusola Bandele Oyewole (Secretary-General, AAU), Professor Damtew Teferra (Director, Directorate of Research and Programs, AAU), Ms. Nodumo Dhlamini (Director, Directorate of ICT Services, Communication and Knowledge Management, AAU), Mr. Ransford Bekoe (Partnerships Manager) and Mrs. Ruth Nyarko (Program Officer, Directorate of Research and Programs, AAU).

In their opening remarks at the MoU signing event, both Presidents of CAHE and the AAU, Mr. Du Yubo and Prof. Bakri Saeed Osman respectively highlighted the importance of education to socio-economic development and emphasised the crucial role the Memorandum of Understanding between the two sister organizations will play in facilitating cooperation and collaboration among the institutions of higher education in China and Africa.

“The demographic dividend of a youthful Africa requires the provision of quality education to them as a key intervention to overcoming poverty, ignorance, and diseases. The AAU, as Africa’s apex higher education institution, has positioned itself to promote interchange, contact and cooperation among African universities and between them and the international academic community. We will continue to partner with strategic institutions and stakeholders as we pursue our goals and objectives”– said Prof. Olusola Oyewole, Secretary General of the AAU.

Mr. Jiang Enlai listed the multi-tiered and diversified China-Africa higher education collaboration including the Forum of China Africa Education Ministers, the 20+20 Cooperation plan of China’s Ministry of Education establishing partnerships between 20 Chinese and 20 African Universities (in 17 African countries) and the Africa-China Vocational Education plan that has been established. This current MoU is thus a great addition to its portfolio of collaboration with African higher education institutions.

Overall, the cooperation, kick-started with the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding between the Association of African Universities and the China Association of Higher Education is a leap for both institutions in enriching their partnerships at a global level and in creating the platform for sharing of experiences and deepening of exchanges to support their respective efforts of advancing higher education in Africa and China.

About the Partnering Organizations

The Association of African Universities (AAU) | aau.org

The Association of African Universities (AAU) is the apex higher education organization in Africa and represents the voice of Africa’s higher education on regional and international bodies. Established in Rabat (Morocco) in 1967, the AAU currently has a membership of over 400 institutions of higher learning across all the linguistic and geographic divides of Africa. Its headquarters is in Accra, Ghana and it currently has two regional offices – East Africa Regional Office (hosted by the University of Khartoum in Sudan) and the North Africa Regional Office (hosted by the Al Azhar University in Egypt), as well as a Country Office in Abuja, Nigeria. The AAU has partnership offices in North American universities.

The AAU supports African universities to deliver quality higher education and, as its niche, creates a platform for networking among its members. The Association enjoys a unique capacity for convening most of the higher education community in Africa to reflect and consult on key issues affecting education on the continent. The thrust of its base is the nimble deploying of advocacy, commissioning of studies, and acting and becoming the clearing house and intelligence arm for these higher education institutions on the continent.

The AAU operates in four languages namely, English, French, Arabic and Portuguese. It endeavours to raise the quality of higher education in Africa and strengthen its contribution to Africa’s development by fostering collaboration among its member institutions; providing support to their core functions of teaching, learning, research, and community engagement; and facilitating critical reflection on, and consensus-building around, issues affecting higher education and the development of Africa.

The China Association of Higher Education (CAHE) | chinahighereducation.org

China Association of Higher Education (CAHE) was founded in 1983, as a non-profit academic organization, CAHE is an alliance of voluntary social organizations, institutions and professionals that are engaged in or support higher education.

CAHE is the largest, oldest and the most influential national academic organization of higher education. Currently, CAHE consists of 68 branches and nearly 1700 higher education institution members with their own members, forming a platform covering a wide range of disciplines and management areas by connecting more than 3000 Chinese Universities. CAHE performs the following functions in accordance to the CAHE Charter: theoretical research, academic communications, professional training, demonstrations and exhibitions, international co-operations, consultations, books and journals editing and industry monitoring etc.

In recent years, CAHE has built brands around the five constructional pillars, namely: first – the “Annual International Forum on Higher Education”, which has held 21 sessions so far, attracting experts and scholars from more than 50 countries and from important organizations such as UNESCO, the World Bank, and the OECD; secondly – the “China Higher Education Expo”, which has so far held 57 sessions, and is a comprehensive brand exhibition in the field of higher education in China; third – the “China Higher Education Research” Journal, an authoritative academic journal in the field of higher education in China; fourth – a new high-end think tank platform, which gathers top experts and scholars to carry out research and provide consulting services for government’s policy decision; and fifth – the China Higher Education Training Center, which mainly carries out teacher training.
