GSU states in its frequently asked questions that admission decisions are generally released within 60 days after the relevant application deadline. A request to defer an admission offer should normally be submitted within seven days of receiving the offer, although deferral approval is not guaranteed.

About Global Studies University in Sharjah

Global Studies University is based in Al Manakh, Sharjah, United Arab Emirates. Its academic model combines the humanities, social sciences, arts and language study, with particular attention to Africa and its historical and contemporary relationships with other parts of the world.

The university operates from the restored former Khalid bin Mohammed School, a mid-1970s landmark. Its campus covers more than 23,000 square metres and includes:

Classrooms and collaborative learning spaces

A university library

Research archives

Galleries and exhibition areas

Student lounges

Courtyards

A café and bookshop

Recreational courts

Prayer rooms

Accessible washrooms and facilities

Parking areas

Africa Hall, first inaugurated in 1976 and reopened following renovation in 2018, provides a venue for conferences, public lectures, film programs and musical events. Additional information is available on the official GSU campus page.

GSU states that it is licensed by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research through the Commission for Academic Accreditation. The university’s institutional licensure, MA program and PhD program are listed as active from January 2025 to January 2028. The institution reports that its two graduate degrees received accreditation on January 28, 2025. Prospective students can examine the university’s official accreditation information and should independently confirm whether the degrees satisfy any professional or academic recognition requirements relevant to their plans.

Programs Available at Global Studies University

GSU highlights three principal study routes:

A two-year MA in Global African Studies.

A five-year PhD in Global Studies.

Short certificate courses in Arabic, Amharic, Hausa and Kiswahili for non-native speakers.

The MA and PhD are full-time, on-campus degrees taught in English in Sharjah. They are not advertised as online or distance-learning programs. The shorter language certificates follow a different structure and are available through online and hybrid delivery.

MA in Global African Studies

The MA in Global African Studies is a two-year, full-time, on-campus degree taught in English. It requires 36 credits and is intended for students seeking advanced interdisciplinary knowledge of Africa’s intellectual, political, social, cultural and international dimensions.

The curriculum combines common theory and methods courses, specialization courses, electives, African-language study, an internship and an independently researched thesis. Students select one of three tracks.

Museum and Critical Heritage Studies

The Museum and Critical Heritage Studies track investigates how museums, archives, archaeology, cultural property and heritage institutions influence interpretations of the past.

It examines questions involving ownership, restitution, colonial legacies, exhibition ethics, cultural representation and professional museum practice.

Published specialization courses include:

Who Owns the Past? Politics and Heritage in Africa

History and Theory of Museums

Decolonizing Heritage

Museum Collections Management and Politics of Exhibitions

Ethics, Archaeology and Heritage

Museum Management and Heritage as a Career

This track may appeal to applicants interested in museums, galleries, archives, cultural policy, archaeology, curatorial practice, collections management, heritage conservation or debates about the ownership and representation of cultural objects.

Diplomacy and Africa’s International Relations

This track concentrates on diplomacy, international relations, foreign policy, global governance, political economy and Africa’s historical and contemporary position within international society.

Published specialization courses include:

Diplomacy Studies

Advanced International Relations Theory

Africa in the World: Past and Present

Political Economy of Africa

International Finance and Global Economic Governance

State, International Society and Empire

The track may be relevant to students considering careers or further research in diplomacy, foreign affairs, government, international organizations, development, policy analysis, political economy and global governance.

Afro-Arab Relations

The Afro-Arab Relations track explores the long and complex interactions between African and Arab societies. Its historical scope extends from ancient periods through the Ottoman era and into modern political, intellectual and social formations.

Published courses include:

Introduction to Afro-Arab Relations: From Ancient Times to the Ottoman Empire

Comparative Slavery: The Transatlantic and Indian Ocean Worlds

Comparative Apartheid and Settler Colonialism: Palestine and South Africa

The Casablanca Group and Monrovia Group: The Formation of the Organisation of African Unity

Africa in the World: Past and Present

State, International Society and Empire

This track provides a structured foundation for studying the Red Sea, Indian Ocean networks, colonialism, slavery, liberation movements, international institutions and the political histories connecting African and Arab societies.

MA Program Structure

The 36-credit MA is organized as follows:

Six credits of common core courses

Eighteen credits of specialization core courses

Six credits of electives

A pass-or-fail language component

A pass-or-fail internship

A six-credit master’s thesis

The two common core courses are Theory and Method I and Theory and Method II.

Electives listed by GSU include:

Foreign Policy Analysis

Social and Political Thought in Africa

Government and Politics of Africa

The State in Africa

Every MA student studies one African language for three semesters. The available languages are Arabic, Amharic, Hausa and Kiswahili. Students receive a language certificate in addition to completing their degree requirements.

Students must also complete a thesis, which is written, examined and defended through a viva voce examination.

The required internship adds practical experience to the academic program. GSU’s career services advertise internship assistance, career advising, employability workshops, employer engagement, institutional visits and career events.

MA Admission Requirements

Prospective MA students should prepare the following:

A bachelor’s degree from an independently accredited institution recognized by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research and GSU.

A minimum bachelor’s cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent.

An official bachelor’s transcript and graduation certificate with the required attestations.

A legal English translation of academic documents not originally issued in English.

A UAE Certificate of Recognition for a qualification awarded outside the UAE.

A valid passport.

A recent passport-sized photograph.

Emirates ID and UAE visa copies, where applicable.

IELTS Academic 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 91.

A current curriculum vitae.

Two recommendation letters issued within one month before application submission.

A Statement of Interest of approximately 1,000–1,500 words.

One substantial academic writing sample comparable to a journal article.

A national-service no-objection certificate where required for male Emirati applicants.

The AED 365 non-refundable application fee, unless the early complete-application waiver applies.

The Statement of Interest should explain the applicant’s personal and academic journey, motivation, future aspirations, suitability for GSU, research interests, proposed area of study and preferred MA track.

The academic writing sample can be an article, essay, book chapter, thesis chapter or comparable piece of scholarly work. A strong sample should demonstrate research ability, critical thinking, logical organization, evidence-based argument and appropriate academic referencing.

Shortlisted candidates may be invited to an interview in person or through Zoom. GSU states that applications remaining incomplete after the deadline will be rejected. The university also says that applicants previously dismissed from another institution for academic-integrity violations are not eligible for admission.

PhD in Global Studies

The PhD in Global Studies is a five-year, full-time, on-campus doctoral program taught in English. Its structure combines two years of coursework with approximately three years devoted to advanced research and the doctoral dissertation.

The program requires 81 credits:

Twenty-four credits of core coursework

Nine credits of language study

Twenty-four credits of electives

Six credits for reading and preparation for the A Examination

Eighteen credits for the doctoral project

The completed dissertation is evaluated and defended in a viva voce examination.

PhD Tracks and Concentrations

Applicants select one of two broad tracks.

Cultural, Visual and Literary Studies

This track includes three concentrations:

African Languages and Translation

History of Art, Visual and Performance Studies

Literary and Cultural Studies

It supports research involving language, translation, literature, cultural production, performance, visual culture, art history and connected forms of intellectual and creative expression.

Historical, Political and Social Studies

This track includes:

Historical Studies

Social and Political Studies

It supports doctoral work in history, politics, society, institutions, political economy, international relations and related interdisciplinary fields.

Across the tracks, GSU identifies seven thematic areas that can shape research and supervision:

African-Arab Relations

Intellectual Thought in Global Studies

Diaspora

Gender Studies and Feminist Futures

Political Economy

The Indian Ocean World

The Muslim World

PhD Coursework and Language Study

The doctoral core covers subjects such as:

Globalization and Capitalism

Colonization and Decolonization

From Area Studies to Global Studies

Theory and Method

Summer Research Lab

African and African Diaspora Intellectual Tradition and Critical Imagination

Students complete six electives worth 24 credits in consultation with an adviser and the Director of Graduate Studies. Depending on the proposed dissertation, up to two electives may be taken outside the student’s primary track when they provide necessary research preparation.

Doctoral students also complete three semesters of a non-Western language, selecting Arabic, Amharic, Hausa or Kiswahili. This nine-credit requirement is intended to support direct engagement with sources, communities and scholarship relevant to each student’s research.

PhD Admission Requirements

GSU’s published doctoral requirements ask applicants to provide:

A bachelor’s or master’s qualification in a relevant humanities, social sciences or arts field from an independently accredited institution.

A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent.

A qualification from an institution recognized by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research and GSU.

A bachelor’s program representing at least three years of study for equivalency purposes.

Official and attested bachelor’s and master’s transcripts and certificates, as applicable.

A UAE Certificate of Recognition for qualifications awarded outside the UAE.

Legal English translations of documents issued in another language.

A valid passport.

A recent passport photograph.

Emirates ID and UAE visa copies, where applicable.

IELTS Academic 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 91.

An up-to-date curriculum vitae.

A Statement of Interest of approximately 1,000–2,000 words.

A separate research statement of approximately 2,000–2,500 words.

Two substantial academic writing samples comparable to journal articles.

Two recommendation letters issued no more than one month before submission.

A national-service no-objection certificate where required for male Emirati applicants.

The AED 365 non-refundable application fee, unless an application-fee waiver applies.

The Statement of Interest should explain the applicant’s intellectual development, motivation, academic and professional aspirations, teaching or research experience, publications and other relevant preparation.

The separate research statement should present a coherent proposed project, identify the intended track, define the applicant’s specific research interests, explain previous preparation and describe the project’s anticipated academic, social or professional contribution.

Shortlisted PhD applicants are interviewed online through Zoom. Because doctoral admission depends strongly on academic and supervisory fit, applicants should explicitly connect their proposed projects with GSU’s tracks, concentrations and interdisciplinary themes.

English-Language Requirements

The standard English-language threshold for both graduate degrees is:

IELTS Academic: overall score of 6.5; or

TOEFL iBT: score of 91.

GSU’s frequently asked questions indicate that home-based or online IELTS examinations are not accepted. Applicants should take an accepted paper-based or computer-delivered academic examination and ensure that the score remains valid.

An English-language waiver may be considered, subject to institutional review, for a native English speaker with an English-medium degree or a graduate of an English-medium program who can document that an accepted IELTS or TOEFL threshold was required when entering that program.

Applicants should not assume that studying previously in English automatically guarantees a waiver. Anyone seeking an exemption should provide supporting evidence and obtain written confirmation from GSU.

Comprehensive GSU Graduate Scholarships

GSU advertises competitive scholarship assistance for admitted graduate students. The published support can include:

Full tuition coverage

UAE student-visa sponsorship

Health insurance

Air tickets for international students

Accommodation support

A monthly stipend

Research funding

The general funding pages do not publish the monthly stipend amount, research-funding limit or precise air-travel entitlement. Applicants should request the current financial terms before making travel, housing or enrollment commitments.

Most importantly, admission and scholarship selection are separate processes. An applicant who receives admission to the MA or PhD is not automatically guaranteed financial support.

GSU’s funding pages refer to a 3.5 out of 4.0 academic threshold in the relevant previous degree or degrees. However, different sections of the published scholarship information use slightly different language about whether the threshold must apply to one or multiple previous qualifications. Applicants should confirm how the requirement applies to their academic history directly with Admissions or Academic Affairs.

Scholarship recipients must normally:

Enroll full time, ordinarily for six to 12 credits per semester.

Maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0.

Remain in good academic standing.

Avoid unnecessary course withdrawals or conduct that delays academic progress.

Comply with academic-integrity and student-conduct requirements.

Obtain permission or provide notification before travelling outside the UAE.

Remain in the approved academic program.

Avoid holding another scholarship simultaneously unless GSU approves an equivalent alternative arrangement.

Academic underperformance, academic-integrity violations, misconduct or failure to comply with scholarship conditions can lead to termination of financial support.

Prospective applicants should examine the official MA scholarships and financial-aid page or PhD financial-support page for current terms.

Tuition Fees and Additional Charges

Students who do not receive full financial support should plan carefully for tuition and related costs.

Published MA Tuition

GSU lists the MA tuition rate as AED 7,288 per credit. At 36 credits, the published base calculation is:

Thirty program credits: AED 218,640

Six dissertation credits: AED 43,728

Base total: AED 262,368

Published PhD Tuition

GSU lists the PhD tuition rate as AED 7,891 per credit. At 81 credits, the published base calculation is:

Sixty-three program credits: AED 497,133

Eighteen doctoral-project credits: AED 142,038

Base total: AED 639,171

These totals are mathematical calculations based on the published credit rates and do not necessarily represent every amount payable. Additional charges and 5 percent VAT may apply.

Other published charges include:

AED 365 non-refundable application fee

AED 3,000 non-refundable registration deposit

AED 200 thesis or extension-related fee

AED 500 first-time residence reservation fee, which is described as non-refundable but deductible from residence fees

AED 200 utility-service fee

AED 500 late-payment, returned-cheque or declined-card charge in applicable cases

The published refund schedule generally provides:

A 100 percent tuition refund before the end of the first week, excluding non-refundable deposits.

A 50 percent tuition refund during the second week.

A 25 percent tuition refund during the third week.

No tuition refund after the third week.

A tuition deposit may be refunded when a student visa is refused and satisfactory evidence is submitted. This provision does not apply in the same manner to fully funded students. Applicants should examine the official MA tuition information or PhD tuition information before paying.

GSU also advertises a 30 percent first-semester tuition discount. Different sections of the university’s published information appear to use different GPA thresholds for this discount. Applicants should obtain written confirmation of the current academic threshold, whether the discount is automatic or competitive, and whether any other limitations apply.

The discount cannot ordinarily be combined with a scholarship or another tuition waiver and normally requires the recipient to maintain a GPA of at least 3.0.

Fall 2026 Arabic, Amharic, Hausa and Kiswahili Courses

GSU’s language certificate program is designed for non-native speakers seeking structured instruction in Arabic, Amharic, Hausa or Kiswahili.

For Fall 2026, the university lists Elementary I and Intermediate I levels. Program features include:

Twelve weeks of instruction

Twenty-four sessions

Thirty-six contact hours

Two 90-minute sessions per week

Online and hybrid delivery options

A published course fee of AED 1,440

Discounts of up to 15 percent in eligible cases

A free placement test for applicants seeking entry above Elementary Level I

A completion certificate issued by GSU under licensing from the Sharjah Private Education Authority

The teaching model develops speaking, listening, reading and writing while introducing relevant cultural knowledge.

The Fall 2026 courses run from September 14 to December 17, 2026. The extended registration deadline is September 13, 2026, and places are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

Foreign Degree Recognition and Attestation

Applicants educated outside the UAE should begin the recognition process early. GSU requires overseas qualifications to receive a Certificate of Recognition from the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research.

Depending on the country and document, applicants may need authentication by:

The institution that issued the qualification.

The responsible education authority in the country of study.

The foreign affairs ministry in that country.

The appropriate UAE embassy or consulate.

Relevant UAE authorities after arrival, where required.

Applicants should follow the official UAE recognition process and GSU’s instructions rather than relying only on an informal translation or scanned copy. Original records may be requested for verification following arrival.

How to Apply to Global Studies University

Step 1: Select the Appropriate Program and Track

Review the structure, research areas and career relevance of the MA and PhD. MA applicants must select one of the three specializations. PhD applicants should identify the broad track, concentration and themes that best match their intended research.

Step 2: Confirm Recognition of Previous Qualifications

Verify that the awarding institution is independently accredited and recognized by the UAE Ministry and GSU. International applicants should begin the UAE Certificate of Recognition process as early as possible.

Step 3: Arrange an Accepted English Test

Book an accepted IELTS Academic or TOEFL iBT examination if a valid result is not already available. Do not assume that an online or home-based examination will be accepted.

Step 4: Request Recent Recommendation Letters

Both degree programs require two recommendation letters issued within one month before the application is submitted. Applicants should brief their referees in advance while coordinating the issue date carefully.

Step 5: Prepare the Written Application Materials

Complete the applicable Statement of Interest, research statement and academic writing samples. Every document should be specific, organized and aligned with the selected program.

PhD applicants should present an original but manageable research problem, suitable methods and a credible explanation of the sources or evidence they intend to use.

Step 6: Collect Academic and Identity Documents

Gather the passport, photograph, transcripts, certificates, translations, attestations, recognition records, Emirates ID and visa copies where applicable, and the national-service document where required.

Step 7: Submit a Complete Online Application

Begin through the official GSU application portal. Upload every required document, pay the application fee unless a waiver applies, and save the submission confirmation.

Step 8: Prepare for the Selection Interview

Shortlisted candidates should be ready to discuss their academic background, reasons for choosing GSU, intended track, proposed research and how the degree connects with their longer-term goals.

Step 9: Review Admission and Scholarship Decisions Separately

An admission offer does not confirm a scholarship. Applicants should read every decision letter carefully and obtain clarification about funding, visa sponsorship, accommodation and enrollment deposits before accepting.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

Apply early because the fee waiver is limited to the first 40 complete applications for each graduate program.

Follow every published word limit.

Refer specifically to the selected track and relevant GSU research themes.

Submit a writing sample that demonstrates a focused research question, logical organization, evidence-based analysis and academic integrity.

Ensure the proposed research is realistic and sufficiently focused.

Coordinate recommendation-letter dates carefully because letters must be recently issued.

Request written clarification about scholarship or tuition-discount conditions when the published wording is unclear.

Budget on the assumption that expenses remain the student’s responsibility until a scholarship is formally confirmed.

Keep copies of submitted documents, correspondence, test results and payment receipts.

Do not wait until the deadline to begin UAE degree-recognition and attestation procedures.

Student Visa, Accommodation and Family Considerations

International students normally require a UAE student visa. GSU states that it sponsors admitted international students and provides detailed instructions following admission. Final visa approval remains subject to UAE immigration rules.

The university does not currently provide on-campus student housing. It assists students with off-campus arrangements and identifies The Nest at Aljada, approximately 12 kilometres from campus, as a recommended residence.

The accommodation advertises:

Shared and private room arrangements

Separate provisions for male and female residents

Furnished rooms

Utilities and Wi-Fi

Security

Study and library spaces

Recreation and gaming spaces

Sports facilities

Pools and gyms

Applicants should confirm current availability, transportation and costs before making a commitment. Scholarship-supported accommodation should not automatically be interpreted as an on-campus room. More information is available through the GSU student residences page.

GSU indicates that family members may accompany a student where immigration rules permit, but the university does not pay family expenses. Students planning to relocate with dependants should budget separately for visas, housing, health insurance, education and everyday living costs.

Employment and Career Development During Study

The graduate degrees require full-time commitment. According to GSU, scholarship students or research assistants may undertake limited work of up to eight hours per week under the applicable rules.

MA students may do so only during their second academic year, while PhD students may do so only during their third year. Students should receive formal approval and ensure that any employment complies with scholarship, visa and academic regulations.

GSU’s career services include:

Individual career advising

Internship assistance

Employability workshops

Employer engagement

Organizational visits

Career events and career days

These services can help students connect interdisciplinary research, language competence and regional expertise with careers in education, policy, government, diplomacy, museums, heritage, media, civil society, research and international organizations.

Career outcomes depend on each student’s background, academic performance, professional networks and applicable employment regulations. Admission to the university does not guarantee employment.

Questions to Ask Before Accepting an Offer

Applicants may wish to request written answers to these questions:

Is the previous qualification fully recognized for GSU admission and UAE equivalency?

Has the English-language requirement been satisfied or formally waived?

Is the admission offer unconditional?

Has a scholarship been awarded separately from admission?

What exact stipend, travel, accommodation and research-funding amounts apply?

Which GPA rule applies to the scholarship or first-semester discount?

Which deposits, fees and taxes remain payable with financial support?

What is the semester-by-semester payment schedule for self-funded students?

Which faculty members and research resources align with the proposed project?

Which visa and accommodation steps must be completed before arrival?

Degree-admission questions can be sent to admissions@gsu.ac.ae. Language-course questions can be sent to languages@gsu.ac.ae.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Fall 2027 graduate application deadline?

The deadline for both the MA in Global African Studies and the PhD in Global Studies is Tuesday, October 27, 2026. Applications opened on August 3, 2026.

Are the GSU graduate programs available online?

No. The MA and PhD are advertised as full-time, on-campus programs in Sharjah. The separate language certificates have online and hybrid options.

Does every admitted graduate student receive a scholarship?

No. Scholarships are competitive. An admission offer does not automatically include funding.

What can the scholarship cover?

The advertised package can include full tuition, UAE visa sponsorship, health insurance, air tickets for international students, accommodation, a monthly stipend and research funds. Applicants should confirm the exact value and conditions through their award documents.

What GPA is required?

Graduate admission generally requires at least 3.0 out of 4.0 or the equivalent. The scholarship pages refer to a higher 3.5 threshold in the relevant previous degree or degrees. Applicants should confirm how the scholarship rule applies to their qualifications.

What English score is required?

The published standard is IELTS Academic 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 91. Any waiver is subject to review and supporting evidence.

Is there an application fee?

Yes. The standard non-refundable fee is AED 365. According to the program pages, the first 40 applicants who complete an application for either Fall 2027 graduate degree can receive an application-fee waiver.

Can international students apply?

Yes. GSU publishes procedures covering international applicants, overseas qualifications, student visas and international-student travel support. Every candidate must still satisfy the academic, documentation, English-language and immigration requirements.

When is the Fall 2026 language-course deadline?

The extended registration deadline is September 13, 2026. Classes run from September 14 to December 17, 2026, subject to available places.

Conclusion

Global Studies University’s Fall 2027 intake offers an interdisciplinary route into postgraduate study in Sharjah. The MA in Global African Studies integrates theory, specialization, African-language learning, an internship and a research thesis across museum and heritage studies, diplomacy and African international relations, or Afro-Arab relations.

The PhD in Global Studies offers an extended research pathway spanning cultural, literary, visual, historical, political and social inquiry. Its themes include diaspora, gender, political economy, the Indian Ocean, the Muslim world and African-Arab connections.

GSU’s competitive scholarship package is potentially extensive, but applicants must distinguish clearly between admission and funding. No applicant should make financial plans based on scholarship support until a formal award has been issued.

Degree recognition, document attestation, recent recommendation letters, English testing and substantial written submissions also make early preparation essential. Candidates for the Fall 2027 MA or PhD should submit complete applications well before October 27, 2026. Learners seeking the shorter Fall 2026 language certificates must act sooner because the extended registration deadline is September 13, 2026 and places are limited.

TITLE: UNDP Economist – Development Strategy Job 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand: Eligibility, Requirements, Responsibilities and How to Apply

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has announced an exciting international professional opportunity for an experienced economist to join its Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific in Bangkok, Thailand.

The UNDP Economist – Development Strategy position is designed for a highly experienced economics, development policy, research, or quantitative analysis professional who can contribute to evidence-based economic policy development, growth diagnostics, labour market analysis, inclusive growth strategies, structural transformation research, and government advisory work.

The position is particularly connected to UNDP’s Inclusive Growth Team and its Building Opportunities for Leadership in Development (BOLD) initiative, which supports governments in translating economic evidence, diagnostics, and foresight into practical and strategically prioritized development reforms.

This is a senior-level professional opportunity at IPSA-11 level, with a one-year contract and full-time schedule. The position is based in Bangkok, Thailand, and successful candidates will work closely with economists, policy specialists, UNDP Country Offices, government counterparts, development partners, research institutions, and other stakeholders across Asia and the Pacific.

For professionals with substantial experience in applied economic analysis and development policy, this opportunity provides the chance to contribute to major development strategy and economic transformation initiatives within the UN development system.

Opportunity Overview

The UNDP Economist – Development Strategy vacancy has the following key details:

Job Title: Economist – Development Strategy

Organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)

Job Identification: 36454

Job Category: International professional job

Contract Type: International Personnel Service Agreement (IPSA)

Grade: IPSA-11

Duty Station: Bangkok, Thailand

Practice Area: Inclusive Growth

Bureau: Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific

Work Schedule: Full time

Contract Duration: 1 year

Required Language: English

Posting Date: 24 August 2026

Application Deadline: 9 September 2026 at 3:59 AM

Application Tier: Tier 0, Tier 1 and Tier 2 applicants

Education Requirement: Master’s degree with 7 years of relevant experience, or bachelor’s degree with 9 years of relevant experience

Primary Focus: Economic analysis, development strategy, inclusive growth, labour markets, productivity, inequality and structural transformation

About UNDP

The United Nations Development Programme is a major organization within the UN development system that works with countries and institutions to advance sustainable development and improve people’s lives.

UNDP operates at the intersection of development policy, institutional strengthening, economic transformation, poverty reduction, governance and the Sustainable Development Goals.

The organization uses research, policy advice, technical expertise and development partnerships to help countries address complex development challenges.

Through its Global Policy Network (GPN), UNDP connects international expertise with national and local priorities. This approach allows the organization to support governments in developing policies and institutional capabilities that can deliver sustainable and inclusive development outcomes.

The Economist – Development Strategy will therefore work within an environment where economic research and quantitative evidence are used to influence real-world development strategies.

About the Inclusive Growth Team

The position is located within the Inclusive Growth Team (IGT) at the UNDP Bangkok Regional Hub.

The team provides support to governments and UNDP Country Offices throughout Asia and the Pacific on economic and development-related challenges.

Its work includes analysing issues such as:

Economic growth

Productivity

Employment and job creation

Labour markets

Inequality

Poverty

Structural transformation

Social protection

Inclusive economic policies

Economic development strategies

Institutional capacity

The team combines economic research and policy expertise to help countries identify opportunities for sustainable and inclusive growth.

The successful Economist will contribute to this work by producing high-quality analysis, supporting policy discussions and helping translate complex economic evidence into practical recommendations.

What Is the BOLD Initiative?

A major component of the role is supporting Building Opportunities for Leadership in Development (BOLD).

BOLD is a UNDP high-level advisory initiative designed to help governments translate economic evidence, diagnostics and foresight into strategically prioritized reform pathways.

Rather than focusing only on producing economic research, the initiative seeks to connect analysis with government decision-making.

The Economist will therefore need to be capable of working with economic data while also understanding how evidence can be translated into development strategies and policy recommendations.

This makes the position particularly suitable for an economist who enjoys both technical research and policy-oriented work.

Key Responsibilities of the Economist – Development Strategy

The successful candidate will undertake a wide range of analytical, advisory, programme coordination and knowledge management responsibilities.

1. Conduct Technical Analysis and Research

One of the central responsibilities of the Economist will be conducting and supporting economic research under the BOLD initiative.

The successful candidate will be expected to analyse different aspects of economic development, including:

Economic growth

Structural transformation

Employment

Labour market trends

Productivity

Inequality

Inclusive development

Economic opportunities

Development policy

The Economist will use quantitative and qualitative research methods to produce economic diagnostics that can help governments and UNDP Country Offices understand development challenges and identify potential policy responses.

Growth and Development Diagnostics

The role requires experience or capability in conducting economic diagnostics.

This can involve examining why an economy is growing or underperforming, identifying structural constraints, assessing productivity and employment patterns, and determining which reforms could potentially improve economic outcomes.

The Economist may also support assessments of different economic sectors and identify opportunities for transformation and job creation.

Quantitative and Qualitative Analysis

The position requires strong analytical skills.

The Economist will apply quantitative and qualitative methods to economic and development questions.

This may include working with:

Economic datasets

Microdata

Labour market information

Poverty and inequality indicators

Productivity statistics

Sectoral data

Macroeconomic information

Development indicators

The objective will be to transform data and research findings into useful insights for policymakers and development practitioners.

Economic Models and Microdata

The Economist will also support the development and application of growth and inclusion models.

This includes working with microeconomic datasets and other quantitative resources to understand economic and social outcomes.

Strong data analysis capabilities will therefore be important for the successful candidate.

2. Prepare Technical Papers and Policy Briefs

Another important responsibility involves communicating economic research effectively.

The Economist will prepare materials such as:

Technical papers

Data-driven policy briefs

Background research notes

Analytical reports

Presentations

Evidence packs

Technical guidance materials

These documents may be used by senior economists, government officials, UNDP Country Offices and other development stakeholders.

The ability to communicate complicated economic concepts clearly will therefore be essential.

A successful candidate should be comfortable presenting technical information to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.

3. Contribute to Regional Knowledge Products

The Economist will contribute to regional knowledge products focused on economic transformation and inclusive growth.

These products can help capture research findings, policy lessons and analytical approaches that may be relevant across countries in Asia and the Pacific.

The role therefore involves not only producing analysis for individual assignments but also helping develop knowledge that can support broader regional development efforts.

Government Advisory and Country Engagement

The position also has an important government-facing component.

The Economist will support high-level policy dialogues and country-level development engagements.

4. Support High-Level Policy Dialogues

The successful candidate will provide technical inputs to policy discussions led by the IPSA-12 Senior Economist and other Inclusive Growth Team experts.

This could involve preparing:

Economic analysis

Data

Presentations

Briefing materials

Evidence summaries

Policy recommendations

Background research

The Economist will help ensure that policy discussions are informed by credible evidence and rigorous analysis.

5. Support UNDP Country Offices

The Economist will assist UNDP Country Offices in delivering BOLD analytical work.

This includes supporting activities such as:

Country capability assessments

Economic diagnostics

Growth analysis

Labour market assessments

Inclusion analysis

Development strategy work

The position therefore requires someone who can work effectively across teams and adapt analytical work to different country contexts.

6. Prepare Presentations and Data Visualizations

The Economist will also assist with preparing presentations, data visualizations and evidence packs for government engagements.

This means the successful candidate should not only be able to analyse data but should also be able to communicate findings visually.

The ability to convert complex economic information into clear charts, tables, presentations and concise messages can be particularly valuable in this role.

7. Participate in Missions, Consultations and Workshops

The Economist may participate in:

Technical missions

Government consultations

Workshops

Policy dialogues

Stakeholder meetings

Country-level engagements

This provides an opportunity to engage directly with policymakers, development practitioners and other stakeholders.

Programme Implementation and Coordination

Beyond research and analysis, the Economist will contribute to the planning and implementation of BOLD activities.

8. Support Planning and Delivery

The Economist will contribute to planning, monitoring and delivery of BOLD activities at both regional and country levels.

This may require coordinating different workstreams, tracking deliverables and ensuring that analytical activities are delivered according to programme objectives.

9. Support Reporting and Quality Assurance

The position will also provide analytical and reporting inputs for:

Donor updates

Internal reporting

Quality assurance

Project documentation

Programme monitoring

Strong organizational and communication skills will therefore complement the technical economics requirements.

10. Coordinate With Multiple Stakeholders

The Economist will coordinate with:

UNDP Country Offices

External research partners

Internal UNDP teams

Economists

Policy specialists

Government counterparts

Development partners

The ability to collaborate across institutions and professional disciplines is therefore important.

Knowledge Management and Learning

The role also includes responsibilities related to knowledge management.

The Economist will help ensure that analytical tools, datasets, methodologies and lessons from country-level implementation are properly maintained and documented.

11. Maintain Datasets and Analytical Tools

The successful candidate will maintain and update datasets, analytical tools and templates used across the BOLD programme.

This requires attention to detail and an understanding of data quality.

12. Capture Lessons Learned

The Economist will synthesize lessons learned from country implementation.

These lessons can then be used to improve regional guidance and strengthen future economic analysis.

13. Prepare Technical Guidance

The successful candidate may also prepare technical guidance notes covering areas such as:

Inclusive growth analysis

Job creation diagnostics

Economic transformation

Labour market analysis

Development strategy

Related economic policy topics

Reporting Structure

The Economist will report directly to the UNDP Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific Chief Economist, who also serves as the head of the Inclusive Growth Global Policy Network Team.

The successful candidate will work closely with several important stakeholders, including:

Inclusive Growth Team Regional Advisor

Economists

Policy specialists

BOLD Project Manager

UNDP Country Office economists

UNDP programme teams

Government counterparts

External partners

Global Policy Network colleagues

Other Regional Hubs where necessary

This means the position involves substantial cross-functional and international collaboration.

Competencies Required

UNDP has identified several core competencies for the position.

Achieve Results

The candidate should be able to set and align challenging but achievable objectives across multiple projects and contribute to work that creates lasting impact.

Think Innovatively

The Economist should be able to identify risks, develop new ideas and find innovative solutions to complex economic and development problems.

Learn Continuously

The role requires a willingness to continuously expand professional knowledge and diversify experience.

Adapt With Agility

The successful candidate should be comfortable managing multiple competing demands and supporting change in a complex development environment.

Act With Determination

The candidate should demonstrate initiative and remain focused on achieving results even when facing challenges or barriers.

Engage and Partner

Strong stakeholder-management skills are essential.

The Economist should be politically savvy, able to navigate complex institutional environments and capable of supporting inter-agency collaboration.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

The candidate should appreciate the value of a diverse workforce and contribute to an inclusive working environment.

Technical Competencies

In addition to general professional competencies, the position requires technical capabilities in several areas.

Inclusive Growth and Development Planning

The candidate should understand development planning and how economic policies can contribute to inclusive growth.

Growth Strategies

Experience with economic growth strategies is relevant to the position.

Structural Transformation

The Economist should understand structural transformation and its relationship with productivity, employment and economic development.

Jobs and Livelihoods

Knowledge of labour markets, employment and job creation is important.

Poverty and Inequality Metrics

The position also requires an understanding of poverty and inequality measurement and analysis.

Data Analysis

The successful candidate should be capable of extracting, analysing and visualizing data to generate meaningful insights and support effective decision-making.

Systems Thinking

The role requires the ability to understand how different elements of an economic or development system interact.

The Economist should be able to analyse problems objectively and consider how changing one part of a system can affect other components.

Educational Requirements

Applicants must meet one of the following educational pathways.

Master’s Degree Route

An advanced university degree, such as a master’s degree or equivalent, in one of the following areas is required:

Economics

Applied Economics

Statistics

Public Policy

A related field

Applicants using the master’s degree pathway must also have at least 7 years of relevant professional experience.

Bachelor’s Degree Route

A first-level university degree in:

Economics

Applied Economics

Statistics

Public Policy

A related field

may be considered in combination with additional qualifying experience.

Under this pathway, candidates are required to have at least 9 years of relevant professional experience.

PhD

A PhD in Economics or a related discipline is considered desirable.

A doctoral degree is therefore not stated as mandatory, but it could strengthen an applicant’s profile.

Professional Experience Requirements

The vacancy requires substantial professional experience.

Candidates must have a minimum of:

7 years of relevant experience with a master’s degree, or

9 years of relevant experience with a bachelor’s degree.

The experience should be relevant to areas such as:

Applied economic analysis

Economic research

Development policy

Economic diagnostics

Labour market analysis

Inclusive development

Quantitative research

Economic modelling

Applicants should carefully demonstrate how their previous professional experience directly relates to these areas.

Required Professional Skills

The vacancy identifies several specific skills that applicants should possess.

Growth Diagnostics

Applicants should have experience conducting or supporting growth diagnostics.

This is particularly relevant because the BOLD programme works with governments to understand economic constraints and identify strategic development pathways.

Labour Market Analysis

Experience analysing labour markets is required.

Applicants should ideally understand employment trends, job creation, labour-force dynamics and related economic issues.

Poverty, Inequality and Inclusion Analysis

Experience with inclusion and inequality assessments is also required.

This may include working with poverty statistics, inequality indicators and other measures of socioeconomic outcomes.

Quantitative Analysis

Strong quantitative analytical capabilities are essential.

Applicants should be comfortable working with economic data and using analytical approaches to generate evidence-based insights.

Microeconomic Data

Experience working with microeconomic datasets is required or highly relevant.

Candidates should be able to work with data to investigate economic and social outcomes.

Macroeconomic Modelling

Experience with macroeconomic modelling is also identified as a required skill.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate quantitative economic expertise rather than relying solely on qualitative policy experience.

Government and Development Partner Experience

Candidates should have experience working with one or more of the following:

Governments

International organizations

Research institutes

Development partners

This requirement reflects the policy-oriented and advisory nature of the position.

Desired Skills and Experience

Some qualifications are not mandatory but are considered advantageous.

Previous UNDP or UN Experience

Previous experience working with UNDP or another UN organization is an asset.

Applicants who have already worked within the UN development system may therefore have relevant institutional experience.

Knowledge of Asia and the Pacific

Familiarity with development challenges and policy contexts across Asia and the Pacific is highly desirable.

This is particularly relevant because the role is located within UNDP’s Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific and involves supporting countries across the region.

Technical Guidance Experience

Experience preparing technical guidance notes on subjects such as inclusive growth analysis and job creation diagnostics is also desirable.

Language Requirement

Fluency in English is required.

Applicants should therefore be able to communicate effectively in written and spoken English, particularly because the position involves preparing technical documents, participating in policy discussions and engaging with international stakeholders.

Who Should Apply?

This position is most appropriate for experienced economists and development professionals who have a strong combination of technical economic expertise, quantitative analysis skills and development policy experience.

Potentially suitable professional profiles include:

Economists

Development economists

Applied economists

Economic policy specialists

Economic researchers

Labour market specialists

Inclusive growth specialists

Public policy professionals with strong economics experience

Quantitative development researchers

Economic analysts

Professionals working on poverty and inequality

Development strategy specialists

However, meeting a professional profile alone is not enough. Candidates must also satisfy the vacancy’s Tier 0, Tier 1 or Tier 2 eligibility requirements.

Understanding the UNDP Tiered Application System

One of the most important aspects of this vacancy is its tiered application process.

The vacancy is specifically advertised as:

“Economist – Development Strategy [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]”

Applicants should therefore determine whether they fall within one of these categories before investing time in the application.

Tier 0

Tier 0 includes UNDP, UNCDF and UNV international personnel holding permanent or fixed-term appointments whose posts will be abolished, or whose contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Tier 1

Tier 1 includes other UNDP, UNCDF and UNV staff members holding permanent or fixed-term appointments.

Tier 2

Tier 2 includes:

UNDP/UNCDF/UNV personnel holding temporary appointments

Personnel on regular PSA contracts

Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

Tier 3 and Other Candidates

The vacancy description explains that Tier 3, or vacancies without a tier indication, generally cover other contract types and external candidates.

However, this particular vacancy explicitly states Tier 0, Tier 1 and Tier 2.

Therefore, external applicants who do not fall into one of these categories should not assume that they are eligible simply because they meet the educational and professional requirements.

Nationality, Race and Geographic Eligibility

The vacancy does not specify a particular race, ethnicity or nationality as an eligibility requirement.

UNDP states that it is an equal opportunity employer and encourages qualified applicants from diverse backgrounds.

However, this should not be confused with the tier eligibility requirement.

For this specific vacancy, eligibility is primarily determined by:

The applicant’s UNDP/UNCDF/UNV personnel status and applicable tier;

Educational qualifications;

Relevant professional experience;

Required technical skills;

English language proficiency;

Other requirements specified in the vacancy.

TITLE: IDOS Researcher Position 2027 in Water Governance and Water Security – Germany

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS) is inviting applications for a Researcher (m/f/diverse) position within its Research Department “Environmental Governance.” The position focuses on water governance, water security, water politics, environmental governance, and policy advice, particularly in low- and middle-income countries and potentially conflict-affected settings.

The opportunity is particularly suited to researchers with a background in the social sciences, sustainability science, environmental governance, political ecology, or related fields, and with demonstrated research and publication experience on water security issues.

The successful candidate will become part of the IDOS water governance team, contributing to academic research, policy advice, networking, science communication, and potentially third-party funding applications for interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary projects.

The position is based at IDOS in Bonn, Germany, is offered at 50% part-time employment equivalent to 19.5 hours per week, and is initially limited to three years, with a possible extension.

Researcher Position at IDOS: Overview

The German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS) conducts research and provides policy advice at the intersection of development and sustainability. Its work aims to contribute to a cooperative and sustainable multipolar world through research, policy engagement, knowledge cooperation, and education.

For this vacancy, IDOS is seeking a researcher who can contribute to its work on water governance and water security, with a particular focus on issues affecting low- and middle-income countries.

Position details

Position: Researcher (m/f/diverse)

Position number: 2026-C-02

Institution: German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS)

Research Department: Environmental Governance

Research area: Water governance and water security

Location: Bonn, Germany

Working time: 50% part-time

Weekly hours: 19.5 hours per week

Salary: German public sector tariff, EG13 up to EG14 TVöD Bund, depending on qualifications

Gross salary: Approximately €31,250–€48,000 for a 50% position

Start date: From 1 January 2027

Contract duration: Three years, with a possible option for extension

Potential increase in working time: The position may potentially increase to 60% in 2028 and 2029

Application deadline: 7 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST

Expected interview date: 3 November 2026

About the Research Area: Water Security

The researcher will join the IDOS water governance team and conduct research and policy advice on selected questions relating to water politics, water policies, water governance, and water security.

The work will focus particularly on low- and middle-income countries and may include settings affected by conflict or other forms of instability.

Water security is understood broadly as ensuring access to an acceptable quantity and quality of water for:

Human health

Livelihoods

Ecosystems

Economic and productive activities

It also considers the need to maintain an acceptable level of water-related risks for people, the environment, and economies.

This broad definition means that the successful researcher could work across several interconnected dimensions of water security.

Key Water Security Topics

Research under this position may address one or more of the following areas:

1. Surface and Groundwater Use

The role may examine the governance and political dimensions of surface and groundwater resources, including:

Overuse of water resources

Groundwater governance

Surface-water management

Competition over water resources

Institutional arrangements for water management

Policies governing water use

Environmental and social impacts of water exploitation

2. Wastewater Treatment and Reuse

The researcher may also investigate issues surrounding:

Wastewater treatment

Wastewater management

Reuse of treated wastewater

Governance of wastewater systems

Environmental risks

Policy frameworks for wastewater reuse

Sustainable approaches to water resource management

3. Water-Related Extreme Events

Another potential area of research involves water-related risks and extreme events, such as:

Flooding

Drought

Water scarcity

Climate-related water risks

Disaster risk governance

Institutional responses to extreme events

Policies for adapting to changing water-related risks

4. Access to Sanitation Services

The position may also cover questions related to:

Access to sanitation

Sanitation governance

Public policy

Inequality in access to services

Institutional challenges

Sustainable sanitation systems

Health and environmental implications of inadequate sanitation

5. Transboundary and Multilateral Water Relations

The researcher may conduct research on water relations that cross national borders, including:

Transboundary water governance

International water politics

Cooperation between countries

Water-related conflicts

Multilateral water governance

International institutions and agreements

Political dimensions of shared water resources

Main Responsibilities

The successful candidate will have responsibilities spanning research, policy advice, networking, communication, and funding development.

Conducting Academic Research

The researcher will undertake independent and collaborative research related to water security and governance.

The role requires the ability to identify important research questions, develop appropriate conceptual frameworks, conduct research, analyse findings, and communicate results to academic and policy audiences.

Research may involve studying institutional arrangements, political processes, environmental governance systems, and the relationships between different levels of government and stakeholders.

Providing Policy Advice

An important part of the position is translating research into useful knowledge for policymakers and other stakeholders.

The successful applicant should therefore be comfortable working beyond purely academic research and responding to demands for policy advice.

This could involve:

Developing policy-oriented research outputs

Communicating research findings to policymakers

Contributing to policy discussions

Responding to emerging policy questions

Translating complex research findings into accessible recommendations

Engaging with stakeholders outside academia

Supporting IDOS Networking and Positioning

The researcher will also contribute to the institute’s broader networking and positioning on water security topics.

This involves helping IDOS strengthen its profile and relationships in the field of water governance and security.

The successful applicant is expected to engage with relevant researchers, institutions, policymakers, practitioners, and other stakeholders.

Supporting Third-Party Funding Applications

The position also provides an opportunity to contribute to the development of externally funded research.

Candidates are encouraged to support third-party funding applications for inter- and transdisciplinary projects related to water security.

Experience with third-party funding acquisition is considered an advantage.

The possibility of increasing the position to 60% in 2028 and 2029 is connected to successful acquisition of third-party funding.

Required Qualifications

Applicants must demonstrate a strong academic and research background relevant to the position.

Master’s Degree

A Master’s degree is required.

The degree should preferably be in an area such as:

Social sciences

Political science

Economics

Human geography

Anthropology

Sustainability science with a social science focus

Another closely related field

PhD Preferred

A PhD is preferably expected, although the advertisement does not state that it is an absolute requirement.

Applicants with strong research experience and relevant publications may therefore be considered based on their overall qualifications.

Excellent Academic Performance

The position calls for candidates with excellent grades in their relevant university education.

Research Experience in Water Security

One of the most important requirements is demonstrated social science research experience in one or more of the specified water security fields.

Candidates should be able to demonstrate their research expertise through peer-reviewed academic publications, including submissions.

Relevant research areas include:

Surface-water governance

Groundwater governance

Water overuse

Wastewater treatment

Wastewater reuse

Water-related extreme events

Sanitation

Transboundary water governance

Multilateral water relations

Water politics

Water policy

Water security

Environmental governance

Political ecology

Applicants do not necessarily need to have worked across every one of these areas. Experience in at least one of the specified water security topics can be relevant.

Conceptual and Theoretical Skills

The successful candidate should have strong conceptual abilities, particularly in areas such as:

Institutional Analysis

The ability to examine how institutions shape environmental and water governance processes is important for this role.

Multi-Level Environmental Governance

Applicants should understand how water-related decisions and governance operate across different levels, potentially involving:

Local institutions

Communities

Municipal authorities

National governments

Regional organisations

International institutions

Other relevant stakeholders

Political Ecology

Knowledge of political ecology is also relevant, particularly for understanding the relationships between:

Environmental resources

Political power

Institutions

Communities

Economic interests

Inequality

Resource access

Research Methodology Requirements

The position requires experience with qualitative research methodologies in the social sciences.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate familiarity with approaches used to investigate complex social, political, institutional, and environmental questions.

Mixed Methods

Experience with mixed-methods research is considered an additional asset.

Candidates who can combine qualitative approaches with quantitative data, statistical analysis, surveys, or other methods may therefore have an advantage.

Experience in Low- and Middle-Income Countries

Research or professional experience in a low- or middle-income country context is specifically required.

This is an important aspect of the position because IDOS’s work on water security focuses particularly on challenges and governance systems in such contexts.

Relevant experience could include research, fieldwork, professional work, development projects, policy work, or other substantive engagement with low- and middle-income country settings.

Policy and Science Communication Experience

The successful applicant should be willing to engage in:

Policy advice

Science communication

Research dissemination

Stakeholder engagement

Communication with non-academic audiences

Previous experience in policy advice or science communication is considered an advantage.

Third-Party Funding Experience

Experience with third-party funding acquisition is an asset.

Candidates who have participated in activities such as:

Grant proposal development

Research funding applications

Consortium development

Donor engagement

Fundraising for research projects

Competitive funding applications

may therefore be particularly well positioned for the role.

Interdisciplinary and Transdisciplinary Collaboration

IDOS is looking for someone who is eager to work in inter- and transdisciplinary teams.

This means the researcher should be comfortable collaborating across disciplinary boundaries and potentially working with people from academia, government, civil society, development organisations, practitioners, and other stakeholder groups.

Communication and Organisational Skills

Strong skills in the following areas are expected:

Academic writing

Policy writing

Professional communication

Organisation

Independent work

Research planning

Collaboration

Time management

The advertisement particularly emphasises the ability to work in a self-directed manner.

The researcher should also have the flexibility to respond to changing demands for policy advice.

International Travel and Tropical-Country Work

The position requires a willingness and ability to travel abroad, including to countries with tropical climates.

The advertisement specifically mentions “Tropentauglichkeit,” referring to the ability or suitability to work and travel in tropical-climate environments.

Candidates should therefore be prepared for international research or professional travel where required.

Employment Conditions and Salary

The position is offered on a 50% part-time basis, equivalent to 19.5 hours per week.

The salary follows the German public-sector pay system:

EG13 up to EG14 TVöD Bund, depending on the applicant’s qualifications.

The advertised gross salary range for the 50% position is approximately:

€31,250 to €48,000 gross

The position is initially limited to three years, beginning from January 2027, with a possible option for contract extension.

There is also an opportunity for the position to increase to 60% in 2028 and 2029, depending on successful third-party funding acquisition.

Benefits and What IDOS Offers

IDOS lists a range of employment and social benefits for the successful candidate.

Flexible Working Hours

The role provides flexible working arrangements within the 50% working-time framework.

The standard working week is:

19.5 hours per week

Mobile Working

The position offers the possibility of mobile working from within Germany for up to 60% of the working time per week.

At least 40% of working time per week must be spent in person in Bonn.

This means candidates should be prepared to work from the IDOS workplace in Bonn for the required proportion of their working time.

Public Transportation Benefits

Employees can make use of a subsidised Deutschland-Job-Ticket, supporting access to public transportation.

The institute also highlights good access to public transport.

Special Annual Payment

Employees receive a special annual payment in accordance with the TVöD Bund collective agreement for the German federal government.

Annual Leave

Up to 30 days of annual vacation

An additional 6 days of company vacation

Professional Development

IDOS offers training opportunities intended to support employees’ continuing professional development.

These may help researchers strengthen their academic, professional, methodological, and organisational skills.

Additional Benefits

Diversity and Equal Opportunity

IDOS explicitly states that it actively promotes equality between women and men and diversity within the institute.

The organisation welcomes applications from people of different backgrounds and explicitly states that it welcomes:

People of colour

People of all nationalities

People of all religions and beliefs

People of different sexual orientations

People of all gender identities

People across all age groups

People with disabilities

People with a family migration history

Therefore, the vacancy is not limited to applicants from Germany or Europe on the basis of nationality.

Qualified applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas, the Middle East, Oceania, and other regions can apply, provided they meet the academic, research, professional, and other requirements of the position.

They should attach the relevant Anabin database excerpt to their application documents as evidence of recognition of the foreign degree by the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB) of the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs (KMK).

International applicants should therefore pay particular attention to this requirement before submitting their applications.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly relevant for researchers who have a combination of:

A Master’s degree or preferably a PhD in a relevant social science or sustainability field.

Strong academic performance.

Research experience related to water security.

Peer-reviewed publications or submissions demonstrating relevant research experience.

Experience with qualitative social science research.

Research or professional experience in a low- or middle-income country.

Knowledge of institutional analysis, environmental governance, or political ecology.

An interest in water politics, water policy, and water governance.

Strong academic and professional writing skills.

An interest in policy advice and science communication.

An ability to work independently.

Application Requirements

Applications must include the following documents:

THE INSTITUTION

The University of The Gambia (UTG) is the oldest University in The Gambia. It was established in 1999. With 288 academic staff and 6,950 students, UTG is a vibrant institution making a significant contribution to the economic, social and cultural prosperity of The Gambia and the sub-region. Its vision is to provide relevant, sustainable and high quality tertiary education and research to promote socio-economic, scientific and technological advancement and development. The campus extends throughout The Gambia and is based across four locations in Kanifing, Brikama, Faraba, and Farafenni. It has grown over the past twenty years and now has ten Schools and Faculties-

Agriculture & Environmental Sciences

Arts & Sciences

Business & Public Administration

Engineering & Architecture

Education

Graduate studies

Information & Communications Technology

Journalism & Digital Media

Law

Medicine & Allied Health Sciences

FUNCTION

At the University of The Gambia, the Vice Chancellor, under the direction of the University Governing Council, is the academic head and chief executive officer of the University responsible for leadership, management and development of the University, and spearheading the realization of its vision and mission. Among the many responsibilities of the position, the Vice Chancellor will:

 oversee strategic planning and provide strategic leadership for the University staff and students;

 lead and manage the Senior Management Team of the University of The Gambia in the day-to-day

administration of the University and the general supervision and direction over the academic and

administrative work of the institution and its faculty officers and employees;

 lead fund-raising efforts to mobilize sustainable resources for the University;

 ensure that appropriate strategies are implemented to make the University of The Gambia financially

independent;

 oversee the preparation of the annual estimates of income and expenditure for consideration by the

Council and for the management of the budget and resources within the estimates approved by the

Council;

 account to Council for the academic and financial performance of the University through periodic

submissions of quarterly financial and activity reports on the University’s financial status,

activities, achievements, plans and developments;

 ensure the University complies with national and international regulatory bodies ;

 act as the main point of contact for national policymakers and other stakeholders within The

Gambia and external agencies such as research funding bodies, and donors;

 serve as Chair of Senate and also ex officio member of the Council, Faculty Boards, and other

university committees and bodies;

 exercise general authority over the staff of the University, with power to suspend from duty any

member of staff, and reporting the matter without delay to the Council; and,

 meet performance goals that the Governing Council will review annually.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

The applicant should be a strategic thinker and a visionary to grow the University with regards to quality,

and contribution to society; an individual who is comfortable with change management and has a proven

track record as a leader who creates successful teams that generate measurable outcomes; a person with

enthusiasm and energy and good at mobilizing resources; an excellent communicator and listener with a

broad range of contacts and known in academic circles for excellence in academics with a prolific research

output.

SPECIFICATIONS

The Candidate must:

 Hold relevant postgraduate qualifications that includes a doctoral qualification or equivalent, must

be of a professorial rank for at least ten (10) years and must have served in a University or Institution

of similar status for a minimum of 15 years.

 Must demonstrate a track record of outstanding achievement in an academic discipline and be an

internationally recognized academic with a track record in academic achievements reflected in

extensive peer-review publications including publications within the last 3 years.

 Have a successful record of academic leadership and management and/or business achievement,

including significant and demonstrably successful experience in managing change, people and

financial resources, through leadership and management of a significant academic unit. Experience

as Dean and/or Deputy Vice Chancellor will be recognized.

 Demonstrate a proven capacity for strategic thinking and planning.

 Understands the tertiary education system and its policy environment, and how to respond

effectively to this environment.

 Have the credibility, experience and judgement to operate effectively at a senior level in a university

setting.

 Must have a broad range of international contacts and show an ability to identify and develop

partnership and business development opportunities.

 Demonstrate experience and has a track record in mobilizing resources.

 Have the ability to work at pace and under pressure.

 Have sound communication skills, and the ability to inspire the work of faculty and other staff.

 Possess highly developed skills in decision-making, persuasion, influencing and negotiation.

SALARY AND FRINGE BENEFITS:

Salary and Condition of Service attached to the position are attractive.

TERM OF APPOINTMENT

The Appointment, which is full-time, shall be for FIVE (5) YEARS in the first instance and may be renewed for a final term of up to FIVE (5) years only.

HOW TO APPLY

Interested persons are requested to submit their Application Letters together with the following:

• Curriculum Vitae, including names and contact details of three (3) Referees; and, a 1200-word Statement of the Candidate’s Vision for the University of The Gambia

All applications are to be sent to chairgovc@utg.edu.gm and copied to registrar@utg.edu.gm or mltarro@utg.edu.gm not later than July 15, 2021. Shortlisted candidates shall be invited for an interview.

Please download the call posted by the University here – https://blog.aau.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/ADVERT-FOR-THE-POSITION-OF-VICE-CHANCELLOR-UNIVERSITY-OF-THE-GAMBIA-1.pdf
