TITLE: Call for Innovative Green Education Action Projects 2026: Share Your Climate Education Project and Win a Fully Funded Visit to Brussels

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Education for Climate Coalition has launched its Call for Innovative Green Education Action Projects 2026, inviting students, educators, schools, institutions, organisations and other education stakeholders to showcase innovative projects that are helping communities respond to climate change and advance sustainability through education.

The initiative comes ahead of Education for Climate Day 2026, which will take place on 22 October 2026. The call is designed to identify strong, practical examples of climate and sustainability education that can inspire other education communities across the European Education Area.

Three projects from each of the three thematic areas will be selected to present their work during Education for Climate Day 2026. Representatives of selected projects will also receive a fully funded visit to Brussels to participate in the event and interact with other participants working in climate education across the European Education Area.

The application deadline is 6 September 2026.

What Is the Education for Climate Coalition 2026 Call About?

The Education for Climate Coalition is looking for real examples of green education projects that have already been implemented or are currently being implemented.

Rather than focusing solely on ideas or proposals for future projects, the call seeks projects where concrete actions have already taken place. These could include initiatives in schools, universities, communities, civil society organisations, public institutions, cultural settings, professional environments or other formal and informal learning contexts.

The selected projects are intended to demonstrate how education can contribute to:

Climate action

Sustainability

Intergenerational cooperation

Youth participation

Green citizenship

Institutional transformation

Sustainable development

Future-oriented learning

Community engagement

Green competences

Innovative teaching and learning

The initiative particularly seeks projects that can provide practical evidence of impact, such as learning materials, activities, educational tools, photographs, videos, documents, implementation records or other tangible outputs.

Three Thematic Areas for the 2026 Call

Applicants can submit projects under one of three thematic areas. Each theme focuses on a different aspect of green education and climate action.

1. Youth Leadership and Intergenerational Dialogue for Climate Action

The first theme focuses on projects that give young people an active role in climate and sustainability action.

The emphasis is not simply on teaching young people about climate change. Instead, projects should demonstrate how learners can become active participants in creating solutions and influencing decisions within their schools, institutions and communities.

The theme also recognises schools and other educational institutions as potential living environments for sustainability, where green values and sustainable practices can become part of everyday life.

Projects may involve collaboration between:

Students and young people

Teachers and educators

Families

Schools

Local authorities

Civil society organisations

Community organisations

Other local stakeholders

The Education for Climate Coalition is particularly interested in initiatives that create meaningful connections between different generations.

This reflects the Coalition’s 2026 priority of intergenerational fairness. The underlying idea is that young people should not only be prepared to deal with future challenges but should also have opportunities to influence the present and help shape the future.

Questions applicants should consider

Projects under this theme should be able to demonstrate:

How young people actively participate in climate or sustainability action.

How learners contribute to designing, leading or influencing activities.

How young people participate in decisions connected to the project.

How schools work with families and local communities.

How different generations collaborate.

How the project supports a whole-school or whole-institution approach to sustainability.

How the project is connected to local needs.

Whether the approach could be adapted or transferred to another community or education setting.

A strong application should therefore go beyond simply stating that young people participated. It should explain what they did, what decisions they influenced, what actions they led and what changed as a result.

2. Citizenship Education and Institutional Action for Sustainability

The second theme looks at projects that help citizens, learners and communities understand sustainability challenges and take practical action.

This category is broader than traditional classroom education. It recognises that learning about sustainability can happen in many environments and can involve a wide range of organisations and professionals.

Eligible projects under this theme may be led by:

Civil society organisations

Companies

Public institutions

Researchers

Cultural organisations and actors

Non-formal education providers

Educational institutions

Other organisations working to advance sustainability education

The theme encourages initiatives that connect knowledge and expertise with public engagement and practical action.

For example, a project could take research findings or professional knowledge and turn them into accessible educational programmes for communities. Another project could use cultural activities, public engagement or community-based learning to help people understand environmental challenges and participate in the green transition.

Questions applicants should consider

Applicants should explain:

How the project helps citizens, learners or communities understand green and sustainability issues.

Who leads the project.

Which groups participate in the project.

How different target groups are engaged.

How research, professional expertise, institutional knowledge or community knowledge is converted into accessible learning.

How the project encourages participation.

How it promotes responsibility and behavioural change.

How the project addresses the needs of different groups.

What makes the initiative inclusive and practical.

Why the project is relevant beyond the immediate learning environment.

The strongest projects will demonstrate that sustainability education can lead to participation, responsibility and action, rather than remaining purely theoretical.

3. GreenComp: Envisioning Sustainable Futures in Teaching and Learning

The third thematic area focuses on the GreenComp framework and how sustainability competences can be incorporated into teaching and learning.

Particular attention is given to the competence area of envisioning sustainable futures.

This theme is aimed at projects that help learners think beyond immediate challenges and explore what different possible futures could look like.

Projects may encourage learners to:

Imagine alternative futures.

Examine the long-term consequences of current decisions.

Compare different possible sustainability pathways.

Think critically about environmental, social and economic consequences.

Develop the competences required to contribute to sustainable development.

Translate future-oriented thinking into practical action.

Educators, trainers and facilitators also have an important role under this theme because they create the learning environments in which future thinking and sustainability competences can develop.

Questions applicants should consider

Projects should demonstrate:

How GreenComp or sustainability competencies are incorporated into teaching and learning.

How learners imagine or explore sustainable futures.

How current decisions are connected to future environmental, social and economic consequences.

Which practical tools or methods are used to develop future thinking.

How learners are given agency to contribute to sustainability.

How the approach could be adapted by other educators or learning communities.

Applicants should make the connection between learning, future thinking and practical sustainability action clear.

Who Can Submit a Project?

The call is open to a broad range of participants across formal and informal education.

The organisers welcome submissions from

Students

Educators

Schools

Education institutions

Civil society organisations

Companies

Public institutions

Researchers

Cultural actors

Non-formal education providers

Other education stakeholders

Community organisations and partners involved in education and sustainability

Projects can be small or large, local or international, and public or private.

This broad approach means applicants do not necessarily need to represent a large institution or operate a major international programme. A smaller, locally rooted initiative can also be considered if it demonstrates innovation, participation, tangible implementation and meaningful community impact.

Geographic Eligibility

One of the key eligibility requirements is that the green education action must be based in and across a European Education Area country.

The eligible geographic area includes the 27 European Union Member States, as well as the following:

Iceland

Liechtenstein

North Macedonia

Norway

Serbia

Türkiye

Therefore, the call is specifically focused on projects operating within the European Education Area.

Projects from outside this geographic area would not meet the stated location eligibility requirement.

What Types of Projects Are Eligible?

The initiative is looking for projects that have moved beyond the idea stage and have had concrete implementation actions.

A project can be

Already completed

Currently ongoing

Started within the eligible period

Recently completed within the last five years

The important consideration is that actual implementation must have taken place.

This means applicants should be prepared to demonstrate what they have done rather than submitting only a proposal for something they intend to do in the future.

Previous Applicants Can Apply Again

Projects that participated in previous editions of the call are not automatically excluded.

They may still be eligible if they have developed:

New workstreams

New materials

New activities

New project elements

Other significant developments

This creates an opportunity for previous participants to showcase how their initiatives have evolved.

What Will the Organisers Be Looking For?

The Education for Climate Coalition wants to showcase projects that demonstrate education innovation in practice.

Applications will be assessed according to several important dimensions.

1. Location

The project must be implemented in or across an eligible European Education Area country.

2. Ambition

The organisers want projects that are inspiring, courageous and innovative.

Applicants should demonstrate what makes their approach different and why it represents an important contribution to climate or sustainability education.

3. Relevance

The project should clearly address the theme under which it is submitted.

Applicants should avoid vague descriptions and explain exactly how their activities respond to the selected thematic area.

4. Interdisciplinarity

Projects are encouraged to demonstrate connections across different disciplines and areas of education for climate innovation.

The assessment also considers the number and type of GreenComp competences addressed by the project.

5. Participatory Nature

Participation is a particularly important element of the Education for Climate Coalition community.

Projects should ideally demonstrate collaboration between at least two education actor categories identified in the application survey.

This means applicants should clearly explain who was involved and how different groups contributed to the project.

Simply having multiple stakeholders associated with a project may not be enough. The application should show how they actually participated in shaping or implementing the initiative.

6. Education for Climate Innovation Area Coverage

The project must cover at least one of the five Education for Climate Innovation Areas.

Applicants should therefore identify the relevant innovation area covered by their work and explain how the project addresses it.

7. GreenComp Engagement

Projects must address at least one of the twelve GreenComp competences.

Applicants should identify the relevant competence or competences and explain how these are reflected in their activities, learning experiences or outcomes.

8. Innovation Learning Engagement

The project should incorporate at least one learning or teaching method identified in the June 2022 Council Recommendation on learning for the green transition and sustainable development.

Applicants should also explain the learning goals and the didactic or pedagogical approach used.

This means the submission should not only describe what participants did but should also demonstrate the educational reasoning behind the approach.

9. Tangibility

Evidence is a major consideration.

Applicants should provide concrete and codified evidence of their project, which could include:

Educational materials

Activity descriptions

Learning resources

Photographs

PDFs

Videos

Documents

Other project outputs

Evidence of activities

Other materials demonstrating implementation

This criterion is important because the call is designed to showcase real-world examples of education innovation.

10. Community Impact Beyond Learning and Teaching Environments

The project should ideally have an impact beyond the classroom or immediate learning environment.

The organisers want to highlight projects that connect education with actual community needs.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their work contributes to the wider community and addresses practical environmental, social or sustainability challenges.

How Will Applications Be Evaluated?

Each thematic area will be reviewed by a dedicated panel from the Education for Climate Secretariat, involving representatives from EACEA, DG EAC, and experts.

Applications will first undergo an eligibility check.

Eligible projects will then be evaluated using five main criteria:

Ambition

Multi-disciplinarity

Participation

Tangibility

Community impact

Each criterion is scored from 1 to 10.

Community impact receives additional weighting and can contribute up to 12 points.

The overall evaluation can therefore reach a maximum of 52 points.

This scoring structure means applicants should not focus exclusively on how innovative their idea sounds. They should also provide convincing evidence of participation, implementation, tangible outputs and real community impact.

How to Strengthen Your Application

Applicants can improve their submission by presenting their project as a clear story from problem to action to outcome.

A strong application should answer questions such as the following:

What sustainability or climate challenge were you addressing?

Why was the project necessary?

Who identified the problem?

Who participated?

What role did young people, educators or other stakeholders play?

What activities were implemented?

What educational methods were used?

Which GreenComp competences were addressed?

What changed because of the project?

What evidence can demonstrate the results?

How did the project benefit the wider community?

Could another school, organisation or community adapt the approach?

Where possible, applicants should support their claims with specific examples and tangible evidence.

For example, instead of simply stating that a project “engaged young people in sustainability”, explain how many young people participated, what responsibilities they had, what activities they led and what measurable or observable outcomes resulted.

What Do Selected Projects Receive?

The call offers significant visibility and networking opportunities for successful projects.

Presentation at Education for Climate Day 2026

Three projects will be selected from each thematic area.

With three thematic areas, this means a total of nine project examples will be selected to present their work and discuss their outcomes at Education for Climate Day 2026.

The event will take place on 22 October 2026.

Fully Funded Visit to Brussels

Representatives of selected projects will receive a fully funded visit to Brussels to participate in Education for Climate Day 2026.

This gives selected representatives an opportunity to:

Present their project.

Discuss their implementation experience.

Share lessons learned.

Participate in hybrid sessions.

Meet other climate education practitioners.

Exchange ideas with education stakeholders.

Build connections across the European Education Area.

Gain visibility for their work.

The opportunity is therefore not simply about recognition. It provides a platform for knowledge exchange and collaboration among people and organisations working on climate education.

Important Application Requirement: Verified User Status

Applicants should note that they need to be a verified user to submit a project.

The call advises applicants who need to update their user status to join an onboarding session.

This requirement is important because completing the project submission may depend on having the appropriate verified-user status before the application is finalised.

Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final day to resolve account or verification issues.

Submission Requirements

The Education for Climate Coalition states that applicants need to complete the required submission components, including the survey and blog.

Only complete applications, including both required components, will be considered.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they do not submit an incomplete application.

Before submitting, it is advisable to check that:

The project falls under one of the three themes.

The project meets the geographic requirement.

Concrete implementation has already taken place.

The project is within the eligible five-year period where applicable.

Relevant education actors have participated.

GreenComp competences are addressed.

The project covers at least one Education for Climate Innovation Area.

Appropriate learning and teaching methods are explained.

Tangible evidence is available.

Community impact is clearly demonstrated.

Both the survey and blog components are completed.

User verification requirements have been met.

Copyright, Privacy and Intellectual Property Requirements

Applicants must also ensure that they have the appropriate rights to all media submitted as part of their project.

This includes materials such as:

Photographs

Videos

Music

Documents

Other copyrighted materials

By submitting a project, applicants confirm that they either own the copyright to the media used or have the necessary licence or permission to use it.

Applicants must also ensure that their submission does not violate privacy rights, copyright or other intellectual property rights belonging to another person or organisation.

Plagiarism or copyright infringement can result in disqualification.

This makes it essential for applicants to verify the origin and usage rights of every photograph, video, piece of music, graphic, document or other copyrighted material included in their submission.

Key Dates for the Education for Climate 2026 Call

The timeline is important for anyone planning to participate.

Call opens: 18 June 2026

Application deadline: 6 September 2026

Selection notification: End of September 2026

Education for Climate Day 2026: 22 October 2026

Presentation of selected projects: 22 October 2026 in the hybrid event

Deadline: 6 September 2026

Applicants should submit their complete applications by 6 September 2026.

Because the submission requires both the survey and blog, applicants should allow sufficient time to prepare their materials, verify their account status, and check that all supporting evidence meets the requirements.

APPLY HERE

Why This Opportunity Matters for Climate Education

Climate change requires more than scientific knowledge. Communities also need the skills, values, participation mechanisms and educational approaches necessary to translate knowledge into action.

This is where initiatives such as the Education for Climate Coalition’s call become particularly relevant.

The programme highlights education as a mechanism for helping people understand sustainability challenges while also giving learners and communities opportunities to participate in developing solutions.

The three thematic areas also reflect different dimensions of climate education.

Youth leadership focuses on agency and intergenerational collaboration.

Citizenship education focuses on participation, institutional action and community engagement.

GreenComp focuses on competence development and the ability to envision sustainable futures.

Together, these areas provide a broad framework for demonstrating how education can contribute to the green transition.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be particularly relevant to organisations and individuals that have already implemented innovative sustainability education initiatives.

You should consider submitting if you have a project that:

Engages students or young people in climate action.

Connects different generations around sustainability.

Turns schools or institutions into living environments for sustainability.

Brings families and communities into climate education.

Uses education to promote green citizenship.

Connects research with public education.

Uses community knowledge to advance sustainability.

Incorporates GreenComp competences.

Helps learners imagine sustainable futures.

Uses innovative teaching and learning methods.

Produces tangible educational resources.

Demonstrates meaningful community impact.

Has already been implemented or is currently ongoing.

Small projects should not automatically be discouraged from applying. The call explicitly welcomes initiatives of different sizes and from different types of education settings.

Visit HERE for more information about the Innovative Green Education Action Projects 2026.

Pro Tip for Applicants

Do not describe only the idea behind your project — demonstrate the action and its impact.

The evaluation criteria place significant emphasis on participation, tangibility and community impact. Therefore, applicants should make their submission evidence-based.

Show:

The challenge → the people involved → the action taken → the educational approach → the evidence → the results → the community impact → what others can learn or replicate.

If photographs, videos, learning materials, reports, activity records or other documentation are available and can legally be shared, use them to demonstrate that the project has been implemented in practice.

It is also important to explicitly connect the project to the selected thematic area, GreenComp competence and relevant Education for Climate Innovation Area rather than expecting evaluators to make those connections themselves.

Final Thoughts

The Education for Climate Coalition Call for Innovative Green Education Action Projects 2026 provides a platform for showcasing practical examples of how education can contribute to climate action and sustainability.

The call is particularly valuable for projects that combine innovation with participation, education with action, and learning with community impact.

Applicants can submit projects under three thematic areas: Youth Leadership and Intergenerational Dialogue for Climate Action; Citizenship Education and Institutional Action for Sustainability; and GreenComp: Envisioning Sustainable Futures in Teaching and Learning.

Nine projects in total — three from each theme — will be selected to present their work at Education for Climate Day 2026 on 22 October. Representatives of selected projects will receive a fully funded visit to Brussels, providing an opportunity to showcase their work, exchange knowledge and connect with other climate education stakeholders across the European Education Area.

However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The project must be based in or across an eligible European Education Area country, have undergone concrete implementation, and satisfy the relevant thematic and evaluation criteria. Applicants must also complete all required components, including the survey and blog, and ensure that submitted media complies with copyright and privacy requirements.

With the 6 September 2026 deadline approaching, eligible applicants with strong, already-implemented climate or sustainability education projects should begin preparing their submissions without delay. The strongest applications will clearly demonstrate not only what makes their project innovative, but also who participated, what was implemented, what evidence exists, and how the project created meaningful impact within and beyond the learning environment.

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027, an initiative providing UK research organisations with funding of up to £62,500 to establish and deliver Policy Fellowship programmes for public and civil servants.

The programme is designed to strengthen connections between the UK research community and the public sector by creating opportunities for public and civil servants to spend dedicated time engaging with academics and researchers on real-world policy challenges.

Eligible research organisations across the United Kingdom can apply to EvEx to develop and run their own funded Policy Fellowship programme. Successful organisations will host Policy Fellows between January and May 2027, providing opportunities for problem-solving, professional development, network building, knowledge exchange and access to academic expertise.

Approximately 10 EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards are expected to be offered across the UK during the 2026–2027 programme cycle, with applications closing at midday on 8 October 2026.

About the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Programme

The EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship programme has been created to increase the number, capacity and diversity of Policy Fellowship opportunities available across the United Kingdom.

Through the programme, research organisations can receive financial and practical support to establish and deliver fellowships that connect researchers with UK public and civil servants.

Research organisations selected as hosts will be responsible for developing programmes that allow participating public and civil servants to spend meaningful time engaging with researchers and exploring specific policy questions and challenges.

Policy Fellows can be selected from any public bodies and across all levels of seniority.

The programme is intended to provide participating public and civil servants with opportunities to:

Explore specific policy challenges and questions with relevant researchers.

Access specialist academic and research expertise.

Develop new approaches to problem-solving.

Build relationships between researchers and policymakers.

Expand professional networks.

Participate in professional development and knowledge-exchange activities.

Explore policy issues through interdisciplinary academic perspectives.

The Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards are specifically intended to create additional capacity and diversity by supporting research organisations outside the existing EvEx consortium to establish their own Policy Fellowship programmes.

This funding call is complementary to EvEx’s separate call for individual and small-team Policy Fellows, which is administered and hosted directly by the EvEx consortium.

Funding Available Through the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship

Eligible organisations may apply for a maximum budget of £62,500 to deliver their proposed Associate Policy Fellowship programme.

EvEx suggests that organisations use the funding to offer approximately three to 10 Associate Policy Fellowships.

However, the programme also allows some flexibility in how organisations design their fellowship activities.

EvEx is open to proposals that use alternative approaches to engaging Associate Policy Fellows, provided that participating public or civil servants spend a minimum of five days during the five-month programme period exploring policy questions with research input from one or more participating research organisations.

This flexibility gives organisations the opportunity to develop a fellowship model suited to their institutional strengths, available expertise and the policy challenges they want to address.

When Will the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowships Take Place?

Successful host organisations will deliver their Associate Policy Fellowship programmes between January and May 2027.

Policy Fellows must spend a minimum of five days engaging with researchers at the host organisation or organisations during this five-month period.

For the standard fellowship model, Fellows or Fellowship teams will spend a minimum of five days in person at a university or universities, with those days distributed across January to May 2027.

The programme does not necessarily require Fellows to complete all five days consecutively. Instead, host organisations will need to design a programme that best meets the needs of their Fellows and the policy questions being explored.

What Can an Associate Policy Fellowship Include?

Each successful host organisation will be responsible for designing a programme that responds appropriately to its Fellows’ policy needs.

Activities may include:

1. Meetings Between Policy Fellows and Researchers

Policy Fellows can meet directly with researchers to discuss particular policy questions, challenges or areas where specialist knowledge would be valuable.

These engagements may take the form of individual meetings between a Fellow and a researcher or broader interdisciplinary discussions involving researchers from several fields.

Roundtable discussions may also be used to bring different academic perspectives to a policy problem.

2. Participation in Relevant Seminars and Events

Policy Fellows may participate in seminars, workshops, lectures or other relevant events taking place at the host university or research organisation.

This can provide Fellows with additional exposure to emerging research, specialist expertise and wider academic conversations related to their policy responsibilities.

3. Professional and Institutional Network Building

Host organisations can use the Fellowship programme to establish stronger connections between participating public and civil servants and the research community.

These relationships can help facilitate longer-term knowledge exchange and potentially create future opportunities for collaboration between policymakers and researchers.

Who Can Apply for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards?

The EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards are open to research organisations in the United Kingdom that are eligible for UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) funding.

Eligible organisations may include:

Universities.

Colleges.

Research centres.

Research institutes.

Public sector research establishments.

Other eligible independent research organisations.

Importantly, organisations do not need previous experience running Policy Fellowships.

EvEx specifically encourages applications from organisations that have never previously offered Policy Fellowships, as well as organisations that already have experience delivering similar programmes.

Groups of research organisations are also permitted to apply together and jointly operate an Associate Policy Fellowship programme.

Do Organisations Need to Have Policy Fellows Identified Before Applying?

No.

Applicants do not need to know who their prospective Policy Fellows will be when submitting their proposal.

Successful organisations can subsequently operate an open application process through which eligible Policy Fellows can apply.

The EvEx team can provide support and help amplify these recruitment opportunities.

This means organisations interested in establishing a programme should not be discouraged from applying simply because they have not already identified specific public or civil servants to participate.

Can Organisations Propose a Specific Fellowship Theme?

Yes.

Applicants may design their proposed Fellowships around a particular theme or policy topic.

However, EvEx advises organisations to consider avoiding themes that are excessively narrow, as broader themes may provide greater flexibility when recruiting Fellows and matching them with appropriate researchers.

Organisations uncertain about whether their proposed theme is suitable are encouraged to contact the EvEx team before submitting their application.

Who Can Participate as an EvEx Associate Policy Fellow?

For this programme, Policy Fellows are UK public and civil servants.

Host organisations can recruit individuals from different public bodies and at different levels of seniority.

Fellowships may be offered to:

Individual public or civil servants.

Small teams from the public or civil service.

Participants from different public bodies.

Participants across different levels of professional seniority.

Each Fellow or Fellowship team should engage with researchers for at least five days during the January–May 2027 programme period.

Benefits for Successful Host Organisations

The programme provides more than financial support.

Organisations receiving an EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Award will participate in a dedicated Coaching and Learning Programme designed to support them in developing and delivering effective Policy Fellowship programmes.

Successful hosts will receive assistance covering important stages of fellowship delivery.

Support From the EvEx Team

The EvEx team will provide advice and guidance on designing and delivering a Policy Fellowship programme.

Support can cover areas including:

Selecting and recruiting Fellows.

Matching Policy Fellows with appropriate researchers.

Designing fellowship activities.

Managing Fellows’ time within participating institutions.

Developing effective approaches to knowledge exchange.

Application and Documentation Templates

Successful host organisations will receive access to template application forms and other documentation.

These resources can be used directly or adapted to suit an organisation’s individual recruitment and programme requirements.

Coaching and Learning Support

Host teams will have access to ongoing assistance from a Coaching and Learning Consultant.

This will include:

Training.

Facilitated workshops.

Specially developed shared resources.

Practical guidance for Fellowship delivery.

Knowledge Exchange Between Host Organisations

Successful organisations will also have opportunities to interact with other participating hosts.

This provides an additional platform for sharing experiences, exchanging ideas and discussing best practices for running effective Policy Fellowship programmes.

Longer-Term Organisational Benefits

Running an Associate Policy Fellowship programme can also help participating institutions develop stronger relationships with policymakers and public sector professionals.

Potential organisational benefits highlighted by EvEx include:

Building networks of public and civil servants.

Establishing connections between public sector professionals and researchers.

Strengthening institutional policy engagement.

Developing the skills of staff responsible for managing Policy Fellowships.

Accessing training, workshops and shared learning resources.

Creating opportunities to demonstrate case studies and impacts resulting from policy-to-research engagement.

Policy Fellows recruited through participating organisations will also be invited to join the wider EvEx Policy Fellows network, through which they can receive invitations to relevant networking activities and events.

EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027 Timeline

Applicants should take note of the following key dates:

1 September 2026: Applications open.

9 September 2026: Online information session for prospective applicants.

8 October 2026: Application deadline.

By 30 October 2026: Applicants expected to be notified of outcomes.

Late January 2027: Fellowships begin.

March 2027: Interim report submitted.

By 31 May 2027: Fellowships completed.

30 June 2027: Final report submitted.

The source also lists “By 11 January 2026 – EvEx Policy Fellows recruited.” This appears chronologically inconsistent with the surrounding 2027 programme dates, so prospective applicants should refer to the official guidance or confirm the intended year directly with EvEx rather than assuming a correction.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards is midday on 8 October 2026.

Applications opened on 1 September 2026.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to prepare their proposals early and carefully review the official guidance before completing the online application.

Online Information Session for Applicants

EvEx will host an online information session for prospective applicants on:

9 September 2026 at 1:30 p.m.

The webinar will provide an opportunity to learn more about the Policy Fellowships and ask questions about either the Fellowship model or the application process.

Prospective applicants can register for the session through the official EvEx website.

How to Apply for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship

Organisations interested in applying should first review the complete programme guidance and application form provided by EvEx.

Applicants can then prepare their proposal and submit the final application using the online application form available through the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship webpage.

The application guidance and a downloadable application form are available to help organisations prepare their responses before completing the online submission.

Applicants are also encouraged to discuss their proposed project with the EvEx team before submitting an application. This provides an opportunity to check whether the proposed organisation and programme meet the scheme’s eligibility requirements and intended scope.

Applicants wishing to arrange a discussion can contact Christina Rozeik and the EvEx team at evex@csap.cam.ac.uk.

Applications may also be submitted in Welsh. Welsh-language guidance is available, and applicants who want the application form in Welsh can request it directly from the EvEx team.

APPLY NOW

Reporting Requirements for Successful Organisations

Successful organisations will be required to report on their Fellowship activities and expenditure at two key stages.

Interim Report – March 2027

Around the midpoint of the programme, participating organisations will complete an interim reporting form.

The interim report is expected to cover:

Information about the EvEx Policy Fellows recruited.

Progress achieved to date.

Programme activities undertaken.

Budget expenditure.

Final Report – June 2027

Following completion of the Fellowship programme, host organisations will submit a final report.

The report will request fuller information concerning:

Delivery of the programme.

Overall expenditure.

Activities undertaken.

Outcomes and impacts that have emerged from the programme.

The source states that the final report is due 30 June 2027.

How Many Hosting Awards Are Available?

For the 2026–2027 programme, EvEx expects to offer approximately 10 Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards across the United Kingdom.

Because the number of awards is limited, eligible organisations interested in participating should carefully develop proposals that demonstrate how their Fellowship programme can create meaningful engagement between researchers and public or civil servants.

About Evidence Exchange (EvEx)

Evidence Exchange, or EvEx, is supporting stronger connections between research and policymaking through initiatives such as the Associate Policy Fellowship programme.

The programme is funded by the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) and delivered by the Centre for Science and Policy (CSaP) at the University of Cambridge, together with partners across the United Kingdom.

Through the Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards, EvEx aims to expand Policy Fellowship opportunities beyond its existing consortium and help additional research organisations develop the capacity, expertise and networks required to engage effectively with policymakers.

Conclusion

The EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027 represents a substantial opportunity for UK research organisations seeking to strengthen connections between academic research and public policymaking.

With funding of up to £62,500, successful organisations can establish programmes that bring UK public and civil servants into closer engagement with researchers, creating space to explore real policy challenges, access specialist expertise, develop professional networks and strengthen knowledge exchange.

The opportunity is particularly accessible because applicants do not need previous experience running Policy Fellowships, and organisations can receive extensive practical support through EvEx’s Coaching and Learning Programme. Universities and other eligible research organisations may also collaborate and submit joint proposals.

Approximately 10 hosting awards are expected to be available during the 2026–2027 cycle.

Eligible UK research organisations interested in applying should review the official programme guidance, consider attending the 9 September 2026 information session, and prepare their proposal ahead of the final application deadline.

Application Deadline: Midday, 8 October 2026.

Visit the OFY website for more Grant and Fellowship opportunities.

TITLE: EGU 2025 in Vienna, Austria – by MIT/WHOI Joint Program Student Sean Chen

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Pictured left to right: Guest Investigator Maurice Huguenin, Senior Scientist Caroline Ummenhofer, MIT/WHOI JP Student Cora Hersh, Postdoctoral Investigator Ali Exley, Postdoctoral Investigator Carolina Camargo, MIT/WHOI Joint Program Student Sean Chen and MIT/WHOI Joint Program Student Hiroki Nagao. Photo provided by Sean Chen.

It was a warm and beautiful week in central Europe. Several of us from the PO department had a wonderful time presenting and learning everyone else’s research, while also soaking up a lot of sunshine in Vienna. We were lucky that the weather this year was perfect, and we were happy to see many familiar faces across the pond.

The European Geoscience Union (EGU) general assembly takes place every year around April/May at the Vienna International Centre in Austria – always the same venue. It is a relatively compact space and easy to get around. Many of us were in the Ocean Science sessions – covering the Atlantic Ocean, Southern Ocean, and Indian Ocean. I was in the Atlantic session on Tuesday, when Senior Scientist Magdalena Andres, Joint Program Student Hiroki Nagao, Postdoctoral Investigator Ali Exley, and I gave talks. Joint Program Student Cora Hersh presented on Thursday, when we also took a group photo.

Personally, EGU is my favorite conference – it covers a wide variety of geoscience and is effectively the AGU equivalent in Europe. But the fact it is at the same venue every year means it is rather predictable, and I like the sense of familiarity in subsequent years. Vienna is also a hub of music and theatre, with its ornate urban landscape reminiscent of the high days as the capital of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. The Donau Park next to the conference center provides a wonderful place for conference attendees to enjoy sunshine together during the long lunch breaks; there’s a very cute train that operates on a well-defined timetable, as frequently as the Clark-Village shuttle at WHOI. Highly recommend…

Joint Program Student Hiroki Nagao presents his work. Photo by Sean Chen.

TITLE: Ozyegin University Summer Program 2026 in Turkey

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Ozyegin University Summer Program 2026 is now open and invites international students from around the world to apply for a fully funded summer research program in Turkey. This is the first summer research program launched by Ozyegin University, providing undergraduate students with hands-on experience in scientific research processes. Several research projects have been announced, and participants may choose the ones that best match their interests. The program in Turkey runs from June to August 2026, offering an excellent opportunity for students to gain practical research skills while working in a vibrant academic environment.

Moreover, the Ozyegin University Summer Program 2026 is a funded program that focuses on both technical training and academic mentorship. Students will receive guidance from experienced faculty and access state-of-the-art laboratories to carry out their projects. They will also participate in workshops and collaborative activities that enhance their problem-solving and research capabilities. Consequently, participants gain valuable interdisciplinary skills and experience, which can strengthen their future academic and career prospects.

Furthermore, students in this summer program will engage in research projects across multiple disciplines, including engineering, robotics, artificial intelligence, data science, business, legal AI, sustainability, logistics, social sciences, and economics. Each project combines theory with practical application, allowing participants to develop critical thinking, analytical skills, and technical expertise. This approach ensures that students not only learn advanced scientific methods but also apply them to solve real-world problems.

Additionally, the Ozyegin University Summer Program is funded, which means selected participants will not have to worry about basic expenses. Accommodation, meals, laboratory access, technical support, and guidance are fully covered. Moreover, the international research program offers a structured environment that connects learning with research practice, helping students prepare for higher studies, graduate programs, and professional careers in science, technology, and related fields.

Overall, the Ozyegin University Summer Program in Turkey offers a unique opportunity for international undergraduate students to gain hands-on research experience, develop technical and analytical skills, and work closely with expert faculty across diverse fields. This international research program not only covers accommodation, meals, and laboratory access but also provides mentorship and guidance to help students excel in scientific research. If you are eager to explore research in Turkey, build a strong academic profile, and prepare for future studies or careers in science, technology, and innovation, this program is the perfect choice for a transformative and enriching summer experience.

TITLE: Anheuser-Busch University & Early Career Opportunities 2026: Internships, Co-Ops and Full-Time Jobs for Students and Recent Graduates

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
If you are a university student, recent graduate, or early-career professional looking for an opportunity to gain practical industry experience, develop professional skills, work alongside experienced professionals, and build a strong foundation for your career, Anheuser-Busch offers a range of University & Early Career Opportunities designed to help emerging talent enter and grow within the company.

Anheuser-Busch’s early-career opportunities are designed around a learn-by-doing approach. Rather than limiting participants to classroom-style training, the company provides opportunities to gain hands-on exposure to real business functions and understand how different teams work together.

The available opportunities include full-time positions, internships, and co-op programs across areas such as logistics, supply chain, procurement, technology, marketing, sales, finance, legal, sustainability, brewing, people, communications, corporate affairs, and other business functions.

For students and graduates who want to develop practical experience with a major global beverage company, these opportunities can provide exposure to real business operations, professional mentorship, senior leadership, technical development, and potential long-term career growth.

Opportunity Overview

Anheuser-Busch describes its early-career opportunities as programs and positions created to help individuals at the beginning of their professional journeys develop through practical experience.

The opportunities are particularly relevant to people who want to combine academic knowledge with real-world business experience.

Depending on the position, applicants may be considered for:

Full-time early-career positions

Internship opportunities

Co-op opportunities

Talent programs

Trainee opportunities

Opportunities across technical and non-technical business functions

The company’s early-career approach is centered around giving new talent meaningful exposure to the organization and its operations.

Rather than simply observing experienced employees, participants can gain experience working within business functions and learning how teams contribute to the company’s broader objectives.

What Is the Anheuser-Busch University & Early Career Program?

The University & Early Career platform brings together opportunities for students, recent graduates, and early-career professionals.

According to Anheuser-Busch, its early-career opportunities are designed to provide individuals with opportunities to learn through practical experience.

This approach can be particularly valuable for individuals who have academic qualifications but are looking for opportunities to develop workplace experience.

Participants can potentially learn how a large organization operates, understand professional expectations, collaborate with colleagues, develop technical and interpersonal skills, and gain insight into how different departments contribute to the company’s operations.

The programs are also designed to support professional development and help identify and develop future leaders.

Types of Opportunities Available

1. Full-Time Early Career Opportunities

Anheuser-Busch provides full-time opportunities for individuals who are ready to begin or continue their professional careers.

These positions may be suitable for recent graduates and early-career professionals, although the exact eligibility requirements depend on the individual vacancy.

Full-time employees can gain direct experience within their selected business function while becoming part of the company’s workforce.

Applicants should carefully review each vacancy because qualifications, experience requirements, location, and other conditions can differ from one position to another.

Interested candidates can explore the company’s full-time early-career opportunities through the official Anheuser-Busch careers platform.

2. Internship Opportunities

Internships provide students and early-career candidates with opportunities to gain practical workplace experience.

An internship can help bridge the gap between university education and professional employment by allowing participants to apply knowledge in a real business environment.

Anheuser-Busch’s internship opportunities can involve different areas of the business, depending on the positions available during each recruiting cycle.

Interns may have opportunities to:

Work on real business activities

Learn from experienced professionals

Develop technical and professional skills

Understand organizational operations

Collaborate with colleagues

Gain exposure to business decision-making

Develop their professional networks

Explore potential career paths

The company highlights the importance of hands-on experience as part of its early-career programs.

3. Co-Op Opportunities

Anheuser-Busch also offers co-op opportunities as part of its early-career programs.

Co-op experiences can be especially valuable for university students who want to gain professional experience before completing their education.

Depending on the individual position, participants may be able to work within a specific business function and gain a deeper understanding of how their academic background connects with professional responsibilities.

Because co-op requirements vary by position, applicants should review the eligibility criteria for each vacancy before applying.

Key Benefits of Anheuser-Busch Early Career Opportunities

One of the major attractions of these opportunities is the emphasis on professional development.

Hands-On Business Experience

Anheuser-Busch’s programs are designed around learning by doing.

Participants can gain exposure to actual business functions and workplace responsibilities instead of relying exclusively on theoretical learning.

This type of experience can help students and graduates develop a better understanding of how organizations operate.

Exposure to Multiple Business Functions

Anheuser-Busch operates through a wide range of departments.

Early-career participants can potentially gain exposure to areas including:

Brewing

Logistics

Supply chain

Procurement

Marketing

Sales

Technology

Communications

Corporate affairs

People and human resources

Finance

Legal

Sustainability

Brewery operations

Craft operations

This diversity means that individuals with different academic and professional interests may find opportunities relevant to their career goals.

Mentorship and Senior Leadership Exposure

Anheuser-Busch states that its early-career programs provide exposure to senior leadership through mentorship opportunities and facilitated events.

This can be an important advantage for individuals who are still developing their professional identities.

Interacting with experienced professionals can help participants understand workplace expectations, learn from established leaders, receive guidance, and build professional relationships.

Professional Growth and Development

The company emphasizes growth and development throughout its early-career opportunities.

Participants can receive relevant training and gain exposure to business operations from the beginning of their experience.

This development-oriented environment can help individuals build capabilities that may remain useful throughout their careers.

Potential Leadership Development

How to Use the S.T.A.R. Method

The S.T.A.R. method can help candidates structure answers to behavioral interview questions.

S.T.A.R. stands for:

Task: Describe what you were responsible for accomplishing.

Action: Explain the specific actions you personally took.

Result: Explain what happened as a result of your actions.

For example, instead of simply stating that you are a good team player, you can describe a real situation where you worked with others to solve a problem, explain your responsibility, outline the actions you took, and conclude with the measurable or meaningful result.

TITLE: Czech Republic Government Scholarships 2027/2028 for Developing Countries: Fully Funded Master’s and PhD Study Opportunities

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Government of the Czech Republic has opened applications for its Government Scholarships for Developing Countries for the 2027/2028 academic year, providing eligible international students from selected developing and specific third countries with an opportunity to pursue higher education at public universities in the Czech Republic.

The scholarships are offered as part of the Czech Republic’s Foreign Development Cooperation Programme and are designed to support the education and professional development of nationals from selected countries. Depending on the applicant’s country and chosen programme, the opportunity supports selected follow-up Master’s and Doctoral programmes, with studies available in either Czech or English.

For the 2027/2028 academic year, applications are open from 21 August 2026 until 30 September 2026. Prospective applicants are therefore encouraged to begin preparing their academic documents, motivation letter, tests and other application requirements well before the deadline.

Opportunity Overview

Opportunity: Government Scholarships – Developing Countries

Host country: Czech Republic

Academic year: 2027/2028

Study level: Follow-up Master’s and Doctoral studies

Study mode: Full-time

Study language: Czech and English, depending on the programme and applicant’s country

Host institutions: Public higher education institutions in the Czech Republic

Application period: 21 August 2026 to 30 September 2026

Application deadline: 30 September 2026

Programme framework: Czech Republic Foreign Development Cooperation

About the Czech Government Scholarships

The Government of the Czech Republic has a long-standing tradition of providing scholarships to international students from developing countries.

The programme forms part of the country’s international development cooperation efforts and seeks to contribute to the educational and professional development of people from selected developing and specific third countries.

According to the Czech Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports, more than 20,000 foreign nationals have completed studies at Czech universities with support from Government of the Czech Republic scholarships since the late 1950s.

The current scholarship programme is governed by Resolution of the Government of the Czech Republic No. 870 of 27 November 2024 and is implemented through cooperation between the Czech Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Health.

Applicants should therefore understand that this is not simply a university-specific scholarship. It is a government scholarship programme connected to the Czech Republic’s broader foreign development cooperation policy.

Which Countries Are Eligible for the 2027/2028 Scholarships?

One of the most important aspects of this scholarship is that eligibility is restricted to nationals of specific countries.

For the 2027/2028 academic year, Government of the Czech Republic scholarships are available only to citizens of the following countries:

Europe and Eastern Europe

Bosnia and Herzegovina

Georgia

Ukraine

Belarus, specifically democratic forces

Africa

Ethiopia

Gabon

Mauritania

Zambia

Asia

Bangladesh

Cambodia

Palestine

Latin America

Guatemala

Honduras

Applicants should carefully verify their nationality before beginning the application because nationals of countries outside the official eligible-country list cannot apply under this particular scholarship call.

What Study Programmes Are Available?

The Government of the Czech Republic scholarship supports selected full-time programmes rather than every degree programme offered by Czech universities.

The available programmes are divided into studies conducted in Czech and studies conducted in English.

1. Czech-Language Study Programmes

For eligible applicants from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine and Belarus, the scholarship can support selected follow-up Master’s programmes taught in the Czech language.

These programmes generally consist of:

A one-year preparatory Czech language course; followed by

A two-year follow-up Master’s degree programme in a selected field.

The preparatory language training is part of the scholarship and is provided by the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies of Charles University.

Applicants interested in Czech-medium studies should consult the official list of selected areas of study before choosing a programme.

2. English-Language Master’s Programmes

Applicants from all countries included in the eligible-country list can apply for selected follow-up Master’s programmes delivered in English.

The English-medium Master’s programmes are generally two years in duration.

However, applicants should not assume that every Master’s degree offered by Czech public universities is covered by the scholarship. Candidates must select a programme from the official list of eligible English-medium programmes published for the scholarship call.

3. English-Language Doctoral Programmes

The scholarship also supports selected Doctoral study programmes taught in English.

These programmes generally last between three and four years, depending on the specific programme.

Doctoral applicants must have already completed a Master’s degree before they can qualify for scholarship support at the doctoral level.

Academic Requirements

Applicants should pay particular attention to the academic qualification requirements because the required previous degree depends on the level of study being pursued.

Requirements for Master’s Applicants

To receive a government scholarship for a follow-up Master’s programme, an applicant must have completed a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent undergraduate study programme.

The Bachelor’s qualification should provide the academic foundation necessary for the selected Master’s programme.

Applicants should also check the admission requirements of their selected university and degree programme because meeting the general government scholarship requirement does not necessarily mean that the applicant automatically meets every university-specific admission requirement.

Requirements for Doctoral Applicants

Applicants seeking a government scholarship for a Doctoral programme must have completed a Master’s degree or equivalent qualification.

Doctoral applicants should pay particular attention to the requirements of their selected doctoral programme, including any academic, research or admission requirements specified by the university.

English Language Requirement

Applicants seeking scholarships for English-medium studies have an additional requirement.

They must complete an online entrance English language test during the scholarship application process.

The purpose of the test is to establish whether the applicant has sufficient command of English for the proposed English-medium studies.

This means prospective applicants should not wait until the final day of the application period to begin completing the online application. The application is not considered complete simply because an applicant has registered.

Applicants should ensure that all mandatory components, including the applicable tests, have been completed.

How the Application Process Works

Applications for the Government of the Czech Republic scholarships are submitted electronically.

The application platform is available through the official Study in Czechia portal under the relevant scholarship call.

Applicants should follow the application process carefully and provide accurate information throughout the registration and submission stages.

Step 1: Confirm Your Eligibility

Before creating an application, determine whether:

You are a citizen of one of the countries listed in the official call.

You are applying for an eligible study programme.

You have the required previous academic qualification.

You meet the requirements for the selected university and programme.

You are not excluded because of your residence or citizenship status.

You can complete the required online tests.

You can submit the complete application before the deadline.

This initial eligibility check can save applicants considerable time.

Step 2: Select an Eligible Study Programme

Applicants should review the official lists of selected programmes before making their academic choice.

The scholarship does not cover every programme available at Czech public universities.

There are separate official lists covering:

Selected areas of study for programmes offered in Czech;

Selected Master’s programmes offered in English; and

Selected Doctoral programmes offered in English.

Applicants should therefore identify an eligible programme rather than selecting a course simply because it is offered by a Czech university.

Step 3: Register on the Application Portal

Applicants must access the relevant scholarship call through the official Study in Czechia portal and register to begin the electronic application.

Each applicant is allowed to register only once and submit only one application.

This makes it particularly important to carefully consider the selected programme and review all information before submitting the application.

Step 4: Complete the Electronic Application Form

Applicants must provide the information requested in the online application form.

The information should be accurate, consistent and supported by the relevant documentation where required.

Candidates should avoid waiting until the final hours before the deadline because technical or connectivity problems can interfere with submission.

Step 5: Write the Motivation Letter

The application is complete only after the applicant has completed the required motivation letter.

The motivation letter should be treated as an important part of the application rather than a formality.

A strong motivation letter should clearly explain the applicant’s:

Academic background;

Reasons for choosing the proposed programme;

Interest in studying in the Czech Republic;

Academic and professional objectives;

Relevant experience and achievements;

Future career plans; and

How the proposed education can contribute to the applicant’s professional development and, where appropriate, development in their home country.

Applicants should ensure that their motivation is specific to the chosen field of study rather than submitting a generic scholarship essay.

Step 6: Complete the Mandatory Tests

Applicants must also complete the mandatory tests associated with the scholarship.

Candidates applying for Czech-language studies complete the general study prerequisites test.

Candidates applying for English-medium studies must complete:

The general study prerequisites test; and

The English language test.

Applicants should therefore allocate sufficient time to complete all mandatory components.

Important Exclusions

The Government of the Czech Republic makes clear that these scholarships are specifically intended to support foreign nationals from developing and specific third countries.

As a result, the following people cannot apply for this particular type of government scholarship:

Citizens of the Czech Republic;

Citizens of European Union member states; and

Other foreign nationals who have a permanent residence permit in the Czech Republic.

Applicants should carefully review their citizenship and residence status before submitting an application.

There is also no legal entitlement to receive a scholarship simply because an applicant submits an application. Meeting the eligibility requirements allows an individual to apply, but it does not guarantee that the scholarship will be awarded.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The scholarship is designed to cover the standard length of full-time study under the supported programme.

The exact structure of the scholarship depends on the study pathway.

For eligible Czech-language studies, the support includes the one-year Czech language preparatory course followed by the relevant Master’s programme.

For English-medium studies, the scholarship supports selected two-year Master’s programmes and selected three- to four-year Doctoral programmes.

Applicants should consult the official scholarship guidelines for the detailed financial and administrative conditions applicable to scholarship holders.

Duration of Study

The expected duration depends on the programme selected.

Czech-medium Master’s pathway

One year of Czech language preparation

Two years of follow-up Master’s study

English-medium Master’s pathway

Approximately two years of follow-up Master’s study

English-medium Doctoral pathway

Approximately three to four years of Doctoral study

The scholarship is intended to support the standard duration of the relevant full-time study programme.

Application Deadline

The application period for the 2027/2028 Government of the Czech Republic Scholarships for Developing Countries opened on:

21 August 2026

The final application deadline is:

30 September 2026

Applicants must complete and submit the electronic application by 30 September 2026 at the latest.

Successful applicants are expected to begin their studies during the 2027/2028 academic year.

Because the application contains several components, including a motivation letter and mandatory tests, applicants are strongly advised not to leave submission until the deadline.

Official Application Portal

Applications are submitted electronically through the official Study in Czechia portal.

The Government of the Czech Republic scholarship information is also published by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports of the Czech Republic.

Prospective applicants should rely on the official scholarship documentation when making decisions about eligibility, study programmes and application requirements.

Important Scholarship Documents

Applicants are encouraged to read the official guidelines carefully before submitting an application.

The Government of the Czech Republic provides detailed guidance covering the terms and conditions of the scholarship.

The official documentation includes:

Guidelines for Granting Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic – English version

Guidelines for Granting Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic – Czech version

Frequently Asked Questions

Lists of selected study programmes

Information concerning personal data processing

The official English guidelines are particularly important for international applicants because they explain the applicable rules and conditions in greater detail.

Frequently Asked Questions and Additional Support

Applicants who cannot find answers to their questions in the official scholarship guidelines and FAQ documents can contact the programme support team.

The official information identifies registr@dzs.cz as the contact email for enquiries that are not addressed in the published documentation.

Applicants should first consult the official guidelines and FAQ before contacting the support team, particularly for questions concerning information already explained in the published documents.

Personal Data and Privacy

Applicants should also familiarize themselves with the information concerning the processing and protection of personal data.

The scholarship application involves the collection and processing of personal information, and the Czech authorities provide information about data protection in accordance with applicable European Union data protection requirements.

Applicants should review the relevant privacy information before submitting their applications.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Although meeting the eligibility criteria is essential, applicants should also focus on the quality and completeness of their submission.

1. Start Early

Do not wait until September to begin preparing.

The application involves multiple stages, including registration, programme selection, the motivation letter and mandatory tests.

Starting early gives applicants enough time to identify and correct errors.

2. Choose the Programme Carefully

One of the most important decisions is the selection of the study programme.

Applicants should confirm that their chosen programme appears on the official list of programmes supported by the scholarship.

3. Check Your Academic Qualification

Master’s applicants should confirm that they have completed a Bachelor’s degree.

Doctoral applicants should confirm that they have completed a Master’s degree.

Applicants should also consider whether their academic background aligns with the admission requirements of the programme.

4. Take the English Test Seriously

Applicants applying for English-medium studies must complete the online English language test.

Candidates should prepare for the test and make sure they have adequate time and a suitable internet connection when completing it.

5. Prepare a Targeted Motivation Letter

A generic motivation letter can weaken an otherwise strong application.

The letter should connect the applicant’s academic background, chosen programme and future ambitions.

Applicants should demonstrate why the proposed field of study matters to their professional development and explain why the selected programme is appropriate for their goals.

6. Read the Official Guidelines

Applicants should not rely solely on summaries posted on third-party websites.

The official guidelines contain the authoritative conditions governing the scholarship.

Candidates should read the guidelines before submitting their application and use the FAQ to clarify common questions.

7. Submit Before the Deadline

The deadline is 30 September 2026.

Submitting early reduces the risk of missing the deadline because of technical problems, incomplete tests or other unforeseen circumstances.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This scholarship may be particularly valuable for eligible nationals who want to pursue postgraduate education in Europe but need financial support to access higher education abroad.
