TITLE: The Association of African Universities Expresses Solidarity and Urges Global Support for Sudan’s Academic Community Amidst Crisis

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
October 23, 2023 – In response to the ongoing crisis affecting universities and other higher education institutions in Sudan, the Association of African Universities (AAU), headquartered in Accra, Ghana, has expressed great concern for the plight and current travails of both the staff and students, who are caught in the midst of the devasting war in the country. The Association wants to put on record the great contributions of the many Sudanese scholars to Africa’s development. [DOWNLOAD A VERSION OF THIS STATEMENT in ENGLISH, FRENCH, and ARABIC.

Amid the turmoil and adversity faced by these universities, the Association of African Universities calls upon the warring parties to earnestly seek a resolution through peaceful means. We also extend a heartfelt appeal to universities around the world to join hands in offering support to Sudanese scholars who are currently enduring immense hardships, through no fault of theirs.

In August 2023, Sudan’s Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research highlighted in a statement that condemned the ongoing destruction that a total of 104 government and private higher education institutions, as well as research centres and the National Fund for Student Welfare, had been damaged and vandalised since April. The Ministry’s offices had also recorded some destruction in a fire that affected several floors. This scale of destruction and interruption is one that calls for urgent attention.

It is the AAU’s fervent hope that global leaders will continue to allocate the necessary resources needed to support immediate humanitarian relief efforts. We also align our voice with that of the Sudanese National Academy of Sciences, urging the global scientific community to collaborate in mobilizing potential donors within their nations to contribute to the critical reconstruction efforts aimed at revitalizing the academic infrastructure destroyed by the conflict.

Our unwavering commitment to this cause stems from our belief that we cannot turn a blind eye to the profound suffering, anguish, and pain that a large number of researchers, university administrators, and students in Sudan are experiencing at this critical juncture. The support of the international community is hereby being sought to help restore normalcy to the operations of universities in Sudan and to ensure that the pursuit of knowledge and academic endeavours can continue without hindrance.

The Association of African Universities remains dedicated to fostering peace, stability, and the advancement of education on the African continent. Together, we can play a pivotal role in alleviating the suffering faced by the academic community in Sudan and contributing to the restoration of their educational institutions to their rightful place in the pursuit of knowledge and progress.

Prof. Olusola Oyewole

(Secretary-General)

Association of African Universities

TITLE: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027: Apply for Graduate Study at the University of Hawai‘i

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027 is now accepting applications from eligible students seeking to pursue graduate-level study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa in the United States.

The fellowship is offered by the East-West Center (EWC) and is designed to support graduate study in academic fields that are relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center. The fellowship is awarded through an international competition, giving eligible applicants from the United States and selected countries across the Pacific, Southeast Asia, South Asia and East Asia an opportunity to compete for graduate study support.

For prospective applicants, this is an important opportunity to combine advanced academic study at the University of Hawai‘i with the broader educational, cultural and international community associated with the East-West Center.

The application deadline is December 1, 2026.

East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027 at a Glance

Opportunity: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship

Academic year: 2026–2027

Host institution: University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa

Host country: United States

Study level: Graduate

Selection method: International competition

Opening period: August 2026

Application deadline: December 1, 2026

University admission deadline for new UH Mānoa applicants: December 1, 2026

Supporting documents deadline: January 10, following the application deadline

Eligible applicants: Citizens or permanent residents of the specified eligible countries and territories

Academic requirement: Four-year bachelor’s degree or equivalent

General GPA requirement: Minimum 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or equivalent

Study location: University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa

Application contact: scholarships@eastwestcenter.org

What Is the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship?

The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship is a graduate education opportunity supporting students undertaking advanced study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa.

The fellowship focuses on graduate study in fields that are relevant to the objectives and mission of the East-West Center. Successful applicants therefore have the opportunity not only to pursue graduate education but also to become part of an international academic environment bringing together students and professionals connected to the United States and the Asia-Pacific region.

The fellowship is awarded annually through an international competitive process. Applicants should therefore expect their academic background, qualifications and overall suitability for the fellowship to be considered alongside applications from other eligible candidates.

For the 2026–2027 academic year, applications are being invited during the 2026 application cycle.

Why Consider the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship?

Graduate education in the United States can provide students with access to advanced academic training, international exposure, research opportunities and professional networks.

The East-West Center fellowship is particularly significant because it connects graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i with the broader East-West Center environment.

Successful fellows can therefore benefit from an academic experience situated within an institution whose work focuses on relationships and understanding among the United States and countries and peoples of the Asia-Pacific region.

The opportunity may be particularly relevant to students whose academic and professional interests intersect with areas connected to the East-West Center’s goals and objectives.

Where Will Fellows Study?

The fellowship supports graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa, commonly known as UH Mānoa.

The University of Hawai‘i’s graduate application process is separate from the East-West Center fellowship application. This means prospective applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa need to complete the relevant University of Hawai‘i admission process in addition to the East-West Center fellowship application.

Applicants should therefore treat the two processes as connected but distinct requirements.

Who Can Apply for the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship?

Eligibility is geographically restricted.

The East-West Center states that individuals who are citizens or permanent residents of the specified countries and territories may apply.

The eligible locations are divided into the following groups:

1. United States

Citizens and permanent residents of the United States are eligible to apply.

2. Pacific Region

Eligible Pacific locations include the following:

American Samoa

Cook Islands

Federated States of Micronesia

Fiji

French Polynesia

Marshall Islands

Palau

Samoa

Tokelau

Tonga

Vanuatu

Wallis & Futuna Islands

3. Southeast Asia

Eligible Southeast Asian countries include the following:

Brunei

Cambodia

Indonesia

Laos

Malaysia

Myanmar

Philippines

Singapore

Thailand

Timor-Leste

Vietnam

4. South Asia

Eligible South Asian countries include:

Afghanistan

Bangladesh

Bhutan

India

Iran

Maldives

Nepal

Pakistan

Sri Lanka

5. East Asia

Eligible East Asian countries and territories include:

China

Hong Kong

Japan

Macau

Mongolia

North Korea

South Korea

Russia

Taiwan

Important Eligibility Note for African Applicants

Applicants should carefully review the geographic eligibility requirement before investing time in the application.

The eligible-country list provided by the East-West Center does not include African countries. This means applicants from countries such as Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Ethiopia and other African countries are not included in the eligible-country list provided for this fellowship.

There is also no separate race or ethnicity-based eligibility category stated in the information provided. Eligibility is primarily determined by citizenship or permanent residency, academic qualifications and other fellowship requirements.

Academic Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy specific academic requirements before the fellowship begins.

For graduate programs, applicants must have obtained a four-year bachelor’s degree or equivalent.

The degree must be from either:

An accredited college or university in the United States; or

A recognized institution of higher learning outside the United States.

This means applicants with undergraduate qualifications obtained outside the United States can still be considered, provided their qualification is recognized as equivalent to the required four-year bachelor’s degree.

Minimum GPA Requirement

Applicants are generally expected to have a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale, or an equivalent academic performance.

The GPA requirement applies to:

The applicant’s last four semesters of undergraduate study; or

The applicant’s last six quarters of undergraduate study; and

All post-baccalaureate academic work, where applicable.

This is an important distinction because applicants should not assume that only their cumulative undergraduate GPA will be considered.

Applicants who have completed postgraduate coursework should also take their post-baccalaureate academic performance into account when assessing their competitiveness.

What If Your University Uses a Different Grading System?

The East-West Center recognizes that universities outside the United States may use different grading systems.

The stated requirement is a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent.

Therefore, applicants whose universities do not use the U.S. 4.0 GPA system should consider how their academic results correspond to the required standard and provide accurate academic documentation during the application process.

Applicants should avoid independently converting grades in a way that misrepresents their academic record. Where official documentation or institutional guidance is available, applicants should follow the appropriate process.

Fields of Study

The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship supports graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i in fields relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center.

This means prospective applicants should not focus only on whether a graduate program is available at UH Mānoa. They should also consider whether their intended field of study aligns with the broader purpose and objectives of the East-West Center.

Applicants are encouraged to review the fellowship’s official information, frequently asked questions and award details before submitting an application.

How the Application Process Works

The fellowship application process involves more than simply completing the East-West Center application.

Applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa must also apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester.

Consequently, prospective applicants should plan their application in two parallel tracks:

Apply for the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship.

Apply for admission to the appropriate University of Hawai‘i graduate program.

Both processes should be planned carefully because missing a university admission requirement can affect the overall application timeline.

University of Hawai‘i Admission Requirement

If you are not already enrolled as a classified graduate student at UH Mānoa, you must apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester by December 1, 2026.

The University of Hawai‘i launches its online graduate application system on August 1 each year for admission the following year.

Prospective applicants should therefore begin preparing their university application well before the fellowship deadline.

This is particularly important for applicants applying to graduate departments that may have additional admission requirements.

Supporting Documents Deadline

The East-West Center also provides an important date after the main application deadline.

To ensure timely processing of the East-West Center application, supporting documents for both the University of Hawai‘i admissions office and the relevant department applications must be completed by January 10.

This requirement applies regardless of whether the particular UH departmental deadline falls after January 10.

Applicants should therefore not assume that a later departmental deadline automatically gives them additional time for the East-West Center process.

A good strategy is to aim to complete all required university and departmental materials before January 10.

Application Forms Required

The East-West Center provides specific application forms that prospective applicants should review and complete as applicable.

Two important forms highlighted in the application information are the following:

1. Academic Letter of Reference Form

Applicants are required to use the Academic Letter of Reference Form and accompanying instructions provided by the East-West Center.

The form is available as a fillable PDF and is intended to support the academic reference component of the application.

Applicants should identify an appropriate academic referee early enough to allow the referee sufficient time to prepare and submit the required documentation.

2. Civic Engagement Letter of Reference Form

The application also includes a Civic Engagement Letter of Reference Form and instructions.

This component highlights the importance of applicants demonstrating engagement beyond academic achievement.

Prospective applicants should therefore pay close attention to the reference requirements and select referees who can provide meaningful, specific and credible information relevant to the respective areas being assessed.

Start Preparing Your References Early

Reference letters can become one of the most time-sensitive components of a competitive fellowship application.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final days before December 1 to approach their referees.

Instead, prospective applicants should:

Identify suitable academic referees early.

Identify an appropriate civic engagement referee.

Provide referees with sufficient information about the fellowship.

Share relevant application instructions with referees.

Explain the deadline clearly.

Follow up professionally before the deadline.

Confirm that all required reference documentation has been completed.

Strong references should ideally provide evidence rather than simply confirm that an applicant is hardworking or academically capable.

Application Timeline for 2026–2027

The fellowship application cycle follows several important dates.

August 1, 2026

The University of Hawai‘i launches its online graduate application system for admission the following year.

August 15, 2026

The East-West Center states that applications for the 2026–2027 competition open on August 15.

The fellowship webpage itself lists an opening date of August 16, 2026, so applicants should rely on the live official application portal for access and submission status.

December 1, 2026

This is the main application deadline.

The East-West Center states that applications for the 2026–2027 competition close on December 1.

Applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa must also apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester by this date.

January 10

Supporting documents for the University of Hawai‘i admissions office and relevant department applications should be completed by January 10 to ensure timely processing of the East-West Center application.

Step-by-Step Guide to Applying

Step 1: Confirm Your Geographic Eligibility

Before preparing the application, confirm that you are a citizen or permanent resident of one of the countries or territories listed by the East-West Center.

This should be the first screening step because applicants from countries outside the eligible geographic areas may not qualify.

Step 2: Check Your Academic Qualification

Confirm that you will have a four-year bachelor’s degree or equivalent before the fellowship begins.

The qualification should come from an accredited U.S. institution or a recognized higher education institution abroad.

Step 3: Review Your Academic Performance

Check your grades for the final four semesters or six quarters of undergraduate study as well as any post-baccalaureate coursework.

The general minimum requirement is a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale or equivalent.

Step 4: Identify an Appropriate Graduate Program

Research graduate programs at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa and identify a program that corresponds with your academic and professional objectives.

Applicants should also consider whether the field is relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center.

Step 5: Apply to the University of Hawai‘i

If you are not already a classified graduate student at UH Mānoa, submit the required graduate admission application by December 1.

Do not treat the fellowship application as a substitute for university admission.

Step 6: Complete the East-West Center Fellowship Application

Complete the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship application and provide the information and documentation requested.

Applicants should carefully check every section before submitting.

Step 7: Arrange Your References

Complete the academic and civic engagement reference requirements using the forms and instructions provided by the East-West Center.

Give referees sufficient time to complete their responsibilities.

Step 8: Complete Supporting Documentation

Ensure that the required supporting documents for both the University of Hawai‘i admissions process and departmental applications are completed by January 10.

Step 9: Review the FAQs

The East-West Center strongly encourages prospective applicants to review its Frequently Asked Questions before applying.

This is an important step because applicants can use the FAQs to clarify common issues before submitting their applications.

Step 10: Submit Before the Deadline

The final application deadline is December 1, 2026.

Applicants should avoid submitting at the last minute because technical problems, incomplete information or missing documents could create unnecessary complications.

APPLY HERE

Important Documents and Application Resources

Prospective applicants should consult the official East-West Center fellowship resources before beginning their application.

The key resources include:

East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship application page

University of Hawai‘i graduate admissions information

Academic Letter of Reference Form and instructions

Civic Engagement Letter of Reference Form and instructions

East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship FAQs

East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship Award Details

East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship Student Life information

Applicants who are unable to access the application materials can contact the East-West Center scholarship team at scholarships@eastwestcenter.org for assistance.

What Makes a Strong Applicant?

Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not necessarily mean that an applicant will be selected.

Because fellowships are awarded through an international competition, applicants should aim to present a strong overall profile.

A competitive application should clearly communicate:

Strong academic preparation.

A clear reason for pursuing the proposed graduate degree.

A coherent academic and professional trajectory.

Evidence of leadership or meaningful engagement where relevant.

Demonstrated civic engagement.

A clear understanding of the applicant’s intended field of study.

A strong connection between the proposed study and the broader objectives of the East-West Center.

Well-prepared references.

Complete and accurate application documentation.

Applicants should ensure that their application tells a consistent story rather than presenting disconnected achievements.

Pro Tip for Prospective Applicants

Do not wait until the December deadline to begin your application.

The application involves both the East-West Center and, for applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa, the University of Hawai‘i graduate admission process.

A strong preparation strategy is to begin with eligibility verification, identify your preferred graduate program, review the admission requirements, contact potential referees, prepare your supporting documents and then complete the fellowship application well ahead of the deadline.

Applicants should also review the official FAQs and award information before submitting the final application.

Key Deadlines to Remember

For the 2026–2027 East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship competition, applicants should keep the following dates in mind:

August 1, 2026: University of Hawai‘i graduate application system launches for the following year’s admission.

August 15, 2026: East-West Center states that the fellowship application period opens.

December 1, 2026: East-West Center fellowship application deadline.

December 1, 2026: Deadline for new applicants to apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester.

January 10: Supporting documents for the UH admissions office and departmental applications should be completed for timely EWC processing.

Visit HERE for more information about the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027.

Where to Get Help

Applicants who experience difficulties accessing the East-West Center application materials can contact the fellowship team by email.

Email: scholarships@eastwestcenter.org

Applicants should use the official East-West Center resources for the most current information because application requirements, university admission procedures and fellowship details can change from one application cycle to another.

Final Thoughts

The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027 presents an opportunity for eligible students from the United States and selected countries and territories across the Pacific, Southeast Asia, South Asia and East Asia to pursue graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa.

The fellowship is particularly relevant to applicants who have strong academic backgrounds and whose proposed graduate studies align with areas relevant to the East-West Center’s goals and objectives.

However, applicants should carefully distinguish between fellowship eligibility and university admission requirements. If you are not already a classified graduate student at UH Mānoa, you must also complete the appropriate University of Hawai‘i graduate admission process.

The most important date to remember is December 1, 2026, which is the stated deadline for the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship application and the deadline for new UH Mānoa applicants to apply for the following fall semester. Supporting documentation should then be completed by January 10 to facilitate timely processing.

Before applying, prospective candidates should verify their citizenship or permanent residency eligibility; confirm that they meet the bachelor’s degree and GPA requirements; identify an appropriate graduate program; prepare their academic and civic engagement references; review the FAQs; and submit all required materials well before the deadline.

For the official application and the latest requirements, applicants should use the East-West Center’s official fellowship application resources.

TITLE: Sutton Trust 2026 Programmes: Free Access Apprenticeships and Pathways to the Professions for UK Students

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Sutton Trust has opened applications for two major programmes designed to help young people from less advantaged backgrounds explore university, degree apprenticeships and professional careers.

The Access Apprenticeships and Pathways to the Professions programmes provide students with practical guidance, exposure to leading career sectors and opportunities to build confidence as they prepare for their next steps after school or college.

Unlike many career-development opportunities that require participants to cover participation costs, Sutton Trust programmes are completely free to attend. According to the organisation, costs including travel, accommodation, food and activities are covered by the Sutton Trust and its university and employer partners.

For students considering competitive professional careers or degree apprenticeships, these programmes can provide an opportunity to gain a better understanding of different career routes while receiving practical advice about future education and employment decisions.

About the Sutton Trust

The Sutton Trust is an organisation focused on improving social mobility and access to educational and career opportunities for young people from less advantaged backgrounds.

Through partnerships with universities, employers, schools and other organisations, the Sutton Trust runs programmes intended to help students make informed decisions about their futures and improve their access to leading universities and careers.

Its programmes cover areas including:

Higher education

Schools and colleges

Apprenticeships

Access to professional careers

Career exploration

Educational progression

Social mobility

The organisation states that its programmes are designed to give young people practical advice, inspiration and greater confidence about their future.

For 2026, two opportunities currently open for applications are Access Apprenticeships and Pathways to the Professions.

1. Sutton Trust Access Apprenticeships 2026

The Access Apprenticeships programme is designed for students who want to understand more about degree apprenticeships and the opportunities available through this alternative route into higher education and professional employment.

Degree apprenticeships combine elements of university-level study with workplace experience. This means that students can gain academic qualifications while developing practical experience in an employment environment.

For students who are uncertain about whether the traditional university route is the right option for them, learning about degree apprenticeships can help them understand the range of pathways available after completing school or college.

Applications Are Now Open

Applications for the 2026 Access Apprenticeships programme opened on:

1 September 2026

The stated closing period is:

November 2026

The information provided does not specify one exact closing day in November, so prospective applicants should check the official Sutton Trust programme page for the precise deadline applicable to the programme.

Where Is Access Apprenticeships Held?

The programme is offered in:

London

Manchester

Students selected for the programme therefore have the opportunity to participate in activities connected with these locations.

Who Can Apply for Access Apprenticeships?

The programme is intended for students at the following educational levels:

Year 12 in England

Year 12 in Wales

Year 13 in Northern Ireland

S5 in Scotland

The programme is particularly focused on young people from less advantaged backgrounds, consistent with the Sutton Trust’s broader social mobility mission.

Applicants should therefore carefully review the detailed eligibility requirements on the official programme page before applying, as the information provided here gives the core educational-year requirements but does not reproduce every possible eligibility criterion.

What Can Students Gain from Access Apprenticeships?

One of the central purposes of Access Apprenticeships is to help students understand how degree apprenticeships work and what they can offer.

Participants can gain greater awareness of:

Understanding Degree Apprenticeships

Students can learn how degree apprenticeships differ from conventional university programmes and how academic study can be combined with employment.

This can help participants understand the structure of apprenticeship-based higher education and whether this route aligns with their interests and career goals.

Exploring Career Opportunities

The programme can introduce students to career possibilities that may be available through degree apprenticeships.

Rather than simply focusing on academic qualifications, participants can gain insight into how education, employment and professional development can be connected.

Building Confidence

Choosing a career pathway can be challenging, particularly for students who may not have extensive access to professional networks or career guidance.

The Sutton Trust’s programmes are designed to provide practical advice and help students feel more confident about their future decisions.

Exposure to Employers and Professional Environments

Because Sutton Trust programmes are delivered in partnership with universities and employers, participants can gain exposure to organisations and professional environments that may otherwise be difficult to access.

Understanding Alternative Routes into Professional Careers

Degree apprenticeships can provide an alternative pathway into higher education and employment.

By learning about this option at an early stage, students can make more informed decisions when considering what to do after school or college.

2. Sutton Trust Pathways to the Professions 2026

The second opportunity currently open for applications is Pathways to the Professions.

This programme is designed to introduce students to a range of professional careers and provide practical information about what it takes to enter different sectors.

The programme covers several highly competitive professional fields, including:

Banking and Finance

Engineering

Law

Medicine

Veterinary Medicine

This makes the programme particularly relevant to students who already have an interest in one of these areas or who are still exploring which professional pathway they would like to pursue.

Applications Are Now Open

Applications opened on:

1 September 2026

The closing dates vary depending on the specific programme.

The Sutton Trust states that applications close at different points across:

October and November 2026

Students should therefore check the individual Pathways to the Professions programme they are interested in because the precise deadline may differ according to the career pathway and programme location.

Where Is Pathways to the Professions Available?

The programme is described as being available through:

National programmes

Regional programmes

Online programmes

In-person programmes

This gives students different ways of participating depending on the specific pathway and programme being offered.

The availability of online opportunities can also make it possible for students to participate without necessarily travelling to a central location, although students should check the format of the specific programme they wish to apply for.

Professional Fields Covered by Pathways to the Professions

Banking and Finance

Students interested in financial services can use the programme to learn more about careers in banking and finance.

The sector encompasses a wide range of roles, including financial analysis, investment, banking, accounting, economics, risk management and related professional areas.

Exposure to the sector at school level can help students understand the qualifications, skills and career pathways associated with financial services.

Engineering

Engineering is another professional area covered by the programme.

Students can explore the broad range of opportunities available within engineering and gain a better understanding of the relationship between science, mathematics, technology and professional practice.

The programme can be particularly useful for students who are considering technical or STEM-related careers but want greater insight into what professional engineering careers involve.

Law

For students considering a career in law, the programme provides an opportunity to learn more about the profession and the pathway towards becoming a legal professional.

Students can use such exposure to develop a better understanding of the legal profession and the academic and professional preparation it requires.

Medicine

Medicine is another major professional pathway covered by the Sutton Trust programme.

Students interested in becoming doctors can gain exposure to the profession and receive information that can help them understand the pathway towards a medical career.

This type of early career guidance can be particularly valuable because medicine typically involves a lengthy and highly structured educational and professional pathway.

Veterinary Medicine

Students interested in working with animals and pursuing veterinary careers can also explore veterinary medicine through the programme.

The opportunity can help students gain greater awareness of the profession and consider whether the field aligns with their academic interests and long-term career aspirations.

What Makes the Sutton Trust Programmes Different?

A major feature of both opportunities is their focus on access and social mobility.

The Sutton Trust works to support young people who may face greater barriers to accessing leading universities and professional careers.

The programmes are therefore not simply designed to provide career information. They are intended to connect students with practical guidance, institutions, employers and experiences that can help them better understand opportunities that may otherwise be unfamiliar.

The Programmes Are Completely Free

One of the most important benefits for applicants is that the Sutton Trust states that its programmes are free to attend.

The Trust and its partners cover costs including:

Travel

Accommodation

Food

Activities

This can reduce financial barriers that might otherwise prevent students from participating in educational and career-development programmes.

For students and families concerned about the cost of attending external programmes, this is an important feature to consider.

Universities and Employers Play an Important Role

The organisation works in partnership with universities and employers to provide students with practical information and experiences.

This partnership model can give participants exposure to both sides of the education-to-employment pathway.

Students can learn about:

What it is like to study at university.

What professional careers involve.

The qualifications required for particular professions.

Different routes into employment.

The skills employers value.

How to prepare for future education and career opportunities.

This combination of educational and professional exposure can help students develop a broader understanding of the choices available to them.

Key Benefits of the Sutton Trust 2026 Programmes

Students selected for these programmes can benefit from several forms of support and exposure.

1. Free Participation

The programmes do not charge students to attend, with the Sutton Trust and partners covering key participation costs.

2. Career Exploration

Participants can explore professional careers before making major decisions about university courses, apprenticeships and employment.

3. Practical Advice

The programmes focus on practical guidance rather than solely theoretical information.

4. University and Employer Exposure

Participants can gain insight into both higher education and professional environments.

5. Greater Career Awareness

Students can develop a clearer understanding of what different professional careers involve.

6. Confidence Building

The programmes are intended to leave students feeling more informed, inspired and confident about their future.

Access Apprenticeships provides students with an opportunity to explore degree apprenticeships as a route combining employment and higher education.

8. Access to Professional Pathways

Pathways to the Professions allows students to explore careers in areas such as finance, engineering, law, medicine and veterinary medicine.

9. National, Regional and Online Opportunities

10. Reduced Financial Barriers

Because programme-related costs are covered, students may be able to participate without the financial burden associated with many external educational opportunities.

Career decisions can have long-term consequences, yet students do not always have equal access to information about professional pathways.

TITLE: Invitation to Participate – Panel Discussion on Artificial Intelligence  & Africa’s Future

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Stakeholders of Africa’s higher education are invited to participate in a panel discussion focused on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Africa’s Future. A distinguished panelist, consisting of the following high-level personalities, will be engaging with the discussion topic and sharing their expertise: Dr. Conrad Tucker, Dr. Moses Asom, Dr. Faye Briggs, Dr. Omowunmi Sadik, and Dr. John Kamara. Further details are provided below:

Date: Sunday, March 2, 2025

Time: 5 PM Nigeria / 7 PM Kenya /10 AM Austin/ 11 AM New Jersey

Register to Participate via this link: https://www.tfinterviews.com/post/AI-Africa

Join Via Zoom: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/83778660235

Watch on YouTube: https://youtube.com/@tfinterviews/live

Professor Sadik Omowunmi will be joining the Panel Discussion on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Africa’s Future, holding on March 2, 2025. Professor Sadik Omowunmi “Wunmi” Sadik is a Distinguished Professor and Vice Provost for Academic Faculty Affairs at the New Jersey Institutes of Technology (NJIT). She is the Director of NJIT’s BioSMART Center. Sadik joined NJIT in 2019 after more than two decades at the State University of New York (SUNY) at Binghamton, where her exceptional research innovation and teaching performance saw her progress to full professorship and served as Director of the Center for Research in Advanced Sensing Technologies & Environmental Sustainability (CREATES). She received a PhD in Chemistry from the University of Wollongong, Australia, and did her postdoctoral research at the US Environmental Protection Agency. Sadik has held appointments at Harvard University, Cornell University, and the Naval Research Laboratory.

Sadik holds five US patents and has been recognized for research innovation in biosensors and sustainable nanotechnology. Her group focuses on the understanding of interfaces, in particular, electrochemical interfaces, and how to use this knowledge to pursue innovative bio (analytical) sensing technologies for improving human health and the environment. She has led her team in translating basic biosensor research into a portable, fully autonomous, and remotely operated sensing device known as an Ultra-Sensitive Portable Capillary Sensor, or U-PAC. Funded by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and the National Science Foundation, her group has developed sensors for the blue-green mold Penicillium italicum, among the most problematic post-harvest plant infections limiting the integrity of citrus and other crops. Sadik’s inventions have helped drive changes in many areas, including nanotechnology, pain management, and counter-terrorism.

Professor Sadik has published over 220 peer-reviewed publications and has given over 450 invited lectures and conference contributions worldwide. Her works have appeared in journals such as the Journal of the American Chemical Society, NanoLetters, ACS Sensors, Analytical Chemistry, ACS Catalysis, Chemical Communications, and Biosensors & Bioelectronics. Sadik has secured over $9 million in research grants and contracts from government agencies and private sector institutions such as the National Science Foundation, National Institutes of Health, Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Energy, Defense Threat Reduction Agency, Naval Research Laboratory, and by private and non-profit sectors such as Procter & Gamble and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

Sadik is a fellow of the American Chemical Society (ACS), The Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC), the American Institute of Medical and Biological Engineering (AIMBE), and the National Academy of Inventors. She receives the Jefferson Science Fellowship, the National Institute of Health Outstanding Scientific Achievement & WALS Lectureship, the SUNY’s Award for Outstanding Inventor, the Chancellor’s Award for Scholarship and Creative Activities, and NSF’s Discovery Corps Senior Fellowship. In 2024, she won the Wallace Coulter Lifetime Achievement Award at the Pittcon Conference of Analytical Chemistry and Applied Spectroscopy. Sadik was the fourth woman and the first female scientist to be honored with the Nigerian National Order of Merit Award and the first Nigerian American awarded the distinguished Harvard University Radcliffe Fellowship. As the Co-Founder and inaugural past president of the Sustainable Nanotechnology Organization (www.susnano.org), Sadik continues to build support for science while promoting the understanding of its broader relevance to society. She has channeled her experiences into inspiring and mentoring the next generation of scientists. At NJIT’s BioSMART Center, Sadik and her team are developing a portable biomarker sensor and artificial intelligence coupled with the patient’s self-assessment of perceived pain. This point-of-care technology will not require highly trained staff but will allow cheap and minimally intrusive measures of pain-related biomarkers.

TITLE: British High Commission Islamabad Education Advisor Job 2026: Apply for FCDO Grade 7 Role with PKR 924,324 Monthly Salary

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The British High Commission in Islamabad is accepting applications for the Education Advisor, Grade 7 (G7) position, offering an experienced education and development professional the opportunity to lead and influence the United Kingdom’s education engagement in Pakistan. Based in Islamabad, this senior-level position sits within the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and will involve education policy leadership, programme oversight, strategic partnerships, government engagement and management of a major education programme.

The successful candidate will play an important role in shaping the UK’s education strategy and influence in Pakistan. This includes working closely with provincial governments, development partners, civil society organisations, research institutions, private-sector stakeholders and multilateral organisations to advance education reform and strengthen education systems.

One of the most significant responsibilities attached to the position is serving as Senior Responsible Owner (SRO) for the FCDO’s flagship bilateral education programme, GOAL — Girls and Out of School Children: Action for Learning. The programme has a total value of up to £130 million, placing substantial responsibility on the successful candidate for programme performance, governance, safeguarding, risk, commercial oversight and value for money.

Applications must be submitted online by 31 August 2026 at 23:55 Pakistan Standard Time (PST). Candidates should carefully complete every required section of the online application because incomplete applications will not be considered.

About the Education Advisor Grade 7 Position in Islamabad

The Education Advisor will lead the UK’s education influence in Pakistan through a combination of technical leadership, policy engagement, programme management and strategic partnership building.

Working under the strategic direction of the Human Capital and Governance Group Lead, the Education Advisor will have considerable autonomy in managing day-to-day education policy engagement and programme delivery.

The successful candidate is expected to help shape an integrated UK education offer in Pakistan while ensuring that FCDO education programmes remain aligned with wider portfolio objectives, the Pakistan Country Business Plan and relevant UK priorities.

This is therefore much more than a traditional education advisory position. It combines high-level education policy expertise with programme leadership, diplomacy, stakeholder management, financial and commercial oversight, evidence-based decision-making and institutional relationship building.

Key Job Details

Candidates considering the British High Commission Education Advisor vacancy should note the following:

Position: Education Advisor

Grade: Grade 7 (G7)

Organisation: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

Job category: FCDO Programme Roles

Job subcategory: Education

Location: Islamabad, Pakistan

Region: South Asia & Afghanistan

Type of post: British High Commission

Employment type: Full-time, permanent

Working hours: 41 hours per week

Number of vacancies: One

Salary: PKR 924,324 per month

Salary currency: Pakistani Rupee

Proposed start date: 12 October 2026

Application deadline: 31 August 2026

Final application time: 23:55 PST

The advertised start date is tentative, and an appointment remains subject to the successful completion of required clearances, including police verification, references, medical checks, educational checks and professional checks.

What Is the Main Purpose of the Education Advisor Role?

The Education Advisor will be responsible for leading the UK’s education influence in Pakistan.

The position combines three major areas of responsibility:

Education policy leadership and strategy

Influencing and external engagement

Programme leadership and Senior Responsible Owner accountability

Through these areas, the successful candidate will help determine how the UK uses its policy influence, evidence and programme resources to contribute to education reform in Pakistan.

The Education Advisor will also lead high-level engagement with government institutions, development partners, civil society organisations, private-sector organisations and other stakeholders.

A key objective will be to build coalitions capable of supporting politically informed, systems-level education reform while maintaining the UK’s position as a credible and influential partner in Pakistan’s education sector.

Policy Leadership and Strategy – 30%

Approximately 30% of the position is dedicated to policy leadership and strategy.

The Education Advisor will help shape and deliver the FCDO’s education strategy in Pakistan and will take responsibility for technical analysis, policy advice and ongoing engagement with provincial education systems.

Key responsibilities include:

Shaping and delivering FCDO’s education strategy in Pakistan.

Providing technical analysis and policy advice.

Managing day-to-day engagement with provincial education systems.

Contributing to broader portfolio priorities and Pakistan’s Country Business Plan.

Identifying areas where the UK should invest its influence, evidence and programme resources.

Advising senior leaders on policy opportunities, risks and trade-offs.

Providing policy leadership on education reform and education financing.

Supporting work related to public financial management and domestic revenue mobilisation to strengthen education systems.

Preparing strategic analysis and high-quality briefings for senior leaders.

Providing evidence-based advice to Heads of Mission and Ministers.

Ensuring education programming reflects relevant evidence and aligns with Pakistan portfolio priorities.

Supporting technical engagement involving data, research and evidence to improve learning, accountability and policy impact.

The position therefore requires someone capable of translating research, technical expertise and evidence into practical policy advice and strategic decisions.

Influencing and External Engagement – 40%

The largest portion of the position, approximately 40%, is focused on influencing and external engagement.

The Education Advisor will need to develop trusted relationships with government and major education-sector stakeholders while representing UK education priorities.

Responsibilities in this area include:

Building and maintaining senior relationships with provincial governments.

Leading engagement around education policy, financing and reform.

Managing politically sensitive issues and escalating matters where necessary.

Establishing effective partnerships with development partners.

Working with multilateral institutions.

Engaging research organisations and institutions.

Developing relationships with private-sector organisations.

Collaborating with civil society organisations.

Representing the UK in high-level education policy discussions.

Participating in donor coordination mechanisms.

Representing the UK in relevant national and international education forums.

Leading strategic engagement with major multilateral institutions, particularly the World Bank.

Working with FCDO headquarters, technical cadres and other UK Government partners to maximise UK influence.

The successful candidate must consequently be comfortable operating in complex environments involving multiple organisations, competing priorities and significant political and institutional considerations.

Programme Leadership and GOAL Programme Responsibilities – 30%

Another 30% of the Education Advisor’s responsibilities will focus on programme leadership, particularly the FCDO’s GOAL programme — Girls and Out of School Children: Action for Learning.

The successful candidate will serve as the programme’s Senior Responsible Owner.

This is a substantial leadership responsibility because GOAL has a programme value of up to £130 million.

As Senior Responsible Owner, the Education Advisor will oversee:

Overall programme performance

Delivery of programme outcomes

Governance

Risk management

Safeguarding

Value for money

Commercial oversight

Compliance with FCDO requirements

Results reporting

Partner performance

Programme implementation

Monitoring and adaptation

Sustainable impact

The Education Advisor will also lead or chair programme governance arrangements and ensure that decisions are made effectively and that important strategic risks are escalated appropriately.

Day-to-day programme decisions will fall within the postholder’s delegated authority. These can include decisions relating to partner performance, adaptive programme delivery, use of evidence and value-for-money assessments.

Major changes involving programme scope, budget, strategic direction or risk exposure may require senior approval.

The Education Advisor will additionally contribute to the strategic design and development of future education investments and business cases.

Leadership and Interpersonal Expectations

The British High Commission is looking for someone who can demonstrate strong professional leadership alongside technical expertise.

The Education Advisor will be expected to demonstrate the UK Civil Service values of:

Honesty

Impartiality

Integrity

Objectivity

The successful candidate should be able to build effective and trusting relationships across teams and cultures while creating an inclusive and high-performing working environment.

The position also requires close collaboration across the British High Commission and the broader UK in Pakistan network.

This includes working with organisations and departments such as:

British Council

Department for Education

Department for Business and Trade

Other UK Government partners

Cultural sensitivity, collaboration, respect and commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion are important expectations of the position.

Resources and Programme Budget Managed

The Education Advisor is expected to line-manage at least one staff member, although the final staffing structure is subject to confirmation.

More significantly, the postholder will be the Senior Responsible Owner for GOAL and will hold delegated responsibility for a programme with a total budget of up to £130 million and an estimated annual expenditure of up to £6 million.

This responsibility includes oversight of:

Programme delivery

Risk

Commercial performance

Safeguarding

Value for money

Results

Candidates should therefore have significant experience managing complex programmes, commercial arrangements, partners, risks and substantial budgets.

Language Requirements

Expert-level proficiency in both English and Urdu is required.

Candidates must have excellent communication abilities in both languages, including particularly strong English drafting and speaking skills.

Given the senior stakeholder-facing nature of the position, the successful candidate must be capable of communicating complex education policy, programme and technical matters clearly and persuasively.

Travel Requirements

The successful Education Advisor will be expected to travel frequently within Pakistan.

Travel will particularly involve:

Punjab

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP)

Sindh, to a more limited extent

Candidates should therefore be prepared for regular provincial engagement rather than expecting the position to operate exclusively from Islamabad.

Essential Qualifications, Skills and Experience

Applicants must carefully review the essential criteria before applying.

1. At Least Five Years of Relevant Experience

Applicants need at least five years of experience working in Pakistan’s education and development sector.

They should have demonstrated experience influencing:

Government

Development partners

Experience working closely with provincial stakeholders is considered advantageous.

2. Programme and Project Management Leadership

Applicants should have programme or project management oversight and leadership experience.

They must be capable of managing multiple responsibilities while supporting agility within teams and work programmes.

3. Ability to Operate in Complex Environments

Candidates need demonstrated ability to work effectively in complicated operating environments requiring:

Strong stakeholder management

Influencing capabilities

Understanding of Pakistan’s political economy

Knowledge of incentive structures

4. Coalition-Building and Influencing Skills

The Education Advisor must be capable of building coalitions and influencing stakeholders to support:

Policy reform

Public investment

Sustainable systems change

This is particularly important because the position involves working across a complex ecosystem of government, donors, multilaterals, civil society and private-sector organisations.

5. Analytical and Problem-Solving Abilities

Applicants should demonstrate excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.

They must be capable of applying research and evidence to decision-making rather than relying solely on administrative or operational approaches.

6. Large-Scale Education Programme Experience

Experience working on large-scale education programmes is required.

Given the scale of GOAL and the responsibilities attached to serving as its Senior Responsible Owner, candidates need the experience necessary to oversee complex programme delivery.

7. Multilateral and Private-Sector Engagement

Experience engaging with and influencing multilateral organisations and the private sector is listed as a bonus. Examples of relevant multilateral organisations mentioned in the vacancy include:

World Bank

Global Partnership for Education (GPE)

Education Cannot Wait (ECW)

The essential criteria emphasise extensive experience within Pakistan’s education and development sector, government engagement, programme leadership, stakeholder management, coalition building and evidence-based decision-making.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience

In addition to the essential criteria, the FCDO identifies several areas of desirable experience.

These include:

Experience working on large-scale education programmes.

Experience engaging with and influencing multilateral organisations such as the World Bank, GPE and ECW.

Experience working with the private sector.

Experience connecting education with broader human-capital outcomes.

Relevant human-capital areas may include:

Gender

Economic growth

Demography

Candidates who combine strong education-sector expertise with broader human-capital experience may therefore be particularly well aligned with the strategic scope of the position.

Required Civil Service Behaviours

Applicants will be assessed against several important behaviours:

Communicating and Influencing

Leadership

Working Together

Candidates should prepare strong, specific examples demonstrating these behaviours from their professional experience.

Salary for the Education Advisor Position

The advertised basic salary for candidates other than existing BHC candidates is:

PKR 924,324 per month

The vacancy states that this salary is non-negotiable.

For existing British High Commission candidates, applicable Country Based Staff BHC Terms and Conditions will apply.

Benefits Offered by the British High Commission

In addition to the salary, the British High Commission provides an employment benefits package.

Medical Insurance

The Medical Insurance Scheme includes PKR 1,700,000 floater coverage per family.

The coverage applies to:

The employee

One spouse or long-term partner

Eligible children under 19

Eligible children under 23 when they are in full-time education and are not gainfully employed

Annual Domiciliary Cover

Employees can receive annual domiciliary coverage for day-to-day medical expenses of up to PKR 300,000 per family, based on the submission of actual bills.

Retirement Provision

Additional Employment Benefits

The vacancy also highlights:

Five-day working week

Annual leave

Public holidays

Maternity leave provisions

Special leave

Paid sick leave

Professional development opportunities

Travel opportunities

Performance management and appraisal system

Potential increments and staff bonuses

Organisational culture focused on respect and equality

Work-life balance

The FCDO also operates an agile workforce, meaning employees may occasionally be required to undertake other reasonable duties depending on organisational needs.

Important Information About Relocation

Applicants should carefully consider the location requirements before applying.

The FCDO states that no relocation assistance or related costs will be provided.

The organisation will not cover travelling, accommodation or relocation expenses associated with taking up the position. It will also not accept financial liability for cancellation or rescheduling costs.

Candidates applying from outside Islamabad should therefore consider their own ability to relocate or otherwise meet the location requirements before submitting an application.

Equality, Diversity and Inclusion

The British Government describes itself as an inclusive and diversity-friendly employer and welcomes applications from people of different backgrounds.

The vacancy states that the organisation does not discriminate on grounds including:

Disability

Race

Colour

Ethnicity

Gender identity

Religion

Sexual orientation

Age

Veteran status

Other legally protected categories

The British High Commission also states that it maintains zero tolerance for discrimination, bullying and harassment and is open to applications from candidates seeking flexible working arrangements where operational and security requirements permit.

How to Apply for the British High Commission Education Advisor Job

Applications must be submitted through the official British Government recruitment platform.

Importantly, applicants must complete the full online application form.

The recruitment process does not shortlist candidates simply on the basis of a CV or cover letter. The vacancy specifically warns that the application form must contain all required information.

Applicants need to:

Complete the online application form.

Provide complete employment information.

Provide complete educational information.

Complete the Experience and Professional Skills sections.

Complete the behaviour-based sections.

Complete any required motivational section.

Review the application carefully to ensure no mandatory information has been omitted.

Submit the complete application online before the deadline.

Applications that are incomplete in any respect will not be considered for shortlisting.

Important Guidance on Using AI in the Application

Candidates should pay particular attention to the FCDO’s guidance concerning artificial intelligence.

The vacancy requires applications to be authentically written based on the applicant’s own experiences.

While AI tools may be used for limited purposes such as formatting consistency and keyword relevance, the core application content, personal narratives and responses to behaviour- and skills-based questions must genuinely represent the applicant’s own professional experiences and achievements.

Originality and individual effort are important parts of the recruitment process, and plagiarism can lead to immediate disqualification.

Use the STAR Method When Preparing Your Application

Candidates are also encouraged to use the STAR method — Situation, Task, Action and Result when developing examples.

A strong STAR response generally explains:

Situation: The professional context or challenge you faced.

Task: What you personally needed to accomplish.

Action: The specific steps and decisions you took.

Result: The measurable or meaningful outcome produced by your actions.

Applicants should use genuine examples from their own careers to demonstrate the required behaviours and technical or professional capabilities.

Special Requirements for Internal Candidates

An internal candidate applying for the Education Advisor position must:

Not be subject to an active formal written warning.

Internal candidates who do not meet these conditions will not have their applications considered.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the Education Advisor, Grade G7 position at the British High Commission Islamabad is 31 August 2026.

Applications must be submitted no later than 23:55 Pakistan Standard Time (PST).

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to complete their applications because the vacancy requires several detailed sections covering employment, education, experience, professional skills and behaviours.

Selection, Security Checks and Reserve List

Candidates who are considered appointable but are ultimately unsuccessful may be placed on a reserve list for 12 months. If the same or a substantially similar position becomes available during that period, it may potentially be offered to another appointable candidate from the reserve list.

Appointment is also dependent upon successful completion of required clearances, including:

Police verification

References

Professional checks

British High Commission security requirements

The British Government warns that applications completed and submitted through other websites will not be received through its official recruitment system.

The Education Advisor position provides an opportunity for an experienced education and development professional to work at the intersection of policy, diplomacy, programme management and international development.

Unlike roles that focus exclusively on programme administration, this position gives the successful candidate significant responsibility for influencing education policy and investment decisions while developing relationships across government, international organisations, civil society and the private sector.

The scale of responsibility is also notable. Serving as Senior Responsible Owner for an education programme valued at up to £130 million means the successful candidate will have substantial responsibility for ensuring that public resources translate into effective, sustainable education outcomes.

The position is particularly suited to an experienced professional who understands Pakistan’s education sector, political economy and provincial systems and who can combine technical education expertise with high-level communication, influencing and programme leadership skills.

Conclusion

The British High Commission Islamabad Education Advisor Grade 7 vacancy represents a senior career opportunity for an experienced education and international development professional seeking to influence large-scale education reform in Pakistan.

With a salary of PKR 924,324 per month, a comprehensive employment benefits package and responsibility for influencing UK education policy and overseeing major education investments, the position carries both significant professional opportunities and substantial leadership responsibilities.

The successful candidate will need at least five years of relevant experience in Pakistan’s education and development sector, excellent stakeholder and programme management capabilities, experience with large-scale education programmes, strong analytical abilities and expert proficiency in English and Urdu.

Candidates should pay close attention to the application requirements. The FCDO will assess the information supplied through the complete online application rather than shortlisting applicants simply on the basis of a CV or cover letter. OPPORTUNITY TEXT:

Applications are open for the WFP Innovation Accelerator x Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator (AFCIA) 2027. Extreme weather events are placing growing pressure on food systems around the world. Droughts, floods, storms and rising temperatures are disrupting food production, threatening livelihoods and increasing food insecurity for vulnerable communities.

Latin America and the Caribbean is one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable regions. Increasingly frequent shocks and environmental degradation are putting additional strain on livelihoods and food systems, making it harder for communities to adapt and thrive. Yet across the region, innovators are developing new ways to build resilience and help communities adapt to the new realities.

To support these efforts, the World Food Programme (WFP), in partnership with the Adaptation Fund, launched the Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator (AFCIA). Through its third edition in Latin America and the Caribbean region, WFP implemented AFCIA aims to identify, support and scale innovative solutions from across the region, or those with strong potential for implementation there, that strengthen resilience, improve food security and help vulnerable communities adapt.

Eligibility

Your organization must be an established legal entity (for-profit, not-for-profit, social business, NGO, INGO).

Your organization should have a presence in one of the three countries of implementation (Dominican Republic, El Salvador and Peru). This could take the form of a country office or other permanent presence, subsidiary, long-term operations or partnerships in the country.

Your innovation addresses at least one of the above-mentioned priority areas related to pressing challenges faced in the climate adaptation space of the country of implementation.

Your innovation must be at least in the seed stage. Solutions that are still at the idea, research or early pre-seed stage are not eligible.

Your innovation should have a clear pathway to scale, adequate resources and a proposed plan to implement during the nine-month Sprint with the available funding.

Applicants are expected to have strong intentions to collaborate with relevant humanitarian stakeholders, build relationships with the country offices, and connect with the innovation ecosystems.

Evaluation Criteria

Following the requirements mentioned on the left, your application will be evaluated according to the following criteria:

Level of innovation/innovativeness: The solution is novel, innovative and has a strong climate adaptation regarding the mentioned themes.

Relevance to the context: The solution addresses at least one of the above-mentioned priority areas, is suitable for at least one of the three country contexts, and provides concrete solutions to end-users or the ecosystem.

Financial sustainability and scalability: The solution showcases a clear business model and a robust sustainable revenue model relative to its maturity stage.

Team expertise and capabilities: Proven competence, technical coherence, commitment, motivation, entrepreneurial mindset and a diverse and inclusive team.

Climate adaptation: The solution effectively enhances resilience to climate impacts, promotes sustainable practices, improves resource efficiency and facilitates adaptive measures to address climate-related challenges.

Level of Impact: Evidence of tangible historical and projected impact towards solving a defined challenge related to climate adaptation, demonstrating long-term, sustainable change beyond the grant period.

Environmental and social sustainability: The solution adheres to the environmental and social principles of the Adaptation Fund.

Gender and Inclusion: Solutions must address diverse user needs, enable inclusive participation and decision-making and use disaggregated data and feedback to inform design and impact.

Application
