TITLE: Maastricht University Social Justice Scholarship 2027–2028: Full Master’s Funding for Non-EU/EEA Students in Globalisation and Law

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications will open on 1 October 2026 for the Maastricht University Social Justice Scholarship 2027–2028, a highly competitive full scholarship for talented international students who want to pursue the full-time Master’s programme in Globalisation and Law at Maastricht University in the Netherlands.

The scholarship is particularly aimed at applicants who have already demonstrated a meaningful commitment to human rights and/or strengthening the rule of law through academic, extracurricular, professional or community initiatives.

Only one full scholarship is awarded each academic year, making this an exceptionally selective funding opportunity.

The scholarship provides substantial financial support for the entire 13-month programme, including:

Full tuition fees

€20,150 in living expenses for 13 months

Health and liability insurance

Visa application costs

Mandatory pre-academic training

Participation costs for the first block of the International Student Ambassador Programme

Arranged accommodation as part of the scholarship package

The scholarship is available to applicants from outside the European Union and European Economic Area, subject to additional nationality, residence, academic and visa requirements. Maastricht University describes the programme as supporting its commitments to diversity, inclusivity and strengthening the rule of law, including through its wider human rights and peace initiatives.

There are two particularly important deadlines:

Master’s programme application deadline: 10 December 2026

Scholarship application deadline: 1 February 2027

Applicants should understand that they must first apply to the Globalisation and Law Master’s programme before completing the separate Social Justice Scholarship application.

About the Maastricht University Social Justice Scholarship

The UM Social Justice Scholarship is an international funding programme created by Maastricht University to support academically excellent students who have demonstrated a record of contributing to:

Human rights

Rule of law

Social justice

Related initiatives and projects

The scholarship reflects Maastricht University’s broader emphasis on diversity, inclusion and global engagement.

The University explicitly connects the scholarship to its Global Engagement Policy and to its commitment to strengthening the rule of law.

Unlike a general international scholarship available across all Maastricht University programmes, this scholarship is tied to one specific Master’s degree:

Globalisation and Law

Applicants seeking admission to another Maastricht University Master’s programme cannot use that programme to qualify for this particular scholarship.

Number of Scholarships Available

Maastricht University awards:

One full Social Justice Scholarship per academic year.

This means competition is likely to be extremely strong.

Academic excellence alone is therefore unlikely to be sufficient.

Applicants must also demonstrate a convincing combination of:

Strong academic results

Clear motivation

Previous human rights and/or rule-of-law engagement

Financial need

Strong recommendation

Programme fit

Potential for future impact

The scholarship is designed for highly talented students from outside the EU/EEA who have already made demonstrable contributions to human rights or the rule of law.

Eligible Master’s Programme

The scholarship is available only for the:

Full-time Master’s programme Globalisation and Law

at Maastricht University.

Applicants must apply for the:

2027–2028 academic year.

Applications to other Law Faculty programmes do not qualify for the UM Social Justice Scholarship.

This restriction is explicitly stated in the application procedure.

Why Globalisation and Law?

The programme is particularly relevant for students interested in legal questions shaped by international and transnational developments.

The scholarship’s own selection criteria emphasize applicants with previous involvement in:

Human rights

Rule of law

Social justice-related activities

As a result, it may be especially attractive to applicants whose academic or professional interests concern:

International law

Human rights law

Global governance

Rule of law

Legal institutions

International justice

Legal responses to globalization

Rights protection

Applicants should still review the actual Globalisation and Law curriculum before applying and ensure that their interests align with the programme itself.

Scholarship Duration

The UM Social Justice Scholarship covers:

13 months

for the one-year Globalisation and Law Master’s programme.

This extended funding period is important because the scholarship is designed to support students not only with tuition but also with living expenses throughout their stay.

Scholarship Financial Benefits

The Social Justice Scholarship is a substantial full funding package.

For the 2027–2028 cycle, the published support includes several components.

Living Expenses: €20,150

Scholarship recipients receive:

€20,150 for 13 months

in living expenses.

This is equivalent to:

€1,550 per month.

The living allowance is paid to the student by the Maastricht University International Services Desk.

The published amount is subject to change for the 2027–2028 academic year.

Monthly Living Expense Breakdown

Maastricht University provides a detailed estimate showing how the monthly €1,550 living allowance is intended to cover expenses.

The indicative monthly breakdown is:

Housing: €960

Groceries and personal hygiene: €160

Telephone: €60

Travel: €100

Books and study materials: €90

Clothing, hobbies and going out: €125

Miscellaneous: €55

These amounts are estimates and may change.

Applicants should therefore understand that the €20,150 living allowance is designed to cover normal student living costs rather than being an additional discretionary cash award on top of accommodation and everyday expenses.

Tuition Fees

The scholarship covers:

Tuition fees at cost.

The Maastricht University International Services Desk arranges and pays the tuition component.

For scholarship recipients, this effectively provides full tuition funding for the eligible programme.

Health and Liability Insurance

The scholarship includes:

€700 for health and liability insurance

based on the current published amount.

The International Services Desk arranges and pays for the insurance.

The amount may change for 2027–2028.

Visa Application Costs

The scholarship also covers:

Visa application costs at cost.

These are arranged and paid by the University’s International Services Desk.

This is particularly important because the scholarship is specifically intended for many students who will need Dutch immigration authorization.

Applicants must nevertheless meet all eligibility conditions for obtaining the appropriate entry visa and residence permit.

Pre-Academic Training Costs

The scholarship covers the cost of Maastricht University’s:

Pre-Academic Training programme

at cost.

This training is not optional for scholarship recipients.

It is a:

Mandatory two-week component

and is scheduled to begin in the:

First week of August 2027.

Successful applicants should therefore plan to arrive in time to participate.

International Student Ambassador Programme

The scholarship also covers the cost of the:

International Student Ambassador Programme, or ISAP

for the:

First block only.

Applicants should consult Maastricht University for the current structure of this programme and any later participation costs that may fall outside the scholarship.

Accommodation Is Mandatory

A particularly important condition of the Social Justice Scholarship is its accommodation arrangement.

Scholarship recipients are allocated a room until:

July 2028

and accepting the scholarship means accepting this accommodation.

The University explicitly states that:

Refusing the allocated room results in cancellation of the scholarship.

This is therefore not an optional housing service.

It is a mandatory part of the scholarship package.

Accommodation and Families

The accommodation allocated to scholarship students is:

Not suitable for partners, spouses and/or children.

Applicants planning to move to the Netherlands with family members should consider this condition carefully.

Maastricht University does state that accommodation preferences connected to considerations such as religious beliefs will be taken into account where possible.

Is Airfare Included?

No.

The scholarship explicitly states that:

Air tickets are not included.

Students are responsible for paying for their own flight or other travel to the Netherlands.

This is an important distinction when describing the scholarship as “fully funded.”

It comprehensively covers tuition, living support, accommodation allocation, insurance, visa costs and training, but it does not cover airfare.

Cleaning Fee

The scholarship also does not cover the accommodation cleaning fee.

The current estimate is approximately:

€75

and must be paid directly to Maastricht Housing by the student.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must satisfy all published eligibility conditions.

This includes requirements concerning:

Nationality

Residence status

Academic programme

Human rights/rule-of-law involvement

Academic performance

Age

Visa eligibility

Previous Master’s education

Nationality Requirement

Applicants must hold nationality in a country:

Outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and Surinam.

They must also meet the requirements for obtaining the appropriate Dutch:

Entry visa

Residence permit

This means the scholarship is specifically aimed at international students from outside those listed jurisdictions.

Dual Nationality Restriction

Applicants are not eligible if they have dual nationality from:

An EU/EEA country, or

Switzerland

A candidate holding both a non-EU nationality and an EU nationality would therefore not satisfy this condition.

Existing Schengen Residence Permit

Applicants who already hold a residence permit for another Schengen country may still potentially apply, but special conditions apply.

The permit must remain valid until at least:

2 September 2027

If it expires before that date, applicants can only apply for the scholarship through the applicable MVV visa procedure from their home country.

Applicants with complicated immigration status should review Maastricht University’s Visa Office guidance before applying.

Programme Admission Requirement

Applicants must have applied for:

Full-time Globalisation and Law

at Maastricht University for:

2027–2028

and must submit the complete programme application, meeting all admission requirements, before:

10 December 2026.

This deadline is earlier than the scholarship deadline.

Applicants cannot wait until February to start their Master’s application.

Human Rights or Rule-of-Law Contribution

One of the defining requirements is that applicants must have already made a:

Proven contribution to supporting the rule of law and/or human rights

through:

Intracurricular initiatives

Extracurricular initiatives

Projects

This means simply stating an interest in human rights is unlikely to satisfy the requirement.

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate actual involvement.

What Could Count as Human Rights or Rule-of-Law Experience?

The official source does not provide an exhaustive list, but applicants should use their application to document relevant activities clearly.

Potential evidence could include, where genuinely applicable:

Human rights advocacy

Legal aid

Student human rights initiatives

Rule-of-law programmes

NGO work

Community projects

Research

Relevant internships

Policy initiatives

Legal awareness programmes

The strongest applications will describe both:

What the applicant did

What contribution or impact resulted

rather than listing organization names without context.

GPA Requirement

Applicants must demonstrate excellent academic results.

The minimum required GPA is:

7.5 out of 10

or equivalent.

The application guidance further explains that this corresponds to approximately:

75% out of 100%, or

3.0 out of 4.0

depending on the grading system.

Applicants must provide both:

An official transcript or university document showing their GPA.

A document explaining their institution’s grading system.

GPA Must Be Cumulative

The scholarship application instructions state that Maastricht University only accepts candidates with a:

Cumulative GPA of at least 75% of the maximum scale in the Bachelor’s degree.

Applicants should therefore not rely only on a particularly strong final semester if their cumulative result does not meet the threshold.

Age Limit

Applicants must be:

35 years old or younger on 1 September 2027.

Candidates older than 35 on that date are not eligible under the published rules.

Previous Master’s Degree

Applicants who already hold a Master’s degree are not automatically excluded.

However:

Preference will be given to candidates who have not yet obtained a Master’s degree.

This distinction matters.

An applicant with a previous Master’s may still apply if all other conditions are met, but they may be at a disadvantage compared with an otherwise similarly strong candidate seeking their first Master’s.

Only One Scholarship Application

Candidates may:

Apply once and for one scholarship only.

After submission, Maastricht University will not add or replace documents.

Applicants should therefore check every document carefully before submitting the final scholarship application.

Important Application Dates

Applications for the Social Justice Scholarship open on:

1 October 2026.

The major deadlines are:

Globalisation and Law programme application

10 December 2026

UM Social Justice Scholarship application

1 February 2027

By the scholarship deadline, candidates must have completed the relevant registration requirements except for:

Legal residence

Tuition payment

Hard copy of the diploma

Application Process

The Social Justice Scholarship application involves two main stages.

Step 1: Apply for Globalisation and Law

Applicants must first apply to the:

Globalisation and Law Master’s programme

through:

Studielink

After submitting the programme application, the applicant will receive a Maastricht University student ID number.

This student number is required for the scholarship application.

Programme Application Deadline

For scholarship eligibility, the complete Globalisation and Law application must be submitted by:

10 December 2026.

This includes fulfilling the admission requirements.

Applicants should not confuse this with any later general programme deadline that may apply to candidates who are not seeking the Social Justice Scholarship.

APPLY HERE

Handling Fees

If the programme requires an admissions handling fee:

The scholarship does not cover it.

The applicant is personally responsible for paying any applicable fee by:

10 December 2026.

Step 2: Complete the Scholarship Application Form

After obtaining a Maastricht University account and student number, applicants complete the scholarship application through the official online form.

The University accepts scholarship applications only through this form.

Supporting documents may be uploaded in:

DOC

DOCX

PDF

Please fill out the application form here.

Required Scholarship Documents

Candidates must prepare several important documents.

1. Curriculum Vitae

The CV must:

Be current

Include relevant educational information

Include relevant employment experience

Mention awards and prizes where applicable

Be no longer than two A4 pages

Because the scholarship is highly competitive, applicants should prioritize evidence relevant to:

Academic excellence

Human rights

Rule of law

Leadership

Community involvement

Professional development

2. Motivation Letter

Applicants must use the:

Official Maastricht University scholarship motivation letter template.

The template focuses specifically on motivation for the scholarship.

Applicants are instructed to emphasize:

What they have already done to improve human rights.

This is especially important.

The scholarship is not intended solely for applicants who want to work in human rights in the future.

It seeks people with a proven record of engagement already.

How to Strengthen the Motivation Letter

A competitive motivation letter should explain:

Why Globalisation and Law fits the applicant’s goals

What human rights/rule-of-law work the applicant has already undertaken

What role the applicant personally played

What impact resulted

Why the scholarship is necessary

How Maastricht University will help the applicant extend that work

Applicants should avoid making the letter entirely aspirational.

Evidence of past contribution is a formal eligibility factor.

3. Proof of Academic Excellence

Candidates must upload:

Transcript or official university documentation showing a GPA of at least 7.5/10 or equivalent.

Documentation explaining the grading scale.

This requirement is particularly important for applicants whose universities use grading systems that differ substantially from the Dutch system.

4. Personal Statement of Financial Need

Applicants must submit a:

Personal statement of financial needs.

The University asks candidates to explain why receiving the scholarship would benefit them.

Examples of relevant personal circumstances explicitly mentioned include:

Financial difficulty

Sole-parent responsibilities

Caretaking responsibilities

Medical conditions

Disability

Refugee status

The statement should be factual and personal rather than generic.

5. Reference Letter

Applicants must submit:

One reference letter.

The University provides specific scholarship reference-letter guidelines that should be sent to the referee.

Eligible referees include:

Current or former professors

Lecturers

Employers

Family members cannot act as referees.

Reference Letter Date Requirement

Recommendation letters must be:

Dated no earlier than February 2026.

Letters failing to follow the official guidelines will not be considered, which can cause an application to be treated as incomplete.

Applicants Upload the Reference Letter Themselves

Unlike some scholarship systems where referees upload recommendations directly, the UM Social Justice Scholarship requires:

The applicant to upload the reference letter.

The referee cannot submit it directly through the scholarship application.

Applicants should therefore request their reference well before the deadline.

6. Referee Contact Details

Applicants must also provide one referee’s contact information.

This includes:

Relationship to the applicant

Work telephone number with country code

Work or institutional email address

A recommendation linked only to a:

Personal email address

will be rejected.

The University may contact the referee to verify the authenticity of the recommendation.

Selection Process

Because only one scholarship is available, selection involves several stages.

Stage 1: Completeness Check

After:

1 February 2027

the UM International Services Desk checks whether applications are complete.

Incomplete applications do not progress.

Stage 2: Faculty Review

Complete applications are sent to the:

UM Law Faculty

in:

February 2027.

Faculty reviewers assess eligible candidates.

Stage 3: Top Three Candidates

The Law Faculty selects and ranks its:

Top three scholarship applicants

and sends their files to the International Services Desk for a final check in:

March 2027.

This means only a very small final group moves forward to the interview stage.

Stage 4: Online Interview

By the end of March, Maastricht University confirms the Faculty selections and invites selected candidates to:

An online interview.

Candidates invited to interview must prepare an:

Action plan

explaining how studying at Maastricht University will enable them to contribute to strengthening:

Human rights

Rule of law

in their home country and/or elsewhere.

This makes future impact an explicit part of final selection.

Preparing the Action Plan

Applicants who reach the interview should be prepared to explain:

The human rights or rule-of-law problem they want to address

What skills or knowledge they currently lack

How Globalisation and Law will help fill that gap

What they plan to do after graduation

Which institutions, communities or systems they want to influence

How they will translate the Master’s degree into practical impact

A generic career plan will likely be less persuasive than a specific and realistic pathway.

Final Results

Following interviews, applicants will be informed of their status in:

April 2027

with final statuses communicated by:

The beginning of May 2027 at the latest.

Possible outcomes include:

Selected

Waitlisted

Rejected

Waitlisted candidates will receive a final selected/rejected result during May 2027.

Africa in the field of logistics and transport within the faculty of
engineering. He predicted that in future people would come to Djibouti to learn
about transport and logistics or to do cutting edge research in the areas of transport
and logistics.

Remarks by the Minister of Higher
Education and Research, Djibouti

H.E. Dr Nabil Mohamed Ahmed welcomed the participants to “Djibouti
the land of encounters, the land of peace and the land of engagements”.
He expressed his joy that this event had materialized as per his vision. He
paid tribute to the World Bank and AAU for supporting the Government of
Djibouti to hold the ACE meetings in Djibouti City. He also congratulated the
University of Djibouti Vice Chancellor for successfully spearheading the
associated planning and logistics. He emphasized that it was the responsibility
of Africans to work hard and ensure that educational institutions were
effective and that the certificates given were recognized internationally. He
said that Africa needed to catch up in the area of applied new technologies.
Djibouti needs to optimize the transport chain by harnessing technology.
Djibouti must exploit its competitive advantage as a transport hub. There is
also an urgent need to increase the number of Djiboutian women Professors

The Message from the Honourable
President of the Republic of Djibouti

His Excellency Mr Ismail Omar Guelleh the President of the Republic of
Djibouti congratulated the organizers and the participants for the holding of
the conference and the launch of the ACE IMPACT Project. He thanked the
partners for positioning Higher Education to support the socio-economic
development of African countries. He voiced his delight that Djibouti was now a
member of the restricted club of ACE universities. He reminded the audience
that he was a firm believer in providing African solutions to African problems.
Therefore, he was thrilled that the ACE Djibouti would focus on logistics and
transport. The President said that the transport sector was the “lungs of Djibouti”. Djibouti was ready
to exploit its strategic location. There was a need to digitize the transport
and transit procedures for the Djibouti transport sector. He underscored that scientific
and technical development was therefore key. He ended his remarks by stating
that he believed in the capacities of African countries, the youth and African researchers.
He officially declared the conference opened.

TITLE: Liberté, I write your name, 4th fundraising campaign of IHES

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
A manifesto for the freedom of research

Written in 1942, Liberté by Paul Éluard is a universal poem born from resistance to oppression. In a world where scientific thought is often expected to move quickly, IHES has made it the signature of its campaign — a poetic gesture paying tribute to the beauty of the mathematical world and to that essential and fragile freedom without which research can neither be written nor illuminate the future.

In parallel, “Liberté, I write your name” invites everyone — in Europe, the United States, Asia, and beyond — to join this initiative for science and freedom.

“Guaranteeing freedom of research and allowing the circulation of knowledge are essential pillars of any democratic society. IHES has defended these principles since its creation and now fully aligns with the Stand Up for Science movement, in solidarity with all scientists whose work and independence are under threat today.”

Emmanuel Ullmo, Director of IHES

TITLE: Erasmus Mundus Scholarship 2027–2029: Up to €33,600 Plus Full Tuition for a Joint Master’s in Public Policy

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications for the 2027–2029 Erasmus Mundus Master’s Program in Public Policy (Mundus MAPP) are expected to open on 1 September 2026, offering students from around the world the opportunity to complete an interdisciplinary, international Master of Arts in Public Policy across leading European universities.

Mundus MAPP is a two-year, full-time, in-person Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programme designed to prepare future leaders for careers in public policy, government, international organizations, development institutions, civil society, academia, and the private sector.

The programme is delivered by a consortium of four European institutions:

Central European University Private University (CEU PU)

International Institute of Social Studies of Erasmus University Rotterdam (ISS)

Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals (IBEI)

University of York

Students choose one of four mobility tracks covering Global Public Policy, European Public Policy, Political Economy and Development, or Governance and Development.

For outstanding applicants, the programme offers the prestigious Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) Scholarship. The scholarship is calculated at €1,400 per month for 24 months, providing a maximum scholarship value of €33,600, together with a full tuition-fee waiver. The monthly contribution is intended to assist students with living, travel, visa, installation, and related costs.

The scholarship application is integrated into the main Mundus MAPP admission application; there is no separate scholarship application.

For the 2027–2029 intake, candidates who want to be considered for financial aid must submit their applications by:

1 December 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time (CET).

The programme is open to applicants from both within and outside the European Union, subject to academic, mobility, English-language, and other admissions requirements.

About the Mundus MAPP Erasmus Mundus Master’s Program

Mundus MAPP is the Erasmus Mundus Master’s Program in Public Policy, a joint postgraduate programme supported by the Erasmus+ action of the European Union.

Its overall purpose is to provide both scholarly education and practical preparation for people who may become future policy leaders in:

Government

International organizations

Public administration

International development

Nonprofit organizations

Civil society

Think tanks

Research institutions

Academia

Private-sector organizations working on policy and governance

The programme aims to give students a detailed and systematic understanding of how:

Political institutions operate

Public policies are developed

Political processes interact with policy

International and transnational governance functions

Economic and political forces influence policymaking

European governance interacts with national and global processes

Mundus MAPP combines theoretical policy studies with practical exposure to real-world policymaking.

What Makes Mundus MAPP Different?

One of the defining characteristics of Mundus MAPP is its international mobility structure.

Instead of completing the entire degree at a single university, students study in two different countries and at two consortium institutions according to their chosen mobility track.

The programme is built around the belief that effective policy professionals need both:

The ability to understand and situate complex policy problems

The ability to develop and assess practical policy solutions

Students therefore combine academic learning with practical experiences such as:

Internships

Study trips

Case studies

Research projects

Interaction with policymakers and practitioners

Cross-cultural academic collaboration

Approximately 60% of the curriculum is common across the programme, while around 40% consists of track-specific coursework.

This structure gives all Mundus MAPP students a common foundation in policy studies while still allowing significant specialization.

Four Mundus MAPP Mobility Tracks

Applicants may apply to only one of the four available mobility tracks.

Each track combines two consortium institutions and leads to a different specialization.

1. CEU PU–IBEI Track: Global Public Policy

The CEU PU–IBEI track specializes in:

Global Public Policy

This pathway is particularly relevant to students interested in public-policy challenges extending across national borders.

Potential areas of interest may include:

Global governance

International organizations

Transnational policymaking

Global political economy

International development

International institutions

Cross-border policy challenges

Students study through Central European University and IBEI.

2. CEU PU–York Track: European Public Policy

The CEU PU–University of York track focuses on:

European Public Policy

It is particularly relevant for students interested in:

European governance

European institutions

Policy coordination

Multi-level governance

Public administration

European political processes

Students combine study at CEU with the University of York.

3. ISS–IBEI Track: Political Economy and Development

The ISS–IBEI track specializes in:

Political Economy and Development

This pathway may be especially attractive to students interested in relationships between:

Economic systems

Development

Inequality

Institutions

International political economy

Public policy

Social transformation

Students study through ISS and IBEI.

4. ISS–York Track: Governance and Development

The ISS–York track specializes in:

Governance and Development

The track provides a strong route for applicants interested in:

Governance

International development

Public institutions

State capacity

Development policy

Political and institutional change

Students combine study at ISS with the University of York.

Compulsory International Mobility

Physical mobility is a mandatory component of Mundus MAPP.

Every enrolled student must complete:

Two study periods in two different countries

with each study period comprising at least:

30 ECTS credits

Importantly, both countries must be different from the student’s country of residence at the time of application or enrollment.

For example, someone applying to the ISS–IBEI track must normally be resident outside:

The Netherlands

Spain

at the relevant application/enrollment stage.

Applicants must provide evidence of residence before enrollment.

Possible evidence can include:

Municipal residence certificate

Rental contract

Utility bills

The compulsory mobility requirement cannot be replaced with virtual study.

Degree Awarded

Students who successfully complete Mundus MAPP receive a:

Master of Arts in Public Policy

The degree is jointly awarded by the two consortium institutions attended by the student.

Graduates also receive a diploma supplement.

The MA qualification is recognized by the appropriate bodies in:

Austria

Netherlands

Spain

United Kingdom

Students studying on CEU tracks also receive a programme that fulfills the requirements for CEU’s Master of Arts degree in Public Policy registered with the New York State Education Department in the United States.

This gives the programme both European and, for CEU tracks, additional U.S.-accredited degree recognition.

Who Can Apply?

Mundus MAPP is open to:

European and third-country nationals.

In other words, eligibility is not limited to EU citizens.

Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas, the Middle East, Oceania, and other regions may apply if they meet the academic, mobility, and language requirements.

Academic Qualifications

Applicants must hold a Bachelor’s degree representing at least:

Three years of university-level study

from a recognized university or higher-education institution.

Candidates need to have achieved at least:

Upper Second Class / 2.1, where applicable

and:

GPA of at least 3.17 out of 4.0 or equivalent.

Applicants must provide their GPA on a 4.0 scale.

If their university transcript uses another grading system, candidates may use conversion tools such as:

Scholaro GPA Calculator

WES iGPA Calculator

to determine an approximate 4.0-scale GPA.

Preferred Academic Background

Applicants with degrees in:

Social sciences or equivalent disciplines

are normally given preference.

This could potentially include areas such as:

Political science

International relations

Public policy

Economics

Sociology

Development studies

Social sciences

Governance studies

Related fields

However, applicants should judge their eligibility based on the formal programme requirements rather than assuming every degree in a broadly related area will automatically qualify.

Natural Sciences and Engineering Applicants

The admissions requirements explicitly state that candidates holding only a Bachelor’s degree in:

Natural Sciences

Engineering

are not eligible to apply.

Prospective candidates from multidisciplinary backgrounds should therefore review the programme’s academic eligibility rules carefully.

Applicants Who Already Hold a Master’s Degree

Having a previous master’s degree does not automatically make an applicant ineligible for Mundus MAPP.

However, candidates who already hold a master’s degree must also have obtained at least:

Upper Second / 2.1 where applicable, and

GPA of at least 3.17/4.0 or equivalent

during the master’s programme.

There is also an important scholarship consideration:

Priority for Erasmus Mundus scholarships is given to candidates who have not previously had the opportunity to study in a master’s degree programme.

This does not mean existing master’s degree holders cannot apply for Mundus MAPP. It means they may be at a disadvantage in the competition for limited scholarships.

Special Requirement for IBEI Tracks

Applicants selecting either:

CEU–IBEI, or

ISS–IBEI

must meet the requirements associated with Spanish higher-education regulations.

Their undergraduate degree must have been obtained from a fully accredited higher-education institution and must qualify the applicant for admission to master’s-level studies in the country where the undergraduate diploma was issued.

Motivation for Public Policy

Applicants are expected to demonstrate:

High motivation and interest in European and international public policy.

This is assessed through the:

Statement of purpose

The motivation statement is therefore a central component of the admission process.

A strong statement should explain more than simply why the applicant wants a master’s degree.

It should demonstrate:

Why public policy matters to the applicant

Which policy challenges interest them

Why Mundus MAPP is the right programme

Why the selected mobility track fits their objectives

What professional or academic trajectory they hope to pursue

How their previous education or experience prepares them for the programme

Mundus MAPP and the Use of AI in Applications

The programme acknowledges that applicants increasingly use artificial intelligence tools when preparing written materials.

However, Mundus MAPP explicitly emphasizes that it values:

Authentic and personal motivation statements.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their statement genuinely reflects their:

Experiences

Motivations

Intellectual interests

Career objectives

Personal reasons for choosing the programme

A generic or heavily automated statement may fail to communicate the individual qualities that admissions reviewers are looking for.

English Language Requirements

Mundus MAPP is taught in English.

Applicants who do not qualify for a language-test exemption must submit an accepted English-language test score with the application.

Late submission of English scores is not permitted.

Accepted tests and minimum scores include:

TOEFL iBT

95 or above

The test must have been taken within two years of the application deadline.

IELTS Academic

7.0 or above

The test must have been taken within two years of the application deadline.

Cambridge C2 Proficiency

C2 or above

The test must have been taken within five years of the deadline.

Cambridge C1 Advanced

C1 or above

The test must have been taken within five years of the deadline.

Pearson PTE Academic

76 or above

The test must have been taken within two years.

Duolingo English Test

130 or above

The test must have been taken within two years.

English-Language Test Exemptions

Applicants who are citizens of certain countries may be exempt if they completed a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree taught exclusively in English.

The listed countries include:

Australia

Botswana

Canada

Gambia

Ghana

Ireland

Jamaica

Kenya

Liberia

Malawi

Namibia

New Zealand

Nigeria

Philippines

Rwanda, English-speaking region

South Africa

Tanzania

Trinidad and Tobago

Uganda

United Kingdom

United States

Zambia

Applicants must still satisfy the degree-language conditions specified by the programme.

English Waiver for Other Applicants

Citizens of other countries may request an English-language waiver if they completed a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree taught exclusively in English in:

Australia

Canada

New Zealand

United States

European Union

United Kingdom

Iceland

Liechtenstein

Norway

Switzerland

or at eligible satellite campuses of U.S. or UK universities.

Candidates must provide supporting documentation confirming that the language of instruction was English.

Additional Requirements for ISS Tracks

Candidates applying for:

ISS–IBEI

ISS–York

who will require a student visa for the Netherlands may face additional English-language requirements connected with Dutch immigration procedures.

Applicants should therefore review the programme’s current visa-related language guidance before applying.

Is Work Experience Required?

No.

Professional experience is not a formal eligibility requirement.

Applicants can therefore apply directly from undergraduate study if they otherwise meet the admissions criteria.

However, the programme states that:

Candidates with relevant work experience receive preference.

Relevant experience could potentially include work or internships in areas such as:

Public policy

Government

International organizations

NGOs

Development

Research

Advocacy

Public administration

Think tanks

Policy consulting

Spanish Language Requirement

Spanish proficiency is:

Not required

for any Mundus MAPP track.

However, students studying through IBEI may have opportunities to take selected elective courses taught in Spanish during their second year.

Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarship

One of the most attractive features of Mundus MAPP is the availability of Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships for outstanding candidates.

The scholarships are open to top-ranked applicants from:

EU countries

Non-EU countries

A limited number are available and are awarded based on academic merit.

Erasmus Mundus Scholarship Value

The EMJM scholarship is calculated using a monthly unit cost of:

€1,400 per month

for:

24 months

This gives a maximum total scholarship value of:

€33,600

Scholarship recipients also receive:

A full tuition-fee waiver.

The €1,400 monthly contribution is intended to help students meet expenses including:

Subsistence

Installation

Travel

Visa-related costs

Other living and participation expenses

However, applicants should understand that this is a monthly scholarship payment rather than a promise that every individual expense will be separately reimbursed.

Costs Not Separately Covered by the EMJM Scholarship

The financial-aid information identifies several costs that students must meet themselves rather than expecting additional dedicated reimbursement.

These include:

Study Visit during Year 1, estimated at approximately €600–€1,000

Winter School during Year 2, estimated at approximately €600–€1,000

Travel and visa costs between the student’s home country and consortium countries

Travel connected with moving to the Year 2 university

The monthly €1,400 contribution can help students manage overall living and mobility costs, but applicants should budget carefully for these specific expenses.

Health Insurance

The Mundus MAPP Consortium purchases health insurance meeting relevant EACEA minimum requirements for:

All enrolled students.

Coverage applies for the study period and also extends for a limited period before and after the programme.

Additional Support for Students With Individual Needs

Additional financial support may be available to scholarship recipients with individual needs, depending on the level of disability or support required.

Applicants who may require such support should review the applicable Erasmus Mundus and programme provisions carefully.

Previous Erasmus Mundus Scholarship Holders

Applicants who have already received an:

Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarship

are not eligible to receive another EMJM scholarship.

Additionally, an EMJM scholarship holder cannot simultaneously benefit from another EU-funded scholarship scheme to undertake the same or another Erasmus Mundus Joint Master during the relevant enrollment period.

Mundus MAPP Institutional Scholarships

The Erasmus Mundus scholarship is not the only financial-aid route.

The Mundus MAPP Consortium also offers:

One Institutional Scholarship per study track.

There are four tracks, meaning this support is distributed across the programme’s mobility pathways.

Institutional Scholarship recipients receive:

50% tuition-fee waiver at both the Year 1 and Year 2 institutions.

However:

The Institutional Scholarship does not include a stipend.

Applicants should therefore distinguish between the two awards.

EMJM Scholarship

€1,400 monthly contribution

Up to €33,600 over 24 months

Full tuition-fee waiver

Institutional Scholarship

50% tuition waiver

No living stipend

No Separate Scholarship Application

Applicants do not complete a separate Erasmus Mundus scholarship application.

During the normal Mundus MAPP application, candidates indicate whether they wish to be considered for financial aid.

Applicants who submit by the scholarship deadline and indicate interest will be considered for available scholarships.

Scholarship Application Deadline

For the 2027–2029 intake, applicants seeking financial aid must submit by:

1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

This deadline also serves as an early application deadline for candidates who are self-funded.

Candidates seeking the Erasmus Mundus scholarship should treat this as the critical application deadline.

When Will Scholarship Results Be Released?

First-round admission decisions, including EMJM scholarship results, are scheduled to become available in the applicant portal on:

14 April 2027.

The deadline for appeals against first-round decisions is:

20 April 2027.

Self-Funded Deadline for Non-EU/EEA Residents

Candidates who:

Do not want to be considered for financial aid, and

Are residents outside the EU/EEA

have a later deadline:

15 April 2027 at 23:59 CET.

Their admission decisions are expected by:

30 June 2027

with appeals due by:

6 July 2027.

Self-Funded Deadline for EU/EEA Residents

EU/EEA residents who do not require financial aid may apply until:

1 July 2027 at 23:59 CET.

Their decisions are expected on:

15 July 2027

with appeals due by:

21 July 2027.

Official Academic Records Deadline

The deadline for successful applicants to submit official academic records is:

31 July 2027.

Candidates should make arrangements early if their universities require significant processing time to produce official documentation.

Complete 2027–2029 Admissions Timeline

The major dates are:

1 September 2026: Applications expected to open

1 December 2026, 23:59 CET: Financial-aid and early self-funded deadline

14 April 2027: First-round decisions, including EMJM scholarships

15 April 2027, 23:59 CET: Self-funded deadline for non-EU/EEA residents

20 April 2027: First-round appeal deadline

30 June 2027: Decisions for self-funded non-EU/EEA applicants

1 July 2027, 23:59 CET: Self-funded deadline for EU/EEA residents

6 July 2027: Non-EU/EEA self-funded appeal deadline

15 July 2027: EU/EEA self-funded decisions

21 July 2027: EU/EEA self-funded appeal deadline

31 July 2027: Official academic-record deadline

The financial-aid deadline of 1 December 2026 is the most important date for anyone hoping to receive the Erasmus Mundus scholarship.

Appeals

Applications meeting the formal eligibility requirements are reviewed by at least two evaluators.

Applicants may appeal admission decisions, but the appeals procedure is limited.

Simply repeating information already included in the original application is not considered sufficient grounds for appeal.

Decisions are overturned only on:

Procedural grounds.

Candidates therefore need to ensure that the original application is as strong and complete as possible.

Deferral Policy

Mundus MAPP generally does not offer deferrals to applicants unable to arrive at the beginning of the first term because of:

Visa problems

Financial difficulties

The Consortium reserves the right to consider particularly well-justified requests exceptionally and on a case-by-case basis.

Applicants from visa-sensitive countries are strongly encouraged to apply by the earliest deadline.

How to Apply

Admissions are administered centrally by:

Central European University Private University

Candidates cannot submit separate Mundus MAPP applications directly to ISS, IBEI, or York.

Applicants must use the central CEU application system.

Only applications submitted through the designated CEU process will be considered.

Applicants need to:

Select one mobility track.

Complete the online application form.

Upload all required documentation.

Submit proof of English proficiency or applicable waiver documentation.

Indicate whether they want financial-aid consideration.

Submit before the relevant deadline.

Candidates do not need to pay the CEU application fee when applying only to Mundus MAPP. The fee applies if they also apply to other CEU programmes.

Official programme website:
https://www.mundusmapp.org/

Admissions information:
https://www.mundusmapp.org/admissions/

Admissions calendar:
https://www.mundusmapp.org/admissions-calendar/

Financial aid:
https://www.mundusmapp.org/financial-aid/

Required Supporting Documents

The user-provided programme information indicates that applicants must upload supporting documentation through the online application process.

Because the complete admissions checklist is maintained separately by Mundus MAPP and CEU, applicants should consult the current official checklist before submitting.

This is particularly important for:

Degree documents

Academic transcripts

English-language documentation

Statement of purpose

Residence evidence

Other formal admission materials

Applicants should avoid relying on older application checklists because requirements can change between admission cycles.

Practical Component of Mundus MAPP

Mundus MAPP is not designed solely around theoretical classroom study.

The programme includes a strong practical component through:

Internship

Study trip

Spring course

Case studies

Interaction with practitioners

Policy research

These activities allow students to observe policymaking processes directly and apply academic concepts to practical issues.

Internship Experience

Internships are part of the wider Mundus MAPP learning model.

They can help students:

Apply policy theories to real organizations

Gain professional experience

Build networks

Understand institutional processes

Explore potential career pathways

Collect empirical material relevant to research

The internship component also distinguishes Mundus MAPP from more purely academic public-policy master’s programmes.

Learning Outcomes

Graduates are expected to develop advanced knowledge across several areas.

Policy Theory and Institutions

Students develop systematic understanding of:

Public-policy theories

Policy paradigms

Policy concepts

Policy formation

Government institutions

International institutions

Intergovernmental coordination

Global and European Policy

Students learn about:

National policy processes

International policy

Transnational policymaking

European governance

Global governance

International development

Political, Economic and Legal Context

Graduates should be able to understand the:

Political

Economic

Legal

Geopolitical

Social

implications of public-policy formulation.

Policy Analysis and Problem Solving

Students learn how to:

Critically analyze policy problems

Evaluate public policies

Evaluate policy instruments

Use quantitative methods

Use qualitative methods

Develop research questions

Collect and analyze data

Produce policy reports

Advise decision-makers

Participate in policy design and implementation

These skills can be relevant across international organizations, governments, consulting, NGOs, and research institutions.

Interdisciplinary and Multicultural Skills

Mundus MAPP also emphasizes the ability to:

Work across social-science disciplines

Handle complex policy questions

Analyze incomplete information

Work in multicultural teams

Engage with different governance traditions

Understand accountability and transparency

Recognize ethical responsibilities in public service

The physical mobility component reinforces these skills by placing students within different institutional and national environments.

Communication Skills

Graduates are expected to develop professional-level English-language communication abilities.

They should be able to:

Produce academic and policy writing

Make presentations

Explain complex issues to specialist audiences

Communicate with non-specialists

Present evidence and recommendations clearly

These competencies are valuable for policy careers requiring frequent interaction among government officials, researchers, donors, civil society, and international partners.

Career Relevance

Mundus MAPP is explicitly designed to prepare future academic and policy leaders.

Graduates may pursue careers across areas such as:

International organizations

Government ministries

European institutions

NGOs

Development agencies

Policy consulting

Think tanks

Research institutions

International development

Public administration

Academia

Private-sector public policy

Different mobility tracks allow students to align their education with different professional priorities.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Mundus MAPP Application

1. Choose Your Mobility Track Carefully

Applicants can apply to only one track.

Do not select a track simply because one partner university is more familiar to you.

Consider whether your interests align more strongly with:

Global Public Policy

European Public Policy

Political Economy and Development

Governance and Development

Your choice should reinforce your academic and career objectives.

2. Prioritize the December 1 Deadline if You Need Funding

Scholarships are limited and competitive.

If you want to be considered for either major financial-aid opportunities, submit by:

TITLE: FAQs – Fellowships for Indian Citizens

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
What are the application opening and closing dates?

Please visit our website for the current application dates. The call for applications typically opens in February each year. Be sure to check the specific deadline for your program to confirm the closing date. Applications submitted outside the official announcement cycle will not be accepted.

How many letters of reference/recommendation do I need to submit?

Depending on the grant category, applicants are advised to request two to three referees to complete the letters of reference online by the application due date. Please read the applicant instructions for details.

Who should I ask to provide a reference/recommendation?

Applicants should ask people who will best support their application and who can objectively assess their ability to successfully undertake a program of research or study in the U.S. and their potential to contribute to the U.S. and India relationship. Where possible the referees should include academic supervisor/s, colleagues and key contacts who can provide relevant information on the applicant’s personal and professional attributes.

If I am employed, do I need my employer’s approval as part of my application?

If you are employed, you are required to route your application through the proper channel. Your application will be considered ineligible without the employer’s endorsement/Letter of Support from Home Institution. The employer must indicate that leave will be granted for the fellowship period. Please obtain the endorsement in the specified format from the appropriate administrative authority. Postdoc candidates working under government-funded projects are required to get an endorsement from their affiliating institutions in India.

For the Fulbright-Nehru Doctoral, Postdoctoral, Academic and Professional Excellence Fellowships, does it help to establish contact with potential U.S. host institutions at the time of application? Is it mandatory?

You will be affiliated with only one U.S. host institution for the entire duration of your grant. USIEF strongly recommends applicants to identify institutions with which they wish to be affiliated and to correspond, in advance, with potential host institutions. If you have secured a letter of invitation from a U.S. institution, please include it as a part of your application. It is not mandatory but highly preferred.

How long does the review process take?

The review process takes three to four months after the application deadline. For the timeline and placement process, please visit the grant specific webpages on our website.

If selected, when can I begin my fellowship in the U.S.?

For the 2027-2028 cycle, most Fulbright fellows will begin their grants in August/September 2027. Depending upon the fellowship category, some fellows could begin in January 2028.

What does the selection process involve?

Subject experts review all eligible applications. Applicants recommended by the subject experts will be required to appear for an online interview with the USIEF National Selection Committee. Shortlisted candidates are notified at least three weeks prior to the interview date. Depending on the grant category, the national selection committees meet between August and December.

Fulbright-Nehru selection panels will generally use the following criteria to evaluate applications:

Academic credentials and professional ability

Merit of the proposed Fulbright project

Communication skills

Commitment to the community or national service

Need to conduct research in the U.S.

Outcomes, Potential Impact and Benefits

Motivation, Seriousness of Purpose, Maturity, Leadership, Cultural Adaptability

Ability to contribute as a cultural ambassador beyond his/her specific field of study

The national selection committees recommend a slate of semi-finalists for further consideration of the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board (FFSB) in Washington, D.C. Finalists are notified of the outcome typically in March/April.

Will the Fulbright Commission staff review my application before submitting?

No. Please note that Fulbright staff are unable to access your application prior to submission.

How can I ensure my application is successful?

The Fulbright application process emphasizes the individuality of each applicant, and there is no universal “formula” for success. Each application should reflect the applicant’s unique background, experiences, and goals, while highlighting how the time in the program will be used effectively. Applicants must demonstrate how their proposed project aligns with the aims of the Fulbright program and how their work may contribute.

Can you tell me why I was not selected?

Unfortunately, we cannot provide individual feedback to applicants. As with all Fulbright awards, applications are evaluated by expert panels. The assessment is competitive, merit-based and in accordance with the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board (FFSB) policies.

Are Fulbright-Nehru and other Fulbright grants available for attending conferences, seminars and paper presentations in the U.S. and other countries?

Fulbright-Nehru, , and other Fulbright grants are not for the principal purpose of attending seminars and conferences or for presenting papers.

Who is eligible to apply for the Fulbright-Nehru and other Fulbright Fellowships?
Please see the eligibility criteria listed with respect to each grant category in addition to the General Prerequisites.

Can I avail of a Fulbright Fellowship for a project that I want to work on in India?

No. These grants are offered for study, research, teaching or professional development in the U.S.

What is the duration of the grants?

It can range from six weeks to two academic years depending on the grant category. See individual grant descriptions on our website.

Is there a preferred age for each fellowship category?

Fellowship categories do not have age limits/age preferences.

I had applied for a Fulbright Fellowship in the past but did not make it. Can I apply again?

Yes, you are strongly encouraged to apply again. Please review the eligibility criteria carefully. In a given academic year, you are eligible to apply for only one Fulbright-Nehru Fellowship.

Where can I get information on Indian Fulbright fellows?

Please visit the “Our Community/Meet our Indian Fulbrighters” page on USIEF website to learn about our fellows currently in the U.S. and their Fulbright projects.

Can I have multiple U.S. host institutions?

In the interest of maintaining a consistent, coherent program of research/study, applicants are strongly encouraged to propose to work with no more than one host institution while in the United States. This is to ensure that program participants have sufficient time to develop ties with their host institutions and communities, an integral part of the cultural and academic exchange component of Fulbright. Short visits (up to 1 week) to other institutions are acceptable exceptions to this.

Must I return to India at the completion of my Fulbright program?

Fulbright scholars travel on a J-1 visa. You (and your J-2 dependents, where applicable) are subject to Code of Federal Regulations rule 212(e), the two-year, home country residence requirement associated with the J-visa. This is intended to ensure that scholars fulfil the exchange nature of the program.

TITLE: YOU-DARE kicks off

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
News | Project News

ESF is proud to announce the launch of YOU-DARE (YOUth Debunking the gendered Arguments of far-Right Extremism), a new project that it will be coordinating, funded by the European Commission.

A Pan-European Project Tackles Gender Narratives in Far-Right Youth Movements

YOU-DARE brings together interdisciplinary expertise from across Europe to investigate how far-right youth groups construct and mobilise gender identities, and how these narratives erode democratic values and behaviours.

In recent years across the globe, far-right movements have increasingly utilised gender identities to promote exclusionary ideologies, simultaneously undermining democratic values. The YOU-DARE project seeks to illuminate this paradox by examining these dynamics through an intersectional lens that uncovers both the complexities and contradictions of gender constructions within far-right youth movements.

Key focus areas include:

Intersectional Analysis: Challenging oversimplified views of far-right ideologies on gender by exposing the nuanced interplay between hyper-masculine/feminine tropes and pro-equality rhetoric within anti-immigration campaigns.

Youth Leadership: Exploring how youth leaders, including online influencers, shape far-right gender discourses.

Local and Transnational Dimensions: Conducting comparative case studies across eight countries-Denmark, Spain, the United Kingdom, France, Hungary, Italy, Romania, and Sweden-to understand how local dynamics connect to global trends.

Policy and Practice Innovation: Establishing a Policy Lab to co-design and pilot-test practical solutions for reducing the appeal of far-right ideologies among youth.

Through its work and results, YOU-DARE will demonstrate the need for intervention across society. The YOU-DARE Toolkit and policy recommendations are designed to help policymakers tackle the spread of extremist gender ideals. The project will also offer powerful mutual learning opportunities through the Open Policy Lab, capacity-building workshops, and a Knowledge Sharing Platform. By clearly illustrating the influence of (hyper-)masculinity and femininity models within identity politics and presenting innovative solutions, the initiative will strengthen cross-national networking and collaboration among those working to prevent the spread of far-right ideologies among young people. It will also provide policymakers with the knowledge and evidence required to safeguard democratic values against the corrosive impact of far-right gender narratives.

United by Expertise

The YOU-DARE consortium brings together organisations from across Europe, combining diverse expertise in social sciences, gender studies, far-right politics, and participatory research. Partners include the European Science Foundation (project coordinator), Aalborg University in Denmark, Smart Venice, Goldsmiths University of London, Stockholm University, University of Glasgow, Universitat Oberta de Catalunya, Political Capital, University of Bucharest, ALDA (European Association for Local Democracy), and NetHood. Together, the consortium gathers decades of experience in research, policy design, and community engagement, and will collectively address the challenges posed by far-right youth movements.

“We aim to research and expose the gendered narratives of far-right ideology and its appeal to youth, while providing evidence-based strategies to safeguard democracy and equality. YOU-DARE represents a unique research collaboration across disciplines and borders to generate robust and actionable knowledge for change.” said (Susi Meret, Aalborg University, Scientific Coordinator).

To learn more about YOU-DARE, including its objectives, activities, and outcomes, please visit https://you-dare.eu or reach out to contact[at]you-dare[dot]eu.

You can find YOU-DARE on LinkedIn via linkedin.com/company/you-dare-eu/

Key Facts

YOU-DARE (YOUth Debunking the gendered Arguments of far-Right Extremism) is funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Actions Programme.

Funded under Call No. “HORIZON-CL2-2024-DEMOCRACY-01”, at a cost of €2 999 642.50.

Grant Agreement No. 101178147.

The YOU-DARE will run for 36 months, starting 1st February 2025, to 31st January 2028.

YOU-DARE is coordinated by The European Science Foundation (ESF).

Pilot Action for Securing a Sustainable European Next Generation of Efficient RE-free magnets

PASSENGER (Pilot Action for Securing a Sustainable European Next Generation of Efficient RE-free magnets) is a four-year project funded by the European Union from the climate action, environment, resource efficiency and raw materials work programme. The project aims to address the lack of sustainable access to critical raw materials faced by the European Raw Materials sector, where permanent magnets represent one of the most vulnerable categories.

Bearing in mind the importance of permanent magnets in present and emerging technologies, PASSENGER aims to develop innovative solutions for the EU dependency on rare-earth raw materials for permanent magnets, avoiding bottlenecks in the material supply-chain and diminishing the environmental impact. This sustainable substitution model will rely on resources that are widely available in Europe and innovative technologies. It will involve 8 innovative pilot plant activities, covering the whole value chain and including electromobility as a main key-driving sector.

The ambitious project relies on a multidisciplinary consortium involving major European industries, academic leaders, and associations dealing with permanent magnets manufacturing, alloy production, powder fabrication, electric motors, e-vehicles, eco-design and product/process standardisation. The project is thus able to cover the whole magnets production value chain, from studying fundamental properties to the production of high-technology end products, while aiming at making the transition from a linear to a circular model involving citizens, international platforms and relevant stakeholders.

Project partners

PASSENGER relies on a consortium of 20 partners from 8 European Countries, including key end users and SMEs/LEs for a total of 14 companies.

The fund is divided into five strands, accessed via two simple application processes:

Festivals and Showcases

Interactive/immersive/XR Grants: for XR creatives to attend eligible festival/showcase events with an interactive/immersive/XR project

Labs and Co-Pro Forums

Co-Production Forum Grants: for producers with feature projects looking for finance and partners to attend eligible market/co-production forums

Grant

Awards for Short and Feature Film Festival Grants range from £150- £1,500* but will not normally exceed £750.

Awards for XR projects are divided into two tiers: Travel only (£150 – £1,500), and Large XR grants (£1,500 up to £5,000) for A category showcases only, as per the Key List.

Awards for Lab Grants are capped at £6,000 but rarely exceed £3,000. They cannot support a filmmaker or project with more than one lab grant in any single year.

Awards for Co-Production Forum Grants are capped at £2,000. Each film or project can receive a maximum of two grants.

Eligibility

Festivals and Showcases

Applications can be made by a project’s director, producer or writer, who must be aged 18 or above and a UK resident or citizen.

All applicants must have had their short/feature/XR project selected by one of the festivals or showcases on our Key List, and must provide evidence of selection in an official festival programme (not side-bar or guest programme).

Labs and Co-Pro Forums

Eligible applicants must have been selected by one of the eligible events on the ‘Key List: Labs and Co-Production Forums’.

For Co-production Forums and where a Lab is project-based, the selected film or project must be a UK production or co-production.

For Lab attendance priority is given to those who are yet to make (or who are developing) their first feature.

Each film or project can receive a maximum of one grant per event.

They cannot accept applications for travel to a Lab or Forum that has already taken place when the application is made. You must apply at least two weeks before the event start.

Application
