TITLE: NASA Pathways Internship Program 2027: Launch Your Career with NASA Through the Spring 2027 Internship

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The NASA Pathways Internship Program offers students an opportunity to gain meaningful professional experience while working with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Designed as a long-term talent-development pathway, the program provides multi-semester internship experiences intended to prepare students for careers at NASA and can provide a direct route to full-time employment after graduation.

For students interested in science, engineering, technology, communications, public relations, business, administration, information technology, social sciences, and other fields, NASA Pathways can provide an opportunity to apply academic knowledge in a professional environment while contributing to NASA’s mission.

The Spring 2027 NASA Pathways Internship application window is scheduled to open on September 21, 2026, and close on September 25, 2026. Successful applicants will begin their Spring 2027 internships on January 25, 2027.

NASA Pathways Internship Program 2027

NASA strategically recruits Pathways interns based on their long-term potential and alignment with the agency’s future workforce requirements. Unlike short-term internship opportunities, the Pathways program specializes in multi-semester experiences that are designed to help students develop the knowledge, skills, and professional experience necessary for future employment.

The program is therefore more than an opportunity to spend a few months at NASA. It is structured as a career-development pathway, allowing students to gain experience, receive professional development, work on meaningful assignments, and potentially transition into NASA employment after completing their academic program.

NASA describes the program as an opportunity for students who are passionate about its mission and interested in contributing to work connected with exploration, innovation, science, technology, and the advancement of humanity.

Spring 2027 NASA Pathways Application Deadline

Applications for the Spring 2027 Pathways Internship cycle will open on:

Opening date: September 21, 2026

Deadline: September 25, 2026

Internship start date: January 25, 2027

Applicants should pay close attention to the short application window. NASA states that links to the relevant USAJOBS vacancies will be added to the Spring 2027 positions listings when applications open on September 21, 2026.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to research available positions and NASA center locations before the application period begins so that they can identify opportunities that correspond with their academic major, professional interests, and preferred geographic location.

What Does the NASA Pathways Internship Offer?

The NASA Pathways Internship Program is designed around long-term professional development rather than simply providing students with temporary workplace exposure.

As a Pathways intern, students can expect to be given challenging and meaningful assignments connected to their academic or career interests. NASA also emphasizes learning, growth, and the development of a supportive professional community.

The experience can include:

Meaningful work related to the intern’s academic or career interests.

Opportunities for lifelong learning and professional growth.

Exposure to NASA’s working environment and organizational culture.

Professional assignments designed to develop practical skills.

Training and learning opportunities.

Opportunities to work toward clearly defined career goals.

Development of an Individual Development Plan.

Potential consideration for employment with NASA after graduation.

The program gives interns a degree of autonomy in defining their career trajectory. Rather than simply completing assigned tasks, participants work with NASA to develop an Individual Development Plan that helps establish assignments, training events, and learning opportunities relevant to their career objectives.

Career Opportunities After Graduation

One of the most significant features of the NASA Pathways Internship Program is its potential connection to employment after graduation.

Throughout the internship, NASA evaluates the intern’s experience and, as the student approaches graduation, may consider the individual for full-time permanent employment or term employment lasting between one and six years.

Importantly, NASA states that interns who are considered for such employment do not need to submit an additional job application.

This makes the Pathways program particularly valuable for students who want to build a long-term career with NASA. The internship provides an opportunity to demonstrate capabilities and develop experience within the agency while still completing an academic program.

However, participation in the internship should not be interpreted as an automatic guarantee of employment. NASA states that interns are evaluated as they approach graduation and may be considered for permanent or term employment.

Academic Fields and Disciplines Available

NASA offers Pathways opportunities across a broad range of disciplines. The specific disciplines and skill sets recruited may vary by application cycle, and NASA posts the specific vacancies before applications open.

The occupational classifications listed for the program include areas in engineering, physical sciences, business, communications, administration, information technology, mathematics, statistics, and related fields.

Engineering, Science and Technology

Opportunities listed in this area include:

GS-899: Engineering

GS-1399: Physical Sciences

These areas may be relevant to students pursuing academic programs connected with engineering, physical sciences, scientific research, and related technical disciplines.

Business and Related Fields

NASA also lists a broad range of business and professional occupational classifications, including:

GS-0099: Safety and Occupational Health

GS-199: Social Sciences

GS-299: Human Resources

GS-399: Administration and Program Management and Analysis

GS-599: Accounting and Budget

GS-1099: Communication and Public Relations

GS-1199: Procurement and Contracts

GS-1599: Mathematics and Statistics

GS-2299: Information Technology

The inclusion of Communication and Public Relations is particularly significant for students studying communications, public relations, strategic communication, media, or related fields.

The availability of a specific discipline, however, depends on the vacancies posted for the particular recruitment cycle.

What Type of Students Does NASA Look For?

NASA states that it seeks students who are captivated by its vision, mission, and core values and who demonstrate characteristics that contribute to the agency’s success.

The agency emphasizes that its strongest candidates are well-rounded students from a variety of backgrounds.

NASA identifies several qualities it looks for in Pathways candidates, including:

Curiosity

Team orientation

Excellence

Passion for exploration

Agility

Resilience

An important point for prospective applicants is that prior professional experience is not required.

Instead, NASA assesses applicants through seven non-technical competencies:

Attention to Detail

Flexibility

Interpersonal Skills

Learning

Problem Solving

Self-Management (Achievement)

Technology Application

Students should therefore consider how their academic work, projects, teamwork, leadership activities, problem-solving experiences, and other accomplishments demonstrate these competencies.

NASA Pathways Internship Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy NASA’s stated eligibility requirements to participate in the Pathways Internship Program.

All Pathways interns must:

Be a U.S. citizen.

Be at least 16 years old.

Be enrolled or accepted for enrollment on at least a half-time basis at an accredited educational institution and maintain at least half-time enrollment as defined by that institution.

Be pursuing a degree or certificate.

Have and maintain a cumulative 2.9 GPA on a 4.0 scale.

Be able to complete at least 480 hours of work before completing their degree or certificate requirements.

Sign a Pathways Participant Agreement.

Undergo a pre-employment background investigation.

There is also a Selective Service requirement for certain male applicants. Male applicants born after December 31, 1959, must certify that they have registered with the Selective Service System or that they are exempt under the Selective Service Law.

In addition, individual vacancies may establish requirements concerning when applicants must be available to begin work. NASA states that vacancies typically require applicants to be available to begin during a predetermined period, generally within the subsequent two semesters following the closing date of the vacancy.

Applicants should therefore review the individual vacancy carefully because requirements can differ depending on the position.

Where Are NASA Pathways Internships Located?

NASA operates multiple centers across the United States, with different facilities involved in different areas of work.

The Pathways program offers opportunities associated with NASA centers located across the nation. Because each vacancy can involve different locations, applicants are encouraged to research NASA’s facilities before applying.

When submitting an application, candidates should identify vacancies that align with both:

Their academic major; and

Their preferred geographic location or locations.

This approach helps ensure that applicants are considered for work corresponding to their educational background and professional interests.

How to Apply for the NASA Pathways Internship

The NASA Pathways application process requires applicants to conduct research, prepare an appropriate application, and apply to an eligible vacancy during the specified application period.

Step 1: Research NASA Facilities and Opportunities

Before applying, applicants should research the types of work performed at NASA facilities.

Understanding the activities and responsibilities of different NASA centers can help applicants determine which locations and opportunities best correspond with their academic background and career interests.

NASA provides information about its centers and facilities to help prospective applicants make informed decisions.

Step 2: Prepare Your USAJOBS Profile and Resume

Applicants should visit USAJOBS.gov and create a profile if they do not already have one.

After creating the profile, applicants must build or upload their resume.

NASA emphasizes that the resume is an important part of the application because it gives candidates an opportunity to explain their background and demonstrate what distinguishes them from other applicants.

Applicants should make sure that their resumes are clear, concise, and relevant to the vacancy.

A particularly important requirement is that resumes submitted through USAJOBS must be two pages or fewer. NASA states that resumes longer than two pages will be automatically rejected.

NASA recommends using the USAJOBS resume builder to help applicants include relevant information while following the required format.

Applicants are also encouraged to consult NASA’s Pathways Applicant Guide for additional information about the application process, assessment, and hiring procedures.

Step 3: Apply During the Open Window

Once applications open, applicants should select a vacancy that corresponds with both their academic major and preferred geographic location.

For the Spring 2027 cycle, the application window is scheduled for September 21 through September 25, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final day if they can submit earlier. Preparing the USAJOBS profile, resume, academic information, and other required materials in advance can make the application process more manageable.

NASA’s Policy on Artificial Intelligence in Applications

Applicants should pay particular attention to NASA’s policy concerning artificial intelligence tools.

NASA explicitly prohibits candidates from using ChatGPT or other artificial intelligence or AI-assisted tools when creating narrative responses for the employment application and assessment.

Candidates are required to create their own original responses and must not plagiarize, copy, or adapt responses from other sources.

NASA states that information provided during the application process may be subject to verification and that it may discontinue a candidate’s candidacy if it determines that the candidate violated the prohibition on AI tools.

This means applicants should ensure that all narrative responses submitted as part of the NASA Pathways application are genuinely their own work.

APPLY HERE

Preparing a Strong NASA Pathways Application

Although NASA emphasizes that previous experience is not required, applicants can still strengthen their applications by presenting their academic background and experiences clearly.

Candidates should consider how their experiences demonstrate the competencies NASA assesses.

For example, applicants can review their academic projects, group assignments, research, volunteer activities, leadership responsibilities, extracurricular activities, or other experiences and identify evidence of:

Careful attention to detail.

Ability to adapt to changing circumstances.

Effective interpersonal communication.

Willingness and ability to learn.

Practical problem-solving ability.

Self-management and achievement.

Appropriate use of technology.

Applicants should also make sure that their resume is tailored to the vacancy rather than submitting a generic document that does not clearly demonstrate alignment with the position.

Why the NASA Pathways Program Is Significant

The NASA Pathways Internship Program stands out because it combines academic study with structured professional experience at one of the world’s best-known space and aeronautics organizations.

The multi-semester structure gives students the opportunity to develop experience over a longer period, while the Individual Development Plan helps connect internship assignments, training, and learning opportunities with longer-term career objectives.

The possibility of being considered for NASA employment after graduation also makes the program particularly relevant to students who are interested in establishing careers within the agency.

For students in communications and public relations, social sciences, administration, information technology, engineering, physical sciences, mathematics, human resources, procurement, accounting, and other listed fields, the program can provide a pathway for applying academic knowledge in a professional government environment.

Visit HERE for more information about the NASA Pathways Internship Program 2027.

Important Dates for Spring 2027

Prospective applicants should take note of the following dates:

Applications open: September 21, 2026

Application deadline: September 25, 2026

Internship begins: January 25, 2027

NASA indicates that USAJOBS application links for the relevant Spring 2027 positions will be added to the listings when applications open on September 21.

Final Thoughts

The NASA Pathways Internship Program provides students with an opportunity to gain meaningful experience while developing toward a potential career with NASA. Its multi-semester structure, professional development opportunities, Individual Development Plan, and potential pathway to employment after graduation make it more than a conventional short-term internship.

The program is open to eligible U.S. citizen students who meet NASA’s educational, academic, age, work-hour, and other requirements. Opportunities span numerous disciplines, including engineering, physical sciences, social sciences, communications and public relations, human resources, administration, accounting and budget, procurement, mathematics and statistics, information technology, and safety and occupational health.

Students interested in the Spring 2027 cycle should prepare ahead of time because the application window is short. Creating a USAJOBS profile, preparing a compliant two-page-or-less resume, researching NASA centers, identifying suitable vacancies, and reviewing the application requirements before September 21 can help applicants be ready when applications open.

Most importantly, applicants should carefully follow NASA’s instructions concerning original application responses and the use of artificial intelligence. Candidates are responsible for ensuring that their submitted materials comply with NASA’s stated application rules.

For students who meet the eligibility requirements and are interested in building a career connected to NASA’s mission, the Spring 2027 Pathways Internship represents a significant opportunity to gain practical experience, develop professional competencies, and potentially progress toward future employment with the agency.

For more global Internship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

TITLE: Fully Funded Commonwealth Master’s and PhD Scholarships 2027/28 in the UK: Applications Now Open

Applications are now open for the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships and Commonwealth PhD Scholarships for the 2027/28 academic year, offering talented students and researchers from eligible Commonwealth countries an opportunity to pursue fully funded postgraduate study at universities across the United Kingdom.

Funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and administered by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC), these prestigious scholarships are designed for individuals with strong academic ability and clear potential to contribute to sustainable development in their home countries.

Both the Master’s and PhD scholarship competitions opened in September 2026, with successful candidates expected to begin their studies in the United Kingdom in September or October 2027.

The final CSC application deadline for both programs is:

16:00 BST on Tuesday, 20 October 2026.

However, candidates should be aware that their national nominating agency or other approved nominator may impose an earlier application deadline. Applicants must therefore satisfy both the CSC deadline and any separate requirements established by their nominating organisation.

About the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission

The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK manages UK government scholarship programs focused strongly on international development.

Operating within the framework of the Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan, the CSC aims to identify talented individuals who can become leaders, researchers, innovators and agents of positive change after returning to their home countries.

The scholarships do more than provide access to postgraduate education. They are structured around the expectation that scholars will use the knowledge, technical expertise, professional networks and leadership capabilities gained in the United Kingdom to address development priorities in their countries and communities.

The Commonwealth Master’s and PhD Scholarships are funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office and are particularly aimed at candidates who would otherwise be unable to afford postgraduate study in the United Kingdom.

Two Major Commonwealth Scholarship Routes for 2027/28

The current scholarship call includes two distinct postgraduate opportunities:

The two schemes share a strong emphasis on development impact, academic merit and leadership potential, but applicants must carefully determine which program corresponds to their academic level and country eligibility.

Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships 2027/28

The Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships are intended for talented candidates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries who want to undertake a full-time taught Master’s degree at a UK university.

The program is particularly designed for applicants who demonstrate the academic ability and development potential necessary to benefit from postgraduate education but would not otherwise be financially able to study in the United Kingdom.

What Can You Study Under the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship?

The CSC funds one-year taught Master’s programs.

Applicants should carefully select courses that relate to their professional objectives, their country’s development priorities and one or more of the CSC development themes.

Importantly, the CSC does not fund MBA programs through this particular Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship route.

Candidates are advised to identify up to three appropriate UK universities and courses in order of preference. Applicants should research these options carefully because the CSC takes course suitability, development relevance and value for money into account when making placement decisions.

Applicants are also strongly encouraged to apply separately for admission to their preferred universities rather than waiting for the Commonwealth Scholarship selection process to be completed.

Commonwealth PhD Scholarships 2027/28

The Commonwealth PhD Scholarships support high-quality graduates from eligible least developed Commonwealth countries and vulnerable states who demonstrate the potential to undertake internationally significant doctoral research.

The scholarship is intended to strengthen research and teaching capacity while supporting research projects capable of generating meaningful development impact.

The CSC particularly seeks candidates who have the potential to become influential researchers, educators, specialists and leaders after returning to their home countries.

Duration of the Commonwealth PhD Scholarship

Commonwealth PhD Scholarships normally support 36 months of full-time doctoral study at an approved UK university or higher education institution participating in the relevant CSC funding arrangements.

The CSC does not support four-year PhD programs under this scheme.

PhD applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed research can realistically be completed within the CSC-supported 36-month period.

UK Supervisor Requirement for PhD Applicants

One major difference between the Master’s and PhD application processes is the requirement for academic supervisor support.

PhD applicants must obtain a supporting statement from a proposed supervisor at a UK university.

The supporting statement must come from a supervisor at at least one of the institutions listed in the candidate’s application. Applicants are strongly encouraged to obtain this statement from a supervisor at their first-choice institution.

Candidates should therefore begin contacting prospective UK supervisors well before the application deadline.

The supervisor’s support is significant because it provides evidence that the proposed research is academically feasible and aligns with expertise available at the proposed UK institution.

Six Commonwealth Scholarship Development Themes

Both scholarship programs operate under the CSC’s six principal development themes:

Science and technology for development

Improving population health, health systems and capacity

Promoting innovation and entrepreneurship

Strengthening peace, security and governance

Strengthening resilience and response to crises

Access, inclusion and opportunity

Applicants should demonstrate clearly how their proposed study or research connects with relevant development problems in their home country and how the skills gained through their UK education can contribute to addressing those challenges.

Financial Benefits of the Commonwealth Scholarships

Both schemes provide extensive financial support, making them among the most attractive fully funded postgraduate scholarship opportunities available for students from eligible Commonwealth countries.

Benefits Available to Both Master’s and PhD Scholars

Selected scholars receive:

Full approved tuition fees, meaning scholars are not required to personally pay the approved tuition charges.

Approved airfare from the scholar’s home country to the United Kingdom at the beginning of the scholarship.

Return airfare to the home country following completion of the scholarship.

A monthly living allowance or stipend of £1,712 at the current published rate.

Scholars studying at universities within the London metropolitan area receive £2,000 per month at current published rates.

A study travel grant toward approved study-related travel within the United Kingdom or overseas.

Assessment for additional financial assistance where a scholar discloses a disability and qualifies for support.

These rates are quoted by the CSC at current levels and may be subject to change before or during the 2027/28 academic year.

Additional Benefits for Commonwealth PhD Scholars

Because doctoral study involves a longer research period, PhD scholarship recipients may also qualify for additional benefits depending on their circumstances.

These can include approved support toward overseas fieldwork, a paid mid-term visit to the scholar’s home country in qualifying circumstances, and certain family allowances.

At current published rates, eligible PhD scholars may receive specified spouse and/or child allowances depending on their family circumstances and whether qualifying dependants live with them in the United Kingdom.

The CSC emphasizes that these family allowances are contributions toward costs rather than guarantees that all expenses associated with accompanying family members will be covered.

Eligibility for Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships

Applicants for the Master’s Scholarship must satisfy the CSC’s core eligibility requirements.

Candidates must be citizens of, have been granted refugee status by, or otherwise fall within the permitted status categories for an eligible Commonwealth country. They must also be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country.

Applicants must be available to begin their academic studies in the UK at the beginning of the academic year in September 2027.

By September 2027, candidates will normally need to hold at least an upper second-class first degree, equivalent to a UK 2:1 honours degree. Candidates with a lower second-class degree may qualify where they also hold an appropriate postgraduate qualification, normally a Master’s degree.

Applicants must also demonstrate that they would be unable to afford postgraduate study in the United Kingdom without the scholarship and must submit all required documentation correctly.

There is no general age limit imposed by the CSC.

The CSC also states that it would not normally fund a second Master’s degree. Applicants seeking funding for another Master’s qualification must provide convincing justification for why the additional degree is necessary.

Candidates who have already undertaken Master’s-level study at a UK institution or have already received a Commonwealth Scholarship at Master’s level should carefully check the applicable eligibility restrictions.

Eligibility for Commonwealth PhD Scholarships

The PhD Scholarship has several similar basic requirements.

Candidates must:

Have citizenship, refugee status or another qualifying status connected with an eligible Commonwealth country.

Be permanently resident in an eligible country.

Be available to commence their UK studies in September 2027.

Normally hold at least the equivalent of a UK upper second-class undergraduate degree, or possess a lower second-class degree combined with a relevant postgraduate qualification.

Demonstrate financial need by showing that they could not otherwise afford to study in the UK.

Provide all compulsory supporting documentation.

The current CSC PhD page also contains a condition regarding prior registration for a PhD or an MPhil leading to a PhD. Applicants who are already enrolled in doctoral study should therefore review the current official eligibility wording particularly carefully before submitting an application.

Application Process: You Cannot Apply Directly to CSC Alone

An important feature of both programs is that submitting an application through CSC Central is not the only step.

Candidates must also apply through an approved nominating organisation.

The main nomination routes are:

National nominating agencies; and

Selected non-governmental organisations and charitable bodies participating in the program.

The nominating organisation conducts its own selection process and forwards a limited number of nominated candidates to the CSC.

A nomination does not automatically guarantee that the candidate will receive a Commonwealth Scholarship.

Nominating agencies may also establish additional eligibility rules, documentation requirements and earlier closing dates. Candidates should therefore check the requirements of their country’s nominating authority as soon as possible.

How to Apply Through CSC Central

Applications to both programs must be submitted electronically through the CSC Central application system.

The CSC states that it cannot accept applications or required documentation submitted through alternative channels.

Applicants are encouraged to draft important written responses separately before transferring them into the online form.

Candidates should also save their work regularly. Once an application has been formally submitted, it cannot be edited.

Because the application portal can become very busy close to the deadline, applicants are strongly advised not to wait until the final hours to submit their forms.

Required Supporting Documents

Failure to submit all mandatory documents by the deadline can make an application ineligible.

Master’s applicants are generally required to upload:

Proof of citizenship or qualifying refugee status, such as an eligible passport or national identity document containing the necessary identification information.

Complete academic transcripts for all higher education qualifications.

Certified English translations where original documents are not in English.

References from at least two appropriate referees.

PhD applicants need the relevant citizenship and academic documentation and references, but they must additionally submit a supporting statement from a proposed UK supervisor at one or more of the universities identified in their application.

The CSC does not accept required supporting documentation after the deadline through email or other channels, so candidates should verify completeness before submission.

What Applicants Must Write in the Application

The Commonwealth Scholarship application goes substantially beyond basic personal and educational information.

Candidates are asked to provide information on their academic background, employment experience, professional development, relevant achievements, publications or prizes where applicable, referees, study objectives and career plans.

One of the most important sections is the Development Impact Statement.

Applicants need to demonstrate how their proposed study or research relates to development challenges at national, local and broader levels; what changes they expect to achieve after completing the scholarship; who will benefit from their work; how long those outcomes may take to achieve; and how the resulting development impact could be measured.

Candidates are also asked to describe their future career objectives, leadership and voluntary activities, and the personal experiences that have influenced their desire to contribute to development in their home country.

How Commonwealth Scholarship Applications Are Assessed

Selection is highly competitive.

The CSC evaluates applicants across three central areas.

For both schemes, candidate merit is important and is assessed through indicators such as academic results, transcripts, referees’ assessments, relevant achievements, professional development and experience.

For Master’s applicants, the quality of the study plan is assessed. Applicants should demonstrate that they understand what they want to study, why they selected their proposed course and university and how the program supports their objectives.

For PhD candidates, the quality of the research proposal is crucial. Evaluators examine the clarity, originality, relevance and feasibility of the research, the candidate’s engagement with potential supervisors and whether the proposed research can reasonably be completed within the required period.

For both programs, substantial weight is given to potential development impact in the candidate’s home country.

Eligible Countries for Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships 2027/28

The current CSC list for the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship includes:

Bangladesh, Belize, Botswana, Dominica, Eswatini, Fiji, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Grenada, Guyana, India, Jamaica, Kenya, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Malaysia, Maldives, Mauritius, Montserrat, Mozambique, Namibia, Nauru, Nigeria, Pakistan, Papua New Guinea, Rwanda, Saint Helena, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Samoa, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu and Zambia.

The CSC particularly welcomes applications from Small Island Developing States in line with relevant Commonwealth commitments.

Eligible Countries for Commonwealth PhD Scholarships 2027/28

The Commonwealth PhD Scholarship for least developed countries and vulnerable states has a narrower country list.

The currently published eligible countries are:

Bangladesh, The Gambia, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, Pakistan, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Togo, Tuvalu, Uganda and Zambia.

Candidates should therefore not assume that eligibility for the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship automatically means they are eligible for the Commonwealth PhD Scholarship.

Important Information for Applicants from Pakistan

Pakistan is currently included in the eligible country lists for both the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship and the Commonwealth PhD Scholarship.

Pakistani candidates must still satisfy all academic and CSC eligibility conditions and follow the applicable nomination process.

Applicants should pay particular attention to the deadline and requirements established by the relevant Pakistani nominating authority because this may differ from, and may close earlier than, the CSC’s own final deadline.

University Admission Is a Separate Process

Receiving or applying for a Commonwealth Scholarship should not be confused with applying for admission to a UK university.

Candidates need to investigate and apply to their proposed universities separately.

University admission requirements can include academic conditions, English-language requirements, research proposals, references, departmental requirements and individual application deadlines.

The CSC strongly recommends that candidates take appropriate steps toward university admission in advance. If a candidate is selected for the scholarship but has not secured admission to an appropriate course or research program, it may not be possible for the scholarship placement to proceed.

IELTS and English Language Requirements

The CSC itself states that it does not require candidates to take IELTS as a general scholarship requirement.

However, this should not be interpreted as meaning that every UK university will waive its English-language requirements.

Individual universities may impose their own English proficiency requirements as part of the admissions process. Applicants must therefore check the policy of each institution and course to which they apply.

Requirement to Return to the Home Country

Commonwealth Scholarships are fundamentally development-focused awards.

Successful scholars are expected to return to their home countries after completing their scholarships and use the knowledge and skills gained through their studies to support development.

The CSC states that scholars commit to returning home at the end of the scholarship and that switching to a UK Graduate visa or another visa for the purpose of remaining in the UK after the award is not permitted under the scholarship conditions.

Key Dates for the 2027/28 Commonwealth Scholarships

Applications opened: Tuesday, 8 September 2026

CSC application deadline: Tuesday, 20 October 2026 at 16:00 BST

Nominator selections: Participating nominators are expected to nominate candidates to the CSC by December 2026.

Scholarship results: Applicants can expect to receive the outcome of their applications by approximately July 2027.

Studies begin: September/October 2027.

Applicants should remember that their nominating agency may establish an earlier closing date.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Commonwealth Scholarship Application

Applicants should begin preparations well before the deadline.

A competitive application should clearly demonstrate strong academic performance, carefully researched university choices, realistic career objectives and an identifiable development problem that the proposed education will help address.

Rather than making broad claims about wanting to “help society,” candidates should describe specific development challenges, identify intended beneficiaries, explain realistic interventions and show how results could eventually be measured.

Master’s applicants should research their proposed courses thoroughly and demonstrate why the modules, expertise and learning opportunities at their chosen universities are specifically relevant.

PhD candidates should invest substantial effort in their research proposal and engage seriously with potential UK supervisors before submitting the application.

Candidates should also choose referees who know their academic or professional capabilities well enough to provide detailed and credible assessments.

Above all, every major part of the application should answer a central question: how will this scholarship enable the candidate to create measurable development impact after returning home?

Conclusion

The Commonwealth Master’s and PhD Scholarships 2027/28 provide an exceptional opportunity for talented students and researchers from eligible Commonwealth countries to undertake fully funded postgraduate education at leading universities across the United Kingdom.

With support covering approved tuition fees, international airfare, monthly living allowances and additional study-related assistance, the scholarships can remove many of the financial barriers that prevent highly capable candidates from accessing postgraduate education abroad.

The Master’s route is aimed primarily at individuals seeking a one-year taught postgraduate qualification that can strengthen their ability to address development challenges, while the PhD route is designed for high-quality researchers seeking to undertake three years of development-focused doctoral research.

Applications for both programs are currently open, and the CSC deadline is 16:00 BST on Tuesday, 20 October 2026.

Prospective applicants should immediately begin checking their national nominating agency requirements, researching appropriate UK universities, preparing supporting documents, approaching referees and, in the case of PhD candidates, contacting potential UK supervisors.

As these scholarships are highly competitive, candidates should focus not only on academic excellence but also on demonstrating leadership potential, a credible career trajectory and a specific, realistic plan for generating lasting development impact in their home country.

TITLE: Tracking Black-browed albatrosses in the South Atlantic

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
by Francesco Ventura

As part of NASA grant 80NSSC25K7836, PO’s Francesco Ventura led a field campaign to the Falkland Islands to track Black-browed albatrosses (Thalassarche melanophris) nesting on Steeple Jason. Between December 2025-January 2026, the team deployed GPS trackers and accelerometers to study how wind shapes the movement and energetics of albatrosses flying over the stormy South Atlantic Ocean.

Albatross mates preening each other. Albatrosses are socially monogamous, forming long-term bonds and often remaining with the same partner for life. Image courtesy of Francesco Ventura.

During breeding, despite having to periodically return to their nest, albatrosses routinely travel thousands of miles to forage over large ocean areas in search of food. They do so by adopting a flight behavior known as “dynamic soaring,” through which albatrosses extract energy from the wind for their long journeys. Thanks to the small GPS and accelerometry loggers attached to the back of albatrosses with tape, the team will understand where the animals went in search for food over the ocean, and how much energy they used to go there.

The breeding colony on Steeple Jason. As a storm approached, albatrosses sat tightly on their nests, all facing into the strong wind. Image courtesy of Francesco Ventura.

Upon arrival on the island, the team was welcomed by thousands of fur seals, rockhopper penguins, gentoo penguins, magellanic penguins, and, of course, countless black-browed albatrosses. Steeple Jason is one of the largest albatross colonies in the world, hosting approximately 200,000 breeding pairs. This spectacular concentration of wildlife highlights the high productivity of the Patagonian Shelf, which sustains large populations of marine predators as well as important fisheries.

Map showing some of the foraging trips carried out by black-browed albatrosses tracked between December 2025 and January 2026. The data collected will enable the team to understand where the albatrosses traveled, the wind conditions they used, and how much energy they expended to reach their foraging areas. Map courtesy of Francesco Ventura.

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
UNICEF is inviting qualified professionals to apply for the Mixed-Methods Impact Evaluation Consultant – Adolescent Girls & Violence Against Children consultancy within the UNICEF Evaluation Office (EO) in New York, United States. The opportunity is designed for an experienced impact evaluation specialist with strong expertise in quantitative and qualitative research, violence against children, adolescent girls, child protection, and rigorous evaluation methodologies.

The consultancy will be undertaken remotely, with travel to selected project locations when required, and will run for 12 months. The successful consultant will contribute to important UNICEF impact evaluation initiatives addressing issues such as child marriage, social norms, violence in and around schools, and the agency, health and wellbeing of adolescent girls.

This opportunity may be particularly relevant to experienced researchers, evaluators, development professionals, public health specialists, economists, social scientists, and policy experts who have a strong record of conducting rigorous impact evaluations in low-income settings.

Opportunity Overview

Advertised: 28 August 2026

About UNICEF

UNICEF works across more than 190 countries and territories to protect children’s rights, save children’s lives and support children and adolescents in reaching their full potential.

The organization works across a broad range of areas, including child protection, education, health, nutrition, water and sanitation, adolescent development, gender equality, social policy and humanitarian response.

The UNICEF Evaluation Office plays an important role in strengthening evidence-based decision-making throughout the organization. Its work supports organizational learning and accountability by helping UNICEF understand what works, what does not work, why interventions produce particular outcomes, and how programs can be improved.

Through its network of regional evaluation teams, the Evaluation Office supports UNICEF country offices in generating and using evidence to improve programs for vulnerable children and communities.

About the UNICEF Evaluation Office

The Evaluation Office is one of UNICEF’s core evidence functions. It is responsible for supporting high-quality evaluations that can improve organizational performance, accountability and learning.

The office conducts several types of evaluations, including:

Strategic global evaluations

Institutional effectiveness evaluations

Humanitarian evaluations

Impact evaluations

Demand-driven evaluations

The Evaluation Office also develops and promotes standards, guidelines, norms and processes designed to strengthen the quality and use of UNICEF evaluations.

A major focus is the generation of rigorous impact evidence that can help UNICEF understand whether interventions are actually producing meaningful changes in the lives of children and adolescents.

The organization has emphasized impact evaluation as an increasingly important function, particularly as governments, donors and development organizations face increasing pressure to demonstrate results and make effective use of limited financial resources.

What Is the Purpose of This Consultancy?

The successful consultant will support UNICEF’s work on several important impact evaluation initiatives involving adolescent girls, child marriage, social norms, violence against children and child protection.

The consultancy will primarily support the implementation of the Impact Catalyst Fund (ICF) thematic windows and the demand-driven evaluation portfolio under the Power4Girls initiative.

The consultant may also support the scoping, development and implementation of broader impact evaluation opportunities involving:

Adolescent girls

Violence against children

Child protection

Child marriage

Social norms

Violence in schools

Girls’ agency

Girls’ health and wellbeing

This means the position requires more than general research experience. The successful candidate should be capable of applying rigorous mixed-methods evaluation approaches to complex and sensitive issues affecting children and adolescents.

Key Areas of Work

The consultancy is connected to several significant UNICEF initiatives.

1. Impact Catalyst Fund

The Impact Catalyst Fund is a flagship initiative designed to strengthen UNICEF’s ability to generate rigorous impact evidence.

The first thematic window was developed through a partnership with the Global Program to End Child Marriage (GPECM), focusing on child marriage and social norms.

The consultant will support work associated with this thematic area and contribute to strengthening evidence around interventions designed to address child marriage and related social and behavioral factors.

2. Preventing Violence in, Through and Around Schools

A further Impact Catalyst Fund initiative is being launched in 2026 around Preventing Violence in, Through and Around Schools.

This work is being undertaken in partnership with the Safe to Learn Initiative and focuses on understanding approaches that can prevent violence affecting children in school-related environments.

The consultant may therefore be involved in evaluation activities examining interventions, outcomes and implementation processes related to violence prevention.

3. Power4Girls

The Evaluation Office is also working with UNICEF’s Adolescent Girls Hub on demand-driven impact evaluations under the Power4Girls initiative.

These evaluations focus on increasing girls’:

Agency

Health

Wellbeing

The consultant will support this portfolio and help generate evidence that can inform programs designed to improve outcomes for adolescent girls.

Why This Consultancy Is Important

Violence against children, child marriage and challenges affecting adolescent girls are complex development issues. Effective responses require strong evidence about which interventions work, for whom, under what circumstances and at what cost.

Impact evaluation can help answer these questions.

Through rigorous quantitative and qualitative research, the consultant will contribute to evidence that can potentially influence program design, implementation, resource allocation and policy decisions.

The work is therefore closely connected to UNICEF’s broader mission of promoting the rights, safety and wellbeing of every child.

UNICEF is seeking a highly experienced impact evaluation professional with an advanced academic background and substantial practical experience in rigorous evaluations.

The successful candidate should be comfortable working with both quantitative and qualitative research methods and should have experience dealing with sensitive research involving children and adolescents.

The position requires a combination of academic knowledge, research experience, technical evaluation skills, subject-matter expertise and strong communication abilities.

Selected candidates may also be required to provide additional information to facilitate the background-check process.

Documents Required to Apply

Qualified applicants are required to submit their application through UNICEF’s online Talent Management System (TMS) Here

The application should include the following:

1. Updated TMS Profile and CV

Applicants should ensure that their UNICEF TMS profile is complete and up to date.

The CV should clearly demonstrate:

Academic qualifications

Relevant professional experience

Impact evaluation experience

Research experience

Violence-against-children research experience

Technical software skills

Publications

Relevant language skills

International or low-income-setting experience

2. Cover Letter

Applicants should provide a cover letter explaining their suitability for the consultancy.

A strong cover letter should connect the applicant’s experience directly to the requirements of the position.

Candidates should emphasize their most relevant impact evaluation projects, methodological expertise, research publications and experience involving adolescent girls, violence against children or related themes.

3. Financial Proposal

A separate financial proposal is required.

UNICEF states that the financial proposal must be submitted using the specified template.

Applicants should therefore pay careful attention to the required format and avoid submitting the financial proposal in an alternative format if the official template is available.

Important Note About the Terms of Reference

The vacancy refers applicants to the complete Terms of Reference (TOR) for additional information about the consultancy.

Candidates should review the full TOR before submitting an application because the vacancy announcement may not contain every technical detail relating to the consultancy’s deliverables, methodology, timelines and responsibilities.

The vacancy also provides a financial proposal template that applicants are expected to use.

If the TOR or financial proposal documents cannot be downloaded through certain recruitment platforms, UNICEF advises applicants to visit its official vacancies page.

How to Apply

Applicants interested in the consultancy should:

Review the vacancy and complete Terms of Reference carefully.

Confirm that they meet the Master’s-level education requirement.

Verify that they have more than five years of relevant impact evaluation experience.

Ensure they can demonstrate experience in low-income settings.

Review their experience with violence-against-children research and ethical data collection.

Confirm proficiency in the required quantitative and qualitative analysis tools.

Update their UNICEF TMS profile.

Prepare an up-to-date CV.

Prepare a tailored cover letter.

Complete the required financial proposal template.

Submit all required materials through UNICEF’s online recruitment portal before the deadline.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

13 September 2026, Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).

The position was advertised on 28 August 2026.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications, particularly because the application requires multiple documents, including a separate financial proposal.

For more information visit the UNICEF website HERE

More UNICEF opportunities are on the OFY Website HERE

Important Fraud Warning

UNICEF clearly states that it does not charge a processing fee at any stage of recruitment, selection or hiring.

Applicants should not be asked to pay money for:

Application processing

Interviews

Validation

Appointment

Training

Recruitment

UNICEF also states that it will not ask applicants for their bank account information during the recruitment process.

Applicants should be cautious of individuals or websites falsely claiming to represent UNICEF and requesting payment or sensitive financial information.

Selection Process

As with other UNICEF vacancies, all positions are advertised through the organization’s recruitment system.

Only candidates who are shortlisted will be contacted and advanced to the next stage of the selection process.

Meeting the minimum requirements does not automatically guarantee selection.

Candidates should therefore make sure their applications clearly demonstrate how their education, professional experience, research expertise, technical skills and publications correspond with the consultancy requirements.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This consultancy is particularly suited to experienced professionals working in areas such as:

Impact evaluation

Monitoring and evaluation

Development research

Economics

Public health

Public policy

Political science

Sociology

Development studies

Child protection

Adolescent development

Gender development

Social policy

Research and evidence generation

Violence prevention

Child marriage research

It is not primarily an entry-level opportunity. The requirement for more than five years of professional impact evaluation experience, combined with the advanced degree and technical research requirements, makes this a specialist consultancy aimed at experienced professionals.

How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Applications

Candidates should make their applications evidence-based and directly connected to the vacancy.

When preparing a CV and cover letter, applicants should consider highlighting:

Specific impact evaluations they have led or contributed to

Their role in evaluation design and implementation

Quantitative and qualitative methodologies they have used

Experience collecting primary data

Experience researching violence against children

Experience working with children or adolescents under appropriate ethical protocols

CITI or equivalent human-subject research certification

Experience in low-income settings

Experience with Stata or R

Experience with NVivo or ATLAS.ti

Relevant peer-reviewed publications

Research involving child marriage or social norms

Experience evaluating education or school-based interventions

Experience with adolescent girls’ programs

Cost-effectiveness or economic evaluation experience

Experience communicating technical findings to non-technical audiences

International and multi-stakeholder collaboration

Applicants should avoid relying on generic descriptions of their responsibilities. Instead, they should demonstrate measurable contributions and outcomes wherever possible.

Conclusion

The UNICEF Mixed-Methods Impact Evaluation Consultant – Adolescent Girls & Violence Against Children consultancy offers an opportunity for an experienced evaluation professional to contribute to evidence generation on some of the most important challenges affecting children and adolescent girls.

Through the UNICEF Evaluation Office, the consultant will support impact evaluation activities connected to child marriage and social norms, violence prevention in and around schools, and the Power4Girls portfolio focused on girls’ agency, health and wellbeing. The work will also contribute to the broader development and scoping of impact evaluations involving adolescent girls, violence and child protection.

The position requires a strong combination of academic qualifications, professional impact evaluation experience, quantitative and qualitative research expertise, knowledge of violence against children, ethical research capabilities and strong communication skills. Familiarity with statistical and qualitative analysis software, relevant peer-reviewed publications and experience working in low-income settings are also important.

The consultancy is for 12 months, is primarily remote, and may involve travel to project locations. Interested and qualified professionals should prepare their UNICEF TMS profile, CV, cover letter and financial proposal carefully and submit their applications before the 13 September 2026 deadline.

Applicants should also review the complete Terms of Reference and ensure that every required document is submitted in the correct format.

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Consilium traineeships are now open for applications. Twice a year, the Council offers 5-month paid traineeships in Brussels, providing graduates with the opportunity to gain valuable insights into the work of the European Union and first-hand experience of EU policy-making.

Opportunity: Consilium traineeships

Organisation: Council of the European Union

Location: Brussels, Belgium 🇧🇪

The traineeship programme

The Consilium traineeship programme allows graduates from a range of backgrounds to gain first-hand experience of EU policy-making.

The Council offers traineeships in different areas, such as:

Policy

Law

Administration

Communications

Translation

IT

110 traineeship positions are available each year.

The programme offers an opportunity to gain valuable insights into the work of the European Union, contribute to the Council’s daily activities and learn from colleagues and advisors.

Applications are now open!

Applications are now open for the Consilium traineeships running from 1 February to 30 June 2027.

You can apply until:

📅 15 September 2026, at 12:00 (Brussels time)

APPLY NOW: https://consilium.gestmax.eu/2279/1/paid-traineeship-february-june-2027/en_US

Who can apply?

Consilium traineeships are open to everybody, subject to certain eligibility criteria.

🇪🇺 EU citizenship

🎓 A bachelor’s degree or higher

Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree or higher.

🌍 Language requirements

Applicants must have a very good knowledge of English or French and of at least one other EU language.

💼 Previous EU institutional experience

Applicants must have no previous work experience at another EU institution, subject to the detailed eligibility requirements of the programme.

👉 Who can apply for a traineeship: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/general-secretariat/careers/traineeships/who-can-apply-for-a-traineeship/

What is offered

The Consilium traineeship programme gives young professionals the opportunity to:

Gain insights into the work of the EU

Be involved in the Council’s daily activities

Learn from colleagues and advisors

Contribute to shaping important decisions

Gain practical experience of EU policy-making

Traineeships are paid and include allowances and other benefits.

Positive action programme for trainees with a disability

Traineeships for students from national administration schools

Frequently asked questions

Candidates can consult the Council’s frequently asked questions for more information about the Consilium traineeships, including eligibility, applications and the traineeship programme.

👉 Traineeships: frequently asked questions: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/general-secretariat/careers/traineeships/frequently-asked-questions/

Council rules on traineeships

The Consilium traineeship programme is governed by the Council’s rules on traineeships.

👉 Decision No. 14/25 on traineeships: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/media/5gicvwb1/de00014en25.pdf

Traineeships: frequently asked questions

Answers to the most popular questions regarding traineeships at the Council.

Please find below the most frequently asked questions. You can find the full list of questions and answers in the following document:

Frequently asked questions – traineeships

If you don’t find an answer to your question, you can contact the traineeships office:

traineeships@consilium.europa.eu

Application

Can I do a traineeship during the summer?

No. Traineeships are not offered during the summer.

Traineeships are only possible during the two official periods:

February to June (first period)

September to January (second period)

Are spontaneous applications considered?

No. All applications for a traineeship must follow the application procedure described on the website.

I am a citizen from a candidate country. Can I apply for a traineeship?

No. Traineeships are only open to candidates from candidate countries that have concluded EU accession negotiations. As there are currently no candidate countries that have concluded negotiations, it’s not possible for their citizens to apply.

What proof do I need of EU citizenship?

Applicants must hold a passport or ID card from an EU country. Residence permits are not accepted.

I have not yet received my bachelor’s degree. Can I apply for a paid traineeship?

To be eligible, the candidate must obtain a diploma at bachelor (BA) level or higher by the closing date for applications at the latest.

Can I apply for a traineeship in different EU institutions at the same time?

You can apply for a traineeship at different EU institutions at the same time if you fulfil the eligibility criteria.

Selection procedure

How are trainees selected?

Trainees are selected based on merit, considering the information provided in the application form.

Candidates might be interviewed by telephone or online. In this case the traineeships office will contact candidates beforehand to arrange a suitable time. Where candidates are judged to be of equal merit, the traineeships office endeavours to secure a healthy geographic (i.e. as many nationalities represented as possible) and gender balance (aiming for 40% of the underrepresented gender) of selected trainees. Applications are scrutinised and compared against the profile sought by the various departments of the General Secretariat of the Council.

Do I have to send copies of certificates concerning my language skills?

You do not need to send any certificates at the application stage.

If you are selected for the traineeship, you will need to prove all language skills that you mention in your application form.

If you do not have a specific document (diploma from language studies, copy of evaluation reports including the language or other proof), you will need to write, date and sign a short declaration explaining the circumstances justifying the lack of supporting documents (e.g. a course, your second mother tongue, living in a country, etc.).

After selection

Should I provide translations of supporting documents?

No. Supporting documents are accepted in all official languages of the EU. It is helpful to also provide an English or French version of diplomas, if available.

Do the copies of supporting documents need to be certified as authentic copies of the originals?

No. Supporting documents need to be sent by email. There is no need to provide certified copies. Upon arrival trainees might be asked to present the originals of supporting documents.

During the traineeship

Am I entitled to annual leave?

Trainees are entitled to 2 days leave per worked month, in addition to public holidays and days when Council offices are closed.

Health insurance is mandatory. Is the European health insurance card for my country enough?

Yes. We accept the copy of your European health insurance card as proof. It is your responsibility to check the cover it offers. In the absence of other cover (e.g. European health insurance card), trainees can opt for health insurance through the Council. In this case, paid trainees pay circa €20 per month, which corresponds to one third of the premium, and the Council pays the remaining two thirds.

Are trainees insured?

All trainees benefit from accident insurance.

Financial aspects

How much is the grant?

Presently the grant is €1 538.16 net/month.

Does the Council of the European Union cover the cost of travel from my place of residence to Brussels?

Trainees receive a travel allowance as a contribution towards their travel expenses. Trainees who are recruited from a place more than 50 km from Brussels are entitled to a contribution towards travel expenses at the beginning and at the end of the traineeship.

You must complete at least half of the period of your traineeship in order to be entitled. No requests for change of address will be accepted after the signature of the traineeship agreement by the Council.
