TITLE: Stanford Graduate School of Business Research Fellows Program 2026–27: Research Projects, Eligibility, Requirements and Application Guide

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Stanford Graduate School of Business (Stanford GSB) Research Fellows Program is inviting applications for its Dedicated Research Fellow Track, providing aspiring researchers with the opportunity to work directly with Stanford faculty on advanced research projects across accounting, economics, finance, and organizational behavior.

The program is particularly relevant for candidates interested in academic research, economics, finance, accounting, data analysis, public policy, quantitative social science, computational research, and future PhD study.

The application for the Research Fellows Program opens on Thursday, September 3, 2026. Applicants interested in the Dedicated Track can explore the available projects and select up to three projects of interest as part of their application.

About the Stanford GSB Research Fellows Program

The Stanford Graduate School of Business Research Fellows Program provides opportunities for researchers to gain practical experience working on faculty-led research at Stanford.

The Dedicated Research Fellow Track allows fellows to work more closely with a particular faculty member or research project. The projects are organized according to their primary field, although Stanford notes that many projects are multidisciplinary.

The currently listed fields include:

Accounting

Economic Analysis & Policy

Finance

Organizational Behavior

Applicants are encouraged to explore projects outside their primary field where appropriate, particularly because several projects combine concepts and methods from multiple academic disciplines.

What Is the Dedicated Research Fellow Track?

The Dedicated Track is designed for applicants who want to work intensively on a specific research area.

When applying, candidates can:

Select the Dedicated Research Fellow Track.

Review the available research projects.

Choose up to three projects of interest.

Indicate their research interests and relevant skills.

Potentially work directly with Stanford faculty, PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and other members of the research community.

The projects have different requirements. Some emphasize economics and econometrics, while others involve programming, data management, experiments, literature reviews, financial research, or computational modeling.

Available Dedicated Research Fellow Projects

1. Stanford Tax Lab (STAX): Accounting

Faculty: Rebecca Lester

Field: Accounting

Status: Open

Rebecca Lester, Associate Professor of Accounting at Stanford Graduate School of Business, is seeking predoctoral research fellows to conduct accounting research through the Stanford Tax Lab (STAX).

Fellows will work directly with Professor Lester in a collaborative research environment involving postdoctoral researchers and PhD students in accounting and economics.

The Stanford Tax Lab examines a broad range of taxation issues at international, federal, state, and local levels.

Potential Research Topics

Research may cover:

Complex multinational corporate structures

International taxation

Cross-border income shifting

Tax competition between countries

State and local tax policy in the United States

R&D tax incentives

Innovation and economic growth

The emerging fiscal impacts of artificial intelligence adoption

How firms respond to tax-policy changes

How governments respond to taxation policies across jurisdictions

The project is therefore relevant to applicants interested in taxation, accounting, economics, public policy, business behavior, innovation, and technology.

Research Activities and Tools

The fellow’s work may involve:

Detailed empirical analysis

Literature reviews

Theoretical modeling

Analysis of tax policies

Examination of firm behavior

Data analysis

Stata

Claude Code

GitHub

Requirements

A background in public economics or accounting is not required, although it would be helpful.

The project particularly seeks candidates who are curious about how fiscal policy shapes firm behavior.

This means candidates without a traditional accounting background may still be considered if they demonstrate strong research interest and relevant analytical abilities.

2. Stanford Tax Lab (STAX): Economics

Faculty: Juan Carlos Suárez Serrato

Field: Economic Analysis & Policy

Status: Open

Juan Carlos Suárez Serrato, the Edward B. Rust Professor of Economics, is seeking predoctoral research fellows to conduct economics research through the Stanford Tax Lab.

The fellow will work in a collaborative environment involving postdoctoral researchers and PhD students in economics and accounting.

The research examines taxation at international, federal, and local levels and explores how tax policies influence businesses, workers, governments, and economic activity.

Potential Research Topics

Possible areas of research include:

Complex multinational corporate structures

International tax policy

Environmental regulations

The economic impact of environmental regulations

R&D tax incentives

Administration of fiscal policy in developing countries

Labor-market effects of business taxes

Business incentives

Economic consequences of government policy

The project could be especially relevant to applicants interested in public economics, development economics, labor economics, taxation, international economics, and public policy.

Data and Research Methods

The work may involve:

Empirical economic research

Literature reviews

Structural modeling

Analysis of large administrative datasets

Economic policy analysis

Quantitative research

Some projects could involve large administrative datasets from the U.S. Census and Internal Revenue Service.

3. Empirical Market Design for Transforming Marketplaces

Faculty: Shoshana Vasserman

Field: Economic Analysis & Policy

Status: Open

Shoshana Vasserman, Associate Professor of Economics, is seeking a predoctoral research fellow to contribute to ongoing research examining the empirical evaluation and design of policies that transform marketplaces.

Technology is changing how traditional markets operate, while also providing market designers with new tools for improving market outcomes.

The research explores how these changes can be understood and addressed using empirical and computational methods.

Possible Research Topics

Projects may include research on:

Congestion pricing for road use

Supply and demand frictions

Homeowners’ insurance

Natural-disaster risk

Technology and changing marketplaces

Policy design

Market efficiency

Expected Research Activities

The fellow may contribute to several areas of empirical research, including:

Data management

Data cleaning and munging

Data visualization

Simulation

Basic econometrics

Empirical policy evaluation

Depending on the fellow’s interests, there may also be opportunities to learn and apply more advanced computational techniques and economic theory.

This project could be particularly suitable for applicants interested in economics, data science, policy analysis, market design, technology, and quantitative research.

4. Global Capital Allocation Project

Faculty: Matteo Maggiori

Field: Finance

Status: Open

Matteo Maggiori, the Moghadam Family Professor and Professor of Finance, is seeking a predoctoral research fellow to join the Global Capital Allocation Project (GCAP) Lab.

The GCAP combines data, economic theory, and analytics to understand how capital moves around the world and how international financial activity affects economic policy.

Current Research Areas

Current projects include:

Mapping how global firms finance themselves through foreign subsidiaries

Understanding capital allocation and financial integration in the Eurozone

Examining China’s growing presence in global financial markets

Studying the relationship between geopolitics and economic statecraft

Analyzing international capital flows

Understanding global financial integration

Studying international macroeconomic and financial issues

The research has potential implications for international economic policy and may attract media attention.

Research Environment

The position provides opportunities to collaborate with:

Stanford faculty

PhD students

Fellow researchers

The fellow may also have opportunities to:

Present research findings

Gain advanced research training

Work with large datasets

Apply quantitative methods

Contribute to research with international policy implications

Requirements

Applications are welcomed from candidates with:

A strong quantitative background

Excellent programming skills

A passion for economic research

Importantly, prior economics experience is not required.

This makes the project potentially attractive to candidates from quantitative disciplines who want to transition into economics and international finance research.

5. Dedicated Research Fellow Position in Finance

Faculty: Vikrant Vig

Field: Finance

Status: Open

Vikrant Vig, the William R. Timken Professor and Professor of Finance at Stanford Graduate School of Business and a senior fellow at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research (SIEPR), is seeking a predoctoral research fellow.

The research focuses on asset quality, pricing, and reallocation over the business cycle.

Current Research Areas

Current work includes:

Asset quality

Asset pricing

Asset reallocation

Business-cycle research

Recession-period quality loss

Transaction-level data

Effective-age estimation

Recession-period price discounts

Industry distress

Financial regulation

One current research project uses transaction-level post-sale flying-hour measures to study quality loss and asset reallocation during recessions.

Another project develops Delta-method standard errors for effective-age estimation.

The research also examines recession-period price discounts using alternative recession definitions and continuous measures of industry distress.

Fellow Responsibilities

The fellow will assist with:

Construction of transaction-level datasets

Analysis of transaction-level data

Empirical research

Econometric analysis

Financial research

Research related to financial regulation

Other related research projects

This position may be particularly suitable for candidates interested in finance, econometrics, financial markets, asset pricing, empirical research, and financial regulation.

6. Models and Empirical Studies in Cultural Evolution

Faculty: Helena Miton

Field: Organizational Behavior

Status: Open

Helena Miton, Assistant Professor of Organizational Behavior, is seeking a predoctoral research fellow to work on research examining cultural evolution.

In this research context, cultural evolution refers to how information changes as it is transmitted from one person to another and across generations.

The project combines organizational behavior with experimental research, statistics, data analysis, and computational modeling.

Potential Research Activities

Depending on the fellow’s interests, activities may include:

Re-analyzing published experiments

Designing new experiments

Running experiments

Collecting research data

Building computational models

Extending existing computational models

Comparing model predictions with real-world cases

Collecting and cleaning large datasets

Conducting statistical analyses

Synthesizing academic literature

Producing clear figures and tables

Writing reproducible code

Testing research code

Requirements

Applicants are expected to have some background in:

Statistics

Data analysis

R

Python

Prior exposure to mathematical or computational modeling is considered a plus but is not required.

The project could therefore be particularly relevant to candidates with backgrounds in statistics, data science, psychology, organizational behavior, computational social science, or related fields.

Fields Without Current Dedicated Positions

Stanford GSB states that dedicated positions are not currently being offered in:

Marketing

Operations, Information & Technology (OIT)

Political Economy

However, Stanford notes that additional projects may be added as they become available.

Applicants interested in these areas should continue checking the program for future updates.

Stanford Research Fellows Standard Track

Applicants who do not find a suitable Dedicated Track project can consider the Standard Track.

The Standard Track follows a rotational model, allowing fellows to rotate between projects with different faculty members each quarter.

Rotations depend on:

Project availability

Applicant interests

Available faculty research opportunities

The Standard Track may be particularly useful for candidates who want to gain exposure to multiple areas before specializing in a particular field.

It can also be an alternative for applicants whose preferred research field does not currently have an available Dedicated Track position.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Stanford GSB Research Fellows Program may be suitable for candidates interested in:

Academic research

Economics

Accounting

Finance

Organizational behavior

Public policy

Data analysis

Econometrics

Quantitative social science

Computational social science

International economics

Taxation

Financial regulation

Market design

Business research

Experimental research

Computational modeling

Because each research project has its own requirements, applicants should evaluate the individual project descriptions carefully.

For example, candidates with strong programming and quantitative skills may be particularly interested in the Global Capital Allocation Project.

Applicants with statistics and R or Python experience may find the Cultural Evolution project relevant.

Candidates interested in taxation and public policy may consider either of the Stanford Tax Lab projects.

How to Apply

Applicants interested in the Dedicated Research Fellow Track should take the following steps.

Step 1: Explore the Projects

Review all available projects rather than looking only at the field that matches your degree.

Many of the projects are multidisciplinary.

Step 2: Identify Your Research Interests

Consider the research questions that genuinely interest you and identify the projects that align most closely with your academic and professional goals.

Step 3: Compare Your Qualifications

Review the requirements for each project and determine whether your background matches the skills being requested.

Relevant skills may include:

Statistics

Programming

Data analysis

Econometrics

Research methods

Literature review

Economic theory

Computational modeling

Financial analysis

Step 4: Select Up to Three Projects

Applicants to the Dedicated Track can select up to three projects of interest.

It is advisable to prioritize projects where your academic background, technical skills, and research interests demonstrate a strong match.

Step 5: Prepare Your Application

Your application should clearly explain your research interests and demonstrate how your academic background, technical abilities, previous experience, and career objectives align with the projects you have selected.

Step 6: Submit the Application

The application opens on Thursday, September 3, 2026.

Applicants should consult the official Stanford GSB application page here for the complete application requirements and current closing date.

Application Deadline

Application opening date: Thursday, September 3, 2026.

The information supplied for the program does not state a specific application closing deadline.

Applicants should therefore verify the current deadline directly through Stanford Graduate School of Business before submitting their applications.

Important Things to Know Before Applying

1. The projects are multidisciplinary

Stanford encourages applicants to consider projects outside their primary academic discipline.

A project listed under economics, for example, may require programming, data analysis, policy knowledge, or other interdisciplinary skills.

2. Requirements differ by project

There is no single set of technical requirements for every position.

Some projects prioritize quantitative skills, while others emphasize research experience, statistics, programming, experiments, or economic theory.

3. Prior subject-specific experience is not always required

For example, the STAX Accounting project states that a background in public economics or accounting is not required.

The Global Capital Allocation Project also welcomes candidates with strong quantitative and programming skills with or without prior economics experience.

4. Programming and data skills can be valuable

Several projects involve programming and quantitative research.

Relevant tools and technologies mentioned include:

Stata

Python

R

GitHub

Claude Code

Applicants should emphasize relevant technical skills in their applications where applicable.

5. Fellows participate in active research

The projects involve genuine faculty-led research rather than simply classroom-based study.

Depending on the project, fellows may collaborate with professors, PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and other researchers.

6. The Standard Track provides another option

If none of the Dedicated Track projects matches your interests, the Standard Track provides the opportunity to rotate between different research projects.

Benefits of Participating in the Research Fellows Program

Although the supplied information does not describe a specific scholarship or financial package, the research experience itself can provide significant professional and academic value.

Depending on the project, fellows may gain experience in:

Faculty-led academic research

Empirical research

Data analysis

Econometrics

Programming

Computational modeling

Experimental research

Literature reviews

Economic theory

Policy analysis

Financial research

Data visualization

Reproducible research

Research presentations

Working with large datasets

The experience can be especially useful for individuals considering future graduate study or research-focused careers.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Stanford GSB Research Fellows Program?

It is a research program that provides fellows with opportunities to work on faculty-led research projects at Stanford Graduate School of Business.

When does the application open?

The 2026 application opens on Thursday, September 3, 2026.

How many projects can I select?

Applicants to the Dedicated Track can select up to three projects of interest.

Which fields currently have open Dedicated Track projects?

The supplied information lists open projects in Accounting, Economic Analysis & Policy, Finance, and Organizational Behavior.

Are there currently Dedicated Track positions in Marketing?

No. Stanford states that dedicated positions in Marketing are not currently being offered.

Are there currently Dedicated Track positions in OIT?

No. Stanford states that dedicated positions in Operations, Information & Technology are not currently being offered.

Are there Dedicated Track positions in Political Economy?

No. Stanford states that there are currently no dedicated positions in Political Economy.

Do I need an economics degree?

Not necessarily.

Requirements vary by project. For example, the Global Capital Allocation Project welcomes applicants with strong quantitative and programming skills with or without prior economics experience.

Is accounting experience mandatory for the STAX Accounting project?

No.

Stanford states that a background in public economics or accounting is not required, although it would be helpful.

Do I need mathematical modeling experience for the Cultural Evolution project?

No.

Prior exposure to mathematical or computational modeling is considered a plus but is not required. Some background in statistics or data analysis using R or Python is expected.

Can international applicants apply?

The supplied program information does not identify a nationality-based restriction. Applicants from different countries should review the official Stanford application information and any applicable eligibility, employment, or immigration requirements.

Conclusion

The Stanford Graduate School of Business Research Fellows Program offers an excellent opportunity for aspiring researchers to gain hands-on experience through faculty-led research at Stanford.

The Dedicated Research Fellow Track currently features projects covering taxation, accounting, economics, market design, international finance, asset pricing, financial regulation, organizational behavior, cultural evolution, data analysis, and computational research.

One of the major strengths of the program is the variety of research opportunities available. Candidates with accounting or public-policy interests can explore the Stanford Tax Lab, while applicants with strong quantitative and programming skills may be interested in the Global Capital Allocation Project. Those interested in market design can consider Shoshana Vasserman’s project, while candidates with statistics, R, or Python experience may find the Cultural Evolution project particularly relevant.

Applicants can select up to three projects of interest when applying to the Dedicated Track. Candidates who prefer broader research exposure can instead explore the Standard Track, which allows researchers to rotate between projects with different faculty members each quarter.

The application opens on September 3, 2026. Because the supplied announcement does not provide a closing deadline, applicants should confirm the latest deadline and complete application requirements through Stanford GSB before applying.

Official program information is available through the Stanford Graduate School of Business Research Fellows Program website.

TITLE: UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge 2026: Submit Your Frontier Technology Solution and Present at the Global Supply Chain Forum in Saudi Arabia

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge 2026 is now accepting proposals from innovators around the world with ideas for using frontier technologies to build more sustainable, resilient, efficient and inclusive global supply chains.

Organized as an integral part of the Second United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) Global Supply Chain Forum (GSCF), the challenge provides individuals and teams with an international platform to propose practical and innovative solutions to some of the most pressing disruptions affecting supply chains worldwide.

The UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum 2026 will take place in Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, from 29 November to 1 December 2026.

Building on the inaugural Supply Chain Innovation Challenge held during the first Global Supply Chain Forum in Barbados in 2024, the second edition seeks original proposals demonstrating how frontier technologies can help countries, businesses and communities anticipate, withstand and recover from current and emerging supply chain disruptions.

The winning proposal will be presented at the Second UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum in Saudi Arabia, with travel and accommodation expenses covered.

The deadline to submit a proposal is 4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2).

About the UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge 2026

Global supply chains are essential to international trade, food security, economic development and the movement of goods and services around the world. However, recent years have demonstrated how vulnerable supply networks can be to unexpected shocks and long-term structural challenges.

The Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge seeks ideas capable of responding to these challenges through technology-driven innovation.

This year’s challenge focuses specifically on the potential of frontier technologies to improve the ability of supply chains to anticipate disruption, withstand shocks and recover effectively.

Successful proposals should consider how technological innovation can contribute to supply chains that are:

More sustainable;

More resilient;

More efficient;

More inclusive;

Better prepared for future disruptions; and

Practically applicable in real-world supply chain environments.

Rather than focusing only on theoretical concepts, UNCTAD is looking for proposals that demonstrate how innovative ideas could work in practice and create meaningful improvements across supply chains.

What Is the UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum?

The Global Supply Chain Forum is an international UNCTAD platform focused on the challenges, opportunities and transformations shaping global supply chains.

The second edition of the forum will be held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, from 29 November to 1 December 2026.

The 2026 Supply Chain Innovation Challenge forms an integral part of this international forum, giving innovators an opportunity to contribute practical solutions to the broader global discussion surrounding resilient and sustainable supply chains.

The challenge follows the success of the first Supply Chain Innovation Challenge held during the inaugural Global Supply Chain Forum in Barbados in 2024.

The winning proposal from the 2026 challenge will have the opportunity to reach an international audience through presentation at the forum.

Focus of the Second Supply Chain Innovation Challenge

The central focus of the challenge is:

How can frontier technologies help anticipate, withstand and recover from global supply chain disruptions while making supply chains more sustainable, resilient, efficient and inclusive?

Applicants are encouraged to think beyond conventional approaches and demonstrate how emerging and frontier technologies could address existing problems or prepare supply chains for challenges likely to emerge in the coming years.

Proposals should combine innovation with practical implementation.

UNCTAD particularly emphasizes solutions that demonstrate a commitment to:

Sustainability;

Inclusivity;

Resilience;

Practical applicability; and

Real-world impact.

Priority Areas for Proposals

Applicants are welcome to propose solutions addressing a wide range of supply chain challenges.

However, UNCTAD particularly encourages proposals addressing the following areas.

1. Making Supply Chains Greener

Applicants may explore how frontier technologies can reduce the environmental impact of supply chains and contribute to more sustainable trade and logistics systems.

Solutions could consider challenges associated with transportation, logistics, resource efficiency, environmental monitoring or other aspects of sustainable supply chain management.

The fundamental objective should be to demonstrate how innovation can contribute to greener supply chains while remaining practical and scalable.

2. Ensuring Food Security Through Resilient Supply Chains

Food supply chains can be particularly vulnerable to disruptions, making resilience critical to ensuring that food reaches communities reliably and efficiently.

Applicants may propose innovative technological solutions capable of strengthening food-related supply chains, improving their resilience or helping stakeholders anticipate and respond to disruptions.

Solutions should demonstrate how technology can contribute to reliable, resilient and sustainable supply systems.

3. Streamlining Cross-Border Procedures in Supply Chains

International supply chains frequently involve multiple jurisdictions, procedures and stakeholders.

The challenge therefore encourages solutions that explore how frontier technologies can make cross-border supply chain processes more efficient and resilient.

Applicants may consider innovative approaches that improve processes associated with international movement, coordination or supply chain management.

Importantly, applicants are not restricted to these three areas.

Innovative proposals addressing other relevant supply chain disruptions are also eligible, provided they align with the overall objectives of the challenge.

What Applicants Must Submit

Participants must submit an original proposal written in English.

The proposal should be between 1,500 and 3,000 words maximum, including the bibliography and footnotes.

Applicants should ensure their submission clearly explains both the challenge they are addressing and how their proposed technological solution could address it.

UNCTAD specifies four core components that should be included.

1. A Clear Problem Statement

Applicants should begin by clearly identifying the supply chain problem or disruption they intend to address.

The problem statement should provide enough context to explain:

What the problem is;

Why it matters;

Who or what is affected;

How it affects supply chain resilience, efficiency, sustainability or inclusion; and

Why an innovative solution is needed.

A well-defined problem statement provides the foundation for the remainder of the proposal.

2. Detailed Description of the Innovative Solution

Applicants must explain the solution they are proposing.

The proposal should demonstrate how frontier technology can be applied to prepare for, counter or respond to supply chain disruptions.

The description should be sufficiently detailed to allow evaluators to understand how the proposed solution would work and what makes it innovative.

3. Anticipated Impact

Applicants should explain the expected impact of their solution.

The proposal should demonstrate how the innovation could contribute to stronger supply chains and what improvements could reasonably result from its implementation.

Applicants should consider the broader objectives of creating supply chains that are sustainable, inclusive, resilient and effective in real-world environments.

4. Feasibility Assessment

Innovation alone is not enough. Applicants must also demonstrate that their proposed solution has practical applicability.

The feasibility assessment should explain why and how the idea could realistically be implemented.

This is particularly important because feasibility is one of the official criteria that will be used to assess proposals.

Proposal Length and Language Requirements

Applicants should carefully follow the submission requirements.

The proposal must:

Be an original submission;

Be written in English;

Contain between 1,500 and 3,000 words maximum;

Include the bibliography and footnotes within the stated word limit;

Present a clear supply chain problem;

Explain an innovative frontier technology solution;

Discuss anticipated impact; and

Demonstrate practical feasibility.

Applicants should review their final submission carefully before submitting it to ensure it complies with these requirements.

Who Can Apply for the UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge?

The challenge is open to natural persons, meaning individual people rather than organizations or legal entities.

Applicants may participate individually or form a team.

Teams may consist of up to four people.

If a team is selected as the winner, one member of the team will represent the group in Saudi Arabia.

This is an important consideration for teams preparing their applications, particularly when deciding who may be available to participate in the Global Supply Chain Forum if selected.

International Eligibility

The call invites innovators from around the world to propose solutions.

The information provided for the challenge does not specify a particular nationality, region or continent to which applicants must belong.

This gives the competition an international scope and allows innovators from different backgrounds and geographic regions to contribute ideas addressing global supply chain challenges.

Applicants should nevertheless carefully review the official application form and any associated terms before submission for any additional requirements.

Evaluation Criteria

Proposals submitted to the Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge will be assessed according to five major criteria:

Innovation

Evaluators will consider the originality and innovative qualities of the proposed solution.

Applicants should demonstrate what makes their idea distinctive and how frontier technology provides a meaningful approach to the supply chain challenge identified.

Feasibility

Proposals should demonstrate that the solution can realistically be implemented.

A highly innovative concept should therefore be accompanied by a credible explanation of how it could work in practice.

Scalability

Evaluators will consider the potential for the proposed solution to expand or be applied more broadly.

Applicants should think about whether their innovation could move beyond a limited pilot or local application and potentially address supply chain challenges on a larger scale.

Sustainability

Sustainability is a core theme of the challenge.

Applicants should demonstrate how their proposed solution contributes to sustainable supply chain development and avoids treating sustainability as an afterthought.

Resilience

Proposals should show how the innovation can help supply chains prepare for, withstand or recover from disruption.

Resilience should therefore be integrated into the fundamental design and expected impact of the solution.

What Does the Winner Receive?

One of the most significant opportunities offered through the challenge is the chance for the winning proposal to be presented at the Second UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

The forum will take place from 29 November to 1 December 2026.

For the winning proposal, travel and accommodation expenses will be covered.

For team submissions, only one team member will represent the group in Saudi Arabia if the proposal is selected.

Beyond the covered travel and accommodation, presenting at the Global Supply Chain Forum provides the winner with an international platform for showcasing an innovative solution addressing major global supply chain challenges.

Why Consider Applying?

The UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge provides an opportunity for innovators to move their ideas into an international policy and supply chain discussion.

Potential reasons to consider participating include:

Presenting an innovative solution on an international platform;

Contributing ideas addressing major global supply chain challenges;

Exploring the potential of frontier technologies in trade and supply chains;

Demonstrating solutions focused on sustainability and resilience;

Showcasing an idea at the UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum;

Engaging with a challenge organized within a United Nations forum; and

Receiving covered travel and accommodation if selected to present the winning proposal in Riyadh.

The challenge may be particularly relevant to people working on ideas at the intersection of technology, international trade, logistics, sustainability, food systems, resilience and cross-border processes.

How to Strengthen Your Proposal

Because proposals will be evaluated on innovation, feasibility, scalability, sustainability and resilience, applicants should ensure these qualities are clearly visible throughout their submission.

A strong proposal should not simply describe an interesting technology.

Instead, it should establish a logical connection between:

Supply chain problem → frontier technology solution → practical implementation → measurable impact.

Applicants should clearly explain why their chosen technology is appropriate for the identified problem and why the proposed approach represents an improvement over existing practices.

The feasibility section should also receive significant attention. Applicants should avoid presenting a solution that is technically impressive but difficult to implement in realistic supply chain environments.

Similarly, applicants should consider scalability from the beginning. A solution designed for a particular location or sector may still demonstrate how the underlying approach could potentially be adapted or expanded elsewhere.

Finally, sustainability, inclusivity and resilience should be integrated throughout the proposal rather than addressed only briefly at the end.

Important Dates

Applicants should take note of the following dates:

Proposal submission deadline: 4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2)

Second UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum: 29 November–1 December 2026

Forum location: Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

Applicants are strongly encouraged not to wait until the final hours before submitting their proposals.

Submission Deadline

The official deadline for the Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge is:

4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2).

Applications submitted after the deadline may not be considered, so prospective participants should prepare and submit their proposals as early as possible.

Applicants in other time zones should carefully convert the deadline to their local time to avoid missing the submission window.

How to Apply

Interested participants should complete the official application process and submit their proposal through the designated application form.

Before submitting, applicants should ensure that their proposal:

Is original;

Is written in English;

Meets the 1,500–3,000-word requirement, including bibliography and footnotes;

Contains a clear problem statement;

Provides a detailed explanation of the innovative solution;

Explains the anticipated impact;

Includes a feasibility assessment;

Demonstrates sustainability and inclusivity;

Addresses practical application in real-world supply chain settings; and

Is submitted before 4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2).

Applicants should use the official UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge application form to complete their submission.

APPLY NOW

Questions and Further Information

Applicants who have questions about the challenge can contact the organizers at:

gscf@unctad.org

Prospective participants should also consult the official UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum information for updates and further details relating to the forum and challenge.

Conclusion

The Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge 2026 offers innovators worldwide an opportunity to contribute practical technology-driven ideas to one of the most important challenges facing international trade: creating global supply chains capable of anticipating, withstanding and recovering from disruption.

With a strong emphasis on frontier technologies, sustainability, inclusivity, feasibility, scalability and resilience, the challenge is seeking more than theoretical concepts. It is looking for innovative proposals with genuine potential for real-world application.

Individuals can apply independently, while teams of up to four people are also eligible to participate. Applicants must submit an original English-language proposal of between 1,500 and 3,000 words, including bibliography and footnotes.

The winning proposal will be presented at the Second UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, from 29 November to 1 December 2026, with travel and accommodation expenses covered.

Innovators with ideas for greener supply chains, resilient food systems, streamlined cross-border procedures or other technology-enabled approaches to global supply chain disruption are encouraged to consider applying.

Applications must be submitted by 4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2).

Visit the OFY website for more opportunities on global competitions.

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Department of Quantitative Biomedicine at the University of Zurich (UZH) is inviting applications for a PhD position focused on Medical Imaging AI, offering an opportunity for researchers interested in artificial intelligence, computer vision, medical image computing and clinically relevant machine learning research.

The PhD position is jointly affiliated with the University of Zurich (UZH) and the University Hospital Zurich (USZ), with the possibility of an additional affiliation with the ETH AI Center for an appropriate candidate. The research will also be conducted in active collaboration with the AWS for Healthcare team, giving the successful candidate an opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced AI research, medical imaging and real-world healthcare applications.

The position is particularly relevant to candidates with academic backgrounds in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering or closely related disciplines who have a strong interest in medical applications of artificial intelligence and are motivated to develop and scale AI algorithms through the AWS ecosystem.

Host Institutions and Research Environment

The position is hosted by the Department of Quantitative Biomedicine at the University of Zurich and is jointly affiliated with the University Hospital Zurich. The research environment also has strong connections to ETH Zurich, with the possibility for a suitable candidate to affiliate with the ETH AI Center.

A distinctive feature of this opportunity is the collaboration with the AWS for Healthcare team. Rather than focusing solely on theoretical or laboratory-based research, the PhD will combine methodological research with direct clinical relevance and opportunities to translate research outcomes into practical algorithms and applications.

This makes the position particularly attractive for researchers who want to develop expertise not only in artificial intelligence and medical imaging but also in the transition of research innovations into real-world healthcare technology.

Research Areas for the PhD

The PhD position focuses on several interconnected areas of medical imaging artificial intelligence. Applicants should be prepared to engage with advanced computational methods and their application to medical data.

1. Vision-Language Modeling for 3D Medical Imaging

One of the central research directions is vision-language modeling (VLM) for three-dimensional medical imaging.

Vision-language models seek to connect visual information with language-based information. In the context of medical imaging, this can involve developing AI systems capable of understanding complex medical images and relating their visual content to textual descriptions, clinical findings or other forms of medical knowledge.

The position specifically highlights work involving 3D medical imaging, including research associated with CT imaging and the CT-RATE dataset.

This research area has significant potential applications in medical image interpretation, automated reporting, clinical decision support and multimodal healthcare AI.

2. Image Segmentation

Another major research focus is medical image segmentation.

Image segmentation involves identifying and delineating specific structures, organs, tissues, lesions or other clinically relevant regions within medical images.

For a PhD researcher, this area may involve developing machine learning and deep learning approaches that can accurately identify structures within complex medical images and improve the reliability of automated medical image analysis.

The position references research including CADS and vesselFM as part of its segmentation and visual grounding focus.

3. Visual Grounding

The PhD will also address visual grounding, an area concerned with linking language or semantic descriptions to specific regions or objects within visual data.

In medical imaging, visual grounding can contribute to AI systems that do more than simply classify an image. Such systems can potentially identify and associate particular anatomical structures or abnormalities with corresponding clinical concepts or descriptions.

This creates an important connection between computer vision, natural language processing and medical image understanding.

4. Clinical Validation

The research will not stop at developing AI models.

A major component of the position is clinical validation, meaning that developed approaches will need to be assessed for their usefulness and performance in medically relevant settings.

This clinical orientation is one of the defining features of the opportunity. The research will combine methods-driven artificial intelligence research with direct clinical relevance through the UZH and University Hospital Zurich environment.

5. Benchmarking and Public Challenges

The PhD researcher will also have the opportunity to participate in public benchmarking initiatives.

Benchmarking allows researchers to compare AI systems using common datasets, evaluation procedures and performance measures. It can help determine whether a proposed method provides meaningful improvements over existing approaches.

The position specifically references initiatives including VLM3D and BRATS.

Participation in such initiatives can also help researchers build an international research profile and contribute to the broader medical AI research community.

What the PhD Position Offers

The University of Zurich’s opportunity provides an interdisciplinary research environment combining academic research, healthcare and industry collaboration.

According to the official position announcement, successful candidates can benefit from several important opportunities.

1. Research at the Intersection of AI and Medicine

The position combines advanced computational and AI methods with direct clinical applications.

This means the PhD researcher will have the opportunity to investigate sophisticated artificial intelligence methods while considering how those methods can address real healthcare and medical imaging challenges.

2. Affiliation with Leading Swiss Research Institutions

The position is based at UZH and USZ and has strong ties to ETH Zurich.

For an appropriate candidate, there is also the possibility of affiliation with the ETH AI Center, providing an additional connection to Switzerland’s highly developed artificial intelligence research ecosystem.

3. Collaboration with AWS for Healthcare

The successful researcher will work closely with the AWS for Healthcare team and participate in joint activities.

This provides exposure to an industry environment alongside academic and clinical research.

For candidates interested in developing AI systems that can eventually operate at scale, this industry connection may be particularly valuable.

4. Translating Research into Real-World Applications

The PhD offers an opportunity to contribute to the translation of research into real-world algorithms and applications within the AWS ecosystem.

This practical orientation can help bridge the gap between academic research and technology implementation.

5. Access to Clinical Collaborators

The position provides access to clinical collaborators, enabling researchers to work in an environment where medical expertise can inform the development and evaluation of AI systems.

This is especially important in medical AI because successful models need to address real clinical requirements rather than simply perform well on technical datasets.

6. Curated Medical Datasets

The researcher will have access to curated datasets relevant to medical imaging research.

High-quality datasets are essential for developing, training and evaluating machine learning systems, particularly in specialized areas such as 3D medical imaging.

7. Modern Computing Infrastructure

The position also provides access to modern computational infrastructure, including AWS cloud computing resources.

This can be important for computationally intensive research involving large medical imaging datasets and advanced AI models.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The position is aimed at candidates with a strong technical and research background relevant to artificial intelligence and medical image computing.

The official announcement identifies the following candidate profile.

Academic Background

Applicants should have a degree in:

Computer Science

Physics

Mathematics

Engineering

Or a closely related field

The position is therefore particularly suited to graduates whose academic training provides a strong foundation in quantitative, computational or technical research.

Interest in the Medical Domain

An intrinsic interest in the medical domain is required.

The university indicates that this interest should ideally be demonstrated through previous academic work, such as a related Master’s thesis or research project.

Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate more than a general interest in artificial intelligence. A convincing application should explain why the applicant is interested in applying AI and computational methods to healthcare and medical imaging.

Interest in AWS and Scalable AI

Applicants are also expected to have a genuine interest in working with AWS to establish and scale algorithms and applications through the AWS ecosystem.

Candidates should therefore consider highlighting any relevant experience or interest in areas such as:

Machine learning

Deep learning

Computer vision

Medical image analysis

Cloud computing

Artificial intelligence

Data science

Algorithm development

Research software

Scalable computing systems

Who Can Apply?

The official announcement does not specify a particular nationality, race, ethnicity or continent restriction. The listed eligibility requirements focus primarily on academic background, interest in medical research and motivation to work with AWS.

Therefore, based on the published criteria, the opportunity can be considered open to qualified applicants internationally rather than being restricted to applicants from a particular country or continent.

Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions may be considered provided they satisfy the academic and research requirements. The announcement does not identify a nationality or racial restriction.

However, applicants should rely on the official university announcement for any additional admission, immigration, employment or doctoral-registration requirements that may apply during the application or enrollment process.

Application Requirements

Interested candidates are required to submit three key documents.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants should submit an updated CV highlighting their academic background, research experience, technical skills, projects, publications and other experience relevant to medical AI and computational research.

Where applicable, candidates should emphasize experience with:

Artificial intelligence

Machine learning

Deep learning

Computer vision

Medical imaging

Image segmentation

Natural language processing

Vision-language models

Data science

Programming

Cloud computing

Research projects

Scientific publications

2. Transcript of Records

Applicants must provide their transcript of records.

The transcript helps demonstrate the candidate’s academic preparation and performance.

Candidates should ensure that the submitted transcript is clear and readable and adequately reflects their relevant academic coursework.

3. Brief Statement of Motivation

Applicants must also submit a brief statement of motivation.

This document should explain why the candidate is interested in the PhD position and why their academic and research background makes them suitable for the project.

A strong motivation statement should connect three major elements:

Your academic and technical background

Your interest in medical imaging and AI

Your motivation to work with UZH, USZ and AWS

Rather than simply stating that you are interested in artificial intelligence, the statement should demonstrate how your previous studies, research projects or technical experience have prepared you for the proposed research area.

How to Apply

Applications should be sent directly by email to:

bjoern.menze@uzh.ch

Applicants should include:

CV

Transcript of records

Brief statement of motivation

The email subject line should clearly state:

“PhD Position UZH-AWS”

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The official UZH webpage currently states the deadline as 31 September 2026.

However, September has only 30 days, meaning 31 September is not a valid calendar date. In addition, a recent post by the research group supervisor, Prof. Bjoern Menze, has publicly indicated 30 September 2026 as the deadline.

Applicants should therefore treat 30 September 2026 as the likely intended deadline and, importantly, confirm the deadline directly with UZH before submitting.

Because the official university webpage itself contains the apparent date error, applicants should avoid waiting until the final day and should submit their applications as early as possible.

How to Make Your Application Competitive

This is a specialized PhD opportunity, so applicants should carefully demonstrate their suitability rather than submitting a generic doctoral application.

1. Demonstrate Technical Preparation

Show evidence of your ability to work with quantitative and computational research.

Relevant coursework, research projects, programming experience and technical projects can strengthen your application.

2. Connect Your Experience to Medical Imaging

If you have previously worked on medical imaging, biomedical engineering, healthcare AI, computer vision or related research, make this connection explicit.

If your background is primarily in computer science or another technical discipline, explain clearly how you intend to apply your existing expertise to medical research.

3. Explain Your Interest in AI for Healthcare

The project is not simply an AI research position. It is specifically concerned with medical imaging AI.

Your motivation statement should therefore explain why you want to work on healthcare applications and what makes this research area particularly meaningful to you.

4. Highlight Research Experience

Where applicable, mention:

Master’s research

Research assistant positions

Academic publications

Conference presentations

Machine learning projects

Computer vision projects

Medical research projects

Open-source contributions

Relevant software or technical projects

5. Demonstrate Interest in Industry Collaboration

Because the PhD involves close collaboration with AWS for Healthcare, applicants should demonstrate that they are interested in translating research into practical applications.

Experience working with industry, cloud technologies, applied AI projects or scalable computational systems can therefore be useful to highlight.

6. Explain Your Long-Term Research Goals

A strong application should demonstrate how the PhD fits into your broader research and professional ambitions.

For example, candidates may explain their interest in developing AI systems that can improve medical image interpretation, clinical decision-making, healthcare efficiency or biomedical research.

Why This PhD Opportunity Stands Out

The UZH-AWS PhD position brings together four important components that are increasingly influential in modern healthcare research:

Artificial Intelligence + Medical Imaging + Clinical Research + Cloud Technology

The combination provides a distinctive research environment.

Instead of developing AI models in isolation, researchers will have opportunities to work with clinical collaborators, medical datasets and industry partners while investigating advanced approaches such as vision-language modeling, segmentation and visual grounding.

The position also provides exposure to benchmarking and clinical validation, allowing research outcomes to be evaluated against established standards and potentially translated into practical healthcare applications.

Visit HERE for more information about the PhD Position in Medical Imaging AI at the University of Zurich and AWS.

Conclusion

The PhD Position UZH-AWS in Medical Imaging AI offers an opportunity for technically trained researchers to pursue doctoral research at the intersection of artificial intelligence, medical imaging and healthcare.

With research spanning 3D vision-language modeling, image segmentation, visual grounding, clinical validation and benchmarking, the project is designed for candidates who want to tackle challenging problems in medical image computing while maintaining a strong connection to real-world clinical applications.

The collaboration between the University of Zurich, University Hospital Zurich and AWS for Healthcare, together with potential links to the ETH AI Center, creates a multidisciplinary environment in which doctoral research can connect academic innovation with practical healthcare technology.

Applicants with backgrounds in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering or related disciplines should carefully assess their academic preparation, research interests and motivation for working in medical AI before applying.

TITLE: Call for Participation – Workshop on Advocacy and Capacity Building in Open Access (OA) and Open Science (OS)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Association of African Universities is inviting its stakeholders to a workshop on Advocacy and Capacity Building in Open Access (OA) and Open Science (OS) to top management staff (Vice-Chancellors, Presidents and Rectors and Deputy Vice Chancellors Directors of Research and Library Services of AAU member Institutions).

This workshop is aimed at improving the capacity of participants towards creating and Implementing Open Access and Open Science policies and mandates in the respective AAU member institutions.

It is planned for 26th-27th October in Cairo, Egypt and will adopt a blended workshop format, running from 9am to 2pm EAT each day. The host for this event is the British University of Egypt (BUE).

As defined by the UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science, Open Science is a movement aiming to make science more open, accessible, efficient, democratic and transparent. The transition to Open Science allows scientific information, data and outputs to be more widely accessible (Open Access) and more reliably harnessed (Open Data) with the active engagement of all relevant stakeholders (Open to Society).

The Open Access/Open Science workshops targeting the research leadership in AAU member regions and universities is holding with the objective of creating awareness and education on the importance and best practice of Open Access/Open Science. The desired outcome is engagement and buy-in by the academic community on the adoption of Open Science.

TCC Africa and PLOS are the supporting partners in this initiative.

Outcomes

• Effective adoption of Open Science and Open Access practice among members

• Increased education and awareness on Open Science and Open Access in the AAU member academic community

Objectives of the workshop

• To advocate for institutions to embrace open science and open access in the respective member academic communities

• To understand the current developments on open science, challenges faced in their respective academic communities and opportunities on open science and open access

• To reduce the push back on the adoption of Open Science and Open Access by early career researchers.

• To create awareness on how Open Science aids in higher education institutions competitiveness

The meeting is free to attend. Participants are responsible for their accommodation and/or transportation for the two days.

The registration link is https://tinyurl.com/mr2ana33

Applications are open for the Human Rights Advocates Program (HRAP) 2027-2028. Founded in 1989, HRAP leverages the resources of Columbia University and those offered by NYC as a hub of NGOs and international organizations to provide human rights advocates with academic, skill-building, mentoring, and networking opportunities. Through seminars, participation in University courses, and workshops led by staff from leading human rights organizations as well as meetings with policymakers and funders, advocates share their experiences, reflect critically on their work, and plan future campaigns.

More than 350 advocates from nearly 100 countries have attended the program since it was created in 1989. Funding

TITLE: CONDOLENCE MESSAGE AFTER A CAR BOMB ATTACK IN MOGADISHU SOMALIA

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Condolence Message Following The Car Bomb Attack In Mogadishu Somalia

Accra, Ghana, 28 December 2019

It is with deep sorrow, concern and regret that the Secretary General of the Association of African Universities (AAU) received the news of a car bomb attack in Mogadishu Somalia on Saturday 28 December 2019. On his own behalf and that of the Governing Board of the AAU, the 400 AAU member universities, AAU partner organizations and the African Higher Education stakeholders we extend our heartfelt condolences on the scores of lives that were lost. We wish those that were injured a speedy recovery.

It is quite unfortunate that most of those killed were university students and other students returning to their schools and universities to resume their learning activities. We mourn the deaths of so many young people as Somalia tries to rebuild itself after decades of conflict.

The AAU continues to prioritize programmes to encourage a peaceful and secure Africa through Quality Higher Education. These include activities to promote peace and security, stimulate multidisciplinary approaches to dealing with peace and security in Africa and accelerating the development of systems, programmes and policies to deal with threats to national and continental peace and security.

Our support to the AAU Member Universities in the Federal Republic of Somalia will continue through Higher Education. The AAU will continue to support the legitimate desire of the people of Somalia to live in freedom, peace and security.

About the Association of African Universities (AAU)

The AAU was established in 1967 and is the current implementing agency of the African Union Commission’s initiatives and activities related to Higher Education. Read more about the AAU from www.aau.org and blog.aau.org

TITLE: CFJ Fellowship Programme 2027: Legal Fellowship for Early-Career Women Lawyers Across Africa

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
CFJ Fellowship Programme 2027: Legal Fellowship for Early-Career Women Lawyers Across Africa

The CFJ Fellowship Programme 2027 offers an opportunity for early-career African women lawyers to develop practical legal, strategic litigation, legal representation, and advocacy skills while working with human rights and justice organizations in Africa.

The programme, offered by the Clooney Foundation for Justice (CFJ) in partnership with the Legal Empowerment Fund at the Fund for Global Human Rights, places fellows in organizations working to protect the rights of women and children. Fellows gain hands-on experience in legal research, legal drafting, client support, court representation, advocacy, and the use of innovative technology to expand access to justice.

Beginning in August 2026, the programme formerly known as the Waging Justice for Women Fellowship Programme is being renamed the CFJ Fellowship Programme. According to CFJ, the recruitment process, eligibility requirements, and application procedures remain unchanged.

CFJ Fellowship Programme 2027 Overview

The fellowship is designed for lawyers at the early stages of their careers who want to strengthen their ability to use law and advocacy to advance justice for women and children.

For the 2027 programme, CFJ plans to fund and place 10 early-career women lawyers in human rights and justice organizations across Kenya, Malawi, South Africa, and The Gambia.

These host organizations include legal aid providers, universities with legal aid clinics, and government prosecution services.

What Is the CFJ Fellowship Programme?

The CFJ Fellowship Programme is an annual legal fellowship intended to help develop the next generation of justice advocates for women and children in Africa.

The programme gives early-career women lawyers the opportunity to work directly within organizations involved in human rights and justice work.

Rather than being limited to classroom-based legal education, the fellowship emphasizes immersive practical experience.

Fellows can work on real legal and justice issues and develop skills through practical assignments, mentoring, training, and engagement with experienced professionals.

The programme focuses particularly on issues affecting women and children, including:

Violence against women and children

Child marriage

Gender-based violence

Reproductive rights

Access to justice

Women’s rights

Children’s rights

Human rights

Legal advocacy

Partnership Behind the Fellowship

The programme is administered in partnership with the Legal Empowerment Fund at the Fund for Global Human Rights.

The partnership supports the programme’s focus on strengthening legal capacity and expanding access to justice for women and children.

What Do CFJ Fellows Do?

Fellows are placed within host organizations where they can gain direct experience in legal and justice-related work.

Their responsibilities may include:

1. Legal Research

Fellows conduct legal research relating to cases, human rights issues, legislation, policies, and other matters relevant to their host organization.

This provides an opportunity to strengthen research skills while working on real-world legal issues.

2. Legal Drafting

Fellows may contribute to drafting legal documents and other materials required in their work.

This can help early-career lawyers develop practical legal writing skills beyond what they may have encountered during their formal legal education.

3. Client Support

The programme allows fellows to support clients and communities requiring legal assistance.

Working directly with clients can help fellows develop practical skills in understanding legal needs, communicating legal information, and supporting people navigating justice systems.

4. Legal Representation

Fellows may undertake legal representation in court as part of their responsibilities.

This provides practical exposure to the justice process and allows fellows to develop their legal advocacy and representation skills.

5. Advocacy

The programme also develops fellows’ ability to advocate for women’s and children’s rights.

Advocacy can involve working on broader legal and policy issues alongside direct legal assistance.

Focus on Women and Children’s Rights

A central focus of the fellowship is strengthening legal protection for women and children.

Fellows are equipped with tools to advocate for rights, particularly in relation to issues such as child marriage and violence against women and children.

The programme also addresses wider areas of justice, including gender-based violence, reproductive rights, legal assistance, and legal education.

This combination of direct legal work and advocacy allows fellows to engage with both individual cases and broader justice issues.

Technology and Access to Justice

An additional component of the CFJ Fellowship Programme is its focus on technology.

CFJ has partnered with Microsoft’s AI for Good Lab and the Oxford Institute of Technology as part of its efforts to explore how technology can increase access to justice.

Fellows will receive training in innovative technological tools and are encouraged to consider how these tools can be applied to their legal and advocacy work.

This means the fellowship is not solely focused on traditional legal practice. It also introduces fellows to approaches that can potentially improve how legal services and justice advocacy are delivered.

Mentoring and Professional Development

CFJ provides fellows with mentoring and training throughout the programme.

Fellows have access to professionals working across the African human rights and justice sector, including:

Human rights experts

Lawyers

Judges

Activists

Academics

This gives fellows opportunities to learn from professionals with experience in different areas of justice and human rights work.

The mentoring component can also support fellows as they develop their professional interests and build relationships within the wider legal and human rights community.

CFJ Fellowship Alumni Network

The fellowship does not end when the placement concludes.

Upon completing the programme, fellows are inducted into the CFJ Fellowship Alumni Network.

The alumni network provides opportunities for:

Ongoing support

Knowledge sharing

Professional growth

Continued connections with other fellows

Engagement with the wider CFJ community

This creates a longer-term professional network for lawyers who have completed the fellowship.

Programme Impact Since 2023

According to CFJ’s programme information, the fellowship has already contributed to legal assistance and advocacy for women and children.

Since the programme launched in 2023, CFJ reports that its fellows have:

Worked on more than 500 cases involving women’s and children’s rights.

Supported more than 2,000 women and children through legal assistance, advocacy, and legal education.

The work has addressed areas including:

Gender-based violence

Reproductive rights

Child marriage

Women’s rights

Children’s rights

These figures are reported by CFJ as part of its description of the programme’s impact.

What Makes the Fellowship Practical?

A major feature of the programme is its emphasis on practical experience.

Fellows do not simply participate in lectures or theoretical training. They are placed within organizations where they can undertake professional responsibilities related to legal services and justice.

Through these placements, fellows can develop experience in:

Legal research

This practical structure is intended to help early-career lawyers develop skills that can be applied in their subsequent professional careers.

Strategic Litigation and Advocacy Skills

Strategic litigation is an important part of the programme’s professional-development focus.

Strategic litigation involves using legal cases and legal processes to address broader human rights or justice issues.

For fellows, exposure to this area can provide experience in connecting individual legal matters with broader questions concerning rights, access to justice, and legal protection.

Alongside litigation, fellows develop advocacy skills that can be applied both within legal proceedings and in wider efforts to promote women’s and children’s rights.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The fellowship is designed for early-career African women lawyers who want to develop their legal practice and contribute to human rights and justice work affecting women and children.

How to Prepare for the Fellowship

Prospective applicants can begin preparing by considering the areas emphasized by the programme.

Develop Your Legal Experience

Review your existing legal experience and identify work that demonstrates your interest in human rights, justice, women’s rights, or children’s rights.

Highlight Practical Skills

The programme involves practical legal work, so applicants should clearly present relevant experience in areas such as:

Legal research

Demonstrate Your Interest in Women’s and Children’s Rights

Consider Technology and Justice

Conclusion

The CFJ Fellowship Programme 2027 provides early-career African women lawyers with an opportunity to gain practical experience in human rights and justice organizations working across Kenya, Malawi, South Africa, and The Gambia.

Fellows can work on legal research, drafting, client support, court representation, and advocacy while focusing particularly on issues affecting women and children.

The programme also incorporates an emerging technology component through partnerships involving Microsoft’s AI for Good Lab and the Oxford Institute of Technology, giving fellows opportunities to explore innovative approaches to improving access to justice.

Since its launch in 2023, CFJ reports that fellows have worked on more than 500 cases involving women’s and children’s rights and supported more than 2,000 women and children through legal assistance, advocacy, and education.
