TITLE: Smithsonian James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027: U.S. Postdoctoral Researchers Can Receive a $62,000 Stipend and $5,000 Research Allowance

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are open for the Smithsonian James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027, a prestigious 12-month research opportunity for early-career postdoctoral researchers in the United States working across science, the humanities, and the arts.

Administered through the Smithsonian Institution’s Office of Academic Appointments and Internships, the James Smithson Fellowship Program provides researchers with an opportunity to pursue independent research while drawing on the Smithsonian’s extraordinary network of experts, research facilities, databases, and extensive collections.

For the 2027 cycle, the fellowship is centered on the theme “Regeneration.” Applicants are invited to develop interdisciplinary research proposals exploring how societies, environments, technologies, communities, and cultural traditions renew, recover, adapt, and maintain continuity over time.

Successful fellows will receive a $62,000 stipend and a research allowance of up to $5,000. Additional support may include a one-time travel allowance and a contribution toward health insurance costs.

The fellowship is primarily conducted in residence and lasts for 12 months. Appointments may begin as early as June 1, 2027, and must begin no later than May 1, 2028.

Importantly, this opportunity is restricted to eligible U.S. citizens, and applicants must generally be no more than five years beyond receiving their doctorate degree. Candidates holding terminal professional degrees may also be eligible.

James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027 Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027 James Smithson Fellowship Program is:

October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. Eastern Time (ET).

Applicants must submit their complete applications through the Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA) by the deadline.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin preparing their submission. The application requires a substantial research proposal, identification of a Smithsonian research advisor, references, transcripts, a budget, bibliography, curriculum vitae, and several other components.

In addition, applicants are responsible for ensuring that their required recommendation letters are submitted by the deadline.

About the James Smithson Fellowship Program

The James Smithson Fellowship Program was established to provide early-career postdoctoral researchers with an opportunity to deepen their disciplinary expertise while gaining a broader understanding of the relationship between academic scholarship, research, and public policy.

Rather than viewing research solely through the lens of an individual academic discipline, the program encourages fellows to examine the wider implications of their work.

The fellowship creates an immersive research environment where participants can work alongside Smithsonian researchers, interact with relevant collections and facilities, and consider how their research can contribute to wider conversations within society.

The program is particularly intended for a new generation of researchers and leaders interested in conducting innovative scholarship while exploring the potential policy implications and public significance of their research.

Fellows undertake independent empirical research within an interdisciplinary environment designed to encourage new ways of thinking, researching, and creating.

Theme for 2027: Regeneration

The theme of the 2027 James Smithson Fellowship is “Regeneration.”

The Smithsonian is inviting research proposals that examine how societies, environments, and cultural traditions renew and adapt over time.

Regeneration can occur in numerous forms and across many disciplines. The theme recognizes that renewal does not necessarily mean abandoning the past. Instead, regeneration can involve adapting to changing circumstances while preserving important elements of continuity.

Applicants are encouraged to explore processes including:

Restoration;

Resilience;

Adaptation;

Renewal;

Continuity;

Ecological recovery;

Cultural revitalization;

Community rebuilding;

Heritage conservation; and

Technological innovation.

The theme provides considerable room for interdisciplinary research.

What Does “Regeneration” Mean for the 2027 Fellowship?

The Smithsonian identifies several potential ways in which regeneration may be understood.

1. Restoration of Ecosystems

Researchers may investigate the ways natural environments recover, adapt, or are restored following environmental degradation, climate pressures, human activity, or other forms of disruption.

Research could potentially consider ecological adaptation, environmental resilience, restoration processes, conservation, or related questions.

2. Revitalization of Cultural Practices

Regeneration can also occur through the preservation, adaptation, and revitalization of cultural traditions.

Researchers working within history, anthropology, heritage, the humanities, arts, or related fields may consider how cultural knowledge and practices survive, change, or are renewed across generations and changing social environments.

3. Rebuilding Communities Following Disruption

The theme can extend to the ways communities rebuild and adapt following periods of disruption.

This creates opportunities to investigate resilience, social transformation, continuity, collective memory, recovery, and other processes through which communities respond to change.

4. Technological Innovation

Regeneration may also be considered through technological change and innovation.

Researchers may explore how technologies contribute to renewal, adaptation, preservation, resilience, or transformation across societies and environments.

These examples are not necessarily exhaustive. The broad nature of the theme allows researchers from science, the humanities, and the arts to approach regeneration through different disciplinary and interdisciplinary perspectives.

What Are the Goals of the James Smithson Fellowship?

The fellowship is designed to provide participants with several significant opportunities.

Fellows can:

Access Smithsonian facilities;

Work with extensive Smithsonian collections;

Utilize relevant Smithsonian databases;

Engage with Smithsonian research experts;

Encounter perspectives from multiple disciplines;

Conduct independent research;

Explore connections between academic scholarship and public policy;

Consider the wider implications of their research;

Develop skills that can help inform policy conversations; and

Deepen their disciplinary expertise within an innovative research environment.

The fellowship therefore goes beyond simply providing financial support for a research project.

It places researchers within the wider intellectual environment of the Smithsonian and encourages them to consider how their work connects with broader academic, cultural, scientific, societal, and policy questions.

Who Is Eligible for the James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027?

The James Smithson Fellowship Program is open to postdoctoral researchers in science, the humanities, and the arts.

Applicants must satisfy the program’s eligibility requirements.

Candidates must:

Be U.S. citizens;

Be postdoctoral researchers in science, the humanities, or the arts;

Generally be no more than five years beyond receipt of their doctorate degree; and

Meet the other requirements of the fellowship.

Candidates with terminal professional degrees are also eligible to apply.

Applicants should carefully review the official program guidelines before submitting an application to confirm their eligibility.

Smithsonian Research Advisor Requirement

One of the most important requirements of the James Smithson Fellowship is the identification of an appropriate Smithsonian research advisor.

Applicants are required to identify a Smithsonian expert listed in the Smithsonian Opportunities for Research and Study (SORS) guide who can serve as their research advisor during the fellowship.

This is not an optional component.

Only applicants who have identified a research advisor will be reviewed for the fellowship.

Applicants should therefore make identifying an appropriate advisor one of the first steps in preparing their application.

Before submitting an application, candidates should contact their prospective research advisor to:

Introduce themselves and their proposed research;

Determine whether the Smithsonian expert’s research interests and expertise are a good fit for the project;

Confirm that the expert is available to serve as an advisor during the proposed fellowship period; and

Discuss the research proposal and, where appropriate, anticipated research costs.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to correspond with their proposed Smithsonian advisor while developing their proposal.

Fellowship Duration and Starting Dates

The James Smithson Fellowship appointment lasts for:

12 months.

The fellowship is described as primarily in-residence, providing fellows with an immersive opportunity to engage with Smithsonian researchers, collections, facilities, and other relevant resources.

Appointments may commence:

As early as June 1, 2027;

No later than May 1, 2028.

Applicants should take these dates into account when preparing their proposed research timetable.

James Smithson Fellowship Stipend and Research Funding

Successful fellows receive significant financial support during the 12-month appointment.

Fellowship Stipend

Each fellow receives:

$62,000 stipend

Research Allowance

Fellows also receive:

Up to $5,000 in research allowance

The research allowance can support eligible costs associated with conducting the proposed research.

Applicants are required to prepare a budget and justification addressing expenses such as:

Equipment;

Supplies;

Research-related travel; and

Other support necessary to conduct the research.

The research budget should not include stipend or relocation costs.

Funding for direct hires may not be included.

Applicants are encouraged to discuss anticipated research costs with their proposed Smithsonian advisor before submitting their application.

If a research project requires more funding than the maximum $5,000 research allowance, the applicant must explain where the additional funding will come from.

Potential Additional Support

Additional fellowship support may include:

A one-time travel allowance; and

A contribution toward health insurance costs.

Applicants should consult the official program information for applicable conditions surrounding additional support.

How to Apply for the James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027

Applications must be submitted electronically through the Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA).

The complete application must be submitted by October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. ET.

Applicants should allow sufficient time to prepare all required documents and coordinate with their Smithsonian research advisor and references.

Required Application Documents

The James Smithson Fellowship application requires several detailed components.

1. Research Abstract

Applicants must provide an abstract summarizing their proposed research.

The abstract must be:

No more than one page; and

Double-spaced.

The abstract should clearly communicate the core research question, approach, and significance of the proposed project.

2. Research Proposal

Applicants must prepare a detailed research proposal.

The proposal must be:

No more than six pages;

Double-spaced;

Prepared on approximately 8.5 x 11-inch (210 mm x 297 mm) paper;

Formatted with one-inch margins; and

Written using a font no smaller than 11 point.

The six-page limit excludes other application components such as the abstract and bibliography, but includes images, tables, and similar materials contained within the proposal.

The proposal must address several important areas.

Proposed Research and Methodology

Applicants should describe the research they intend to conduct at the Smithsonian and explain the methodology they will use.

Potential Public Policy Implications

A significant component of the fellowship is the relationship between scholarship and public policy.

Applicants must therefore explain how their proposed research could potentially inform public policy.

Importance of the Research

Applicants should discuss why their research matters.

This should address its importance both:

Within the broader academic or professional discipline; and

In relation to the applicant’s own scholarly goals.

Why the Smithsonian Is Necessary

The proposal must justify why the research should be conducted at the Smithsonian Institution.

Applicants should explain how they plan to use relevant Smithsonian:

Collections;

Facilities;

Databases;

Research expertise;

Staff; and/or

Other resources.

A strong proposal should demonstrate a meaningful connection between the project and the resources available through the Smithsonian.

Smithsonian Principal Research Advisor

Applicants must identify the Smithsonian research staff member who will serve as their principal advisor.

Again, identification of an eligible Smithsonian advisor is mandatory.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to communicate with their proposed advisor while developing the research proposal.

3. Research Timetable

Applicants must submit an estimated timetable covering the entire fellowship period.

The timetable should explain when the major phases of the proposed research are expected to occur.

A clear timetable can help demonstrate that the research project is realistic and can be completed within the fellowship period.

4. Budget and Budget Justification

Applicants must submit a budget explaining anticipated research expenses.

Eligible categories can include:

Equipment;

Supplies;

Research-related travel expenses; and

Other support required to conduct the research.

Applicants cannot use this budget to include direct hires.

The budget also excludes the fellowship stipend and relocation costs.

If anticipated research expenses exceed the maximum $5,000 research allowance, applicants must identify and explain the source of additional funding.

5. Bibliography

Applicants must provide a bibliography covering literature relevant to their proposed research.

The bibliography must not exceed:

Two pages.

It should demonstrate familiarity with relevant scholarship and provide intellectual context for the proposed research.

6. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide a current curriculum vitae.

The CV should highlight areas including:

Education;

Expertise;

Academic and professional achievements;

Honors;

Publications; and

Research interests.

The CV should not exceed five pages.

Applicants whose native language is not English must also describe their proficiency in:

Reading English;

Speaking English; and

Writing English.

7. Academic Transcripts

Applicants must submit transcripts from their terminal degree institution or institutions.

Unofficial transcripts are acceptable.

Applicants should ensure that the submitted documentation appropriately reflects their academic background and qualifications.

8. Two References and Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must provide the:

Name; and

Email address

of two non-Smithsonian individuals who are familiar with their research.

These references will be asked to submit confidential letters of recommendation online.

Applicants may provide their references with:

A copy of their research proposal; and

The Smithsonian’s Letter to Reference document.

Applicants are responsible for ensuring that both recommendation letters are submitted by the application deadline.

This is particularly important because applications containing fewer than two letters of recommendation may not be considered.

Candidates should therefore contact their references well before October 15 rather than waiting until the application deadline approaches.

How Applications Will Be Evaluated

Applications will be reviewed by Smithsonian scholars working in appropriate fields.

The selection process considers several factors.

Innovation and Relationship to the 2027 Theme

Reviewers will examine the extent to which the proposed research is innovative and meaningfully connected to the theme of Regeneration.

Applicants should therefore make the relationship between their research and the fellowship theme clear within their proposal.

Potential Public Policy Relevance

Reviewers will consider how effectively the proposal addresses the potential for the research to inform public policy.

Applicants should demonstrate that they have considered the wider implications of their work rather than simply describing an academic research project.

Ability to Conduct the Research

The selection process will consider whether the applicant has the knowledge, skills, experience, and academic background necessary to successfully conduct the proposed project.

Feasibility

Reviewers will assess whether the research can realistically be completed within the requested fellowship period.

This makes the research timetable, methodology, scope, and project design particularly important.

Relevance of Smithsonian Resources

Applicants will be evaluated on the extent to which Smithsonian research staff and institutional resources can contribute to the proposed research.

Candidates should clearly demonstrate why conducting the project through the Smithsonian would provide meaningful value.

Alignment With Career Goals

Reviewers will consider how the fellowship aligns with the applicant’s broader career objectives.

Applicants should therefore think carefully about how the experience will contribute to their development as researchers and future leaders.

Leadership Potential

A candidate’s potential for leadership will also be assessed, including evidence demonstrated through previous performance and accomplishments.

Academic Record

The quality of the applicant’s academic record forms another part of the selection process.

Taken together, these criteria mean that a competitive application should combine a strong academic profile with an innovative, feasible research project that clearly connects with the theme of Regeneration, makes meaningful use of Smithsonian resources, and demonstrates potential relevance to public policy.

Important Restrictions for Smithsonian Employees and Contractors

Current employees and contractors of the Smithsonian Institution cannot hold a Smithsonian fellowship while simultaneously employed or contracted by the institution.

The Smithsonian also states that former employees or contractors generally need one year of separation before applying for a fellowship, unless prior approval is obtained from the Office of Academic Appointments and Internships.

Anyone affected by these conditions should consult the official fellowship guidelines or contact the Office of Academic Appointments and Internships for clarification.

Equal Employment Opportunity and Non-Discrimination

The Smithsonian Institution states that it does not discriminate based on:

Race;

Color;

Religion;

Sex, including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy;

National origin;

Age for individuals aged 40 or older;

Disability;

Genetic information;

Parental status; or

Military service.

Applicants should note, however, that the James Smithson Fellowship itself has a citizenship eligibility requirement: candidates must be U.S. citizens.

Important Dates at a Glance

Prospective applicants should keep the following dates in mind:

Application deadline: October 15, 2026

Application closing time: 4:59 p.m. ET

Earliest fellowship start date: June 1, 2027

Latest fellowship start date: May 1, 2028

Fellowship duration: 12 months

Applicants outside the Eastern Time Zone should pay particular attention to the 4:59 p.m. ET closing time and submit well in advance to avoid time-zone confusion or last-minute technical difficulties.

Key Fellowship Details at a Glance

Program: James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027

Host Institution: Smithsonian Institution

2027 Theme: Regeneration

Research Fields: Science, humanities, and arts

Fellowship Duration: 12 months, primarily in residence

Stipend: $62,000

Research Allowance: Up to $5,000

Additional Potential Support: One-time travel allowance and contribution toward health insurance costs

Eligibility: Eligible U.S. citizen postdoctoral researchers and candidates with qualifying terminal professional degrees

Application Platform: Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA)

Deadline: October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. ET

Earliest Start: June 1, 2027

Latest Start: May 1, 2028

Important Tips Before Applying

Because this is a research-intensive fellowship, applicants should begin preparation well ahead of the deadline.

In particular, candidates should:

Confirm their eligibility before preparing the full application. The program is restricted to eligible U.S. citizens and primarily targets postdoctoral researchers within five years of receiving their doctorate.

Identify a Smithsonian research advisor early. This is mandatory, and applications without an identified advisor will not be reviewed.

Contact the prospective advisor before applying. Confirm that the Smithsonian expert is an appropriate fit and is available during the proposed fellowship period.

Build a clear connection to the theme of Regeneration. Reviewers specifically evaluate how innovative the proposed research is and how it relates to the annual theme.

Explain the public policy dimension. Applicants should clearly articulate how their research could potentially inform public policy.

Demonstrate why the Smithsonian is essential to the project. The proposal should identify specific experts, facilities, collections, databases, or other resources relevant to the research.

Prepare a realistic 12-month timetable. The selection process considers whether the project can reasonably be completed during the requested period.

Coordinate with references early. Two confidential recommendation letters are required, and the applicant is responsible for ensuring they arrive on time.

Review the research budget carefully. If anticipated research expenses exceed the $5,000 allowance, explain how the additional costs will be funded.

Submit before the final deadline. Applications must be completed through SOLAA by October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. ET.

How to Apply

Eligible applicants should complete their applications through the Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA):

https://solaa.si.edu/

Before beginning the application, candidates should also carefully review the official James Smithson Fellowship Program Guidelines:

https://fellowships.si.edu/james-smithson-fellowship

Applicants looking for a potential Smithsonian research advisor should consult the Smithsonian Opportunities for Research and Study (SORS) resources:

https://fellowships.si.edu/SORS

Questions about the fellowship may be directed to the Smithsonian Institution’s Office of Academic Appointments and Internships at:

InternsAndFellows@si.edu

APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The Smithsonian James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for eligible early-career U.S. researchers to pursue ambitious independent research within one of the world’s most prominent research, museum, scientific, historical, and cultural institutions.

With a $62,000 stipend, up to $5,000 in research funding, potential additional travel and health insurance support, and access to Smithsonian researchers, facilities, databases, and extensive collections, the fellowship provides much more than financial support. It gives researchers an environment in which they can deepen their expertise, work across disciplinary boundaries, and examine the wider societal and public policy significance of their scholarship.

The 2027 theme, Regeneration, creates a particularly broad interdisciplinary framework. Researchers may investigate ecological restoration, cultural revitalization, community resilience, adaptation, technological innovation, heritage conservation, continuity, or other processes through which societies, environments, and traditions renew and transform over time.

A particularly important step for prospective applicants is finding an appropriate Smithsonian research advisor. Since applications without an identified advisor will not be reviewed, candidates should begin exploring Smithsonian experts and establishing contact well before preparing their final submission.

Eligible researchers interested in the program should begin preparing their proposal, identifying an advisor, contacting references, developing their research budget and timetable, and gathering the necessary academic documents as early as possible.

All applications must be submitted through SOLAA by October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. ET.

TITLE: GovAI Research Manager (UK Fellowships) 2026: Salary Up to £105,000, Visa Sponsorship and How to Apply

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
GovAI is inviting applications for a Research Manager (UK Fellowships) position within its Talent Development team. The role offers an opportunity for an experienced professional to help design, select, manage, and deliver GovAI’s UK Seasonal Fellowships while coaching talented individuals pursuing impactful careers in artificial intelligence governance and policy.

The position is particularly suited to someone with excellent project management abilities, strong interpersonal and communication skills, a coaching mindset, professional judgement, and a strong interest in developing talent in the field of AI governance.

The successful candidate will play a significant role in shaping future cohorts of AI governance professionals. Their responsibilities will extend beyond managing fellows to include selection, programme design, events, workshops, stakeholder engagement, programme evaluation, and continuous improvement.

GovAI is also open to candidates who show strong potential but are not yet ready to take on the full responsibilities of Research Manager. Such applicants may be considered for a Research Management Associate role as an initial position.

The application deadline is Sunday, 27 September 2026, at 11:59 PM BST.

About GovAI

GovAI was founded with the mission of helping humanity navigate the transition to a world with advanced artificial intelligence.

The organisation conducts research and works to provide knowledge and assistance to decision-makers across government, industry, and civil society. Its research agenda, first published in 2018, helped contribute to the development of the emerging field of AI governance.

GovAI researchers have published research in prominent academic journals and conferences, including:

Science

Nature

NeurIPS

FAccT

ICML

The organisation’s researchers and staff have also contributed commentary to influential publications and policy outlets such as TIME, Foreign Affairs, War on the Rocks, and Lawfare.

GovAI’s work has received coverage from major media organisations including The New York Times, Vox, and the Financial Times.

The organisation has staff working across the:

United Kingdom

United States

European Union

One of GovAI’s major approaches to advancing its mission is developing the next generation of talent working on AI governance and policy. The Talent Development team leads these efforts, and the Research Manager position is part of this team.

About the GovAI Seasonal Fellowships

The Research Manager will be closely involved in GovAI’s flagship Seasonal Fellowship programme.

Seasonal Fellowships are three-month opportunities designed to help launch or accelerate impactful careers in AI governance and policy.

GovAI runs two fellowship programmes each year from its London office. Each cohort typically brings together approximately 40 to 50 fellows.

The programme is highly competitive. GovAI reports receiving nearly 20,000 applications each year for approximately 100 places, resulting in an acceptance rate of only around 0.5%.

The fellowship attracts applicants and participants from a remarkably broad range of backgrounds.

While GovAI aims to admit a substantial number of early-career individuals, previous cohorts have also included:

Senior government officials

Senior academics

Software engineers

Lawyers

Journalists

Accomplished professionals from other sectors

A New York Times bestselling author

A Nobel Peace Prize nominee

This diversity means that the Research Manager will have the opportunity to work with fellows at very different stages of their careers and with a wide range of professional and academic experiences.

What Do Seasonal Fellows Do?

During the fellowship, participants work on projects of their choice.

There are two primary tracks:

Research Track

Fellows on the Research Track conduct a research project related to AI governance or an appropriate area of interest.

Applied Track

Fellows on the Applied Track work on projects outside traditional academic research.

Each fellow is paired with a supervisor drawn from the GovAI team or its wider network.

During the first two weeks, fellows explore the project or projects that would be most valuable for them to pursue. This process involves input from:

Their supervisor

Their Research Manager

The wider GovAI community

The remaining ten weeks are focused on executing the selected projects.

However, the fellowship is not solely about completing an individual project. Fellows also spend time developing their knowledge and skills in AI governance while building professional networks.

GovAI organises activities such as:

Q&A sessions with AI governance experts

Weekly seminars

Skills-development workshops

Work-in-progress meetings

Peer feedback sessions

Social events

Career discussions and networking opportunities

Fellows are also encouraged to explore follow-on career opportunities through GovAI’s team and professional network.

Impact of the Seasonal Fellowship

The programme has a strong emphasis on long-term career development.

GovAI reports that approximately 90% of fellows say they are very likely to recommend the fellowship to friends or colleagues.

Participants have also reported that the programme was substantially more valuable to their long-term careers than the alternative activities they would otherwise have pursued.

In its most recent alumni survey, respondents reported that their time at GovAI increased the impact they expect to have in AI governance by approximately 40%.

The Research Manager will therefore have a direct role in helping fellows maximise the long-term value of their fellowship experience.

Why Consider the Research Manager Role?

This position offers the successful candidate the opportunity to combine programme management, talent development, coaching, research, recruitment, events, and strategic decision-making.

1. Help Accelerate Important Careers

A Research Manager will coach approximately 10 to 15 fellows per cohort.

These fellows may range from recent graduates and early-career professionals to highly experienced individuals, including senior government officials.

The manager will help fellows:

Define meaningful project goals

Develop realistic timelines

Overcome challenges

Execute ambitious projects

Improve their professional skills

Navigate career transitions

Identify future career opportunities

Remain accountable for their objectives

For someone passionate about developing people and helping talented professionals enter or advance in AI governance, this is a central attraction of the role.

2. Help Shape the Future AI Governance Talent Pipeline

The Research Manager will participate in the selection of fellowship cohorts.

Because GovAI receives approximately 20,000 applications annually for around 100 fellowship places, the selection process is extremely competitive.

The successful candidate will therefore contribute directly to decisions about which candidates receive the opportunity to enter the programme.

This responsibility can include:

Grading applications

Conducting interviews

Recommending candidates

Participating in decision-making meetings

Helping improve the selection process

Potentially contributing to fellowship outreach

Attending or organising promotional events

This makes the position more than a conventional programme-management role. The Research Manager will help determine which individuals receive opportunities to develop careers in the AI governance field.

3. Grow With a Rapidly Developing Organisation

GovAI describes itself as a rapidly growing organisation with funding in place to continue expanding.

As the organisation develops, the Research Manager is expected to have opportunities to take on additional responsibilities.

The position is therefore intended to provide room for the successful candidate to develop the role according to their:

Interests

Strengths

Experience

Skills

Capacity

This may make the opportunity particularly attractive to candidates who want a role with significant responsibility and potential for professional growth.

Research Manager Responsibilities

The Research Manager will have a broad set of responsibilities covering fellowship management, recruitment, programme design, events, evaluation, and talent development.

1. Manage Seasonal Fellows

One of the most important responsibilities will be research managing approximately 10 to 15 fellows per cohort.

This involves meeting with each fellow weekly.

The Research Manager will have primary responsibility for making sure fellows:

Set clear goals

Establish realistic timelines

Receive appropriate support

Make progress on their projects

Address obstacles effectively

Successfully navigate their career searches

The Research Manager will also communicate with each fellow’s supervisor.

Supervisors have primary responsibility for providing feedback on fellows’ work, while the Research Manager focuses more broadly on ensuring that the fellowship experience remains productive and that fellows receive the support they need.

2. Participate in Fellowship Selection

The Research Manager will contribute to selecting future fellowship cohorts.

This includes reviewing applications and helping identify candidates who have the potential to make significant contributions to AI governance.

Responsibilities may include:

Grading applications

Conducting candidate interviews

Making candidate recommendations

Participating in selection decisions

Helping design or improve the selection process

The role may also involve supporting outreach activities intended to attract strong applicants.

The Research Manager may attend or organise events designed to promote the fellowship and communicate opportunities to potential applicants.

3. Help Set Up Each Fellowship

Before each fellowship begins, the Research Manager will contribute to programme preparation.

This can include:

Soliciting project suggestions from GovAI’s team and network

Recruiting fellowship supervisors

Pairing supervisors with incoming fellows

Engaging guest speakers

Arranging events

Developing seminar materials

Developing workshop materials

Preparing educational and pedagogical resources

This means the role requires strong planning and coordination skills because many programme components need to be prepared before fellows arrive.

4. Run the Day-to-Day Fellowship Programme

The Research Manager will also contribute to the everyday operation of the fellowship.

Responsibilities can include:

Running events

Organising workshops

Moderating expert Q&A sessions

Facilitating discussions

Hosting fellowship guests

Supporting fellows throughout the programme

Ensuring a positive and productive participant experience

The successful candidate will therefore need to be comfortable taking responsibility in front of groups and interacting with people from a variety of professional backgrounds.

5. Evaluate Programme Impact

The Research Manager will contribute to assessing the impact of the fellowship programme.

This involves helping GovAI understand whether the programme is achieving its intended outcomes and identifying opportunities for improvement.

Programme evaluation can help determine:

What is working effectively

Where fellows need additional support

Which programme activities create the greatest value

How the fellowship affects participants’ careers

What changes could improve future cohorts

6. Improve the Fellowship Programme

The Research Manager will be expected to identify and implement changes that could increase the fellowship’s impact.

This requires someone who can:

Identify weaknesses

Analyse programme outcomes

Develop practical improvements

Communicate recommendations

Implement changes

Evaluate whether those changes work

The position therefore combines operational execution with strategic thinking.

Additional Talent Development Responsibilities

Beyond the Seasonal Fellowship itself, the successful candidate may contribute to other aspects of GovAI’s talent development work depending on their skills, interests, experience, and capacity.

Potential responsibilities include:

Talent Database Management

The Research Manager may contribute to managing GovAI’s talent databases.

This can involve maintaining information about individuals in the AI governance ecosystem and helping ensure that relevant talent information remains organised and useful.

External Career Recommendations

The role may also involve providing candidate recommendations for external opportunities when requested.

This could require the Research Manager to understand the skills and career interests of people within GovAI’s network and identify potentially suitable opportunities.

Alumni Career Support

The Research Manager may provide ongoing career support to fellowship alumni after their formal fellowship has ended.

This extends the role beyond the three-month fellowship and allows the Research Manager to contribute to longer-term talent development.

Selection Criteria

GovAI is looking for candidates who combine strong operational skills with interpersonal ability, professional judgement, and a commitment to its mission.

The organisation identifies several core selection criteria.

1. Impact Motivation

Candidates should be genuinely excited by GovAI’s mission.

The successful applicant should want to contribute to making the fellowship programme as effective and impactful as possible.

A strong candidate will therefore be able to demonstrate why AI governance and talent development matter to them and why they want to contribute to GovAI’s work.

2. Excellent Project Management Skills

Strong project management ability is essential.

The Research Manager will need to manage multiple complex workstreams simultaneously.

This requires:

Structured working habits

Strong organisation

Effective prioritisation

Attention to detail

Reliable execution

Ability to manage deadlines

Ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders

Candidates should be comfortable working on several priorities at the same time without losing track of important details.

3. Strong Interpersonal Skills and a Coaching Mindset

The position involves working closely with fellows who may be facing challenges in their projects or careers.

The Research Manager needs to be able to provide support while also holding fellows accountable.

This requires a balance between:

Empathy

Encouragement

Constructive feedback

Accountability

Clear expectations

Problem-solving

A coaching mindset is therefore an important part of the position.

4. Professional Judgement and Communication

The Research Manager will represent GovAI to a variety of stakeholders.

These can include:

Fellows

Internal supervisors

External supervisors

Fellowship guests

Researchers

Professionals

Other members of GovAI’s network

Candidates must therefore be able to communicate clearly and professionally with people from different backgrounds and at different levels of seniority.

Strong judgement will also be important because the role involves making decisions that affect fellows, programme activities, and selection processes.

5. Drive for Excellence

GovAI is looking for people who are committed to continuously improving themselves.

Candidates should demonstrate:

High standards

Willingness to learn

Receptiveness to feedback

Commitment to self-improvement

Desire to produce excellent work

The organisation specifically identifies feedback and self-improvement as important components of its culture.

6. Research Experience

Research experience is preferred but not required.

This is because the Research Manager may need to provide feedback on fellows’ research plans and outputs.

Candidates with research experience may therefore have an advantage, particularly if they can demonstrate the ability to assess research questions, methodologies, project plans, and written outputs.

However, applicants should not assume they are ineligible simply because they do not have a traditional research background.

7. Facilitation and Hosting Experience

Experience facilitating or hosting is also preferred but not required.

The Research Manager will be expected to run:

Seminars

Workshops

Expert Q&A sessions

Discussion sessions

Events involving fellowship guests

Candidates who have experience facilitating professional events, training sessions, workshops, conferences, seminars, or group discussions may therefore find this aspect of the role particularly relevant.

Research Management Associate Alternative

GovAI recognises that some promising applicants may not yet be ready to take on the entire scope of the Research Manager position.

For these candidates, the organisation may consider offering a Research Management Associate role first.

This provides an alternative pathway for strong candidates who demonstrate potential but may need additional experience before assuming full Research Manager responsibilities.

Therefore, candidates should not necessarily rule themselves out solely because they do not meet every aspect of the Research Manager profile.

Salary and Compensation

The position is full-time.

GovAI expects successful candidates to receive annual compensation in the range of:

£83,000 to £105,000 per year

The organisation notes that there may be some flexibility in compensation in situations where salary considerations would otherwise prevent a strong candidate from accepting an offer.

Candidates with specific questions or concerns about compensation or benefits can contact GovAI’s recruitment team.

Employee Benefits

In addition to salary, GovAI lists a range of benefits for the position.

These include:

Health insurance

Dental insurance

Vision insurance

10% employer pension contribution

£5,000 annual wellbeing budget

£5,000 annual professional development budget

£5,000 annual childcare budget

£1,800 annual commuting allowance

Flexible working hours

Extended parental leave

33 days of annual leave, including public holidays

The professional development budget may be particularly valuable for a candidate looking to continue building expertise in AI governance, management, research, leadership, or related areas.

Location and Visa Sponsorship

The fellowship periods are:

January to April

June to August

Outside fellowship periods, short periods of remote work are possible.

TITLE: Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 in Germany: International Postdoctoral Researchers Can Receive €3,000 Per Month for Contemporary History Research

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
International historians and postdoctoral researchers specializing in twentieth-century German, European, or Eastern European history have an opportunity to spend two months conducting independent research in Germany through the Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 at the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam (Leibniz-Zentrum für Zeithistorische Forschung Potsdam – ZZF).

For the 2027 fellowship cycle, ZZF is inviting applications for two Leibniz Summer Fellowships focused on German and/or European, including Eastern European, History in the Twentieth Century. The program is specifically intended for international scholars who already hold a doctoral degree and are residing outside Germany when they apply.

Successful fellows will spend two consecutive months in Berlin or Potsdam between April and October 2027. Each fellow will receive a monthly grant of €3,000, meaning that a two-month fellowship provides €6,000 in total grant support. The funding is intended to cover the fellow’s living costs, travel and appropriate insurance during the fellowship period.

The application deadline is November 30, 2026.

About the Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027

The Leibniz Summer Fellowship is a research residency offered by the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam for established international scholars working in areas relevant to twentieth-century German and European history.

The program combines two important elements: independent scholarly research and active participation in the intellectual life of ZZF.

Rather than requiring fellows to work on a predetermined institutional project, ZZF allows successful applicants to continue research based on their own scholarly interests. Preference, however, is given to proposals that connect with one or more of the Centre’s existing research departments.

This approach makes the fellowship particularly attractive to postdoctoral historians who already have a developed research agenda and would benefit from access to German academic networks, historical resources and interaction with specialists working on related themes.

Host Institution: Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam

The Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam, commonly known as ZZF, is a major German research institute specializing in twentieth-century contemporary history and its connections with the present.

Its work places particular emphasis on German and European social history after 1945 while situating those developments within broader international contexts. In addition to fundamental historical research, ZZF is involved in research infrastructure, digital knowledge transfer and cooperation with universities and research institutions in Germany and abroad.

ZZF is a member of the Leibniz Association, one of Germany’s major networks of non-university research institutions. The Centre has held Leibniz Association membership since 2009 and receives institutional support from both federal and state-level public funding.

The institute also has an extensive international academic orientation, including cooperation with universities and research organizations as well as a visiting-researcher program. These connections help make the fellowship more than simply a short period of individual archival or library research.

Two Fellowships Available for 2027

ZZF has announced two positions under the 2027 Leibniz Summer Fellowship program.

The thematic field is:

German and/or European, including Eastern European, History in the Twentieth Century

This is broad enough to accommodate scholars working across multiple subfields of contemporary history, provided that their research has a substantive connection to German or European twentieth-century history.

The opportunity is intended for international postdoctoral researchers rather than doctoral students or applicants who have not yet completed their doctorate.

Fellowship Duration

Each fellowship lasts for:

Two consecutive months

The research stay must take place between:

April and October 2027

Successful candidates are expected to live in either Berlin or Potsdam, Germany, throughout their two-month fellowship period.

Applicants should therefore consider their availability carefully before applying and identify a feasible two-month period within the April-to-October window.

The requirement to remain locally based is important because the program is designed around participation in ZZF’s academic environment rather than functioning as a remote research grant.

Financial Support: €3,000 Per Month

One of the major features of the Leibniz Summer Fellowship is its financial support.

Each successful fellow receives:

€3,000 per month

Because the fellowship runs for two months, the total fellowship grant amounts to:

€6,000 for the full two-month period

ZZF states that this funding is expected to cover costs associated with the fellowship, including:

Living expenses

Travel expenses

Appropriate insurance

Applicants should understand that these costs are expected to be met from the €3,000 monthly fellowship payment rather than assuming that accommodation, flights or insurance will automatically be paid separately by the institution.

Researchers considering the fellowship should therefore prepare an estimated budget covering transportation to Germany, temporary accommodation in Berlin or Potsdam, local transportation, meals, insurance and other personal expenses.

Research Facilities Provided by ZZF

In addition to the financial grant, fellows receive access to institutional research infrastructure.

ZZF states that fellowship recipients will be provided with facilities including:

Office space

Computer access

Other relevant institutional facilities

These resources are designed to allow fellows to work from the Centre and participate meaningfully in its research community.

This is particularly valuable for international researchers who want more than financial support and instead seek an immersive period within a specialist academic environment.

Access to an Important Contemporary History Library

Research fellows can also benefit from ZZF’s specialist library.

The ZZF library concentrates on German and European contemporary history after 1945 and includes material covering social and economic history, political and cultural history, media history, and the history of German division and reunification.

Its catalogue also incorporates electronic and audiovisual resources, journal holdings and thousands of indexed academic articles.

For scholars whose work relies on German-language scholarship or European contemporary history literature, proximity to such a specialized research collection can considerably strengthen a short research stay.

ZZF’s Main Research Departments

Applicants have considerable freedom to pursue their own research, but there is a strategic advantage in demonstrating how a proposed project connects with ZZF’s institutional expertise.

The Centre’s academic research is structured around five major research areas:

Communism and Society

Knowledge – Economy – Politics

Media and Information Society

Regimes of the Social Sphere

Globalizations in a Divided World

ZZF’s overall research agenda covers twentieth-century German and European contemporary history from political, social, cultural, economic, media and transnational perspectives.

Applicants should therefore study these departments before preparing their project proposal and identify where their own work has an intellectual connection with ZZF researchers.

Research on Communism, Eastern Europe and Post-Communist Transformation

Scholars specializing in Eastern European history may find the fellowship particularly relevant.

For example, ZZF’s Communism and Society department examines governance and social practices in the German Democratic Republic and Central and Eastern Europe. Its research also addresses transformations surrounding and extending beyond the political changes of 1989–1991, along with issues including violence, civil society and social developments in late and post-communist societies.

This institutional expertise helps explain why the fellowship announcement explicitly includes Eastern European history within its thematic scope.

Global and Transnational Perspectives

The Centre’s work is not limited to national German history.

Its research also examines how German and European societies interacted with wider global transformations, including the Cold War, decolonization, changing international orders and transnational connections.

ZZF’s work on globalization examines how European societies both influenced and were influenced by international structures and cross-border developments.

Applicants whose projects use comparative, transnational or global-history approaches may therefore find relevant intellectual connections at the Centre.

Who Is Eligible for the Leibniz Summer Fellowships?

Eligibility is comparatively straightforward but academically demanding.

Applicants must meet the following central conditions:

Hold a doctoral degree at the time the application is submitted

Have postdoctoral standing

Demonstrate an outstanding academic record

Be an international applicant

Reside outside Germany at the time of application

Propose research relevant to twentieth-century German and/or European history, including Eastern European history

ZZF explicitly defines the international character of the fellowship in terms of residence: applicants should be based outside Germany.

This is therefore not a fellowship for applicants who are still completing their PhD or expect to receive the doctorate only after submitting the application.

Do You Need to Be a German Citizen?

No nationality requirement restricting the fellowship to German citizens is stated.

In fact, the fellowship is designed for international researchers residing outside Germany.

This means applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe outside Germany, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions may potentially apply, provided they meet the academic and residency requirements and their proposed research fits the fellowship’s scholarly field.

Nationality and residence should not, however, be confused. The explicit requirement concerns being an international applicant residing outside Germany at application stage.

What Academic Background Is Required?

This is an advanced research fellowship rather than a student scholarship.

A completed doctoral degree is mandatory.

The official call additionally emphasizes postdoctoral standing and a strong academic record.

Accordingly, the fellowship is most appropriate for researchers such as:

Postdoctoral scholars

University lecturers

Academic historians

Research fellows

Early- or mid-career researchers with completed PhDs

Independent scholars with an established academic record, provided they satisfy the formal requirements

The strongest applicants are likely to have a clearly defined research agenda, publications or other evidence of scholarly achievement and a project that can make productive use of a two-month stay at ZZF.

Research Project Requirements

Applicants are not required to join a predetermined research project.

Instead, fellows can pursue their own individual research interests.

However, ZZF specifically indicates that preference will be given to applicants whose projects relate to one or more of its research departments.

Applicants should therefore avoid presenting the proposed project as completely isolated from the host institution.

A strong proposal should explain why conducting the research specifically at ZZF would be useful.

Relevant questions to address when developing the proposal include:

How does the project relate to contemporary German or European history?

Does it engage with Eastern European history where relevant?

Which ZZF department has the strongest connection with the project?

Which methodological or thematic conversations at ZZF could benefit the research?

What specific progress can realistically be achieved within two months?

Why is residence in Berlin or Potsdam valuable for the project?

What scholarly output may result from the fellowship?

These are strategic application considerations rather than additional formal requirements published by ZZF.

Integration Into ZZF’s Academic Community

Successful applicants will not simply receive funding and work independently.

Each fellow will be affiliated with one of ZZF’s research departments.

Fellows will be able to participate in departmental academic activities and will also be expected to present their research project through the institute’s research seminar.

This makes communication skills and willingness to engage academically with other researchers important aspects of the fellowship experience.

Applicants should therefore approach the program as both an individual research residency and an academic-exchange opportunity.

Required Application Documents

The application package consists of four main documents:

Letter of Interest

Curriculum Vitae

List of Publications

Research Project Proposal of no more than 1,500 words

All documents must be combined into one PDF attachment and submitted electronically.

The application may be prepared in either:

English or German

This allows international scholars who do not write academically in German to apply in English.

No Recommendation Letter Required

An important feature of the application process is that applicants do not need to submit a letter of recommendation.

This simplifies the application process because candidates do not have to arrange an external academic referee or wait for recommendation letters before the deadline.

The application will therefore depend heavily on the quality of the applicant’s own academic record, CV, publication record, statement of interest and research proposal.

How to Prepare the 1,500-Word Project Proposal

The project proposal is likely to be one of the most important components of the application.

Because it cannot exceed 1,500 words, applicants should make every section purposeful.

A useful structure could include:

Research Title

Use a precise academic title reflecting the central historical question or argument.

Research Background

Briefly explain the historical issue, scholarly debate or research gap that motivates the project.

Research Questions

State clearly what the project seeks to investigate.

Sources and Methodology

Identify the types of sources, archives, publications or methodological approaches that will be used.

Contribution to Scholarship

Explain what new knowledge, argument or perspective the project could add to existing research.

Relevance to ZZF

Identify the ZZF department or research themes that connect most directly with the project.

Fellowship Work Plan

Explain what can realistically be accomplished during the two-month stay.

This suggested structure is application guidance rather than a format mandated by the official call.

How to Prepare the Letter of Interest

The letter of interest should complement rather than duplicate the research proposal.

Applicants can use it to explain:

Their current academic position and research trajectory

Why they are applying for the Leibniz Summer Fellowship

Why ZZF is an appropriate host institution

What they hope to achieve during the residency

How interaction with the Centre’s scholars may support the project

How the fellowship fits into their broader academic development

Candidates should keep the letter focused and professional.

Preparing the Publication List

Because ZZF asks applicants to demonstrate a strong academic record, the publication list provides important evidence of scholarly development.

Depending on the applicant’s career stage, it may include:

Peer-reviewed journal articles

Academic books or monographs

Edited volumes

Book chapters

Published research reports

Relevant scholarly publications

Applicants should provide complete bibliographical information and organize their publications clearly.

How to Submit the Application

Applications must be submitted electronically by email.

The official fellowship email address is:

fellowships@zzf-potsdam.de

All required documents should be consolidated into one PDF attachment. ZZF does not request a recommendation letter.

Applicants should carefully check that all four required components are included before sending the application.

Application Deadline

The final deadline is:

November 30, 2026

Applications should be completed and submitted by this date.

ZZF states that fellowship decisions will be communicated no later than:

December 31, 2026.

This relatively short decision period gives successful applicants several months to organize travel, accommodation, insurance and research arrangements before the fellowship period begins in April 2027.

Key Dates at a Glance

Stage
Date / Period

Application deadline
November 30, 2026

Fellowship decisions
By December 31, 2026

Fellowship period
Two consecutive months

Eligible residency window
April–October 2027

Location
Berlin or Potsdam, Germany

Monthly fellowship grant
€3,000

Total for two months
€6,000

These dates and funding conditions are stated in the official 2027 fellowship announcement.

Why Researchers Should Consider This Opportunity

For eligible historians, the Leibniz Summer Fellowship offers several advantages in one program.

It provides direct financial support, a temporary institutional base in Germany, access to academic facilities and the opportunity to interact with scholars specializing in contemporary European history.

The fellowship may be particularly useful for researchers who are:

Developing an article or book project on twentieth-century Europe

Conducting postdoctoral research involving Germany

Working on Central or Eastern European contemporary history

Expanding a project into comparative or transnational European history

Seeking intellectual exchange with German-based scholars

Planning research that benefits from spending time in Berlin or Potsdam

ZZF’s international cooperation, specialist research departments and contemporary-history resources provide an academic environment particularly relevant to these objectives.

Important Points to Remember Before Applying

Applicants should pay particular attention to several requirements.

First, a doctorate must already have been completed when the application is submitted.

Second, this call is intended for international applicants residing outside Germany.

Third, although applicants can propose their own research, aligning the proposal with ZZF’s research profile can strengthen its institutional relevance.

Fourth, the fellowship lasts exactly two consecutive months and fellows must reside in Berlin or Potsdam during that period.

Finally, the €3,000 monthly payment is intended to cover multiple types of expenditure, including living, travel and insurance costs. Applicants should therefore plan their budget accordingly.

Conclusion

The Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 at the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam offer an excellent short-term research opportunity for international postdoctoral historians interested in twentieth-century German, European or Eastern European history.

With two fellowships available, a €3,000 monthly grant, access to ZZF’s academic facilities and specialist research environment, and the opportunity to participate directly in departmental and seminar activities, the program provides both financial support and meaningful scholarly engagement.

Applicants must already hold a doctorate, demonstrate a strong academic record and reside outside Germany when applying. Successful researchers will spend two consecutive months in Berlin or Potsdam sometime between April and October 2027.

The most important date to remember is November 30, 2026, when applications close. Candidates should prepare a letter of interest, CV, publication list and a research proposal of no more than 1,500 words, combine everything into one PDF and submit it to the official fellowship email address.
