TITLE: NIKE Global Sustainability Graduate Internship 2027: Paid 10-Week Graduate Internship in the United States

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The NIKE, Inc. Global Sustainability Graduate Internship offers graduate students an opportunity to gain practical experience working on sustainability initiatives at one of the world’s most recognized sports companies. The internship is designed for graduate-level candidates interested in sustainability, climate and environmental issues, supply chains, operations, analytics, human rights, sustainable materials, compliance and other areas that contribute to responsible business practices.

Based at NIKE’s Philip H. Knight campus in Beaverton, Oregon, the 10-week paid internship gives selected participants the opportunity to work with teams across the company and contribute to projects that connect sustainability with business, manufacturing, operations and marketplace activities.

The internship is particularly relevant to graduate students pursuing an MBA and/or Environmental Science graduate degree who want to develop experience working on large-scale sustainability challenges within a global organization.

About the NIKE Global Sustainability Graduate Internship

Nike describes sustainability as an important part of its approach to innovation and long-term business development. The company’s Global Sustainability team works across its value chain to address environmental and social issues while supporting business and operational objectives.

The internship provides graduate students with the opportunity to become part of this work and contribute to projects involving different functions and stakeholders across Nike.

Rather than simply observing sustainability activities, interns are expected to take ownership of one or more projects. These projects can involve research, strategic thinking, data analysis, stakeholder engagement, problem-solving and the development of recommendations that can help move business initiatives forward.

The position therefore combines sustainability knowledge with business strategy, project management, analytics and cross-functional collaboration.

These include:

Work related to climate strategy, environmental impact and resource management.

Projects may involve emissions reduction and broader environmental initiatives.

Engagement

Supporting efforts to engage employees, stakeholders or other audiences around sustainability priorities.

Working on sustainability priorities and initiatives connected to particular geographic markets or regions.

Marketplace Sustainability

Exploring how sustainability can be incorporated into Nike’s marketplace activities and consumer-facing initiatives.

People & Human Rights

Working on social sustainability, human rights and responsible business practices.

Raw Materials & Traceability

Supporting initiatives involving sustainable materials, sourcing and the ability to track materials through supply chains.

Supply Chain Compliance

Working on sustainability and compliance considerations throughout Nike’s global supply chain.

Sustainable Chemistry

Contributing to efforts involving cleaner chemistry and reducing the environmental impact of materials and production processes.

Sustainability Compliance & Reporting

Supporting sustainability reporting, compliance and related corporate responsibility activities.

This broad range of areas means that the internship can expose participants to different dimensions of sustainability, from environmental and climate issues to supply chains, human rights, reporting and business operations.

The Global Sustainability Graduate Intern will work with teams across Nike to help integrate sustainability into various areas of the business.

Conduct research.

Analyze information and datasets.

Develop strategic recommendations.

Communicate findings to different audiences.

Apply critical and strategic thinking.

TITLE: A Tribute to the late Prof.  George Magoha – Former President, Association of African Universities (AAU)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Secretary-General of the Association of African Universities (AAU), on behalf of the Governing Board and all African Universities, express the AAU’s deepest condolences to the family and friends – near and far – of the late Prof. George Albert Omore Magoha, who sadly passed on, on 24 January 2023.

Prof. Magoha served the Association of African Universities in various leadership positions, spanning more than a decade, with extraordinary commitment and dedication to duty, in a manner which earned him the respect of many higher education stakeholders across the continent. His words as captured in the AAU’s 50th Anniversary Brochure (produced in 2017), demonstrates his interconnectedness and the long-standing relationship with the Association’s leadership – ‘I have been a member of the AAU Governing Board from early 2005 to date [2017] having been elected at the Cape Town meeting. During these twelve and half years, I also served the AAU as the first Vice President in 2009-2010, and as President in 2011-2013. The AAU has made tremendous transformative progress with prolonged stability during this period. I congratulate the President, Secretary General, Executive Board and the entire AAU fraternity on the occasion of the AAU’s 50th Anniversary.’

Long before assuming leadership positions at the AAU, Prof. Magoha was not a new face to the Association – ‘I am a beneficiary of the Inter-African Universities Program (INTERAF) which began in 1967 and was managed by the Association of African Universities. I received a scholarship that enabled me enroll with the College of Medicine at the University of Lagos Nigeria from 1973 to 1978. The impact of this investment has been unquestionable – I am a full professor of Urological and Transplant Surgery, was Vice Chancellor of the University of Nairobi for 10 years and took up several distinguished leadership positions in many institutions’ – said Prof. Magoha in a document which profiled beneficiaries of the AAU’s previous initiatives.

The Association of African Universities wishes to place on record, our deep appreciation to Prof. George Magoha for his tenacity and resourcefulness in serving Africa’s higher education sector and for his great contribution to advancing education excellence in the continent and beyond. As a seasoned educator, he inspired and touched the lives of many students in profound ways, contributing to the shaping of a young generation that will honour his legacy and continue to lead the agenda of driving Africa to its next development phase.

The higher education sector in Africa is indeed filled with deep sadness and will miss his warmth and camaraderie, the frank and robust exchanges and discussions with him at various platforms where key decisions setting the agenda and targets of higher education in Africa were taken.

Through his good leadership and key results achieved on various fronts, Prof. Magoha leaves us with fond memories and meaningful learning from his unswerving sense of duty – that hard work and professionalism are great qualities worthy of emulation.

Prof. Magoha will forever be celebrated for playing a key role in transforming the African higher education sector and for being a mentor to many people, impacting and inspiring generations to build an even stronger African higher education system.

The Association of African Universities sends out its heartfelt condolences to the immediate family of Prof. George Albert Omore Magoha, the President and People of the Republic of Kenya, as well as the entire African Higher Education fraternity.

More About Prof. George Magoha

Prof. George Magoha was a Professor of Surgery at Maseno University School of Medicine in Kisumu County in Western Kenya at the time of his demise. He also served as the Cabinet Secretary of Education in the Cabinet of Kenya under the President, H.E Uhuru Kenyatta’s second term from 2019. Prior to that, he was appointed the Chairman of the Kenya National Examination Council (KNEC) from 2016 until 2019. His task as the Chairman of KNEC was to reform the council to arrest the widespread academic dishonesty and corruption in the administration of national examinations. He is credited with dismantling cartels that had propagated exam cheating for years and restoring the credibility of exams in Kenya.

Prof. Magoha’s passion and dedication to academia and the development of the African higher education sector spurred him to rise through the ranks from being in administrative positions at the University of Nairobi, Kenya to becoming chairman of the Academic Department of Surgery in 1999, Dean of the School of Medicine, Principal of the College of Health Sciences, Deputy Vice-Chancellor in charge of Administration and Finance to finally being the Vice-Chancellor in January 2005 after a competitive recruitment process. He was also a Professor of Surgery at the University of Nairobi’s College of Health Sciences, and concurrently served as a consultant urologist at the Kenyatta National Hospital, the university’s teaching hospital.

Prof. Magoha was the author of the book – Tower of Transformational Leadership, published by Kenway Publications in 2017. It is an autobiographical account of his experience as a leader in various roles in medicine, surgery, academia, and the community. As of May 2017, he was the chairman of the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Board.

He leaves behind his wife – Dr. Barbra Magoha, a Nigerian, and his son, Michael Magoha who are both medical doctors.

TITLE: Call for Papers-  2nd International Leadership Conference for Women in Higher Education

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Nairobi, Kenya|March 6-8, 2019

‘‘Theme: Promoting Women in Science to Address the 21st
Century Challenges’’

The Association of African Universities (AAU) is calling for papers for its second International Leadership Conference for Women in Higher Education in Nairobi, Kenya in 2019.

The
conference comes off from March 6-8, 2019 with the final date (March 8)
coinciding with the celebration of International Women’s Day, 2019, a day set
aside to celebrate women and push for gender equality and equity worldwide.

As
the apex organization and forum for consultation, exchange of information and
co-operation among institutions of Higher Education in Africa, AAU is cognisant
of the gender imbalances in African higher education and has thus been
dedicated to ensuring gender inclusiveness in its various initiatives and
projects.

The
International Leadership Conference for Women in Higher Education is one of
such key platforms provided by AAU for the discussion of innovative and
creative ways of empowering women, especially young women in higher education
to reach their full potential and aspire to the topmost leadership positions in
their chosen fields.

The
maiden edition, which was held in Accra, Ghana was highly successful and
brought women across national and international boundaries together to share
knowledge, ideas and strategic management skills required for success in
various leadership positions.

Focus
on Women in STEM

As
reflected by the theme, the focus of the 2019 Conference is on Promoting Women
in Science to address the 21st Century Challenges. Africa’s progress is
challenged by a myriad of problems ranging from lack of employment for its youth,
the existence of tropical diseases, weak entrepreneurial drive and low levels
of university-industry linkages, among others. It is widely accepted, that
Science and Technology do have a key role to play in overcoming the continent’s
developmental challenges.

However,
studies have revealed that though the number of women in science and
engineering is growing, men continue to outnumber women, especially at the
upper levels of these professions (AAUW, 2010). With only 24% of Science,
Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) occupations being filled by
women, various barriers, ranging from culture, implicit bias and subtle
stereotyping to wilful ignorance and blatant discrimination have been
identified as contributing factors (Pierce, Margo, 2013). Africa needs to
ensure that its human resource – both men and women, are fully engaged in the
STEM fields in solving its developmental challenges, and thus should make
significant investment into women in STEM to increase their contribution to
solving the continent’s challenges.

The
promotion of Women in Science to contribute massively and equally to a
developed Africa must therefore form an integral part of various plans and
strategies aimed at achieving the African Union’s vision of ‘Africa We Want’ by
the year 2063.

CONFERENCE
THEME AND SUBTHEMES

The Conference Theme is: Promoting Women in
Science to address the 21st Century Challenges. Based on the Conference theme,
the AAU is calling for papers under the following subthemes:

a)
Addressing Africa’s Challenges: the Role of Women in Science.

b) Current Developments on Women in Science,
Technology, Engineering and Mathematics in Africa.

c)
Breaking the Glass Ceiling – Policies, Strategies and Mechanisms to support
Women in STEM.

d) Resource Mobilization Strategies to support
STEM research.

e)
Barriers to Female Participation in STEM fields.

The concept paper for
this conference is accessible here – http://blogmain.aau.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/Concept-Note_Womens-Conference-in-Kenya.pdf
for further information

Conference Registration Link: https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/WoHE19

SPONSORSHIP

With support from the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida), authors whose papers are accepted for presentation will be funded to make their presentation at the conference.

Paper abstracts not exceeding two pages, must reach the AAU Secretariat not later than February 4, 2019

The abstract
should indicate the scope of the research, research objectives and methods of
inquiry. The paper abstracts must also include research results and
conclusions, as well as a discussion of how these findings differ from previous
work on the same subject.

Please submit
abstracts online at: https://www.aau.org/subs/wohe19/

Presenters of
successful Abstracts will be notified by February 7, 2019 and full papers will
be expected to be submitted by February 28, 2019.

Additional
information about the Conference will be shared with authors whose papers will
be selected. Abstracts should include name(s), institutional affiliation(s),
contact details of author(s) and the paper title.

Authors of papers
not selected will have the option to do a poster exhibition during the conference
on condition that they fund their participation.

you have challenges uploading your abstract, kindly contact Miss Georgina
Maison at: gdmaison@aau.org

TITLE: MYCP Policy Lab: Young Migrants Worldwide Invited to Shape Climate, Migration, AI and Future of Work Policy

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Young people with lived experience of migration and displacement are being invited to take part in the Migration Youth and Children Platform (MYCP) Policy Lab, an online programme designed to bring youth perspectives into international discussions surrounding climate change, migration, artificial intelligence, labour policy and the future of work.

Under the theme “Climate, Migration, AI & the Future of Work,” the MYCP Policy Lab brings together young people from around the world to learn directly from policymakers, international experts and practitioners while developing practical policy recommendations.

The programme is particularly focused on a major global challenge: as climate change transforms economies, livelihoods and patterns of human mobility, young migrants are among those directly affected by changing labour markets and climate-related displacement, yet their perspectives are often underrepresented in the development of policies that affect them.

Through the Policy Lab, participants will have an opportunity to move beyond simply discussing these challenges. They will work collaboratively to develop a policy brief focused on climate-labour policy and migrant youth inclusion, with the strongest work contributing to MYCP’s international advocacy.

The programme is delivered entirely online, opening participation to eligible young people from around the world.

About the MYCP Policy Lab

The MYCP Policy Lab is an interactive youth policy programme developed by the Migration Youth and Children Platform (MYCP).

Rather than functioning only as a series of lectures or presentations, the Policy Lab combines learning, discussion, teamwork and policy development.

Participants will engage with experts and other young people before working in teams to translate what they have learned into concrete policy recommendations.

The programme brings young participants into conversations with high-level policymakers and experts, including individuals with experience across international organisations, the United Nations system, the World Bank, academia, medicine and advocacy.

Through this combination of expert knowledge and youth experience, MYCP aims to create an environment where young migrants can contribute meaningfully to discussions that influence international migration and climate policy.

Why Climate Change, Migration and the Future of Work Matter

Climate change is not only an environmental challenge. Its consequences extend into employment, migration, health, education, gender equality and economic opportunity.

Changes in climate conditions can affect where people are able to live, which industries can provide sustainable employment and what types of jobs will exist in the future.

For migrants and young people on the move, these transformations can create additional challenges.

Climate-related disruption can contribute to displacement and migration, while changes in economies and labour markets can determine whether young migrants have access to secure and inclusive employment opportunities.

At the same time, emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, are transforming the nature of work.

The MYCP Policy Lab places young migrants within this wider conversation about climate, migration, AI and employment, giving participants an opportunity to examine these interconnected issues and contribute ideas for more inclusive policies.

What Participants Will Do During the MYCP Policy Lab

A major component of the programme is collaborative policy development.

Participants will work in teams to develop a policy brief addressing climate-labour policy and migrant youth inclusion.

This provides participants with an opportunity to apply what they learn during the expert sessions and discussions to a practical policy-making exercise.

Instead of simply learning about international policy processes, participants will experience elements of the policy-development process themselves.

Teams will explore challenges, discuss potential solutions and formulate recommendations that can contribute to broader advocacy surrounding migrant youth.

The programme culminates in final team presentations before a jury.

The winning policy brief will be published on the MYCP website and incorporated into MYCP’s advocacy for COP31, providing an avenue for participants’ ideas to reach broader international policy discussions.

What Participants Will Gain

Participation in the MYCP Policy Lab offers several learning, professional development and networking opportunities.

1. Expert Insights Into Climate, Labour and Migration

Participants will explore the relationship between climate change, employment and migration through perspectives provided by international organisations, activists and practitioners.

This can help young people understand how these issues intersect and how policies in one area may influence outcomes in another.

2. Perspectives Across Health, Gender and Education

The programme takes an intersectional approach rather than examining migration solely as an isolated policy issue.

Participants can expect perspectives relating to areas including:

Health

Gender

Education

Migration

Climate change

Labour and employment

Youth inclusion

International policy development

MYCP states that perspectives will include specialists associated with organisations such as UN Women, the World Bank and the International Labour Organization (ILO).

3. Practical Policy Development Experience

Participants will have the opportunity to work directly on the development of a policy brief.

This provides practical exposure to activities such as identifying policy challenges, working collaboratively, considering evidence and developing recommendations.

For young people interested in international relations, migration, sustainable development, advocacy or public policy, this can provide valuable introductory experience in policy development.

4. Certificate of Participation

Participants will receive a certificate of participation.

The certificate can serve as formal recognition of involvement in the programme and may be included on a participant’s CV or professional profile.

5. International Youth Network

Another significant aspect of the programme is the opportunity to connect with young people from different parts of the world who share an interest in migration and international policy.

Participants can build relationships with peers who are interested in contributing to migration policy, youth advocacy and international development.

6. Opportunity to Contribute to COP31 Advocacy

The programme is designed to lead to a tangible policy output.

The winning team’s policy brief will be published by MYCP and used as part of the organisation’s advocacy for COP31.

This gives participants an opportunity to contribute ideas that may form part of wider advocacy concerning climate change, labour and migrant youth inclusion.

MYCP Policy Lab Programme Schedule

The Policy Lab is structured around two principal days of online activities followed by separate final presentations.

Day 1: Introduction, Policymaking and Intersectional Approaches

The first day of the Policy Lab is scheduled to include:

An introduction to the Migration Youth and Children Platform

An introduction to the Policy Lab and its objectives

Exploration of the policymaking process from the perspective of international organisations

Discussion of community policy programmes

Examination of intersectional approaches to policy

This opening day is designed to provide participants with foundational knowledge that they can use during the collaborative policy-development process.

Day 2: Thematic Learning and Policy Brief Development

The second day moves further into thematic discussions and practical teamwork.

Activities are expected to include:

Thematic sessions addressing health, gender and education

Team breakout sessions

Collaborative policy brief development

Discussion of prizes

Information about next steps following the Lab

The team breakout sessions will provide participants with an opportunity to collaborate directly with other young people and begin translating discussions from the programme into policy recommendations.

Final Presentations

Following the two main Policy Lab days, teams will participate in final presentations.

According to MYCP, the presentations are scheduled for 17 or 18 October, with the final date to be confirmed.

During the final stage:

Participating teams will present their work before a jury.

Teams will showcase their policy proposals and recommendations.

A winning policy brief will be selected.

The winning brief will contribute to MYCP’s COP31 advocacy.

This final presentation stage adds a practical dimension to the programme by requiring participants to communicate and defend the ideas developed through their collaborative work.

Who Can Apply for the MYCP Policy Lab?

The opportunity is intended for young people on the move from anywhere in the world.

MYCP particularly encourages participation from young people with lived experience of climate migration.

Importantly, applicants are not required to have an established background in public policy.

According to MYCP, no previous policy experience is required. The organisation emphasises curiosity and commitment as sufficient foundations for participating in the programme.

This makes the Policy Lab potentially accessible to young people from a variety of educational, professional and personal backgrounds.

Applicants may therefore be interested in areas such as migration, climate change, youth advocacy, sustainable development, international relations, public policy, human rights, education, gender equality, health or the future of work without necessarily having formal qualifications in those fields.

Is Previous Policy Experience Required?

No formal policy background is listed as a requirement for participation.

This is an important feature of the MYCP Policy Lab because policy opportunities can sometimes appear inaccessible to young people without academic or professional experience in government, international relations or public policy.

MYCP instead describes curiosity and commitment as sufficient.

Participants will learn about policymaking during the programme and then have the opportunity to apply that knowledge through collaborative policy brief development.

Is the MYCP Policy Lab Open Internationally?

Yes. MYCP describes the programme as being for young people on the move from anywhere in the world.

The online format further supports international participation by removing the requirement to travel to a physical venue.

Applicants should nevertheless review the official application form and programme information carefully for any additional participation requirements, scheduling considerations or eligibility conditions.

About the Migration Youth and Children Platform

The Migration Youth and Children Platform (MYCP) works to increase the participation of children and young people in international migration policymaking.

MYCP operates by, with and for children and young people on the move and forms part of the Major Group for Children and Youth (MGCY).

MGCY serves as an official, formal and self-organised space through which children and young people under the age of 30 can contribute to and engage in certain United Nations intergovernmental and related policy processes.

MYCP’s broader mission is to bridge the gap between children and youth and the United Nations system, particularly on migration-related issues.

The organisation seeks to promote meaningful youth participation across four major areas:

Policy and Advocacy – supporting youth engagement with migration and sustainable development policymaking.

Capacity Building – helping children and young people develop the knowledge and capabilities necessary to participate effectively.

Youth Action – supporting youth-led engagement and initiatives.

Knowledge – strengthening access to information, research and knowledge relevant to children, youth and migration.

Through these areas of work, MYCP aims to ensure that young people affected by migration are not simply discussed within international policy processes but have opportunities to participate in them.

MYCP Policy Lab Dates and Format

The official MYCP webpage currently lists the following programme information:

Format: Online

Policy Lab: 10–11 October 2025

Final presentations: 17 or 18 October, with the final date to be confirmed

Application status displayed by MYCP: Applications open now

Prospective applicants should note that there is an apparent date inconsistency on the official webpage. Although the page currently states that applications are open, it lists the Policy Lab dates as 10–11 October 2025. Applicants are therefore strongly advised to verify the applicable programme year and dates directly with MYCP before applying.

Application Deadline

No specific application deadline is currently stated on the official MYCP Policy Lab webpage.

The page states that applications are open now, but does not provide a closing date.

Because the published programme dates and current application status appear inconsistent, prospective applicants should check the official MYCP website or application form for the latest information before submitting an application.

How to Apply for the MYCP Policy Lab

Interested candidates can apply online through the application form available on the official MYCP Policy Lab webpage.

Applicants should:

Visit the official MYCP Policy Lab webpage.

Review the programme information and eligibility criteria.

Navigate to the Apply Now section.

Open the online application form.

Complete all required information carefully.

Review the information provided before submission.

Submit the application according to the instructions in the form.

Because no application deadline is displayed on the programme page, interested applicants should avoid unnecessary delays if the application form remains open.

APPLY NOW

Why the MYCP Policy Lab Matters for Young Migrants

The MYCP Policy Lab is built around the principle that young people affected by migration should have opportunities to contribute to policies concerning their lives and futures.

Climate change, technological transformation and changing labour markets are increasingly interconnected. These changes can have significant consequences for migrants and displaced communities, particularly younger generations preparing to enter or already participating in the workforce.

Creating opportunities for young migrants to participate in these discussions can bring lived experience into policy conversations that might otherwise be dominated by institutional or technical perspectives.

The Policy Lab therefore combines capacity building with participation. Young people learn about policymaking while simultaneously developing recommendations that can feed into MYCP’s broader advocacy.

Conclusion

The MYCP Policy Lab on Climate, Migration, AI & the Future of Work provides an international online space for young people on the move to learn about policymaking, exchange perspectives with experts and peers, and contribute to policy recommendations concerning some of the most significant challenges affecting migration and employment.

Through expert sessions, thematic discussions, collaborative teamwork and policy brief development, participants can strengthen their understanding of the climate-labour-migration nexus while gaining practical exposure to international policy development.

The programme is particularly notable for welcoming young people without requiring previous policy experience and for placing lived experience at the centre of discussions concerning migrant youth.

Participants will also have the opportunity to receive a certificate, expand their international networks and develop a policy brief, with the winning submission published by MYCP and incorporated into its COP31 advocacy.

However, prospective applicants should carefully verify the programme dates before applying. The official MYCP webpage currently states that applications are open while displaying the Policy Lab dates as 10–11 October 2025, with final presentations scheduled for 17 or 18 October. No specific application deadline is currently published.

Interested young people should therefore consult the official MYCP Policy Lab webpage and application form for the latest programme information before submitting an application.

TITLE: PRESS RELEASE: 2024 Africa Universities’ Day Celebrations

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
PRESS RELEASE

Accra, Ghana, 10 October 2024 – The Association of African Universities (AAU) is calling on all higher education institutions across the continent to join the commemoration of this year’s Africa Universities’ Day. A week-long schedule of activities, slated from Monday November 11, through to Friday November 15, 2024, have been lined up for the celebrations, which also marks 57 years of the AAU’s existence and service to Africa’s higher education sector.

This year’s theme, “Educate an African fit for the 21st Century: Building resilient education systems for increased access to inclusive, lifelong, quality, and relevant learning in Africa”, is aligned to recognizing the year 2024 as the African Year of Education. The theme for this year was carefully selected to highlight activities in recognition of 2024 as the Year of Education, focusing on this important subject. For the first time, the African Union Commission has emphasized education as a central theme. The decision to prioritize education in 2024 was inspired by the global summit on transforming education, hosted by the United Nations Secretary-General in September 2022.

The Africa Universities’ Day is a key statutory event on the AAU’s calendar, observed annually to commemorate the founding of the Association on November 12, 1967, in Rabat, Morocco, as well as to highlight the contributions of the higher education sector to the development of the African continent. In 1994, and to coincide with the inaugural anniversary of the AAU, the Organisation of African Unity declared 12th November of every year as Africa Universities’ Day in pursuant to Resolution CM/Res.1534 passed by the OAU Council of Ministers in June of that year. The Africa Universities’ Day has been observed and celebrated by AAU member institutions since then. It also seeks to bring together academic leaders, policymakers, students, and industry experts to deliberate on key challenges and opportunities facing African universities.

“African Higher Education Institutions play a vital role in the overall success of the higher education system. They are essential in supporting all sectors of the economy and serve as the foundation for Africa’s development. As we celebrate 2024 as the Year of Education during our annual Africa Universities Week, we anticipate increased support for Africa’s education system and call on African governments and development partners to enhance and sustain their support for education across the continent.” – Prof. Olusola Oyewole, Secretary General, AAU.

This year’s events will be hosted virtually via the AAU-Zoom platform and streamed live on AAU TV as well as our social media pages on Facebook and YouTube.

This year’s commemoration will feature a series of insightful high-level panel discussions and keynote presentations by experts, scholars, and leaders from academia, industry, and the public sector. Further details on the theme and topics to be discussed are highlighted in the concept notes which can be accessed in ENGLISH, FRENCH, ARABIC and PORTUGUESE.

The registration link is made available here – https://bit.ly/2024AfricaUniversitiesDay .

The 2024 Africa Universities Day promises to be an engaging and thought-provoking event that will provide the much-needed platform for deliberations on the contributions of higher education to Africa’s development. African higher education institutions are encouraged to commemorate the day within their campuses by arranging engaging events in the form of seminars, debates, exhibitions, social media dialogues, conferences, webinars, and other activities, aimed at exploring the theme and maximizing Africa’s gains from higher education. Alternatively, in cases where such initiatives are not feasible, higher education institutions and other stakeholders are urged to participate in the AAU Secretariat’s planned activities.

AAU encourages the management of universities, to circulate information concerning the 2024 Africa Universities Day celebrations to the Ministries of Education, University Councils, Committees of Vice-Chancellors, and all institutions involved in the management of Higher Education Institutions for their attention and participation in the events. Other public and private universities in each country which are non-members of the AAU, research institutions, the media and public should also be invited to join the celebrations to give visibility to the Africa Universities Day and promote the activities of Higher Education Institutions in each country.

AAU – The Voice of Higher Education in Africa!!

—————————————————————————————————————

Media Contacts

Ms. Naomi Darko, Communications Assistant, AAU – ndarko@aau.org

Ms Nodumo Dhlamini, Director ICT Services, Comms & KM – ndhlamini@aau.org

About the Association of African Universities

The AAU is an international non-profit, non-governmental organization created by African Universities to promote cooperation among them on the one hand, and between them and the international academic community on the other. Created in 1967, the AAU is the voice of higher education in Africa and aims to improve the quality of African higher education and strengthen its contribution to Africa’s development by supporting the core functions of higher education institutions and facilitating critical reflections and consensus building on issues affecting higher education. The AAU headquartered in Accra, Ghana has a membership of more than 400 Higher Education Institutions and is the technical implementing arm of the African Union Commission (AUC) in higher education. The Association is also the coordinating agency of the Higher Education Cluster of the Continental Education Strategy for Africa (CESA 16-25). Through our guidance, our member universities are also responsible for implementing the AUC’s Science, Technology, and Innovation Strategy for Africa (STISA 2024).

TITLE: Global Research Initiative launched to advance Open Science through evidence-based approach

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Network News

Photo credit

A new international collaboration, the Global Research Initiative on Open Science (GRIOS), is being officially announced to provide comprehensive synthesis and evidence-based recommendations for advancing open science practices globally for the benefit of society and research itself. Supported by the French National Open Science Fund, and hosted at the European Science Foundation (ESF), GRIOS currently brings together key partners, including the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research, the Dutch Research Council (NWO), the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) and the French Committee for Open Science (Ouvrir la Science).

Open Science gets reality check

GRIOS emerges at a crucial time when research funders and institutions worldwide are seeking effective ways to implement open science policies. The initiative will use meta-research methods to address the need for robust evidence about what interventions in research culture and practices actually work. Responding to the G7 Science and Technology Ministers’ call from May 2023, GRIOS aims to leverage existing scientific research findings to inform and enhance open science policies globally.

Chaired by Marin Dacos, National Coordinator for Open Science, French Ministry of Higher Education and Research, and co-chaired by Henriikka Mustajoki, Secretary General for Open Science in Finland, and Hans de Jonge, Director of Open Science NL at NWO in the Netherlands, GRIOS will bring together international experts and organisations to advance three core objectives: delivering state-of-the-art analysis of open science research; identifying critical knowledge gaps and promoting new research; fostering international coordination along with knowledge sharing in open science research.

“NWO is proud to participate in GRIOS. As a funder who actively supports Open Science, it is crucial that we understand how to maximise the impact of our funded research,” explains Hans de Jonge. “As open science becomes mainstream, firmly embedded in policies, and expected in practice, it is more important than ever to understand what works and what doesn’t and thus base our actions on solid evidence. GRIOS can contribute valuable knowledge and evidence about Open Science policies to decision-makers, which will ultimately strengthen the global research ecosystem.”

Over the next four years, GRIOS will produce comprehensive reviews and evidence-based recommendations and propose a research roadmap on Open Science to fill knowledge gaps. This output will advance understanding, enhance practices, inform policies, guide further research, and strengthen collaboration in open science. All findings will be published in open access format, ensuring widespread accessibility and impact.

“Open Science has widespread support in principle, but making it work in practice requires understanding of what helps and what hinders researchers in sharing their work more openly”, says Marc Schiltz, GRIOS ambassador. “GRIOS will help us understand where communities are on the path to Open Science, what encourages change, and what is holding them back”.

Getting involved

The initiative welcomes partnerships with research organisations, funding bodies, and other stakeholders committed to advancing open science. For more information, please visit grios.org.

TITLE: New text on coastal oceanography, by PO Senior Scientist Emeritus Ken Brink

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Ken Brink, PO Senior Scientist Emeritus, recently published Physical Oceanography of the Continental Shelf, a graduate-level text. The book focuses on the dynamics of ocean currents in waters deeper than about 3 m and shallower than about 1000 m. This is a particularly important part of the ocean because of its high biological activity and its concentrated exposure to human presence, among other phenomena. Despite the importance of this region, a comprehensive volume of this sort has not been published since WHOI’s Gabe Csanady published Circulation in the Coastal Ocean during the 1980s.

The content builds on Ken’s Joint Program teaching experience. Topics treated include turbulent boundary layers, wind-driven upwelling, coastal-trapped waves, tides, buoyancy currents, instabilities and coupling with the deeper ocean. In each case, the underlying dynamics are discussed in light of ocean observations. Along the way, explanations are given for why winds off California drive currents off Oregon, why tides on the shelf can be so energetic, and the effects that make shelf currents so different than those in the deep open ocean.

The book is published by Princeton University Press, both as a hard copy and electronically. For those buying the book at the PUP website, use discount code BRINK30. It can also be purchased from other online merchants.

Ken Brink arrived at WHOI in 1980 and has been here ever since, even though he nominally retired in 2015. His research embraces observational, theoretical and numerical approaches. He has served as president of the Oceanography Society (1998-2000) and as chair of the National Academy’s Ocean Studies Board (1996-2001).

TITLE: 2022 Africa Universities Day Celebrations to Focus on Bringing Equity to Research and Publishing Through Open Science

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Accra, Ghana, September 02, 2022 In commemoration of this year’s Africa Universities’ Day, the Association of African Universities (AAU) is inviting all Higher Education Institutions across the continent to join the AAU mark this important statutory event on the Association’s calendar, while turning their focus on open science.

The Africa Universities’ Day which falls on November 12th each year, is set aside to celebrate the establishment of the AAU on November 12, 1967, as well as to highlight the contributions of the Higher Education Sector to the development of the African continent. The Day also provides an opportunity for critical dialogues targeted at improving the quality of Africa’s higher education towards the growth of the continent.

A weeklong celebration, featuring key events from November 7 -12, 2022, are planned to rally various higher education stakeholders, including African Universities, ministries of education, industry and development partner institutions as well as others to a common platform for high-level intellectual discussions, as part of the celebration.

The theme for this year’s celebration is Open Science -Bringing Equity to Research and Publishing. It is inspired by the need to increase the higher education community’s participation in research, visibility of African research, publication rate, and the overall number of researchers through the promotion of the accurate verification of scientific results. The concept note for the celebrations is available in English and French for stakeholders attention.

The celebrations seek to increase advocacy for the adoption of best practices to further generate knowledge about Open Science, and its impact on interdisciplinary science research, as well as highlight opportunities created for scholars and communicators of research to learn from one another. The Africa Universities’ Day will also provide a platform for peer learning and networking to foster collaborations among participating institutions. The concept note for the 2022 Africa Universities’ Day celebration is accessible via this link for further information on the theme.

Through high-level presentations and panel discussions, this year’s Africa Universities’ Day celebration, will provide the much-needed platform for higher education stakeholders to discuss important open science sub-themes including – Open data practices in research processes; instituting research data management plans for data management in higher education institutions; supporting open review for research transparency; building a culture of open scholarship in African higher education institutions; and building, revamping, and increasing awareness of African institutional repositories.

African higher education institutions are encouraged to mark the day in their institutions by organising high level and participatory event such as seminars, debates, exhibitions, social media conversations, conferences, webinars and several others to dissect the theme and to help Africa reap the most benefits from open science. In the absence of these, higher education institutions and other stakeholders are encouraged to join the activities lined up by the AAU Secretariat.

AAU encourages the management of universities, to circulate information concerning the 2022 Africa Universities’ Day celebrations to the Ministries of Education, University Councils, Committees of Vice-Chancellors, and all institutions involved in the management of Higher Education Institutions for their attention and participation in the events. Other public and private universities in each country which are non-members of the AAU, research institutions, the media, and the general public are also invited to join the celebrations to give visibility to Africa Universities’ Day and promote the activities of Higher Education Institutions in each country.

AAU – The Voice of Higher Education in Africa!!

About the Association of African Universities

The AAU is an international non-profit, non-governmental organization created by African Universities to promote cooperation among them on the one hand, and between them and the international academic community on the other. Created in 1967, the AAU is the voice of higher education in Africa and aims to improve the quality of African higher education and strengthen its contribution to Africa’s development by supporting the core functions of higher education institutions and facilitating critical reflection and consensus building on issues affecting higher education. The AAU is headquartered in Accra, Ghana has a membership of more than 400 Higher Education Institutions and is the technical implementing arm of the African Union Commission (AUC) in higher education. The Association is also the coordinating agency of the Higher Education Cluster of the Continental Education Strategy for Africa (CESA 16-25). Promptly reporting suspected fraud, corruption, collusion, coercion, conflicts of interest, or other procurement irregularities to the Procurement Specialist.
